Arriving too late to stop the ceremony, Ivar led the restored Skorgrím away, tasking Marrec with slaying you. Fortunately, with your help, Dwalin was able to defeat Marrec.
Elrohir told you that he did not think Ivar and Skorgrím would be a threat to Ered Luin for at least a little while.

'I consulted with the Elves while you were away and learned that Elrohir, one of the sons of Elrond, is exploring the Mirkstone Tunnels to the north-west of here.
'He intends to learn more about the Dourhand's plans, and I want you to be there when he does! The entrance to the Mirkstone Tunnels can be found at the top of the Axe-head Path, north-west of here.
'The Dourhands have much to answer for!'

'Welcome, Master Dwarf. I presume you come at the behest of Dwalin? I have found some intriguing information here in the cave. At a campsite near here, I found a letter.
'It was penned by a man called Marrec, and I sense something foul is afoot. He speaks of a dark master and a plan to return the dead leader of the Dourhands to life. For this, the Dourhands would pledge their loyalty to Angmar!
'It is imperative that Marrec and his master be stopped. The letter speaks of a tomb...I believe I know where it may be found, so I am going to go there, but I would like you to return the letter to Dwalin. Tell him that the Elves and dwarves must unite to drive the Dourhands from Ered Luin!'

'This is madness! Restoring a dwarf to life? The lore of my people has always told that certain dwarves are returned to us, but deliberately restoring one to life? It is not possible! There is no power in Middle-earth that can do so.
'I think that there is something far more sinister at work here. I have heard that necromancers once sent fell spirits into the Dead to stir them....
'We must stop the Dourhands and their new allies before it's too late. I will tell my dwarves to band together with the Elves, but I cannot just stand here as Elrohir goes into that tomb alone. We must follow...I fear for him.'
'Did you find Elrohir?'
Bring the letter to Dwalin
Intro: Goblins in the Crags
The Elves told Dwalin that Elrohir, son of Elrond, entered the Mirkstone Tunnels near Thorin's Hall to discover more about the plans of the Dourhands.

'Elrohir should be in the Mirkstone Tunnels, if the Elves words are true, and I've no reason to think they aren't!
'The entrance to the Tunnels lies at the top of the Axe-head path, north-west of here.'
'Return this letter to Dwalin. We must put an end to the Dourhand's plans!'

Elrohir may be found somewhere in the Mirkstone Tunnels. The entrance to the Tunnels lies at the top of the Axe-head Path, north-west of Frerin's Court.
Elrohir, son of Elrond, entered the Mirkstone Tunnels to search for answers to the mystery of why the Dourhands have allied themselves with goblins. Dwalin asked you to meet with Elrohir to see what he may have learned.

Dwalin can be found in Frerin's Court, south-east of the Mirkstone Tunnels.
Elrohir gave you a letter to take to Dwalin.

'Oh, hello there! You are the one who came with that Ranger, Amdir, the other night, aren't you? What a tale he told of your adventure. You must be quite brave!
'Oh, don't mind my blather! I think Amdir wanted to speak with you. Last I saw him, he was resting on the ground just south of here, around the corner of the big building there.
'He looked awfully pale. That hurt he took must be worse than it looked.'

'Gracious, just look where they want me to stay! This is nothing like home. And they say I can't go home until those Blackwold fellows are dealt with. This is outrageous!
'Well, I don't need you hanging about now, bothering me. Go talk to that Amdir fellow. He's sitting just south of here.
'I've no interest in sharing my troubles with the likes of you. Now leave me be!'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}. It is good to see you whole and hale. You proved yourself quite the hero, leading the hobbits and me here to Archet last evening. I must confess that I do not recall much of the journey.
'Nay, do not concern yourself with my injuries; though they appear grave, I have taken worse. My only fear is that the blade may have been poisoned, but young Celandine is seeing to my needs.
'There is a matter that needs immediate attention, one that I cannot undertake. Captain Brackenbrook, the founder of the garrison here in Archet, suffers my presence only because of my injuries. Few in Bree-land trust Rangers.'
Intro: Amdir's Request

After rescuing you from the Blackwold brigands and a mysterious Black Rider, the Ranger Amdir brought you to the village of Archet in the Chetwood, east of Bree-town. The town, under threat of attack, prepares a defence against the Blackwolds.
'That Amdir fellow who brought you in has been asking for you. He's outside The Mad Badger Inn, near the centre of town.'

'I've got nothing to tell you. I just want out of this village! I tell you, this whole affair has been an insult!
'If you want to talk to someone, go see that Amdir fellow.'

Amdir may be found resting on the ground near the centre of Archet, outside The Mad Badger Inn.
The Ranger Amdir has spread word that he wishes to speak with you.
Defeated Celandine's captors (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Mundo's captor

'Thank you, thank you, thank you! I was hoping that hooded fellow -- you said his name was Amdir? -- I was hoping he was here to rescue me. When I didn't see him return, I feared these men caught him! But it seems he was only getting help!'
'My friend Mundo is nearby, I think. We must save him as well! These brigands have been saying terrible things!
'We'll need a distraction...and I know just what to do!'
'Poor Amdir is hurt! We need to take him to Archet...it's not far! Someone there will know what to do!'

'You...you found them. You rescued the hobbits.
'Do not...concern yourself with me. The greatest danger...has passed. The Nazgûl fear those who wield fire....'

'It's about time! Was I expected to...to rescue myself?
'Come on, you big clodpole! Get me out of here before those ruffians return. They want to sell me off like a sack of potatoes!'

'I hope you found a weapon you can use, for now our paths must part for a time. While you see about freeing the hobbits, Celandine Brandybuck and Mundo Sackville-Baggins, I will follow that Éogan fellow and see what I can learn of his plans with the Black Rider.
'Free Celandine first, for Éogan's words tell me that she is in the greatest danger. It is Mundo they want alive. When you have both hobbits safe, seek me near the main gate. We will return the hobbits to Archet and expose Calder Cob's treachery to Jon's father.
'Now, do you have everything you need before you go on? I would not recommend venturing forth without a weapon!'

'Good, you are awake. The Blackwolds gave you quite a knock on the head, and I feared you would not awaken soon enough. There is little time to talk, but I will tell you what I may.
'I am what some in Bree call a Ranger. I have come here to learn what connexion these men have with a Black Rider I was tracking from the Shire. However, the situation has worsened. I learned from Jon Brackenbrook, a hunter in Archet, that a guard from his father's garrison -- Calder Cob by name -- is working for the Blackwolds and captured two visiting hobbits. Indeed, I have seen them here. I will need your help if I am to free the hobbits.
'First, I must free you from this pen. When you are free, search the crate just outside the fence for a weapon. Speak with me again when you are armed. Quietly now! We must await the right moment....'
Speak to Amdir
After arming yourself, speak to Amdir
Defeat Celandine's captors (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Mundo's captor
Find Amdir
Instance: Jail Break
While travelling through the Chetwood, you were waylaid by brigands and taken captive. You now find yourself in a cell, searching for a means of escape.
You awake in a holding pen in a brigand camp. A strange man stands before you, beckoning to you.

The crate containing the Blackwolds' gear rests just outside the gate of the enclosure.
Amdir told you to gather weapons from among the brigands' gear, then speak with him again when you are armed.

Celandine Brandybuck is being held elsewhere in the brigand camp.
After you armed yourself, Amdir told you to rescue the hobbits, starting with Celandine, while he followed Éogan. You will need to dispatch any brigands you come upon while searching for the hobbits.

Celandine is being held in a cage against the wall of the enclosure.
You have defeated Celandine's captors, but your task is not yet fulfilled. Celandine may be able to tell you where Mundo is being held.

Mundo Sackville-Baggins is being held in the courtyard beyond the gate of Celandine's holding pen.
Celandine's distraction was a success. Only one brigand remains behind to guard Mundo. You should dispatch him quickly.

Mundo is tied to a post in the courtyard.
Despite the defeat of his captor, Mundo Sackville-Baggins appears particularly displeased. You should encourage him to join you.

Amdir awaits you and the hobbits at the main gate.
You have freed both of the missing hobbits, but you have not yet escaped the camp.

Amdir lay just beyond the main gate.
The Ranger Amdir was struck down by the Black Rider. You should tend to his wound.

Celandine waits near the main gate.
Amdir is dying, and you do not have the skill to heal him. Celandine may know where he may receive help.
If you would like to skip the remainder of the introductory tutorial experience and be transported to Archet following the burning of the town, speak to the Ranger Amdir again.

If you choose to skip the introductory tutorial experience, you will be transported to Archet after it has been burned and will be unable to travel to Archet prior to those events.
Are you sure you want to continue?
Talk to Amdir to skip the Introduction
Skip Introduction
If you would like to skip the remainder of the introductory tutorial experience and be transported to Archet following the burning of the town, speak to the Ranger Amdir again.

'As I believe I mentioned to you before, I came to Archet to learn what connexion the Blackwolds had to the Nazgûl. Here I met Jon Brackenbrook, Captain Brackenbrook's son. It was from him that I learned the location of the Blackwolds' camp and of Celandine and Mundo's capture.
'Jon and his father recently had a terrible falling out. Jon believed that a member of the Captain's garrison, Calder Cob, was in league with the Blackwold brigands. Before I came to you, I witnessed Cob and Éogan discussing a raid on the town. Jon's suspicions are correct, and his father must be warned.
'Captain Brackenbrook, like many, distrusts Rangers and will not heed anything I have to say. Perhaps, if the news comes from you, he will listen. He commands the garrison from The Mad Badger. The entrance is just to the south there, up those steps.'

'I had feared this may happen. Captain Brackenbrook is a good man, but set in his ways.
'Calder Cob has done his job too well. We will need to find another way to expose Cob's treachery.'

'You are the one who brought the Ranger back to Archet? My son was foolish enough to befriend him and dared accuse one of my finest guards of betrayal.
'If you are here to tell me the same tale, I say be off with you. Calder Cob personally apprehended Otto, the leader of the Blackwolds. He is in the stocks now if you would like to see him. In the last week, he has captured two more brigands, so I will hear no more of this traitor nonsense.
'If you wish to aid Archet, take up arms and make your way to the sheep-farm to the south and west and help Dirk Mudbrick against the wolves that plague the farmers! And tell that Ranger friend of yours to mind his own concerns.'
Intro: Captain Brackenbrook

Jon Brackenbrook, the son of the captain who organized Archet's garrison, feared the presence of a traitor within the garrison's ranks. The Ranger Amdir confirmed Jon's suspicions at the Blackwolds' camp.
'Captain Brackenbrook is set in his ways and will not heed my words. Nevertheless, he must be informed that Calder Cob is playing him the fool.'
'I have no time for nonsense. The Blackwolds are leaderless, and soon I'll have these townsfolk ready to assail the brigands' encampment. That will end their threat once and for all!'

Captain Brackenbrook commands the garrison from The Mad Badger Inn to the south of Amdir.
Amdir fears that Captain Brackenbrook will not heed his tidings of the traitor Calder Cob, but hopes that if the news comes from you, he will listen.

Amdir rests against the building north of The Mad Badger Inn.
Captain Brackenbrook was not willing to hear what you had to say about Calder Cob. Instead, he told you to tell Amdir to stay out of Archet's troubles, after suggesting you help the local farms fend off wolves.

'While the wolves in this part of the Chetwood are not as fierce as others, they can still present a threat to an untrained warrior. I think it might be best if you train further before coming to Archet's aid.
'Fortunately, I have heard that an experienced ${CLASS} has come to Archet to aid in her defence. That ${CLASS} might just be able to help you improve your own abilities. I believe the ${CLASS} is up the slope, west of the training grounds near Archet's gate.
'Once you are through training, return to me here.'

'Ah, good. You have returned. I hope you found your time with your fellow ${CLASS} enlightening.
'If you find it strange that I have given you food, think upon this: If you are to maintain your strength, you must eat. Should you find yourself in need of more provender, you may speak to Peg Pruner, the garrison's quartermaster, to the north of here.
'Now, I think it is time you take my place and come to Archet's defence, if you are prepared.'

'So you want to learn the ways of the burglar? Well, I'm the one to teach you then! I don't mind sharing a few tricks with you, but before I do, there's a bit of advice I should give you.
'Before getting into a fight, study your enemy's weaknesses and use those against him. And never forget that in many cases, your enemy's greatest weakness is his mind. You'd be surprised how often a simple trick will give you an advantage in a fight.
'Good fortune to you in the days ahead!'

'I welcome you to Archet. Dark days lie ahead for this village, but with another Captain here, there may yet be hope. I will gladly train you, if you would have me, but I would share a word of advice before we continue.
'What you must keep in mind is that a Captain best serves his companions not when he is at the front line. Nay, it is when he stands behind and directs their efforts that he truly shines. There he can see weaknesses in his enemies or press his companions forwards and inspire them to victory.
'Keep this in mind in the days ahead.'

'Ah, another strong arm for the fight! Welcome, friend! I long for the battle ahead, yet I will pause from my preparations to aid you, if I can.
'A champion is not one who waits at the rear of the battle. No, he stands to the fore, challenging all who dare come before him! And if things come to their darkest -- and sometimes they shall -- a champion will gladly lay down his life so that his fellows may survive.
'Keep my words in mind, and you shall enjoy many a glorious battle!'

'A fine day to you. It warms my heart to see another who has chosen the path of the Guardian. Few truly understand what it means to be a Guardian.
'Victory is hollow if what you were fighting for was lost in the battle as well. In battle, a Guardian always seeks to draw the ire of his enemies, keeping the weak in his charge safe from their blows. And many times a Guardian can use the anger he inspires to his advantage, turning his enemy's attacks back upon him.
'Never forget those who depend upon you, Guardian.'

'Welcome to Archet. This village is in a difficult spot, but with another Hunter around it might just survive, eh? I'd be happy to share what skills I have with you, but before I do, I'll give you a couple of pieces of advice.
'Unlike some of the other warriors you may run into, we Hunters don't like to get into the thick of things. It's better if we stand off at a distance and fling a few arrows into our enemy. And if the enemy decides he wants to get up close, we end it quick. If it doesn't end quick, well, you might be in a spot of trouble yourself.
'Of course, if your aim is true, that won't be a problem, now will it?'
Speak to the trainer
Intro: Honing Your Skills
Amdir recognizes that your skills, while significant, need improvement if you are to deal with the threats posed to Archet.

'I can tell that you have a willing spirit, but such a spirit may not be enough to deal with the threats here. You should speak to the ${CLASS} who lingers west of Archet's training grounds.
'That ${CLASS} may be able to help you improve your own abilities.'
'What? You want me to share all my secrets? A greedy one, aren't you? I think you had best go back to Amdir now.'
'I am sorry, but I have taught you all you are ready to know. You should return to Amdir.'
'You'd best be getting back to that Amdir fellow. I've taught you what you need for now.'
'Always remember: It is your task to risk your life. Now go back to that Amdir fellow.'
'I have taught you the skilful use of the bow...what more is there to learn? You should return to Amdir.'
'It is best that thou return to Amdir. There is no more I can teach thee at this time.'
'Here...just hum the scales a few times. You should return to Amdir now.'

'I bid thee welcome. It is good to meet another walking the path of wisdom, and I will gladly share what insight I have gained with thee.
'As thou grow in knowledge and ability, thou will find that thou will have many allies to call upon in your struggles. The birds and animals of the land will lend their strength to thee. Even the strength of the very land can be drawn upon, if thou gain such knowledge. Thou will also find that thy companions will come to depend upon thy knowledge and wisdom, especially in the treatment of the various maladies and tricks the Enemy uses.
'There is much wisdom to be found in Middle-earth. Use it well.'

'A good day to you! I am pleased to find another Minstrel here in Archet. The spirits of many in this village need the soothing comfort of a silver voice and gentle melody! And, of course, I would be happy to share what skills I have with you. First, though, I will share some small advice, if you are willing to lend an ear to it.
'As you may already know, a Minstrel possesses a great power...the power to stir the spirit and raise hopes when all seems lost. We can even strengthen the resolve of our fellows to face what may at first appear insurmountable odds!
'Use your gifts well, and you shall never know defeat!'

The ${CLASS} trainer can be found west of Archet's training grounds.
Amdir suggested you train further before coming to Archet's defence.

Amdir can be found outside The Mad Badger Inn in the centre of Archet.
Now that you have spoken to the more experienced ${CLASS} and have learned new abilities, you should return to Amdir.
Defeated wolves near Archet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It appears you are prepared for battle, ${PLAYER}. You should make your way to the sheep farm south and west out of Archet's gate. Seek Dirk Mudbrick and tell him that you are there to assist him at the behest of Captain Brackenbrook.
'If the wolves are truly threatening the sheep, then we should do what we can to assist the people here in Archet.
'Also, if you have not spoken to her yet, Celandine Brandybuck could use your help. I have asked her to help me treat my wound as if it were poisoned and will need athelas, or \qkingsfoil\q as it is commonly known. Might I ask that you help her in this as well?'

'Well now, what with the Captain paying no heed to the talk o' traitors, I guess ye be needing some work? There's more to do down Combe-way, but the roads are too dangerous for travelling.
'Well, far be it from me to refuse help. These wolves are proving bad. We've lost more sheep than I care to mention. And that's just about all I've got to guard, what with most folk already pulled within the walls o' the village.
'I need ye to clear out as many o' the wolves beyond the gates as ye can. The longer they're about, the bolder they'll get!'

'You're stouter than I thought. Well done with those wolves. There's much more to be done though!
'The Captain won't see the true threat, though. I shouldn't say anymore...my mouth is why I was assigned to this place.'

Intro: Seeing to the Defence
Amdir has asked you to see to the defence of Archet by helping Captain Brackenbrook.

'If Captain Brackenbrook wants you to help Archet by hunting wolves with DIrk Mudbrick, then do so. I will see what I can do to expose Calder Cob.
'You should find Mudbrick at the sheep-farm south and west outside Archet's gate.'
'I see the trophies of your hunt about yous. You should return to Dirk Mudbrick and let him know of your success!'
'The wolves are becoming a serious threat, thanks in no small part to the Blackwolds. You can find them to the south of Archet's gates.'

Wolves can be found east and south of the farm.

Collected Blackwold orders

'Well, since I already opened my mouth, I guess I should explain myself a little. I mentioned to the Captain that the Blackwolds seemed a bit stronger than we'd been told, and that we ought to listen to Jon and spy out their camp. If we'd done that, we might have stopped them from grabbing them two hobbits.
'Now, when I says this, the Captain re-assigns me from gate-duty to watching these sheep here. I see brigands making their way through the woods here and there, and I can't help thinking that they are trying to get a good look at us.
'We need to know what they've learned and what they're up to. If ye can, confront one of their spies and see what ye can discover. Bring me any orders or messages ye find. I swear I saw some of their spies sneaking about to the southeast, between here and Bronwe's Folly.'

'Did ye read this, ${PLAYER}? It was just like Jon said! Calder...Calder was in league with the Blackwolds!
'Jon was right. He warned us about Calder, but the Captain paid him no mind. Calder used the Captain's stubborness against him and turned him on his own son!
'There must be some devilry at work here! Calder will see the inside of our jail before the day is over! Quickly, take these orders to Captain Brackenbrook and show him what you've found.'
'So have you found anything yet?'

'Jon was right. I've been a fool. My son warned me against Calder Cob, but I paid him no mind. Calder has always been an able and trustworthy man.
'All the while, he was driving me towards training rather than confronting the brigands. How much information do the brigands have? How much time do we have to prepare? I must get word to my son.
'But first, Calder must pay for this affront!'
'Have you dealt with those wolves yet? Don't keep Mudbrick waiting.'

Intro: The Spies
The Blackwolds have sent spies to appraise the situation in Archet, which has become a cause of concern for Dirk Mudbrick.
'The Blackwold spies are hiding between here and Bronwe's Folly, to the south-east. They must be dealt with!'
'Quickly now, bring that letter to Captain Brackenbrook at The Mad Badger. He needs to know about Calder before he learns more secrets to take to the Blackwolds. Hopefully, we're not too late.'
'Ah, you're the one who done this to me! I'll have my revenge on you yet!'
'You'll pay for sticking your nose where it don't belong!'
'Just wait until when the Blackwolds come and free me!'

'I have been such a fool. With Calder Cob turned traitor, I do not know whom to trust anymore. How many more spies dwell among us?
'I would ask a favour of you. Go speak with my son Jon and ask for his help against the Blackwolds. Jon spends most of his time at the Hunter's Lodge to the east of Archet. From the town-gate, follow the road that wends to the east, and you will eventually make your way to the lodge.
'If you can sway my son's heart, I will reward you handsomely.'
'So my father's eyes have been opened to the truth? And none too soon! The Blackwolds are preparing to move against Archet, and the defences are ill-prepared.'
Intro: The Captain's Son

Captain Brackenbrook has been estranged from his son, Jon, ever since they fought over the loyalty of Calder Cob. Captain Brackenbrook trusted Cob, while Jon had been suspicious of him. The orders you found proved Jon right.
'Go to the Hunter's Lodge and speak with my son, Jon. The east road that leads from Archet's gate will take you there.'
'I cannot believe I was so fooled by Calder.'
'If Archet it so to be saved, it will be through the strength of people like you and my son.'
'I wonder if my son will ever forgive me?'

Jon Brackenbrook can be found at the Hunter's Lodge that lies along the road east of Archet.

'What's that? You're a burglar? Oh, of course, of course! I did some burgling in my day, you know. I helped Thorin and the dwarves regain their lost home in the Lonely Mountain. I'm afraid I didn't do a very good job and bungled the whole thing right up, but I suppose everything turned out all right in the end.
'A burglar needs to be light on his feet and just as quick in his own head! If I hadn't been both of those, old Smaug would have cooked me until I was well-done on several occasions!
'I wrote it all down, you know. There might be a lesson or two in there for an aspiring burglar, if you were of a mind to look. The best advice I can give to you about burgling is this: don't! It caused me only grief for a long while, and I know that Thorin would tell you the same, if he were still here. At any rate, I'm glad we had this conversation, ${PLAYER}. 'While you were gone, Lindir told me he has come up with something interesting for our game. Apparently, he found a new riddle on the back of some old parchment out of Gondor.'

'What is this? A game? Ha, ha, I see, a riddle out of Gondor is it? Well, you have come to the right man, indeed!
'Nay, I fear I cannot give you my horn, even for a minute, because it is my trust and duty to bear it, but I will give you something that should suffice.
'This is the badge of my position, as the Steward's heir. As you can see it shows a horn above the White Tree of Gondor. I daresay that Elf-loremaster will be satisfied with this token.'

'Parchment can be difficult to find at times in the world of Men, so I am not all that surprised to find a riddle scrawled on the back of some old chronicles of Gondor. Perhaps some young scribe of the Tower had overmuch time on his hands....
'It just so happens that the answer can again be found in Imladris:
'Breath is needed Warning heeded Some will arrive With sword and knife My work is completed 'Til once more I'm needed'
'Excellent! You found the answer. I will see that it is returned to Boromir. Well-played. I trust the fact the item was not just laying on a shelf was no obstacle?'
'The answer to this riddle is certainly here in Imladris, but it may not be here for long!'

'Hello there, friend ${RACE}. I wonder if you can help out an old hobbit who is not as spry as he used to be? Lindir and I are playing a friendly riddle-game. Here is his latest:
'I often hold your hand, But I have no hands wherewith to hold. I often sleep in summer, But I do my best when it grows cold. I often lose my mate, But I feel no sorrow, if truth be told.
'If truth be told, I'm quite stumped! Speak to Lindir about it -- it could be he has forgotten an important line or two.'

Lindir smiles. 'I thought for once I would try one of the homely riddles that Bilbo loves so well, rather than an involved mystery of Elf-lore. And so it seems that with his mind in the clouds of Sindarin poetry, our friend here cannot solve old-fashioned riddles of the hobbit-kind!
'But I will give you the hint I gave Bilbo. The answer to this riddle can be found here in Imladris. Just find the answer and bring it here to solve the riddle.'

'Ha! Well done. The answer fits like a glove, does it not?'
Bilbo shakes his head ruefully. 'You have out-foxed me, Lindir! I was rummaging through all my small stock of Elf-lore searching for some poem or tale to fit your verse, but I should have been thinking of more prosaic things, after all. I wonder if you can answer my next little puzzle, though, my friend!'
Lindir smiles. 'I did not think this riddle was very difficult, but it seems sometimes the simplest puzzles are the hardest to solve.'

'You have proven yourself an expert riddle-solver. Bilbo and I have of late been contemplating a riddle of the most interesting sort -- one for which no answer is yet known. This riddle seems to bear on the lineage of the House of Elrond itself and may be of great import if it is solved.
'For once we cannot say for sure that the answer truly lies in Imladris, but it is certain that the riddle is concerned with Rivendell more than with any other place.
'Bilbo can tell you more, but I think for the full story of this riddle you will have to speak to others as well.'

'Well, this was written by Elrond's wife, Celebrían, who long ago sailed into the West. Just before she departed Middle-earth, she inscribed these words. The verse was probably not meant as a riddle, but its meaning is nevertheless hidden, even to her own family. I hope you will excuse my poor translation into Westron. The riddle goes like this:
'The jewel of the moon, Enshrined in the water, From mother to daughter Is given a boon.
'Ships sail to the west, Forgetting all sorrow, Landfall on the morrow, The isles of the blest.
'It may be that Master Elrond will be able to tell you something more about these words. It would be splendid if the riddle could be solved after all these years, and even more wonderful if some lost legacy could be found and delivered to Lady Arwen.'

'Those old words...alas, I had hoped not to have those evil days recalled to me. But I know that Lindir must mean well. Indeed, if there was some legacy of her mother I could give to Arwen, I would do so gladly.
'But the meaning of the words is a mystery to me, and those who might once have known have been gone for long years.
'I wonder at it, since this has come to my mind after so long a space. Glorfindel was present at the time these words were written. I have never thought to speak with him on this subject. Seek him by the falling water outside my house and ask him the meaning of the old words.'

'A riddle? A mystery? Had but Elrond inquired of me, I could have unravelled these last sad words of his wife long ago.
'There was a splendid white gem, a very jewel of the moon as the verse says, which long ago was hidden away in a secret vault. This is Arwen's legacy, that was meant to go to her. Even I do not know where this vault was hidden, but I am sure it could not have been far from Imladris.'

'So, you say you have defeated the wraiths? I fear that they were not wholly destroyed, for they are bound to this world by the spells upon those hilts.
'The malice of their spirits still remains, and they will return in time. I have read all I can from the morgul-hilts. They are twisted and black, but they bear strange devices for works of the Enemy. I would ask you to bear the hilts as quickly as may be to the vale of Rivendell to the house of Elrond Halfelven...he will know how best to deal with them.
'Rivendell lies deep in the Trollshaws, far to the south and east. Destroying the hilts should break the spell that binds their unseen sinues to this world. I caution you again: do not handle the hilts, but carry them as swiftly as possible to Rivendell.'

'These are old hilts and well-crafted. Their original make appears to have been by a craftsman of Eregion, for they bear many of the markings and style of their smith-work, but that craft has been twisted and corrupted into their current form.
'The morgul-runes upon the hilts bear the oaths of their owners. It is a dark oath that I will not have spoken aloud in my halls. Because of their craft, I do believe that they can be unmade...bring them to Hemeldir at the Forges of Rivendell.'

'I can unmake the morgul-hilts. It is strange that their craftsmanship is similar to that of the Elven smiths of old, though they bear marks of great pain and malice. These hilts cast a shadow upon my heart. I fear a greater evil in their making than even Master Elrond may have surmised.
'Their destruction should indeed break the spells that bind them to this world.'

'Welcome to Imladris, ${PLAYER}. It is good that you have come. Rest well, but not too deeply or too long! We have need of adventuring folk, for there is evil beyond the vale.
'Not more than two months ago, a hobbit by the name of Frodo Baggins and his companions were pursued to the Ford of Bruinen by servants of the Enemy. I speak of the Nine, the Nazgûl, fell creatures in the service of Sauron, and though the Bruinen fell upon them at my command, we have found the steeds of only eight. One of the Riders is unaccounted for.
'My sons set forth with scouts bound to them by friendship to seek this missing Rider. I ask that you speak with Elladan at their camp of Thorenhad, among the Bruinen Gorges, and lend your aid to the search. We must learn where this Nazgûl has gone, and most importantly, his designs.'

'My father has sent you to aid us? It is good that you have come, for we have made an unsettling discovery. It seems likely the missing Rider is still somewhere within the wilderness of the Trollshaws.'

Lord Elrond has asked you to lend your assistance to his sons Elladan and Elrohir, currently seeking the missing Nazgûl.

'You are fortunate. The creature which you faced could not have been a true Onod. You could not possibly have faced the might of one of the Old Ones.
'Nor would you have to, for the Onodrim are friendly to the Free Peoples on the rare occasion their paths meet. The great forests are less-travelled now than they were in days past, and few now ever see one of the great tree-herds.
'A small company of Elves from Mirkwood came to Imladris to consult with my father. Perhaps one of them will know what manner of creature you faced. Speak with my father to arrange an audience.'

'I am glad you so ably serve my sons, ${PLAYER}. I feel that you are close to locating the Nazgûl that escaped the raging waters of the Bruinen.
'And yet more evils reveal themselves. The Elves of Mirkwood have encountered such evil before. My son was right to send you to me.
'Speak with Legolas, son of Thranduil, at the Haven of Orladion, just outside my house. He has been often in thought while he remains here and may be able to help you find and defeat the source of the evil.'

'Hail to you, ${PLAYER}. If you did not bring such dire news I would greet you more heartily, but your tidings are troubling.
'We of Mirkwood have indeed encountered these creatures before, but it is not something I expected to see again. A tribe of troll once lived near Dol Guldur, and we who fought them called these creatures Wood-trolls. Once these were wandering, individual creatures, loathe to unite or even live near to their fellows. At Dol Guldur, however, something caused them to join together. A king was raised among them, and he unified the Wood-trolls into a terrible force. My father sent many warriors to defeat the Wood-trolls, and it was done.
'I believe something has once again united the Wood-trolls of the Trollshaws, ${PLAYER}. But this place is far from Mirkwood -- my father's warriors will not avail us.'
Chapter 7: The Aid of Mirkwood
Elladan is greatly concerned about the evil that seems to grow from deep within the Trollshaws and knows that you cannot face it alone.
'Speak with my father at Imladris, far to the east and above the Bruinen. He can arrange an audience with the Elves from Mirkwood.'
'I believe Legolas is often deep in thought at the Haven of Orladion, just outside my house. You may find him there and speak to him about the creature you encountered.'

Master Elrond is at Imladris, far east of Elladan's camp of Thorenhad and above the Bruinen.
Elladan has asked that you speak with his father about arranging an audience with the visiting Elves from Mirkwood, who might have some experience with creatures of the manner which you encountered.

Legolas is at the Haven of Orladion, just outside the House of Elrond.
Master Elrond has told you of an Elf-prince named Legolas, currently staying in Imladris for a time. He hails from Mirkwood and may have some knowledge of the creature you faced in the Trollshaws.

'I do not think this is the end of our search for the Nazgûl that escaped the waters of the Bruinen, ${PLAYER}. Indeed, we have only seen the beginning of the trouble he may cause.
'We must tell Master Elrond what has transpired. A task of great secrecy has been set before some of us at Imladris, and I fear we have been too long delayed already.
'Speak to Master Elrond inside the Last Homely House and tell him of our journey into the lair of Taushakh and what we beheld there. The time for delays is past.'

'I am glad to hear your news, ${PLAYER}. Do not grieve overmuch for the loss of the Nazgûl -- his fell designs with the Wood Trolls were ended by your brave actions and the skills of Legolas.
'Yes, your encounter with the Nazgûl has revealed to me what I must do. I will speak with Gandalf, for the errand of which you heard whispers has become all the more urgent because of the news you bring.
'For you though, I would ask that you keep your attention focused on the Nazgûl.'
Chapter 9: Hasten Their Departure
Legolas has been dismayed by the events in the lair of the Wood-trolls and thinks Elrond should be told of them at once.

'Master Elrond must be told of our adventure within the lair of Taushakh, king of the Wood-trolls. That Taushakh was bested is small consolation for losing the Nazgûl so quickly after revealing his location.'
'You have done well. The Nazgûl will be found once again.'
'An errand of secrecy has become more urgent because of the news you bring.'
'You are a good companion, ${PLAYER}. Within the Gladdalf you showed your courage.'
'The Wood-trolls are most dangerous when something unites them.'
'The Nazgûl has fled once again, but he will be found.'
'You have been of great service to us, ${PLAYER}.'
'The Trollshaws have been made safer by your aid, ${PLAYER}.'
'The Nazgûl cannot hide from us forever.'

Master Elrond is within the Last Homely House.
Legolas has asked you to go to Elrond at once and tell him what transpired in the lair of Taushakh, king of the Wood-trolls.

'Good, you've arrived hearty and hale. I hope the journey from the Northdowns was uneventful.
'Dark riders have come to the vale, servants of the Enemy. Glorfindel and I dispatched them but I fear they will return.
'Elrond is waiting for you in the library with the wizard. Go now and speak with him. He will have further news for you.'
The Elf lord smiles and nods in your direction as you approach. Gandalf the Grey does the same and you notice the twinkle in the old wizard's eye is gone, a grave expression on his bearded face.
Foreword: The Troubles of Rivendell
A council of Free Peoples was called and you were sent to speak with Aragorn in the Elf refuge of Rivendell.
'It would not be wise to keep Elrond waiting, ${PLAYER}.'

Elrond waits in the library of Rivendell.
Aragorn told you that Rivendell is under threat from the Enemy. Elrond wishes to speak with you about the nature of this threat.

'I fear that while the Nazgûl you drove off has fled the Trollshaws, he still schemes to assault Rivendell. To the north and east of Rivendell, there are goblins and worse that he might bend to his will and use against us.
'I would ask that you continue in your pursuit of the Nazgûl and travel into the Misty Mountains. There you may seek the aid of Glóin, who has established a camp at the end of the pass out of Rivendell that leads to the Misty Mountains.
'Go now, for not only the safety of Rivendell is at stake. All of Middle-earth depends on your actions.'

'A Nazgûl? One of the Nine Ringwraiths they spoke of at the Council of Elrond? I have not forgotten the honeyed words conveyed through one of those Riders to us back at the Lonely Mountain! Such poison! They wished us to betray old Bilbo Baggins to Mordor.
'I'll help you as best I can, although Dáin did task me with another matter. I can share some information though.'
Book V, Chapter 1: Into the Misty Mountains
Elrond feels that the Nazgûl you drove off from the Trollshaws has fled into the Misty Mountains. He has asked you to continue your pursuit of the Nazgûl with the aid of Glóin.
'The threat presented by the Nazgûl has not yet passed. Please continue your pursuit of the creature with the aid of Glóin at his camp atop the pass that leads to the Misty Mountains.'

Glóin can be found at this camp at the top of the pass that leads from Rivendell into the Misty Mountains.
Elrond suggested that you seek Glóin's aid in the hunt for the Nazgûl

'I am a master of earth, stone and axe, ${PLAYER}, not of these fell wights and evil artifacts. Go to Master Elrond in Rivendell and tell him all of what has transpired. He will be able to tell you what should be done next.'

'So you have returned and with evil tidings. This is the mark of a Gaunt-lord..perhaps you have seen one before? Sometimes Gaunt-lords use these sigils to summon the fell spirit that animates the wight.
'The sigil you have brought is a mark of Drugoth the Black, a powerful Gaunt-lord. As for what drew the Nazgûl and this Gaunt-lord to Helegrod, I fear I now know what they seek....'
'Yes? Is there some matter you wish to speak on?'
Bring the Sigil of Drugoth to Master Elrond
Chapter 7: Evil Tidings
Troubled by the wights you discovered at the entrance to Helegrod's treasury and the sigil you found on one of the wight's bodies, Glóin suggested it was time to speak with Master Elrond.
'Please, go to Master Elrond in Rivendell and speak with him of the things you have seen. The hour is late indeed if we are only now seeing the true threat that festers in the north.'

Elrond is in the library of Imladris.
Glóin has asked you to speak with Elrond about what you have discovered outside of Helegrod's treasury.

'What the Nazgûl seeks has become apparent to me, ${PLAYER}. Glóin told you of the fall of Helegrod, I expect: Durin, the fifth such dwarf to bear that name, slew the dragon Thorog but perished during the battle alongside most of his company? When it became clear that Helegrod was a place of evil and their attempts to restore it futile, the dwarves removed the riches from the treasury and left the dragon's body to moulder.
'However, I fear the cold and ice of Orod Lostol may have preserved the body of the dragon far longer than any would have thought. Even after death and the passage of so many years, the body of Thorog would possess much power. I fear that Drugoth the Gaunt-lord might use his arts to place some spirit within that corpse, raising the most terrible of wights to the service of Angmar.
'A dragon-wight within reach of Imladris is too grave a threat to be ignored. I must ask you to go into the treasury of Helegrod and put an end to the plans of Drugoth and the Nazgûl. It will be a difficult task, so gather a party of mighty warriors and go forth.'

'You have done a great thing today, ${PLAYER}! Few have faced the might of a Nazgûl and lived to tell the tale. Fortunately, the waters of the Bruinen and your pursuit of him weakened him to the extent that you could defeat him and send him back to Mordor.
'As for the matter of the dragon, it would appear that although the ritual was partially successful, the dragon-wight is not fully under the control of Drugoth. It still presents a threat to Rivendell, but not so great as would have been had the ritual been completed.
'For now, we can turn our attention to other matters, although someday you may wish to return to Helegrod and end this threat completely.'
Enter the Helegrod treasury and end the Nazgûl's schemes
Chapter 8: Fire and Ice

Elrond told you that after the dwarf-king Durin defeated Thorog the dragon, the body of the dragon was left to moulder in the empty treasury of Helegrod. He fears that the ice and cold of Orod Lostol will have preserved the body to such an extent that the arts of the Gaunt-lord, Drugoth, may be able to instill it with a fell spirit and raise it as a wight.
'Our time may be short. Please hurry and gather a party of warriors and enter the treasury of Helegrod. There the body of the dragon, slain by Durin so many years ago, was left to moulder.'
'I wonder what new evil is stirring in Angmar, and why it chooses now to come forth?'
'You have been a great help to us, ${PLAYER}.'

Helegrod is north of Rivendell and Glóin's camp.
Elrond has asked you to enter the treasury of Helegrod and put a stop to the Nazgûl's schemes. He warned you to gather allies.

Elrond can be found in the library of Imladris.
In the treasury, you encountered the Nazgûl and were able to defeat him. You also interrupted the ritual being performed by the Gaunt-lord to restore the dragon Thorog, although part of the process was completed, and the dragon flew off. Elrond should be made aware of what happened.
Invoked the name of Elbereth at the obelisks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

A plaque on the side of this obelisk is written in several tongues. It reads:
'I, Durin, lord of Khazad-dûm, have delved this vault with the aid of the Gwaith-i-Mírdain. To protect the great riches found here, there are obelisks crafted by the arts of Elves as a token of friendship.
'Only those who invoke the name of the Star-kindler may pass. Three times three are the obelisks, and three times must you speak.'
End the Nazgûl's plans
Examine the obelisk
Invoke the name of Elbereth at the obelisks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
End the Nazgûl's plans
Instance: Fire and Ice
At the behest of Master Elrond of Imladris, you have entered the abandoned treasury of Helegrod to end the Nazgûl's scheme to restore the dragon Thorog.
Seek out the Nazgûl and end his schemes.

Examine the obelisk.
You have encountered an obelisk that was glowing faintly.

Seek out the obelisks and open the way to the centre of the treasury.
Examination of the obelisk found at the entrance to the treasury revealed that the only way to enter the centre treasury is to invoke the name of Elbereth at obelisks found scattered through out the treasury.

Seek out the Nazgûl and end his schemes.
Now that you have invoked the name of the Elbereth at three of the obelisks in the treasury, the way to the centre of the treasury is open.

'I would wish you to remain here away from the troubles of the world. But alas, the Enemy does not rest and so neither can we.
'Angmar grows in power with each passing day and without a means to stem its evil, we have no hope of winning this war.
'Speak with Aragorn. He waits for you outside.'
'With matters in hand here, it is time to turn our attention to the north.'
Talk to Aragorn
Foreword: Turning to the North
The shadow of Angmar -- Sauron's hand in the North -- grows steadily, threatening the peace and security of Eriador.
'The time has come for you to leave this place of refuge. Go now, and speak to Aragorn.'

Aragorn waits outside the library at Rivendell.
Elrond warned you of a growing evil within Angmar and asked you to speak with Aragorn.

'I fear we may have been deceived, ${PLAYER}, for this scroll is written in Black Speech and may say nothing of value. I cannot say, for Black Speech is not a tongue with which I am familiar. Even so, I would know what this says.
'Perhaps the Elf Laerdan may have some proficiency in this writing. He is an old friend of my father's and is here in Gath Forthnír.
'Take the scroll to him and ask him his opinion. If it may help us free my father, then we must learn its secrets at once!'

'Alas, but I have never taken the time to learn the cruel mutterings of the Orcs. I have no desire to speak with them with other than my sword.
'If this scroll did indeed come from Carn Dûm, Elrond Halfelven may have an interest in it, and he assuredly knows the Black Speech. Go to Rivendell and seek out the Master of the Last Homely House, if you would know the answer to your riddle.'

'What is this? You were sent by the daughter of Golodir and by the Elf Laerdan? What a strange fate has brought you hither. The Shadow of Angmar has grown with the Shadow in the East.
'Give me the scroll...I will unravel this mystery for you.'
'What brings you to Rivendell, ${PLAYER}? What errand are you upon?'
Bring the scroll to Elrond Halfelven
Chapter 3: Opening the Way
You retrieved the scroll from Raghnall, but it was written in Black Speech, which Lorniel is unable to translate.
'I can be of no aid to you with this scroll, for the Black Speech is not my study. Take it to Elrond of Rivendell.'
'Take the scroll to Laerdan, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps he has some knowledge of the Black Speech.'
'Elrond Halfelven? Yes, I should have thought of that myself. It is a long journey, but one you must make!''

Laerdan is in Gath Forthnír.
Lorniel suggested you seek out an Elf named Laerdan in hopes of learning what Raghnall's scroll would reveal.

Elrond Halfelven is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws.
Laerdan, also unable to translate the scroll, sent you to Rivendell to speak with Elrond Halfelven.

'Here, take Golodir's gear, and travel to Rivendell and speak to Master Elrond. I doubt not that he will be able to assist you. His smiths are among the greatest of the Elf-smiths of this day.
'Do not tarry here. If this will help to renew Golodir's broken spirit, then you must make haste to Rivendell!'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, your tale saddens me, for I know Golodir, and he was a good man. It pleases me to know that he lives, but it grieves me that this False King was able to break him so.
'That a wraith has returned to power in Angmar troubles me even more. I have never heard of Mordirith...that is a mystery upon which I must dwell.
'Now go to Hemeldir, my chief smith, and instruct him to reforge Golodir's sword. You will find him near Imladris' forges.'

'The work is done, ${PLAYER}. It little resembles the weapon from which it was birthed, but I believe it will better serve its master.
'Take it now to Master Elrond for his approval.'

'Master Elrond requires this sword to be reforged? Very well. It is a minor essay in Elf-craft...it will not take long.
'But what is this? I daresay this shield did not belong to your friend Golodir. This shield is far older, from near the fall of the North Kingdom. It is also from Gondor, not the North. Indeed, it looks familiar...I seem to recall its like among the royal line of Gondor.
'I will speak to Master Elrond about this later. For now, I will turn my hand to the task required of me.'
'What do you require of me, ${RACE}?'

'As always, Hemeldir's mastery shows forth in the work of his hand. This sword shall henceforth be known as \qDúnachar,\q Avenger of the West, for it shall avenge the death of Lorniel, daughter of Golodir.'
'Have you returned with the sword?'
Bring Golodir's gear to Elrond
Bring Golodir's gear to Hemeldir
Collect Golodir's sword from Hemeldir
Bring Golodir's sword to Elrond
Chapter 3: Forging the Sword
The Rangers of Esteldín were able to repair Golodir's shield and mail shirt, but the sword was of Elf-craft beyond their skill.
'We haven't the ability to reforge this sword. You should take it to Elrond in Rivendell.'
'We haven't the ability to reforge this sword. You should take it to Elrond in Rivendell.'
'You left Golodir's sword in Rivendell? You go there at once and retrieve it!'
'You left Golodir's sword in Rivendell? You go there at once and retrieve it!'
'Hemeldir, my chief smith, will reforge Golodir's sword.'
'I am certain Hemeldir has finished reforging Golodir's sword. You should retrieve it from him and return to me.'
'Maste Elrond will want to inspect that sword before you return it to Golodir.'

Elrond is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws.
Daervunn suggested you take Golodir's sword to Elrond of Rivendell to be reforged.

Hemeldir can be found near Rivendell's forges.
Elrond instructed you to take Golodir's sword to his chief smith, Hemeldir, to be reforged.

Hemeldir can be found near Rivendell's forges.
You should check with Hemeldir to learn if he has finished reforging Golodir's sword.

Elrond is in Rivendell.
Hemeldir returned Golodir's reforged sword to you and told you to bring it to Elrond for approval.

'Dúnachar is a fine sword, and I foresee that one day the Steward of Angmar will rue its reforging.
'Go now. Return to Laerdan and bring him Golodir's gear. I hope that Golodir will see his despair for what it is -- the machinations of the Enemy.
'Laerdan awaits you at Gath Forthnír in Angmar.'

'You have returned, ${PLAYER}! What news? The sword has been reforged? Dúnachar it is named...yes, I can feel the virtue within it.
'And what did you say about the shield? It is not Golodir's? It shall have to make do.
'Take the gear to Golodir in his quarters.'
'Were the Rangers able to salvage Golodir's gear?'

'What is this? My mail shirt? I thought it lost forever! And this shield, it is not mine, but it is a thing of wondrous beauty!
'But this sword...is this my sword? It was forged long ago by the Elves of Rivendell, an heirloom of my family. I thought it lost forever, but now it is returned as Dúnachar!
'It is well-named Avenger of the West. Indeed, it will avenge my daughter....'
'Leave me be!'
Bring Golodir's gear to Laerdan
Bring Golodir his equipment
Chapter 4: A Beacon of Hope
Elrond renamed Golodir's sword Dúnachar, Avenger of the West, and prophesied that it would one day avenge the death of Lorniel, Golodir's daughter.
'Bring Golodir his gear...I hope that it will spark at least a small flicker of the bright flame he once was.'
'Make haste, ${PLAYER}. Laerdan awaits your return.'
'You should return at once to Laerdan and take him Golodir's gear.'

Laerdan is at Gath Forthnír in the eastern reaches of Himbar.
Elrond gave you the sword Dúnachar and told you to take it and the rest of Golodir's gear to Laerdan.

Golodir is at Gath Forthnír in the eastern reaches of Himbar.
Laerdan instructed you to return Golodir's gear to him.

'I think the time has come -- indeed it is long past time -- that the Elves and dwarves confront the enemy in Angmar together. In our past council, we discussed...other matters...and Angmar was not our main concern.
'Until now, we Elves have not paid too much heed to the Dourhands, deeming them a problem for dwarves to deal with. But now we see that Skorgrím is a servant of Angmar, and that he has roused the giants of the Misty Mountains against us. It is time for us to think again.
'Please go to Glóin and speak to him in my name, asking him to join again in council against our foes.'

'Ho! So at last the Elves deign to notice our concerns, now that we have almost paid the Dourhands ourselves!
'Still, I should not be so hasty. It is true that there has not been true amity between our peoples of late, but if we do not cleave together against the real Enemy, we shall most certainly be cloven by their black blades.
'Well, I thank you and Master Elrond for his words, and I will certainly meet with him to discuss our plans to deal with these Angmarim who have been causing both our houses so much trouble.'
An Alliance with the Dwarves

Troubled by the Thunder-lord's mention of Skorgrím and by reports of hostile dwarves occupying a fortress in the Misty Mountains, Elrond bids you speak to Glóin to request that the dwarves and Elves work together against the forces of Angmar.
'Please go to Glóin and speak with him in my name.'

Glóin is at the dwarves' mountain camp north of Rivendell.
Elrond has asked you to speak to Glóin of a new council against Angmar.
Found Arwen's legacy

'I said that I do not know where lies the vault containing Arwen's legacy, but it may be that I can help you to gain entrance when it is found.
'The riddle itself may be the key to the vault. If in your travels near Imladris you find a sealed vault, those words may offer you passage within. There should be a rock in front of the entrance. Place your hand on the rock and recite the verse.
'I would be surprised if the jewel is in the vale of Imladris itself as these carefully tended gardens and groves are too often frequented by the Elves for a vault to be easily hidden. I have no doubt it is close by, somewhere in the Trollshaws not far from Imladris.'
'Yes, indeed, this is the jewel itself...Arwen's legacy. Please bring it to Elrond, as it is his duty to give it to his daughter.'
'You have found the vault, have you not? The jewel should be within.'

'To think that the vault has remained sealed for so long past its time! Even those counted among the Wise can be foolhardy, it seems!
'But I must thank you for your perseverance, Master of Riddles. You seek the truth in all things, even though it brings you into darkness -- your skill and cunning bring you back out into the light again.'
'What tidings do you bring of your quest?'
Bring Arwen's legacy to Glorfindel
Collect Arwen's legacy
Deliver Arwen's legacy to Elrond
The Riddle-master
Glorfindel does not know where Arwen's legacy is, but he has given you some advice which may help you to find it.
'On Arwen's behalf, and on my own, I thank you for your service.'
'You are truly a Master of Riddles, ${PLAYER}.'
'To think you solved that old riddle! Well done, well done!'
'You have done very well to unravel the mystery. Master Elrond must be well pleased.'
'I thank you for finding my mother's gift to me. Alas for my father and mother, I will not be bearing it into the west, but perhaps I will some day find another who will bear it for me.'

The lost Elf-vault is somewhere in the Trollshaws in the vicinity of Rivendell. Once the legacy is found, return to Glorfindel outside the house of Elrond, by the waterfall.
Glorfindel advised you to place a hand on a rock by the entrance of the Elf-vault and to recite the verses of the riddle. Arwen's legacy, a white jewel, should be somewhere in the vault. If you find the jewel, return to Glorfindel with your prize.

Elrond is in the library of Rivendell.
Glorfindel asked you to bring Arwen's legacy to Elrond.

'The giants have always been fiercely independent, following a lord or chief only rarely. This Thunder-lord may have been elevated by Angmar or by Mordor, maintaining his position through strength of will and force of arms. If he commands the giants against us, we may not long survive their assault.
'We must defeat the Thunder-lord before he can extend his influence to any other giants in the mountains. It may be, too, that if the Thunder-lord can be defeated now, the giants who follow him will turn away from the path of war.
'The Thunder-lord must rule from the furthest reaches of Iorbar, south and east of the Giants' Table. Beware, for he must be a deadly opponent, and only a determined group of warriors could hope to defeat him. Once you have put an end to the Thunder-lord, deliver the news to Master Elrond in the library of Imladris at once.'

'You have defeated a mighty foe, ${PLAYER}, and have proven yourself worthy beyond any need, but I remain troubled. The words of the Thunder-lord have planted an unease in my heart.
'Dark days are ahead, for all of Middle-earth. Remain wary, ${PLAYER}! I fear a terrible shadow has been cast upon the land from afar.'
Thunder in the Mountains
The Thunder-lord, leader of the giants, has ordered them to battle. If he can be defeated, this threat might fall with him.
'Seek out the Thunder-lord in Iorbar, south and east of the Giants' Table, and defeat him. We must put an end to him before he commands all the giants of the mountains to descend upon us!'

'You have bested the Thunder-lord, ${PLAYER}, and all of Imladris will rejoice! Bring this news at once to Master Elrond himself, in the library of Imladris. He will be as pleased as I am to hear it!'
'Your defeat of the Thunder-lord was a mighty deed.'

The Thunder-lord rules the giants from Iorbar, south and east of the Giants' Table in the Misty Mountains.
The Thunder-lord is the source of the giants' recent hostility, and he must be defeated before all the giants in the region heed his commands. You will need the aid of brave allies if you hope to defeat him.

Elrond is in the library at Imladris.
You must tell Elrond that the Thunder-lord is now defeated and the threat of the giants has been lessened.

'I can fashion you a piece of equipment that will reflect the depth of your knowledge, ${PLAYER}, and aid you in your further pursuit of wisdom.
'Take these, my notes. Within, you will find a list of components I will need if I am to make this equipment for you.
'Do not quail from the danger, for you are a learned lore-master and have come through all hazards to reach this point. You are wise enough to survive your coming trials.'

'I am glad to see you return, ${PLAYER}, and with the components I sought. These will be of much use to me as I fashion your equipment.
'Now consult the notes I gave you, for there is more I require of you.'
'You do not have the components for which I have asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'I thank you for these items, ${PLAYER}. Are you ready to collect the last set of things I will need?
'I hope that you are, for these will be most difficult to acquire. I believe you to be up to the challenge, but know that it will take you into the very heart of the land of Angmar.
'You are wise, ${PLAYER}. Now you must be strong as well.'
'You do not have the components for which I am waiting.'

'I marvel at your success, ${PLAYER}, though I should not do so -- I have seen your great deeds and heard of your wisdom, but still I doubted. I am not as wise as I supposed.
'Allow me now to present you with this equipment I have fashioned. May it serve you long and well!'
'You do not have the components for which I asked. Why is this, ${PLAYER}?'

'I am pleased to meet you at last, ${PLAYER}. The years may be long, but they are full of joy for those who seek learning. The passing of the seasons cannot blunt the sharp mind eager for wisdom.
'I wonder at your garb, ${PLAYER}. Why have you not sought to fashion articles appropriate to our calling that reflect your desire for study? Gladly will I help you with this, if you wish it!
'But I give to you words of caution, for such articles will not come easily. Their tale will be one of hardship and sorrow, but its end will be full of triumph and victory. Do not despair, for though the road be hard, a lore-master knows its end is sweet. Speak to me if you are ready, and I will tell you what awaits beyond dark corners, down your road.'

'This riddle has me puzzled. Why would anyone seek to remember goblins? And what's this about \qa mighty swing?\q Did someone kill a goblin? Now, that's something of which I can approve!'

'I don't know what the rest of the riddle means.'

'I don't know the riddle, but if you walk \qhalf a day towards the sun and half a day away from the sun,\q you have gone one day's journey, for if you start in the morning, half of the day has you approaching the sun and for the other half it sinks behind you!'

A Lore-master's Will
A Lore-master seeks to dissolve all the mysteries of the world, but whether he chooses to share them with others is often a defining characteristic.
'I gave you the riddle, ${PLAYER}. Solve it, and you will know the location of one of the keys to the legacy Berenin left me, I am certain!'
'I gave you the second of Berenin's riddles, ${PLAYER}. Solve it, and you will know the location of another one of the keys to the legacy Berenin left me.'
'I gave you the third of Berenin's riddles, ${PLAYER}. Solve it, and you will know the location of the last of the keys to the legacy Berenin left me.'

'Are you ready to go? The cave is not far from here, and then we will learn what secrets Berenin left in my care.'

'I know the answer to this riddle, ${PLAYER}! You're looking for the statue of Bullroarer, who knocked off the head of the evil Golfimbul a long time ago and invented the game of Golf while he was at it!
'The statue of Bullroarer is in Brockenborings on Greenfields, in the Shire.'

'I think I know the solution! It sounds like the traveller started at the Prancing Pony and then walked one full day eastward. What is one day's journey east of Bree? The Forsaken Inn.
'And furthermore, the Inn has a large hole in the roof! From one point of view, that does sound like a window that couldn't be closed!'

'This riddle seems very easy to me, ${PLAYER}! Think about it! \qShe runs through the blue\q almost certainly refers to the Blue Mountains, known among the Elves as Ered Luin. \qThe shadow of passage\q just has to be a bridge, and in riddles \qa silent guardian\q is almost always a statue!
'You just need to look near a statue beneath a long bridge in Ered Luin for the solution to this riddle, I warrant!'
'This riddle has stumped me. I am sorry!'
'I do not know the answer to the riddle, but Bilbo might know better than I.'

'This is the last key, ${PLAYER}, and now we can open the three boxes that Berenin left for me! I have stored them in a nearby cave for safe-keeping, a cave I once explored with Berenin, long ago. The water on the walls made a sort of music, I remember, as it fell into pools on the floor -- though the cave has been bare and dry now for many years.
'You are a part of this now too, ${PLAYER}. Let me know if you are ready to go, and we can travel to the cave together, and together learn what secrets Berenin has left behind.'
'You have not misplaced the key, have you?'

'Isferon himself is a most learned lore-master -- I wonder what puzzle could evade his understanding?'

'You have heard of my puzzle, ${PLAYER}? I do not know why I cannot discover the solution -- I, who have studied the arts of flame and ash, and the mysteries of cinders and coal!
'My friend Berenin despaired of Middle-earth and sailed West some time ago. He left me three small boxes, and said that when I was able to solve the riddles he left in my possession, I would be able to open them. I grieve that Berenin has gone and would learn what secrets he has left to me, but I am unable to determine the solution to the riddles! Poultices and mixes are my prime interests, not word games and trifles.
'I am sure that Berenin left the keys to each box at the locations that solve each riddle, but where these may be, I do not know. I will give you the first riddle, and if you can bring me the key, then I will give you the second riddle, and we will continue in this fashion until we have learned what secrets Berenin left for me when he sailed West. I give you the first riddle and wish you good fortune in deciphering it!'

'I cannot thank you enough, ${PLAYER}. Hearing Berenin's words brought a joy to my heart that it has not felt in too many years, and to better know his thoughts is the greatest secret your aid could have brought me.
'I am not as clever with words as you are, or as Berenin was, but with the dancing flames I am unmatched. Perhaps I can teach you some measure of knowledge in return for the joy you have brought to me, ${PLAYER}. It is not much, but I hope it will help you in your journeys.'

'You found the first key, ${PLAYER}! I am impressed, for I was certainly thinking about it the wrong way. \q She runs through the blue\q seemed to me to indicate a cloud in the sky, and from there I was already on the wrong path.
'But these are the Blue Mountains, if you remember one of their names, and from there it is not as difficult. Berenin always saw things more simply than I did. I remember he would often chide me for overcomplicating things -- this riddle of his seems a lesson, now that I think on it!
'I wonder what is inside the boxes he left in my care when he sailed West? Two riddles remain, ${PLAYER}! Solve this one, and we will be closer to discovering Berenin's legacy to me!'
'You haven't misplaced the key, have you?'

'You continue to amaze me, ${PLAYER} -- you are a more learned lore-master than I, that much is clear! On the movements of fire, perhaps, I could teach you something, but for the dissolving of riddles you are far better than I!
'Berenin was the same -- he would often pose confusing entertainments for me to try and decipher, and I only managed to reveal the solutions on rare occasions. He was always on hand to provide hints when I strayed too far from the heart of the matter, and his laughter at my confusion was always warm -- there was no mockery in it. I had forgotten the sound of his laughter until now.
'One riddle remains, ${PLAYER}. Berenin would be impressed with your untangling of the first two, I am sure of it!'
'You haven't misplaced the key, have you?'

'I thank you again, ${PLAYER}! My father's library is a confusing place.'
'My father's organizational skills might have needed some work, to tell it honestly.'

'Your studies continue apace, ${PLAYER}. Creatures of nature see in you a friend and ally, and the mysteries of the past lie untapped before you. There is always more to learn, but you have an understanding of this Middle-earth that few others can reach.
'One of the greatest lore-masters of our day was a man by the name of Benton Oakes. He maintained a vast store of knowledge -- old tomes and scrolls, small trinkets of unusual heritage. It is said that Benton came to an unhappy end, but he is survived by his son Dorset. Dorset, too, is a lore-master and undoubtedly learned much from his father before Benton met his fate.
'A great tree grows south-east of the village of Staddle, known for the golden leaves it bears all year-round, and Dorset Oakes often tarries there in contemplation. Seek him out, and perhaps he will divulge some of his father's mysteries to you.'

A Well-Ordered Mind
There are many secrets to be found in the histories of the Free Peoples, waiting only for the careful study of a lore-master of skill and patience.

'Are you ready to travel with me to the cave that contains my father's library? I ask only that you keep its location a secret.
'I hope you do not think I am being too forward, but...have you located any pages of my father's catalogue yet? We can search unaided, but perhaps you will be able to learn on which shelf \qOn the Hardiness of Animals in the Wilderness\q resides from them where I failed. No doubt some goblin, brigand, or treasure-seeker of Bree-land has found the pages and carried them off by now.
'If you feel confident that you know on which shelf the book resides, I am ready to travel as well!'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. Rumour of my father's wisdom has oft brought lore-masters such as yourself to hear my words, and I fear sometimes that they leave me in disappointment. I do not have the knowledge my father had; indeed, his way of thinking was so very different from my own that I cannot comprehend even what he considered most simple!
'Consider the organization of his library. He found a suitable cave in the rocky hills of Bree-land and took it for his private library, filling it with books and scrolls collected over the course of his long life. But whenever I seek to find one of the books of which he spoke to me, I am completely at a loss. He entrusted me with a catalogue detailing which books could be found on which shelves, but the system simply made no sense to me, and I was careless with the pages. Now I have only the last one! Brigands and goblins have no doubt found the others by now. Without the full catalogue, how am I to find \qOn the Hardiness of Animals in the Wilderness\q? My father assured me before his death that it was on a shelf in his library.
'I will share with you the wisdom contained between its covers if you help me find this book, ${PLAYER}. The library is large, and we can search it unaided if you like, but it would certainly be easier with every page of the catalogue. I do not know where they may be, but searching for them will make the book easier to locate. We will need haste, for the goblins have been digging dangerously near to it and are certain to break into the library soon. Speak with me when you are ready to go -- here is the only page of the catalogue I still possess.'

'You have my thanks, Lore-master ${PLAYER}, and more besides, for I will share with you the teachings that lie between the covers of the book we retrieved.
'Such is the path of wisdom, my friend. It is best shared!'
'Well, where is the book? You haven't lost it, have you?'

You have been told to speak with Dorset Oakes in the hope that the lore-master may be able to instruct you.

Dorset is waiting to speak with you after your successful retrieval of the book he sought.
You found the book sought by Dorset Oakes!
