'You found it, ${PLAYER}! I can hardly believe it! Quickly, now -- are you ready to leave?'
'Let's get out of here before the goblins make things even more difficult!'
Find the bookshelf containing the book Dorset Oakes is seeking before the Goblin-champions arrive
Private Instance: A Well-Ordered Mind
Dorset Oakes has shown you into the cave that once served as his father's library.
'Somewhere within that library is the book I'm seeking, ${PLAYER}. I hope you know which bookshelf it can be found on, for the goblins are sure to come poking around before too long!'

This cave was once the library of the great Benton Oakes, and its main room is full of bookshelves.
Dorset Oakes is waiting for you to find the bookshelf that contains \qOn the Hardiness of Animals in the Wilderness\q.

Dorset Oakes is at the entrance of the cave.
Dorset is waiting for you to return with the book he asked for.

'Many who have travelled with us are reflecting on the events of so many years ago. You would benefit from spending time with them and doing the same.
'Hopefully you will not interrupt their contemplation for long, but such reflection may help in the days to come. Return to me when you are done. The insight you gain may be of aid in the days ahead.'

'Did you learn much from the talk with your fellow ${CLASS}? Good.
'What is this? You wonder why I have given you food? It will do you no good to drive yourself to the task at hand without sustenance. You must have food to keep your strength. If you find yourself in need of more, you should speak with Gailthin, here at our camp.
'Now to the task at hand!'

'It angers me to see what has become of Edhelion since we left. The Dourhands did much to dishonour us. Together we can reflect on the path of the Champion. Then we shall be ready to bring justice to these dwarves.
'The Champion does not stand at the back of the ranks. We stand on the front lines, shoulder-to-shoulder with our brethren. \qA! Elbereth Gilthoniel tol-ammen!\q we cry, vowing to lay down our lives so that our fellows may survive.
'Reflect on these words, and together we can bring justice to this Middle-earth.'

'Ah, if only I were here in the dark days when Edhelion fell. Perhaps things would have been different? Alas, such thoughts do us no good. We are here to protect the future, not dream about the past...for both you and I chose the path of the Guardian.
'There is no glory in battle if it comes to naught. Guardians challenge and taunt our enemies, keeping our allies from harm and shielding them with our own steel and our own sinews. You will learn that even the fiercest enemy has a weakness. It is our calling to strike out against that weakness and save the day.
'May you never forget those that depend upon you, Guardian.'

'I never knew the fire of wrath until I set my eyes upon the ruins of Edhelion. Mourn for the past, but do not let anger cloud your mind and lead you from the path you follow.
'The Hunter must keep himself under control, lest his arrows fly wild. We are a special breed of warrior. While others dwell on strength of arms and furious emotions, we act with sure, swift strokes and keen-eyed precision. And should the enemy close in, we must strike fast and true.
'Keep your eyes sharp and your mind clear. I have faith in you.'

'Greetings. You are a fellow sage, yes? I am glad to see another walking the path of wisdom. Preserving the knowledge of the past is our sacred duty.
'I sense greatness in you, ${PLAYER}. There are dark clouds on the horizon, and the shadow of doom. Some may call upon you to face this threat, one greater than any faced in your many years. But you are not alone. The birds and beasts of the land will aid you, as will the very land itself. Your knowledge of forgotten lore and remedies will be of great use to both you and your companions.
'A bright future awaits you. For now, I will share what knowledge I can to start you on your path.'

'With Edhelion a shadow of its former glory, I fear that even the sweetest song will never again raise my spirits. Yet the soothing comfort of a silver voice and a gentle melody is exactly what is needed at this moment in time.
'The power to stir the spirit and raise hope...that is the greatest power of the Minstrel. Even when all seems lost, our voices strengthen the resolve of those around us. Hope in the face of despair, light in the face of darkness.
'We must use our gifts well, for only then can we hope to chase the shadow from Middle-earth.'
Speak to the ${CLASS} trainer
Intro: Meditating on the Past
The eldest and wisest of the Elves spend their time contemplating the past in an effort to glean wisdom from it.
'You should go speak to the ${CLASS}, ${PLAYER}.'
'Are you ready to go? Good. I have more to teach but you are not quite ready to learn. Go talk to Dorongúr and practice what I taught you.'
'You have done well, Guardian. Now you must return to Dorongúr.'
'Now you must leave me, for Dorongúr has a task for you. Fare well, ${PLAYER}.'
'You learn quickly. Now return to Dorongúr and use what I have taught you.'
'You are quite a capable student, and I wish you good fortune in the years to come. Now we must part ways, for Dorongúr wishes to speak with you.'

The Elf-${CLASS} is in the ruins near Dorongúr Whitethorn.
Dorongúr suggested you speak to one of the Elves reflecting on the events that happened in Edhelion so long ago. You must learn all you can from those who contemplate the past. Listen to their words and learn from their wisdom.

Dorongúr can be found in the Elf-ruins.
You sought counsel with the other Elves and learned from their wisdom. Now you should return to Dorongúr.

'Now that you are prepared for whatever lies ahead, I have another task for you. One of Elrond's sons, Elladan, went down to the Silver Deep, as the Dwarves call it, to see if the halls of Edhelion remain undisturbed. Go now and speak with him.
'The entrance to the Silver Deep can be found by following this mountain path to the west. Once the path branches, take the northern path.'

'Goblins! Goblins here in the the halls of Edhelion! I slew a goodly number and drove the rest off. I must keep watch that the goblins do not return, yet I must know what they sought within Edhelion's ruined halls. Will you help me learn this?'
Intro: Scouting the Ruins
One of the sons of Elrond, Elladan, scouted ahead to see if anyone entered the ruined halls of Edhelion.

'Elladan can be found near the entrance to the dwarf-mine named the \qSilver Deep.\q Go there and learn what he found.
'The entrance to the Silver Deep lies along this mountain path to the west. Once the path branches, take the northern branch to the Silver Deep.'
'Goblins? This is ill news indeed.'

Elladan can be found near the entrance to the Silver Deep, west of the ruins of Edhelion. It is reached by travelling down the mountain path, then north to the mine's entrance.
Elladan is investigating the Silver Deep mines for signs of danger.

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. I know it has been many, many years since you last laid eyes on Edhelion. I know the pain you feel on seeing it as it is, for I too was here when Edhelion fell. It is hard to bear seeing what has become of it, and harder to hold back the anger such a sight stirs in my breast...
'There are matters though that we must attend to. Dorongúr Whitethorn is here and wishes to speak with you. He waits beyond the western gate. Follow the path and you will find him.'

'Ah, it is good to see you once more, ${PLAYER}. Lord Elrond was concerned that some great evil was about to be committed here, though he could not see clearly what it is. I would like your help in discovering the nature of the evil.
'Before we delve into this mystery, it is wise to reflect on the events of the past. Perhaps they can guide us in the present...and the future. You should seek the counsel of another.'
Intro: Elrond's Premonition
After being away for centuries, you return to the refuge of Edhelion, along with Elrond's sons and Dorongúr Whitethorn.
'Dorongúr waits for you. Follow the road west out of the ruins.'
'Even after all these years, the pain of what happened here is still fresh in my mind...'

Find Dorongúr Whitethorn on the road west out of the ruins of Edhelion, beyond the western gate.
Dorongúr wishes to speak to you about a matter of great importance.
Defeated invaders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So the relics of Edhelion were hidden inside the halls? I am glad to hear that, as that means Talagan's sacrifice was not in vain. The death of Skorgrím and the ruin caused by Talagan should be enough to keep the relics safe. If for at least a little while...
'I fear though that Edhelion will no longer offer respite for our kind. We were too few in number to keep Edhelion safe. Rebuilding here would be folly.
'No, Edhelion will fade... yet I feel that you shall return here again someday.'

'You have hidden the relics? Good! Fortunately, we have been able to push the Dourhand dwarves and their goblin allies back. However, the battle is not yet won.
'I have received news from a lookout in our eastern pass. He has caught sight of Skorgrím, the Dourhands' lord, and another war party coming towards the refuge. What is worse is that he has a snow troll in his company. I did not think Skorgrím would sink so low! His greed for Edhelion's relics knows no bounds.
'Skorgrím will be on us any moment. We must brace ourselves for the attack. What I would ask of you is to help defend the courtyard. However, to do this, you must have a better weapon. Sadly, Haerandir has succumbed to his wounds, but I know he would wish for you to take up his weapons.'

'Elrond has answered my summons from those long months ago! I had sent him word of our troubles with Skorgrím and his dwarves, and it seems he has come to help us. We may yet win this day!
'Quick, now that you are armed, go to the courtyard of Edhelion. Edhelben below will direct you there. Dorongúr Whitehorn and other survivors of the attack are entrenched there, holding out against attack. Make your way to the courtyard and help them defend it. We need hold on only for a little while longer, then Elrond and his Elves shall be here!
'Be careful though, there may be a few invaders still lurking behind Edhelion's walls. You may need to fight your way to the courtyard.'
'On hearing the horn-call of Elrond, I thought the battle was over, yet you have brought dire news, that the worst may be yet to come! Let us just hope Elrond comes in time.'
After arming yourself, speak to Talagan Silvertongue
Follow Edhelben
Defeat invaders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Follow Dorongúr Whitethorn
Speak with Dorongúr
Follow Elrond and Dorongúr Whitethorn
Instance: The Refuge of Edhelion

While visiting the refuge of Edhelion on a sojourn from your woodland home, the refuge was attacked by a clan of dwarves called the Dourhands. These dwarves are led by Skorgrím, a vicious dwarf intent on taking the treasures of Edhelion for himself.
In the initial attack, the dwarves broke through the refuge's defences, but the elves rallied and pushed the dwarves back.

'Ah, you have survived. Good! Those Dourhands and their goblin minions were everywhere! I honestly didn't think we would survive, but Dorongúr had the sense to bar the doors to the courtyard. With the courtyard as our final redoubt, we were able to push the dwarves back. Although there are probably a few stragglers still about.
'I know though that if the courtyard falls, all of Edhelion may go with it. You must help in the defence of the courtyard until Elrond arrives. Go up the stairs to the west and travel along until you come to the back gate. Once there, Dorongúr should let you in.
'Be careful, a few of the invaders may still be about.'

'Good ${PLAYER}, you are hale. Do not worry about me, I will be fine. It is but a minor wound. Once I bind it, I will make my way into the courtyard to help as I may. But do not wait on me, go to the courtyard now and help in its defence until Elrond arrives.
'This gate is barred, for fear the other gates will not hold, but the back entrance may be open. Go up the stairs to the west and travel along until you come to the back gate. Once there, Dorongúr will let you in.
'Be careful though, there may still be a few stragglers left behind.'

'Those in the courtyard will need your help until Elrond arrives. The main gates are barred, so you should travel to the west and go up the stairs. From there travel along to the back entrance. Hopefully someone will let you in there!
'Be careful though, there may still be a few stragglers left behind that you may have to deal with.'

Collected dwarf-pickaxes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'In my battle against the goblins, I managed to kill many before the rest retreated into the mines. The beasts I slew lay about the Silver Deep. While I keep watch for the beasts to return, I would ask that you search the remains for clues as to the reason why they are here.
'The door into the mines is found at the north-eastern end of this path. Be quick now, we must learn what those beasts were up to!'

'All of the goblins were carrying dwarf-pickaxes? Most curious...
'I would understand one or two -- the spoils of some battle with the dwarves, perhaps. But all of them? No, it cannot be but a coincidence. You must bring this information to Durin's Folk.'
'Did you find anything on those bodies? We must discover the reason why the goblins were in the Silver Deep!'
Search dead goblins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the dwarf-pickaxes to Elladan
Intro: The Halls of Edhelion
Elladan entered the Silver Deep and found it rife with goblins. He slew many of the foul creatures and drove the others away.
'Enter the Silver Deep through the entrance north-east of here and search the dead goblins for information. We must learn why they were here.'

The entrance to the Silver Deep lies to the north-east of Elladan.
Elladan killed several goblins and wants you to search the dead for clues while he guards the entrance.

Elladan is outside the Silver Deep.
Your search revealed that many of the goblins carried dwarf-made pick-axes. Elladan will be most interested in your find.

'There is a party of Longbeard dwarves that has recently come from Erebor. Their leader, Dwalin, was a member of Thorin's Company, which journeyed forth long ago on the Quest of Erebor, and he is a friend of my father's.
'You will find Dwalin standing at Frerin's Court west of here. Bring him the picks and tell him of the goblins. They will wish to know this disturbing news.'

'Greetings, good Elf! What's this? Pick-axes from the Deep? I must say you are not the only one who has brought me such news. I think that the Dourhands are falling back to their old ways, but I cannot yet prove it.
'You may have heard tales of Skorgrím, the leader of the Dourhands, and the fall of the Elf-refuge? You were there? Then you know more than I. Still, you may learn something yet.'
Bring the pick-axes to Dwalin
Intro: The Longbeards

Goblins were discovered in the Silver Deep mines and Elladan fought many of them. He is troubled by what you discovered when you searched the bodies: Dwarf-made pick-axes carried by each of the slain goblins.
'Go speak to Dwalin. He will be found in Frerin's Court.'

Dwalin can be found in Frerin's Court, west of the Silver Deep.
Elladan has instructed you to take the dwarf-made picks to Dwalin and tell him of the goblins in the Silver Deep.
Collected dwarf sword

'The Elves told me about goblins digging in the Silver Deep, and what with the mine guards and the red-robed man...well it's got me thinking. Are the Dourhands involved? The twitch in my whiskers says yes, but I need solid evidence before I start hurling accusations.
'The first thing to do is learn if the Dourhands are using goblins cohorts. Kill one of the goblins prowling about west of here and search its body for proof of the Dourhands' involvement.
'The goblin prowlers are found hunting the aurochs, west of Frerin's Court. Some have been seen up on the Axehead Path to the north-west, as well.'

'I knew it! Goblins with dwarf-craft weapons? This has the stink of Dourhand devilry. They've gone back to the old ways, have they? Well we'll give them something to think about!
'It's time to get to the bottom of this, once and for all....'
'Have you found anything suspicious on those goblin-prowlers yet? They should hunting the Aurochs west of here.'
Bring the dwarf-made sword to Dwalin
Search a goblin prowler
Intro: Goblin Prowlers
Long ago, Skorgrím, lord of the Dourhands, allied himself with goblins and trolls. Dwalin believes the Dourhands are returning to their old ways.

Goblin-prowlers are found to the west of Frerin's Court, hunting the aurochs. Some have also been seen on the Axehead Path, north-west of Frerin's Court. Dwalin is at Frerin's Court.
Dwalin has asked you to slay a goblin and search it. If you find anything interesting, return it to Dwalin at once.

'Gormr Doursmith, the Dourhand steward, is responsible for the guards' deaths, and nearly mine as well! He's been seen having dealings with a strange red-robed man and...and...goblins!
'Dwalin must know about this. Find him at Frerin's Court in the centre of town.'
'Fool Dourhands! But we'll need further evidence if we are going to prove they are going back to their old ways.'
Intro: Gormr's Deeds
Olin felt much better after taking a remedy made with Elven mushrooms. Free of pain, Olin told you of Gormr Doursmith, the dwarf who leads the Dourhands.
'Dwalin must be told of Gormr's treachery. Find him at the centre of Frerin's Court.'
'If you hadn't brought those mushrooms when you did, ${PLAYER}, well...I shudder to think what would have happened!'

Dwalin can be found in Frerin's Court, the central square of Thorin's Gate.
Olin revealed that Gormr Dourhand is in league with goblins and may have contributed to his poisoning.
Collect nestedelais in the Rockbelly Pit (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I'll not last long if...if help cannot be found for me. Fortunately, I know of something which may be of aid. There are mushrooms which grow in some caves, which the Elves call nestedelais.
'Venture along the rise to the east that leads to the Winterheight. There's a cave there called the Rockbelly Pit where you'll find the mushrooms. They are said to have healing properties. Gather some and bring them to me. They may well be my only chance.
'Now don't get lost! The entrance to the Rockbelly Pit can be found in the Winterheight east of Frerin's Court.'
'Good, good. Just the smell of these mushrooms is helping to ease the pain. Now I will tell you what I know!'
'Do you have the nestedelais yet? They are found in Rockbelly Pit. The cave's entrance can be found in the Winterheight, a rise that lies east of Frerin's Court.'
Bring the nestedelais to Olin
Collect nestedelais in the Rockbelly Pit (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Intro: Dark Places
A type of mushroom called nestadalas grows in a nearby cave. Olin can use the mushrooms to purge himself of the poison the Dourhands gave him.

The Rockbelly Pit, where the nestedelais may be found, is in the Winterheight, a rise found due east of Frerin's Court. Follow the road east from Frerin's Court until it branches, then take the south-east branch up the mountain and to the Winterheight.
Once you have gathered all the mushrooms, return to Olin.

'Before we left for the Lonely Mountain, Thorin asked a few dwarves to stay behind and guard the Silver Deep. They were led by Olin and it was he who was charged with sending reports to King Dáin. Nobody's heard from Olin in quite a while...long enough to make us worried.
'The Guard House is west of Frerin's Court. If he's there, he may be able to tell us what happened.'

'A friendly face at last! You must help me, for I've been poisoned...no doubt by one of those ruffianly Dourhands. I'm weak as a babe...too weak to get help for myself. But a cure is...is near. You must get it for me!
'I must rest now...so very tired. I would tell you more of the Dourhands but I haven't the strength....'
Intro: Guards of the Silver Deep
The Guards of the Silver Deep are a group of dwarf-guardians charged by Thorin to ensure that the Silver Deep remains undisturbed.
'Get to Olin's home and find out why his reports are late. It's west of Frerin's Court.'

Olin may be found in the guard-house west of Frerin's Court.
Dwalin asked you to find Olin, one of the Guards of the Silver Deep, and learn what he knows about the situation at Thorin's Hall.
'I heard from the ${RACE} trainer that you're doing well. Good job!'
'I'd be proud to have you by my side when battle calls, ${PLAYER}.'
'How does your training fare? You look like you can handle anything.'
'I bet you're ready for anything, ${PLAYER}!'
'I heard from the ${RACE} trainer that you're doing well. Good job!'
'I'd be proud to have you by my side when battle calls, ${PLAYER}.'
'How does your training fare? You look like you can handle anything.'
'I bet you're ready for anything, ${PLAYER}!'

'Fortunately, there is a ${CLASS} here with us. You should spend some time with him and learn a thing or two. When he's finished with you, you'll be prepared for whatever lies ahead!
'You can find the ${CLASS} near the centre of the Berghold to the west.'

'Ah, yes! I can see a difference already. You seem like a proper ${CLASS} at last!
'Are you wondering why I have given you food? Why, you're a dwarf! What dwarf can survive on air alone? You need food to keep up your strength! If you find yourself wanting more, you can speak with Bogi out in Frerin's Court...he provisions our company.
'Now, about those pesky Dourhands....'

'Ah, how I long for the fires of battle. I should be out there fighting, not talking to some wet-behind-the-ears -- but you are here to learn the Champion's ways, eh? Let me tell you something...
'The Champion does not stand at the back of the ranks. We stand on the front lines, shoulder-to-shoulder with our brethren. \qBaruk Khazâd! Khazâd ai-mênu!\q is our battle call, and we will fight until our breath has left us!
'Learn all you can as quickly as you can, I say. We'll need your strength if we're to drive the shadow from this land.'

'Ah, hello to you! Good to see another Guardian about. It's not an easy task we choose to undertake, you know. Most would break under the strain. But not you! You're like me...a born defender.
'You see, it's not all about winning. It's about surviving to fight another day. In battle, a Guardian shields his captain and fellow warriors, enabling them to attack without fear of harm. You're the bulwark. If you fall, all is lost.
'Never forget those who depend upon you, Guardian.'

'Good day! Just standing here in the Blue Mountains makes me want to break out into song! But you're a Minstrel like me, here for some advice not a performance. Well, lend an ear!
'As you may know, the Minstrel holds great power...the power to stir the spirit and raise hopes when all seems lost. We'll sing of the glory of our past, songs that can rout armies and crack stone.
'It's not a game, friend. You've a great responsibility, and you had best do your fellow Minstrels proud. Use your gifts well, and you will never know defeat!'

'It feels good to breathe the air of the Blue Mountains once more! And there's plenty of hunting to be had, eh? If you want a little training, I'm happy to share what I know. Before I do, I'll give you some advice.
'Unlike the Champion or the Guardian, we Hunters don't like to get into the thick of things. It's better if we stand off at a distance and rain arrows down upon the enemy. And if the scoundrel gets too close, we end it...quick. If it doesn't end then and there, you best hope your Guardian is near...ha ha!
'Of course, if your aim is true, then that won't be a problem!'
Speak to the ${CLASS} trainer
Intro: Sharpen Your Skills
Dori recommended that you sharpen your skills a bit before confronting the Dourhands.
'You should find your fellow ${CLASS} over on the western side of the Berghold.'
'Well done, ${CLASS}! I'll have more to teach you later, but for now, return to Dori and tell him what you learned.
'Good, good. You'll make a fine Guardian yet, ${PLAYER}. Now head back to Dori. I understand he has an important task for you.'
'You're coming along well, ${PLAYER}. Until you're ready for more training, you should return to Dori and see what he has planned.'
'Excellent work! There's still more to learn, but we'll get to that when you've proven yourself ready. Go and speak to Dori. I'm sure he has a job for you to do.'
'I heard from the ${RACE} trainer that you're doing well. Good job!'
'I'd be proud to have you by my side when battle calls, ${PLAYER}.'
'How does your training fare? You look like you can handle anything.'
'I bet you're ready for anything, ${PLAYER}!'

The ${CLASS} trainer awaits you near the centre of the Berghold to the west of Dori.
Dori suggested that you spend some time training with the visiting ${CLASS}.

Dori can be found just east of the Berghold.
You should return to Dori and find out what he means to do about the Dourhands.

'It's hard to see the old place a mess like this. You'd think with all the tribute they've been holding on to, they could keep the place neat and tidy. Bah, ill-mannered louts is what they are. But there I go running my mouth off again.
'Dori wants to speak to you, though I do not know for what reason. You'll find him nearby. Just up those eastern stairs. You might want to be quick, he's been waiting for you.'

'Can you believe how the Dourhands let this place go? Dáin was right to mistrust the word of their envoy. \qWe cannot pay the tribute,\q indeed!
'We should confront these Dourhands about their poor stewardship, but before we do, you need to sharpen your skills.'
Intro: Return from the Lonely Mountain
After many years of absence, a party of Longbeards has returned to the Blue Mountains and Thorin's Hall.
'You should go talk to Dori. He's waiting for you at the top of those stairs to the east.'
'It'll take years to clean up the mess these Dourhands have made of the place!'

Dori can be found up a set of stairs east of Bolli.
Bolli told you that Dori wished to speak with you.

'Thanks to you, the town of Overhill has been made safe. I am glad.'
'It was a tough thing, ${PLAYER}, but we were able to defeat the Wargs.'
'I haven't forgotten that you helped us, ${PLAYER}. Thank you again!'
'You're an excellent hunter, ${PLAYER}, and we of Overhill are grateful!'

'A traveller brought word to me that Gytha Lainey is seeking your help, ${PLAYER}. He was given the message not long ago, and he impressed upon me the urgency of the task, though she did not convey to him its nature.
'You should go to Gytha Lainey at once! It must be something serious to have troubled so great a hunter as she.
'Look for her at Adso's Camp, on the road between Bree-town and Buckland.'

'I'm glad you came with such haste, ${PLAYER}, for I don't know who else I could trust to help me with this -- few hunters have proven themselves to me as you have, for the demise of Yellowfang is unmatched as proof of your worth.
'But Yellowfang is merely a pup compared to the danger of which I have learned -- a hunting-party of Wargs, a great breed of wolves, have come out of the north and are even now making their way into the lands of the Little Folk. What little I could learn from the frightened folk of the North Downs told me that these Wargs are looking for one of their number who came south and disappeared.
'This search might have brought them to the Shire, but when they find such a wealth of defenceless \qmorsels,\q they will surely forget their mission and prey upon the people there! We have to find and stop these Wargs before they reach any towns, ${PLAYER}! Let me know if you are ready to travel at once, and with haste!'

'I was not wrong about you this time, ${PLAYER}, for I knew that you were up to the task at hand, and now the Wargs know it too! Though their fellow may remain missing, I do not think they will trouble the Shire again...not for a while yet.
'I charge you with this: always maintain your focus, ${PLAYER} -- a true hunter does not stray from her path, no matter the distraction.
'You have my thanks, Hunter ${PLAYER}.'

Gytha Lainey is at Adso's Camp in Bree-land, on the road between Buckland and the town of Bree.
Gytha Lainey has sent word to you that she urgently needs your help.

Gytha Lainey is at Adso's Camp in Breeland, on the road between Bree-town and Buckland.
Gytha Lainey is waiting to speak with you and then travel into the Shire to intercept the hunting-party of Wargs that have come south in search of one of their own.

Gytha Lainey is at Adso's Camp in Breeland, on the road between Bree-town and Buckland.
Gytha Lainey is waiting to speak with you about your defence of the town of Overhill.

'What's that you said? Wargs? Oh my, what kind of creature is that? Well, whatever they are, they don't have any business coming to Overhill, and I don't mind saying it!
'It's late, and I was planning on going inside soon anyway. I'll turn in for the night, and I hope that in the morning these creatures will have come to their senses and left Overhill alone!'

'Wargs? If these creatures are anything like the big black bear that's caused me no end of grief, they're sure to be fierce!
'I don't want any trouble with none of these Wargs. I'll go inside now, and no questions asked!'

'Well, you bring disturbing news, ${PLAYER}, don't you? Of all the times for my cart to run into trouble, too! I'm sure these Wargs you mentioned wouldn't come anywhere near my home on Bree-hill!
'I'll stay with my friend Everard until this blows over. Thanks for letting me know!'

'Wargs? What could have ever brought such frightening creatures into the Shire?
'I'm going to go inside at once -- you don't need to tell me twice, not this hobbit!'

'It seems that we're not too late, ${PLAYER} -- we have arrived before the Wargs, but I do not know how long it will be before they reach the town.
'Quickly, run into town and tell everyone you see to go inside their homes and not to come back out until we say the danger has passed. Do not take \qno\q for an answer, ${PLAYER} -- their lives may depend on doing what we say.
'I will try and determine how far away the creatures may have come since I lost their trail.'

'You have done it, ${PLAYER}, and I cannot thank you enough! The people of Overhill would have been helpless without our warning and subsequent aid, and though they might not have appreciated the danger, it does my heart good to know that such a place is safe once again from the ravages of war.
'I think the wargs will not come again into this land, not for a time, yet. I wonder what it is that brought them here?
'Let me know when you are ready to go, and we can travel back to Adso's camp.'

'I am ready to return to Adso's camp, if you are ready as well. The folk here are always polite, even if they do not always appreciate the presence of \qBig Folk\q like myself. Today, however, I think they do. It makes me smile.'

'Good, you have done well, ${PLAYER} -- now, at least, the hobbits here should be safe for a time should we fail to stop the Wargs.
'Judging from the direction of their tracks before I lost the trail, the Wargs are surely in the Bindbole Wood by now. Look to the north, and try to stop them before they reach the town! They will have split up by this time, and are surely prowling cautiously southward.
'I will try and stop any that reach the town, ${PLAYER}, but I am counting on you to defeat as many as you can as they approach -- if too many of the creatures arrive at Overhill at once, I will surely be overwhelmed, and then all hope of stopping the creatures will be gone.'

Instance: A Hunter's Charge
You have travelled with Gytha Lainey to the town of Overhill, in the Shire, to defend its people from the ravages of a prowling group of Wargs that have come down from the north.
'Hello? The danger has passed, then? I am glad to hear it. You and your friend have my thanks, of course.'

'So the Wargs have gone, then? Good, good. I would have been out here too, of course, just to see what the fuss was all about, but I had the tea on and couldn't get away.
'Good work, though, no mistake about that!'
'It sounds like you took care of things. Thank you for that!'
'A job well done, ${PLAYER}!'
'It's safe now, isn't it?'
'I don't understand what's been happening to the Shire lately.'

Gytha Lainey is on the road outside Overhill.
You have come to Overhill with Gytha Lainey to save its people from the danger that threatens them. Gytha is waiting to speak with you about how to proceed.

The people of Overhill are going about their business, oblivious to the danger that lurks somewhere north of their town.
Gytha has told you to warn the people of Overhill to stay inside their houses until the danger has passed.

Gytha Lainey is in the town of Overhill.
Now that you have told the people of Overhill to go inside their houses, it is up to you and Gytha to stop the intruding Wargs.

Gytha Lainey is in Overhill.
You have successfully defeated the Warg hunting-party that intruded into the Bindbole Wood and should now speak of your success to Gytha Lainey.

Journey with Gytha Lainey into the Old Forest
The Hunter's Path
For a true hunter, speed and precision are everything. A lack of one brings ill fortune. A lack of both brings disaster.

'Are you ready to go? We will travel into the Old Forest, and I will judge your merit -- if you can defeat Yellowfang, you might be worthy of my teaching.
'Keep in your mind these two warnings, however. The Old Forest is a confusing place for the unwary, and it seems as if the trees move about when you are not looking. Even if you have journeyed beneath the canopy before, you might find that the paths are unknown to you now.
'And secondly, Yellowfang is no fool. She will not challenge you unless you can somehow draw her out of hiding. Your combat ability, as well as your skill at tracking, will be tested.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>

'You say you are a hunter, but what proof do you have that you have chosen the right calling? Perhaps you should have been a minstrel, like that Prescott fellow who sometimes sings of my doings. Or perhaps the calling of burglar would have suited you better, like the hobbit back there with his eyes on Adso's roast?
'Still you say you are worthy of calling yourself a hunter! I shall be the judge of that, then, for I have a challenge for you. A mighty wolf stalks among the fallen leaves of the Old Forest, but she displays unusual cunning for her kind and is a menace to those who stray from the paths.
'Speak with me if you are willing to undertake this challenge, and I will go with you into the forest. There will I judge your skill in bringing down the terrible Yellowfang.'

'You surprised me, ${PLAYER}. I did not believe you were capable of finding and defeating Yellowfang, and for that you have my apologies.
'You are a hunter of great promise, and I will teach you a technique you are already well on your way to learning on your own: the ability to more quickly let fly your arrows.'

Gytha Lainey, a hunter of great skill, can be found in Bree-land at Adso's Camp on the road between Bree and Buckland.
You have been told to speak with Gytha Lainey for instruction in the art of the hunter.

Gytha Lainey, a hunter of great skill, can be found in Bree-land at Adso's Camp, on the Great East Road between Bree and Buckland.
Gytha is waiting to speak with you about your victory over Yellowfang within the Old Forest.
'Yellowfang is no more? I am surprised, ${PLAYER}, but I have no reason to doubt your words. It could be that I misjudged your worth as a hunter.'
'I will lead the way back to Adso's Camp, ${PLAYER}, if you are ready to leave.'
Instance: The Hunter's Path
Gytha Lainey has brought you into the Old Forest to challenge your skill as a hunter.

'Yellowfang is hiding somewhere within the Old Forest, but you will need to show some cunning of your own if you are to locate her, ${PLAYER}.
'I will wait for you to defeat the mighty wolf. If you are worthy of calling yourself a hunter, you should be able to do this deed.'

Yellowfang is somewhere within the Old Forest.
Gytha Lainey has tasked you with defeating Yellowfang, a deadly wolf that stalks the Old Forest. She warned you that Yellowfang is cunning, and you will need to devise some way to lure her out of hiding.

Gytha Lainey is waiting for you somewhere in the Old Forest.
Gytha will be both pleased and surprised to know that you have defeated Yellowfang.

'It is an honour and a privilege to meet you, ${PLAYER}. Many good folk depend on us for their protection and the safety of their borders, though they may not know it. We have the respect of the Rangers of the North for a reason, and our paths often cross with theirs, to the betterment of all.
'You are deserving of equipment that reflects your well-honed skill, ${PLAYER}, and I would be delighted to help you fashion it. Be advised, however, that no path worth following is an easy one. The things I can help you prepare will only be as good as the story behind them, and the story behind these implements and articles will be one of fell dangers and the ultimate triumph over evil.
'A hunter of lesser stature would despair of this road into the dark, but you, I know, will come again into the light of the sun. Speak with me if you are ready to set upon this path.'

Fenton Marshley is outside the Hunting Lodge east of the town of Archet and north of Bree, in Bree-land.
You have been told to speak with Fenton Marshley, a skilled hunter who may have some words for you.

'I can make you a piece of equipment worthy of your skill as a hunter, ${PLAYER}, but with this offer I give to you a warning: the tale of this piece will be hard-fought and purchased with great toil.
'I give to you a list of components that I will need. Bring these things to me, and I will do what I must to lend strength to the article I make for you.
'I will need time between each stage of the process, so do not bring me everything at once. The notes I have given you will tell you when to give me each component. I will first need the matted hide of Zorrgolug, a great Warg of Fasach-falroid, and five sulfur-tinged Tarkrîp helmets affected by the great swamp of Malenhad. Begin your hunt with confidence and finish it with triumph!'

'You return in victory, ${PLAYER}! I am pleased to see that you bring with you the hide of Zorrgolug and helmets of the Tarkrîp tinged with sulfur. The tale of your deeds grows ever longer!
'There are more components to seek, ${PLAYER}. Look to the notes I gave you and begin your hunt for glossy cave-claw skin and corroded Neekerbreeker-horns.
'If you have the benefit of allies, they may be of use to you in the collection of these unpleasant trophies. I will await your return.'
'You do not have the first set of components I asked for, ${PLAYER}? How can this be?'

'I welcome you once again, ${PLAYER}, for I see that you have returned with the glossy skins and corroded horns I tasked you with obtaining.
'The last set of components remain, and obtaining these will not be easy. Do not despair! I am confident that you can retrieve them, even from the blackest depths of the shadow itself!'
'You have not returned with the second set of components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'You emerge triumphant from the darkness, ${PLAYER}, and I rejoice to see it!
'I marvel at your hunting prowess, my friend. Wear this small token with pride, for you have earned it with your hard work and your dedication!'
'You have not brought me the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'Allow me to congratulate you on your great accomplishments, ${PLAYER}. Few hunters can boast of the dangers you have braved and the dark places into which your hunts have taken you, and you should be proud of your deeds, for they are worthy of commendation!
'My home is in Dale, but the way of the hunter is one that wanders. As I passed through the Mirkwood on the journey that eventually brought me here, I chanced upon a party of Elves that were leaving Thranduil's halls on some errand to speak with Elrond of Rivendell. One of that company, a fair Elf named Legolas, seemed to be a hunter of no small skill.
'I can teach you nothing more, but I am sure this Legolas could give you some manner of instruction. If he is still at Rivendell, seek him out and you may find a willing teacher.'

'I bid you welcome, ${PLAYER}, as one hunter to another! I remember Fenton Marshley, for we were not far from my father's halls when we came upon him and offered to show him the way there to rest. He politely refused, saying he still had some miles left in him to walk that day. He seemed a hardy sort.
'There is little I need to teach you, ${PLAYER}, for you are already possessed of many skills! I can give you this, however: it is more important to be watchful, to be always aware of your surroundings, than it is to be strong. Strength of arm is important, for the bow-string must be taut before her arrow will fly, but strength of mind is more important than all! Be ever-watchful, ${PLAYER}, and your bow will never want for targets.
'I will see you again, my friend, and it is to be hoped in happier days! It is always a pleasure to speak with one who follows the same course, though the paths be different.'
A Lesson from Legolas
Fenton Marshley, impressed by your dedication and your ability, has recommended that you speak with Legolas, an Elf possessed of great skill in the hunt.
'I do not know the nature of the errand that brought Legolas and his people to Rivendell, but he seemed a hunter of no small skill. He may be able to impart to you even more hunter's wisdom.'
'Greetings, fellow hunter!'
'It is always a pleasure to speak with you, ${PLAYER}.'

Legolas may still be in Rivendell.
Fenton Marshley encountered a party of Elves on his journey through the Mirkwood and believes that one of that company might still have things to teach even a skilled hunter such as yourself.

'I can make you a weapon that befits your great skill as a hunter, ${PLAYER}, but you must steel yourself for hardship, for its tale will not be easily won. I give to you a list of things I will need for its making. Bring these items to me from out of the darkness, and their destruction will bring strength to the weapon I make for you.
'I will need time between each stage of the process, so do not bring me everything at once. The notes I have given you will tell you when to give me each component. I will first need five corroded iron-crown staves and a razor-sharp claw belonging to Driftclaw, a great bear of the Misty Mountains. Look to my instructions for his story.
'May fortune smile upon you during your hunt, ${PLAYER}. It has to this point, and I know it will continue to do so.'

'I rejoice at your return, ${PLAYER}, for Driftclaw was of old a fearsome opponent! His claw now will be of use to me in fashioning a weapon worthy of such a hunter as you!

'Shortly after Frodo Baggins and his company came to Rivendell, my father sent us to search for signs of the Nazgûl, the Nine Riders of the Enemy. We found the bodies of eight horses downstream, but of the last there was no sign. We searched further, but still found nothing.
'We travelled far afield, into lands to the south, and still found no sign of the fleeing Rider. Only on our return journey did we find something: hoofprints in the South Trollshaws, far south of the road. There are many narrow valleys in that region -- the Nazgûl might lie there, sheltered from prying eyes, waiting for his time to strike.
'Journey far south of the road in the South Trollshaws, ${PLAYER}, and seek out the missing Rider. The ruins within those narrow channels have a fell reputation. Minas Agor that place was called of old, and the Nazgûl may have sought it out for that reason.'

'Your tale begins to fill in this puzzle for me, ${PLAYER}, and I think I now see what has happened.
'Caught between the remainder of Frodo's company and the raging of the Bruinen, the Nine were forced into the torrent -- but one escaped in the chaos. Near death, his steed bore him through hidden channels into some place where, nearly formless, he gathered his strength.
'His horse he abandoned, and he vanished into the wild. Without his cloak he would be all but invisible to us -- a malice on the wind. If he takes it onto himself again, it is only to give shape to his strength. It means he has survived the ordeal unharmed and will surely strike at us again. We are running out of time, ${PLAYER}.'
'You have not returned with the bridle, ${PLAYER}. How am I to examine it to see that this is truly that of the missing Nazgûl's steed?'

'Nan Tornaeth was once home to a great city of Rhudaur, but it fell into ruin in the great battles of long ago and has been largely reclaimed by the wilderness. Hill-men make their homes among the ruins, cursed still for their ancient betrayal.
'Calenthon set out with his falcon Malloval to search the ruins of Nan Tornaeth, but neither have returned. Find him and lend him what aid you may. It could be he has encountered some difficulty and cannot send word to us.
'Do you have a map of the wilderness? I will show you where Calenthon may be found. Look to the north-west of Thorenhad... there. Do you see there, by the 'T' in Nan Tornaeth? Look for him there, and happy fortune go with you.'
'You have come from Thorenhad? I would have sent word to Elrohir, but I do not yet understand the nature of the evil I have discovered here. Will you lend me your aid?'
A Scout in Nan Tornaeth
Many scouts were dispatched across the Trollshaws to keep watch for signs of evil, and the sons of Elrond want to know if anything has been found.
'Calenthon should be somewhere to the north-west, investigating the ruins of Nan Tornaeth. Take out your map, and look for him by the 'T' of Nan Tornaeth.'
'Nan Tornaeth is full of danger. The echoes of the past lie heavily on this land.'
'The sons of Elrond dispatched many of us into the wilderness.'

Calenthon was sent forth from Thorenhad to investigate the ruins of Nan Tornaeth, north-west of Thorenhad. Elrohir identified a likely location on your map: by the 'T' in Nan Tornaeth.
Elrohir has asked you to learn the fate of Calenthon, sent forth to scout Nan Tornaeth.

Slain Tenebrous Dire-weavers(${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Destroying the eggs was a start towards stifling the evil of this brood for the future, there is much to be done still.
'We are uncertain how many generations the brood-mother hidden deep in the lair has borne. We do know that the lesser of children have made their way out of the lair and into the forested areas.
'Her brood can be found along the western edge heading into the northern Trollshaws. Find them and eliminate a host of the creatures. Do not attempt this alone as her brood is unusually potent.'

'The more of the enemy that falls, the better we are prepared. You are to be thanked for your contributions so far, ${PLAYER}.
'Prepare yourself and your fellows for soon we must move against the matron.'
Kill Tenebrous Blight-fangs(${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Kill Tenebrous Dire-weavers(${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Kill Tenebrous Weald-delvers(${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Elrohir
Slaughtering the Brood

Elrohir identified a source of terrible danger and evil in the north-west area of the Trollshaws.
Hidden through a dark section of the woods an ancient brood of spider lurks and waits for victims. The brood-mother has busily been laying her eggs and if unchecked her offspring will soon tear through the Trollshaws and infest areas east and west of the Bruinen River.

Spiders dwelling in the north-west section of the Trollshaws are a potent threat to the area. They must be eliminated.
Elrohir sent you into the north-west to eliminate a host of the brood.

Return to Elrohir at the camp in the Trollshaws and tell him of your success.
You made your way into the forest and dispatched a host of the spiders.

'You have been a boon to those of us assigned to watch the Trollshaws, ${PLAYER}. Recovering the stones stolen from Heithur's couriers was no small task, but you did so without complaint. I know that Barachen is pleased with your service, and I add my voice to his. You have our thanks.
'If you are of a mind to continue lending your aid, I would have you introduce yourself to Elladan and Elrohir, the sons of Elrond. They have established a camp, Thorenhad, east of here and to the north, and I know your services would be appreciated. Their camp is within a set of hilltop ruins north of the bear-dens of the Bruinen Gorges.
'They have organized a concerted effort to watch the wilderness for signs of evil. If you go to them, they will surely find a use for you. Tell Elrohir that you have come with Barachen and Rochwen's commendations.'

'You are welcome to join our company, ${PLAYER}, for there is much work to be done if we are to keep this land safe from servants of the Enemy. I have known Rochwen for a very long time, and I tell you truly that she does not give her recommendation lightly. I fear that she still does not approve entirely of my brother, for example, despite his best efforts to impress her.'
The Sons of Elrond
The Elves of Barachen's company were impressed by your recovery of Heithur's stolen stones and have asked you to aid Elladan and Elrohir, the sons of Elrond, with their duties in the Trollshaws.

'I give you my greetings, ${PLAYER}. You are welcome at Thorenhad, and I hope you will be a help to us in our duty. My brother Elrohir can better acquaint you with what needs to be done, but I look forwards to facing the evils of the wild at your side.'
'You will find Elrohir at his camp of Thorenhad, east of here among the Bruinen Gorges and north of the bear-dens, among a set of hilltop ruins.'
'The wilderness is full of danger.'
'Keep all your senses sharp, for the Trollshaws harbour hidden dangers.'
'Our father has sent us to keep watch over the wilderness.'
'Stay alert, for the Enemy has servants in all corners of the world.'

Elrohir is at Thorenhad, the camp he established with his brother Elladan. Thorenhad is east of the Elf Rochwen, among the Bruinen Gorges, to the north of the bear-dens.
Rochwen is impressed by your skill and determination and has asked you to lend your aid to the sons of Elrond, who keep watch over the Trollshaws from their camp near the Bruinen Gorges.

'I do not believe you have been told yet of Thorenhad. Elrond has sent scouts there to patrol the wilds of the Trollshaws and to search out the evil that lurks in those old hills.
'I am sure you would be welcomed there, for the Trollshaws are a broad land, and our people too few. Seek out Elrond's son Elrohir and say that I have sent you to support him.
'Thorenhad is a ruin atop a hill north of the bear-dens of the Bruinen Gorges. It is to the east of Barachen's camp and some distance west of here.'
'You are welcome to join our company, ${PLAYER}. My brother and I have done our best, but there is more still to be done if we are to keep this land safe from servants of the Enemy.'
To Thorenhad
Elf-scouts are encamped at Thorenhad, charged with patrolling the Trollshaws for signs of evil.
'Please, seek out Elrohir at Thorenhad.'

Thorenhad is a ruin atop a hill north of the bear-dens of the Bruinen Gorges. It is to the east of Barachen's camp, and some distance west of Rivendell.
Anhebir has sent you to Thorenhad, to report to Elrond's son, Elrohir.
'My friends Fimgris and Narlinn can be found at Thorenhad.'
'Imladris is far to the east, beyond the Bruinen.'
'You have already been a great help to Barachen and to all of us.'
'Rochwen told me of your brave recovery of Heithur's stones.'
'Heithur Ironfist told me all about your efforts on my behalf. I thank you!'
'We are well-met in friendship, ${PLAYER}!'

'We are very close to recovering the stones, ${PLAYER}, I am sure of it! Tóki Whitebeard has repaid my trust in him ten-fold, for now we know the culprits: the stone-trolls of this inhospitable place!
'The Elf Rochwen was right to send you to the ruins where you found the Whitebeard, and I expect she will be able to tell us where these trolls make their lair.
'Speak to Rochwen, north of here by the road, and recover those stones, ${PLAYER}! Lord Glóin should not be made to wait any longer for the delivery he requested!'

'As you might expect, the Trollshaws are a wild place and home to many different tribes of troll, but all of them are dangerous. They are not to be crossed lightly.
'It is most unusual for a stone-troll to covet stones of the sort Heithur Ironfist has described -- these are of historical value only and would never be confused for precious gemstones.
'To the north-east, you will find the home of many stone-trolls. One of them will have these stones, if any do. Nan Tornaeth or the Bruinen Gorges are too far away for any troll there to be responsible for this theft, so do not travel too far afield. And you should bring allies, for even a single stone-troll is a difficult foe.'

'You have recovered the stones from the stone-trolls! You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}, and more besides -- you have the thanks too of Lord Glóin of the Lonely Mountain!
'Take this reward as well and bear it in memory of the good you have done for me and my master!'
'Where are the stones? I thought you were going to recover them from the stone-trolls?'
Bring the unremarkable stones to Heithur Ironfist
The True Thieves
Heithur Ironfist believes that you are now very near to recovering the stones that were stolen from his couriers.
'You'll find Rochwen to the north of here, on the road. She may be able to tell us which lair of the stone-trolls is home to the beast that stole the stones from my dwarves!'

'Travel east and north to find the home of the stone-trolls responsible for the loss of the stones sought by Heithur Ironfist. If you reach Nan Tornaeth or the Bruinen Gorges, you have gone too far afield.'

'You have recovered the stones! Heithur Ironfist will be most pleased! Deliver them to him at Barachen's camp, south of here and to the right, atop the sloping hill that lies in the shadow of the tall cliffs!'
'Why would the stone-trolls steal such stones as these? Most peculiar.'
'I am at your service, ${PLAYER}.'
'I am glad that you were able to help Heithur with his troubles.'
'Elrohir and Elladan expect much of us, and we maintain our vigilance for their sake.'
'Barachen, Alphlanc, and I watch for threats in the South Trollshaws.'
'The sons of Elrond maintain a camp at Thorenhad to the north-east.'

Rochwen is north of Barachen's camp, on the road that runs through the South Trollshaws.
Heithur Ironfist has asked you to speak with Rochwen about the stone-trolls of the region so you may retrieve the stones stolen from his couriers.

Stone-trolls in the South Trollshaws can be found north-east of Rochwen's post.
Rochwen believes that one of the stone-trolls of the South Trollshaws must have taken the stones from the dwarf-couriers, though that is most unusual. She advised you to bring friends with you, for even a single stone-troll is a dangerous opponent.

Heithur Ironfist is at Barachen's camp, south of the road, atop the sloping hill that lies in the shadow of the tall cliffs.
Heithur Ironfist is waiting for you to return with the stones stolen from Glóin's couriers.
The goblin-camps sprawl along the ridges of the Pinnath Fenui

'So you say that Elrond mentioned goblins in his direction to come here? It doesn't surprise me. I ran into some troublesome goblins up here when I crossed the Misty Mountains in Thorin's great quest. That time we were sorely beset by goblins.
'Now, it does seem the foul things are even more stirred up lately, and perhaps your Rider is the cause. One of the scouts here reported them moving far from their holes far to the east and heard them chanting \qGurzmat\q...their leader no doubt.
'Aye, that's what needs to be done. Slay this Gurzmat, and the goblins will be in such a disarray they won't present a problem to anyone -- and maybe you'll find the trail of this Rider you seek. Seek out the goblin fires to the north and east along the Pinnath Fenui, and you'll likely find Gurzmat holed up deep in one of the camps. I wish I could help you more, but as I said, there's a more pressing task from Dáin that I must give my attention to.'

'What! Dourhand dwarves with the goblins? Oh, yes, it's all coming together now!
'While you were away, one of my scouts reported something interesting. You see, the task given to me by King Dáin was to track down the Dourhands' last refuge. The scout seems to have found it, as there were a large number of Dourhands around an old dwarf-fortress called Gabilazan. But that wasn't all that he found!
'As the scout watched from a high ridge, two figures rode up to the fortress. One was a dwarf, the other a cloaked figure. At first he didn't know what he was seeing, but when all the Dourhands stopped what they were doing and cheered, he knew the dwarf could only be one person: Skrogrím! Now, with what you've told me, the other figure with him must have been the Ringwraith. It would seem our two tasks are but one, friend.'
Find the goblin-camp
Chapter 2: Troublesome Goblins
Glóin told you that the goblins seem very active of late, and that he would not be surprised if the Nazgûl you are pursuing were the cause.

'The goblins have a camp out there someplace, hidden somewhere among the snows. Look east and north of here, along the ridges of the Pinnath Fenui. Once you find this camp, work your way deep inside. If you can put an end to this Gurzmat, you'll likely put an end to that Rider's schemes.'
'You've found the camps, but Gurzmat still lives? ${PLAYER}, that just will not do. You need to ascend into that goblin-camp and put an end to Gurzmat!'

The goblins have many camps among the ridges of Pinnath Fenui, far to the east and north of Glóin's camp.
Glóin told you that if you search for the goblins' camps in the Misty Mountains, you should find a goblin named Gurzmat. He appears to be their leader, and by defeating him, you should throw the goblins into disarray and perhaps find the trail of the Nazgûl.

Gurzmat is somewhere deep within the goblin-camp that sprawls along the ridges of the Pinnath Fenui.
Glóin told you that by defeating the goblin Gurzmat, you would throw the goblins into disarray and perhaps find the trail of the Nazgûl you seek.

Glóin is at his camp north of Rivendell.
In defeating Gurzmat, you find him accompanied by hostile Dourhand dwarves. Glóin should be made known of this development immediately.
Collected Gabilazan plans

'If we can but enter this fortress, we will end two problems with one fell stroke. By ending the threat of this Rider, we can ensure Rivendell's safety, and by putting an end to Skorgrím, we will crush the Dourhands. However, it won't be easy, as the scout reported the two entered the the inner keep of the fortress. That keep is nearly impregnable.
'This is what you must do, ${PLAYER}. Every dwarf-fortress has a secret entrance, and although I do not know the secret of Gabilazan, I know how to learn it. When the cornerstone for Gabilazan was laid down, a copy of the fortress' plans would have been stored within. Around that cornerstone the fortress was built, and can now only be accessed by entering Gabilazan's vault. Once we have the plans, we will be able to learn the fortress' secret entrance.
'Gabilazan can be found in the more westerly of the two passes that gate entrance to Iorbar. The easternmost pass, Rakhâs-bizar, is not guarded by dwarves and may give you a roundabout means of approaching the keep.'

'Ah, wonderful, you found the cornerstone, and the plans were within. I didn't mention it before you left, but there was a very good chance the plans were taken or destroyed years ago. Yet it seems fortune is smiling upon us this day!
'Oh, and look here. Here's the inner keep's secret entrance!'

'The pass to Gabilazan runs from north to south and will be guarded by Dourhands. Find the vault in Gabilazan. Within that vault you should be able to find the fortress' cornerstone. Within that stone, there should be the original plans for the fortress.
'With those plans, we should be able to learn the secret entrance into the fortress' inner keep.'
Bring the Gabilazan plans to Glóin
Collect plans from Gabilazan cornerstone
Chapter 3: The High Fortress

Glóin told you that the Nazgûl you are pursuing can be found in the old dwarf-fortress of Gabilazan, in the company of Skorgrím Dourhand. The two entered the nearly impregnable inner keep of the fortress. Glóin believes the only way to enter the inner keep is to learn its secret entrance.

The cornerstone containing the plans is located inside Gabilazan's Vault, located in one of the two passes east of Glóin's camp. Glóin's camp is north of Rivendell.
Glóin told you that to learn how to access the secret entrance to Gabilazan's inner keep, you will need to take the plans for the fortress placed in its cornerstone.
Collected the key-stone

'Ah, yes, why it will be just like when Burglar Bilbo crept into Smaug's lair! We'll just need the key to open the secret door, and you'll be in the inner keep. Finding that key, though, could present a challenge.
'Now the old tales of Helegrod -- that's the great dwarf-hall to the north that fell to the dragon Thorog -- say that after it was abandoned, all the surrounding dwarf-halls were abandoned as well. The key-stones that opened the secret doors to all those halls were hidden in a small dwarf-vault near the source of the Bruinen. The building might be in ruins now, but the vault is surely still there. Once we have the key-stone, the inner keep of Gabilazan will be open to us!
'Journey north to the source of the Bruinen and look for the vault at Iskeld's Lookout. You will need to brave the snowbeasts that make their homes among the drifts, but that should not be a problem for you, I would expect!'
'Yes, yes, this is the key-stone of which I spoke! Good work, ${PLAYER}! Now the real business will begin.'
'Please get that key-stone. We won't be able to get into the inner keep without it! Look to the source of the Bruinen for the dwarf-vault.'
Bring the key-stone to Glóin
Collect the key-stone
Chapter 4: The Key-stone
Glóin discovered the secret entrance to the inner keep of Gabilazan, but the way is locked and will require an artifact of the old days.

The dwarf-vault that contains the key-stone is at Iskeld's Lookout, near the source of the Bruinen. Glóin is at his camp north of Rivendell.
Glóin has asked you to retrieve a key-stone from an old dwarf-vault. The key-stone will allow you entry into the Dourhand-occupied dwarf-keep.

'Now that we have the keystone, the back way into the Dourhand keep will be open to us! You should be able to confront both the Nazgûl and Skorgrím. However, the task will be a great one, and you will need help, so gather a company of allies. Also, since completion of this task may mean the end of Skorgrím, a great boon to Durin's Folk, I will send my son Gimli along with you to aid in the battle. I will entrust him with both the key-stone and the secret dwarf-lore needed to open the gate.
'Now go and gather a company of allies and prepare for the battle ahead. Once you are prepared, speak to Gimli. Together you will set off for the keep, and he shall open the secret way into the inner keep.
'This will be a great day for the Free Peoples, ${PLAYER}! I am eager for your return with the tale of your victory!'

'You bring tidings both joyous and dark, ${PLAYER}. The Dourhands are done! They will never hope to threaten the Longbeards again.
'While the news of the spirit that was driven from Skorgrím is unsettling, it is not as disturbing as the news of the Rider's escape. What is worse, you tell me that he spoke of bringing men to Helegrod. What he seeks in that old dwarf-hall is a mystery to me.
'Unfortunately, there is more that must be done if Rivendell is to be secured. Know, though, that I will give you whatever help I can.'
Speak to Gimli
Chapter 5: The Last Refuge
With the key-stone in hand, you can now enter the dwarf-keep in Gabilazan, the last refuge of the Dourhands and confront both the Nazgûl and Skorgrím.
'That was a good fight, ${PLAYER}! Such exercise does not come along every day!'

'Ah, hello ${PLAYER}. A glorious battle awaits us!
'Are you and your allies ready? My father has given me the key-stone, so I am prepared. Let us go now into the Mountains to defeat Skorgrím and his Dourhands!'
'Speak to Gimli when your allies are ready, and he will lead you to the dwarf-keep.'
'That was a glorious battle we had with those Dourhands!'
'You have done the Longbeards a great service, my friend! The line of Durin is in your debt!'

Gimli is at his father's camp, north of Rivendell.
When you have gathered a fellowship, seek out Gimli, and he will accompany you to the dwarf-keep where the Nazgûl and Skorgrím may be hiding.

Glóin is at his camp north of Rivendell.

Defeated Skorgrím

'You fought well, ${PLAYER}, and we have put an end to Skorgrím's menace! I am troubled by the escape of the Nazgûl and the apparition that appeared upon Skorgrím's death, but there is nothing we can do about that right now. At least we have paid the Dourhands for their treachery! Ha ha!'
'It was a good battle, but I think it is time to leave. I am ready to journey back to my father's camp when you are.'

'Skorgrím must think that the walls of his fortress will keep him safe, tall and broad as they are, but he does not know about the key-stone you recovered.
'We will fight our way through his remaining defences, and perhaps I will give him one chance to come out of the main gates of the keep to face me in combat. He has no honour, so my challenge will probably go unanswered. It is just as well, but my axe is anxious for the chance to end this fool Dourhand!
'Are you ready? The Dourhands cannot hope to stand against us!'
'I am ready to go on, if you are as well. I will challenge Skorgrím to come down, and if he does not, we will seek out the hidden door.'

'It seems these Dourhands were not expecting us to come in by the hidden door, ${PLAYER}.
'This is amusing, but I tire of dealing with lesser Dourhands. Let us find Skorgrím with no further delay!'

'Skorgrím has nowhere left to hide, ${PLAYER}, and I think he now realizes it. His doom stands outside his door, and he has no choice but to face it!
'Are you ready for battle?'

'If you have a moment, allow me to tell you some of the tale of Helegrod, the ruins of which lie north of here. The tale may shed light on what the Rider seeks to accomplish, though I cannot guess what that might be. Helegrod was delved beneath the mountain of Orod Lostol; it remained the northern-most outpost of Khazad-dûm for long years. Mithril was never found here, but a good many other stones and riches were. Those riches drew a dragon to Helegrod. Thorog, he was named; he slew all the dwarves and made his bed in Helegrod's treasury.
'In Khazad-dûm, which the Elves call Moria, Durin marshalled a company of dwarves to journey to Helegrod and slay the beast. Thorog was defeated, but Durin was slain by the dragon's dying breath. He was the fifth of that name; the next too had a sad end, but I will not speak of that now. Dwarves sought to reclaim Helegrod in the years that followed, but death hung heavy over that place and they abandoned the halls and removed Helegrod's riches to Khazad-dûm.
'I do not know what the Rider might seek to gain by taking to Helegrod. Perhaps he simply wants to fortify it, but I would wager there is more to this deed than we can see. Perhaps by scouting the borders of Helegrod we can learn more of his plans.'

'Wights! Surely this is the doing of the Rider! And that sigil you found on one of them...I can tell that it is an artifact of evil, but its true meaning is beyond me. Perhaps it is time we ask for help from Master Elrond!'

'Wights! You should go back and search one of them. Surely this is the doing of the Rider. But we must learn more. Perhaps there might be some clue as to what brought them here. Defeat one and search its remains!'
Scout the borders of Helegrod

Upon hearing that the Nazgûl fled to Helegrod, Glóin told you some of the tale of that ancient fortress.

'Elrond's hospitality is all well and good, but we tarry here longer than we expected, and I wonder if we begin to overstay our welcome. We brought gifts for the Elves when first we came, but I think perhaps that we have become tiresome guests, eating the Elves out of house and home, as once we did for a certain hobbit....
'Be that as it may, I would find another guest-gift for Elrond. There are great white bears roaming the Misty Mountains to the east and south of here, and I am of a mind to give Elrond a gift of their hides. I wonder if you would help us by hunting these beasts and collecting their hides?'
'Fine hides, fine hides indeed. You have proven a worthy hunter of beasts, ${PLAYER}. I hope this gift will please the Elves.'

'Never thought you for a coward, or maybe there are more pressing needs that you must attend. I understand that the whimsy of an old dwarf rates lower than the requests of these fine upstanding Elves.'
Bring the hides back to Glóin

'Trolls! There are trolls in the north and I cannot abide them to walk the world. None should, they are creatures of pure evil.
'You will need others to fight them, I am certain of that, but they must not survive. Fight them and kill them. We should be proud to drive such vile beasts from this world and see that they never rise again.
'When you have finished this task, return to me and I shall see that you get a reward that you richly deserve.
'Return to the snow-bound area of the Misty Mountains through the north pass from Rivendell and hunt the trolls deep in the mountains.'

'Ha! Should I desire to make my way into the goblin's halls to the north-east, I shall remember to call on you, ${PLAYER}.
'You have proven worthy of a hero's reward and I shall not disappoint you. I am greateful for all that you done and ask you to be cautious should you find yourself venturing further into the northern wilds.
'The Dwarfs lost something precious in those mountains a long time ago and what took it from them may be the same as what took the Lonely Mountain. Elrond and the others here say that its miserable life was quashed many years back but we Dwarfs know that evil tends to stay about long after you think it is gone.
'Thank you again, ${PLAYER}.'

A Company of Trolls

Gloín, after seeing Master Bilbo Baggins, recalled the stories told to him of the goblins who made the mountains their home. He wishes to venture out into the mountains himself but cannot, until his duties are complete. 'The text you recovered told of a dire champion of Angmar, an Orc of great strength that slew many of my people.
'Is this a legend of old or are these the words of truth? That I cannot say, but this Mordirith's servants are many and powerful...I do not doubt these claims.
'You should investigate the matter. Return to Minas Caul and strike its gates. Should this fabled champion exist, he would be ill-advised to ignore such a challenge.'

'Felling the Champion of Minas Caul is an impressive task. The Orcs will soon realize the threat you pose to their master.
'Celebrate your victory, ${PLAYER}, but do not forget the Orcs' love for vengeance.'
'That text you hold should summon the Orc champion.'

'I have stood shoulder to shoulder with our dwarf-allies, and I can attest to their skill in battle. That you fought a champion of the Dourhands and survived is an amazing feat, and one that those treacherous villains will not soon forget.'

'A scout from Esteldín, Muiladan, needs your help, and time is of the essence. If the Enemy discovers him, they will redouble their efforts to attack us before help arrives.
'Escort him through the valley from his hiding place south of here, atop a ridge that overlooks Nan Gurth. The terrain is treacherous and there are many hazards on the way to Gath Forthnír.
'His companions won't be far behind and with their numbers they should have little trouble fighting their way to us, if need be.'

'Your actions saved the scout from certain doom, but the Enemy is resourceful and will find a way to this safe-haven.
'We must show the Angmarim an even greater gesture of our strength. If they resume their attacks, I fear the worst.'
'I am glad you made it through. The eyes of the Merrevail are everywhere, and I feared I would be spotted before someone arrived.'
Find Muiladan
Help from the South

Return to Areneth in Gath Forthnír.

'Yes, I know a way to take the fire from the Angmarim. But I must warn you that this is no mean feat. I cannot promise you will return from this battle.
'There is a creature that commands the Angmarim. The wraith Garthamendir, a Cargûl that guards the gate of Carn Dûm. It is the thing that spurs the Angmarim into battle, the thing they fear more than your steel or the arrows of my Rangers.
'Find the Cargûl at the gates of Carn Dûm to the west. Rest first and gather your strength. You will need all of it if you are to triumph.'
'Your courage inspires my men, ${PLAYER}. With the wraith defeated, the Angmarim scurry in search of a new leader. We will attack them while they are at their weakest.'
The Keeper Garthamendir
Your journey with the Esteldín scout was not without peril, a sure sign that the Angmarim fear something far more terrible than death.
'Garthamendir will fall this day, I can feel it on the wind.'

Garthamendir guards the gates of Carn Dûm to the west.
Areneth warned you of the Cargûl and its terrible wrath. But killing the fell creature is the only way to break the Angmarim forces.

Areneth is at the eastern Ranger camp of Gath Forthnír.
Garthamendir was destroyed and his forces shattered. You should return to Areneth with the news.

'You have proven yourself to me, ${PLAYER}, and for that I will share something with you. A while ago, a company of Rangers and Hillmen led by a man named Golodir crossed Rammas Deluon. They were almost destroyed by the power of the watching stones, but many escaped.
'The survivors have established a camp far to the north of here in a place called Gath Forthnír. Perhaps you should go there. They may be able to use your aid.
'You are strong in your own way, and brave. Go with valour!'
'You have come from Gabilshathûr? Welcome, friend. Your aid is indeed welcome here.'
Onward to Gath Forthnír
The Captain of the Guard is impressed with your performance and believes he knows of someone who can use your aid.

Gath Forthnír is far to the north of Gabilshathûr.
The Captain of the Guard at Gabilshathûr told you that Golodir's army was not completely destroyed and has established a camp at Gath Forthnír. He suggested you journey to Gath Forthnír and offer your services to the Rangers.
Collected broken swords from Angmarim warriors (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected broken crossbows from Angmarim marksmen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I received word of reinforcements coming from the south. If this is true, they can help us strike out against Carn Dûm. We must make a show of strength to the Angmarim, lest they become emboldened and attack us before help arrives.
'Set out to the west, to Himbar, and defeat the Angmarim warriors and marksmen. Take their weapons and place them upon the altars scattered throughout Himbar. The Angmarim high-priests use these shrines to honour the Dark Lord of Mordor.
'Such a display will strike a blow to their morale and allow our friends the time they need to move north. You will find the Angmarim and their altars scattered across Himbar.'

'Thank you for helping us, friend. Perhaps there is still hope that we can win this war? The Angmarim are routed, but I fear they will soon find their strength and rally their forces.
'We must move with all due haste. My Rangers report that a scout from Esteldín needs our help.'

A Tenuous Thread
The Angmarim, servants of the Dark Lord, threaten the Rangers of Gath Forthnír.
'If we can strike fear into the black hearts of the Angmarim, they will not harry the movement of our allies to the south.'
'You defeated many Angarim, and that is good. Now show the others your prowess in battle by placing their broken arms on the altars.'

The Angmarim are to the west, near Carn Dûm.
Areneth said that a display of strength could break the spirits of the Angarim loyal to Mordor. He asked you to collect the weapons of those you defeat.

Angmarim altars can be found throughout Himbar, near the road or within the Angmarim camps.
Areneth said that a display of strength could break the spirits of the Angarim loyal to Mordor. He asked you to place the captured weapons upon the altars of the Angmarim as a form of intimidation.

The Rangers of Gath Forthnír wait for you at their camp to the east of Carn Dûm.

'So you wish to help us? Very well. We have been here a very long time, without sufficient supplies to carry us. Our tools are nearly rotted away.
'As much as it pains me to suggest it, I want you to enter an Orc-camp that lies to the northeast and burgle some of their tools. We need saws, axes, and picks.
'Gabilshathûr is in such a poor state of repair, and the threat of the Orc-host grows ever nearer.'

'Excellent work, ${CLASS}! These tools, though clearly the shoddy work of Orcs, will serve our purposes.
'Stay a moment...I may have something else for you to do.'
'We need those tools, ${RACE}! Go to the camp northeast of here and find us some!'

'Truly, we have many problems. Our most pressing concern is, of course, the Orc-army camped on our doorstep. If they should discover this place, we would be in dire straits. This is what concerns poor Avar the most, I think, this worry -- for there is little we can do against an army.
'Though a few of our skilled people may be able to slip by the enemy forces, taking terrible risks, we can hardly move all of our people past the armies of the Enemy -- so in effect we are trapped here.
'I'm sure that our guard-captain, Gisur, knows much more of these things than do I. He will be able to tell you if there is anything you can do to help us here.'

'You came here, alone, from the south? I suppose there is more to you than one would guess at a glance.
'Here, you can indeed be of some help to us. We wish to distract the Orcs here from our position. They have scouts and foragers in the lands north and east of here.
'If you can slay some of those Orcs, you would be providing a great distraction for us. The Orcs camped at Ongbíshuk to the north would no doubt turn their attention to the east, and perhaps we would have a bit of a breathing-space.'
'You have done well, but I fear that your efforts may come to naught, through no fault of your own.'

The mining-outpost of Gabilshathûr is in grave danger. An army of Orcs is not far away, and their scouts and stragglers must not be allowed to locate the dwarves.
'You should speak to Captain Gisur if you wish to help us here.'
'Please slay those Orcs. It is but a drop in the Sea as regards their numbers, but if we can distract them from this area we will have accomplished something, at least.'

The guard-captain Gisur is at Gabilshathûr.

There are Orcs at Ongbíshuk, north and east of the dwarf-outpost of Gabilshathûr.
