'Listen, I know this is a lot to ask, but you've done well for me so far, and I thought that maybe you could do one more thing for me. The only thing I can think of that might keep those Orcs off my land for a while is to raid their camp before they can gather their strength to attack again.
'One of my hands said he saw an Orc-camp to the south-west of my land. He said it was a pretty large camp, so you'll probably want to gather your friends again.
'If this works, I'll be mighty grateful!'

'What? You did it! Wonderful! You've saved me! Hooray!
'I know it's not much, but I want you to take this reward. You're a true hero, and there's no denying it!'
Defeat Dead-aim Ongbúrz in Gurzlum (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Grim Ongbúrz in Gurzlum (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Farmer Gatson has asked you to raid the Orc-camp to prevent them from gathering enough force to drive him off his land.
'I can't thank you enough for what you've done! You saved my farm!'
'Thanks to you, my farm and my workhands are safe!'

The Orc-camp is south-west of Gatson's fields.
Farmer Gatson is sure the Orcs will attack his farm again if they are not deterred first. He has asked you to gather friends and raid the Orcs' own camp before they have the chance to regroup.

'It seems there is, after all, one last farmer in the North Downs. A fellow named Gatson refuses to leave his land to the Orcs.
It may be that he still has grain to sell us. If you would, pay Gatson a visit to learn if this is true. Tell him we will pay him good silver for his produce.
'Gatson's farm is not too far south of the hills.'

'Aye, it's true, I had a rich harvest this year, and I'd gladly sell it off, if I could. I'd not done business with the dwarves in the past, because those Dourhands were nasty fellows, but now that Durin's Folk are in charge, I'd be more than willing to do business with them.
'Or rather, I should say, I would happily sell the grain if I still had it! Those cursed Orcs have raided my farm and taken most of the harvest. Alas, it looks like I will not be able to help you. Unless....'
The Dwarves of Othrikar are beset by supply troubles, stemming from the incursion of Orcs and Wargs from the north and the betrayal of the Dourhands.
'Plese go talk to the farmer Gatson to see about getting us some grain.'

Gatson's Farm is south of Othrikar in the plains below the hills.
Almost all of the farmers of the North Downs have abandoned their lands in the face of the Orc incursion. Hornbori learned that one, a man named Gatson, is refusing to leave, however. Hornbori has asked you to speak to Farmer Gatson about purchasing grain.
Collected grain sacks (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})

'There may just be a chance that you could help me and your dwarf-friends together. It seems to me that the stolen grain may still be at the Orcs' camp not far from here. If you can recover that grain for me, I'll be happy to offer it to the dwarves at half my normal price.
'The Orcs have a big camp to the south and west of here. I don't know where in the camp they would be keeping the stolen grain, but you should retrieve three large sacks.
'Bring me those sacks, and I'll see what I can do for the dwarves.'
'Aye, that's the grain. You've done a good job. Send these on to Othrikar, and tell their quartermaster, Hornbori, that he can send the payment another day.'
'Were you able to find the Orc camp? Did they have my grain?'

'Oh, so you had to get the grain yourself from the Orcs? Well, half-price is half-price! This Gatson sounds like an honest man. We'll do more business with him if we can -- if things don't get too much worse around here.
'Be that as it may be, you deserve an extra reward for fighting those Orcs. Please accept this silver with our gratitude!'
'Could you not get the grain from Gatson?'
Return the Grain Sacks to Gatson

'If you need to fight orcs to get us some grain, well, that just so much more to the good, eh?'
'You ought to bring that grain back to your Dwarf friends at Othrikar.'

Hornbori awaits your return at Othrikar.

This waggon has been plundered, its barrels and crates thrown and smashed, and their contents carried off. There is little to suggest what cargo the waggon might have carried, save for a small box of finely wrought spoons and knives, which you place in your pack.
It is certain that the waggon was waylaid by orcs, and that its owner will want to know what has become of his goods.

Jantson frowns. 'Seems I recall seeing a waggon pass from the north, nigh on six days ago. Must have been just before the Wargs came and the troubles down in Trestlebridge. Aye, I remember it, now. It was a dwarf waggon, with a dwarf driver, from their settlement in the north, and laden with goods of iron and silver!'
The farmer shakes his head. 'Bad luck the dwarves have, now as ever. The orcs must have happened upon that waggon even as they skulked towards Trestlebridge.'

'Filthy, skulking orcs! Poor Eldji, alone in a waggon, was easy prey for cowards. And this!' He shakes the box of silverware. 'This is all that remains of our handiwork!
'Woe that the blades and mail of the Dwarves should end in the hands of orcs. But the woe shall be theirs.' A pale light flickers in Torfi's eyes. Torfi glances back to you. 'Thank you, friend, for bringing this matter to me. I shall see that things are put to right.'
Torfi's eyes narrow. 'You bring news of my waggon's fate, but you bring no proof. What of this silverware you found? Did you not think to bring it hither?'
Inquire about the plundered waggon at Jantson's farm
Seek Torfi Hammerhorn and tell him of his waggon's fate

At an orc campsite, you happened upon a plundered waggon. All its goods had been stolen, except for a small box of finely-wrought silverware. The waggon's owner will surely want to know what has become of his goods.

These bones are smaller than those of a man, but heavy and strong. A few strings of cooked flesh still cling to them, and they bear gouges from orc teeth. The ends have been smashed, and the marrow sucked out.

'The dwarves' settlement lies to the north, in the hill-country. Never been there myself, but that's likely where you'll find the owner of that ill-fated waggon.'

The orcs smashed this barrel, which seems to have contained hunks of dried meat and bread. It was likely the food supply of the unfortunate driver. One of the broken planks bears a simple picture of a hammer, painted in grey.

The orcs smashed this barrel, which seems to have contained hunks of dried meat and bread. It was likely the food supply of the unfortunate driver. One of the broken planks bears a simple picture of a hammer, painted in grey.

'Listen, friend, we have problems here. Big problems. Those cursed Dourhands weren't content to ruin the operation of the mines while they were here, but when they left, they ruined or stole what food we had.
'Then there's Orcs and Wargs that came down from the north, driving the farmers who used to supply us out of their fields. And when we venture out of Othrikar, we have to do so in force, due to the Dourhands camped nearby. In short, we are having a lot of trouble with supplies.
'We need meat. I can give you a fee in good silver, if you could hunt some bears for us. They wander the hills to the south.'
'Good, good. That meat should last us quite a while. Thank you for your help, friend.
'It will take a lot of bear meat to feed the hungry miners.'

'You've done a good job for us with that bear-meat and the grain. You've proved yourself a friend to Othrikar. But now I have some grave and serious news, and I need to ask for your help once again.
'Before those blasted Dourhands left, they stole most of the yeast and poisoned the rest. You do know what that means, don't you? No beer! This is an outrage not to be borne!
'Morale around here is bad enough without running out of beer for our miners. I need you to go to the Dourhand camp north of here and get that yeast back!'

'Ah, yes, this is the stuff! Certainly enough to supply us for the winter!
'From now on, I'll see to it that all the dwarves in Othrikar remember you as the ${RACE} who saved their beer!'
'We need that yeast! Without it, we cannot brew anymore beer!'

The Dwarves of Othrikar are beset by supply troubles, stemming from the incursion of Orcs and Wargs from the north and the betrayal of the Dourhands.
'Aye, we'll be drinking to your name as soon as the beer's done brewing!'
'Thank you for your help, ${PLAYER}. I don't know how we would have managed our supply problems if you hadn't come!'

The stolen yeast is at the Dourhand camp north of Othrikar.
After you returned from Gatson's farm, Hornbori told you that the Dourhand dwarves had stolen or poisoned all of Othrikar's yeast, which threatens their supply of beer. He has asked you to rectify this outrage by recovering the stolen yeast.

'My people and the Jorthkyn, or Earth-kin in the tongue of southern Men, have been ever close. It was only with their aid that we weathered the first few years here in Othrikar. Since then they have always aided us dwarves in times of need.
'My cousin, Ragnarr Hornsounder, has gone to the Jorthkyn hunting camp, in the hills of eastern Nan Amlug, to learn more of their ways and bring our people closer together.
'It has been long since I have heard from Ragnarr. Seek him out in the camp of the Jorthkyn to the east, and if he is still well, deliver my words of concern to him.'

'Hornbori sent you, eh? Well your task is done. If you wish, return to him and tell him I am safe, for now. Or you could sit, and I would tell you what happened. If Hornbori trusted you to safely trek through the Nan Amlug alone you may be of use to us.
Common Blood
Hornbori's cousin, Ragnarr Hornsounder, has journeyed to the camp of the Earth-kin in Nan Amlug. Hornbori is concerned because he has received no word from his cousin.
'I have still not heard from Ragnarr. Have you not travelled to the Jorthkyn camp yet?'
'You have spoken to my cousin Ragnarr it is good to hear he is alive, if not well. My aunt would not let me live if something foul were to happen to him.'

Ragnarr Hornsounder is at the Earth-kin camp along the western mountains in eastern Nan Amlug, east of Othrikar.
Hornbori has asked you to find his cousin in the Earth-kin camp and make sure he is still safe.
Collected Aurochs Skull

'The Jorthkyn have always been a mystery of sorts; helping my people without asking for payment. I came here to live among them so that our people could know each other better.
'This group is all that remains of a hunting party from beyond the Ram Dúath. After crossing the pass, their First Hunter turned on them, throwing the party into chaos.
'I am still a stranger and not fully trusted, especially after this recent betrayal. I will need to gain their trust again. I understand their tribal totem is the aurochs. When the First hunter's group turned, they took one of the totem skulls. I have seen a totem shrine among the hills north-east from here. Collect this skull for me so that I might win the trust of the tribe.'
'This is good, you have done fine but...well, I might have made a mistake....'
'The Jorthkyn are still unsure of my intentions; you must bring me that aurochs skull.'
Bring the aurochs skull to Ragnarr.
Collect the Aurochs Skull
A Token of Worth
Ragnarr Hornsounder went to live among the Earth-kin, but a recent betrayal has made the Earth-kin distrustful.

The aurochs skull can be found in the Warg territory to the north-east of the Earth-kin camp.
In order to regain the trust of the Earth-kin, Ragnarr Hornsounder has asked you to collect an aurochs skull from the totem in the hills of eastern Nan Amlug and return it to him at the Earth-kin camp. A group of Wargs currently roam this territory.
You return the skull of the Great Aurochs

'I seem to have misunderstood the Jorthkyn. The skull that was taken by the First Hunter was not just any aurochs skull, but the skull of the Great Aurochs -- the namesake of their tribe, Suuri-lehmä.
'This skull has been a symbol of the tribe's hunters for generations. If you could retrieve this totem it would prove my purpose is pure and without ill intent.
'Go to the camps of the traitorous Jorthkyn -- the Rauta-lehmä -- eastward across the Nan Amlug. That is where the skull of The Great Aurochs has been taken. Look for a place of reverence or altar, for even these lowly curs could not have abandoned all they once held dear. You should take allies, for the land is dangerous, and the skull will be difficult to carry.'
'The gift of their returned totem will surely win the trust of the Jorthkyn! My thanks to you.'
Collect the skull of the Great Aurochs
Heritage Restored

When First Hunter Jarkko betrayed the Suuri-lehmä, he left with the totem of the tribe's hunter; the skull of the Great Aurochs -- the namesake of the Suuri-lehmä. You brought a totem skull to Ragnarr, but it appears that it is not sufficient.
'Have you not found the skull yet? I'm very sorry about the last incident. I promise, if you do this for me, I'll not ask another favour of you.'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}! The return of the Great Aurochs skull has gained me great favour with the Elder and has shown my true purpose here.'
'It is said that dwarves and Jorthkyn are actually related!'
'As Elder, I am shamed, Our hearts were shadowed by the betrayal of Jarkko. His falseness made us distrust Ragnarr.'
'Because of you, ${RACE} from afar, we will trust Ragnarr Hornsounder.'

The skull of The Great Aurochs is being held in the lands of the Rauta-lehmä, eatsward across Nan Amlug.
In order to prove his benign intent to the Earth-kin, Ragnarr Hornsounder has asked you to retrieve the stolen skull of The Great Aurochs from the Rauta-lehmä. He suggested taking allies.

Ragnarr Hornsounder is at the camp of the Suuri-lehmä, west of the Rauta-lehmä camp.
You should return the skull of the Great Aurochs to Ragnarr Hornsounder.
You have escorted the aurochs-yearling to safety

'Everyone on a farm needs to pull their own weight, even fancy strangers out o' the south. We've got our hands full here dealing with the harvest and worrying about them Orcs nearby.
'Anyways, Master Gatson's little herd of cattle could use some new blood. Wild aurochs would do nicely, but the bulls are far too aggressive to drive into the pasture. So what I want you to do is to pick out a good-looking yearling from the wild aurochs herd not far to the south-east.
'A young aurochs should be pretty docile...just don't get in the way of any of the bulls and you should be fine. And, oh yes, I've seen some Orcs out there lately, so be careful of them too, hear me?'
'That's a fine job, a right fine job, I say! Thanks for your help with that there aurochs. Master Gatson asked me to give you this small payment for your work.'
The young aurochs lows plaintively and runs off ahead of you.
Find an aurochs-yearling

Farmer Gatson's farmhand, Gilmar, says that new blood is needed for the cattle herd. An aurochs-bull would do nicely, but the wild bulls are far too aggressive to drive to his pasture. Gilmar has asked you to obtain a yearling instead.
'An aurochs-yearling's just the thing we need to revive the herd. I saw a wild herd with a yearling the other day, just over the hill there.'
'Yearlings spook easily. It's best to keep him somewhere quiet. Don't you worry though, he'll be running about soon enough.'
'If ye want to prove your worth round here you'll go get that Aurochs for me? Thankee kindly.'
'Ah, it's true the Orc raids have whittled the herd to almost nothing. An aurochs-yearling would go a long way to bringing it back.'
'Good work herding that yearling. You let Gilmar know you're back, he's been fretting since you left.'
'I guess I was wrong about you. You done some good, hard work.'
'Things been rough with just Alwin and me left to mind the farm and them Orcs all about. I'm sorry for thinking you was a bit shifty when ye first showed up.'

Aurochs yearlings can be found amidst the small herd to the south-east of Gatson's farm.
Gilmar, Gatson's farmhand, has asked you to pick out an aurochs-yearling from the local herd and drive it over to his pasture.

Gilmar is back on Gatson's farm.
You have brought the aurochs-yearling to Gatson's pasture, now you should return to Gilmar to tell him of your success.

Stamped across the front of this book is the title, 'Of Arthedain and its Settlements.' The book's cover is worn, as if many hands have held it. It opens easily to a dog-eared page, which reads:
'...In those days, north-eastern Arthedain was dominated by five great settlements, known commonly as The Five Towns. These were Henneth Rhún, south of Fornost; Duintham, astride an ancient stream; Carnoglin, in the northern hills; Ost Ardúlin, in the lake-lands; and Dolindîr, now called Esteldín.'
'Amongst the Rangers of the North Downs, we encourage our people to visit all five of the Towns and discover the locations of their Founding Stones. It is important to remember who we are....'

The monument's face is inscribed with faded words:
Carnoglin
Founded in the name of Malvegil, King of Arthedain. With the skill of Thorhaddur the Dwarf and his kindred was this town built.
'United in purpose, may Dwarves and Men be ever bonded in friendship.'

This old monument is well kept, and is free of dirt and vines. Upon its face is an inscription:
'Here once stood the town and Founding Stone of Dolindîr, in the kingdom of Arthedain, which has passed.
'In this place was established the refuge of Esteldín, by Arassuil, son of Arahad, that these lands might never again stand unwatched.'

The monument's face is inscribed with faded words:
Duintham
Founded in the year 1249 of the Third Age.
'At this place did King Celebrindor establish the Town of Duintham, that his people might cultivate the land and feed the people of his realm.'

The monument's face is inscribed with faded words:
Henneth Rhún
Established in the first year of the reign of Araphor, son of Arveleg.
'Folk shall gather where commerce thrives.'

The face of this monument is marred by what appear to be large tooth-marks, as if several man-like creatures decided to gnaw upon the stone.
Though most of the writing has been destroyed, you can discern the words 'Ost Ardúlin' at the top of the monument, and at the bottom the phrase, 'that we might retreat from our cares, and take solace in such beauty.'

'So, you have found that old journal?' Istuienn arches an eyebrow. 'It is not customary for those not of the Rangers to do so, but if you wish to know more about my kindred, you may want to undertake the journey yourself.'
'This first of the settlements mentioned in the book was called Dolindîr, today we call it Esteldín.'
'Return to me after you have found the Founding Stone of Dolindîr, and we will speak further.'

'Ah, I see you have chosen to begin the journey, very well then.'
'The book speaks of five towns which were Henneth Rhún, south of Fornost; Duintham, astride an ancient stream; Carnoglin, in the northern hills; Ost Ardúlin, in the lake-lands; and Dolindîr, now called Esteldín.'
'You have seen the Founding Stone of Dolindîr, now seek you the other four.'

'Really? You made the circuit of all five towns? I am impressed; I had not really expected you to make the attempt.'
'We often assign novice Rangers this task, as the beasts that lair in such places make such exploration dangerous indeed. Perhaps the Rangers will be able to make further use of your skills in the future.'

Find the Stone of Henneth Rhún

'Remember, the book says the five towns were Henneth Rhún, south of Fornost; Duintham, astride an ancient stream; Carnoglin, in the northern hills; Ost Ardúlin, in the lake-lands; and Dolindîr, now called Esteldín.'

'This water appears to addle the senses but does little else. The Rangers here stated that the water is deadly poison. Perhaps they refer to the western pools?
'If their words are true, collecting the water from the western pools will prove most hazardous. You must be careful lest a single drop touch your skin. The stuff is deadly poison and will stop your heart in your chest.
'Venture back to Imlad Balchorth and draw water from the poisonous, roiling pathes of the western pools. It may provide the answers I seek.'
'Even the smell of the water is enough to cause illness, it seems. I have some thoughts about this water, but there is only one way to bear them out.'
'Where are the phials?'

Discovering the Source
The pools of Imlad Balchorth are noxious pits of foul water. No one knows if the corruption stems from the Enemy's industry or from a more sinister source.
'Draw water from the patches of roiling water that lay in the western parts of Imlad Balchorth. Beware the water is quite dangerous!'

The pools of Imlad Balchorth are to the south of Himbar.
The waters in the western parts of Imlad Balchorth are infused with deadly poison, and Fimreg wishes to determine the cause.

Fimreg is in Gath Forthnír, north and east of Imlad Balchorth.
Your phials are filled with the deadly water from the roiling pools of Imlad Balchorth.
Collected a bony hook

'There are many creatures in Angmar that carry venom or poisonous blood in their veins. But even so, how could all the water be affected so? Could something have spawned in the bowels of Carn Dûm? Something monstrous and poisonous to all life?
'You must travel upstream to discover the source of the corruption. To Urugarth you must go and find evidence of such a creature. It would have to be a large beast, such are the amounts of poison in the water.
'The waters flow from Carn Dûm's sewers down a waterfall into Urugarth. Perhaps you will find something of note where the waters run fastest?'
'It is worse than I feared. This is no ordinary beast we face.'
'What have you found?'
Search Urugarth for the creature poisoning the water
Bring the bony-hook to Fimreg
Further Upstream
Fimreg studied the properties of the water you collected and believes that the source is tainted by something beyond mere machines of industry.
'Go into Urugarth and search for some evidence of the creature fouling these waters. Search near where the waters run from Carn Dûm into Urugarth.'

Urugarth is to the west of Gath Forthnír and north of Imlad Balchorth.
Fimreg believes that a large creature of some kind is poisoning the waters. If such a beast exists, proof of it will be found upstream in Urugarth.

Fimreg is at Gath Forthnír, in eastern Himbar, east of Urugarth.
You found a curious bony hook, like a claw or beak but not resembling part of any animal you have ever encountered before.

'Have you witnessed the foul waters that flow from Carn Dûm? In the past months, we have seen the waters from Urugarth become dark and rank with the smell of decay, but we cannot fathom the reason.
'We must learn more of these waters and the maladies that they cause as they flow into Imlad Balchorth. Here, take this phial and return to me with samples of the water. Please combine 5 drams of this foul water into a single phial.
'You should first draw water from the roiling patches in the pools in the eastern parts of Imlad Balchorth. The waters there cloud the minds and bind the tongues of those who come upon them.'
'Excellent. I will study this water and attempt to glean what knowledge I can from it. We still have much work to do.'
'Where are the water samples?'

Foul Waters
The pools of Imlad Balchorth are noxious pits of foul water. No one knows if the corruption stems from the Enemy's industry or from a more sinister source.
'Make your way to the eastern parts of Imlad Balchorth and draw water from the roiling patches of water in the pools you find there.'

Imlad Balchorth's pools are to the south of Himbar.

Your phials are filled with water from the roiling pools of the Imlad Balchorth.
Defeated Helchgam

'A tooth, perhaps? Or the hooked beak of some bird? Oh, if only it were so, ${PLAYER}. Imagine a half-dozen arms, lined with hundreds of these like teeth with which to grasp its prey. And a hungry maw that spits poison and breathes decay.
'There are tales of this creature, a loathesome eater of carrion. Helchgam, the Watcher. Such a beast will be hard to kill, but kill it you must, for left unchecked, it will continue to feed and grow.
'If you only found traces of its spoor in Urugarth, it must lurk in the waters north of there, somewhere within the sewers beneath Carn Dûm. This creature must be defeated. I would ask that you do this.'
'The beast's corruption will take many years to abate, but with its death, we can be sure that the poisoned waters may yet run clean once more.'
Defeat Helchgam
Heart of the Waters
In searching for the source of the poisoned waters, you found a strange bony hook and showed it to Firmeg.
'The only way to stop the poisoning of the water is to journey into Carn Dûm and defeat Helchgam itself! It is a dangerous task, but one that must be done, I fear.'

Helchgam lurks in the waters of Carn Dûm, beyond the gates to the west of Himbar.
Firmeg revealed the source of the poison to be a many-armed creature she called Helchgam.

Firmeg is in Gath Forthnír to the far-east of Himbar.
You travelled far into Carn Dûm and slew the dread beast known as Helchgam.

'This next task you cannot succeed at alone, or even with your Fellowship. Nay, you must assemble a war-party if you are to defeat Bogbereth.
'No ordinary creature is she, Bogbereth, the Poisoned Queen of Himbar. You must strike swift and true against her, for her hide is as steel armour and her fangs are keen-edged daggers, dripping venom.
'Assemble your band of heroes and journey back to where you fought her broodlings. You will find her there, unless she finds you first.'
'The great beast is fallen? Then her poisonous reign is ended. This has been another blow to the Iron Crown and the forces of Angmar, and we owe it all to you and your compatriots.'
Raid: Bogbereth
Lunathron told you of a great, vile spider, Bogbereth, which hunts in Himbar.
'Have you assembled your war-band yet? Bogbereth will not fall without a fight, and despite your courage, you are no threat to her by yourself.'

Bogbereth hunts in the north-eastern reaches of Himbar.
Lunathron cautioned you not to face Bogbereth with anything less than a fully-armed war-party. She must be defeated, lest she continues to spawn more of her foul brood.

Gath Forthnír is in the easternmost part of Himbar.
Lunathron bade you destroy the great spider, Bogbereth. Now that she is no more, you can return to claim your victory.

'There is a great spider that lurks in Himbar. Her eggs are prized by the Iron Crown, as the hatchlings can be trained by the Angmarim to fight for the Enemy.
'You must kill the spiders and the Angmarim spider-keepers north-east of Himbar. When facing the broodlings, beware. They can burrow into the earth and escape your attacks.
'You must exercise caution while hunting the spiders. Bogbereth stalks those lands, and she may be hunting you as well.'
'Well done, ${CLASS}, but there is one threat that still remains. I speak of the great spider herself, Bogbereth.'

Bogbereth's Brood
Bogbereth the Spider is in league with the Iron Crown. Her progeny is kept by the Angmarim and used as many-legged foot-soldiers.
'The spiders are a threat and must be stopped. Defeat them and their Angarim keepers.'

The spiders and their keepers are to the north-east of Himbar.
Lunathron told you of Bogbereth's spawn, the spider-broodlings that are kept by the Angmarim.

You slew many spiders and their Angmarim keepers, ensuring that Bogbereth's spawn pose no threat to the Rangers.
Destroyed drake-eggs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Gorma tells me that you aim to slay the drake-queen. A noble quest, and I wish you good hunting. But killing the drake-queen is a temporary solution to a much greater problem.
'If left unchecked, her brood of eggs will hatch, and one of her drakelings will grow to take her place. You should destroy her eggs and make sure that nothing exists to inherit her legacy as the Scourge of Urugarth.
'Continue on your quest to Urugarth. It lies far to the west.'
'The eggs are destroyed, yes? That is good. The young drakes are not as powerful as the queen, but they are just as vicious.'
Destroy drake-eggs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Matron's Brood
The drake-queen rules the wilds of Urugarth, spawning broods of drakelings that ravage the countryside.
'Go into Urugarth and destroy the eggs of the drake-queen.'

The drake-queen and her brood of eggs lies in Urugarth to the west.
Húriel advised you to destroy the eggs of the drake-queen.

Return to Húriel in Gath Forthnír to the east.
The eggs were destroyed, ensuring that nothing would take the drake-queen's place in Urugarth.

'There is a great drake-queen which must be slain within Urugarth.
'She is a creature of fierce intelligence and will attempt to evade you. Turn your weapons against her young drakelings and that may goad her into action.
'The fortress of Urugarth lies to the west.'
'The great drake-queen is no more? Then you are truly a ${CLASS} of renown. We shall sing of your deeds this night!'
Quenching the Flames
The drake-queen rules the wilds of Urugarth, spawning broods of drakelings that ravage the countryside.
'Go to Urugarth and slay the drake-queen.'

Travel to the west into Urugarth and kill the drake-queen.

Gath Forthnír lies to the east.
You defeated the drake-queen. Now you should return to Gormal and tell him of your accomplishment.

'Uruks are loathesome, vicious creatures without a shred of honour or courage...only a mindless rage and a lust for blood.
'Their general is no different, save for the fervour of his hatred. He serves the Iron Crown without question and leads his army into battle without mercy. Defeat him, and you will prove your mettle.
'You will find him in the deepest heart of Urugarth to the west.'
'So, it is done. It will not bring back the slain, but it will perhaps give me peace knowing my people have been avenged.'
Ending Terror
You defeated many Orcs in Urugarth, but your task is not yet complete. The Uruk-leader remains.
'Go into Urugarth and defeat their general.'

The leader of the Orc-army makes his home deep within Urugarth to the west.
Donaith told you of a mighty Uruk-general that must be defeated.

Gath Forthnír is far to the east, past Himbar.
Donaith asked you to kill the Uruk-general, which you did after a fierce battle. You should return to Gath Forthnír and tell Donaith the good news.
Defeated Krahjarn Uruks in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Krahjarn Orcs in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It sickens me to know that my people are threatened by the Evil Ones. And what can I do about it? In my youth, perhaps...but time and the rigours of travel across Rammas Deluon have robbed me of my vigour.
'Ah, but you are strong and brave, yes? Brave enough to stand against the Orcs and thin out their accursed ranks?
'Travel to their fortifications to the west. There, in a place called Urugarth, you will find your share of Orcs. Any blow we strike against the False King will help my people survive to see another day.'
'You possess the kind of fighting spirit I recall from my younger days, but your task is not yet complete, ${PLAYER}. The Uruk-leader still lives, does he not?'
Defeat Krahjarn Uruks in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Krahjarn Orcs in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Thinning the Horde
The Hillman called Donaith is concerned about the Orcs in the vicinity of Urugarth.
'Go into Urugarth and thin the Orc-hordes.'

Urugarth is far to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Donaith asked you to support the cause of his people and defeat the Orc-troops which gather in Urugarth.

Donaith can be found at Gath Forthnír.
Return to Donaith in eastern Angmar and tell him of your deeds.

'My brothers and I have not seen our uncle for many years. Rammas Deluon prevents safe passage to the lands beyond, and Uncle Donaith lives far to the east.
'If you find yourself in those distant lands, perhaps you may pay Uncle Donaith a visit? I am sure he would want to hear from us. It has been a long time, and much has happened in his absence.
'I do not know where he is now, only that he dwells far in the east.'

'It is good to meet you as well, ${PLAYER}. And you bring news from Aughaire? What a journey that must have been! And how did you pass through Rammas Deluon?
'Ah, but it matters not. Tell me, how do my nephews fare?'
A Distant Uncle
Rammas Deluon prevents the brothers Eilig, Machar, and Torquil from seeing their uncle Donaith, who lives far in the east of Angmar.

Donaith is somewhere far to the east of Aughaire, well beyond Rammas Deluon.
Eilig and his brothers in Aughaire wish you to find their long-lost uncle.

'The Orc-chieftain Nûlthauk is dead...so now it is Ranghâsh, the War-master of the Tarkrîp, who must be slain.
'All that remains now is to cut the orcs off from their last vestiges of strength,and our vengeance will be complete.
Be warned however - Ranghâsh is not like the other orcs you have faced - his is of Uruk blood, and far stronger. You may need the help of fellows to overcome him!
The Tarkrîp are just north of Tór Gailvin - seek out their cave there.'
'Thank you, friend, for helping us fulfil our vengeance! The dread Ranghâsh has been slain for his crimes and my heart rests easier for it.'
Dark Vengeance
Eilig and his brothers Machar and Torquil are seeking vengeance against Orc-raiders who slew their kin.
'You must slay Ranghâsh, the Orc-leader who murdered our kin!'
'Thehead has been cut from the serpent, and our kindred now rest in peace.'

The Tarkrîp are just north of Tór Gailvin - seek out their cave there.
Eilig has asked you to slay the Uruk-warmaster, Ranghâsh, who led the Uruks who slew his kindred.

Eilig is back at Aughaire.
Ranghâsh is dead, so you should return to Eilig to tell him the tale of your deeds.

'My brothers and I thirst for revenge against Orcs and Uruks who slew our kin. One seeks mindless vengeance, while the other seeks restitution - neither understands our foes truly. Orcs are cowards at heart, fighting only when driven by stern and heartless leaders. If we are to know peace again, then these leaders must be felled before they drive their hordes upon us once again.
It is the ones who led the raid who must be slain. The Ongburz chieftain Nûlthauk can be found deep within their cave north of here. Destroy him and the driving power behind the orcs will be shattered for a time.'
'So, you have slain Nûlthauk? This was a deed well done! But there is more yet for you to do to complete our vengeance.'
Deep Vengeance
Eilig and his brothers Machar and Torquil are seeking vengeance against Orc-raiders who slew their kin.
'You must slay Nûlthauk, the Orc who led his minions when they slew our kin!'

The Orc-cave is north of Aughaire, just east of Dûn Covád.
Eilig has asked you to slay the Ongburz Chieftain, Nûlthauk who led the Orcs who slew his kindred.

Eilig is back at Aughaire.
Nûlthauk is dead, so you should return to Eilig to tell him the tale of your deeds.
Collected silver-nuggets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So, young Torquil believes that a few orc corpses will satisfy the misdeeds against our bloodline does he? Bah. He has always been a simpleton.
'The numbers of the orcs are like grains of sand upon the sea, and they care not at all for the loss of a few of their number -- but their black hearts are full of greed, and it is there that I would stab at them!
'I say, go into their caves and claim weregild for the deaths of my kin. The Orcs are paid in silver by the Angmarim. Collect that silver and bring it back, and perhaps the spirits of my kindred will be appeased. The Orcs value their ill-gotten gains more than their own lives, so expect that they have hidden it away deep within their caves.'
'Silver smeared with Orc-blood! It is good! But there is more still to be done.'
'You must collect weregild for the deaths of my kindred!'
Bring the silver-nuggets back to Machar

'The silver goes to lay our kin to rest. But there is more weregild yet to collect. As Torquil no doubt told you, the Tarkrîp were also allied with the Ongbúrz during their raid.
'I would have you reclaim the gold which they stole from us during their raid, so that it may restitute those who were bereft of family. You may find the Tarkrîp at the cave they call Burzum Pushdug, north of Tór Gailvin.'
'Gold of the Tarkrîp! You have done very well indeed. Now the spirits of my family can rest, satisfied with our vengeance.'
'You must collect weregild for the deaths of my kindred!'
Bring the gold-dust back to Machar

Hidden Hoard
Machar and his brothers Torquil and Eilig are seeking vengeance against Orc-raiders who slew their kin.

'The punishment of the orcs has appeased my kindred.'

'My brothers and I thirst for vengeance, yet we cannot agree how to take it, save that we all agree on the need for revenge! Our kin were slain by the Ongbúrz Orcs, who serve the evil Men of Carn Dûm.
'I say go into their lairs and slay them, one and all. The Ongbúrz came from a cave north of Aughaire, it's just east of Dûn Covád.
'Will you do this for me?'
'Ha. You have spilled rivers of Ongbúrz blood! I am pleased, and I hope my brothers are as well. But there is more yet to do.'
Dark Raiders
Torquil and his brothers Machar and Eilig are seeking vengeance against Orc-raiders who slew their kin.
'You must slay more Orcs. My family's shades cry out for vengeance!'

The lair of the Ongbúrz is just east of Dûn Covád, north of Aughaire.

Torquil is back at Aughaire, south of Dûn Covád.

You have done well for us. I am greatly pleased with you. But there is more yet to do. The Ongbúrz who slew my family were allied with the nearby Tarkrîp tribe. Their cave is just to the north of Tór Gailvin.
'They too must feel the bite of our vengeance!'
'You have slain many of the Tarkrîp and I am well-pleased. Nothing can bring my kindred back to me, but at least the killers have paid for their crimes!'
Dark Hunters
Torquil and his brothers Machar and Eilig are seeking vengeance against Orc-raiders who slew their kin.
'You must slay the Tarkrîp. My family's shades cry out for vengeance!'
'The blood of the slayers will calm the anger of my slain kin. Thanks be to you, friend.'
'The death-cries of the murdering Orc-kind shall sing to the spirits of my kin.'

The lair of the Tarkrîp is just north of Tór Gailvin.
Torquil, seeking vengeance for the deaths of his kin, has asked you to slay them.

Torquil is back at Aughaire.
You have slain many Tarkrîp orcs and should now return to Torquil to claim your reward.

'I cannot believe that someone has come to my aid. I thought this nightmare would never end. My mother is Osbail, perhaps you have heard of her? It has been such a long time without my loved ones.
'Please help me return to her. I fear that I cannot make it back on my own.'
'My Dírdrë is safe? Oh, thank you, thank you, Southron!'

Osbail waits for her daughter's safe return to the east in Gath Forthnír.
