You returned Dírdrë to the Hillmen. You should speak with Osbail, her mother, at once.
Freed slaves in Carn Dûm (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'${CLASS}, you must help me. My people are gone, spirited away by the Orc-slavers of Carn Dûm.
'These slavers raid our villages and take our best warriors away to toil in their work camps. Chained and shackled, they are forced to labour for the False King. Those that become injured or fall ill are left to die.'
'My husband Erscin is among the captured slaves, if he even still lives and breathes. Please hurry! The city lies far to the west.'
'Thank you for doing this. My people will never forget your bravery. But please, tell me...did you find Erscin? Be he living or dead, I must know what happened to him.'
Free slaves in Carn Dûm (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Lifting the Yoke
Carn Dûm is the evil heart of Angmar, a terrible city protected by gates and hordes of Orc-warriors.
'You must free my people from Carn Dûm.'

Carn Dûm lies far to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Osbail's husband Erscin and his fellow warriors were captured by Orcs and taken to Carn Dûm. The woman has asked you to enter Carn Dûm and rescue Erscin.

Osbail is at Gath Forthnír, far to the east of Carn Dûm.
The slaves of Carn Dûm were set free and may now return to their homes, but you were unable to find Osbail's husband, Erscin. You should return to Osbail with the news.
Found Dírdrë

'Could it be that my Dírdrë still lives?
'It may be too much to hope for, but if you did not see her in Carn Dûm, perhaps they took her into Nan Gurth?'
'Please go west and search for her there.'
Find Dírdrë
My Heart's Hope
The bracelet you found belonged to a girl of the Hillmen called Dírdrë. Her mother wonders if she could still be alive.

Dírdrë might be found in Nan Gurth, west of Gath Forthnír.
Osbail's daughter was taken from her many years ago. It could be that Dírdrë still lives.
You escorted Erscin to safety

'My husband remains in Carn Dûm. I know you have already done so much, but please...find it in your heart to help me once more.
'Erscin is strong of back and force of will. I cannot imagine that he fell to the Orcs, though perhaps he tried to escape and was killed. I cannot bear to imagine such things.
'If he lives, I fear he will not live long. I am sure that the Evil Ones will punish any slaves that remained behind. You must return to Carn Dûm and find him!'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for rescuing me. I must return now to my wife. She will be worried that I have left her.
'You may continue on. I know the way from here. Be well, friend.'
'My dear husband has returned to me! Thank you, Southron, for all you have done!'
'Thank you, stranger. Whoever you are, I can see you are no Orc-friend. Let us depart this evil place. And please, whatever you do, do not wake the Gorthorog!'
Find Erscin
Speak to Erscin
The Strongest Back
The slaves of Carn Dûm were set free, but Osbail, a woman of the Hillmen dwelling at Gath Forthnír, is still missing her husband.
'Please, return to Carn Dûm and find Erscin!'

Carn Dûm lies far to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Osbail begged you to find her missing husband, the Hillman-warrior called Erscin.

Erscin is at Carn Dûm, far to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Erscin is waiting to speak with you again.

Osbail is at Gath Forthnír, far to the east of Carn Dûm.
You found Erscin, alive and well within Carn Dûm and returned him to safety. You should now return to Osbail and let her know the good tidings.
Defeated trolls in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'No doubt you're here at the behest of my cousin. But as you've experience in these matters, let me explain the situation.
'Long have my brethren and I suffered the trolls of Angmar, the Gertheryg. We must strike a blow against Angmar by defeating these creatures and their master.
'The fortress-city of Urugarth is their stronghold. Cross the great valley of Himbar, west of here, and pass the evil statues that guard the pass into Rhunendin. High atop Rhunendin you will find the Gate of Shadows, fell entrance to Carn Dûm. Beyond the Gate, the path leads southwest across a narrow bridge, and soon turns east to Urugarth -- or so it is said.'
'You have done well, but there is more to do. The leader of the Gertheryg must be slain now.'
Defeat trolls in Urugarth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Moving Mountains
You journeyed north to Gath Forthnír, a camp of Golodir's Rangers, after assisting Hwati with his problems.
'Go into Urugarth and kill trolls and their leader. Cross Himbar into Rhunendin, climb to the Gate of Shadows, and follow the paths southwest until they turn at last east to Urugarth.'

Urugarth lies west of Gath Forthnír, across Himbar and beyond the Gate of Shadows that lies atop Rhunendin.
Táni asked you to seek out the trolls and their leader and slay them all.

Táni waits for news of the trolls' demise east of Urugarth, in Gath Forthnír.
With the trolls and their leader slain, it is time to return to Táni.

'I can see why Hwati sent you all the way up here to help us. You did good back there against the trolls but you've more work to do.
'The Gertheryg of Carn Dûm are commanded by a vile fiend called Barashal. You must return and slay him.
'Barashal won't go down without a fight, so be sure to rest up before you head out west into Carn Dûm.'
'A great hero is what you are! A few more like you, and we can surely turn the tide against the Enemy!'
Lord of the Gertheryg
You fought the trolls of Urugarth but the leader of the Gertheryg remains a threat.
'Go into Carn Dûm and defeat Barashal, the leader of the Gertheryg.'

Carn Dûm lies far to the west of Gath Forthnír.
Táni was impressed by your efforts to purge the trolls and sent you on another mission: to kill the leader of the Gertheryg.

Táni is at Gath Forthnír, far to the east of Carn Dûm.
You defeated the Lord of the Gertheryg in battle.

'My cousin Táni is facing similar troubles up north. It's the camp of some Men... Rangers, to be exact. If you can help him as you did us, well that would be most appreciated.
'It's a long journey but not without reward. Táni and his allies will pay for your troubles, I'm sure.
'Head to the north. You best steer clear of the Orc camps and keep to the rocks. The camp is called Gath Forthnír and it's in the north-east of Angmar.'
'And how is Hwati? I haven't seen him in many a day. Ah, but there's time for talk when the work is done, eh?'
The Northern Cousin
Hwati's cousins to the north in Gath Forthnír have their own problems with trolls and Gothrog.

Travel to Gath Forthnír in the north-east of Angmar and speak to Hwati's cousin, Táni.
Hwati spoke to you of a cousin living in a Ranger camp to the north. This cousin needed help with a troll problem.

'From what you have told me, I think that we dwarves would not be safe in the east unless the evil Gertheryg who rule Maethad were to be completely destroyed. I must ask you to again venture into the Arena, this time to defeat several of the Gorthorog-champions which can be found there.
'I would not venture into Maethad alone.'
'Your strength and valour is great, indeed! You have defeated great and terrible foes, but it seems that one last foe remains to be dealt with....'
Champions of the Arena
Hwati told you of the Gorthorg-champions who guard Maethad and of their terrible strength.
'We cannot secure a retreat from this place unless the path to the east is made safe.'

Maethad is north and east of Gabilshathûr.
Hwati asked you to gather your comrades once again and go to Maethad to defeat the Gorthorog champions who rule the area.

Hwati is back at Gabilshathûr.
The three Gorthorog-champions have been defeated, but it seems that there is one greater still left to be dealt with. You should return to Hwati to tell him what you have learned.
You found Maethad
Felwarden defeated

'Now that the Orcs know where we are, this place may be too dangerous for us. But we have nowhere else to go. We have considered moving east, away from the Orc-camps, but it seems there is another terrible threat in that region. A place called Maethad, sometimes known as the Arena.
'This valley is guarded by old fortifications, and it is inhabited by trolls...and worse, by the masters of troll-kind called Gertheryg. It is hard to know how dangerous they are, though, for some trolls, evil though they all may be, are reclusive, and others are not as strong as their size might suggest. Yet we cannot send dwarves to challenge them, because we must remain on guard against another orc-attack.
'I would ask you to assemble a party of your friends and find the Maethad. If you are successful, perhaps we may consider the east as an option for flight if the whole Orc-army descends upon us. There are Gorthorog Felwardens that guard the entrance to Maethad. If you can defeat one of these foes we will be able to proceed.'
'It is good that you were successful, but from what you said, it may be that the monsters who rule Maethad are too strong for us to risk flight in their direction.'
Find the arena known as Maethad
Defeat the Gorthorog Felwarden
Into the Arena
To the north-east of Gabilshathûr is a place infested with trolls and their Gorthorog masters, which the dwarves call the Arena.

Maethad is north and east of Gabilshathûr.
Hwati has asked you to find the arena called Maethad and defeat the Gorthorog Felwarden that guards the entrance.

Hwati is back at Gabilshathûr.
Having slain the trolls and the Gorthorog-gatekeeper, you should return to Hwati to tell him how the fighting went.

'From what your past foes have said, there is one last mighty Gorthorog to be defeated: Khurrákh, the Master of the Arena himself!
'It seems that this terrible creature is often called to Carn Dûm to render service to his masters there, but if he hears that his lieutenants have been defeated, I have no doubt he will soon return to Maethad.
'I will ask you for one more great service, ${PLAYER}: assemble your friends once again and return to Maethad. I expect that the great central tower is where the Master of the Arena resides when he is present.'

'Truly, you have achieved a great triumph! With Khurrákh defeated, we will have little to fear of the scattered trolls in the area should we be forced to flee our holdings here.
'You have done very well for us, indeed. I only wish I could give you a greater reward, but you will understand that this is all I can offer.'
Master of the Arena
You have learned that the mightiest Gorthorog of Maethad, Khurrákh, the Master of the Arena himself, remains alive.
'Find and defeat Khurrákh, the Master of the Arena.'
'Only the greatest of heroes could have defeated the Master of the Arena!'

Maethad is north and east of Gabilshathûr. Khurrákh, the Master of the Arena, may be found in the central tower.
Hwati has asked you and your comrades to return to Maethad to defeat the Master of the Arena himself. Hwati suggested you look for the central tower and defeat Khurrákh there.

Hwati is back at Gabilshathûr.
Having defeated the Master of the Arena, you should return to Hwati to tell him the tale of your deeds.
Collected weapons from weapon-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our stores of weapons run low, and we lack the materials to craft more. Without proper weapons, our cause seems hopeless. Unless....
'Yes! I have an idea. We can pillage the supplies of the Enemy at Carn Dûm and bring them back here where they can be reforged. Not only will we have weapons, the Enemy will not! A clever plan, yes?
'It is up to you to travel west into Urugarth and steal away their weapon crates. When you have the crates, return to me.'
'Excellent! I'll get these to the forge, and we'll set about restocking our weapons stores.'
'You were asked to bring back weapons, and all I see are empty hands.'
Collect weapons from weapon-crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the weapons to Throst
The Enemy's Arms

The resistance at Gath Forthnír needs equipment if they are to make a stand against Carn Dûm. If someone were to journey to Urugarth, it may be possible to acquire supplies from the Enemy and put those weapons to better use.
'I can't say it'll be a pleasure to touch Uruk-forged iron, but we'll melt it down into proper swords and axes.'

Urugarth is in Carn Dûm to the west.
Throst hatched a clever plan to steal supplies from the Enemy and use them to equip the resistance.

Throst waits for the supplies back at Gath Forthnír to the east.
You ransacked the supply-crates of the Enemy, collecting a fair amount of weapons. Now you should return with them to Throst.
Collected white Warg-hide
Collected rugged Warg-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Throst told me what you did. An admirable feat! It will be a fine thing when the Enemy realizes we are cutting them down with their own iron and steel.
'If we are to go to battle, we will need more than sharp blades. You must return to Urugarth and hunt the Wargs there for their hides. We can tan their thick hides and fashion them into good quality armour.
'Skin the pelts from the largest Wargs you can find. Their leader will have the toughest hide of them all so be sure to track him down as well.'

'These will do well! It is a shame that we cannot get rid of the rank stench of these furs.
'Ah, well. At least the hides themselves can be saved. I will begin work on that armour right away!'
'Those Wargs are not going to skin themselves.'
Bring the Warg-hides to Thorth
Collect white Warg-hide
Collect rugged Warg-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Skinning the Beasts
You obtained some weapons from the Enemy at Urugarth, which Throst the dwarf plans to re-forge for the Rangers' use.

Urugarth is beyond the gates of Carn Dûm to the west.
Thorth requires Warg hides to craft new armour for the resistance. You should take several hides, as well as the hide of the Warg-leader, and return them to Thorth back at Gath Forthnír in eastern Angmar.

'North of Esteldín, where the land breaks open to a long path through the crags, there is a line of cliffs known as Ram Dúath, which bars the way north into Angmar. For ages, the Earth-kin guarded that path and made their way onto the plains of Nan Amlug to hunt the aurochs each year.
'Until now, there has never been any cause for concern, but word has reached us that many among the Earth-kin hunters, led by Jarrko the First Hunter have betrayed their own people, the tribe of the Suuri-lehmä, and now serve Angmar.
'East from Esteldín and north into Nan Amlug, you will find an encampment of the Rauta-lehmä, as these traitors call themselves. Show them that their betrayal is known and will not be brooked.'

'Your victory brings me no joy. It is a difficult situation with the Earth-kin, one that will not be resolved soon.
'You should seek out Elúr. He is our chief smith. I have charged him with an important duty, with which you may be able to assist.'
Fall of the Earth-kin

For many ages, the Earth-kin protected the pass through Ram Dúath from Angmar, but since the betrayal of the Suuri-lehmä tribe by First Hunter Jarkko and his followers, the Earth-kin have themselves become trapped in the North Downs.
'The Earth-kin, despite their strange aspect, have always been a peace-loving people, until the betrayal of the Rauta-Lehmä. The traitors have little regard for life.'

The Earth-kin of the Rauta-lehmä faction are encamped east of Esteldín in Nan Amlug.
Daervunn, Ranger of Esteldín, has charged you with showing the traitorous Rauta-lehmä that they have chosen the wrong side in the coming war by raiding their encampment.

Daervunn awaits your return at Esteldín.
You defeated the Earth-kin of the Rauta-lehmä at their camp in the eastern section of Nan Amlug. Daervunn will want news of your victory.

'This liquid smells terrible! But...it does smell like the liquid I found on the shards of the gourd I found. This is the proof I need to clear my name!
'Here, take one of the skins to Captain Trotter and show it to him. Tell him that this is what caused me to fall asleep. I would do it myself, but the guards won't let me near him.
'Please hurry, my name must be cleared!'

'So you've been listening to Talbot's tales, have you? Quite disgraceful. Blaming the Orcs for his failures! I might as well look at this liquid you found, just to keep Talbot from bothering me any further....
'What a foul odour! So Talbot was telling the truth! I will have him returned to duty at once.
'But this liquid is troubling. If there is more of this about, all of Trestlebridge could be threatened. This matter must be investigated further!'

'What are you here about? I'm terribly busy and don't have time to be disturbed!
'Return when you have something of import to talk about. Until then, I wish you a good day!'
Bring the waterskin to Captain Trotter
Talbot Redeemed
Talbot told you that the vile liquid you found on the Orc in Nan Wathren was similar to the shattered one he found at his feet. He believes this is the proof he needs to clear his name.
'Hurry, take that skin over to Captain Trotter. I know it will clear my name, and once my name is clear, I won't be treated like a criminal anymore!
'Thanks to you, I'm back on the guard! Thank you!'
'After you showed him the proof of my innocence, Captain Trotter apologized. He's an honourable gent, that one!'

Captain Trotter can be found in Trestlebridge.
Talbot Hinton asked you to bring the gourd you found to Captain Trotter as evidence to clear his name. He cannot do this himself, since the town-guard will not let him approach the captain.

'So good of you to assist us! Several of our guards reported a great commotion during the night. A sound like thunder, with naught a cloud in the sky. So unusual! It's best that you get the whole story from Aggy Digweed. I would go myself but these orc raids are keeping me quite busy.
'Aggy guards the north side of the Trestlespan. In fact, she should be on duty right now. I'm sure it's nothing serious but you can never be too cautious in these dark times.'
'Reynard sent you? Good. We have much to talk about and not a lot of time.'
Find and speak with Aggy Digweed
Trotter's Task

Reynard Trotter is concerned about recent developments in the area. The guards reported hearing a terrible noise during the night. Aggy Digweed, one of the guards, wanted to speak to someone about the event.
Travel to the far side of the Trestlespan and speak with Aggy. Captain Trotter said she'd have more information for you.

Aggy Digweed is to the north of the Trestlespan
Captain Trotter suggests that Aggy Digweed can shed more light on recent events.

'I wonder...I wonder if a \qdefiler\q is behind this! Hrm, a defiler? Oh, it's a breed of Orc that some stories are told about. Supposedly they are masters of vile poisons and diseases, defiling all that they touch.
'It is strange, though...I thought these defilers were just a myth. We've never seen one here before; most of the Orcs that attack us are just violent brutes, attacking without thought.
'If there is a defiler out there, it means more trouble for us. Please, find this beast and slay it! If the defiler is anywhere, it'll be somewhere in the Nan Wathren, which lies east of town. Look for foul patches of water there, that will probably be a sign of his presence.'

'You are truly a brave one. That tale you told tells me this defiler was quite a ferocious Orc! I wonder if there are any more of those creatures out there?
'Now there's a thought. I shudder to think what that would be like. We've enough trouble with the regular Orcs, let alone these \qsmart\q ones, if such a word can be applied to an Orc!
'For now, though, it seems Trestlebridge is safe...at least from this threat!'
Vile Poison

Captain Trotter explained to you that the dried gourd you found was made by a \qdefiler,\q an Orc that relishes in poison and disease. He asked that you slay the creature, before it can spread any of its vile poisons into Trestlebridge.
'This defiler represents a great threat to Trestlebridge and must be slain. The beast will be lurking somewhere in Nan Wathren, likely near foul patches of water.'
'I heard word of your victory! Excellent work, slaying that Orc-defiler!'
'Nasty business, that Orc-defiler. Glad you dealt with him!'
'Your defeat of the Tarkrîp-defiler has saved Trestlebridge from at least one threat. Yet, many others loom....'
'Your victory over the defiler gives me hope that the Enemy will one day be defeated as well!'

The Tarkrîp Defiler should be found somewhere in Nan Wathren, east of Trestlebridge.
Captain Trotter has asked you to hunt down and defeat the Tarkrîp-defiler. He suggested looking for the Orc near foul patches of water.

Captain Trotter can be found in Trestlebridge.
In Nan Wathren, you discovered the hiding place of the Tarkrîp-defiler and slew the Orc. You should tell Captain Trotter of your victory.

'At last, someone who will talk to me! Everyone treats me like a criminal. But I'm not guilty of falling asleep on duty! It's orcs fault!
'I remember being on duty, then next thing I know Captain Trotter is shaking me awake, yelling that I had failed to sound the alarm and that Trestlebridge had been attacked!
'Thing is, I found at my feet the shards of a dried gourd. They were covered in a vile liquid, but no one believes me when I say it was some sort of Orc devilry! I need more proof, and I think it can be found at the Orc camps north of the bridge.
'Here, take these old water skins. At the camps you might find some pots or cauldrons with some vile liquids in them. Collect the liquid in the skins and bring it back here.'
'You've returned, and with some of the vile liquid! Hurry, let me examine it. I must know if it is the same as the remains of the one I found when I woke up!'
'Please, you must find some of the liquid that the orcs used on me! I fear that without such proof, the people of Trestlebridge will forever believe that I fell asleep on duty!'
Collect vile liquid from the orc camps (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Collected vile liquid (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Bring the full water skins to Talbot Hinton
A Poor Guard

Talbot Hinton told you that he was drummed out of the Trestlebridge town guard for falling asleep on duty. He claims though that the Orcs did something to put him to sleep and has asked you to help him prove this.

'Please, take those skins and see if you can find any pots or cauldrons of vile liquid in the Orc camps north of the bridge.
'If you can't do this, I fear the people of Trestlebridge will forever believe that I fell asleep on duty!'

You may find pots or cauldrons of vile liquid at the Orc camps north of Trestlebridge.
Talbot told you that if you could find some of the vile liquid that it might be enough to clear his name.

Talbot Hinton can be found in Trestlebridge.
At the orc camps north of Trestlebridge, you were able to find cauldrons of a vile liquid. You collected some of the liquid in to the skins Talbot gave you.
Collected the crate contents

'I need your help! The Orcs have some foul magic that they hope to use against us! The other night I was keeping watch on this side of Cirith Núr, and I saw dark figures carrying a pair of crates out of Nan Wathren.
'I loosed a fire-arrow at them, to signal the town-guard. The arrow struck one crate, and those carrying it dropped it and ran. Soon after, there was a sound like thunder and a ball of fire! The others hastily retreated carrying the other crate.
'Can you imagine what would have happened if they had gotten that onto the bridge? We must learn what was in that crate! Would you go to the western edge of the Nan Wathren, search for this crate and find out what's inside?'

'Is this what you found in their camp? Here, let me examine it....
'Awful stuff! I've no doubt this stuff is dark magic. And knowing Orcs, this crate wasn't the only source of this \qBlack-fire!\q'
'We must know what was in that crate! You should search the western edge of Nan Wathren for it and bring some evidence back here.'
Bring the crate contents to Aggy Digweed
Collect the crate contents
Defending the Bridge
Aggy Digweed spotted figures carrying a crate out of Nan Wathren. To signal the guard at Trestlebridge, she fired a fire arrow towards them and struck the crate, which exploded in a ball of flame.

The crate was destroyed at the western edge of Nan Wathren.
Aggy Digweed, afraid that this new weapon may be the doom of Trestlebridge, asked you to look for the shattered remains of the crate.
Destroyed the Black-fire on the northern hill
Destroyed the Black-fire on the south-eastern hill
Destroyed the Black-fire on the south-western hill

'I'm sure the Orcs have plenty more Black-fire. I'm going to ask you to find and destroy it all. That means you will have to go deep into Nan Wathren.
'I know the Orcs have camps on three hills in the Nan Wathren. These hills are connected by rope bridges in the heart of the valley. I suspect that more Black-fire can be found there. We must destroy it if we can. It seems that open flame causes this foul powder to explode, so it would be wise to use fire to destroy the crates.
'Also, keep an eye open for half-orcs. I wager it is them I saw carrying the crate. Pure-bred Orcs are brutes and could never work such magic! I'd take some friends along, if I was you -- that area is crawling with Orcs, and you'll need friends to defend you while you destroy the crates.'

'You found more of the Black-fire? Goodness, they had that much of it? I suppose we are lucky I spotted that crate the other night, aren't we?
'I am worried, though. This Lugbas the half-orcs spoke of...could it be that he is the one making this Black-fire?'
Find the Black-fire on the northern hill
Find the Black-fire on the south-eastern hill
Find the Black-fire on the south-western hill
The Black-fire

Aggy Digweed has dubbed the foul substance you found \qBlack-fire\q and called it a dark magic of the Orcs. She believes the Orcs have more and that it must be destroyed if Trestlebridge is to be saved.
This crate is filled with a dark, powdery substance. If you are to destroy it, as Aggy Digweed asked, you will have to use fire.
This crate is filled with a dark, powdery substance. If you are to destroy it, as Aggy Digweed asked, you will have to use fire.
This crate is filled with a dark, powdery substance. If you are to destroy it, as Aggy Digweed asked, you will have to use fire.

'You must search Nan Wathren for more of the Black-fire. In Nan Wathren, there are three large hills connected by rope bridges. You should start your search there.
'Be on the look out for half-orcs, as they are the ones likely behind this devilry! And please hurry...they may try to use the Black-fire on us again at any time!'

The Black-fire crates are on three hills in Nan Wathren.
Aggy Digweed said that there are three large hills connected by rope bridges in Nan Wathren and asked you to search those hills for more Black-fire crates. She told you to keep an eye open for half-orcs, as full-blooded Orcs are too brutish to create magic like the Black-fire. As the Black-fire powder explodes when touched by fire, Aggy asked you to put the Black-fire to the torch, destroying it all. She also suggested you take friends.

Aggy Digweed can be found in Trestlebridge.
In your search of the three hills in the Nan Wathren, you found Black-fire crates atop each hill. You also found half-orcs, who spoke of a someone named Lugbas, who may be their leader. Aggy should know what you found.

'The more I think of it, the more convinced I am that this Lugbas the half-orcs spoke of is behind the Black-fire. He's probably a half-orc himself and leads the ones you slew before.
'If we are truly to end the threat of the Black-fire, we must end this Lugbas! But finding him might be a challenge...ah! My old hiding spot! You see, far in the south-east of the Nan Wathren, on the highest slopes, there's a nook where no one could ever find me when I hid there.
'I'll wager he's hiding there! Go there and, if you find him, slay him!'

'Lugbas is dead? Hooray! Thank you! With him and many of his minions dead, there should be no one left who knows the secret of the Black-fire's magic!
'Trestlebridge is that much safer thanks to your sacrifices! My thanks again!'
Half-orc Schemer
Aggy Digweed believes that to truly end the threat of the Black-fire, this Lugbas the half-orcs spoke of must be slain.

'To end the threat of the Black-fire, Lugbas must be ended. He is likely the leader of the half-orcs.
'Try searching my old hiding spot in the south-east corner of the Nan Wathren. On the highest slopes there you will find a nook. It always served me as an excellent hiding place as a girl, and Lugbas might be hiding there now!'
'With Lugbas dead, Trestlebridge is safe from the Black-fire. Thank you!'
'I shall never forget what you have done for Trestlebridge!'
'May the Black-fire never blight Trestlebridge ever again!'

Lugbas is probably hiding in the far south-east corner of the Nan Wathren.
Aggy Digweed told you of a nook in the south-east corner of the Nan Wathren, atop the highest slopes, where she used to hide as a girl. She believes this is where you will most likely find Lugbas. She beseeches you to slay him before he can make more Black-fire.

Aggy Digweed is in Trestlebridge.
You should return to Aggy Digweed with news of your victory against Lugbas.

'For one so small, you are very good at killing Orcs. The Orcs are many, but we think they run through Ram Dúath because Men tell them to go. Evil Men from the North, from Angmar, have come to Ram Dúath.
'One of the Men is the leader. We think he will send the Orcs against us soon. We cannot fight them in their camp, they are too strong, but you are strong too. Maybe you can help us fight this Man, this Commander from Angmar.
'The Angmarim have a camp in the south-east part of the Ram Dúath.'
'The leader of the Angmarim is dead? Good! Maybe the Angmarim will send another leader, but for now we are safe!'
The Far Reaching Hand
Chief Tuokki is worried that the Angmarim who command the Orcs will send them to fight the Earth-kin.
'The Orcs may not come if you kill the leader of the Angmarim.'

The outpost of the Angmarim is in the south-east part of Ram Dúath.
Chief Tuokki, hoping to discourage the Orcs and the Angmarim, has asked you to defeat the Commander of the Angmarim in Ram Dúath.

Chief Tuokki is at the Suuri-lehmä camp in Ram Dúath.
Now that you've defeated the Iron-crown Commander, return to the Earth-kin Chief and tell him of your deed.
Collected goblin-gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I know you little folk prize the glittering stones. We care little for most of these stones, but we treasure the kind we call Eyes of the Earth. I think in your tongue you call them cat's-eyes and moonstones.
'It seems that the goblins who serve the Angmarim in their fort just north-east of the Ram Dûath have stolen a great many of these stones, including eyes of the earth from our people.
'I would ask you to go to this fort and take back the goblin-treasures. They should be stored in chests filled with many gems. We will take the Eyes of the Earth, and you will take the rest, with our thanks.'
'Ah, yes, you have done it! Here...I will separate out the Eyes of the Earth, and the rest shall be yours!'
'The goblins guard their chests glittering stones well, do they not? And you must beware of the Orcs and trolls on the way!'
Bring the goblins' gems back to Aslak at Lehmä-koti
Collect goblin-gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Goblins' Treasure
Aslak of the Suuri-lehmä, told you that the goblins have collected hoards of gems in the fort they share with the Angmarim on the north-eastern pass of Ram Dúath.

The goblins keep their treasure in the fort at the north-east pass of Ram Dúath.
Aslak has told you where the goblins keep a hoard of stolen gems and offered to split the loot with you if you can find the chests and steal them back again.

'North of here, Ram Dúath opens into the dark land of Angmar. There are many evil Men and Orcs in that land, and worse things too, so we do not go there ourselves. But not all the folk of Angmar are enemies to us. There is one clan of Hillmen in those lands who have ever been our friends, sending south to trade with us when they can. Perhaps they will be friendly to you as well.
'Like us, they hate the Orcs, and they stand against the evil ones who rule in the black city. We want to let them know that the main body of Orcs has now passed south into the North Downs. This may help them in their counsels, and perhaps they can resume their trade with us.
'Find the man called Crannog. He is the Chief in Aughaire. Tell him the news I have told you. Aughaire is west from the northern pass of Ram Dúath, in a concealed valley over a steep rise in the hills. Sometimes in the past, the men of Aughaire travelled a steep trail to our village -- a trail the Jorthkyn are too big to walk, but perhaps you can find it not far from here.'

'Ho, Southron! The Jorthkyn sent you to us? It is long and longer still since last we had enough goods of our own to be able to trade with those strange folk.
'Your words are welcome, though little good do they do us. We are hard-pressed on all sides, even with the Orc-army no longer encamped upon our doorstep.
'Still, I will open the host-hearth of Aughaire to you. You are welcome here, for so long as we ourselves remain.'
Men of the Hills
Pirkka of the Suuri-lehmä, told you of a clan of Hillmen in Angmar who are friendly to them and should be made aware that the main body of the Orc-host has passed south into the North Downs.
'Will you bring the news of the Orc-army to Crannog?'

Aughaire is west of the northern pass of Ram Dúath, a valley concealed and surrounded by hills. There is also said to be a secret trail that goes there directly from the Earth-kin village.
Pirkka has asked you to take the news of the passage of the Orc-army to Crannog, chief of the Hillmen of Aughaire.

'You are a proven friend to our people, but what I ask of you now may be too much. There is a cave in this very place where the merrevail make their lair, and in this cave dwells their leader, a bloody-handed creature we have heard the Orcs call the Mistress of Shadows.
'The merrevail are cruel and vicious, worse even than the Orcs and the evil Men of Carn Dûm. They will continue to prey on us if we do not fight them. I ask you to enter this cave and to destroy this Mistress of Shadows. If she falls, then perhaps the others will leave Ram Dúath and return to whatever foul place in Angmar it is that spawned them.
'These evil things have slain many of the Suuri-lehmä...I think you should take friends with you if you go there.'
'I am pleased that you have returned safely from such a dangerous quest. In the name of my people, I thank you for your deeds.'
Mistress of Shadows
You have assisted the Earthkin scout, but the morroval-threat remains, endangering the Earth-kin and all else who dwell in the hills of Angmar.
'For the sake of my people, I ask you to slay the Mistress of Shadows.'
'It is good that you were able to slay the Mistress of Shadows.'
'The queen of the bat-women will trouble us no more!'

The Mistress of Shadows dwells in a cave on the east side of Ram Dúath, where the other merrevail can also be found.
The Earth-kin scout has asked you to seek out and destroy the leader of the Merrevail for the safety of his people. He also suggested you take friends.

The Earthkin Scout is in the Duvairë on the west side of Ram Dúath.
With the Mistress of Shadows slain, you should return to the Earthkin Scout.

'For much time now, Orcs and evil Men and other evil things have come through Ram Dúath from the North, from Angmar. They go to fight in the South, but they cause much trouble here, too.
'We hate Orcs and their friends, and we try to fight them when we can, but now there are too many for us, and our hunters cannot return from the southern plains. Will you fight the Orc-folk, too? Help us, and kill the Orcs in Ram Dúath. Many Orcs of the Blogmal tribe can be found in the south-east part of the pass.
'We will give you the coins that we take from the dead Orcs. We have little need for them.'
'You have shed much Orc blood. This is good. We thank you for your help.'
Orcs in the Ram Dúath
Orcs marching through Ram Dúath have unsettled the Earth-kin dwelling there and have cut off any hope of safe return for the Earth-kin hunters sojourning in the North Downs.
'As long as the Orcs fill the pass, our hunters cannot return, and our people will starve.'

There are Blogmal Orcs in the south-east part of the Ram Dúath.
The Tuokki, the Earth-kin elder leading the Suuri-lehmä tribe while their chieftain is away south in the North Downs, has asked you to help drive the Blogmal Orcs from Ram Dúath.

Chief Tuokki is at the Suuri-lehmä camp in Ram Dúath.
You should return to Chief Tuokki and tell him of your victory against the Orcs of the Blogmal tribe.
Collected Aurochs Skulls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Many years ago, we brought with us from the South some skulls of lehmä -- what you little people call aurochs. Very important skulls. The skulls honour Suuri-lehmä.
'Jorthkyn take the skulls on path through Ram Dúath to see new sights in this place. This must be done every year. This year, our brethren did not return. Scouts say that Orcs killed Jorthkyn and took the skulls. Orcs are in a strong place in the east side of Ram Dúath.
'Bring back the skulls from the Orcs. Maybe they are in their strong place? Or in the camp of the horrible bat-women who kill? Three skulls were stolen.'

'The skulls have returned to us. Welcome home, skulls! What have you seen amongst the Orcs?
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You are a friend to the Jorthkyn. All the lehmä now rejoice!'
'We need our skulls back.'
Bring the aurochs-skulls back to Santtu at Lehmä-koti
Collect Aurochs Skulls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Stolen Skulls
Aurochs skulls apparently have some significant meaning to the Earth-kin of the Suuri-lehmä, and many have been stolen from them.

The aurochs skulls are probably in the camp of the Orcs and Angmarim in the eastern part of Ram Dúath. Tuokki also mentioned some strange \qbat-women who kill\q who might have them.
Santtu has asked you to recover the stolen aurochs skulls.
Destroyed siege-weapons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Men and Orcs of Angmar have been bringing big wheeled war-carts through Ram Dúath. At first, they often broke on their own. It took many tries before the stupid Orcs learned how to move these clumsy things safely through the pass.
'We thought, they are taking such pains, perhaps we can help them too. So we showed them the strength of stone and broke many of the carts ourselves, seeing as the evil ones seemed to want these carts in the South so badly.
'Now, though, they have learned again, and the war-carts are too well-guarded for us. But maybe you can fight through to the carts. These must be treasures for these evil folk, things they need to make war in the South. You can find the carts in the eastern pass.'

'It is good that those carts were broken. We would not want the Orcs to think they had easy lives!
'I know you fight the Orcs and Men of Angmar for your own reasons, but it is good that we can fight them together in Ram Dúath.'
Destroy siege-weapons (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Strength of Stone
The Earth-kin have been destroying the siege-engines of the Angmarim as they wheel them through Ram Dúath, but now they are too strongly guarded for the Earth-kin to reach.
'Destroy the war-carts and show the Orcs the strength of stone.'
'We have done a great hurt to the evil ones, have we not?'
'Orcs will not find it so easy to fight without their war-carts. You have done well, little ${PLAYER}.'

The war-carts -- siege engines and catapults -- of the Angmarim are in the eastern part of Ram Dúath.
Tuokki has asked you to help destroy the Angmarim siege-engines and catapults he calls war-carts.

Chief Tuokki is at the Suuri-lehmä camp in Ram Dúath.
You should return to Tuokki with word of your success.

'Another thing there is now in Ram Dúath stranger than Men or Orcs, maybe worse than either of them. Evil people like women, but with wings! They are vicious, deadly creatures, while I was scouting the orcs they attacked me.
'You must destroy these bat-women, they are fierce and kill without mercy. Others will come to look for me, they must not hurt more of the Jorthkyn.
'I am afraid of these foul creatures. Such things do not belong in the world.'
'They are cruel creatures, these bat-women; it is good that you have thinned their numbers. My wound is quickly healing, soon I will return and warn the Suuri-lehmä.'
Wings of Darkness and Death
The Earthkin Scout has been attacked by strange folk who have come into Ram Dúath from the North. He told you the women with wings are in league with the Angmarim.
'You must hurry, I do not know when my people will come in search of me. Slay the bat-women, protect Jorthkyn.'

The bat-winged creatures who injured the Earth-kin scout are in the eastern gorges of Ram Dúath.
The Earth-kin scout's request was for you to kill the vicious merrevail so that others will not be injured or worse.

The Earthkin Scout is in the Duvairë in Ram Dúath.
You should return to the Earthkin Scout and tell him of your success against the merrevail.

'So, another Southron comes to trouble us. Well, we are not like those who crawl before the Iron Crown, and we still hallow the guest-law. So... be welcome.
'You will not find much love amongst us for your kind, stranger. We listened to the Southron Golodir and stood against the Iron Crown, but now that he has abandoned us, we are on our last leg. The other clans have joined against us, and only the last frail vestiges of the Treaty of the Hills protects us from war. Soon enough, though, we will fall, one way or the other.
'Oh, you wish to hear more of our troubles? I have no breath to repeat the tale of woe. Ask the Lore-singer, Arzhur, if you must know the long, sad story. He is near the tents to the north.'

'Ah, another stranger. Crannog has sent you, eh? Listen well, then. Some years past, when the evil men of Angmar were busily corrupting and subjugating the men of the hills, a Southron, Golodir by name, came to us. He was a noble man and a strong warrior, and we could tell he spoke truth in all things.
'Golodir warned us not to follow the Iron Crown and showed us the evil secrets of Angmar. He led us to confront our brothers in the other clans and to expel the Angmarim emissaries who whispered in the ears of our elders.
'But then Golodir disappeared. Some say he was slain, others say he has returned to the South, abandoning us to our fate. Now most of the men of Aughaire still stand against Angmar and their slave-clans, but we have lost hope for the future.'
The Free Folk
Chief Crannog has sent you to Lore-singer Arzhur to learn something of the Free Folk of Angmar.
'Speak to Arzhur. I have not the breath to waste.'
'Leave me, southron, I am weary of your presence.'

Arzhur is in Aughaire, northeast of Chief Crannog.
Chief Crannog has sent you to speak to the Lore-singer Arzhur to hear about the history of his clan.
Collected Donnvail pease (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It has come to my ears that you have been making yourself useful in Aughaire, Southron. Well, that is good, perhaps you can aid me as well, if you have the time?
'A staple of our people for feast days is a porridge or pudding made from pease, with maybe a hint of bacon or aurochs-hock. But the pease grow in the fields of Donnvail. Once we traded with Donnvail for such supplies, but now...
'It seems a foolish thing, perhaps, but it might well raise the spirits of our warriors to be able to enjoy this dish before the coming battles. If you could steal away a supply of the pease from the fields around Donnvail, I would be much obliged.'
'You have done well, Southron! The folk of Aughaire owe you for this meal, and I thank you.'
'You could not find enough pease? That is too bad!'
Collect Donnvail pease (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the pease back to Ailsa of Aughaire
Pease-pudding is a favoured meal amongst the Hillmen of Angmar. But the pease used in this dish are grown in the fields of Donnvail, which has cut off trade with Aughaire.

Pease can be found in the fields around Donnvail to the north-east.
Ailsa has asked you to gather enough pease to make a traditional meal to raise the spirits of her people.

Ailsa is at Aughaire, south of the hills.
You have collected the pease that Ailsa requires. You should return to her at once.
Collected food-stores (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'With the other clans of the hills against us, and with the threat of Carn Dûm hanging over our heads, our hunters have been unable to gather enough food for the winter. Yet the farmers of Donnvail have plenty of grain and other food stores, and if only they would let us buy it from them, we would pay them well. But the Angmarim have told them not to sell.
'Indeed, if we even venture near their gates, they will attack us for violating their clan borders. We have not the strength to protect our own hunters, and even if we had the force to do so, raiding Donnvail would break the pact of the clans, so we would never do such a thing. But you are a fierce southron-fighter -- or so I hear -- and you perhaps have friends from the south to support you in the field.
'If you would venture into Donnvail -- on your own, you understand, not with any of our warriors -- we could not be blamed if later we paid you for the food as we would have paid the farmers of Donnvail.'
'Good! I am sure I do not know where you came by this food, of course, but I would be happy to pay you for it!'
'We really need some food stores from someplace....'
Bring the food-stores back to Cuinthorn in Aughaire
Collect food-stores (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Stealing Stores
The constant harrassment of the hunters of Aughaire has resulted in a food shortage. There is plenty of food in the town of Donnvail, however.

There are food stores throughout the town of Donnvail, far to the north of Aughaire. Chief Crannog is in Aughaire, south of Donnvail.
Chief Crannog has suggested that if you were to raid the Angmarim town of Donnvail for their surplus food stores, he would be willing to pay you well for them.
Collected a drake egg

'We of Aughaire have many troubles. Too many, I think for Chief Crannog, who has lost heart and hope. But perhaps you might wish to aid us, as Golodir once did?
'We are trapped in a maze of clan-laws. Those who serve Angmar have tried to make it impossible for us to fulfil our obligations. If we fail, we will be subject to open warfare.
'Our first obligation is to obtain a drake's egg from Nád Nathair. We need this as a token of honour to meet the blood challenges of the other clans. Yet our hunters are mercilessly harrassed by our enemies when we approach the drakes. Will you go to the drake lair not far to the north and obtain an egg for us? The drakes are attended by many hill-beasts, so you will know the lair by their presence.
'Listen well: the drakes are fearsome foes, but they are not devoted parents. It would be best to take an egg from a nest which is not guarded by a drake.'
'Good. You have proven yourself worthy, friend ${PLAYER}.'
'We need a drake egg to present to the other clans.'
Bring the drake egg to Arzhur
Collect a drake egg
The Drake's Egg
A challenge has been set before Arzhur's clan, but a token of honour is required before the folk of Aughaire can fulfil their lawful obligations to the other clans of Angmar.

The drake-lair is Nád Nathair, north of Aughaire. Nád Nathair can be recognized not only by the drakes but by the many hill-beasts in the area.
Lore-singer Arzhur has asked you to obtain a drake egg. The egg is needed as a token for the men of Aughaire to present to the other hill-clans. He has warned you to avoid the drakes themselves in seeking an egg.
You take a stone from the Cairn of Honour
You have slain a hillman: Quest failed!
You have slain a hillman: Quest failed!
You have slain a hillman: Quest failed!
You have slain a hillman: Quest failed!
You have slain a hillman: Quest failed!
You have slain a hillman: Quest failed!

'Another challenge has been placed before us. Again, we need a token of honour before we can fight. This time, I am afraid clan law is set against us, as there has been a dispute over your participation in the last challenge. If we are to win our way free of this morass, you must fight this time alone.
'First, we require a stone from the Cairn of Honour. The Cairn is in Fasach-Falroid to the north, in the territory of the hostile clans, and their scouts and warriors are entitled by clan-law to defend their land. Yet you must not shed any blood of these Hillmen while obtaining the stone, or the stone will be tainted with blood-debt.
'So I must ask you to journey north to the Cairn, and yet you must not kill any of our enemies, no matter if they attack you or not! You will find the Cairn atop a high hill west of the north road, and at night the path up the hill is lit by torches.'
'Well done. Now it is time for you to fight once more.'
'You must obtain a stone from the Cairn of Honour.'
Obtain a stone from the Cairn of Honour
Bring the Cairn-stone to Arzhur
Avoid killing hillmen
The Cairn of Honour
Another challenge was sent to Arzhur's clan. Before the challenge can be accepted, another token of honour must be brought forth.

The Cairn of Honour is in the centre of Fasach-Falroid to the north of Aughaire. It is atop a high hill, west of the north road, and at night the path to it is lit by torches.
Arzhur has asked you to obtain a stone from the Cairn of Honour. You must not spill any blood of the Hillmen who patrol the area.

Arzhur is back at Aughaire.
You should bring the stone you recovered to Arzhur and prepare for the next challenge.

'Alas your victories have not come without cost. Walraig, Chief of the clan of our enemies, has lost all reason after your defeat of his champions, and he has declared a blood-feud against us! This may make him an outcast if he is not successful in his feud, but if he is not stopped, he will lead the full force of his clan against us here in Aughaire.
'Our one hope is to stop this feud before it begins. If we raid his camp in Tór Gailvin to the north-east, not far from Fail-á-Khro, and defeat Chief Walraig in person, we will have obeyed the law, and our enemies will be unable to proceed against us.
'But our Chief, Crannog, refuses to lead such a raid without Golodir's presence to guide him! I must ask you to do what we cannot and defeat Chief Walraig before we ourselves are overwhelmed.'

'You have done a noble deed for us, Southron. Something we should have done for ourselves. Are we doomed forever to wait for others to lead us?
'Well, no matter. We are in your debt. You will always find a warm welcome in our tents.'
The Final Challenge
Enraged by their repeated defeats in duels, Chief Walraig of the hostile Hillmen has declared a feud against the men of Aughaire.
'Please! You must defeat Chief Walraig!'
'We are still in your debt, Outlander.'
'You have shown great honour, friend ${PLAYER}.'

Chief Walraig is with his kin in Tór Gailvin, a camp north-east of Aughaire.
Lore-singer Arzhur has asked you to raid the Hillman fort to the north-east. If you can defeat Chief Walraig, you may be able to forestall a war between the clans.

Arzhur is in Aughaire, south-west of Chief Walraig's camp.
You should return to Arzhur with news of your victory over Chief Walraig.
You are victorious

'Now we must take the egg you found to Aidan, our clan champion, who awaits it at Fail-á-Khro north-east of Aughaire.
'I am afraid we must ask you for another boon, friend from the south. Aidan is a strong fighter, but he is the last such of whom our clan can boast. We have many bold hunters, skilful hearth-keepers, and perhaps even a few wise lore-singers, but of warriors we have few; our foes have been biting away at our strength like dogs worrying a bone.
'The challenge Aidan must face is not a single combat. I ask that you fight by his side, for the honour of our clan, no less than for its survival.'
'You have done well, Southron. But the rival clans have more trouble for us.'
'Now it is time to fight. Let us see who comes against us!'

'Good. I thought no one would come with that egg. But you are to fight at my side? I do not know....
'Well, needs must. I hope you are stronger than you look, Southron!'
'Why do you come to this place, Southron?'
Bring the drake's egg to Aidan
Speak with Aidan when you are ready to fight by his side.
The First Challenge
Lore-singer Arzhur is satisfied that the drake egg you brought to him will suffice as the token of honour required to meet the rival clan's challenge.
'Take the egg to Aidan and fight by his side against the challengers from the other clans.'

Aidan is waiting at Fail-á-Khro to the north-east of Aughaire.
Lore-singer Arzhur has asked you to take the drake's egg to Aidan and then to fight by his side against the challengers from the clans loyal to Angmar.

Aidan is at Fail-á-Khro north-east of Aughaire.
Fight alongside Aidan against the challengers from a hostile clan loyal to Angmar.

Arzhur is at Aughaire, south-west of Fail-á-Khro.
You should return to Arzhur and report of your victory against the first challenge.
Collected Red Lovage (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Silverbell (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Spiky Mugwort (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hail, Southron! I wonder if you can help the folk of Aughaire as you roam these lands? There are some rare but necessary herbs we use to purify water, treat wounds, and to add savour to our food. With the other clans hostile to us, and dire threats coming daily from Carn Dûm, our men of war -- those few who remain -- cannot protect those who gather these herbs.
'I hope that you can help us, if you have an eye for growing things. We require the following herbs that you may find growing in the hills north of Aughaire: If you can gather red lovage plants, and a quantity of spiky mugwort and silverbell as well, I would be most obliged to you.
'Two of these plants grow near Fail-á-Khro, not far to the north-east, the third grows further away to the north around Donnvail.'
'Ah, you have returned. Well done, Southron! These are just what we needed.'
'I hope you can find the herbs we need.'
Collect Red Lovage (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect Silverbell (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect Spiky Mugwort (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the herbs back to Cána
Herbal Essence

The Hillmen of Angmar make the most of their desolate land, gathering herbs from the rugged hills and withered vales. These herbs are used to purify water, treat wounds, and add savour to food.
Now that the other clans are hostile to them, the Hillmen of Aughaire are having great difficult in collecting the herbs they need to survive in their harsh realm.

Spiky Mugwart can be found at the edges of stagnant pools west of Fail-á-Khro.
Silverbell can be found in the shadows of ancient ruins in the hills around Fail-á-Khro.
Red lovage can be found near the edges of cultivated fields south of Donnvail.
Cana, the healer of Aughaire, has asked you to gather some rare herbs needed by her clan.

Cana, the healer of Aughaire, has asked you to gather some rare herbs needed by her clan.
You must return to her with the herbs you have collected.
You are victorious

'Once again it is time to fight for the honour of my clan. You have proven yourself worthy, Southron, but now the rules have changed.
'This time, the two brothers Donnan and Mungan claim to have been slighted by our clan. They lie, but the Judge has permitted both of them to fight us at once. Be wary of the younger brother, Donnan, for he is the fiercer of the two. You can find them here in Aughaire, on the west side of the town, waiting for you to answer their challenge.'
'Again, you have triumphed, Southron, this time against unfair odds. But I fear that despite your victory, matters will soon grow more desperate.'
'Who are you to fight for this clan of weaklings? Well, it matters not, we will crush you, and then the Iron Crown will take Aughaire!'
Accept Donnan's challenge
The Second Challenge
The second token of honour, the stone from the Cairn of Honour, was more difficult to obtain, as it required entering hostile territory without engaging in battle.

Donnan and his brother are at Aughaire on the west side of the Hillman town, awaiting your response to their challenge.
Arzhur has asked you once again to fight against the challengers from a hostile clan loyal to Angmar.

Arzhur is at Aughaire
You should return to Arzhur with news of your victory against the second challenge.

'Ah, Southron! Another challenge awaits us! This time we face the leader of a pack of vicious Wargs.
'I hope that you are ready for a fight!'
'Many thanks, friend. With you by my side, I knew we would not fail.'
Another Challenge
Another challenge awaits at Fail-á-Khro. This time, Aidan has been challenged to face the leader of a pack of vicious Wargs.

Speak to Aidan.
You met the challenge and were victorious.
Defeat shades and dread-mists (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hail and well met, good ${RACE}. If I seem in a fell mood, I beg your pardon, but my heart is heavy. Fornost is overrun with the shades of Oathbreakers who are unrepentant and fell things of Angmar, and the terror of them saps the wills of the men and dwarves who have come to aid us.
'Perhaps you would lend aid to my troubled heart? If you would, enter Fornost and dispel the traitors, sending them to their final condemnation?
Do this, and the terror of Fornost may be broken!'
'The task I gave you was not a simple one, but you have made a fine showing of it. You have impressed even me, which is not easy.'
Defeat shades and dread-mists (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Putting Down the Dead

Fornost is overrun with the shades of those who betrayed the North Kingdom at the Battle of Fornost, yet remain unrepentant, and other fell creatures of Angmar. Maedhrusc is concerned by the terror these creatures instill in the Rangers' allies.
In order to dispel the terror of the Dead from the hearts of his allies, Maedhrusc has asked you to enter Fornost and deal with the shades and other other fell creatures which dwell there.
The sheer numbers of Angmar's foul minions was too great for you to defeat utterly, but your successes may be enough to hearten Maedhros and the alliance from the North Downs.
Defeated Uthagan

'The Beast? Shh! Don't speak of him. He is terrible...perhaps one of these folk will tell you more, but I dare not! Listen, it may be that one of the names I give you will be of service to you. It may be that one of these names will betray you. I cannot say for sure. All I ask you is that you not use my name with them.
'Listen well, I will not say these names twice: Garvan, Morven, Uthagan, and Una. Speak to Una last, if the others will not help you.
'Go now. I am sorry I could not help you more. I know it is unseemly. But you have not seen what I have seen....'

'What! An outlander! What are you doing here?
'No...please go. I cannot help you. I have nothing for you. Please...go now, before I call the guards! Please, I beg you, go away!'

'What is a southron doing here? So strange....
'The Beast? No! Do not speak that name here! We are but humble servants of the Iron Crown.
'I am sorry, stranger, but there is nothing I can do to help you. You should go now, quickly, before you are discovered!'

'What do you here, Southron? Ah, you come from my kin in Aughaire, I suppose.
'I am sorry for the behaviour of some of the townspeople. They are fearful because of the informants, and because the Beast terrifies them with his power. But perhaps the light of hope you bring us from the south will rally their hearts.
'What? Who is the Beast? Listen well, and I will tell you....'

'An outlander come to Donnvail? What impudence! Do you not know this is Angmar? Angmar, where the Iron Crown rules and will soon crush your lands?
'I suppose it makes little difference whether you are killed today, or in a few months with your kin when the armies of Angmar invade the south-lands. But since you are so eager....
'Guards! Guards! Take this fool!'
Talk to Uthagan
The Light of Hope

Crannog sent you to Donnvail in hopes of rousing the folk of the town to rebel against the Angmarim oppressors. Baran seemed too fearful of someone he called the Beast to be very helpful, but he has given you a list of other names of Donnvail folk who may be able to help.
'I'm sorry. Would that I were stronger, but I dare not take any action on my own. Perhaps one of those I have told you of can help you more.'

'Surely Morven would be of more help to you than I.
I have no wish to look any further into the darkness surrounding the lords of this place.'

'Uthagan knows much about those who watch over us. If anyone can help you, he can.
Just be careful, for he keeps his loyalties well hidden and no-one here is certain where they truly lay.'
'I am ashamed for my people and for myself. I did not know that Uthagan had changed his loyalties so. I hope that Una can still help you.'

Garvan is in the hostile town of Donnvail.
Branan told you four names, Hillmen of Donnvail who may be willing to rise against their Angmarim masters. He told you to look for Garvan, Morven, and Uthagan, and if they were of no avail, to look for Una, somewhere in Donnvail.

Morven is in the hostile town of Donnvail.
Like Branan, Garvan has demurred from fear of retribution. You should now go deeper into Donnvail to seek out Morven.

Uthagan is in the hostile town of Donnvail.
Now that Morven has refused to help you, you should continue into Donnvail in search of Uthagan.

Una is in Donnvail, far to the north of Aughaire.
None of the first three Hillmen named by Branan were of any avail to you, and indeed Uthagan sought to have you captured or slain. Of the names given to you by the fearful Branan, only Una remains.

'Your courage and grace give us hope, ${PLAYER}. But as I told you, the threat is not yet vanquished. The merrevail follow a queen, a most powerful creature called Azgoth.
'She is a terror most foul, with many minions at her beck and call. Azgoth nests within Carn Dûm, the fortress of Angmar that lies to the west.
'It will not be an easy journey, and the gates of the city are well protected. I have heard rumour of a key. Perhaps you know of it, or where to acquire such a thing. Beyond this rumour, I have nothing else to offer.'

'You claim that Azgoth is no more, but how can this be? You are but one and succeeded where we Rangers could not!
'Ah, but I can see her black blood and the fire in your eyes. Yes, you speak the truth. This is a great day, a day of celebration where we stood as one against the Enemy.'
Queen of the Host
Though you defeated the merrevail and the bats that plagued the Rangers of Gath Forthnír, Thoriel spoke of an even greater threat, the queen of the merrevail...a creature called Azgoth.

'You must defeat Azgoth, or she will lead her minions against us...and our numbers are dwindling daily.
'You must travel to Carn Dûm and find a way inside.'

Azgoth dwells within Carn Dûm, the fortress of Angmar that lies to the west.
Thoriel told you of the morroval-queen, a creature called Azgoth, that must be slain.

Thoriel is at Gath Forthnír, far to the east of Carn Dûm.
You braved the city of Carn Dûm and defeated Azgoth. The Ranger Thoriel will want to hear of your feat.
Defeated merrevail in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated bats in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'These are dark days, ${CLASS}. The morroval scourge preys upon my men, snatching them from where they sleep and carrying them off to their dens.
'You will find the merrevail stalking the lands of Himbar to the west. They are the eyes of Angmar, watching our movements and preying upon us. Slay them now, lest they return to Gath Forthnír.
'Beware the spies of the merrevail, their kindred, the bats.'

'You alone accomplished what we could not, ${PLAYER}. We are so few in number, and without Golodir to guide us, we feared the worst.
'I can only hope you possess the steel to face an even greater threat. I speak of the morroval-queen, Azgoth.'
Defeat merrevail in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat bats in Himbar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Winged Host
Himbar is haunted by the merrevail and their kindred, the bats. These creatures prey upon the Rangers of Gath Forthnír, showing no mercy.
'If you desire to assist us in our plight, journey west and defeat the winged servants of the Enemy.'

The merrevail and the bats hunt throughout Himbar, the lands west of Gath Forthnír.
Thoriel warned you of the merrevail, winged monsters in service to the Enemy. They prey upon the Rangers and must be eradicated.

Thoriel waits for you in Gath Forthnír, the hidden Ranger camp east of Himbar.
You defeated the winged servants of the Enemy and may now return to claim victory.

'I would like to take a moment to congratulate you on your achievements, ${PLAYER}. You have accomplished many brave deeds, and I marvel at your dedication! You are a mighty champion!
'A company of dwarves visited Imladris not long ago, and a number of champions travelled with them. They are now staying at an outpost in the Misty Mountains north of the vale. You should visit the outpost and see if one of them can advise you, for you have exceeded the teaching that I can provide. I salute you for that, friend champion!
'What was the name, again? Gimli, I think it was.'

'You flatter me, ${PLAYER}! There are some would say I am a champion among dwarves, but certainly I would not do so, not so boldly! Ha ha ha!
'The trick to combat, my friend, is to give it everything you've got. There are no half-measures, not in battle and not ever! If you swing your axe as though every swing were its last, you'll be a real force!
'I understand that you're a mighty champion yourself, ${PLAYER}, and I applaud you! You'll do fine in the times that lie ahead, I'm sure of it. Until we meet again!'
A Lesson from Gimli

Gwesgylliel has heard that a company of dwarves have come to the outpost in the Misty Mountains north of Rivendell, and that among their number is a dwarf-champion, Gimli, who might be able to help you grow in power.

'I do not remember dwarf-names very well. The company at the outpost in the Misty Mountains, north of Rivendell, has a dwarf-champion travelling with them. I believe his name was Gimli, but it might have also been Gisli. Dwarf-names are not easy, like the names of my people.'
'${PLAYER}! How goes the fighting?'
'Champion ${PLAYER}, hello! It is good to speak with you!'

A dwarf-champion is currently staying north of Rivendell at an outpost in the Misty Mountains.
Gwesgylliel has learned that a party of dwarves came to Rivendell not long ago, and one of their company, Gimli, was a champion. This dwarf-champion might be willing to teach you some of his techniques.

'I can make you a piece of equipment that will be a worthy addition to your raiment, ${PLAYER}, but I will need a number of components with which to fashion it.
'I give to you these notes to aid you in obtaining the components I will need. Steel yourself, for many of these items will be difficult to come by.
'But you are a champion! I do not doubt your courage or your dedication and am sure that you will emerge from this task victorious.'

'I am glad you have returned, ${PLAYER}, for it means that you have successfully dispatched Raillug. I see too that you bring the Tarkrîp-boots I need.
'While I make use of these items, consult my notes again and set out to collect the second set of components, ${PLAYER}.'
'You do not have the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'Well done, ${PLAYER}. Only one set of components remain, and acquiring these will be your greatest challenge.
'Look to the notes I gave you, and go forth to triumph.'
'You do not have the components I need, ${PLAYER}?'

'I knew you would return, ${PLAYER}, and with the final components I need!
'I give to you a piece of equipment worthy of your skills, and with it my overwhelming respect.'
'You do not have the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'
Bring first set of components to Gwesgylliel
Bring second set of components to Gwesgylliel
Bring last set of components to Gwesgylliel
Articles of Valour
Gwesgylliel has agreed to help you fashion a piece of equipment worthy of your skill as a champion.
'Look to the instructions I gave you, ${PLAYER}, for the locations of the components I will need for your piece of equipment.'
'Look to the instructions I gave you, ${PLAYER}, for the locations of the components I will need for your piece of equipment.'
'Look to the instructions I gave you, ${PLAYER}, for the locations of the components I will need for your piece of equipment.'

Gwesgylliel gave you her instructions containing the components she will need to fashion you a truly remarkable piece of equipment.

'I am pleased to meet you at last, ${PLAYER}, for your deeds travel ahead of you and speak well of your good heart and your strong arm. Our actions bring hope to those who have none, and that is the greatest gift that can be given.
'You are deserving of equipment that reflects the good you do for the people of Middle-earth, ${PLAYER}, the better with which to serve them. It would be my privilege to help you fashion it, but I must give to you this cautionary word: these articles will not be easily come by, for their tale must be one of danger and of hardship. Only through these perils will they have strength enough.
'Speak to me when you are ready to begin, and I will tell you what must be done to fashion equipment befitting a true champion.'

'I can make you a weapon that you will bear with pride, ${PLAYER}, for those that behold it will know you to be a mighty champion. Mightier still are deeds done with honour, and you have performed many!
'But proceed with caution, ${PLAYER}. The components I will need for this weapon will not be easy to come by.
'I give to you my notes containing a list of the things I will need. It will take some time for me to make use of them, so return the items to me in the order I have requested them.'

'I am pleased to see you have returned, ${PLAYER}, and that you bring with you some of the swords of the Ongbúrz. They will no longer add notches to these for each of our friends they slay.
'I rejoice too that you have deprived Tramug of his hand-axe! His tale ends with you, it seems!
'Look to my notes for instructions on the next set of components I will need.'
'Where are the components I requested, ${PLAYER}?'

'I am glad to see you again, ${PLAYER}. These components will greatly improve the weapon I am making for you.
'I would have a word with you about the final set of components, ${PLAYER}. The Uruk-fortress of Urugarth is a stronghold of evil. Be sure you are prepared before you set forth.'
'You do not have the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'You return victorious, ${PLAYER}! I bow to your skill, for I know Lhugrien and Gruglok to be fearsome opponents!

'Welcome, ${PLAYER}. I heard of your victories in Bree-land and rejoiced in particular that you slew Morley the Fierce. A truer name for him would be \qMorley the False!\q He had long been a foe of my family, and I am glad that you put an end to his villainy.
'It is with confidence that I then ask for your help, ${PLAYER}, for I know you to be a true champion. A band of Orcs have come to the ruins of Ost Cyrn, not far from here, and I know that together we can drive them out. These lands may be wilderness, but every yard of land we allow the Orcs to take brings them one yard closer to Bree-town, and the lands of good folk!
'The leader of these Orcs has the vile name Mosal-ruk, and he, like others of his kind, will not resist a challenge issued from a true champion. Let us journey together to Ost Cyrn, ${PLAYER}, defeat Mosal-ruk's war-band, and put an end to his designs on the Lone-lands!'

'Your victories over Morley, Zhurpukh, and Fair Sherman were not accidental, ${PLAYER} -- you are a mighty champion indeed, and you have proved it sevenfold this day! The defeat of Mosal-ruk is already being spoken of by the minstrels I have seen, and that tale is sure to grow in the telling!
'I have learned, too, the importance of wielding a shield. Were it not for your skill and this shield, we might not have survived the battle within the ruins!
'Always bring a heavy shield with you, ${PLAYER}, that you can bear in the event it is needed. Then your tale is sure to last a good deal longer if things go ill!'

'We are victorious, ${PLAYER}, true champions of the Lone-lands! Mosal-ruk will no more threaten the folk who try to make their living in these hard lands, and we have sent a message to his masters this day -- we will stand against you, no matter the odds!
'Tell me when you are ready, and we will journey back to Ost Guruth with this happy news!'

'What we accomplished today is a thing of which legends are made -- \qThe Song of Slade and ${PLAYER} at Ost Cyrn,\q if you like!
'Are you ready to return to Ost Guruth? Perhaps I'll find a minstrel to whom I can relate this tale!'

'Ost Cyrn lies ahead, ${PLAYER}, and if we are true of heart and strong of arm, the Orcs within will not remain there by this time tomorrow!
'Let us take a circuitous route into the ruins and slay as many Orcs as lie within our path. Mosal-ruk will test our courage even by himself, and the fewer of his band that remain when we face him, the more confident I will be of our victory!'
'Let us continue, ${PLAYER} -- the deadliest leg of our journey lies ahead, for Mosal-ruk has surely learned of our coming by now. We will show him he and his kind are not welcome in these lands!'

'A champion is happiest in battle, ${PLAYER}, protecting the weak and fighting for the helpless. I can see in your eye that you have already come to understand that. Now you need to hone your skills so that you may survive the difficulties this calling will set before you!
'There is a mighty champion, a dwarf by the name of Ultan Foebane, who is sure to give you some advice to help you become even stronger, if you can prove that you are worthy of being called a champion. I know that you can prove this to him, ${PLAYER}.
'As I heard it, Ultan Foebane was looking for adventurers at the Combe-gate, on the eastern side of the town of Bree. Present yourself to him and be ready to prove yourself a champion!'

A Blade of Renown
The name of a champion goes before him, carried on the wind by those for whom he fights. It cows his enemies and lifts the hearts of good people everywhere.
'I gave you my notes on the locations of three deadly foes, ${PLAYER}. Dispatch these opponents and return and I will give you some small measure of training! Are you a champion or are you not?'
'Look for Ultan Foebane at the Combe-gate on the east side of the town of Bree. He has been looking for stalwart champions whose mettle he can test ever since he came to Bree-land.'
'Look for Ultan Foebane at the Combe-gate on the east side of town. He has been looking for stalwart champions whose mettle he can test ever since he came to Bree-land.'
