'As I heard it, Ultan Foebane was looking for adventurers at the Combe-gate, on the eastern side of town of Bree. Present yourself to him and be ready to prove yourself a champion!'

'You say you're a champion, ${PLAYER}, but I have to tell you that I've never heard of you. What great deeds have you performed? None that I have seen, and still there is great danger in the surrounding countryside!
'I will recognize you as a champion only if you can slay three of the evils that threaten this town of Men. I give you their names and their favourite haunts and ask only that you end them and return to me!
'With the use of these notes, a real champion would be able to bring safety to these lands and inspire the people with word of his deeds.'

'News of your battles come before you, ${PLAYER}, for the whole town speaks of them!
'Zhurpukh of the Deeps will no more sneak from the marshes in search of open windows and unlatched doors! Fair Sherman? More lovely in death, they say! And of Morley the Fierce, the people say only this -- that he was not fierce enough to best ${PLAYER}, a worthy champion indeed!
'The people in this town of Men speak the truth, friend champion. I will give you some measure of instruction in the fighting arts, the better to improve the strikes you make at your enemies!'

Ultan Foebane is at the Combe-gate on the east side of the town of Bree.
You have been told to speak with Ultan Foebane, a mighty champion travelling through the Bree-land, for the dwarf may be able to help you become stronger.

Ultan Foebane has given you a list containing the locations of three deadly enemies to dispatch.
To prove you are a worthy champion, Ultan Foebane has tasked you with slaying three threats to the folk of Bree-land.

Ultan Foebane is at the Combe-gate on the east side of the town of Bree.
You have defeated the three opponents that Ultan Foebane challenged you to best and should now return in victory to the dwarf.
The Giants' Table lies partially buried in snow

'Of old, if we wished to treat with the giants, we would travel to a great platform of stone in the mountains -- the Giants' Table. This was a place of peace, and neither Elves nor giants would raise a hand against the other while at the Table, no matter the troubles that stirred between our peoples. The Table fell into the snows long ago, but should still hold its old meaning to the giants.
'Journey to the Giants' Table and ask the giants why they have seen fit to break the ancient understanding that they would stay in the mountains. The Giants' Table is just south of the pass of Rakhâs-bizar, east of here and south, the companion to the guarded pass of Gabilazan. Do not enter Gabilazan, for dwarves of an unsavory sort have occupied the keep there and will not suffer you to pass. Rakhâs-bizar is further east of that guarded pass.
'If the giants do not respect the old ways, you will be in danger at the Giants' Table. Bring allies with you, just in case.'
'These are ill tidings you bring. For the giants to attack without warning at the Giants' Table means that there is no way to negotiate with them at all.'
Find the Giants' Table
Giant Country
Gwaemithrin has sent you on a mission of peace to the giants of the Misty Mountains.

'Please seek out the Giants' Table and treat with the giants there if they still respect the old ways. Look for the Table south of the pass of Rakhâs-bizar, east of here. Do not enter the pass of Gabilazan, west of Rakhâs-bizar, for it is guarded by dwarves of an unpleasant disposition.'

The Giants' Table is south of the pass of Rakhâs-bizar, east of the guarded pass of Gabilazan.
Gwaemithrin has sent you to the Giants' Table in the Misty Mountains to treat with the giants and find out why they have come down into the Trollshaws.

The scout Gwaemithrin is in the highlands north and east of Rivendell at a camp established by the Dwarves.
You found the Giants' Table, but the giants there attacked without warning. They have lost their respect for the old ways, and the Giants' Table is no longer a place of peaceful negotiation. You should return to Gwaemithrin with the news.

'Master Elrond sent a scout into the mountains to watch the activities of the giants while Gailthin is in Ered Luin. At present, Gwaemithrin is encamped at the small outpost our Dwarf-visitors have established north of Imladris.
'Bring Gwaemithrin word of your adventures in Arifael's vale and of the hostile giants there and lend her what assistance you may.
'The dwarf-camp is north and east of Rivendell. Take the hillside path north through the hills and look to your left as you climb above the snow line.'
'You come from Ringhul? I am glad, for the giants are up to something, and I have need of assistance.'
Scouting the Mountains
Concerned about hostile giant activity in the Misty Mountains, Ringhul has sent you to meet with a scout in the highlands north of Rivendell.
'Travel north and east to the camp of the dwarves and aid Gwaemithrin with her task.'

The scout Gwaemithrin is in the highlands north and east of Rivendell at a camp established by the Dwarves.
Ringhul has asked you to assist Gwaemithrin with her investigation into the doings of the giants of the Misty Mountains.
You have saved Arifael

'I am worried for my friend, ${PLAYER}, but I fear there is not much that can be done for him. He is no Elf, neither is he Man, dwarf, nor hobbit. The friend I speak of is Arifael, and he is a giant. Gailthin was ever friendly with the giants, and she often took me with her to visit Arifael.
'Whether it was his kindness to the Elves or some other reason, the rest of his kin were displeased with Arifael, and he sought seclusion. He found shelter in a vale to the south across the High Moor, on the slopes of Amon Nendir, but scouts report hostile giants in the area, and I fear for my old friend's safety. Please seek him out and make sure that he is well!
'The vale is very dangerous, and if the wrong sort of giants are seeking to cause trouble for Arifael, you will wish you had brought allies with you.'
'I am pleased that Arifael is well, but it troubles me that the wrong sort of giants have come down out of the mountains after him. How bold must they become before they turn their gaze to Imladris?'

'Come you from little Ringhul? He and pretty Gailthin be friends to me, though they be small and I be giant. Always do they worry. In truth, I am sore-pressed by my distant kin. Starting to come down from the mountains, they are and bring they with them anger and war!
'I hear them approach even now. If small folk like you can fight, make yourself ready!'
Find Arifael
A Better Sort of Giant
Elf-scouts spotted giants moving out of the Misty Mountains, where Ringhul fears they may threaten Arifael, a giant who has been friendly to Elves over the years.

'Please, search Amon Nendir, south of the High Moor, for my friend Arifael. Ask him if he needs aid, then return to me with news of how he fares. The wrong sort of giant has been seen in that vale, and I fear they may cause trouble for my friend.'

Arifael, a giant and friend to the Elves, may be in danger at his home on the slopes of Amon Nendir, south of the High Moor.
Ringhul has asked you to protect his giant friend Arifael from his hostile kin.

Ringhul is in Rivendell, waiting for news of his giant friend Arifael.
You found Arifael hidden in the hills overlooking the valley south of the High Moor, but were forced to fight to defend him from enemy giants.

'While I am glad that Arifael is well, there is more that concerns me. Long ago, we made treaty with the giants of the Misty Mountains. They agreed not to come down into the hills and vales of the Trollshaws without our leave.
'Yet the hostile giants who threatened Arifael have clearly thrown aside this ancient restriction. What else will they dare to do, if they are not rebuked for this transgression?
'The giants in the Stonemere near Arifael must be dealt with. Their strength must be broken, and their leader defeated. Do not attempt to face these foes alone, for they are as dangerous as they are foolhardy, and fools they be if they risk the anger of the Elves.'
'You have done deeds of great valour, ${PLAYER}, but I am still worried that the giants felt free to come down from the mountains at all. We must learn the cause of this boldness.'
Mountain Raiders
Hostile giants in the Stonemere south of Rivendell have violated an ancient treaty by coming down from the mountains and into the Trollshaws.
'The hostile giants across the High Moor south of Imladris in the Stonemere must be defeated, ${PLAYER}. They are much too dangerous to stay in that valley, so close to Imladris.'

The hostile giants are south of Rivendell, beyond the High Moor, in the Stonemere near the hill where you found Arifael.
Ringhul has asked you to make your way into the Stonemere to defeat the hostile giants and slay their leader.

Ringhul is at Rivendell, waiting to hear that you have defeated some of the giants in the Stonemere.
Ringhul asked you to defeat the hostile giants that have come down from the mountains.
You have successfully defended Tóki Whitebeard!

'My dwarves may be lost now, but the stones they were escorting can be recovered from whomever or whatever has stolen them. This we must do, ${PLAYER}.
'Barachen dispatched an Elf named Rochwen to the road north of here, and she seems to know much about this region. She is sure to know what evil dwells in the area that could have caused my dwarves to come to such an unhappy end. Speaking with her about this may be the first step in recovering the stolen stones!
'Bring allies with you. Any foe that could best my dwarves will surely be too much for you alone, ${PLAYER}. I do not mean to offend, of course.'

'So Tóki lives? This is wonderful news, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for bringing it! Let it not be said that the Whitebeard betrayed my trust, for I know he fought valiantly against overwhelming odds. That the stones were taken from his company is not his fault.
'I have never known trolls to ally with other beasts or to covet such things as my dwarves were transporting. Were it not for their historical merit, the stones would be wholly unremarkable. This is very disturbing.'

'There are cave-claws among the ruins of Ost Dúrgonn, not far north-east of the Last Bridge, but how or why the beasts would carry off the stones Heithur is seeking, I do not know.
'Perhaps some other foe is to blame, but the cave-claws are closest to the Bridge and may have played some part in weakening the dwarf-company or in drawing them off the road.
'Travel north-east of the Last Bridge until you reach the ruins of Ost Dúrgonn and seek within their crumbling walls for either the stolen stones or the dwarves of Heithur's company. Speak with me again if you decide to go that way -- I would have you perform another task among the ruins.'

'Are you...here to help? Be careful, friend! A mighty cave-claw has slain...the rest of my....'
The dwarf shudders with exhaustion. 'This monstrous cave-claw...is some pet...of the trolls...that stole the stones we...were bearing....'
Search Ost Dúrgonn for Missing Dwarves
The Stolen Stones
The dwarves of Heithur Ironfist's company have fallen upon some misfortune near the Last Bridge, and the stones they were transporting to Glóin in Rivendell were lost.
'Hurry and speak to Rochwen about this, north of here on the road -- every minute wasted is a minute in which Lord Glóin's lack of gifts may insult his hosts!'

'What did she say? Ruins to the north-east of the Last Bridge are infested with cave-claws? That could be it, ${PLAYER}, that could be it! Hurry and look for the stones, or for the dwarves that bore them!'
'Rochwen, north of here on the road, is well-acquainted with threats in the area and may know what evil could have befallen Heithur's missing dwarves.'
'You should bring this information to Heithur Ironfist at once.'
'Find Heithur Ironfist...and tell him that the stones were stolen...by trolls. I'll be fine...you must hurry! I will...rejoin him later....'

Rochwen is along the road, north of Barachen's camp in the South Trollshaws.
Heithur Ironfist has asked you to speak with Rochwen about what threats could have overtaken his dwarf-company by the Last Bridge.

Cave-claws infest the ruins of Ost Dúrgonn north-east of the Last Bridge.
Rochwen believes that the cave-claws of Ost Dúrgonn could not have defeated a company of dwarves, but that they may have played some role in the defeat of Heithur's couriers.

Heithur Ironfist is at Barachen's camp, east of the Last Bridge and south of the road, on a sloping hill in the shadow of tall cliffs.
You have learned from Tóki Whitebeard that the stones his company was transporting have been stolen by trolls, apparently aided by the monstrous cave-claw you defeated.
A shattered crate lies near the foot of the Last Bridge

'Heithur Ironfist was telling me about the missing dwarves while you were away, ${PLAYER}. Glóin of the Lonely Mountain requested the delivery of some stones of historical value from Thorin's Hall as a sign of good faith for the Elves of Rivendell -- he is visiting Imladris on a mission of some importance -- and Heithur is worried that Glóin will be made a laughing-stock without such gifts.
'He is mistaken, of course. Master Elrond treats all with respect and honour and has no need for such baubles. I have told Heithur he need not worry on that account, but he does not listen.
'Perhaps the dwarves were surprised before they had come very far into the Trollshaws, ${PLAYER}? Speak with Alphlanc at the Last Bridge...perhaps she has seen some sign of their passing.'
The crate has been smashed open and its contents removed. Whatever it once contained has been stolen by parties unknown.

'You've found the crate my dwarves were bringing with them? I had hoped that you might return with the stones, but it sounds from your tale that someone else has already made off with them.
'This is inexcusable! We have to find them, ${PLAYER}, or Lord Glóin will be made a laughing-stock!'

'I am afraid to say I have seen no sign of these dwarves you are looking for -- is Heithur Ironfist certain they came this way?
'You should search the area around the Bridge very carefully. Some sign of trouble might have been missed, or well-hidden by whatever evil fate befell the dwarves.'
Search the area around the Last Bridge
Search the shattered dwarf-crate
Trouble by the Last Bridge

Heithur Ironfist is concerned about his missing dwarves, but he is especially worried about their cargo of historically-significant stones from Thorin's Hall bound for Glóin, and he wants them recovered.
'Barachen sent one of his Elves to the Last Bridge, didn't he? You should speak with this Elf about my dwarves, and without delay!'
'Alphlanc is at the Last Bridge, on the western edge of the Trollshaws. It could be that she knows the fate of Heithur's dwarves.'
'You have located the crate containing the stones, but they have been removed? You should speak with Heithur about this, but he will not be pleased to hear it, I am certain.'
'The Last Bridge is to the west -- just follow the road. Alphlanc may have seen some sign of the missing dwarves, but I must admit that she has not mentioned it to me.'

'You found the crate Heithur's dwarves were escorting, but the contents were removed? These are grim tidings, ${PLAYER}. Journey to Barachen's camp, south of here, at the top of the shadowed slope, and give the dwarf this news. He will not be pleased to hear it, but he would want to know.'
'Examine the area around the Last Bridge carefully, friend, and you might find some sign of the dwarves for whom you are searching.'
'You found a shattered crate of dwarf-make? You should examine it more closely, ${PLAYER}!'
'You should return to Heithur Ironfist at Barachen's camp, east of here and south of the road, and tell him what you have discovered -- that his dwarves have almost certainly fallen to an ill fate!'

Alphlanc is at the Last Bridge on the western edge of the Trollshaws, where the road passes into the Lone-lands.
Barachen has asked you to speak with Alphlanc at the Last Bridge to see if she has seen sign of the missing dwarves.

The Last Bridge supports the road as it winds west out of the Trollshaws and passes into the Lone-lands.
Alphlanc has asked you to search the area immediately around the Last Bridge closely for some sign of the missing dwarves.

A smashed crate lies at the foot of the Last Bridge, on the water's edge.
You have located a smashed crate by the Last Bridge that appears to be of dwarf-make. You should investigate further.

Heithur Ironfist is at Barachen's camp, east of the Last Bridge, on a sloping hill in the shadow of the southern cliffs. The Elf Rochwen stands on the road north of the camp, ready to aid travellers.
Heithur will want to hear about your discovery of a shattered dwarf-crate at the base of the Last Bridge, emptied of its contents.

'I bid you welcome, friend, but must give you a word of caution. Servants of the Enemy passed across the Last Bridge and swept into the Trollshaws no less than two months ago, pursuing a small company. They were hindered at the Ford of Bruinen, and the good people were brought to safety, but...not all of the evil ones were accounted for.
'Barachen maintains a camp to the east, on a hill south of the road. Bring him this message from me, if you are going that way: \qno agents of evil have entered the Trollshaws by the Last Bridge, but so too have none left it. Whatever evil lurks among the ruins of old Rhudaur...remains there.\q
'I thank you for this, friend. Tread with care and follow the road east until you see my friend Rochwen. She can guide you to Barachen's camp.'

'You bring word from Alphlanc? I am gladdened that she has not encountered any evil creatures, but it is clear to the Wise that an unseen evil is often the worst.
'Still, I am glad of your tidings. If you are willing to help us watch the wilderness for signs of evil, you will be doing us a great service.'
Scouting the Wild
Alphlanc is watching the road as it runs over the Last Bridge for any sign that servants of the Enemy might slip into -- or out of -- the Trollshaws.
'This Elf, Barachen, has agreed to help me with the troubles I have encountered here in the Trollshaws. If you are of a mind to, you could lend him a hand.'
'If you are looking for Barachen's camp, you will find it to the south. Leave the road and follow the slope to the right as it winds up the side of those cliffs.'

'Barachen has a camp not far to the east, on a hill south of the road. Follow the road until you see my friend Rochwen. She can show you the way to Barachen's camp.
'Bring him word that the road over the Last Bridge remains clear, though the evil that crept into the Trollshaws seems to remain here.'
'I will maintain my watch over the Last Bridge and hold it against any servant of the Enemy.'
'The road is always dangerous. Use caution on your travels, friend.'
'Barachen's camp is south of here. Follow the sloping hill to the right as it climbs.'
'My good friend Alphlanc keeps watch over the Last Bridge, west of here.'
'The road winds east to the Ford of Bruinen, and then climbs to Imladris.'

Barachen is at his camp east of the Last Bridge, on a hill south of the road. Alphlanc told you to follow the road east until you see her friend Rochwen, who can further guide you.
Alphlanc asked you to bring word to Barachen that no evil has entered the Trollshaws while she has been watching the Last Bridge, though neither has any left.
Defeated boars in the South Trollshaws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our dwarf-friend here has requested my assistance with a matter of some urgency, and we should do what we can to help him. He was part of a company of dwarves that was commanded to bring certain relics from Thorin's Hall to the dwarf Glóin, currently staying in Rivendell.
'Heithur Ironfist travelled ahead to notify his lord that the dwarves would soon arrive, but after the passage of some days, he grew worried. The company never arrived at Rivendell, and Heithur has now come back along the road seeking them.
'There are many boars to the west, and I fear that the dwarves may have been beset by the creatures and overwhelmed. The fury of creatures in the Trollshaws is often underestimated by those from afar. Defeat some of the boars and look for any sign of the missing dwarves.'
'I am both disappointed and heartened that you did not find any sign of Heithur's dwarves among the boars, ${PLAYER}. They may yet live, though I have little hope of it.'
Defeat boars in the South Trollshaws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Trampling Hooves
The Elf Barachen and his friends have been told to scout the South Trollshaws for signs of evil and have learned that a company of dwarves bound for the area may have fallen to misfortune.
'My dwarves should have come this way, but they're nowhere to be found! If they really have been trampled by the wild boars of this place, the boars will soon taste of my vengeance!'
'No sign of them? Well, go tell Barachen. It seems like he was mistaken -- no boar could best any of my dwarves!'

'The boars of the Trollshaws are most ferocious and are best avoided. If Heithur's dwarves thought to hunt some of the creatures to break the monotony of their journey, they may well have come to an unhappy end.
'Defeat some of the boars to the west and remain alert for some sign of the missing dwarves.'
'You'll find boars further to the west, south of the road. Their hooves often score the muddy earth that lies in the shadow of the tall cliffs.'

Boars can be found in the South Trollshaws, west of Barachen's camp.
Barachen asked you to search for the missing dwarves among the boars to the west of his camp. If the dwarves fell afoul of the creatures, some sign may still remain.

Barachen is at his camp in the South Trollshaws, south of the road and in the shadow of tall cliffs.
Barachen is waiting to hear whether you found any sign of the missing dwarves among the boars of the Trollshaws.

'Greetings, friend, and welcome to Imladris. Are you here at the behest of the Rangers? Perhaps you would aid us in patrolling these lands.
'I believe Barachen could use your assistance. He makes his camp not far to the east of the Last Bridge from the Lone-lands, on a hill south of the road.
'You should speak with him and learn how you might aid him.'
You were sent by Anhebir? If so, you are welcome here indeed. There is much to be done.'
To Barachen
The Elf Barachen patrols near the Last Bridge, guarding the passage from the Lone-lands into the Trollshaws.

Barachen makes his camp not far east of the Last Bridge from the Lone-lands, on a hill south of the road.
Anhebir has sent you to lend what aid you may to the Elf Barachen.
Defeated Stone-trolls in the southern Trollshaws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your news of Tóki Whitebeard has me worried, ${PLAYER}. Trolls should have no interest in unremarkable stones of the sort Heithur has described, and yet it seems that the dwarves were attacked solely for the purpose of attaining them.
'We must do something about the stone-trolls, ${PLAYER}, or I fear this land will slip even further into the wild. The road is already more perilous than it should be, and with Stone-trolls attacking travellers without cause....
'Defeat Stone-trolls in the southern Trollshaws, and we may yet avoid this grim future. Bring allies, for Stone-trolls are hardy foes.'
'You have done us all a great service, ${PLAYER}. I hope that this disturbing new behaviour among the Stone-trolls has been brought to an end by your actions.'
Defeat Stone-trolls in the southern Trollshaws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Very Unlike Trolls
Barachen is concerned by Tóki Whitebeard's tale and fears what implications this unusual behaviour of the Stone-trolls might have for the Trollshaws.
'You should do something about the Stone-trolls, ${PLAYER}, and you should do it at once!'
'The Stone-trolls in the southern Trollshaws are formidable foes, but you and your allies must face them. Their unusual behaviour may have grim echoes if they are not dealt with at once.'

'There are stone-trolls throughout the southern Trollshaws, ${PLAYER}, but I can tell you where you will almost certainly find them. To the east, the road dips southward for a short ways before curving north again. You will find stone-trolls among the trees within this bend, and north of the road.'
'The Stone-trolls are a real threat to travellers in the region.'
'You have been a great help to us, and for that you have my thanks.'

Stone-trolls can be found throughout the southern Trollshaws, but Rochwen may have more information about their location.
Barachen has asked you to defeat some of the Stone-trolls of the southern Trollshaws in an attempt to discourage their newly-aggressive behaviour.

Barachen is at his camp south of the road that runs through the southern Trollshaws, on a sloping hill in the shadow of tall cliffs.
Barachen will be pleased to know that you have defeated many Stone-trolls in the area.

'It appears that we are dealing not with one brood of spiders, ${PLAYER}, but with two! I do not know for what purpose these two broods have formed an alliance within the Wovenvales, but I can guess at it -- to prepare for an assault on the rest of the Trollshaws.
'If these creatures do belong to separate broods, then I propose that the venom of one may be deadly to the other, and that the opposite case may also be true! If this is so, we may be able to turn their own weapons against them, and eliminate each of the deadly broods! The trapdoor-spiders and the flesh-gnawer Spiders cannot be allowed to remain here.
'If you are prepared for another adventure, ${PLAYER}, I ask you to journey once more into the Wovenvales. Defeat spiders of each brood and retrieve their fangs. Then we will sing the next verse of our tale!'
'You have returned with the fangs of the trapdoor-spiders and the flesh-gnawer spiders? Now we shall see if my guess was correct, and if we can turn their own weapons against them.'

'I am still waiting for you to return with fangs from the trapdoor-spiders and the flesh-gnawer spiders. Only then can I prepare the next weapon in our storehouse -- their own venom, used against them!'
Bring trapdoor fangs and flesh-gnawer fangs to Thoroniel
The Deadly Broods
Thoroniel believes that the Wovenvales are infested with two different broods of spider, and she has formed a plan to deal with both of them.
'Search within the Wovenvales to the north-west and collect fangs from trapdoor and flesh-gnawer spiders.'

Two broods of spiders make their home in the Wovenvales of the North Trollshaws.
Thoroniel has asked you to collect fangs from the two different spider-broods in the North Trollshaws: the trapdoor-spiders and the flesh-gnawer spiders.

Thoroniel is just outside the Wovenvales of the North Trollshaws.
Thoroniel is waiting for you to return with the fangs you collected from each of the broods of spider in the North Trollshaws.
Defeated spiders in the Wovenvales (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You have arrived at just the right moment, ${PLAYER} -- any later and the spiders of the Wovenvales might have spilled from their valley and forced me to retreat. Once the creatures escape the valley, there will be little to stand between them and the rest of the Trollshaws, and Imladris would become the only beacon in the darkness.
'This may already be the case, but against the spiders, at least, we can fight. Not all servants of the Enemy are unopposable.
'These spiders are a particularly dangerous breed, or I would have already journeyed into the valley to face them. Bring allies with you, ${PLAYER}, and cleanse the Wovenvales of this filth.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}, but this is only the beginning! Your tale of valour against the spiders of the Wovenvales has encouraged me, but it also contains news that gives me pause. There are more spiders within the Wovenvales than I suspected.
'And yet I believe this may prove a great help to us. If I am correct in my guess, we may be able to turn these great numbers to our advantage. We must find out if this is so, and quickly!'
Defeat spiders in the Wovenvales (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fighting the Brood
Thoroniel has been keeping an eye on the activity of the spiders in the North Trollshaws and has become alarmed at the recent surge in their number.
'The Wovenvales are crawling with spiders, ${PLAYER}. Bring allies with you, for the creatures are both vicious and innumerable.'

Spiders have made their home in the Wovenvales of the North Trollshaws.
Thoroniel has asked you to defeat spiders in the Wovenvales and advised you to bring allies.

Thoroniel is in the North Trollshaws, just outside the Wovenvales in the north-west corner.
Thoroniel is waiting to hear that you have defeated the spiders that stalk the Wovenvales.

'We need to act with haste, ${PLAYER}, or we will squander the opportunity your efforts have given us. We must seek out the queens of the trapdoor-spiders and the flesh-gnawer spiders and put an end to their evil. Only then will we be certain of stopping the increase of spiders in the Trollshaws.
'You and your allies must journey deep into the Wovenvales to confront the trapdoor-spider queen. While you pursue her, I will seek out and destroy the flesh-gnawer queen. Together our efforts will end the threat of spiders in the Wovenvales.
'Fortune smile on you, ${PLAYER}. I will meet you here in victory when you have defeated the trapdoor-spider queen.'

'You have had better fortune than I have, ${PLAYER}, for I was unable to find the queen of the flesh-gnawer brood. I believe there was a struggle between the two broods -- for what reason I do not know -- and the queen of the flesh-gnawer spiders was cast out.
'Or perhaps she was the victor, and the trapdoor-spider queen was left behind to face you in defeat. I do not know. It is a mystery, and one that I cannot resolve to my satisfaction.
'Our task here is half-completed, but we must be satisfied with this for the time being. We have halted the threat, and that must be enough. We will find the flesh-gnawer queen, somewhere, and then we will finish things with her.'
The time for the final leg of Thoroniel's campaign against the spiders of the Wovenvales has come.

'Gather your allies and journey once more into the Wovenvales in search of the trapdoor-spider queen. I will find the queen of the flesh-gnawer spiders and deal with her accordingly. Meet me back here in victory!'
'Thoroniel was pleased with your efforts in the Wovenvales.'
'The flesh-gnawer queen cannot hide forever. We will find her some day.'
'I am glad for your aid, ${PLAYER}.'
'The flesh-gnawer queen cannot escape my blade forever.'

The trapdoor-spider queen is somewhere deep within the Wovenvales.
Thoroniel has asked you and your allies to defeat the trapdoor-spider queen while she seeks the queen of the flesh-gnawer spiders.

Thoroniel should be back outside the Wovenvales if her mission to defeat the flesh-gnawer queen was a success.
Thoroniel will be pleased to hear that you have defeated the trapdoor-spider queen.
Poured flesh-gnawer venom onto trapdoor egg-sacs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Poured trapdoor venom onto flesh-gnawer egg-sacs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If I have guessed right, venom of the trapdoor-spiders will be poisonous to the flesh-gnawer spiders, and the opposite will hold true as well!'
Thoroniel scrapes the venom from the spider-fangs and pours it into two bottles. 'Return to the Wovenvales and pour one brood's venom onto egg sacs of the other, ${PLAYER}. Let us put an end to this spider-threat before the eggs hatch and the trapdoor and flesh-gnawer spiders pour out into the Trollshaws...and then beyond!'

'You have returned! Did you have enough venom for all of the egg-sacs you found?
'I sense the winds turning in our direction, ${PLAYER}. The Wovenvales will soon be free of the trapdoor and flesh-gnawer spiders. I can feel it.'
'You have not returned with the bottles of venom I gave you? Why have you failed to do this?'
Pour flesh-gnawer venom onto trapdoor egg-sacs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Pour trapdoor venom onto flesh-gnawer egg-sacs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring venom-bottles to Thoroniel
Their Own Weapons
Thoroniel has prepared two bottles of poison from the trapdoor and flesh-gnawer fangs you brought to her, hopeful that their venom can be used against them.

'You will find the egg sacs of the trapdoor-spiders and those of the flesh-gnawer spiders within the Wovenvales, guarded by their respective broods. Pour venom belonging to each brood on egg sacs of the other, and we may be able to halt the spread of spiders into the rest of the Trollshaws!'

Trapdoor egg sacs and flesh-gnawer egg sacs can be found throughout the Wovenvales.
Thoroniel has given you two bottles of venom, and asked you to pour venom from one bottle onto egg sacs belonging to the other brood, and to do the same for the remaining bottle.

Thoroniel is outside the Wovenvales in the North Trollshaws.
The Elf-scout Thoroniel is waiting to hear whether you successfully made use of the venom-bottles she gave you.
Defeated Whiskerback Cave-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Cave-claws do not carry away treasures, ${PLAYER}, no matter how precious they seem to us, and the stones Heithur lost were wholly unremarkable to those without an interest in their histories.
'I am more concerned that the whiskerbacks of Ost Dúrgonn have somehow become emboldened, attacking travellers along the road or within sight of the Last Bridge. I believe that some corrupting disease has afflicted the cave-claws, making them more aggressive than they are wont. My friend Calenthon has observed something similar in the bears of Nan Tornaeth -- it could be that the cave-claws have a similar affliction.
'Ost Dúrgonn is north-east of the Last Bridge. Defeat whiskerback cave-claws wherever you find them, but especially among the ruins where they can be found in great numbers. Bring caution with you.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}, and have brought me hope that the spread of this disease among the cave-claws has been curbed.'
Defeat Whiskerback Cave-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Some Disease Affects Them
Rochwen believes that the whiskerback cave-claws in the ruins of Ost Dúrgonn, north-east of the Last Bridge, have become corrupted by some disease.

'Ost Dúrgonn is north-east of the Last Bridge and the whiskerback cave-claws that make their home among the ruins have been corrupted by some foul disease. If they have begun attacking travelers in this land, it is our duty to fight them, wherever they be found.'
'Rochwen has noticed that cave-claws in the South Trollshaws have also been afflicted with this disease? That does not bode well for travelers in this land, ${PLAYER}.'
'I am glad that you defeated some of the diseased cave-claws in the South Trollshaws for Rochwen, ${PLAYER}. It is an unpleasant task, but it is necessary.'
'The cave-claws of Ost Dúrgonn grow more aggressive every day.'
'Some fell disease is at work among the beasts of the Trollshaws.'
'Rochwen sent word to me of disease among the cave-claws of Ost Dúrgonn.'
'You did well to aid Rochwen by fighting the diseased cave-claws to the south.'

Diseased whiskerbacks come down into the low-lands from the ruins of Ost Dúrgonn, north-east of the Last Bridge.
Rochwen has asked you to defeat some of the ferocious cave-claws in the South Trollshaws.

Rochwen is north of Barachen's camp, by the road that runs through the South Trollshaws.
Rochwen will be pleased to know that you have defeated some of the diseased cave-claws that come forth from the ruins of Ost Dúrgonn near the Last Bridge.

'I have travelled throughout much of Nan Tornaeth in recent days, and few things trouble me like the corruption that has taken some of the beasts here. A fell malady has seized the bears that hunt in Nan Tornaeth, twisting their minds and bodies.
'I do not know if this vile malady can spread to other creatures, ${PLAYER}, but I want to know its source. We cannot risk this corruption leaving Nan Tornaeth and spreading across the Bruinen to Imladris itself.
'Bring me pelts from the corrupted bears that stalk the valleys of Nan Tornaeth, and I will examine them for some sign of the malady's source.'

'You have returned with the tainted bear-hides? Good, good. Allow me to examine them, and perhaps they will reveal some sign of the source of their corruption.
'I do not...wait, here is something. Yes, I see that these are present in most of the pelts that you brought: stone splinters of some kind. And here is the one responsible! A large piece of stone...it seems to be a fragment of an arrowhead.
'These bears have all been struck with arrows or spears, and I feel these weapons may be to blame for the disease.'
'You have not yet brought me the tainted bear-hides for which I asked. Without them, I cannot determine the source of the corruption that has afflicted the creatures!'
Bring tainted bear-hides to Calenthon
Beasts Among the Ruins
Calenthon has observed some foul disease corrupting the bears of Nan Tornaeth and wants to ensure it does not pose a threat to travellers in the area.
'Corrupted bears stalk the passes and valleys of Nan Tornaeth, and their pelts may give me some sign of the source of the evil with which they have been stricken.'

Corrupted bears stalk the passes and valleys of Nan Tornaeth.
Calenthon is concerned about the corruption that seems to have affected the bears of Nan Tornaeth and wants you to bring him their pelts for study.

Calenthon is north-west of Thorenhad, keeping watch over Nan Tornaeth.
Calenthon is waiting for you to return with tainted bear-hides from the diseased bears of Nan Tornaeth.
Collected gaunt-man's emblem

'The Hillmen of Rhudaur have some foul connexion to the wights that stalk the ruins of Nan Tornaeth, I am certain of it. I am certain too that this connexion has given rise to the disease that afflicts the beasts of the area.
'We must find and sever this alliance if we are to strike against the descendents of traitorous Rhudaur, ${PLAYER}!
'Defeat the Hillmen throughout Nan Tornaeth. You will find them especially to the north-east, near the ruins of Minas Ciliant and those on Amon Varadh. One of the Hillmen may have an artifact of some kind that will bring their connexion to the wights to light.'

'This emblem is that of a gaunt-man named Gúrdring, ${PLAYER}! I do not know the strength of this creature, but one such as he would have power to command the wights of Nan Tornaeth!
'Gúrdring must have given these emblems to the Hillmen as a sign of mastery over them, or for some other purpose we cannot perceive. It is of no matter, however, for our course is clear.
'We must defeat this Gúrdring, ${PLAYER}, for he is too powerful an ally for the Hillmen and could drive them against us in great force, with wights at their backs and a fell cry on the air.'

'You have not returned with an artifact or emblem that is of any use to us, ${PLAYER}. Defeat the Hillmen of Rhudaur until you find some clue to the association between them and the wights that stalk Nan Tornaeth by night.'
Collect a token from the Hillmen of Rhudaur
Bring Gúrdring's emblem to Calenthon
Keepers of the Dead
Calenthon believes that the Hillmen of Rhudaur in Nan Tornaeth have some foul association with the wights that stalk the ruins by night.

'Defeat the Hillmen of Rhudaur in Nan Tornaeth, ${PLAYER}, north-east of here. Look especially on Amon Varadh and at Minas Ciliant. One of the Hillmen is certain to bear something that will reveal their connexion to the wights that stalk this place.'

The Hillmen of Rhudaur can be found throughout Nan Tornaeth, north-east of Calenthon, at Amon Varadh and Minas Ciliant.
Calenthon has asked you to defeat some of the Hillmen of Rhudaur in Nan Tornaeth and bring him some sign of their connexion with the wights that stalk the area by night.

Calenthon is in Nan Tornaeth, north-west of Thorenhad.
You found a curious emblem on the body of a fallen Hillman. You should bring it to Calenthon at once.
Defeated Gúrdring
Defeated wights in Nan Tornaeth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Gúrdring is sure to be somewhere deep within Nan Tornaeth, hiding within the ruins. He must be defeated if we are to keep the Hillmen from becoming too powerful.
'I would also ask you to defeat some of the wights under Gúrdring's command. Move with caution, for these creatures are terrible.
'Once Gúrdring and his wights are no longer a threat, my task here will be much easier to perform. The wilderness always holds danger, but a gaunt-man and his servants pose an unnatural danger that must be fought wherever it may arise.'

'Gúrdring is defeated, and the wights he commanded have been pushed back? You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. Nan Tornaeth is always a dangerous place, but you have done well to help me combat the rise of new threats in this area.'
Defeat Gúrdring
Defeat wights in Nan Tornaeth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Master of the Risen
Calenthon has learned that the Hillmen of Rhudaur in the area have pledged their lives to a gaunt-man named Gúrdring and the wights he commands.

'The gaunt-man Gúrdring commands the wights of Nan Tornaeth from somewhere deep within the ruins to the north-east, ${PLAYER}. Search beyond the bridge of Thoniant, and you will surely find his evil.
'Put an end to it, my friend, and we will keep old Rhudaur from rising again.'
'The descendents of Rhudaur will walk Nan Tornaeth forever in payment for their old betrayals.'
'Calenthon told us of your victory over the gaunt-man Gúrdring.'
'Malloval has told me of your victory over Gúrdring.'
'The ruins of old Rhudaur are dangerous, but you have braved them to great success.'

The gaunt-man Gúrdring stalks the ruins in north-east Nan Tornaeth.
Calenthon has asked you to defeat the gaunt-man that has allied with the Hillmen of Rhudaur.

Calenthon is within Nan Tornaeth, north-west of Thorenhad.
Calenthon will be pleased to know that you have slain the gaunt-man Gúrdring and defeated many of the wights under his control.
This would be a good place to use Calenthon's whistle
You successfully defended Malloval

'If the Hillmen of Rhudaur are wielding spears and arrows coated with some disease-bearing filth, they are a more deadly foe than we had suspected.
'I sent my falcon, Malloval, to the north-east to spy upon the Hillmen, but he has not returned and I fear for his safety. If he has been struck with one of their fell weapons....
'Nay, I must not think of such things. I use this whistle to summon him when he is flying afar amidst the peaks and valleys...take it and climb the hill to the south. Blow the whistle from its sloping side, and Malloval should come to you, or at the very least answer your call with one of his own. If the latter, go to him, for it is likely he is beset by danger! You may wish to take friends, for this region is not safe.'
The falcon has been wounded by an arrow and hops about restlessly. He must be defended from his foes, or he will surely perish!

'You have earned my gratitude many times over, ${PLAYER}, for the defence of my friend Malloval. He managed to fly back to me, and it appears he has escaped the sting of the corrupting malady. He has already returned to his duties -- such devotion and courage he has!
'Still, my heart is uneasy. I do not like what you tell me of wights and Hillmen working as allies. Something is wrong.'
'You must return my whistle to me, ${PLAYER}. I will have need of it.'
Use Calenthon's whistle on the southern slope
Find and defend Malloval
Locate Malloval
Use Calenthon's whistle on the southern slope
Bring Calenthon's whistle back to Calenthon
Calenthon and Malloval
Calenthon has sent his falcon Malloval to scout the Rhudaur ruins in Nan Tornaeth a long while ago, but Malloval has not returned.
'The slope to the south would be an ideal place to summon Malloval with the whistle I gave you.'

'You have heard a falcon in the skies to the north-east? That must have been Malloval! Quickly, you must hurry to him -- if he has been wounded, he may have fallen onto the bridge of Thoniant, just north and east of here. The Hillmen often travel across that bridge. You must defend Malloval!'

The slope south of Calenthon would be an ideal location at which to blow the whistle he gave you to summon Malloval.
Calenthon gave you a whistle with which to summon his falcon, Malloval. He suggested you take friends for safety.
After using Calenthon's whistle, you heard a falcon cry above the ruins near the bridge of Thoniant in Nan Tornaeth.

Calenthon is south of the bridge of Thoniant, in Nan Tornaeth.
Calenthon will be pleased to hear that you defended his falcon, Malloval, from the Hillmen of Rhudaur and waits for you to return with his whistle.
You have found a perfect feather

'Elladan and Elrohir have entrusted me with watching over the road through the Bruinen Gorges, but my mind keeps drifting, and I cannot keep my eyes upon the road.
'There is an Elf-maiden of unsurpassed loveliness in whose company I delight, and I wish to make her a gift she will recognize as a sign of my affection for her. It must not be any passing thing, but a token of such beauty that her breath will be quite taken away -- nothing less will do!
'And yet, I am charged with watching the road. I do not wish to fail in my duty, so I would ask you a favour, since you are not so charged: search among the high places of the Bruinen Gorges for a hendroval nest and retrieve a perfect feather from it. The creatures are dirty and unwholesome, but sometimes feathers of incomparable beauty are left in their nests...undoubtedly the feathers of the hendroval's prey. I will use the feather in the crafting of my gift.'

'This is a beautiful feather, ${PLAYER}! I pity the bird that fell to the talons of the hendroval to yield such a feather, but the memory of it shall be venerated when this feather is worn by my Narlinn.
'This feather will be an excellent addition to my gift, for I have decided what to make!'
'You do not have the feather you promised to bring me? You make me sad, ${PLAYER}.'
Search hendroval-nest
Bring beautiful feather to Arrod
A Perfect Feather
One of Elladan and Elrohir's scouts, Arrod, is torn between fulfilling his duties and trying to court an Elf-maid with whom he is smitten.

'Narlinn will not wait forever, ${PLAYER}! I refuse to abandon my duty, but my heart is heavy with the sorrow that I may not be able to make this gift for her!
'Hendrevail nest in the high places of the Bruinen Gorges, and sometimes leave the beautiful feathers of their prey behind. Bring me one, and I will use it to make my Elf-maid's gift.'

Hendrevail make their nests in the high places of the Bruinen Gorges.
Arrod has asked you to search the nests of the hendrevail and bring him a perfect tail-feather from one. The creatures are filthy, but sometimes the beautiful feathers of their prey are left in their nests.

Arrod is keeping watch over the Bruinen Gorges from his vantage point near ruins over the road.
Arrod is waiting for you to return with the perfect tail-feather you collected.
Found a perfect lily

'I have decided to craft a necklace for my Elf-maid, ${PLAYER}, and though the feather you brought me is a fine addition, it is not yet enough.
'Lilies grow along the banks of the Loudwater, the Bruinen to the east, and any of them would be pretty enough for an Elf-swain to give his love. Mine is no ordinary love, ${PLAYER}, and these white lilies will not be enough!
'Only a mauve lily of unsurpassing beauty will be lovely enough for my Elf-maid. Look for one somewhere along the Bruinen, and carefully -- lilies of such a shade are exceedingly rare!'

'Such beauty! This lily will do nicely, ${PLAYER}. You have my thanks, of course, and they are most heartfelt!
'It will just be a moment. Narlinn will cherish this necklace and recognize the depth of my affection for her!'
'You have not returned with the lily I requested, ${PLAYER}.'
Find the perfect lily
Bring the perfect lily back to Arrod
Lilies in the Valley
Arrod was pleased with the feather you brought him and has been inspired by it to craft a necklace for Narlinn.
'A mauve lily of unsurpassing loveliness is a rare thing and is only found along the Bruinen. Look with care! None of the white ones will do!'

A perfect lily grows somewhere along the Bruinen east of Arrod's post.
Arrod has asked you to bring him a perfect lily of exquisite beauty. No other kind will do.

Arrod is watching the road through the Bruinen Gorges from his vantage point near a set of hilltop ruins, west of the Bruinen.
Arrod will be delighted to see that you have found a lily of exquisite beauty.
'Arrod used to be so admiring of me, but lately he has been downright dismissive!'
'Arrod must be distracted if he did not make clear to you his intentions.'
'Have you taken Arrod's necklace to Faimir?'

'There, I have finished the necklace, ${PLAYER}. If you will bring this to Narlinn, I will be in your debt! You will find her at Thorenhad, the camp of the sons of Elrond located north-west of here, north of the bear dens.
'Narlinn believes that the maiden for whom I have been sighing is Faimir of Rivendell. She is lovely, and for a time I thought I loved her, but my time here in the wild has taught me that Narlinn is the one for whom my heart sings.
'Bring her this necklace with my fondest affection! I will stay here and continue my duties, though I will look forward to rejoining Narlinn in peace when the dark times against which we must guard have passed.'

'What? This necklace is from Arrod? You must be confused -- he is interested only in Faimir of Rivendell. He has told me this himself!
'You are well-meaning, ${PLAYER}, but I cannot take this. Return with this to Arrod, and tell him that you did not understand his charge.
'I will not hear anymore of this. I do not wish to embarrass you or Arrod any further. You have brought this beautiful necklace to the wrong Elf-maid!'
'Do you have something for me?'

'What? Why do you still have the necklace, ${PLAYER}? Do not tell me that Narlinn refused it!
'I see...I have become a victim of my own subtleties, my friend! So good was my performance that Narlinn believes that Faimir truly is the Elf-maiden for whom I have been sighing!
'I have a solution, ${PLAYER}. I will maintain my watch here, ever-vigilant and meet Narlinn personally when my duty here is done. I will then explain my true feelings to her! I should not have given you this task at all. This task is for Arrod of Rivendell, and Arrod of Rivendell alone!'
'Have you given Narlinn the necklace?'
Bring Arrod's necklace to Narlinn
Bring Arrod's necklace back to Arrod
A Gift for the Elf-maid
Arrod has prepared a necklace for the Elf-maid Narlinn with whom he is smitten.

'Narlinn? Why do you ask me about her? She is off at Thorenhad with Elladan and Elrohir, I think.
'My Arrod is also there, I think. He has been so thoughtful and admiring of me lately, as to inspire envy from the other maidens.'

'That necklace is very shoddily-made, ${PLAYER}. I do not want it.
'I am sure its maker is most ashamed of his hasty craftsmanship.'
'Thorenhad is west of here, and north of the bear dens of the Bruinen Gorges. Bring my necklace to Narlinn with my affection!'

'Arrod is scouting the Bruinen Gorges, and I am worried that by thinking always of Faimir, he pays no heed to his own safety or to his duty! Return this necklace to him, for there has been some mistake. He did not mean for you to bring it to me.'
'My performance must have been very convincing. Too convincing, I think!'
'I have so thoroughly convinced Narlinn that she is not the maiden for whom I was sighing! Alas!'
'I have never been accused of too much subtlety before, ${PLAYER}! How odd!'
'Arrod has grown distant as of late. I cannot imagine why!'
'I do not understand why Arrod has not paid me as much mind as he used to.'

Narlinn is at Thorenhad, the camp of the sons of Elrond located among the Bruinen Gorges, north of the bear dens.
Arrod has asked you to deliver the necklace to Narlinn, the Elf-maid who is the object of his devotion.

Arrod is at his vantage point high above the Bruinen Gorges, by an old set of ruins.
Narlinn has refused Arrod's gift and has sent you to return it to him.

'You are here to help Elladan and Elrohir? I am glad of it, but I would ask you to help me as well, if you have a moment.
'My friend Arrod is a good Elf, but he is not always as cautious as he is well-intentioned, and he often gets into trouble. Master Elrond recommended that he help keep watch over the Trollshaws, and indeed he has been assigned to scout the Bruinen Gorges, but I fear that his mind is not entirely on his duty.
'All of his thoughts dwell on Faimir, an Elf-maiden of our acquaintance in Imladris, and I fear he is not paying the attention he should to his own well-being and safety. Would you seek him out in the Bruinen Gorges and make sure he has not come to harm, ${PLAYER}? He is sure to have taken up a post overlooking the road.'

'You are from Thorenhad? Elladan and Elrohir entrusted me to scout the Bruinen Gorges for signs of evil, and I am doing so. I have not found much, but I must admit that I hope to find something -- there is an Elf-maid I hope to impress with my valour and my prowess in battle!'
A Scout among the Bruinen Gorges
Many scouts were dispatched across the Trollshaws to keep watch for signs of evil, and the sons of Elrond want to know if anything has been found.

'Please look to Arrod for me, ${PLAYER}. He is east of here, probably somewhere in the Bruinen Gorges, and though he should be keeping alert for signs of evil and ensuring his own safety, I fear he is likely daydreaming about the Elf-maiden Faimir.'
'I hope to prove my worth in the eyes of my Elf-maiden!'
'It has been quiet. If I were assigned to Nan Tornaeth, I would see some adventure!'

Arrod is keeping watch somewhere among the Bruinen Gorges, south-east of Thorenhad, at a position where he can overlook the road.
Narlinn has asked you to check on Arrod, currently scouting the Bruinen Gorges, though likely more focused on wooing the Elf-maiden Faimir.
Defeated cave-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'And to think, I wanted to seek adventure with my father on the way to the Lonely Mountain. Adventure decided to come to me instead!
'I think I've had my fill of it for quite a while....'
'Don't dawdle. Go on into the Silver Deep and lend Gimli a hand!'

'The halls of my father and my grandfather beckon to me. I will claim my gold and my birthright as King under the Mountain. No worm shall deny what is mine!
'Ah, to hold the Arkenstone once more....'

'The halls of my father and my grandfather beckon to me. I will claim my gold and my birthright as King under the Mountain. No worm shall deny what is mine!
'Ah, to hold the Arkenstone once more....'
It is plain to see that this once-living troll of flesh and blood has been turned to stone by the light of the sun.

'Cave-claws are such a nuisance! They burrow all over the place and weaken the walls. Oh well, they're better than the trolls that were here before!
'So Thorin's finally setting off, is he? Well it's about time, if you ask me! Fortunately, there's only one more dwarf to call. His name's Tvistur...you can find him deeper in the mine.
'You had best carry arms while you search for him, just in case you run into a cave-claw. You don't want to be caught unawares and defenceless.'

'Tvistur spoke of the Dourhands, did he? There is a long history with those particular dwarves and these halls.
'You see these halls were once part of an Elf refuge. Elves seeking to leave Middle-earth would meditate here before their long trip to the west. These halls also contained many relics -- relics that were much desired by Skorgrím, a lord of the Dourhands in elder days. He assaulted Edhelion, but was slain when the Elves brought the stone crashing down upon him.
'I will take this matter up with Thorin. For now, let us go to the assembly. Time is wasting!'

'Ah, between you and me, I'm glad for your help. The sooner we get done, the sooner we can see my father and the rest of the Company off!
'Here, you take this passage straight ahead, and I'll go off into the side passage.
'And don't take no for an answer...Thorin wants everyone there!'

'Ah, you're here. Took you long enough!
'It's about time for us to set off to reclaim the Lonely Mountain's treasures. Thorin wants to make a bit of a show of it, so he wants everyone gathered to usher him off. Just about everyone is over in front of the halls, west of here, but there are a few stragglers at work in the halls of the Silver Deep.
'I've already sent my Gimli on ahead to gather them, but he'll need your help. Go on in and give him a hand.'

'Did you find a weapon? Or at least something that will make do as one? Good!
'Now, let's go get Tvistur. I'll warn you that he won't come easily. He's a stubborn one...keeps to himself. That's why he's digging so far down in the Silver Deep.
'Well, we should move on. No sense standing here with our jaws flapping when there's work to be done. Let's go!'

'We must be quick. I don't know how long Gimli can keep that troll busy before the beast overpowers him.
'Follow me!'

Thorin and Company are preparing to leave from the Blue Mountains for the ancestral home of Durin's folk, the Lonely Mountain. Thorin has called together all the dwarves of the Blue Mountains for a final assembly.
'This day is long in coming. First we reclaim the Lonely Mountain from Smaug the Golden, then we drive the Orcs from Khazad-dûm!'
'This day is long in coming. First we reclaim the Lonely Mountain from Smaug the Golden, then we drive the Orcs from Khazad-dûm!'

'I just know they're going to give me the heaviest load on this trip. I'm not a pack mule, you know!
'Oh, go bother Glóin, why don't you?'

'I just know they're going to give me the heaviest load on this trip. I'm not a pack mule, you know!
'Oh, go bother Glóin, why don't you?'
'This will be a dangerous quest. The combined force of Girion and Thráin could not stop Smaug from laying waste to Dale and robbing us of our home and our wealth.'
'This will be a dangerous quest. The combined force of Girion and Thráin could not stop Smaug from laying waste to Dale and robbing us of our home and our wealth.'
'This is a pompous waste of time. We've a burglar to hire and a dragon to slay.'

'I'm glad you've come, ${PLAYER}, for the Orcs press us most cruelly. A few men have responded to my call for help, but fewer than I would have hoped.
'Are you ready to take up arms in defence of the town? Tell me when you are, and I will show you to your position!'

'Harper told me the news of your defence when I returned, ${PLAYER}, and you have my thanks! I am happy to report that I and a few others were able to rescue the trapped farmers in the North Downs, a rescue that would not have been possible without your aid here.
'The Orcs grow bolder, that much is clear. We must resist them as long as we can...I hope it will be long enough.
'Ah, do not listen to my dreary words! We won a victory today, and that is enough! Your skills improve with practice -- every attack of the Orcs makes us even stronger, until one day we will strike out at them and defeat them utterly!'

'I received word that some farmers on the North Downs have holed up in a small cave and are requesting assistance from Trestlebridge. Before your arrival, I feared they would be lost, for I could not leave the town with so few defenders -- but with your timely arrival, I see now a chance to save those farmers.
'I will ride to their defence, ${PLAYER}, and I entrust the safety of Trestlebridge to you. If any Orcs attack while I am away, you must keep them away from the bridge at any cost! If the bridge is taken, we lose what small advantage we have. Do not let them reach the bridge!
'A few men have pledged to aid in the defence. Speak to these hardy few and assign them their positions. I will see you again, if both our tasks lead to victory!'

'We meet once again, ${PLAYER}, and I must tell you that my spirits are raised by your presence! After you helped me fight off the Blackwold brigands that threatened my farm, I got to thinking. It isn't right for good people to live in fear. It was time for me to repay the favour you did me.
'Travellers passing through Bree spoke of the Orc-raids against Trestlebridge, and I realized that this was where I was needed. If the Orcs dare show their ugly faces again, we'll turn them away and send them howling back across the Downs, I don't doubt it!
'My son is here, too. He has a keen eye and is handy with his bow, if you remember. I'll stand over in the shade of that tower and keep my weapon at the ready!'

'We have done it, ${PLAYER}, and Trestlebridge is safe, for the moment. I do not think the Orcs will launch another attack for some time -- it is hard to remember, sometimes, that they, too, have need of rest. Though their masters may press them onward with whips and threats, even an Orc can succumb to exhaustion if pressed for too long in service of war.
'Tell me when you are ready to return to the town, and we can await the return of Severin Wheeler. I hope his task went as well, and the farmers he left to save have survived their dangers.
'Some of us were wounded this day, but still we stand against the Orcs, and will continue to do so for as long as it is necessary!'

'You might not remember me, ${PLAYER}, but I remember you! You helped my dad and me fight off the Blackwolds at our farm not so long ago. Cole Culvert would have been eating off our dishes and enjoying the fruits of our labours by now if it hadn't been for you...and don't think we don't appreciate it!
'My dad got to thinking, and one day he just up and asked if I wanted to go with him to fight the Orcs. The way I see it, I'd rather fight Orcs up north, Trestlebridge way, if it means we can avoid fighting them in the streets of Bree-town, or in our own fields! Everyone's got to do his own part.
'I've been practising with this bow since I was just a boy, and I reckon I can fell a few Orcs before they get too close. I'll call out their positions from that rise over there, if they're so bold as to attack the town while we're here.'
'Are you ready to return to the town? We will await the return of Severin Wheeler and recount to him the great deeds that were done today!'

'It is a pleasure to meet a fellow guardian, ${PLAYER}, and the defences will be stronger for your presence here!
'I am ashamed to admit that not long ago I had given up hope -- the darkness that presses in on us seemed too great, and I was filled with despair. But a young captain showed me that hope always remains, even in situations most dire.
'So I took up my sword once more and vowed to fight on in the defence of good people, even when all others have failed. I have come to Trestlebridge, last bulwark between Bree-land and the marauding Orcs of the north and will defend this place until I can defend it no more. We will prevail, ${PLAYER}, but we must remain alert. The Orcs could attack at any time, and if any reach the bridge, it is lost. Keep them away from the bridge at any cost!'

Instance: A Guardian's Duty
Severin Wheeler has enlisted your help in the defence of Trestlebridge. The town is hard-pressed by the Orcs, and guardians are needed to keep them from crossing into Bree-land.

'A guardian like yourself has also come to aid in the defence. His name is Hilton Harper, and I saw him checking the structure of the bridge not long ago. You should speak with him about the plan for defending this place, should the Orcs attack.'
'The town is safe, for the moment, so I count it a victory, ${PLAYER}. The Orcs will attack again, and when they do we will be ready!'

'My dad was talking to another guardian a short time ago -- Harper, his name was. He's probably around here somewhere. You should speak to him about the plan for defending the town, should the Orcs choose to attack while Severin Wheeler is away.'

'We have repelled the Orcs, for now, and we will repel them again if needed! I hope it is not for a while yet -- I need a good night's sleep!
'My dad may be able to fight tirelessly, but I do not yet have his endurance, though I hope to claim I have his courage!'

'I welcome you to Bree, Guardian ${PLAYER}, but I confess I do not have the time to spare in idle conversation -- there are brigands about, and though they have suffered some measure of defeat of late, they are still on the Bree-fields and within the Andrath, and their recent losses only stir them to boldness.
'Unless I am very much mistaken, you surely seek every opportunity to strengthen yourself. Well, I have many such opportunities available! Indeed, the brigands seem eager to present them to us! The worthy farmers of Bree-land are hard put to it, though, and we must protect their lands and their lives whenever either are threatened.
'I will set out to deal with brigand attacks to the north, but I need you elsewhere. Burle Pierson lives on a farm to the south of Bree-town, and he has reported several raids on his land. Each time he has fought them off, but he says they always return with more men, and soon he will be unable to resist them. Help him defend his farm, ${PLAYER}, and the training will surely be of use to you.'

'The light in your eye tells me that you have aided Burle Pierson with the defence of his farm, ${PLAYER}, and I am glad to hear it! It is a guardian's lot to put himself between danger and those who need protecting.
'Always remember that every battle makes you tougher, ${PLAYER}. Even now, your arm is stronger and your senses keener than when last I saw you. Train often, and you will find your ability to fend off attacks increasing. Indeed, that is already the case!
'Go forth, Guardian ${PLAYER}, and protect the good peoples of Middle-earth from the dangers they face. It is your lot to do so.'

'You are a guardian, ${PLAYER}? I am glad to hear it, for the brigands have been a constant threat to me and mine, and I don't know how much longer I can fight them off!
'Let us walk about my property and keep watch for any of the brigands that might have designs on my land. They said they would be back with great numbers, and I fear they will keep their oath!'

'You are known to me, ${PLAYER}, as a guardian of great skill and mighty deeds, and I can see that the tales I have heard do not miss the mark! Hail, and well-met at Noglond!
'You deserve to wield equipment that reflects your opposition to the forces of shadow, and your determination to fight to the last against them. I can help you prepare such equipment, but I tell you now that it will be no easy task.
'The scars we bear tell the tale of the battles we have fought, every conflict etching upon our bodies and minds the memory of all the good that we do. Your equipment should do the same, ${PLAYER}. Do not fear what lies ahead! Though your foes be fearsome, I know you have it in you to triumph. Speak with me if you are ready to begin this greatest of trials.'

The dwarf Wáli is at the outpost of Noglond, south of Thorin's Hall and west of the dwarf-city of Gondamon in Ered Luin.
You have been told to speak to Wáli, a courageous guardian who may have some words for you.

'I can make you a piece of equipment befitting your stature as a guardian, ${PLAYER}, but heed my warning: I will require several components for its making that will take you to dangerous lands and into great danger.
'But you are a guardian! Surely you will not shy away from such a challenge!
'I give to you this note, which contains my instructions on what components I will require and the order I would have you bring them to me. Every stage of the process will take some time, so follow the instructions I have set forth! I eagerly await your return with the first set of components, ${PLAYER}.'

'These boots fill me with anger, ${PLAYER}, anger that the Dourhands would be so bold as to seize Gabilazan from my kinsmen!
'You have done well to bring these and to bring the ashen hide of Grimgore. No longer will he stride the cliffs of Fasach-larran!
'If you can collect the next set of components as quickly, I will finish my work in no time at all! Look to my notes for guidance, and you will surely be back soon, friend Guardian!'
'You have not returned with the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}?'

'These scales look to be just the thing, ${PLAYER}, and these nails have just the right sort of gems! The equipment I make for you is sure to be something special, when it has such components on which to draw.
'Two components remain: a flawless scale of Lhugrien and a Warg-keeper's token. If you can retrieve these items, you will truly be counted among the mightiest of guardians.'
'You do not have the components for which I have asked, ${PLAYER}. What are you doing?'

'I marvel at your courage, ${PLAYER}, for none know better than I the ferocity of Lhugrien! I know too the reluctance with which Athpukh would part with his token.
'You are a mighty guardian, ${PLAYER}, and it is an honour to know you. Take this equipment with my regards, from one guardian to another!'
'You do not have the components for which I asked, ${PLAYER}. Why are you wasting my time?'

'I'd like to take a moment to congratulate you on your accomplishments, ${PLAYER}. You have got to be the most dedicated guardian I have ever met!
'If I am to believe the rumours, though, there is one that puts even your skills to shame! I've heard from my brother down south in a small town called Needlehole that there's an incredible guardian who calls the Shire his home. This guardian is apparently unmatched, and his name is Samwise Gamgee.
'My brother said he's not in the Shire any longer, so he didn't have a chance to meet this Samwise and learn any lessons he might have for a fellow guardian, and no one seems to know where he's gone! If you could find this Samwise, I'm sure he'd teach you a thing or two, since you're such an accomplished guardian, same as he is!'

'You were told what? You were told that I'm an incredible guardian, the finest in the Shire? Someone's pulling your leg, ${PLAYER} -- I'm no guardian! I think this dwarf is having some fun at your expense! Finest guardian....
'Actually, now that you mention it, I think I know what might have happened. You see, I'm not a guardian at all, but I am in fact a gardener, and although it's not right for me to boast, my flowers and vegetables have been quite well-received by my neighbours in the Shire on several occasions, and...
'Oh, bother! This Wáli's brother must have misheard someone, that's all! I don't know much about being a guardian, but I could give you some advice about gardening, if you were of a mind to listen! It's all about how well you watch the health of your plants and how effectively you respond to their changing conditions: by watering them, changing the amount of sunlight they receive, or re-spacing their neighbours. A guardian might learn a thing or two from a gardener, if you ask me!'

'Me, a guardian! Can you imagine?'
'I do miss my garden.'
'I wonder if we'll be setting back to the Shire soon?'
