'I can make you a weapon that befits your tremendous might as a guardian, ${PLAYER}, and I am happy to do so! As with all things, however, I must tell you that something of such worth will require a great deal of toil and hardship. It -- and you -- will be stronger for it!
'I give to you my instructions on how to obtain the components I will need if I am to fashion you such a weapon. I will need time between each stage of the process, so do not bring me everything at once! The notes I have given you will tell you when I will need everything.
'I will first need the cruel bludgeon of the snow-troll Shataz and five sulfur-tinged spears of the Tarkrîp. My notes should guide you right, ${PLAYER}!'

'You have done well to defeat Shataz, ${PLAYER}, and I am pleased that his tale is at last ended, for he brought much grief to my kin in his day.
'I thank you for these spears, as well. Note the poor craftsmanship...it is a wonder to me that weapons of goblin-make don't just fall apart when wielded! I will destroy these weapons and sprinkle the powder over the weapon I make for you to remind it of the fragility of its foes.
'I am ready for the next set of components. The instructions I gave to you will guide you once again.'
'You do not have the first set of components I need, ${PLAYER}? I must ask you, why?'

'Very well-done, ${PLAYER}, and with such speed, as well! Your weapon will become a great deal stronger when the memory of these foes become a part of it.
'I need only one more set of components, and these will be most difficult to obtain. Barashal the Gorthorog and Gruglok of Urugarth are fearsome opponents.
'One more thing, ${PLAYER}, if I could impose. When you face Barashal in Carn Dûm, I would ask you to shout this at him during the battle: \qThus are the kinsmen of Wáli avenged!\q I thank you for this, ${PLAYER}. I know that Svanr, Tralli, and Nossi would be pleased as well.'
'You do not have the things for which I asked, ${PLAYER}? Are you sure you are a guardian?'

'I greet you in victory, ${PLAYER}, and my heart is more glad than it has ever been of late, to know that Barashal is dead! Sleep well, my kinsmen -- you are avenged.
'It is an honour and a privilege to know you, ${PLAYER}, for you are truly mighty among guardians.
'I give to you this weapon with the hope that you will use it well and for the betterment of all the Free Peoples of Middle-earth.'
'You do not have the components I sought, ${PLAYER}? Why is this?'
Bring first set of components to Wáli
Bring second set of components to Wáli
Bring final set of components to Wáli
Implements of Battle
Wáli has agreed to help you fashion a weapon worthy of your might as a guardian. He has assured you that from great toil comes strength.
'My instructions should steer you right, ${PLAYER}. I need the cruel bludgeon of Shataz and five sulfur-tinged Tarkrîp-spears if I am to proceed with this weapon.'
'Have you misplaced my notes? I did not write them for my health, ${PLAYER}, and I am still waiting for those talons, mandibles, and claws! Do you want this weapon or not?'

'If you can defeat Barashal and retrieve from him his crimson horn, you and I will both benefit, ${PLAYER}. And I would appreciate it if you were to say this to Barashal when he falls: \qThus are the kinsmen of Wáli avenged!\q
'Somewhere within Urugarth, uruk commander Gruglok holds vigil over his arena. If you can take from him a Sigil of War, the weapon I fashion for you will be made the stronger.'

Wáli gave you his instructions containing the components he will need to fashion you a truly remarkable weapon.
Wáli asked you to return with the cruel bludgeon of Shataz and five sulfur-tinged Tarkrîp-spears.

Wáli is at the outpost of Noglond, south of Thorin's Hall and west of the dwarf-city of Gondamon, in Ered Luin.
Wáli is waiting for you to return with the first set of components he needs to fashion you a remarkable weapon.

Wáli gave you his instructions containing the components he will need to fashion you a truly remarkable weapon.
Wáli asked you to return with twenty grisly bat-talons, fifteen mottled spider-mandibles, and five hooked Warg-claws.

Wáli is at the outpost of Noglond, south of Thorin's Hall and west of the dwarf-city of Gondamon, in Ered Luin.
Wáli is waiting for you to return with the second set of components he needs to fashion you a remarkable weapon.

Wáli gave you his instructions containing the components he will need to fashion you a truly remarkable weapon.
Wáli asked you to return with a crimson Gorthorog-horn from Carn Dûm and a Sigil of War from Urugarth.

Wáli is at the outpost of Noglond, south of Thorin's Hall and west of the dwarf-city of Gondamon, in Ered Luin.
Wáli is waiting for you to return with the final set of components he needs to fashion you a remarkable weapon.
Collected the Elf-scroll

'I remember when Edhelion fell, though it was so many years ago. But Edhelion, once lost, is found again! While mining the Silver Deep, the dwarves discovered an entrance to Elf-hewn stone ruins.
'I would like you to retrieve some of the lost lore from the ruined libraries. I fear little survived the passing of time...the return of but a single scroll would gladden my heart.
'Find the library within the Silver Deep, in the caves below the ruins of Edhelion. At the foot of the southerly path, turn east and north.'

'Remember our time in the Silver Deep? Did you ever think you would be back? Well, it seems the Elf-ruins that we found housed some important libraries.
'You should venture into the hall and look about for anything of value. Have a look where their libraries once stood and bring back something of interest. Scrolls, books...things of that nature. I'm sure the Elves will be wanting them.
'You know where the Deep is, right? Just north-east of Frerin's Court, around the frozen pond and through the doors.'
Buried amongst piles of stone and ruined books, you manage to find a single scroll, a bit dusty but none the worse for wear.

'You're good and dusty! Like you were crawling through the Deep on your hands and knees!
'Eh? You found a scroll? Well hand it over, and I'll see that the Elves get it. Well done, ${RACE}! And here I thought I was sending you on a fool's errand!'
'Keep searching the ruins for that lore. The Elves will have some kind of reward for us if we're successful, I'm sure.'
'A blessing upon you, ${RACE}. Regardless of its contents, this scroll is a precious gift indeed. Anything that connects us to our past is a rare treasure, and I thank you for its safe return.'
'Do you have anything from the halls of Edhelion? There must be something left, even after all these years.'
Search the rubble of Edhelion for scrolls
Bring the scroll to ${RACE:Otur[D]|Gailthin}
The Lost Lore of Edhelion
The halls of Edhelion, an old refuge of the Elves, were lost for many years. Recent exploration in the Silver Deep mines revealed a passage into Edhelion where lost secrets lie in wait of discovery.
'Go into the dwarf-mines and search for lost lore of Edhelion. The entrance is in the north-east of road's southerly foot.'
'Search the Elf-halls for lore and return to me with anything you find. They are far inside the Silver Deep, to the north and east of Frerin's Court.'
'The lore you have recovered from Edhelion will ensure no one forgets those lost here on that terrible day, so long ago.'
'Those scrolls you recovered from the Silver Deep will go a long ways towards keeping the peace with the Elves!'

The Elf-libraries are deep inside the Silver Deep near the ruins of Edhelion, up the path leading north-east from the southerly foot of the road from the Elves' camp.
${RACE:Otur[D]|Gailthin} asked you to enter in through the abandoned dwarf-mine of the Silver Deep and search for some ruins of a library of Edhelion.
Bring the scroll you found in the ruined halls of Edhelion back to ${RACE:Otur at the Berghold[D]|Gailthin in the ruins of Edhelion}.
Collected lynx-pelts (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})

'The Dourhands do nothing to stem the growth of the lynx in this area. No surprise, to be honest. Despite their newfound ties to their cousins, the Longbeards, the Dourhands are the same dwarves that Skorgrím led against Edhelion centuries ago. We cannot expect them to be proper stewards of the land.
'Go into the wilds and cull the lynx population. You can find them in the wooded areas near the frozen lake down the road from here. You can also find them to the north.'
'Return the pelts of the creatures to me. It would be a waste to leave the furs out on the snow, and I am sure Durin's Folk would appreciate them in the cold nights to come.'

'Blast those Dourhands! They're supposed to be out hunting, but I see nary a one of them out there! There are too many lynx and not enough food to go around. Worse still, our friends, the thrushes, are falling prey to the beasts! We can't stand by and do nothing, so I'm asking you to go out on a hunting expedition for us.
'Kill a few of the lynx and keep them from doing more harm. Just north-east of Frerin's Court I saw a pride of the beasts.
'Oh, and be sure to bring back the pelts! The nights out here are cold and long, and we could use some warm furs to keep away the chill.'
'Well done! These are fine pelts. Fine indeed. I'll send these down to the tanner at once. On behalf of both dwarf and thrush alike, I thank you kindly.'
'Do you have the pelts?'
'You return victorious? Excellent, friend. Perhaps these pelts will garner us trade with the Longbeards of Ered Luin.'
'Do you have the pelts?'
Collect lynx-pelts (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Bring the lynx-pelts to ${RACE:Nos Grimsong[D]|Laergil}
Restoring the Balance
The lynx that prowl Thorin's Gate are too many for the land to support. They attack travellers and the thrushes, long-time friends of the dwarves.
'You will find the lynx prides out in the forested area around the frozen lake down the road from here. You might also find some to the north. Return with pelts and be careful.'
'What are you waiting for? Time to go a-hunting for lynx! And don't let the pelts go to waste. They're roaming the woods to the north of Frerin's Court.'
'Thanks to you, ${PLAYER}, the thrushes will soon be nesting in Thorin's Gate again!'
'Perhaps now that there are fewer lynx about, the balance of nature will be restored to these lands.'

Lynx can be found in the wooded areas north-east of Frerin's Court and to the north of the Elf-camp.
${RACE:Nos Grimsong[D]|Laergil} asked you to defeat the Lynx found throughout Thorin's Gate and bring back their pelts.
Bring the lynx-pelts you gathered back to ${RACE:Nos Grimsong at the Berghold[D]|Laergil in the ruins of Edhelion}.

'I can't ken these runes at all! Why, unless I miss my mark entirely, I think these are some kind of Elf-writing.
'Now, how could directions to a Dwarf-mine have ever been written in some Elvish script? Well, I'm sure I don't understand this, but I'm afraid I'm going to have to ask you to find an Elf lore-master to riddle these records for us.
'I believe there are Elves living at Lin Giliath, some distance to the south of here, in a region of lakes and bogs called Meluinen in the Elf tongue. There is an Elf there called Glambaen who may be able to read these records.'

'You have come from Regin at Othrikar? Strange days, these are, when a Longbeard asks an Elf for aid! Let me see these records.
'Ah, it appears that it was an Elf who found the dwarves' lode in the first place! That explains this writing, and perhaps also why the dwarves of old never mined the lode, being too stubborn in those days to ask an Elf for help. It appears that these records refer to a map that must have once been included with them. I hope Regin has that map, for the records are not detailed enough to stand on their own.
'I will write this out in such letters that Regin should have no trouble reading. Here you go. Please give my compliments to the dwarves!'

'So, we're missing a map, eh? I wonder....
'Well, thank you again for your work.'
'Didn't Glambaen decipher those records?'
Bring the records to Glambaen
Bring the records to Regin
Regin is unable to make sense of the runes in the mining records you found. Strangely enough, they appear to be written in an Elvish script.
'Please find the Elf Glambaen at Lin Giliath, it may be that he can read these old records.'
'Take the translated records back to Regin. I'm sure he's anxiously awaiting your return!'

Glambaen is at Lin Giliath far to the south of Othrikar, in a region of lakes and bogs called Meluinen.
Regin recognized the mining records as being written in an Elvish script. He has asked you to find an Elf named Glambaen to decipher them.

Regin is at Othrikar in the North Downs.
Glambaen has translated the old records, but apparently a map is required before the directions will make sense. You should return to Regin with the deciphered records.
Collected the Dourhand Mining Map (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I believe the map must have been taken by the Dourhands. They must have left the old records you found because they couldn't read them. But I'd guess that the map is in the hands of the Dourhand foreman who used to have my job.
'Unless I miss my mark, I'd say that Foreman Nyrad is with many of the other Dourhands at their camp to the north.
'This is a big request, but if you can get that map back from Foreman Nyrad, I think we'll be able to find the father-lode at last! I suspect you'll find the map in a chest in Foreman Nyrad's tent at the camp, but he might also be carrying it around on his person.'
'Ah! This looks like it's the right map! Let's see now....'
'Get that map from Nyrad!'
Deliver the Mining Map to Regin
Collect the Dourhand Mining Map (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Lost Map
Glambaen deciphered the runes on the old prospecting records, but they reference a map that appears to be missing.

Foreman Nyrad can be found in the Dourhand camp north of Othrikar. Regin is at Othrikar.
Regin believes that Nyrad, the previous foreman, stole the map, but left the records, since he could not read the runes. Regin has suggested that you may find the map either in Foreman Nyrad's tent or on Nyrad himself.
You have taken an ore sample

'Ha! Now we can finally find the father-lode!
'Hm. Wait a moment. These directions are not exactly what I was expecting:
Find the father in the raw rock The lode lies amongst high hills Fell falcons soar through skies and Savage lynx guard the gorges Shining the silver, glittering the gold A cliff's crags keep the secret
'They had a poetic turn back in the old days. But I wish they were more precise....
'Well, I think we at least have some idea how to proceed. The map and those directions together speak clearly to me of a cliff north-west of Othrikar. All you have to do is find a suitable rock formation that is rich with ore. If you do, take a sample, and we'll see if it's the true father-lode.'

'Let's see that rock! I think....
'Aye! This is it! High-quality, gold-bearing ore! We still have to deal with those cursed Dourhands, and there are all kinds of other dangers to take care of as well, but if we can manage, we'll all be rich!
'I cannot thank you enough, friend! You certainly deserve a reward for your work here, and little though it may be, know that you will always be a welcome guest in the mines of Othrikar!'
'Could you not find the father-lode?'
Locate the father-lode and take an ore sample
Bring the ore sample to Regin
The Father-lode
With the map you recovered from Foreman Nyrad and the runes from the old records, Regin may have determined the general location of the father-lode.
'I wish I could give you better directions. But please head out there and look for that lost lode!'
'Now all we need to do is drive out those cursed Dourhands!'
'The father-lode will make us rich!'

The father-lode is somewhere to the north-west of Othrikar.
Find the father in the raw rock The lode lies amongst high hills Fell falcons soar through skies and Savage lynx guard the gorges Shining the silver, glittering the gold A cliff's crags keep the secret
The old records combined with the mining map suggested to Regin the location of the father-lode, but the directions were far from precise. Regin has asked you to find a suitable rock formation and take an ore sample.

Regin is at Othrikar.
You found a rock formation matching the description Regin compiled from the map and old records. You should bring the ore sample you took from the site back to Regin.

'I'm Regin, in charge of smelting here at Othrikar. The yields are down again -- we're running out of silver in this mine -- but I've heard that somewhere in these hills there is a \qfather lode\q with veins rich with gold, and maybe even mithril -- though I find it unlikely, as Moria-silver's not been found anywhere but Khazad-dûm.
'The Dourhands ruined the old prospecting records when they left, though. We need to find the proper records to find the father-lode. I suspect these records are still around Othrikar someplace, perhaps in a chest or locker.
'If you can discover them, you'll be doing us Longbeards a real service!'

'Aye! That looks like it could be it!
'But wait...what is this? Most of these records are just ordinary prospectors' reports, not too useful, but this one....
'I cannot make this page out at all! Could this be the key to the mystery of the father-lode?'
'I'm sure those records are around Othrikar someplace.'
Return the Mining Records to Regin
Collect the mining records.
The dwarf-mine at Othrikar is almost played out. Regin has heard of a rich \qfather-lode\q somewhere in Nan Amlug, and he hopes to determine the location of this lode.

The lost mining records are somewhere around Othrikar probably in a chest or locker.
Regin has asked you to recover old mining records that may give a clue to the location of the legendary \qfather lode\q.
Defeated spiders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated spiders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Follow Bounder Boffin as he tries to open the door to Old Odo's farm.
Bounder Boffin was able to cut through the webs that barred your way, and you are nearly within the safety of Old Odo's farm.

Follow Bounder Boffin in search of safety.
Bounder Boffin found the key to Old Odo's home, but in his haste to open the door, he snapped the key off in the lock.

Speak to Gildor Inglorion and tell him of your task to carry a letter to Archet.
As you followed Bounder Boffin, you came across the Black Rider giving commands to a group of Big Men. The Black Rider caught sight of you and threatened to kill you, but was stayed by the arrival of the Elf, Gildor Inglorion.

Speak with Amdir, who accompanies Gildor Inglorion.
Upon hearing of your task to bring a message to Celandine Brandybuck, Gildor told you that Amdir was travelling there as well and could protect you upon the road.

'Hopefully you found something in my satchel you can use. Can't be picky now, take what you can find!
'Once I get this door open, you'll need to clear the way to the next gate. While you do that, I'll watch for that rider's return.'

'Good, you've cleared the way. There's been no sign of that Rider, but I just know he's still lurking about!
'Let's dash down to the next gate. The sooner we get into Old Odo's house, the better!'

'I overheard your tale. So you travel to Archet to seek Celandine Brandybuck, do you?
'As Gildor has said, I am indeed travelling to Archet myself. It is fortunate that you found me, as I fear that even a hobbit as courageous as yourself would have run afoul of these brigands. I must learn what connexion these Blackwold brigands have with the Ringwraiths.
'Come now, let us travel to Archet. The road ahead is long and not nearly as safe as it once was.'

'That rider was so terrible! I saw him coming down the road, and I tried to ask him his business, and...and...I can't say anymore about it.
'Oh dear, we have to hide! Old Odo's leaf-farm is just down the road. We can hide there.
'While I look for my key, search my satchel there and get a weapon for yourself. With strange folk like this about, who knows what else may be prowling around?'

'I have heard rumour of the troubles Archet is having with these wicked men. You are indeed a brave hobbit to give thought to going to such a place.
'Fortunately, Elbereth must be watching over you this night, because our companion, the Dúnadan Amdir, is travelling there as well. Speak with him. I am sure he would welcome your companionship upon the road ahead.'

'Oh, yes, so glad you came by. I'm sorry, but your letter to Celandine Brandybuck in Archet simply cannot be delivered. I've heard from hobbits living in Staddle that Archet is besieged by ruffians. I would feel awful if one of my good hobbits got hurt!
'If you are set on having your letter delivered, you could go to Archet yourself. I wouldn't recommend it though! It would be wiser to not get involved!
'From the look on your face, I can tell you aren't going to be dissuaded so easily. Well, if you are going to go, follow the Stock Road into Stock proper and then to Buckland from there. Hobbits there are a queer sort...maybe they'll help you get to Archet.'

'I'm sorry, I was so hasty in trying to get the door open that my key broke! Now our only hope for safety is to try to brave the Stock Road on into Woodhall.
'Follow me closely friend, who knows what else we may run into tonight!'
Leave the post office
Travel down the Stock Road
After arming yourself, speak to Bounder Boffin

Speak with Bounder Boffin
Follow Bounder Boffin
Defeat spiders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Instance: A Road Through the Dark

Your good friend Celandine Brandybuck sent you a worrisome letter from the town of Archet in Bree-land, in which she hints at brigands in the area -- and worse! You have written her a letter, urging her to return, but have not received any response from her.
'Don't just stand there, go clear the way ahead to the next gate. I'll keep a watch for that Rider to make sure he doesn't return!'
'Don't just stand there...speak with that Elf. His kind shouldn't be kept waiting!'

'Seems like a terribly foolish thing to want to leave the Shire, but if that Amdir fellow is going there, you might want to speak with him.
'He looks to be a disagreeable sort to me, but if he is a friend of the Elves, then he can't be all bad, I suppose. Maybe just a little strange.'
'If you still wish to travel to Archet, then speak with Amdir. He is travelling there as well, and I am sure would not turn away the company of a doughty hobbit such as yourself!'

'If you are still set on going to Archet, you should travel to the Stock Road and take it into Stock proper.
'From there it isn't far to Buckland, where you might be able to find some hobbits to help you to get to Archet.'
Follow Bounder Boffin
Speak to Bounder Boffin
Perhaps Postman Took will know why you have received no response from your letter to Celandine Brandybuck.

Leave the post office and travel to the Stock Road, where you will begin your journey.
Postman Took told you that, due to the troubles Archet is having with brigands, he was unable to deliver your letter to Celandine Brandybuck. He suggested that you should take it yourself.

Travel down the Stock Road until you reach the town of Stock.
It is not far from Stock to Buckland where you might find someone to deliver your letter.

You should speak with Bounder Boffin.
As you travelled down the Stock Road, you saw a strange rider clad all in black. He seemed interested in the location of a hobbit named \qBaggins.\q After frightening Bounder Boffin nearly to death, he rode off.

After you acquire a weapon from Bounder Boffin's satchel, accompany him to old Odo's leaf-farm.
Bounder Boffin thinks it is best to hide until the Black Rider passes by, and he thinks old Odo's leaf-barn could be such a place to hide.

Bounder Boffin asked you to clear the way to the next gate while he watched for the Black Rider's return.

You should let Bounder Boffin know the way is now clear to the next gate.

With the way cleared to the next gate, follow Bounder Boffin as he opens it.

As Bounder Boffin tries to hack through the spider webs, defend him from the spiders that will surely try to stop him.
As you made your way into Old Odo's farm, you found your way barred by spider webs.

'As I said, I am sorry to intrude upon your reflection, but perhaps you can speak with Cardavor in Celondim proper? He seems quite worried about something, and, from what I know of the tales of your bravery, you may be able to help him.
'You may find him by the piers. Follow the path to the north to the gates, then continue to the water's edge.'
'Ah, hello there. We have not had time to get acquainted. My name is Cardavor. And you are...?'
At the Behest of Cardavor
You were greeted by an Elf-maiden as you paused for reflection in Celondim.
'Did you speak to Cardavor yet? He seemed worried about something.'

Cardavor waits for you by the piers north of where Eilian keeps watch.
Cardavor, an Elf of Celondim, needs assistance with some matter. Perhaps you should speak with him.

'I have heard that you are well-travelled...perhaps you have seen my son Avorthal upon the road? I received a message from him saying that he was coming from Duillond to visit, but he has not yet arrived. That is most unlike him.
'In his journeys here, he oft speaks with the travellers along the road and a friend of his, a dwarf named Athal, who watches the road and helps the few dwarf-travellers who come to Celondim. Perhaps Avorthal is speaking to him now and has simply forgotten the time. Would you seek him?
'Just follow the road north out of Celondim and look for my son. Or if you do not find him there, speak to Athal and see what news he may have of him.'

'The dwarf has not seen my son in days? I have never been pleased regarding my son's friendship with Athal, but I do not think the dwarf would intentionally deceive us about this.
'I fear all the more that some ill has befallen Avorthal, for he is, if anything, punctual almost to a fault.'

'Nay, I haven't seen Avorthal in a few days, which is strange. He comes often along this road, to visit his father and others in Celondim.
'I would not fret. Avorthal is able and wise for an Elf and has no enemies that I am aware of. He treats my folk kindly enough, which is queer for an Elf, but he is welcome among my kindred for it.
'I am sorry I have no other help to give you or Lord Cardavor.'
Unlike Avorthal
Cardavor, an Elf of Celondim, received a message from his son Avorthal saying that he was coming down from Duillond to visit; however, Avorthal is late, and Cardavor is concerned.
'Athal should be patrolling the road north of Celondim that leads to Duillond. If you do not find Avorthal there, he may have some news of my son.'
'I'm sorry that I could be of no help in finding Avorthal. If you could, please convey my regrets to Lord Cardavor.'

The dwarf, Athal, who Avorthal may have paused in his travels to speak to patrols the road north of Celondim.
Cardavor hopes that his son was only delayed by a visit to his dwarf-friend Athal along the road leading from Duillond to Celondim. He has asked you to journey north and east to find him.

Cardavor is by the docks in Celondim, south of Athal's patrol.
You spoke with Avorthal's dwarf-friend Athal, but he had little to tell you, except that he had not seen Avorthal in days. You should return to Cardavor with this news.
You see a slain goblin beside a leather satchel
This satchel is of fine Elf-make, but there is no sign of its owner

'It is not like Avorthal to be late -- at least not without sending word -- nor to put aside his usual habits. Still, he has spent much time in contemplation in recent days.
'When Avorthal desires solitude for quiet thought, he spends much time amidst the ruins to the west of Celondim. Perhaps he is there now. Would you go there and find him?
'Journey north along the road, and near the river head west. Soon you will see the ruins upon the hill. Avorthal must be somewhere within.'

'This is Avorthal's satchel, I am certain of it! Do you see this pattern on the side? Avorthal stitched that himself long ago. And you say there were goblins among the ruins?
'You bring me fell tidings, ${PLAYER}. You are sure there were no other signs of Avorthal? Some sign that my son might have been hiding nearby, safe from the goblins but too far away to reclaim his satchel?
'Nay, that is a weak hope, and I must not trust to it. The goblins have brought down my son, my Avorthal. That is the only answer.'
'Do you have nothing for me?'
Find Avorthal
Retrieve the satchel
Bring the satchel to Cardavor
Avorthal's Favourite Haunts
The news you brought from Athal has caused Cardavor greater worry, for it is unlike Avorthal to be late without sending word, nor to forego his usual habits.
'Avorthal has always been fond of walking among the ruins to the west of Celondim. It reminds him of elder days.'
'A satchel? It could be the one Avorntal used during his sojurns.'

Avorthal may be among the ruins west of Celondim.
Cardavor recalled one more of his son's favourite haunts -- some ruins west of Celondim, where Avorthal goes when he desires solitude -- and has asked you to seek Avorthal there.

A leather satchel lies beside the body of a slain goblin. It could provide clues to aid you in your quest.
Cardavor recalled one more of his son's favourite haunts -- some ruins west of Celondim, where Avorthal goes when he desires solitude -- and has asked you to seek Avorthal there.

Cardavor is at Celondim.
You went to the ruins to which Cardavor directed you, but you did not find Avorthal there. All you found was a discarded satchel and a party of goblins. Perhaps Cardavor will recognize the satchel.

'You have done so much for me already, ${PLAYER}, but there is still much that must be done if my son is to be restored. We have not had dealings with the dwarves for a very long time, and those are not pleasant memories.
'You were at Edhelion, I believe? You remember Skorgrím's final attack on the old refuge, yes? Dwarves are scheming and self-serving, not to be trusted!
'We must gather our strength to lay siege to the dwarves of Ered Luin and rescue Avorthal from their clutches, but only Dorongúr Whitethorn, the Master of Duillond has the authority to muster such a force. Bring him the news of my son, that he is alive, but a prisoner. We must strike at the dwarves before it is too late!'

'Your news is troubling, ${PLAYER}. For dwarves to work peacefully with goblins is unusual enough, but to conspire in the abduction of an Elf-prince seems foolhardy, even for them.
'I will not call our warriors to arms just yet. Cardavor is full of anger, which is to be expected, but as Master of Duillond it is my duty to exercise restraint.
'If the dwarves have indeed taken Avorthal, we will fall upon them with such fury that the mountains shall shake at our passing; but this could also be a trick of the goblins. They would have much to gain by a war between Elves and dwarves.'
The Master of the Refuge

The goblin Pampraush let slip the knowledge that Avorthal was not slain, but handed over to wicked dwarves. Cardavor was further embittered by this news and is prepared to declare open war against the dwarves of Ered Luin to reclaim his son.

'There is little time to spare, ${PLAYER}! The wretched dwarves may not keep Avorthal alive for long. Go to Master Dorongúr at Duillond, to the north, and tell him that he must assemble a force of Elves to move against the dwarves at once!'

Dorongúr Whitethorn can be found at the refuge of Duillond, north of Celondim.
While Cardavor is relieved that Avorthal still lives, he is prepared to wage war upon all the dwarves of Ered Luin to rescue his son. He has asked you to inform Dorongúr Whitethorn of Avorthal's captivity in hopes that Dorongúr will muster a force to reclaim the Elf-prince.
Defeated goblins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The goblins have slain my son, ${PLAYER}, and for that we will sweep them from Ered Luin! No goblin will take as much as three steps into these lands before we are there to greet him with swordblade or arrowhead!
'Go forth and slay goblins wherever you find them and cry aloud the name of Avorthal. I would have the foul creatures know whose doom has come upon them!
'While you were gone, word came to me that Limael's Vineyard has been defiled by goblins led by a vile creature called Pampraush. Seek out Pampraush and his minions and slay them in the name of Avorthal! Limael's Vineyard lies west of Celondim.'

'What is this? Pampraush said that my son still lives? Avorthal was not slain? My heart wants to believe... but believe the words of a goblin? Still, I cannot fathom why he would tell you this if it were not so.
'But if Avorthal is alive, then his capture does not bode well. I fear he will not live long while imprisoned by those outcast dwarves. They are no better than the goblins!'
Defeat goblins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Wrath of the Elves
From all appearances, goblins waylaid Avorthal in Tham Gelair, leaving no trace of him but his satchel.
'Limael's Vineyard is to the north-west of Celondim, on the high-ground above the harbour. I will not be satisfied until you have avenged my son's death.'

Pampraush and his minions are in Limael's Vineyard, north-west of Celondim.
The apparent death of Avorthal has enraged Cardavor against the goblins. He has asked you to seek out a band of goblins led by a creature named Pampraush and slay them all in Avorthal's name.

Cardavor is at Celondim, the harbour south-east of Limael's Vineyard.
You sought out the goblin Pampraush and his minions as Cardavor requested, but learned from Pampraush that Avorthal may still be alive as a prisoner of dwarves. Cardavor should be told at once.

'I have dispatched an emissary to the dwarf-city of Gondamon to relax the growing tensions between Elves and dwarves, but I fear rumour of Avorthal's captivity may prove too great a strain for her to ease.
'Journey north and west along the road to Gondamon and tell Gailthin what has transpired here. Together, you and she must learn the truth of Avorthal's whereabouts and rescue him, if indeed he is a prisoner of the dwarves. I do not wish for war until we are certain of his fate.
'If Avorthal has been harmed or we are unable to free him, I will call our warriors to arms; but not before.'

'Is this true? Cardavor's son has been taken by the dwarves? This is grievous news, if it can be believed. Goblins are fell creatures that rely on treachery and deceit, and the dwarves have ever coveted the precious things of the Elves. Capturing Avorthal might be the first step in some dwarf-scheme to seize some of the relics we keep at Duillond and Celondim.
'I thought the dwarves had put their envy of our people behind them, but if this is true...it seems they may still begrudge us our relics and things of beauty.'
Bring Dorongúr's letter to Gailthin
The Emissary

Dorongúr Whitethorn is willing to go to war for Avorthal, but only as a last resort. Suspicious that Pampraush's news of Avorthal's captivity may be a goblin-ruse, he wishes to first use diplomatic means to learn the truth.
'Gailthin is my emissary to the dwarf-city of Gondamon. Follow the road north and west to reach the city and tell her what has transpired. Together, you must work to find Avorthal and rescue him.'

Gailthin is in Gondamon, north and west of Duillond, in the low-lands of Ered Luin.
In the spirit of diplomacy, Dorongúr has asked you to carry a letter to Gailthin, his emissary to the dwarves of Gondamon, and bids you aid her in finding and rescuing Avorthal.
You successfully defended Aglarchen

'I will see if I can learn anything from the dwarves here. Mathi Stouthand is the Lord of Gondamon, and he has spoken openly to me in the past. I will judge his conversation to see if he is hiding something.
'Do not betray what we have learned to anyone but an Elf. The dwarves will surely raise their guard if they gain any suspicion of what we know. This I do know: there is an encampment of strange dwarves to the north of Gondamon. You should go there and learn if they know anything of Avorthal or his whereabouts.
'If you find Avorthal there, then the dwarves of the low-lands, at least, have turned against us. I would take allies, for the dwarves may be hostile.'

'Avorthal is being held in that encampment after all? You have done well, ${PLAYER}, but this confirms the fears of Master Dorongúr. The dwarves are indeed behind the capture of Avorthal.
'The time has come to confront Mathi Stouthand, the Lord of Gondamon, with this news. If he will not command his dwarves to release Avorthal, then my time as emissary is over. There will be war.'

'Are you here to help me? My friend Avorthal was taken by goblins, and I followed them to this encampment of dwarves. They are holding him high up in the cliffs that divide the low-lands from western Haudh Lin. I tried to free him, but there were too many.
'The dwarves pursued me here, and I doubt not...It is too late! They have come!'
Find Avorthal
Suspicious Encampment
Gailthin has learned that a group of dwarves have established an encampment in the low-lands of Ered Luin, north of Gondamon.

'There is an encampment of dwarves to the north of Gondamon. Search it for signs of Avorthal, but do not attempt to rescue him if you find him there! We must regroup and form a plan that is assured of freeing him safely. Learning if he is there will be enough.
'I will investigate Gondamon and learn what I may.'

The suspicious encampment is in the low-lands of Ered Luin, north of Gondamon.
While Gailthin tries to learn the truth of Avorthal's whereabouts from Mathi Stouthand, the Lord of Gondamon, she has asked you to investigate a suspicious encampment of dwarves. She recommended you take allies with you.

Gailthin is in Gondamon, south of the suspicious dwarf-encampment.
While investigating the dwarf encampment, you stumbled across Aglarchen, a friend of Avorthal, who revealed where Avorthal is being held. You should return to Gailthin with this news at once.

'There are legends about these old bones. Some say they are moved about by fell spirits from a distant Age. Some say that the wights are the restless Dead, but even I know better than that. The will that stirs those bones does not belong in Middle-earth.
'Something should be done about these creatures, but they are beyond my ken. Perhaps the Elf-woman that came here from the refuge in the south will know how to deal with this threat. Gailthin is her name, I believe.
'Take that skull to her, and see if she knows what to do with it. I believe you can find her on this level of Gondamon I think, perhaps in the area off to the south of this little plaza.'
'What is this? How dare you present me with this vile thing...what did you say? Wights in the Edain barrows? Then your merchant friend was wise to send you to me.'
'Why do you trouble me?'
Bring the skull to Gailthin
A Disturbing Affair
The merchant Nithi is disturbed by the skull you brought back from the mounds. He thinks this dark affair needs to be investigated, but not by him.

Gailthin the elf-emissary is in Gondamon. She is on the same level of the city as Nithi, off to the south of Nithi's plaza.
Nithi has asked you to bring the haunted skull to the elf-emissary, Gailthin, in the hopes she will be able to deal with the threat it represents.

'Mathi looked me in the eye this very morning and swore that the dwarves were proud to have the Elves of Duillond as neighbours. Such dishonesty, and right to my face! I thought he was truer than that, but I should have known better. No dwarf can be trusted, when you have works of art or history that he desires to possess!
'Go to Mathi Stouthand and demand that he order his dwarves to release Avorthal. If he wants war, he shall have it. You must tell him this: I do not trust myself to speak to one so dishonest without striking him.
'You will find Mathi on the upper levels of Gondamon. Make haste! We may have need to return at once to Duillond to prepare for war.'

'Hold your accusations, ${RACE}! My people are not responsible for your missing prince! I am offended both by the accusation and by your tone!
'Your Elf-prince is being held in the encampment to the north? Ah, yes, that explains a great deal. You see, my people are Longbeards, an honourable family descended from Durin, the first Father of the Dwarves. The dwarf-camp to the north has been a constant annoyance to me and my folk. It was established by Dourhands, a thoroughly unwholesome family of dwarves who trace their ancestry to the evil Skorgrím Dourhand.
'Dwarves may have taken Avorthal, true...but not my dwarves. The Dourhands are to blame, and they are as much a thorn in my side as they are in yours.'
Reluctant Allies
You discovered that Avorthal is indeed being held captive by dwarves, which seems to confirm that they have turned against the Elves of Duillond.

'You will find Mathi on the upper levels of Gondamon. Tell him that we know where his people are holding Avorthal. If he is not released, we will bring war to the gates of Gondamon and drive the dwarves from Ered Luin.'

Mathi Stouthand is on the upper levels of Gondamon.
Gailthin, angered by Mathi Stouthand's apparent duplicity, has instructed you to confront the Lord of Gondamon with the evidence of Avorthal's captivity and demand the release of the Elf-prince.

'If wights stir the bones of the ancient Edain, then an evil has arisen in these mountains which we should all fear. The fell spirits that stir the bones of the Dead are servants of Angmar, of the Witch-king of old, and of the Shadow in the East. I must ask you to seek out this evil and put whatever end you may to it before its darkness spreads.
'Take this Elf-stone to Glamir. He dwells now in the ruins to the north-east of Gondamon at the southern end of the Grimwater.'

'Greetings, ${RACE}. I receive few visitors here at my home of old. But I am sure you did not come to listen to tales of yore. What brings you to these wasting halls?
'You say that evil wights roam the barrows to the north-east of my home? It is indeed well that Gailthin sent you to me, and with the Elf-stone. I have a task for you, if you are willing.'
'Why have you come to this place?'
Bring the Elf-stone to Glamir
The Elf-stone
After you found a wight skull in the mounds, Nithi advised that you take it to the Elf, Gailthin.

Glamir dwells at the ruins north-east of Gondamon, at the southern end of the Grimwater.
Gailthin gave you an elf-stone and sent you to an Elf named Glamir, who may be able to help you against the wights of Haudh Lin.

'If wights roam the barrows of Haudh Lin, then I fear a shadow has returned to Angmar, for never before have such creatures been seen in these lands. This bodes ill for Eriador and perhaps for all of Middle-earth, for eyes which should be turned south, may turn north instead and be blinded to the larger threat.
'As it ever is with evil, no doubt a greater will drives the lesser amidst the barrows. It is that greater will which must be destroyed. Only thus will Angmar's designs for Ered Luin be hindered. The stone Gailthin gave you is possessed of such a virtue that evil cannot bear its presence.
'Take the Elf-stone into the barrows and place it upon the largest standing stone. It is a white stone near a ruined building. That greater will of which I spoke may be drawn forth, and you must confront it.'

'So, it is done. You have accomplished much. Evil is not vanquished, but at least it is crippled.
'Please return to Gailthin with her Elf-stone and convey to her my thanks for sending you to this place.'

'Well done. These foolish dwarves might have stumbled across something they could not hope to defeat had you not intervened before the evil had gathered its strength. Those cursed lands will still be dark and haunted, but one hopes they will no longer pose an imminent threat.'
'Where is my elf-stone?'
The elf-stone twinkles in your hand
Nothing happens
Bring the elf-stone to the standing stone and defeat its guardian
Bring the elf-stone to Gailthin
The Standing-stone
Barrow-wights roam the ancient Edain mounds in the eastern reaches of Haudh Lin, heralding the coming of a great evil to Ered Luin.
'Your deeds in the haunted hills of Haudh Lin were of great import. I thank you.'
'That such creatures dwell now so close to our refuge is distressing, but at least their will has been sapped.'
'It is sad that the land of my home should be blemished by the terror of Angmar.'
'You have done well in defeating the Wight-master, ${PLAYER}. Well done, indeed.'

The white standing stone is in the old Edain mounds north-east of Glamir's home, near the ruins of an old building.
Glamir told you to take the elf-stone to the Edain mounds and place it upon the largest standing stone. He believes the creature whose will governs the wights of Haudh Lin may be drawn into the open by its presence.

Glamir is at his home, south-west of the ancient Edain mounds.
As Glamir foretold, the elf-stone drew forth the Master of Wights. You should return to Glamir with news of your victory over the creature.

Gailthin is at Gondamon, west of Glamir's home.
You should return the elf-stone to Gailthin and tell her the tale of your deeds.

'I cannot understand the markings on these tusk-rings, ${PLAYER}, but I feel they must have some significance. I know of one who might be able to read their meaning, but she is far from here, and the threat of giants and mammoths is much nearer.
'And yet, if you were to move with haste and chose fast hooves to bear you on your mission, you could reach the one of whom I speak and obtain her counsel. I speak of Gailthin the Elf, once Master Elrond's emissary to the giants. She was one of the few they seemed to respect. She was dispatched to Ered Luin to deal with the troubles in that region and has not yet returned.
'I heard she was to meet with the captain of the dwarf-city of Gondamon in the low-lands of Ered Luin. Seek her out and show her the tusk-rings you wrested from the great mammoths! Her dealings with the giants may give her some insight into what their markings could mean.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. It has been a long time since I was at Imladris, and I must tell you I have missed it.
'You removed these rings from the tusks of mammoths? You must be mighty indeed to have done so, a valiant ${RACE}, beyond measure! I recognize these symbols and read them for what they are: marks of ownership.
'I can tell you the names of the giants that have taken these mammoths for their allies. Only they can stir the mammoths into action against us -- I hope only that my knowledge can help you eliminate this threat before the time for stopping it is past.'
Bring tusk-rings to Gailthin
Few Who Dare
Gailthin the Elf was emissary to the giants in happier days, and she is one of the few who might understand the significance of the tusk-rings you recovered.

'Gondamon of Ered Luin is a long way from here, ${PLAYER}, but Gailthin has experience dealing with the giants, and only she may tell us the significance of the markings on the tusk-rings you collected. Seek her out, and quickly!'

Gailthin is in the dwarf-city of Gondamon, in the low-lands of Ered Luin.
Golhador has asked you to show the tusk-rings to emissary Gailthin.

'It has taken exceptionally powerful giants to bend the will of the mammoths of the Misty Mountains. If these champions are defeated, we will not need to fear the alliance of giant and mammoth until more champions arise. Gather what allies you may, for these champions are truly mighty, even among the already-fearsome giants.
'The rings you brought to me bear the signs of three giants. These champions have never treated with me, but I know their marks and their reputations. Madfurr is a master of unarmed warfare and lives in the cleft east of the Giant's Needle. Few dare pass near the stones he has set aside for his protection from the elements. Other giants are awe-struck by Sukdyr's skill with his great club -- look for him somewhere within the paths north-east of the Giant's Needle, among the rocky chasms.
'Kulgurz is the last, and of him I know less than the others. Beware his skill from afar! It is said that he can strike a mighty aurochs dead with a single toss from a distance of two miles. Kulgurz strides along the slopes high above the Giant's Needle, looking for trouble. May fortune smile upon you, ${PLAYER}. You will have need of it.
'Oh, the Giant's Needle itself? It is a natural black rock spire in a small bowl-like valley. You will find it in the heart of the Giant Halls of the Misty Mountains, some distance southeast of an old Dwarf stronghold called Gabilazan.'

'You have filled me with amazement, ${PLAYER}, and I marvel at your ability to best the giants' mighty champions!
'I have no doubt they will raise new champions against us, but you have purchased us some time, brave ${RACE}, and for that we of Imladris are grateful.'
Towering Champions
Gailthin has identified the giants who have mastery over the mammoths of the Misty Mountains and has asked that you put an end to this dangerous alliance.

'These mighty champions among the giants walk the mountains near the Giant's Needle, ${PLAYER}, and your allies will need to be strong indeed to defeat them.
'Madfurr is a master of unarmed combat, and lives in the cleft east of the Giant's Needle. Sukdyr's skill with the club he wields is legendary -- look for him somewhere within the paths north-east of the Giant's Needle, among the rocky chasms.
'I know less of Kulgurz, but I know to beware his skill from afar! He strides the slopes high above the Giant's Needle, eager to fell his enemies even from a great distance.'

'You have defeated Madfurr, Sukdyr, and Kulgurz? You are mighty indeed, ${PLAYER}!
'Return to Golhador, north of Imladris, and give him this happy news, friend!'

'Gailthin has given you the names of the giant-champions, ${PLAYER}? These are good tidings, for now you and your allies may be able to stem this tide before it crashes down out of the mountains onto Imladris!
'Madfurr can be found in the cleft east of the Giant's Needle, and Sukdyr walks the paths north-east of the Giant's Needle, among the rocky chasms? Where then is the last of these fearsome foes? The slopes high above the Giant's Needle?
'I see. Gather your allies and defeat these mighty opponents, ${PLAYER}! All of Imladris will rejoice at your victory!'
'Behold ${PLAYER}, who triumphed even over the mighty champions of the giants!'
'The great champions of the giants were mighty foes, ${PLAYER}. You are strong indeed.'
'We of Imladris are in your debt, ${PLAYER}! The giants will fear your name!'
'Your deeds speak loudly, ${PLAYER}, and echo about the mountains!'

The Giant's Needle is in the heart of the Giant Halls of the Misty Mountains, southeast of the Dwarf stronghold of Gabilazan.
Madfurr is east of the Giant's Needle, in a cleft of the rock. Sukdyr is north-east of the Giant's Needle, among the stony paths. Kulgurz is on the high slopes above the Giant's Needle.
Gailthin the Elf, once emissary to the giants of the Misty Mountains, has told you the locations of the powerful giant-champions responsible for taming the ferocious mammoths.

Golhador is in the pass north of Rivendell that winds into the Misty Mountains.
Golhador will be pleased to hear that you have defeated the mighty champions responsible for taming the ferocious mammoths.

'That Elf-woman is stiff-necked and suspicious. She does not recognize the difference between Durin's Folk and the Dourhands. If my dwarves attempt to rescue her Elf-prince and fail, she will assume that we are in league with the Dourhands and call for war upon my people.
'What we need is someone trusted by Elves and dwarves alike to this attempt. There is a Man, a Ranger out of the Wilds in the east, who has assisted both of our kindreds at sundry times. He is masterful in the art of hunting and stealth.
'Seek the Ranger Langlas at the hunter's lodge to the east of here. I only hope he will accept this responsibility.'

'Elves and dwarves living as neighbours in Ered Luin is worse than keeping a lynx kitten and a wolf pup in the same house, and I hope you don't take offence at my saying so.
'In the interest of maintaining peace in Ered Luin, I will respect Mathi Stouthand's wishes and arrange for the rescue of Avorthal. I do not want to bear the burden of our rescue ending in failure, but a Ranger does not have the luxury of refusing charges such as this one.
'If I were to refuse, Avorthal's life would be forfeit and so too would be peace in Ered Luin. I will organize the attempt, if you will help me.'
Mutual Dislike

Tensions between the Elves of Duillond and the Dwarves of Gondamon are escalating because of Avorthal's abduction. Mathi Stouthand is afraid that there will be war if his people try to rescue the Elf-prince and fail.

'So, Avorthal was captured by dwarves descended from Skorgrím Dourhand? It is well that Mathi encouraged you to seek the aid of Langlas...not many of my people would trust the Dwarves of Gondamon to the task.'
'Will Langlas help us? It would be a tragedy if this incident should bring my people into conflict with the Elves of Duillond. There is little love lost between our kindreds as it is.'

The Ranger Langlas is at the hunter's lodge, east of Gondamon.
To avoid the appearance of allegiance between the Longbeards and the Dourhands, Mathi Stouthand has suggested recruiting a neutral party to conduct the rescue of Avorthal. He has asked you to seek out a Ranger by the name of Langlas and enlist his aid.

'Dwalin has sent many Longbeards marching to Rath Teraig, and Dorongúr Whitethorn has dispatched many Elf-warriors of his own. Skorgrím sought to divide the peoples of Ered Luin, but his actions have only strengthened their resolve to stand against him.
'Skorgrím Dourhand will die in Rath Teraig, ${PLAYER}. While the Elves and Durin's Folk draw away the greater part of the goblin army, you and your allies will enter behind their lines and join up with Avorthal.
'When you have gathered your allies, return to me and I will show you the path to Avorthal.'

'Many good dwarves and Elves perished at Rath Teraig, ${PLAYER}, and though Skorgrím was not defeated, he has fled and his threat has abated for now.
'I am worried about the lands to the south. If Skorgrím was able to cause so much harm in Ered Luin, he can surely cause as much or more in Bree-land or the Lone-lands. I fear that we have not seen the last of Skorgrím Dourhand.
'We must send word to my captain. He will know what to do. But you must leave right away, ${PLAYER}. Are you prepared?'
Talk to Langlas and defeat Skorgrím
Assault on Rath Teraig
Dwalin of Thorin's Halls and Dorongúr Whitethorn of Duillond have assembled their forces, and you have prepared the way into Rath Teraig. All stands ready for the assault on the goblin-army.
'It is time! The combined armies of the dwarves and Elves have already begun their assault on the cleft of Rath Teraig. Avorthal awaits you within the valley. We must go!'

Langlas is at the hunter's lodge, east of Gondamon.
Langlas told you to gather allies, then return to him. When the assault begins, he will show you a path leading behind enemy lines, where Avorthal awaits you.

Langlas is at the hunter's lodge, east of Gondamon.
Skorgrím was driven from Ered Luin, but not slain. Langlas awaits an audience with you to decide your course.

'Skorgrím has escaped, ${PLAYER}, but I think Ered Luin will be safe from him now...at least for a time. For that, I feel the combined assault of dwarves and Elves was a success.
'It will be a long while before we know the full cost of our actions here. Many good people have fallen in Rath Teraig this day.
'I will tend to my father's wounds, and then together we can report to Langlas and tell him what has happened here today.'
'We should now return to Langlas.'
'I am ready, ${PLAYER}. We will find Skorgrím Dourhand and drive the fell creature not only from Rath Teraig, but from Ered Luin itself!'
'I feel rested enough to continue. Let us continue our search for Skorgrím Dourhand.'

'I am ready to move on, ${PLAYER}. We must find and rescue this Sara Oakheart. Once she is safe, we can continue our search for Skorgrím.
'Perhaps we will find my father up ahead and can lend him our aid, though I am sure he has little need of our blades.'
Speak to Avorthal
Speak to Avorthal
Speak to Avorthal
Speak to Avorthal
Instance: Assault on Rath Teraig
The dwarves and Elves of Ered Luin have begun their assault on the goblin-army in the cleft of Rath Teraig, and Langlas sent you behind enemy lines to meet Avorthal.

Avorthal seeks Skorgrím Dourhand inside the goblin-infested vale of Rath Teraig.
Avorthal has pledged the strength of his arm to your cause and seeks revenge upon Skorgrím for the harm he has caused the peoples of Ered Luin.

Avorthal seeks Skorgrím Dourhand inside the goblin-infested vale of Rath Teraig.
A surprise attack by goblins has thinned the ranks of the Free Peoples in Rath Teraig, and now Avorthal leads a counterattack on the goblins lurking on the heights above.

Avorthal seeks Skorgrím Dourhand inside the goblin-infested vale of Rath Teraig.
Avorthal has vowed to rescue Sara Oakheart, held captive by goblins within Rath Teraig, putting worries of his father's fate out of his mind.
Skorgrím Dourhand has escaped. Avorthal is waiting to speak with you regarding the course you should take next.

'This belonged to a friend of ours, a Dúnedan named Thoram. He died helping us to defend Dol Ringwest many long years ago. We buried him and built a cairn where he fell, in honour of his sacrifice. Perhaps Toronn is right, there are many harsh memories here. In the West we would be free of such pain.
'His sword deserves a better home, away from the goblins that loot the dead. Bring it to Langlas at the hunter's lodge, west of Kheledûl. He is a Ranger of the North and will keep well the history of his kin.'

'Greetings, good ${RACE}! Bregar sent this, did he? I have heard the story of Thoram and will honour his memory.
'The recovery of Thoram's sword must have arisen from Toronn and Bregar's debate. It has long been a concern of mine that they might leave Middle-earth during these dangerous times.
'Give this to Bregar with my thanks. It may prove useful in convincing his brother to remain.'
'Do you have business with me?

'What is this? A gift from Langlas?'
Bregar unrolls the scroll. '\qThe Lay of Nimrodel\q?
'How could Langlas see this while my eyes remained blind? This is the Lay of Nimrodel and Amroth who loved her. A storm took Amroth's ship out to sea before Nimrodel could join him, and Nimrodel herself was lost in the mountains to the south on her journey to the havens in the Bay of Belfalas. Neither were seen again.'
Bring Thoram's sword to Langlas
Bring the scroll to Bregar
Now is Found
Toronn desires to leave Middle-earth, while Bregar, his brother, believes they should remain. Toronn asked you to retrieve an old sword from a cairn in Dol Ringwest.

Langlas is at the hunter's lodge west of Kheledûl.
Swayed by Toronn's reminder of their lost friend Thoram, Bregar asks you to bring the broken sword to Langlas, a Ranger of the North who will honour the sword and Thoram's memory.

Bregar is at Duillond, along the road east and south of the hunter's lodge.
Langlas gratefully accepted Thoram's sword, promising to honour it, then gave you a scroll to deliver to Bregar.
Defeated melee goblins in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated ranged goblins in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I will send word to Mathi Stouthand and Gailthin in Gondamon of Avorthal's safe return and to warn their masters. The Free Peoples of Ered Luin must unite if they are to drive Skorgrím and his goblin allies from this land.
'While Lord Dwalin and Master Dorongúr assemble their forces, I have an urgent task for you, ${PLAYER}. The goblins have mustered in Rath Teraig, and if we are to have any hope of reaching Skorgrím, we must thin their ranks.
'Journey into Rath Teraig, the valley south of Gondamon, and defeat as many of the goblins there as you can. If we can reduce their numbers sufficiently, Dwalin and Doronogúr may have a greater chance for victory.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}. Once the dwarves and Elves have arrayed their forces, the assault on Rath Teraig will begin.'
Defeat melee goblins in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat ranged goblins in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Preparations for the Assault

With the release of Avorthal, the threat of war between the Dwarves of Gondamon and the Elves of Duillond has been averted, but the dangers posed to both kindreds remain, embodied by Skorgrím's Dourhands and the goblin-army they have raised.

The goblins are mustering in Rath Teraig, the valley south of Gondamon.
Langlas has sent word to Mathi Stouthand and Gailthin to begin preparations for an assault on Skorgrím's goblin-army in Rath Teraig. As well, he instructed you to begin thinning the enemy forces there.

Langlas is at the hunter's lodge, east of Gondamon.
You have prepared the way for the assault on Rath Teraig, as Langlas had instructed you. You should return to Langlas with news of your success.

'We must not delay, ${PLAYER}. We must rescue Avorthal from the Dourhands before they are able to set sail!
'The Dourhands control the port-city of Kheledûl, to the east, and the ship they plan to carry Avorthal is surely docked there. Kheledûl is defended by a score of Dourhands, and it is a position of great strength. We cannot hope to attack it directly.
'If we are to have any hope of rescuing Avorthal from Kheledûl, we will need the help of one who knows the city. I know a dwarf, a Longbeard named Svanr, who was harbour-master of the port before the Dourhands captured the city. You will find him to the east of here, not far from Kheledûl.'

'Avorthal is safe, and the promise of peace is much closer than it was, but Ered Luin is not free of the threat of war just yet, ${PLAYER}.
'We must defeat Skorgrím Dourhand and end his menace, and we must do this quickly, before he can put the second stage of his plan into motion.'

'If you want to get inside Kheledûl, I'm the dwarf you need. The Dourhands have let my fine harbour sink into filth and disrepair...any foe of theirs is a friend of mine!
'A ship came out of the north and has been sitting at anchor for a few days now. From what I can gather, she's called the \qIrestone\q, and her captain is a particularly unpleasant-looking Dourhand. If he's planning on taking this Elf-prince back north on his ship, you'll need to hurry. I overheard the guards at the gate saying the ship wouldn't be long in port.
'During the day, you will be too visible, but at night you might be able to sneak into Kheledûl undetected. You'll want to stay clear of the night-watch, or they'll raise the alarm. Gather some allies and let me know when you're ready.'
Talk to Svanr and rescue Avorthal
Rescue by Moonlight
Avorthal had been moved from the Dourhand encampment where he was being held and will soon be taken aboard a ship destined northward and beyond all hope of rescue.

'Svanr is a Longbeard, and he was once the harbour-master of Kheledûl. Long has he watched the city in the days since the Dourhands claimed it, and he may be able to help us retrieve Avorthal from within its walls.'
'If you are prepared, let us go.'
'You have done well to free Avorthal from the filthy Dourhands!'
'Soon I will be able to return to my city. I am sure of it!'

Svanr may be found east of the hunter's lodge, not far from Kheledûl.
Langlas told you that Svanr the former harbour-master of Kheledûl, can help you sneak into the city and onto the ship where Avorthal is being held.

Svanr is just outside the port-city of Kheledûl.
Svanr told you to gather allies and return to him when you are ready to sneak into Kheledûl.

The Ranger Langlas is at the hunter's lodge, west of Kheledûl.
Now that Avorthal is safe, You should return to Langlas and give him the grim tidings the Elf-prince learned during his captivity.
You have successfully defended Avorthal

'We must hurry, ${PLAYER}. Skorgrím has assembled an army of goblins within Rath Teraig, and though my rescue should end the threat of war between dwarves and Elves, I fear that the goblin-army will not long remain within that narrow pass.
'Let us bring this warning out of Kheledûl into the light of morning, and may our chances for peace also shine bright!'
'We must return now.'

'You are here to free me? Skorgrím Dourhand has raised a goblin army in the cleft of Rath Teraig, and unless we stop him, he will sweep through all the free lands!
'There is no time to waste, my friend. We will need to defeat the Captain and his crew if we are to escape from Kheledûl with our lives and bring word of the danger which grows stronger within Rath Teraig!
'The captain will soon return. Quickly, untie my hands! We need to escape from here!'
Find Avorthal
Talk to Avorthal
Instance: Rescue by Moonlight
Svanr, the former harbour-master of Kheledûl, has brought you a down a hidden path to the gates of the city. It is now up to you to sneak into Kheledûl and free Avorthal.

Avorthal is being held on the \qIrestone,\q the ship docked at the port-city of Kheledûl.
Unless you free him tonight, the \qIrestone\q will carry Avorthal far from rescue and doom Ered Luin to war between dwarves and Elves.

Avorthal is on the deck of the \qIrestone,\q still docked at Kheledûl.
The Captain of the \qIrestone\q has been defeated. You should speak with Avorthal and make your escape.

'Rumour of Avorthal's capture have come to me. Mathi's fears have merit. The Elves of Duillond remember the treachery of Skorgrím Dourhand six-hundred years ago and do not easily recognize the difference between dwarves. The short reign of Thráin and his son Thorin in Ered Luin was marked by a grudging peace only because their folk kept to themselves and did not trouble the Elves.
'Very well. I will help you to rescue Avorthal and hopefully avert a war. In these darkening times, strife between the enemies of Mordor can only serve to aid the Dark Lord.
'This rescue will not be easy. Gather allies and return to me when you are ready to depart for the Dourhand camp.'

'This is certainly distressing news. It appears the Dourhands were one step ahead of us all this while.
'Ah well, I suppose we must follow their trail. Kheledûl is the centre of Dourhand power, the last remaining town in Ered Luin which they control. Conflict will not be easily avoided there.'
Talk to Langlas and rescue Avorthal
To Avert a War
Langlas has formed a plan to rescue Avorthal from the Dourhand camp and is ready to carry it out.

'This will be a difficult task. I will guide you to the place I believe Avorthal is being held. We will no doubt have to fight our way through a gauntlet of sturdy Dourhand warriors. We must watch each other's backs, lest we fall.
'Are you ready to leave?'

Langlas is at the hunter's lodge, east of Gondamon.
Langlas told you to return to him after you had gathered allies to assist in the raid on the Dourhand camp.

Langlas is at the hunter's lodge, east of Gondamon.
Though you and Langlas fought to the heart of the Dourhand encampment, you learned that Avorthal had already been moved. Now you and Langlas must devise another plan.
'This has been a waste of time and blood, neither of which we can afford. Let us discuss our possible paths back at the lodge.'
'Hurry, we must return.'
'We should proceed without delay. Together, we may defeat the Dourhands and rescue Avorthal!'

'They know we are here now. The fighting will be worse up ahead.
'Now. It is time to go.'

'This has been a long and dangerous trek, but I am glad to have had you at my side throughout it all.
'Come now, let us end this!'
Speak to Langlas
Speak to Langlas
Speak to Langlas
Speak to Langlas
Instance: To Avert a War
You have travelled with Langlas to the Dourhand encampment in an effort to rescue the Elf-prince Avorthal.
Langlas requires your assistance to find and free Avorthal. You should watch each other's backs, lest you fail.
You have made progress into the Dourhand camp, but the effort was not easy, and Langlas has advised you rest before continuing on. You should let Langlas know when you are ready to go on.
This is the heart of the camp. Skorgrím's lieutenant is waiting for you. Talk to Langlas when you are ready to confront the villain and learn what happened to Avorthal.
Hakon Ironfist has been defeated, but it appears that Avorthal is not here. Speak to Langlas when you are ready to return to the hunting lodge.
You found the broken sword

'If Bregar wishes to evoke memories of the past to sway my decision, then I will respond in kind.
'There is a burial mound within the ruins of Dol Ringwest to the west of Duillond. On the cairn you will find a broken sword. Bring the sword to Bregar...but treat it with reverence and do not disturb the area around it.
'The time has come for us to pass into the West. The Age of Man has come, and Middle-earth is no longer home to us.'
'I know this blade, broken and dulled as it may be. Alas, the passage of time does little to dull my memories of that battle.'
'Have you found the blade ${PLAYER}?'
Search the cairn for the broken sword
Bring the broken sword to Bregar
What Was Lost

Toronn desires to leave Middle-earth, while Bregar, his brother, believes they should remain. Bregar had you bring a leaf from a tree he and Toronn had grown from a seed brought from their home of old. Toronn has decided to answer in kind, evoking memories of the past.

The broken sword is in the ruins of Dol Ringwest which lie west of Duillond. Return it to Bregar in Duillond.
Toronn has asked you to search the ruins of Dol Ringwest for stone cairn and the broken sword it holds. When you find it, bring the sword to his brother Bregar.

Bregar waits for you in Duillond, east of the ruins of Dol Ringwest.
You recovered a broken sword from a burial cairn in the Elf ruins of Dol Ringwest.

'Langlas has indeed done me a great boon by sending this with you. \qThe Lay of Nimrodel\q is a sad story which has bearing upon our plight.
'Please, bring this scroll to Toronn and have him read this passage.' Bregar places a mark beside a stanza and hands you the scroll.
'If this does not make him understand, then we are fated to part.'

'Does Bregar still endeavour to turn aside my path?'
The Elf's eyes widen as he reads the scroll. '\qAnd cursed the faithless ship that bore Him far from Nimrodel....\q Though it is a sad tale, this was ever a favourite of mine. It tells of Amroth and Nimrodel, their parting, and the coming of much sadness to Lothlórien, home of our kindred.
'Bregar is right. There is much to be done here before we go. I will not carry my pain aboard the White Ships and bring it to the West. Thank you for helping me to understand, ${PLAYER}.'
Bring \qThe Lay of Nimrodel\q to Toronn
The Days Ahead

Langlas had given you a scroll to bring to Bregar at Duillond. Bregar recognized the poem as the \qLay of Nimrodel\q and realized that a passage from the Lay might be enough to convince Toronn to remain in Middle-earth.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, for helping my brother see reason.'
'My brother and I will remain to face the Shadow in the East one last time.'
'Thank you for bringing the scroll to me, ${PLAYER}. My leaving would have brought much sorrow.'
'Together, Bregar and I will stand against the Shadow of Mordor one last time.'

Toronn is at Celondim, south of Duillond.
Bregar has asked you to take the scroll to Toronn in the hope that it will convince his brother to remain.
Collected fallen leaf

'Long have my brother and I dwelt upon these shores and much have we seen in that time. Now the time has come for us to leave this place and sail into the West.
'My brother, however, does not see clearly and wishes to remain here. We have always dwelt together, and I could not consider a day in my life without his company and counsel. He is the cord which binds me to this Middle-earth. While he is of a mind to remain, I am forced to wait for him.
'If you would, go to Duillond and see if you can convince Bregar to join me here at Celondim. It is time we begin our journey. The refuge is north along the road.'

'My brother wishes to leave Middle-earth, but I believe it is time for us to stand our ground against the Shadow growing in the East. With your help, perhaps, Toronn will see reason.
'At the feet of the mountains north-west of Duillond, you should find a distinctive red-leafed tree whose leaves should be falling now. Take a fallen leaf from the tree and bring it to Toronn. It should remind him of the woods where we dwelt and perhaps remind him also why we should not depart. My brother will be at his dwelling in Celondim, making arrangements to leave.
'This Middle-earth which we love will soon face great peril, and we are bound to defend it.'

'So this is Bregar's reply? This leaf fell from a tree we planted when we first came to Duillond long ago. The seed was from our home in the east.
'It is true that in departing Middle-earth, we would be leaving much behind, but it is for the best. These shores no longer welcome us, and there is peace to be found in the West.'
Collect a fallen leaf
Bring the leaf to Toronn
Leaving Middle-earth
Toronn wants to leave Middle-earth and journey into the West to the Undying Lands, but will not leave as long as his brother, Bregar, refuses to leave.
'Have you found the leaf?'
'Please persuade Bregar that he must leave this place, no matter his feelings toward it.'

Bregar is at Duillond, north of Celondim.
Toronn has asked you to try to convince Bregar to accompany him into the West.

The red-leafed tree is at the foot of the mountain range north-west of Duillond.
Bregar asks that you collect a fallen leaf from a particular tree and bring it to Toronn. He hopes the leaf will remind his brother why they should not yet depart Middle-earth.

Toronn is on the porch of his dwelling near the docks at Celondim, south of Duillond.
Bregar has asked that you bring the fallen leaf to his brother, Toronn. He hopes the leaf will remind his brother why they should not yet depart Middle-earth.

'That Dourhand burglar said that his folk paid the goblins well to steal a prince? I don't know what that means, but it can't be good!
'Mathi Stouthand became the chief of Gondamon, the great watch-post of the Low-lands, shortly after the Dourhands were driven from Thorin's Hall. If there is a war brewing, Mathi needs to be warned so he can begin the preparations.
'Follow the road east to Gondamon. There, I expect you'll find Mathi on the upper levels. Travel with great haste, ${PLAYER}! I would quicken your feet with a tale of great deeds, but I see that there is no time to spare!'

'You could not have arrived with this news at a better time, ${PLAYER}. An Elf-prince has gone missing, and the Elves are convinced that we abducted him and refuse to believe otherwise! We have learned where their prince is being held...an encampment of Dourhands to the north-east.
'Your information tells us a great deal about his fate, and I hope it is enough. The Elves have sent an emissary to Gondamon, and she insists that we rescue this Avorthal as a sign of our goodwill. A sign of our goodwill! As if the Longbeards need to prove anything!
'I have always considered myself an even-tempered dwarf, but this emissary has gone too far. We need someone who is neither dwarf nor Elf to organize this rescue. I do not want to be responsible for an outbreak of war in the Blue Mountains.'
Gondamon in the Low-lands
Rothgar is concerned about the ominous words you heard from the Dourhand burglar and feels Mathi Stouthand, Lord of Gondamon, should be told that trouble is brewing.

'Mathi Stouthand is the Lord of Gondamon and must be given warning that the goblins and the Dourhands are up to something. War could be brewing, and the forces of Gondamon will need to be prepared!
'Follow the road east to the fortress. I am sure you will find Mathi on the upper levels!'

Mathi Stouthand can be found on the upper levels of Gondamon, along the road east of Noglond.
Rothgar has asked you to deliver word to Mathi Stouthand that the goblins and the Dourhands are planning some new treachery, while he delivers the stolen gold back to Dwalin.
Collected Stolen Longbeard Gold

'The thrushes saw the Dourhands carrying this stolen gold into the old Dourhand city to the west? That is very peculiar. You see, it has been infested with goblins for the past two years!
'I don't know why the Dourhands would bring the gold into a goblin-held city, even if they once called it home. Most peculiar. It reminds me of the tale of....
'I am sorry. You want to head west to the old Dourhand city and search it for the stolen Longbeard gold, I expect. It won't be easy, but I'll be waiting to hear of your exploits! Head west of Noglond and look for the stairs carved into the mountainside...and watch out for the goblins! You should take allies.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}, well done indeed! I will deliver this gold to Dwalin at Thorin's Halls, but it sounds to me like you have a more urgent errand to undertake!'
'Did you find the gold?'
Find Stolen Longbeard Gold
Bring stolen Longbeard gold to Rothgar
The Old Dourhand City
Rothgar told you about the old Dourhand city to the west of Noglond, but does not know why the Dourhands would bring the stolen gold into it -- the city was overrun by goblins two years earlier.

'The old Dourhand city where the dwarves brought the stolen Longbeard gold is to the west of Noglond. Just look for the stairs carved into the mountainside. You'll want to watch out for goblins, of course.'

The old Dourhand city lies to the west of Noglond, up a flight of steps carved into the mountains.
Rothgar has confirmed the existence of an old stronghold of the Dourhands, now goblin-infested, near Noglond. If the thrushes are correct, the Dourhands brought the stolen gold into the city. Rothgar suggested you take allies with you.

Rothgar is at Noglond, east of the old Dourhand city, along the road that runs through the Vale of Thráin.
You have recovered the stolen gold and should return it to Rothgar for delivery, as Dwalin instructed.

'As Thinglaer sent you to me, so might I ask a final favour of you. Our youngest brother has also taken this onus upon himself and likely requires aid as he has not yet returned to us. If you can help him, I would be grateful.
'Be warned that the lands of Haudh Lin to the north are considerably more dangerous than our domain, and our brother is likewise of hotter temperament, as befits his task in that place.
'I last saw him amongst the ruins near the shore of the Grimwater, a small lake north-east of the dwarf-outpost we call Gondamon. He is likely still there.'

'My brother Calengil sent you? I fear that both my brothers and I have sorely underestimated the depth of the defilement of these once bountiful lands. Even with your help, I am not sure we can do more than stem its growth, much less destroy it.
'Nevertheless, I am grateful to have your aid. When you have rested a bit, let us discuss what steps we can take to deal with this sorrowful blight.'
Glamír's Vigil
Glamir, the brother of Thinglaer and Calengil, also has need of your assistance.

Glamír is dwelling near some old Elf-ruins at the southern edge of the Grimwater, north-east of the dwarf-hold of Gondamon. Gondamon is reached by heading due north along the road, then taking the western fork.
Calengil sent you to speak with his youngest brother, Glamír, and lend him what aid you may.

'I have sorry news indeed, ${PLAYER}. I have discovered the source of the evil that haunts this place.
