'It seems that in the years of Arnor's wars with Angmar, the Witch-king sent fell spirits to stir the bones of the dead within the mounds of the Edain. We thought this foul sorcery was performed only upon the mounds of the Barrow-downs in Cardolan, but alas we were wrong. Wights stalk our lands, and we knew it not.
'Please forgive me, ${PLAYER}, but I must ask you to fight these horrible things. Try to loosen their grip on Haudh Lin, while I search for a more permanent means of ridding the land of their presence.'

'Ah, ${PLAYER}, I fear that unlike my brothers, my task shall remain unfulfilled. In truth, there is nothing in the lore I have found to rid the world of such abominations as now call Haudh Lin their home.
'Nevertheless, I must thank you for all you have done for me and my brothers and reward you as befits a valiant warrior.'
Haunted Lands
Glamír has found the source of the corruption of Haudh Lin -- a mound of evil wights.

The wights inhabit the mounds of Emyn Hoedh, east of the Grimwater.
Glamír has asked you to do battle against the mound-wights of Haudh Lin, while he searches for a way to rid the land of their presence.

Glamír is near the Grimwater, west of Emyn Hoedh and north-east of Gondamon.
You should speak with Glamír and discover if he has found a way to defeat the wights once and for all.
Spider defeated (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Talath Ondren, the region of Haudh Lin to the east, was once known as the Shipwright's Grove in Westron, and it is there that many of the famed vessels of the Elves were built in days long past -- but the corruption that haunts it now is much greater than I or my brothers had imagined. Something malignant and evil lurks there now.
'I have not found the true source of the corruption yet, but something must be done nonetheless. If you would help me, then seek out the spiders that infest Talath Ondren east of here and thin their numbers.
'They are not the ultimate source of the corruption, but your efforts should buy me the time I need to find the true source.'

'Good work with those spiders, ${PLAYER}, but as I suspected, they are not the true threat in Haudh Lin, I have uncovered something much more sinister in my exploration.
'Rest a moment, and I shall tell you more.'
Defeat spiders in East Haudh Lin (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Webs of Sorrow
Glamír is concerned by the spiders which infest Talath Ondren.

Talath Ondren is east of the Grimwater.
Glamír has asked you to slay the spiders that infest Talath Ondren, while he continues his search for the source of corruption in the region.

Glamír is near the Grimwater, west of Talath Ondren and north-east of Gondamon.
You should return to Glamír and see if he has made any progress in his search.

'My brother Calengil is staying at Duillond, our refuge to the north. Like me, he also strives to restore the old places to their pristine state and may need your help.
'Follow the road to the high ground above Celondim, then make your way north through a gap in the hills to reach the refuge.'

'So, Thinglaer has succeeded in driving the darkness back from Tham Gelair with your aid? I too have such a task before me -- but, alas, I have no trinket from Rivendell to aid me.
'I do know much of the herbs of these lands however and can mix a draught that should serve to purify the nearby ruins -- will you lend me your aid in this endeavour?'
Calengil's Vigil
Thinglaer's brother Calengil also seeks to restore the ancient Elf-ruins within Ered Luin and requires your aid.
'My brother Calengil resides in Duillond to the north. He could use your aid with his own tasks, I believe.'

Calengil can be found in the Elf-refuge of Duillond to the north.
Thinglaer has asked you to seek out his brother Calengil and lend him what aid you may.
Collected damp fragrant herbs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You have decided to help me? Excellent. There is a draught I know the making of that should cleanse the taint from the ruins of Dol Ringwest. I have most of the ingredients I need, but there is one remaining herb -- a fragrant herb that grows on the shores of the river, a short way north of here.
'Tis a simple matter to gather it, and I would do so myself, but the brewing is at a delicate stage right now, and I must keep a close eye upon it. Would you gather the herbs I need, ${PLAYER}?'
'Ah! There, just in time. The last step of the process is to add the herbs you have collected for me. After that it simply needs to steep for a few minutes, and the draught will be complete.'
'The draught is still brewing, but I will soon need to infuse it with the herbs I sent you for.'
Collect damp fragrant herbs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return the herbs you collected to Calengil
Cleansing Draught
Calengil has asked you to collect some herbs for him as part of a draught he is creating to cleanse a dark taint from the ruins near Duillond.
'You will find that the herb grows on the shores of the river to the north.'

The herbs can be found along the riverside a little ways north of Duillond.
Calengil has asked you to retrieve the herbs that he needs to complete the cleansing draught.

Calengil is at Duillond to the south.
You should return the herbs you collected to Calengil.
Draught used
Use the Cleansing Draught here
Draught used
Use the Cleansing Draught here

'The draught is ready -- all that remains is for it to be sprinkled upon the grounds within the ruins of Dol Ringwest. It will encourage and speed the growth of the natural vines that one often finds in such places -- so much so that by the end of the next spring the ruins will be buried in a great mass of them. In but a short time, they will reduce the ruins to naught but rubble, returning them to pristine nature once again.
'To you I offer the honour of this task, for I find now that I cannot bring myself to destroy the place that I once loved so, even in its decrepit state. Pour the draught onto the ground beneath the two towers that remain standing amongst the ruins.
'Time and the forces of nature will do the deed with no further help from us.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. It pains me that I shall never again walk among the spires, which I remember from my youth, but better this than to leave Middle-earth with the knowledge that they are a home for creatures of darkness.'
'Have you been to Dol Ringwest? It stands to the west of here.'
Use the draught near the first tower
Find the first tower of Dol Ringwest
Use the draught near the second tower
Find the second tower of Dol Ringwest
Return to Calengil in Duillond, east of Dol Ringwest
Cleansing the Ruins

Calengil has prepared his draught and has offered you the honour of cleansing Dol Ringwest. The draught will in time encourage the growth of great vines that will entwine the ruins, tearing them down and returning them to pristine nature.
'Dol Ringwest can be found to the west. Take the draught to the towers there.'

Dol Ringwest is west of Duillond.
Calengil bade you pour the cleansing draught upon the ground at the base of two towers that remain standing in the ruins of Dol Ringwest.

Calengil is in Duillond, east of Dol Ringwest.
You should return to Calengil and inform him that your task in the ruins of Dol Ringwest is complete.
Defeated foul creatures in Tham Gelair (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Token placed

'This is a beautiful land, is it not? I wandered it often in my youth -- but places that were once fair have long since fallen into decay. Some of the older ruins have even become habitations for foul creatures that gnaw at the edges of our lands.
'My brothers and I have set to ourselves the task of cleansing a few of these places before we leave. To this end, I have in my possession a token given to me by Elrond Halfelven long ago. It is imbued with a light that creatures of evil find painful to bear.
'The ruins of Tham Gelair west of Celondim have become infested with foul creatures. If you could slay any you find within, and then place this token there, its light should keep them from slinking back in the night.'

'Your news gladdens my heart, ${PLAYER}, and I am eager to walk among the ruins as I once did, with the sky over my head and the sun on my face. The cool shadows cast by the walls will no longer be a reminder of the Shadow in the East, but of respite and restoration.'
Defeat foul creatures in Tham Gelair (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Place Thinglaer's token upon the stone table
Hallowed Ground
Thinglaer, an Elf lingering at Celondim, seeks to restore a few of the old Elven places before he departs for the Grey Havens.
'You must purge the fell beasts from the land.'

Tham Gelair lies to the west of Celondim.
Thinglaer has asked you to go to the ruins of Tham Gelair and slay some of the foul creatures there.

Tham Gelair is west of Celondim.
Thinglaer has asked you to place his token within the Elf-ruins west of Celondim.

Thinglaer is at Celondim, east of Tham Gelair.
You should return to Thinglaer and let him know that you have done as he asked.
Found a wight-skull for Nithi

'You there, perhaps you can help with a small dispute. While I was away among the barrows to the north-east hunting for loose trinkets, I saw an old, bony wight wandering about the mounds. Fortunately, it didn't notice me, but the sight fairly froze my blood.
'Now, my friend Galti doesn't believe me. He claims there are no barrow-wights out among the old Edain mounds, but he's been no further than the mounds near Gondamon, and those don't seem to be haunted at all. It's only the mounds off a ways to the north-east.
'You look doughty enough to face down a wight or two...perhaps you would go out to those barrows and collect a trophy to prove I wasn't seeing things? I will pay you for the service.'

'Ha! I knew I hadn't been seeing things! This is proof indeed! Here, takes these coins as your reward!
'Wait...something is not right with this skull. Can't you feel it? The chill?
'I should not have sent you to that place, and I certainly should not have had you bring this thing to Gondamon....'
'Eh? What? What kind of trophy do I want? How should I know? Bring me a skull or some such.'
Bring your trophy back to Nithi
Slay wights to find a trophy for Nithi
Old Bones
The dwarf-merchant Nithi claims he saw a barrow-wight amidst the mounds to the north-east of Gondamon, but his friend Galti does not believe him.

The mounds of the old Edain are a distance to the north-east of Gondamon.
Nithi asked you to journey to the old Edain barrows and collect a trophy to prove to Galti that there are wights amidst the old mounds.

'If you are climbing into the mountains, friend, take care to avoid the great mammoths. They are dangerous on all days, but of late the few travellers in this place have mentioned some unusual ornamentation on the mighty beasts -- great silver rings affixed to their dangerous tusks.
'There is only one race that could affix such rings and still live, and it is that of the giants. This alliance is one of ill omen, if alliance it be, and I am concerned not only for the House of Elrond but also for our dwarf friends, who have established a camp not far to the north.
'If by some fortune you are able to defeat some of the mammoths, bring me their tusk-rings for further study. We must learn how deep this alliance of great beasts and giants may go.'

'You have done very well to bring me these tusk-rings, ${PLAYER}. They are most fearsome! It was a terrible giant indeed who affixed these rings, my friend. Let us hope he never approaches this place, or the camp of the dwarves to the north!'
Bring silver tusk-ring to Golhador
The Masters of the Mammoth
Golhador has cautioned you about the great mammoths of the Misty Mountains, some of which seem to have become allies of the giants.
'Mammoths never walk in great numbers, but they can be found near to the giants in many cases. If you can retrieve some of their tusk-rings, we may learn how strong this alliance may be.'

Mammoths can be found throughout the Misty Mountains, but especially in areas where giants walk.
Golhador has expressed concern that the mammoths and the giants have formed an alliance and asked you to bring the silver tusk-rings worn by the mammoths for him to examine.

Golhador is on the northern pass that leaves Rivendell.
Golhador is waiting for you to return with tusk-rings that might illuminate the nature of the alliance between the mammoths and the giants of the Misty Mountains.

'I've received a most distressing letter! My good friend Dora -- she's a chicken farmer near Waymeet -- has written to say that a pack of wolves has invaded the Shire and driven her from her farm! She's staying in Waymeet for the time being, but the sooner she can get her farm back, the better!
'Can you help? Just take the north-east road right to the centre of Waymeet. You just tell Dora Brownlock that I've sent you to help with her wolf problem.
'Wolves in the Shire! What's going on in the world these days?'

'Peony sent you to help me, ${PLAYER}? She's a sweet lady, and a good friend! I'm glad to have your help.
'Yes, the wolves came slavering near to Waymeet recently and seemed to head straight for my farm! It was all I could do to escape to Waymeet without them noticing me!'
Worries From Waymeet
Peony Grubb has received word from her friend Dora Brownlock, a chicken farmer in Waymeet, that wolves have invaded the Shire and are threatening the town.
'Dora Brownlock is a good friend of mine, so you'd best hurry to Waymeet, if you don't want your superiors to hear of this. Wolves! I can hardly believe it! In this day and age!'

Dora Brownlock is at the centre of Waymeet, north-east of Michel Delving.
Peony Grubb has asked you to help her friend Dora with the wolves that have taken over her farm.
Collected Dora's chickens (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'When the wolves chased me off my farm, I didn't have enough time to collect my babies! My poor darlings...what was that? My chickens, of course! If those wolves have gotten hold of them, I just don't know what I'll do!
'You can save them for me, ${PLAYER}, I know you can! Follow the road north up the hill and out of Waymeet, then take the first stone path to your right. You'll see a sign for my farm at the correct crossing.
'Quickly! You must save my little darlings!'

'You saved my chickens! Thank you so much! I don't know what I would have done if the wolves had gotten my darling Rosy, or my precious Georgie, or my lovely Dottie!
'Someone needs to do something about these wolves, and I think that someone is you, ${PLAYER}!'
'Oh dear! You haven't rescued my chickens yet!'
Collect Dora's chickens (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring chickens to Dora Brownlock
Rescue Dora's Chickens
Wolves have invaded the Shire, and some of them chased Dora Brownlock from her farm and have begun to feed on her chickens.
'You simply must rescue my babies from the wolves! You'll find my poor dears at my farm, to the north of Waymeet. Please hurry!'

Dora's chickens are at her farm north of Waymeet, at the end of the first stone path on the right off the main road.
You went to Waymeet to help Dora Brownlock at the behest of Peony Grubb. Dora has in turn asked you to rescue her chickens from her farm, which has been overrun by the wolves.

Dora Brownlock is at the centre of Waymeet.
Dora Brownlock will be pleased to have her chickens returned to her, safe from the threat of the wolves prowling about her farm. You should return to her at once.

'There's been rumour of a scarred, old wolf spotted away from the rest of the pack -- in fact, across the road from the wolf-den north of my farm. I don't know what might have happened, but I think it's fair to say that this old wolf must be their leader, exiled for some reason.
'Now, I think I've done something terribly foolish, ${PLAYER}! My neighbour, Jolly Smallburrow, is a true gentlehobbit, and I suspect he's something of an admirer of mine. Unfortunately, I mentioned this wolf business to him, and he swore to take care of it!
'If you don't mind, would you please find Jolly before the wolf does? I'll feel terrible if something happens to him!'

'You rescued Jolly, ${PLAYER}, and thank goodness! I knew there wouldn't be an old wolf that could do you in, though I'm sure the same can't be said for poor, well-meaning Mr. Smallburrow.
'I have not yet decided whether to take him up on his dinner invitation. Yes, he ran straight here to ask before you even returned!'

'Dora was worried about me? Truly? Perhaps she does have feelings for me! Well, to tell you the truth, I was a little worried myself about what would happen once that wolf showed its muzzle around here.
'I felt sure my bucket of boar meat would lure the beast out of hiding, too. Ah, well. Maybe I didn't get smelly-enough boar meat...
'I'll clean this up, and we can go talk to Dora together....'
Find Jolly Smallburrow
The Wolf in Exile
Dora Brownlock thinks an admirer of hers has gone to try and kill the exiled leader of the wolves near Waymeet.
'Jolly means well, but he's always trying to find ways to impress me. I hope you find him before that dreadful wolf does!'
'We've taught those wolves a lesson, and no mistake!'
'Such excitement! Waymeet is not often like this, I can tell you that!'
'I hear that things are getting back to normal in Waymeet. That's good.'
'The less we see of wolves in the Shire, the better!'

Jolly Smallburrow may be after the wolf that was seen across the road from the wolf-den, north of Dora Brownlock's farm.
Dora Brownlock is worried that her neighbour, Jolly Smallburrow, may be in trouble and has asked you to find him.

Dora Brownlock is at the centre of Waymeet.
Dora will be pleased to know that you have rescued Jolly Smallburrow and defeated the scarred leader of the wolves that have been harassing her farm and town.
Defeated wolves at wolf den (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I don't know that I can go home until I know those wolves are gone for good! What if they come for my babies again?
'You were so brave to rescue my little darlings...I'm sure you could do something about the wolves. The awful beasts that attacked my farm came from the north...there must be a wolf den somewhere among the hills north of my farm!
'Oh, please do hurry! I really would like to go home soon.'

'Thank you for your efforts, ${PLAYER}! We won't need to fear these wolves now that you've killed their leader!
'What? You didn't see their leader at the wolf den? He won't be an ordinary pack-leader, that's for sure. The real leader of the wolves must be in hiding. Until we do something about the chief wolf, no one in the area will be safe!'
Defeat wolves at wolf den (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Wolves At Waymeet
Wolves overran Dora Brownlock's farm and present a threat to Waymeet and the surrounding communities.

'If you're looking for the wolf-den, you want to head back to the road -- the den is on the other side of the road from my camp. I've been watching them, trying to learn which of the wolves is their leader.'
'The wolf-den is somewhere north of my farm, ${PLAYER}! I simply can't return home while they are still wandering around.'
'You haven't taken care of the wolf problem around Waymeet for my friend Dora yet? You'd best get started on that!'

The wolf den is off the road north of Dora Brownlock's farm and Waymeet.
Dora Brownlock is grateful that you rescued her chickens from the wolves, but she is afraid to go home until she is sure that the wolves will no longer trouble her. She has asked you to go to the wolf den and put an end to the threat.

Dora Brownlock is at the centre of Waymeet.
Dora Brownlock will be pleased to hear that you have done something about the wolves threatening the area.
Defeated Spear-wielding goblins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Have you heard the rumours yet? Friends of mine are saying that Pansy Tunnelly down at Scary saw a goblin on the Greenfields, and that there are sure to be more of them creeping into the Shire!
'This is terrible news! The grazing on the Greenfields is better than anywhere else, and I bring my sheep out there every day. What will I do if goblins surprise me out there? I heard some goblins are particularly skilled with spears. I could be a pincushion before I even saw them! You'd be putting my mind at ease if you could make sure there are none of those spear-throwing goblins in the north Greenfields, ${PLAYER}.'
'I would feel a lot better if I knew there really were no goblins out there at all!'
'It's safe? Are you sure? Nothing to worry about? Oh, that is such a relief! Thank you, thank you!'
Defeat Spear-wielding goblins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Distant Dangers
Ponto Hornblower of Brockenborings is concerned about the appearance of goblins in the Shire and wants to protect his grazing rights on the Greenfields.

'There are rumours about goblins in the Shire and about the deadly spears some of them can use to hurt you from a distance! If you could make sure there are no goblins in the Greenfields, my sheep and I will feel much safer, I just know it!'
'The only thing worse than a goblin is a goblin that can hurt you from a distance!'
'My sheep will graze more contentedly now that you've dealt with those goblins!'

Spear-wielding goblins can be found in the north Greenfields.
Ponto Hornblower is afraid that he might be attacked from a distance by goblins throwing spears, if the rumours prove true, and has asked you to remove that threat.

Ponto Hornblower is in Brockenborings, near the centre of town.
Rumours of goblins in the Greenfields had Ponto Hornblower concerned for his safety and the safety of his sheep. He had asked you to make sure there were no spear-wielding goblins in the fields. You found many, but managed to dispatch them without too much trouble. You should let Ponto know it should be safe for him to return to the Greenfields, though tact may be required to avoid panicking the Shire-folk.
Defeated bats (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I don't know what's going on with the animals in the Shire lately, but here in Scary we've been having more than our share of troubles. There have always been bats roosting in dark places throughout the Shire, but hobbits know better than to go near them.
'Something has stirred up the bats, though, and they've begun coming out during the daytime! They've even started attacking folk on the outskirts of town! We can't have that, ${PLAYER}, we can't have that at all!
'If you see any of the nasty creatures, I'd appreciate it if you could put an end to them. You'll find them especially to the south, in and around the Marish. I just wonder what's caused them to start attacking like this?'

'Thank you very much for your help, ${PLAYER}! I don't know what it is that has driven these bats out of their caves, but whatever it is, it's not welcome here! The sooner it leaves, the better!
'Maybe it has already gone, and it's just a matter of time before the bats quiet down again? Oh, I hope so!'
Defeat bats (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Restless Roost
Something has driven the bats near Scary to swoop from their caves and attack hobbits on the outskirts of the town.
'There are bats all around Scary these days, and especially to the south. There never used to be!'
'Something came into the Shire and stirred up all these animals, I think.'
'Whatever upset the creatures of the Shire, it must have been something really scary!'

Prisca Underhill is at the entrance of Scary.
Prisca Underhill wants you to deal with the bats south of Scary which have become hostile, attacking even during the day.

Prisca Underhill is in Scary, near the entrance to town.
Prisca will be pleased to hear that you have done your part to alleviate the threat of the bats outside Scary.
Closed shrew burrows (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You're just the sort I was hoping would come along -- a Bounder!
'My brother up in Brockenborings is a Bounder, so ordinarily I would ask him for help with this, but Brockenborings is such a long way from here, and I really want to get this problem taken care of as soon as possible.
'There's a terrible infestation of shrews to the east of here, beyond the Delving Fields, and they're burrowing deep into the soil and ruining the greenery! If you can find some of their burrows and close them up, that should keep the filthy little beasts from straying near to the town. It's your duty to help me with this, Bounder!'
'Thank you for your help, Bounder ${PLAYER}! That should discourage the shrews from burrowing near the town, for a while at least.'
Close shrew burrows (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Close Up Their Burrows
The shrew population near Michel Delving has increased tremendously recently, and Ruby Primstone wants the Bounders to do something about it.
'There are shrew burrows to the east, beyond the Delving Fields. They need to be closed before the beasts tunnel any closer to the town!'
'I'm glad we don't need to worry about those burrowing shrews anymore!'
'Thank you for taking care of the shrew problem!'

There are shrew burrows to the east of Michel Delving, beyond the Delving Fields.
Ruby Primstone is upset by the ruination of the greenery caused by the shrews and wants you to close up some of their burrows.

Ruby Primstone is in Michel Delving, at her home south-east of the statue of Marcho and Blanco in the centre of town.
Ruby will be pleased to hear that you have closed some of the shrew burrows near the town.
Collected prickly broom leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'He may not accept charity from me, his \qsworn enemy,\q but I think I should try to help this Callum all the same.
'This wound of his, from the boar, most likely needs to be bandaged. To ward off infection and help the wound to heal, we should soak the bandages in an unguent of...let's see, what would be best?
'Prickly broom, I think. I already have the bandages, but I don't have the broom leaves. Could I ask you to help me once more and gather some prickly broom leaves from the bushes south-east of Budgeford, near to the Water?'

'Ah, you have the leaves, please let me have them. This will only take a moment...
'Please take these bandages to Callum at his campsite on the far west side of the Frogmoors. Tell him he should change the bandages daily. There are enough here for seven days. Hopefully that will be enough to help him heal.
'Also, let him know that I hold no malice against him...and ask that he do the same for me!'
'Have you the leaves? I will need a few piles of leaves to make the solution for Callum's bandages. They grow on bushes to the south-east of Budgeford, near to the Water.'

'Bandages? From the little man? I...and this is not treachery of some sort? I...I am not sure what to say. I have hated this mark against my family for so long, I thought it would finally be erased if the little man was dead...but these are not the actions of an enemy....
'Should my anger be aimed at those who forced my ancestor into battle? Or should I lay the blame upon Fate and leave my anger behind? I have much to think upon.
'I thank you. This Wilimar has nothing to fear from me.'
'Why do you bother me? Leave me be to die in peace!'
Collect prickly broom leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring prickly broom leaves to Wilimar Bolger
Bring bandages to Callum
Bandages for Callum

Reading further in the journal, Wilimar has begun to sympathize with Callum, the Hillman who swore to kill him. Learning of Callum's hard-fought life in a realm far in the north, he has decided to aid Callum and help him with the wound he suffered from the wild boar.
'There should be plenty of prickly broom bushes south-east of Budgeford, near the Water. Gather me some leaves from them, so that I can make the unguent I need for Callum's bandages.'
'Please take those bandages to Callum. Hopefully they will help him heal, and perhaps he will lose his malice towards me! His camp is west of here, near the far western edge of the Frogmoors.'
'I was so afraid for my life! Thank you for your help, Bounder.'
'So Callum will leave me be? Ah, that is such a relief!'
'I am not accustomed to mercy from an enemy. Perhaps I have misjudged these little people.'
'Perhaps Wilimar's honour will erase my family's mark of dishonour. Only time will tell.'

Prickly broom grows along the Water, south-east of Budgeford.
Wilimar has decided to provide Callum with bandages for his wound, but to aid in his healing, he wants to soak the bandages in an unguent made from prickly broom leaves. He has asked you to gather these leaves for him.

Wilimar Bolger can be found near his hole on the north-west side of Budgeford.
Wilimar has decided to provide Callum with bandages for his wound, but to aid in his healing, he wants to soak the bandages in an unguent made from prickly broom leaves. He has asked you to gather these leaves for him.

Callum's camp is on the far west side of the Frogmoors, west of Budgeford.
With the prickly broom leaves you gathered, Wilimar was able to prepare an unguent in which to soak the bandages. In addition to giving the bandages to Callum, Wilimar has asked you to tell Callum that he holds no malice against him and hopes he will do the same.

'Oh dear, this isn't good, not good at all. Many of the leaves of the journal are missing, as if it were shaken and torn by a beast. Look here, see the teeth marks?
'Goodness, those teeth marks might be from a wolf! I wonder if some of the beasts took the pages, perhaps to line their dens? Yes, yes, I know it sounds strange, but I've heard a tale or two of them doing such things.
'If you could, slay a few of the wolves east of here and see if they have any of the journal leaves. I seem to be missing about three leaves all told. Once I have all the pages, I should be able to see what the author of the journal was up to!'

'Marvelous, you've found them all. Thank you! Now to see what this means....
'Goodness, this is interesting...and distressing! I will need a moment more to read this, but it would appear the author of this journal was a man named \qCallum.\q And the tale it tells is an astonishing one!
'As hard as it is to believe, it would seem a distant ancestor of mine slew one of his in a great battle! And, oh dear...he means to revenge himself upon me....'

'Have you found all of the missing journal leaves? It looks like wolves tore the journal apart, so slay the beasts you find near Budgeford and see if they are carrying any of the journal's leaves.
'The journal looks to be missing about three of its leaves, and I will need all three if I am to learn who is behind this arrow in my door and if they mean me harm!'
Bring the journal leaves to Wilimar Bolger
A Few Pages Short
The journal you brought back to Wilimar Bolger was missing many of its leaves, thanks to being shaken and torn by some wild beasts.

Wolves can be found east of Budgeford.
Without the missing leaves, it will be impossible to determine who shot the arrow in Wilimar Bolger's door, nor why. Wilimar suspects that wolves tore the journal apart and has asked you to try to recover the leaves from them.

'Goodness, the author of this journal, Callum, has a dark past! It would seem the death of his ancestor to my ancestor at that great battle was a black mark on his family. They bore that mark for centuries.
'After a string of bad luck, which Callum blames on this mark, he decided to try and erase it by killing a descendant of the one who killed his ancestor. After years of tracking, he found the Shire...and me! The arrowhead that killed his ancestor was the one shot into my door.
'I think I know where you can find him. He describes where he has set his camp, and it sounds like it is west of here, on the far west side of the Frogmoors. You have to stop him!'

'So the wretched little man sent you to end my life, did he? I suppose it is only right. My life has been accursed because of the mark of dishonour upon my family.
'Do as you will. I have not the strength to defend myself, as you can see. When that rat-man found the arrow in his door, he raised an alarm. I was afraid of being found before I was ready, so I fled my hiding place. In my flight, though, I startled a boar, and the vile thing gored me.
'It is only a matter of time before I succumb to the wound. If you are not going to kill me, at least do me the service of telling that Wilimar that he has nothing to fear from me now. The tired years of my life are nearly spent....'

'Goodness, what a relief! And yet, I can't help but feel badly for this Callum.
'You see, I have read more of his journal, and his life was a truly pitiable one. The place where he lives, far in the north, seems to be a dark, hard-fought place. Nothing like the Shire, and he's not had much luck.
'I think he may deserve a bit of charity, if you would help me with this.'
The Menace Confronted

By reading the reassembled journal, Wilimar has learned it was written by a Man named Callum. Callum's ancestor was killed in a great battle by Wilimar's ancestor, and the family has borne this death as a black mark for centuries. Callum has decided to erase the mark by coming to the Shire and killing a descendant of that hobbit.

'Why do you stand here? It is clear I pose no threat, and you obviously have no interest in ending my wretched life.
'Away with you! Tell the rat-man that he has nothing to fear from me. Vengeance will not be repaid today...'

'Please hurry, friend, and see if you can find this Callum. You just have to convince him to give up this mission of vengeance! According to his journal, he has camped west of Budgeford, on the western edge of the Frogmoors.'

Callum's campsite is on the far west side of the Frogmoors, west of Budgeford.
In light of the revelations gleaned from Callum's journal, Wilimar Bolger has asked you to go to Callum's camp and stop him from carrying out his intended revenge.

Wilimar Bolger can be found near his hole on the north-west side of Budgeford.
When you arrived at Callum's campsite, you found him wounded. Racked with pain, he told of how he had fled from his hiding place near Wilimar's home, only to startle a wild boar, which gored him. He feels that he will soon succumb to his wounds and told you to let Wilimar know he has nothing more to fear.
You spot a journal on the ground

'I am in desperate need of your help! Look...look what I found stuck in my door this morning!
'Look at this! It is such a strange arrow. The head is certainly of hobbit-make, although very, very old. The arrow's shaft though bears a resemblance to those made by Big Folk. Why would someone do this? What does this mean?
'It looks like the arrow came from somewhere directly north of here, near the hedge-gate leading to the Greenfields. I'm too frightened to go over there -- who knows what is lurking there -- but could you go there for me and see what you can find?'
'So you found this journal near the hedge-gate, did you? Well, hopefully it contains some clues as to who loosed that arrow into my door, and perhaps it will tell if he means me any harm!'
'That journal you spotted, do you have it? Perhaps it has the information I need to find out what is going on with this arrow!'
Search north of Wilimar Bolger's home
Bring the journal to Wilimar Bolger
The Veiled Menace

When Wilimar Bolger woke up this morning, he found a threatening arrow stuck in the door of his home. The arrow's head was of hobbit-make, although very old, while the shaft looked like it was made by Men.
'I think the arrow was loosed from somewhere north of here, not far from my home. I simply must know who shot this arrow and why!'

The arrow came from the area near the hedge-gate that leads to the Greenfields, north of Wilimar Bolger's home.
Wilimar Bolger has asked you to search the place where he thinks the arrow came from, in hopes of finding some sign of the person who loosed it and what it might mean.

Wilimar Bolger can be found near his hole on the north-west side of Budgeford.
In the area Wilimar Bolger asked you to search, you found an abandoned campsite and a journal. Perhaps this journal will contain some information helpful to Wilimar. You should take it back to him.
You have protected Isembard and Imbert Took
Collected Adelard's chapter

'I need your help! I made a terrible mistake and listened to Isembard and Imbert, my fool cousins. You see, old Adelard is always lecturing us young Tooks on the history of the family, and well, it does get tiring. My cousins decided to play a trick on him and convinced me to sneak away with the latest chapter Adelard wrote for the Yearbook of Tuckborough.
'Now I'm worried about the trouble I'm going to get into! Isembard, though, went out to get the chapter from where he hid it, but hasn't returned yet!
'I think he said he hid it in a tall tree east of the Great Smials in Tuckborough. Could you go there and see what is taking him so long?'

'What? Pervinca sent a Bounder out here? She is such a worrier! There's nothing to fear, old Imbert and me will have that chapter of Adelard's in two shakes.
'See, we hid the chapter in a satchel in the tree, but the branch we climbed up on broke off. We have been here scratching our heads on how to get it down...but you just gave me a grand idea!'
'Good, you've found it! Now to sneak this back into the library before Adelard notices it's gone missing. My thanks! You've saved me from a host of troubles!'
'Good, you've found that satchel. Now where is the chapter that Isembard put within it? You must bring it back to me quickly, before Adelard discovers it's missing!'
Speak to Isembard Took
Bring Adelard's chapter to Pervinca Took
Adelard's Chapter

Pervinca Took made the mistake of helping her cousins Isembard and Imbert play a trick on the aged Adelard Took. Pervinca sneaked off with the chapter he wrote for the Yearbook of Tuckborough, and Isembard hid it.
'Oh, good day to you! Are you here about that chapter of Adelard's as well? Best be talking to Isembard, he's the smarter of us two! I'm just here to lend him a hand, if I can.'
'I thought that satchel would never fall from that tree. But, fortunately, old Isembard's plan worked. I always said he was the smarter of the two of us, and this just proved it again!'

'See, I told you we'd have that satchel out of the tree quick enough! You'd best take it to Pervinca.
'Still, I wish we had hung on to it a bit longer...we're sure to hear another of old Adelard's speeches now.'
'Isembard and Imbert should be near that big willow east of the Great Smials in Tuckborough. Please hurry, I don't know how long it'll be until Adelard discovers that his chapter is missing!'
'Thank you so much, Bounder! I won't let Isembard and Imbert get me into trouble again!'
'I felt so awful after taking away old Adelard's chapter. Thank you for getting it back!'

Pervinca thought her cousins Isembard and Imbert Took could be found near the Great Willow east of the Great Smials in Tuckborough.
Pervinca asked you to find her cousins Isembard and Imbert, who went to retrieve Adelard's chapter of the Yearbook, and see what is taking him so long.

Bring Adelard's chapter back to Pervinca Took in the Great Smials.
Having survived Isembard's grand idea for getting the satchel with Adelard's chapter down from the tree, you finally have the chapter in hand to bring back to Pervinca.
Defeated harvest-flies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It used to be that harvest-flies were just a nuisance. They'd chew on our crops and cause some damage, but you learned to live with them.
'Recently, though, the harvest-flies have gone so far as to attack hobbits in the Marish! I don't know what has them stirred up so, but whatever it is, I wish it hadn't!
'If you can deal with our harvest-fly problem, I'd really appreciate it, Bounder! I hear there's a whole nest of them on the Yale-height, a hill a fair piece to the south and east of Budgeford. It's not very far north-east of Woodhall. There are three old pillars atop the Yale-height, so it shouldn't be too hard to find.'

'Well, that's a relief, ${PLAYER}. I don't know what's caused the harvest-flies to begin attacking people, and I don't think I want to know! I just want them to calm down and leave the good folk of the Marish alone!'
Defeat harvest-flies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Trouble With Harvest-flies
Harvest flies are generally just a nuisance to the crops, but recently they have begun attacking hobbits in the Marish.

'You can find harvest-flies all throughout the Marish, ${PLAYER}, but especially on the Yale-height, south-west of Budgeford and north-east of Woodhall. There are three pillars on the crown of the hill, and you should be able to see it from a good distance. We'll all feel a little safer if you can get rid of some harvest-flies!'
'I couldn't stand harvest-flies when all they did was ruin crops, but now they're even worse!'
'Harvest-flies attacking people? That just doesn't seem right! Well, you showed them, I'm sure.'

There is a nest of harvest-flies on the Yale-height a distance to the south and east of Budgeford, not far north-east of Woodhall. The hill is marked by three pillars at its pinnacle.
Bingo Bolger is disturbed by the increased aggression in the harvest-flies and has asked you to help deal with them.

Bingo Bolger is in Budgeford, by a pig pen on the lower slope of the town.
Bingo Bolger reported increased aggression among the harvest-flies in the Marish and asked you to deal with them. You should return to him with word of your success.
Defeated bears on the greenfields (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There have always been bears on the Greenfields, but recently something has made them angry. They've begun attacking shepherds and sheep alike, and I don't know how long it will be before someone is seriously hurt!
'If you can discourage the bears from the Greenfields, it will be much safer for those of us whose work takes us north of Brockenborings, and also for those of us who just like a pleasant walk in the sun!
'Would you be of a mind to help? I'm sure it would be much appreciated.'

'You have braved the claws of the angry bears? Many thanks to you, ${PLAYER}! I will tell my friends here in Brockenborings that soon they will be able to walk the Greenfields again without fear of the bears!'
Defeat bears on the greenfields (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bears On the Greenfields
Something has caused the bears on the Greenfields to become more aggressive recently, and Bodo Goodbody is worried that it is not safe to walk there anymore.
'The bears on the Greenfields, north of Brockenborings, have become suddenly hostile. I wonder what could have disturbed them so?'
'I wonder why the bears have begun attacking us? What might have upset them?'
'The Greenfields were a pleasant place to walk, before the animals began attacking without warning!'
'Thank you for your help with the bears, ${PLAYER}!'

Bears can be found on the Greenfields, north of Brockenborings.
Bodo Goodbody has asked you to discourage the bears from roaming the Greenfields, in hopes that it will once again become safe for people to go there.

Bodo Goodbody sent you to discourage the bears from roaming the Greenfields. He will be pleased to learn that you have reduced the threat.

'I've lost my lucky sling-stone! I had just dropped a deer when suddenly a bear -- a huge, brown bear it was, too -- grabbed the kill and dragged it off! I don't care about the venison, but I need my lucky sling-stone! I can't hunt without it.
'Please, help me if you can and get back that sling-stone from the deer's carcass. The bear dragged it off into that big den to the north of here. He's probably on the slopes north of the Bolestones, feasting on the deer I killed.
'All my luck has gone away with that stone!'
'You've found it! I can't thank you enough! That stone has all my luck in it. I just know it!'
'You weren't able to find the deer carcass and my sling-stone at the bear den? Look for it north of here, on the slopes north of Bolestones.'
Bring the lucky sling-stone to Everard Holebourne
Collect the lucky slingstone
Lucky Sling-stone
Everard Holebourne lost his venison and his favourite sling-stone to a marauding bear.
'Now that I have my lucky sling-stone back, I can feel my fortunes changing!'
'Without my lucky sling-stone, my aim was poorer than it's ever been!'

The bear den is north of Overhill, located on the slopes above the Bolestones. Everard awaits you at his home in the middle of Overhill.
Everard Holebourne has asked you to retrieve his lucky sling-stone from the carcass of the deer he killed, which was dragged off to a bear den.

'My thanks again for taking that last batch of eggs to Holly in Hobbiton, but I've got another cook waiting on some eggs, if you've got the time to deliver them!
'Gammer Tunnelly in Tuckborough is a fine lady...misses her grandson terribly though. If you could deliver the basket of eggs right there to her, I'd really appreciate it!
'Remember, don't let the rooster see you. I can't have the hens all upset by him and not laying!'
'Gammer Tunnelly is such a sweet, old hobbit. I'm glad she got the eggs. You have my thanks again, ${PLAYER}. When my leg gets better, maybe I can do a favour for you, eh?'
Pickup the egg basket
Avoid the rooster
Eggs for Gammer Tunnelly

'Go ahead and grab that basket of eggs there. There should be enough in there for Gammer Tunnelly.'
'Oh, thank you again for bringing me those eggs. Please give my thanks to Farmer Sandson and let him know I hope his leg heals soon!'
'Thank you again for making those deliveries. I'd never done it with this bad leg.'
'That rooster is a watchful one...I'm surprised you sneaked past him like you did!'
'Oh, thank you so much for bringing those eggs!'
'Farmer Sandson is such a gentlehobbit!'

Gammer Tunnelly can be found in the centre of Tuckborough.
When you returned from delivering the eggs to Holly Hornblower, he asked you to make another delivery to Gammer Tunnelly in Tuckborough. Be careful that the rooster doesn't see you with the eggs, as he will let out a call that will upset the hens.

A rooster spotted you

'My thanks again for gathering the eggs, but I need to ask another favour, if you can spare me the time.
'One of the cooks waiting on these eggs is Holly Hornblower, and I'd hate to disappoint her...she makes the most wonderful pies. I've put some of the eggs in the basket next to me, so if you could take the basket up to Holly, I'd appreciate it.
'Holly lives up the road to the east in Hobbiton, behind The Ivy Bush. Please be quick about delivering them, if you would. And again, be careful that the rooster don't see you with 'em. He'll let out a call that'll upset the whole flock if he catches sight of you!'

'Ah, good! I'm glad old Holly got her eggs. Now she can be making those pies everyone loves.
'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}, but I wonder if you'd be up for one last delivery?'
Collect the egg basket
Avoid roosters
Eggs for Holly Hornblower
Due to his bad leg, Farmer Sandson cannot deliver the eggs Holly Hornblower in Hobbiton is waiting for.

'Them eggs for Holly are right there in that basket. Take it to her in Hobbiton, if you would. She lives just behind The Ivy Bush.
'I need to ask you to be quick though, as Holly is waiting on them eggs for her pies. And be careful that the rooster don't see you. If he catches sight of you, he'll call out and upset the hens!'

'Thanks again for those eggs. I just used my last one in my latest batch of pie crust. Not sure what I would have done if ye hadn't come by!
'And please thank Farmer Sandson for the eggs. His chickens produce some of the largest and best eggs in all the Shire! His farm is west of Waymeet.'

Holly Hornblower's house is in Hobbiton, behind The Ivy Bush.
Pick up the egg basket and carry it to Holly Hornblower in Hobbiton. Be careful that the rooster doesn't see you with the eggs, as he will let out a call that will upset the hens.

Farmer Sandson is at his farm, west of Waymeet.

'Good day to you, young ${PLAYER:lady[f]|fellow}. Seems I'm in a spot of trouble, and I wonder if you could help me?
'You see, I've got a couple of cooks who're waiting on eggs from my chickens, but the problem is I've gone and hurt my leg. It's nothing serious, but I can't get out there and gather the eggs them cooks need. Now I don't want to disappoint them, so I was wondering if you could make the rounds and check the nests for eggs?
'The nests are just out in the yard. Four or so eggs should be enough. A bit of warning though, don't let the rooster see you gathering eggs. If he does, he'll let out a call that'll get all the hens upset, and worse -- you're sure to be so surprised that you'll drop the eggs you collected!'

'Good, you've found the eggs!
'Now, if you are still able to help, I've more work for you. With my leg ailing me, I couldn't possibly deliver them!'
'Do you have them eggs from the nests? I just need four or so for them cooks.'

Avoid the rooster

Making the Rounds
Farmer Sandson has hurt his leg and cannot tend to his chickens or their nests.

'Just go on out there and search the nests for eggs. Shouldn't be too hard to find enough of them.
'Remember, don't let the rooster see you, or he'll get the whole flock upset, and the hens won't be laying for days! Worse still, he crows so suddenly that it can startle someone something fierce -- you might drop the eggs!'

The chicken nests are around Farmer Sandson's yard.
Farmer Sandson has asked you to gather some eggs from his chicken nests, but warned you to stay away from the rooster. If he sees you while you are gathering the eggs, they will call out and upset the other chickens. Furthermore, you are sure to drop the eggs you've collected!

Farmer Sandson is at his farm, west of Waymeet.
You managed to gather enough eggs without being noticed by the rooster. You should take them back to Farmer Sandson.
