Cal Sprigley and his wife await you north of the ruins of The Mad Badger Inn in Archet.
Cal and Holly Sprigley are waiting in Archet for the possessions you recovered from their spider-infested farm. You should return to them at once.

'Them spiders have et my workhands and driven me and Holly out of our home. There's got to be some way to get 'em off our land!
'I would think that Atli Spider-bane might know more about spiders than I do. Perhaps you should go speak with him again.
'We can't return home until those awful things are gone!'

You search Bali's corpse and find a journal with several pages missing. The journal text reads:
'I would not believe it, but the spiders have pushed the cave mouth clear! I have entered the cave, and the spiders reacted to me instantly, as if drawn to me. I am unsure why. I spent my day carefully searching near the entrance only and found several corpses bound into cocoons. These spiders seem to wrap everything up into their cocoons! I will write more tomorrow when I go further into the cave.'
Perhaps it would be best to enter the cave to see if you can find the rest of the journal pages before returning to Atli.

'Good, you have returned! It seems there is much more going on here than I first thought. While you were away, my cousin Bali arrived, and I sent him to search some caves in the ruins outside the east wall of Archet. A few of the hunters had dropped a huge stone in front of the cave, and I wanted him to ensure the stone remained. He has not yet returned, and I am worried.
'Now, from what you told me of Sprigley's troubles, the spiders came up through the cellar in his shed. Perhaps seeing the cave blocked off, they tunnelled up through there.
'We won't know for certain, though, until you find Bali. Hopefully he'll have some answers.'

'I cannot believe it. Bali gone. He must be avenged! And this journal tells me what is behind this: a spider-queen from the Blue Mountains. She and her brood must have followed me from Thorin's Halls.
'Know this! Even if I am slain, she will never leave this place...she has found easy prey here. We must destroy her, or Archet shall become a new abode for the queen and her spawn.'
'Have you found the missing pages of Bali's journal?'
Search for Bali
Find missing journal pages (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Found missing journal pages (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Bring the journal and journal pages to Atli Spider-bane
Finding Reason
Cal Sprigley's farm has been overrun by spiders for no apparent reason, leaving Cal and Holly homeless in Archet.
'Go find Bali quickly before something terrible happens! I sent him to the caves in the ruins due east of here.'

'Bali...dead? This is...impossible! And the spiders have pushed the cave open? You must enter the cave and search for the rest of his journal.
'We must avenge Bali, and that journal may hold the knowledge that will help us do that!'
'Them spiders came up through my shed on the far end of the farm, but you should speak with Atli before going there again. He'll know more about what to do, I'm sure.'
'I don't think I can help you. Atli's cousin must be around that cave somewhere.'

Atli Spider-bane can be found just north of Cal Sprigley.
Cal Sprigley suggested that you speak with Atli Spider-bane about the spiders at his farm and how to be rid of them.

The entrance to the cave the hunters blocked off lies in the ruins due east of Archet.
Atli told you that he sent his cousin Bali to check the caves, but he has not yet returned. If you find him, he may have the answer to what has disturbed the spiders.

The missing pages of Bali's journal must be somewhere within the caves. The spiders may have taken the missing pages and webbed them into their cocoons.
You have found Bali's corpse and his journal, but the journal is missing several pages. You need to find the pages before returning to Atli.

Atli Spider-bane can be found at the north end of Archet.
Atli Spider-bane will want to know what you discovered amongst the pages of Bali's journal.

'This spider-queen -- Iornaith by name -- and her ways are known to me. She will have hidden herself in Sprigley's house and blocked all the entrances, save one.
'If you search the tunnels below the house, I would wager you will find a hidden passage leading to Iornaith's lair. The vile thing must be slain, or Archet will be overrun by her brood.
'Would that I were hale and could heft an axe! But that time has passed. Now, the mantle of Spider-bane must pass to you, if you'll have it. I do not suggest you try to face her alone.'

'\qMany seeds did the Dread-weaver sow throughout our mountains....\q
'Because of you, another of those seeds has passed from the world.
'I owe you a great debt...for Iornaith's death and for my life. Accept this reward, and with it, the friendship of Atli Spider-bane!'
An ancient spider-queen has pursued Atli Spider-bane to Archet and invaded Cal Sprigley's farm.
'This spider is clever. Seek the entrance to her lair beneath Sprigley's farm. And beware her fangs! Though I ruined her eyes, she is ancient and full of malice.'
'You are most worthy of the name Spider-bane, O Slayer of Iornaith!'
'I am proud to call you friend, ${PLAYER}. I am at your service and your family's!'

Sprigley's farm south of Bronwe's Folly. One entrance to the spider tunnels lies through the cellar of Sprigley's shed, while the other is through the cave mouth due west of the Hunter's Lodge.
To prevent Iornaith's brood from overrunning Archet, Atli Spider-bane has asked you to find and slay the spider-queen. Atli suggests searching the spider caves beneath Sprigley's farm for a secret entrance into the Iornaith's lair. He also suggested you take allies.

Atli Spider-bane can be found at the north end of Archet, west of the spider-cave, north-west of Sprigley's farm.
You should take news of Iornaith's defeat to Atli Spider-bane.

'With all these folk coming in from the outlying farms, there's just not enough food to go around! My Ned's got his hands full trying to keep the peace inside the walls, and what with everyone else drilling on the training grounds, there's no one left to do the hunting.
'Maybe you could help out? Boars used to be plentiful in the fields south and east of town, if the Blackwolds haven't slaughtered them all. Could you hunt a few and bring me their meat?
'It will take a good amount of meat to feed all these people. I'd appreciate any help you could give me.'

'Did you hunt every boar in the fields? I'll not complain. This'll do well for quite a while! Thank you!
'Here, you should share in this bounty, and if you ever find yourself needing more, just come and see me.'
'The boars should be wandering the fields south of Archet's main gate.'
Bring the slabs of boar-meat to Peg Pruner
Collect slabs of boar-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Must be completed prior to the \qIntroduction.\q
Fresh Supplies
The flood of refugees into Archet has caused a supply shortage, and Captain Brackenbrook's quartermaster, Peg Pruner, is having difficulty providing for the refugees.

There are boars in the fields south and east of Archet.

Collected piles of bilberries (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You're the one what helped discover that old Calder here was a traitor, ain't ye? Ye have me thanks for that, friend! I was just talking to my Peg about that. You're quite a hero!
'Calder here could probably tell us a lot about what them Blackwolds are planning, if only he'd talk. Thing is, he's refusing to talk until he gets some better food, and he wants bilberry cakes. But me Peg don't have no bilberries to make the cakes.
'Could you maybe go out and pick a few piles of bilberries from the bushes near the Hunters' Lodge? The lodge lies at the end of the road leading east from Archet's gates. If I could just get some cakes, maybe then Calder would talk!'

'Those bilberries sure smell good! Too bad I have to feed 'em to a traitor.
'Well, I'm going to just step out for a moment and take them over to Peg. She'll get the cakes baked up and brought over. Then finally we'll get some information out of old Calder there!'
'Do you have those bilberries? Calder Cob won't talk until he has his bilberry cakes.'
Collect piles of bilberries (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the berries to Ned Pruner

Question the Prisoner
The traitor, Calder Cob, refuses to speak with the gullible jailor, Ned Pruner, until he has some bilberry cakes.

'I really need those berries if I'm going to get the cakes that'll loosen Calder's tongue. Bilberry bushes grow near the Hunter's Lodge, east of Archet.
'You can get to the lodge if you follow the road eastward from Archet's gates.'

Bilberry bushes grow near the Hunter's Lodge east of Archet.
Ned Pruner has asked you to gather enough bilberries to bake the cakes that Calder Cob demanded.

'Anlaf wants me to offer better blankets to our guests from Bree. Better blankets! Can you believe that? You come from the town, and you get better blankets. I ask you, is that right by any measure? No, it isn't!
'I have no choice but to see to it. Your first blankets are good enough for those used to the harder life, but their betters need something better, according to Anlaf.
'So I need you to head into Nain Enidh, east beyond Weathertop, and defeat some of the lynx there. Their fur is soft and well-kept. Bring it to me and I will make these blankets, despite my protests.'

'The fur is certainly softer. I may take one of these for my own bedding.
'I owe you a bit of coin, I think, ${PLAYER}. I can think of nothing else that I need done at the moment. You have done wonders for me and freed me to see to all of my other duties.'
'Lynx prowl the lands east of the inn, beyond Weathertop. Don't travel too far, lest you find orcs, spiders, and all manner of things most foul.'
Bring soft lynx-hides to Arinora
Collect soft lynx-hide (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Better Blankets
Arinora is displeased with the preferential treatment that Anlaf is demanding for guests from the town of Bree, but there is little she can do about it.
'You have been a big help to me, ${PLAYER}.'
'There is always work to be done, but for now things are manageable.'

Lynx prowl through Nain Enidh, east of the Forsaken Inn and beyond Weathertop.
Arinora asked you to collect lynx-hides so she can make better blankets for the inn's more affluent guests.
Collected wolf-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There are too many travellers, even through this remote land, and the nearest water sits foul and stagnant. We've the well, of course, but water is rationed among all the guests and does not go as far as it might.
'Blankets need making and mending, and there are no better hides to be found than those of the wolves. The hide of a warg is too coarse, but a wolf's fur can be made soft with a comb. If you've the time and a good heart, I would ask your assistance; you'll not see me stomping through the brush to get to the wolves, as deadly as they are!
'There are a few places you may want to look for wolves with proper hides. Wolves creep among the ruins of Minas Eriol to the south, though that place is also crawling with wargs and goblins. Wolves hunt too among the Weather Hills, to the east and north. Finally, you could travel even further north, but the Midgewater Pass is dangerous and full of even worse things than wolves. When you have the wolf-hides, return to me and I'll see you are rewarded.'

'These are fine furs indeed! I'll cure these and sew a nice batch of new blankets for the guests.
'I'll thank you for your time with a bit of coin from my purse.'

'There are a few places you may want to look for wolves with proper hides. Wolves creep among the ruins of Minas Eriol to the south, though that place is also crawling with wargs and goblins. Wolves hunt too among the Weather Hills, to the east and north. Finally, you could travel even further north, but the Midgewater Pass is dangerous and full of even worse things than wolves.'

Blankets from the Baying Wolves
Arinora has become overwhelmed with the many responsibilities she bears for the maintenance of the Forsaken Inn.
'Wolf-hides can be made into decent blankets for those who have none, at need.'
'There is always work to be done here.'

Wolves can be found in the ruins of Minas Eriol south of the Forsaken Inn, among the Weather Hills to the northeast, and in the Midgewater Pass to the north.
Arinora of the Forsaken Inn asked you to collect wolf-hides so she can make blankets for its guests.
Collected craban-feathers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ever since the Munces showed up, I've had no rest! Normally, we see no guests for months on end, but the glut of guests here has me stretched to my limit!
'Anlaf is under great strain and takes his worries out on me, driving harder to see that the chambers are cared for, the workers watched, and the guests fed. Well, I'm just not able to do it all! You've been a great help so far, and I see no reason why you shouldn't continue being so!
'One thing that still needs to be done is the replacing of the pillows. All the stuffing's gone missing with the use they are getting, and I need to get the fluff back into them. We don't have the luxury of ducks, but the crebain circling about in the north might do in a pinch. There are plenty of the troublesome thorn-talon and sharp-eye crebain lurking about. Bring me some of their feathers and I'll pay you for your trouble. The birds circle often over the summit of Weathertop.'

'Is that awful smell coming from these feathers? Oh my, I had never thought that those terrible, little birds could give off such a stench!
'No matter, I suppose. With the cooking that Old Mugwort does, this stench'll fade into the background of curious smells that haunt the inn in no time!'

'I told you I would pay you well, but I think I should lower my payment if you continue to lay about the inn! You will earn no coin until you bring me the feathers for which I asked. It's only fair, ${PLAYER}!'
Bring craban-feathers to Arinora
Collect craban-feathers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fluffing the Pillows
Arinora's duties became even greater when the Munces arrived at the Forsaken Inn. Anlaf is an unforgiving innkeep, according to Arinora, and she needs help to keep up with everything.
'Craban-wings smell terribly!'
'We do what we can with what we have. That's the way of life in the Lone-lands.'

Thorn-talon and Sharp-eye Crebain can be found on and around Weathertop, in the Lone-lands.
In an effort to see to all the work before her, Arinora asked you to collect craban-feathers to help her stuff the pillows of the Forsaken Inn.

'Old Mugwort does the cooking around here, but I have some recipes of my own that tickle the fancy of some of the guests. So much so that they have bought out all my latest fare! The recent commotion ran off our modest herd of swine, and I need more pork!
'I need boar-feet and leg-bones. Though I'll not share with you all of my recipe, I will tell you that the marrow from the bones gives the soaked feet a richer taste. Once you pull the fur away and cure the feet in salt you've a tasty treat.
'You should find boars in the surrounding area and northeast among the Weather Hills. Be careful, though -- not every foot is good for eating.'

'Oh, these will do nicely. We can pull the marrow from the bones and wrap the peeled feet in marrow and salt. Add a dash of my secret spices, and we'll once again have several helpings of \qArinora's Boar Surprise!\q
'You did very well! Take these coins as your payment.'
'Do your best not to stray too far...the meat'll spoil before you return. You should find boars near the Inn and northeast among the Weather Hills. Get the bones and feet and bring them back here.'

Some of the guests within the Forsaken Inn have developed a taste for Arinora's pork dishes.
'Old Mugwort doesn't like me preparing dishes, but he has to understand that the guests love my creations!'
'Thank you for bringing me the things I needed, ${PLAYER}.'

Boars can be found in the area surrounding the Forsaken Inn and northeast among the Weather Hills.

Found Bethad in the Gorthorog-cave

'Gertheryg are some of Angmar's most terrible minions. Great troll-like creatures, they are cunning, skilled with arms and armour, and are not affected by the light of the Sun as other trolls are.
'We have observed parties of Gertheryg moving back and forth from a worm-infested cave in the vile Malenhad. I sent a scout, Bethad, to find out what he could of the place, but he has not returned, and I fear the worst.
'Please go and explore the cave, perhaps you can find Bethad within. I fear that it would be most unwise to explore this cave alone, so you should go with what allies you can gather.'
'You are a friend of Fonn? It is well that you have found me, for I need your help!'
Find Bethad in the Gorthorog-cave
Ancient Lair
Fonn has learned that Gertheryg have been seen travelling to a particular cave in Malenhad. He has sent a scout to investigate, but the scout has not returned.
'I fear that something has become of Bethad in that Gorthorog-cave. I would ask that you go there and search for him.'

The Gorthorog-cave is in Malenhad, east of Aughaire.
Fonn has asked you to explore a cave in Malenhad to which Gertheryg have been seen travelling.

Bethad is in the Gorthorog-cave in Malenhad, east of Aughaire.
At Fonn's request, you searched the Gorthorog-cave for Bethad. You have found him, but he appears wounded.

'I am glad you are here. I was wounded by one of these cursed worms and have been forced to hide in the dark corners of this cave for some days. But now that my wound is almost healed, I have learned much by spying on the comings and goings of the Gertheryg.
'This cave is inhabited by an ancient Gorthorog called Ulkrank. He is an old one...the oldest such creature I have ever seen. The other brutes seem to treat him with the greatest reverence. He may perhaps be their ruler.
'For my own part, I am ready to leave this place, but if you would, I think you can do more here. Slay as many of these vile worms as you can, and fight your way to the depths of the cave where Ulkrank dwells. Once he is defeated, tell my friend Fonn in Tyrn Lhuig of your victory. He will surely be concerned about me.'

'You bring good tidings! I am very pleased to hear that Bethad is safe, for I had been cursing myself for sending him alone into such danger.
'But it is also a great deed that you have done, too, my friend. The Gertheryg are some of the most terrible fighters for the Iron Crown, and if they can be dismayed or disheartened even a little by the death of their elder, then the Enemy will be sorely weakened as a result. You have truly won a great victory!'
The Old One
The scout Bethad has found that the worm-cave is the home to a venerated elder Gorthorog called Ulkrank.
'I will rest a little longer and then return to Aughaire on my own. Have no fear for my safety -- you must go into the cave to slay Ulkrank!'
'My wound is healed now. Have no fear for me. I will return on my own to Tyrn Lhuig in my own time.'
'Your defeat of Ulkrank was a mighty deed!'
'The ancient Gorthorog was no match for you.'

Ulkrank, the ancient Gorthorog, can be found somewhere in the depths of the worm-cave.
Bethad has asked you to explore the worm-cave, slaying all the worms you find, and finally, Ulkrank himself.

Fonn is back at Tyrn Lhuig.
Having defeated Ulkrank, Bethad asked you to tell his friend Fonn of your deeds.

'I'm not just the server and maid here at the Forsaken Inn, I'm also a fair hand with needle and thread. At the moment, Anlaf has me making a special treat for the goblins of Annunlos.
'I've been trying to finish this terrible, little scarecrow for weeks, but there are none here willing to risk their lives against the goblins to bring me what I need to complete it. I have all the pieces I need except cloth from enough goblin-tabards to complete the scarecrow.
'If you are willing, go to the ruins of Minas Eriol to the southeast, or to the plains of Annunlos, and bring me some tabards from the goblins there so I can finish this dreadful thing.'

'I have little more to offer you than my thanks. My scarecrow will stand outside the Forsaken Inn as a warning to the goblins of Annunlos; they'll think twice when they see that we've made such a mockery of them!
'Thank you for all you have done, ${CLASS}.'

'I need some tabards from the goblins in the ruins of Minas Eriol, southeast of the Forsaken Inn, or on the plains of Annunlos. Any tabard will do. I am making a scarecrow to keep the goblins away from the inn.'
Bring goblin tabards to Lieva Dourlily
A Clear Message
Goblins in the ruins of Minas Eriol southeast of the Forsaken Inn cause a great deal of trouble for people at the inn. Lieva Dourlily is sewing a scarecrow intended to frighten away the goblins.
'You're much braver than anyone here at the Forsaken Inn, ${PLAYER}!'
'Those goblins won't come here when they see my scarecrow!'

There are goblins in the ruins of Minas Eriol to the southeast of the Forsaken Inn, and on the fields of Annunlos.
To finish her scarecrow, Lieva Dourlily requires some of the tabards worn by the goblins of Annunlos, but no one at the Forsaken Inn is brave enough to risk themselves to collect the cloth for her. She has asked you to gather the tabards for her.

'Once you have finished this last errand, the wargs will no longer be a threat to travellers along the Great East Road. I just know it!
'There is a signpost on the road through Nain Enidh, and a path near this signpost winds southward. If you follow the path as it slopes into a mild depression to the southwest, you will arrive at a stone structure, like an ancient table or a flat section of ruin. Bring the gruel I have prepared to that table and pour some of it onto the stone.
'I am certain that the leader will come running to the food, thinking it the cooking of some foolish ${RACE}! When you have slain the creature, come back here. You'll probably want to take some friends with you. I'd wager that the odds of the warg-leader coming to the stone alone are very slim.'

'We did it! You watch, those wargs'll think twice about chasing down anyone now that you've slain their leader.
'We'll be heroes here at the Forsaken Inn. You'll see!
'I owe you, friend. Here take one of these for all that you've done!'
'Get those wargs out of Nain Enidh. My food shouldn't go to waste this way, but if you can use it to draw out the warg-leader and finish him off, I won't call it a waste!'
Summon and slay the warg-leader
Return to Old Mugwort
Drawing the Pack

While you hunted the wargs of Nain Enidh, Mugwort prepared a special meal for their leader. All that remains to ease passage along the Great East Road is to draw this leader out of hiding and into battle.
'Wargs and goblins are awful things! They'll make you miss dinner!'
'You've done a good job, ${PLAYER}!'

The stone table where you should pour Mugwort's gruel is at the end of a southward path near a signpost on the road through Nain Enidh.
Old Mugwort asked you to take the special gruel he prepared to an ancient stone near the lair of the wargs. The stench of it should draw forth their leader. He also suggested you take friends, for the warg-leader might not come alone.

Old Mugwort is at the Forsaken Inn.
After drawing Shadepaw's pack into the open, you defeated the warg-leader. Old Mugwort will want to hear of your victory.
Added Foul-smelling Draught to Goblin Food Barrels (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I hate the goblins, I do! Skulking thieves, the lot of them, sneaking about in the night so they can pick the best herbs and mushrooms! They'll soon pick the Lone-lands dry if they go unhindered!
'I made a special draught for them, though. It'll make them sluggish and unruly -- maybe unruly enough to fight amongst themselves! And if not, well... it'll have other effects that just might make them change their minds about staying here.
'Take these draughts and pour them into the barrels located in the goblins' camps to the northeast of the inn, at Weatherfoot, the base of Weathertop. Return to me when the deed is done.'

'The goblins didn't seem to show any ill effects from the draught? Well, I guess I shouldn't really be surprised. Goblins eat anything and everything!
'No sense fussing about that right now. You did well by me, ${PLAYER}. I owe you a little coin at the very least.'
Add Foul-smelling Draught to Goblin Food Barrels (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Enfeebling the Foe
Old Mugwort has an intense dislike for the goblins that have recently arrived in the Lone-lands, and seeks to drive them away.

'Those goblins have got to go! Get my draught into their food, and quickly, before they get all the good mushrooms and spices! They have camps to the northeast, at Weatherfoot, southwest of Weathertop.'
'The draught didn't work, did it? Confound it all! Goblins must have iron stomachs.'
'Misery me! If the goblins don't leave, they'll pick all the best herbs!'

There will be barrels of uneaten food at the goblin camps of Weatherfoot, northeast of the Forsaken Inn and southwest of Weathertop.
Old Mugwort has asked you to take a special draught he brewed to the goblin camps in the northeast and introduce it into their food supply. The draught is supposed to have properties that Mugwort thinks will encourage the goblins to abandon the Lone-lands.

Old Mugwort awaits your return at the Forsaken Inn.
You added the contents of Mugwort's draught to the food barrels found at the goblin encampments northeast of the Forsaken Inn. Mugwort will want to know of your success.
Collected Boar Meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We're not the wealthiest sort here, friend. We barely make our lives comfortable, and the goblins overrunning the eastward stretch of road have turned our inn into a lonelier place than ever. If you've time to offer, there's work to be done!
'Our fortune is about to change, though -- I've devised a way to make the road safe! Kill the goblin at the top, and the rest will turn aside!
'I need some help making this work. If you're willing, head east or northeast into the brush and get me some boar meat. Long tusks or no tusk... it doesn't matter. Just enough meat to make a meal for a warg or two! What's wrong? Boars are deadly creatures when angry, and their meat will serve my purposes nicely. Don't you want to end the threat of goblins and wargs? Then get out there and hunt some boars! No excuses! We'll be killing two boars with one stone! Ha ha ha!'

'This one is a bit tough and this one a bit tender. Hmm... no matter, they'll all go into the grinder nonetheless! A pinch of sickle-fly eyes, a dollop of gooey crawler flesh. Really tasty things, crawlers.
'This will take me a while, I'm afraid.'

'Get out there and get that boar meat. I can't make something that the wargs will eat without the proper supplies. Without the food, the wargs will keep attacking travellers. Without travellers the inn is barren, and I make no money to send back to my Gammer! So hurry, you fool! It'll be boars, and boars, and boars... and that will mean fewer goblins and fewer wargs!'
Bring boar-meat to Old Mugwort
Collect Boar Meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Fitting Meal
Passage through the Lone-lands has become difficult with the arrival of goblins. Worse still are their pets, the fearsome wargs who roam the plains and attack unwary travellers.
'I have a plan to get rid of the goblins and the wargs!'
'Boars! Boars! Boars! Always with the boars!'

Boars can be found throughout Annunlos and among the Weather Hills, northeast of the Forsaken Inn.
Old Mugwort believes he has come up with a way to drive goblins and wargs from the Lone-lands, but he needs you to collect boar meat first.
Defeated Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It's going to take awhile before the special meal I am preparing will be ready. What should I have you do in the meantime? Hmmm...
'Ah, I have it! Wargs are mean-tempered sort of beast, and they're smarter than your everyday wolf... stronger too. That means that they can get angry, and if they can get angry, they can make mistakes!
'The logic of that all works out, I'm sure of it! Now, you listen well: go east! Go to the far side of Nain Enidh and search the wilderlands off the road near Ost Cyrn for wargs; slay all those you find! Let's get them good and angry, and their leader is sure to come forth, hungry to taste some flesh!'

'So you defeated a goodly number of wargs? You've a hand for this, that much is certain!
'I finished my cooking too, I think. Maybe not quite yet, but I'm sure this will draw out their leader, or leaders, and then...
'Then you'll slay them and make the road safe for travellers, that's what, and we'll have more guests here at the inn!'

'I do hate wargs. I'm glad you've sent the wargs of Nain Enidh my message!'
'We'll soon have more travellers at the inn, I'm sure of it!'

'I am pleased to make your acquaintance, ${PLAYER}. The Fields of Fornost make for an unforgiving library, but that is where the history is to be found. It has always been so. Rarely can you get to the root of the matter from the comfort of your own fire.
'In days past, I journeyed among the Fasach-larran and Fasach-falroid, the foothills of western Angmar, studying the history of the dwarves. I thought they might once have dwelled in that region, but my father disapproved, and I abandoned the idea. I had been tracing the development of a particular chant, the Chant of the Stalwart.
'Reconstructing the chant from any evidence you find in the land of Angmar would prove to me that you have the makings of a master scholar, ${PLAYER}. I give to you my notes on the chant and wish you success in this endeavour. Return with the completed chant, and I will recognize you a peerless scholar.'

'Very well done, ${PLAYER}! It seems the manuscript you found was left by travellers and does not indicate a permanent settlement, but even that is a discovery of much value to those of us interested in such things. It takes a great deal of skill to reconstruct a chant of such complexity from mere fragments, but you have done so with great success. I am delighted at your ability.
'I recognize your mastery of the scholarly arts, ${PLAYER}.'

'You may be able to help me with something, ${PLAYER}. By the advice of Mithrandir, Master Elrond agreed to send several books detailing the histories of the Free Peoples from the library of Imladris to the towns of Men in the Bree-land, to inspire among the people there a sense of unity against the darkness. In this way, Mithrandir argued, free folk would have access to lore of the various peoples and could better understand their neighbours. A waggon-driver of good character, Harry Wheelwright, was chosen to bear the books on their journey into Bree-land and back to Imladris after some time was given for their circulation.
'It would seem that though Master Elrond's faith in the driver was not misplaced, the team of horses selected to pull the waggon was not of similar quality. On the return journey to Imladris, the horses were crazed by the scent of some beast, and the waggon was pulled off the road. Much to our disappointment and Harry's shame, the books were lost. If you would speak to Harry and set about collecting the lost tomes, I would gratefully allow you access to the superior study of Imladris, the finest place that remains between the Sea and the Mountains for scholarly pursuits.
'You will find Harry at the stables of Imladris.'

'You're looking for the waggon-driver who lost those stacks of Deluros' books? That was me. Feel awful about it, too. My team was made up of good horses, but they're still just animals. You can't expect them to face up to spiders...and the horrible ones that creep about the Lone-lands aren't your ordinary breed of spider, either. I'm missing four stacks of books. If you search south of the road that passes through that forsaken land, you might be able to recover them.
'The last I saw, the waggon was headed south off the road through the Lone-lands, towards the southern bog, shedding books as it barrelled into the wilderness. It was all I could do to struggle my way back here. If you could find those stacks of books and return them to Deluros, I'd appreciate it.'

'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. Your diligence and good heart are a cause of great amazement to me! I am grateful that you have recovered what was lost, and am glad to allow you access to the superior studies of Imladris. You will find they contain greater resources and finer materials than you are accustomed to use.
'You have preserved not just the books of Lord Elrond, but the chance as well for all the peoples of Middle-earth to benefit from the knowledge stored within their pages, and that is no small thing.'

'I do not know all the details of where the books were lost. Harry Wheelwright, the waggon-driver and my good friend, is currently staying here in Imladris and will be able to tell you more.
'Look for him by the stables. He seems at times to be more at home with horses than with the Eldar.'
Return the four stacks of books to Deluros
Lost Lore of the Free Peoples

'Speak with Harry Wheelwright, the waggon-driver. I am sure he will be able to help you recover the books that were lost.
'He is despairing over his loss of the tomes, though he is at no fault that I can see, and I know he will be cheered to learn that you will seek them.
'You will find Harry at the stables here in Imladris. He seems at times to be more comfortable in the presence of horses than in that of the Eldar.'
'You have recovered the books! Thank you, my friend, thank you! Take them to Deluros at once and bring to him my apologies once again, as well!'
'You have my earnest thanks for recovering the lost tomes, ${PLAYER}.'
'Knowledge is meant to be shared, certainly, but I do not know if each of the Free Peoples appreciate it.'
'I feel horribly about losing those books, but I'm glad you recovered them!'
'Deluros is a friend, of course, but at times he can be cold. So it is with Elves.'

'Once Master Deluros hears I was correct in my belief that pieces of pottery and other relics could become entangled in the root-like legs of the snow lurkers of the Misty Mountains, he is certain to give me more interesting assignments!
'Bring these relic fragments to him, ${PLAYER}, and tell him from whence you retrieved them! Perhaps he will send you back to me with an invitation to examine the most precious artifacts kept at Imladris. I cannot wait to study them with my own eyes!
'You will find Master Deluros within the library of Lord Elrond's house. He is always to be found there, deep in thought.'

'You retrieved these relic fragments from snow lurkers in the Misty Mountains? That is very interesting, ${PLAYER}, and Glorenglir is to be commended for thinking it possible -- in one blow, the mountain passes are made safer for those who must travel them, and we collect pieces of our history for further study. Worthy accomplishments.
'And yet, I would ask you one question -- did Glorenglir examine these fragments before she sent you to me? I thought not. This has always been her main fault, and it is the reason I refuse to allow her access to the most interesting artifacts kept here.
'Glorenglir is more concerned with boasting of her finds, with celebrating her accomplishments, than with examining the pieces she has uncovered. Until she learns to contemplate and appreciate the history of the pieces, she will never become a true scholar.'
Bring relic fragments to Deluros
Deluros of Rivendell
Glorenglir believed that snow lurkers could be used to unearth fragments of history from the snows of the Misty Mountains, and you have proven her correct.

'Master Deluros is a scholar and jeweller of great skill. Look for him in the library of Master Elrond's House and show him the relic fragments you retrieved from the snow lurkers.
'I eagerly await what he has to say!'
'I cannot wait to hear that Master Deluros will allow me to see the truly interesting artifacts!'
'Thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}! It will only be a little while until I am a master scholar!'
'A true scholar takes her time to appreciate the beauty and history of an item.'
'You cannot hurry understanding. Sometimes it never comes at all.'

'Glorenglir has not understood the significance of these fragments, ${PLAYER}, but I do. These are shards from what must once have been a beautiful vase, crafted long ago by some lord of the Eldar.
'If you can retrieve more fragments of this vase, it might be possible to reassemble it. Its former glory might have been lost to carelessness or necessity, but history leaves us with one certainty -- though broken, something once fair can be made beautiful again through care and good will.
'Return to the source of the Bruinen and search the drifts there for more fragments. The remaining pieces are sure to be most jagged. Whether you dig them out of the drifts yourself or rely on Glorenglir's snow lurkers, I leave to you. Be warned, however, that the chance of finding the remaining fragments will likely be quite low.'

'While you were away, ${PLAYER}, I was able to partially reassemble the vase. It is a thing of beauty, even incomplete! I wonder at its maker, and the circumstances that brought it to lie abandoned in pieces beneath the snow of the mountains.
'I see you have brought some jagged fragments back with you! I will see if any of them belong to this vase.'

'If you can retrieve jagged relic fragments from the same area to which Glorenglir sent you, I may be able to reassemble this ancient vase.
'You may find these jagged fragments on snow lurkers, as you did before, but I do not have as much confidence in this as Glorenglir does. Rather, I would have you search the snowdrifts near the source of the Bruinen, north of Rivendell in the Misty Mountains, to find these fragments.'

'We have been very fortunate, ${PLAYER}, for some of those fragments were indeed once part of this vase. I have repaired it as best I can, and the beauty it once had has returned in some measure!
'I have another task for you, ${PLAYER}. There are tables throughout Rivendell on which pieces of art and history are sometimes placed for contemplation. Bring this vase to a table near Glorenglir. If she recognizes it as being the sum of the fragments you earlier uncovered for her, I shall agree to further her instruction as a scholar and give her leave to study some of the more valuable artifacts kept here at Imladris.
'If she does not recognize the vase, she will have received my final lesson. Place the vase on the table, observe her reactions, then return to me, and we will speak further.'

'It does not surprise me that Glorenglir failed to recognize the vase, ${PLAYER}, even though she had some part in restoring it.
'I thank you for your assistance, and I hope the lesson of Glorenglir will stay with you! Be not so eager to advance that you fail to experience the moment, ${PLAYER}, in life and in all things.'

'In Imladris you can learn much of the past, ${PLAYER}, but true knowledge seems always just out of reach. Long has Master Deluros guided my instruction in the ways of the scholar, but still he insists I am not ready to study the most treasured artifacts kept here by Master Elrond.
'If you wish to share in the trivial duties my master assigns to me, I would welcome the aid. I am to collect fragments of old relics that have become buried by the snows around the source of Loudwater, north of Rivendell in the Misty Mountains.
'Do not dig around in the snow, friend! The snow lurkers will perform the task for you; as they climb among the drifts, fragments of old relics often get tangled in their long, root-like legs. Snow Lurkers will attack you on sight, so defend yourself from the creatures and look for relic fragments they have unwittingly unearthed.'

'You actually found relic fragments on the snow lurkers? I can hardly believe it, ${PLAYER}!
'I suspected that such fragments would become entangled in the legs of the Snow Lurkers, but I had never observed that behaviour myself. My musings have been proven true by your efforts!
'I am pleased as well that you collected these old fragments, but there is no shortage of those in Imladris, and I am more excited that my musings were correct! I thank you, ${PLAYER}!'
'You do not have the relic fragments for me, ${PLAYER}? The Snow Lurkers did not unknowingly unearth them for you?'

'You have begun to learn the discipline all jewellers must possess, ${PLAYER}, but you are like the stone that has not yet been shapen. There is potential in it, but it is rough and unpolished. Still, one must not be deceived by first impressions!

'I am glad you have come to see me, ${PLAYER}. Sometimes the study of the past blinds us to the present, and we forsake our obligations! Consider Henglas, a scholar much like yourself, who borrowed some of my materials and failed to return them! He was composing a song about what became of Aiglos after the Battle of the Last Alliance, but he has returned neither the stanzas I lent him nor the finished verse!
'I taught him much about years gone by, but of common courtesy he seems to have understood nothing. I did not give him those materials so he could carelessly abandon them at the first sign of trouble.
'Your arrival here seems quite fortunate, ${PLAYER}, for piecing together the story of Aiglos will be good practice for an earnest young scholar. Retrieve my lost stanzas and use them to compose the ballad my other student could not. I will give you a recipe for composing the ballad, as well as my notes on where to obtain the sources you will need to consult.'

'You have done an excellent job of weaving the story of Aiglos, ${PLAYER}. Gil-galad owed much to the spear he carried, and indeed none could stand against him while he wielded it.
'And yet, even its mighty power could not protect the great lord who carried it from meeting his fate. For it was not to be Gil-galad at the last, Gil-galad so fair and mighty, who would stand against the Enemy of that dark age.
'But the wind brings with it a chill, and I would not tell that story this day. I am pleased at your understanding of history and your technique of composition, ${PLAYER}. You must continue your studies, with my good favour.'

'You have come to me because you think you have mastered the art of the jeweller, but I tell you that you have not done so. Until you respect your craft, until you fear it, you have mastered nothing. Never forget that the fruit of our labour stirs greed in lesser hearts. We jewellers may not be forging swords or daggers or arrows, ${PLAYER}, but we are forging weapons nonetheless.
'I have learned that a band of Men from the South have foolishly chosen to venture into Ram Dúath in search of treasure. One of these Men carried a Gondorian sapphire and goaded his fellows into the journey with the promise of more gems like it. I expect Ram Dúath has become his grave. If that is the case -- and you can wrest the sapphire from the Orcs that now surely possess it -- it would make an excellent adornment for a memorium ring. Craft me this ring, and I will judge its worth.'

'It will do. You have a good understanding of the technique, and I hope the circumstances in which you obtained the sapphire have taught you something of our art. 'You performed so wonderfully in the acquisition of these relics that I think it only fair that you have the job of delivering them!
'My employer awaits the delivery of these relics -- his name is Ollie Redbrush, and you will find him in the armour and weapons shop east of Bree Town Hall. I have placed all the relics in a sack to make the carrying of them easier.
'If you make this delivery, I am sure that Ollie will give you my payment and send you back to me. Upon your return, I will give you a courier's fair wage.'

'These artifacts are hardly worth a courier's fee. Falster thinks me a fool if he believes I will pay him his full fee for a handful of useless cups and flagons. Trying to make me more accepting of his inadequacies by throwing in a handful of wolf-teeth is maddening!
'Take this. He'll find that it is significantly lighter than he wanted, but it is what he deserves for such a poor collection.
'Make your way quickly, ${RACE}. I want that good-for-nothing trickster to know that Ollie Redbrush is no fool!'
'I have no business to conduct with you, and you're doing nothing more than cluttering the space around my home. Make yourself useful or scarce. It is your choice.'

'Ungrateful! Redbrush has some gall trying to push me around. You made the delivery, but his message to me is that it is not enough. Does he not realize that the fortunes of trade change?
'I'll not forsake you as he has me. Here is your payment. I wish there was more that I could give, but he's made this difficult for me.'
'Didn't Redbrush give you the payment for the goods we brought him?'
Deliver the sack of goods to Ollie Redbrush
Deliver the coinpurse to Falster the Fox
Falster's Delivery
Falster was pleased with your efforts on his behalf, and now wants the items you collected brought to Ollie Redbrush.

'Are you looking for more hand-outs? I've nothing more to give a courier who delivers me useless relics and wolf-teeth. Take the coinpurse to Falster with my disappointment... and bother me no longer.'
'Redbrush will be anxious to see what we've done, and I am anxious to pay you, friend! Look for him in the armour and weapons shop east of Bree Town Hall!'
'Thanks again for your help, ${PLAYER}.'
'I cannot believe that Redbrush paid me so poorly!'
'I'll find some way to get by, with or without Ollie Redbrush!'
'Ollie Redbrush is no fool, I'll tell you that!'
'I am finished dealing with Falster. He is a villain!'

'I make my living trading with the patrons of the Forsaken Inn. Or rather, I used to, until the goblins arrived! Their presence strikes fear into our suppliers and has made trade impossible. Sadly, that doesn't remove my obligation to Ollie Redbrush, my employer in Bree-town!
'A vale beneath the ruins of Minas Eriol, southeast of the Forsaken Inn, contains the coins and heirlooms I need, and more! Wolves inhabit the valley, and Ollie may forgive me the delay if I include some pristine wolf-teeth with the shipment.
'If you assist me in collecting these curiosities, I will ensure that you are paid for the favour! Make your way to the valley beneath Minas Eriol and obtain coins, heirlooms and wolf-teeth for me.'

'Ollie will be pleased with these curiosities, for certain, and the wolf-teeth should help sweeten the deal. I must admit I was not certain that you would succeed! The arrival of the goblins has done much to change the nature of our work here in the Lone-lands.
'You have earned this reward, friend, and I hope you find this sufficient. I know that Redbrush will be pleased with this delivery.'
'Head to the valley beneath the ruins of Minas Eriol, southeast of here. I need some coins and heirlooms to send to Ollie Redbrush. A few wolf-teeth wouldn't hurt either.'

Falster the Fox, a denizen of The Forsaken Inn, needs assistance acquiring certain curiosities for Ollie Redbrush of Bree.
'Thank you for your help. These days, I need all the assistance I can get!'
'I've had enough of goblins. Someone needs to do something.'

'One moment, friend. I've been thinking of ways to help meet my ends, and I may have found one. I'll need some help if this is to work, however, and that's where you come in!
'The constables in Bree have placed a bounty on goblin-scabbards. I have contacts that will deliver the scabbards and collect the money, but no one seems willing to actually gather the scabbards! Surely the goblins in the ruins of Minas Eriol, southeast of here, carry scabbards that will fulfill the bounty.
'If you collect some of their scabbards and deliver them to me, I will gladly share the profits with you.'

'You have brought a number of goblin-scabbards to me, friend? Very good! I am a man of honour, and will pay my debt as I promised! These will fetch a good bounty from the constables. Take these coins with my thanks!
'Use caution if you intend to travel further into the Lone-lands. Danger lurks here at every turn.'
'I'll need a goodly number of scabbards, so hunt the goblins of Minas Eriol, to the south. You will find there plenty of the creatures, I reckon.'
Bring goblin-scabbards to Falster the Fox

'We could make a tidy profit from goblin-hunting, I reckon!'
'Goblins are filthy creatures, and a danger to travellers through remote places.'

Goblins can be found in the ruins of Minas Eriol, southeast of the Forsaken Inn.
Falster wants to collect the bounty on scabbards carried by goblins in the Lone-lands.

'I have need of an adventurer, ${PLAYER}, and it may be that you will serve nicely. The hobbit Frodo Baggins is here at Rivendell for a time, and he will soon be leaving on an errand both urgent and secret.
'Hobbits are remarkable creatures, and Frodo is more remarkable than most -- he has stepped forwards to accept a charge that would daunt even those counted most brave in all the annals of the world.
'Ask me not about his task! And do not ask Frodo, either. He may wish to speak of it, but it is better that he not do so. I do ask you this: speak with him and gauge his feelings. Much depends on his courage and good hobbit-sense, but I am loathe to send him into danger if he is not prepared for what he may face. Speak with Frodo, tell him of your adventures, and return to me with your thoughts on his mood.'

'It is a pleasure to meet you, ${PLAYER}. You are a friend of Gandalf? Yes, he is very mysterious.
'I am sorry, I'm not entirely myself today. There are a lot of things on my mind, you might say. This is a place of peace, and I know that Bilbo is very happy spending his days riddling in the Hall of Fire, but...it just feels like I am so far from home.
'Would you like to take a walk with me? The cool air will do me good, and I would very much like to hear about your adventures. Let me know.'

'Frodo remains as high in my esteem as ever he did, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for accompanying him. He is made of stern stuff, our Frodo, and his worries are natural. They will give him strength in hard times, rather than bring him to weakness. Frodo will be fine.
'I thank you, ${PLAYER}. May your travels bring you out of danger quickly if they chance to bring you into it!'
Talk to Frodo
Frodo's Burden
Gandalf the Grey is concerned for his hobbit-friend Frodo Baggins, who has agreed to undertake a dangerous task of great secrecy.
'Thank you for the walk, ${PLAYER}. I am sorry that I gave you no peace! You can tell me about your adventures another time...and perhaps then I can tell you about mine.'
'A walk will do me good, I think. Are you ready to go? Rivendell is a beautiful place, and I have very much enjoyed walking its paths.'

'You will find Frodo outside the Last Homely House, taking the air, no doubt. Speak with him and gauge his mood. Much depends on his good hobbit-sense, and I would not send him into danger unprepared for what he may face.'
'Frodo is a most remarkable hobbit. He will be fine.'
'Adventurers are a curious sort. As curious as Wizards, if you ask most hobbits!'
'Hello, ${PLAYER}! I hope you are well!'
'Rivendell is a beautiful place. I do miss the Shire, though.'

'Thank you again for the walk, ${PLAYER}. Maybe things are not quite so grim after all.'

'Hello there, friend. I was just thinking of all the things I've got to do and me here on duty.
'I've got my brother's armour to get polished. He'd do it himself, if he had a mind to, but I'm afraid Kalli does not have our family's sense of duty. He'll never earn his commander's respect; always being late, never diligent in his duties, always wearing his old, worn armour and filthy uniform.
'Perhaps you could be of some service to an old warrior? Could you bring this armour up to Brúni Stonehelm and have him polish it for me? Brúni's stands among the smiths in the western chamber of Thorin's Hall, where the canal runs through the mountain.'

'Brúni's got someone else to do his errands for him again, eh? Very well, here's my other armour. You might want to check with Olafr, too. His armour was torn up bad a few days back in a scuffle with some goblins.'

'I've been waiting for Brúni to come down. We expected him the other day, but as usual, he put us off again! I've got a dent in my armour a hand and a half long. Poxy goblin would have cut me from shoulder to belly if not for that hunk of metal!'

'What's this? I know that armour! That's Halli's, unless I miss my guess. I haven't the time to polish his armour again. I'm far too busy!
'I was supposed to go down to Noglond, the way-station to the south, and pick up the guards' damaged armour. No, I have no time to clean Halli's armour today. You will just have to leave it here, and I will see if I can get to it before next week. Unless...you can go down to Noglond and retrieve the guards' armour for me.'
'I'll never have time to polish Halli's armour if I have to travel to Noglond and back again.'

'There you are. What's taken you so long? Let me see these...Thorin's beard! Have they been wrestling oliphaunts? I could forge two suits of armour in the time it will take me to hammer this out.'
The dwarf-smith looks up at you. 'Oh yes, here is the armour you wanted shined.'
'That armour's not going to drag itself up through Thrain's Vale! The Watch in Noglond, the way-station, expects that armour to be picked up today.'
'Aye, that's just the thing. Kalli will look sharp as an axe in this. The commander's sure to notice him now!'
'Have you gotten Brúni to polish Kalli's armour? No, well what are you doing here, then?'

Halli has asked you to help him improve his brother's reputation in the guard by having his tarnished armour polished.
'I don't blame Brúni for not coming out of his nice warm forge up at Thorin's Halls. That's where I'd stay if I were him, not trapessing out here in the cold.'
'That's a handsome suit of armour, but it's not mine. If you're still running errands for Brúni, you'll want to ask him who that armour belongs to.'
'Have you not brought the armour to Brúni yet? Please, he's in the western hall, and Kalli will need his armour shined bright to impress the commander!'
'Have you not brought the armour to Brúni yet? Please he's in the western hall with the other smiths, and Kalli will need his armour shined bright to impress the commander!'
'Have you not brought the armour to Brúni yet? Please he's in the forge, and Kalli will need his armour shined bright to impress the commander!'
'Be sure to tell Brúni to replace that strap on the left side of my armour. He should have plenty of time up there at the forge.'

'I'd be surprised if Durin himself could fix my armour up nice as the set you've got there. You must have me mixed up with someone else. Check with Brúni at the forge to see who that armour belongs to.'
'The Noglond guards have got more damaged armour than that, and it's not going to drag itself up the mountain! If I have to go down there and get it I'll not be able to polish Halli's armour.'
'Halli's going to want his armour back right away. Best you take it to him now. He's usually on duty down by the gate to the courtyard.'

Brúni Stonehelm can be found among the smiths in the western hall of Thorin's Hall, where the canal runs through the mountain.

'I've got some complaints from Noglond, down in the Vale of Thráin to the south, that the canal hasn't been flowing the way it should. Hopefully that repair you made to the leak has solved that problem, as well.
'Could you go down to Noglond and talk to Geitir about the problem? He can tell you if the canal is back to normal. Just follow the road south as it curves through the Vale of Thráin, and you will eventually come upon Noglond.
'With the Dourhands stirring up trouble, we are so short on workhands.'
'Has the waterflow been restored? I should say not. It's just a trickle, really, when it should be a torrent!'
The Flow to Noglond
Tindr hopes the repairs to the canal in Thorin's Hall has restored the flow of water to Noglond, the way-station in the Vale of Thráin.
'Have you not been to Noglond yet?'

Geitir is in Noglond, south on the road from Thorin's Halls.
Tindr has asked you to speak with Geitir in Noglond to learn if the flow of water in the canal has returned to normal.

'This canal water is used down in Gondamon in the Low-lands as well as here in the Vale of Thráin. You should go down there and make sure they know we removed the blockage up here.
'Travel down the road to the east, then turn south at the first crossing and Gondamon will be right there. You will want to talk to old Otkell.
'Their cisterns must be nearly dry down there, what with the blockage as bad as it was!'
'You restored the waterflow? Why it's not flowing nearly enough at all! You may have cleared out some problems over at Noglond, but there must be something else blocking the flow around here.'
On to Gondamon
With the thickets removed from the canal, the waterflow has been restored to Noglond in the Vale of Thráin.
'Gondamon is easy to find. Just take the road east, then turn south at the first crossing.'

Otkell is in Gondamon, east down the road from Noglond, and south at the first crossing.
Geitir has asked you to inform Otkell in Gondamon about the restoration of the canal.
There are thickets clogging the canal
Thickets cleared away (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The water has not been flowing down to Noglond for several days. I sent a message back to the Halls, but I've not received a reply from the builders. I'm not about to send one of my boys to do builder's work, and I can't have them traipsing to the river everytime we need water.
'Would you look into it? The canal runs all the way down the mountain from Thorin's Halls and to Gondamon below. The problem must be up-river from here.
'The above-ground part of the canal, the place that may be blocked, is south and west of here. Just take the road south to the bridge and look underneath it. Follow the canal all the way up to the big gate if you have to, just find the problem!'

'Done already? Good work! We could use someone like you on the guard...better than these layabouts. Can I interest you in signing up? Oh, the pay's not that good, and you'll find yourself in some cold, out-of-the-way post like this, but it's a living. No? I thought not....
'Ah well, thanks for your work, anyway.'
Discover the source of the canal's waterflow problem
Clear away the thickets clogging the canal (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Quenching a Thirst
According to Geitir, the waterflow from the canal has been staunched for several days, and the builders have not replied to his message requesting assistance.
'Have you found the source of the problem?'
'Aye, it would be a great help if you would clear away the thickets clogging the canal.'

The canal can be found south of Noglond, flowing down from Thorin's Halls.
Geitir asks you to investigate the flow of the canal to Noglond and learn the cause of the problem.

There are thickets blocking the canal between Noglond and Thorin's Halls.
Now that you have discovered the problem in the canal, you should clear away enough of the thickets to allow the water to flow more freely. There may be several patches of thickets along the canal.

Geitir is at Noglond to the north of the canal, south of Thorin's Halls.
You should return to Geitir with news of your success.

'The goblins in these hills are causing us no end of grief. They've blocked off the river with debris and slowed the flow to a trickle, and what water exists is fouled by their presence.
'I can send a crew to remove the debris, but I need someone with a stout heart and a strong sword-arm to clear out some of the goblins. I can't afford to lose any workers, what with the Dourhands to contend with.
'You can find the canal west of here, just past the hills. The goblins have a camp west of their make-shift dam.'
'Is it safe for my work crews? Excellent. I wouldn't send my lads out with all those goblins around. We need all the guards here to protect us from the cursed Dourhands in case they attack.'
Clear the Way
The water supply coming into Gondamon is still interrupted, despite your efforts to clear the canal.
'No luck with the goblins? Well keep at it. My crew can clear away the blockage just as soon as your part is done. The goblin camp is west of here.'

The canal near Gondamon is to the west, past the hills.
Otkell, the Chief Builder of Gondamon, informed you that goblins are responsible for the lack of fresh water. He asked you to go to the area west of the canal and remove the goblin threat.

Otkell is at Gondamon to the east of the canal, beyond the hills.
You should return to Otkell and tell him about the goblins you defeated.

'Hurry! Take the mortar and make the repairs before the fissures expand. It's only a matter of time before the wall is breached.'
'That's one less task to concern me. Perhaps that will fix the problems with the water supply they've been reporting down at Noglond, the way-station in the Vale.'
Seal the fissure with Tindr's mortar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Enter Thorin's Hall to the north, then go west to the Hall of Merchants.
Tindr gave you some mortar with which to repair the cracks in the canal walls.

'I am Tindr, Master Builder of Thorin's Hall. The great canal, for which I am responsible, has recently fissured. The crack has not yet become a serious threat, but it is only a matter of time, and I haven't any builders available to assist with its repairs. Could you help me seal the fissure?
'I need to mix a mortar to seal the crack but our stores are barren. I will need stone and gypsum from the old Mirkstone Tunnels and sand from the Rockbelly Pit. The Mirkstone Tunnels are above the great statue of Thorin to the north-west. The Rockbelly Pit is to the south-east in the Winterheight.
'If we do not seal the crack soon, it may break, flooding the Vale of Thráin below.'

'It will just take me a moment to make the mortar. You learn a few tricks when you've done this as long as I have.
'There we are! Now take this mortar to the fissures in the canal walls in the Hall of Merchants inside the western parts of Thorin's Hall.'
'Where are the materials I asked you to gather?'

'The wildcats that roam the hills in Thrain's Vale have become bold with hunger in recent months. There have even been reports of them attacking unwary travellers! I have the unwelcome task to deal with these beasts, but there are too many for me to handle alone.
'Grimkell has ordered me to deal with the problem, but I could use your help. We must teach the beasts to fear the bite of metal again and keep to four-legged game.'
'Good work with those vicious cats. Perhaps now lone travellers will have less to fear in this land. Grimkell will be pleased, for a change.'

'The hunters who've been plying the forests north of Gondamon have come to me with stories of being threatened or even attacked by those backstabbing Dourhand brigands.
'If you're of a mind to lend us a hand, you could head out there and deal with the treacherous thin-beards! They need to learn not to meddle with the hunters of Gondamon!
'The Dourhands have built a small camp to the north of here, in the hills somewhere. You'll find plenty of heads to break there, I'll warrant.'

'Ah good. That should teach the Dourhands a little lesson. You have done us a fair favour, ${PLAYER}, and helped ensure that Gondamon remains secure over the coming winter months.
'Let me see if I can find some suitable reward for you.'
Protecting the Hunt
Since the Dourhands were driven out of Thorin's Halls, they have harried the hunters of the Blue Mountain Dwarves.
'You should be able to find those brigands in a camp in the hills to the north. They mostly stay holed up in there like rats in their warren.'
'Ha! You showed those Dourhands what we're made of!'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! I doubt those Dourhands will trouble our hunters anymore.'

The Dourhand brigands can be found to the north of Gondamon.

'The wind coming down from the mountains makes my bones ache year-round, but even the younger sentries feel the chill when the days grow short.
'We could use more pelts to make blankets and clothing in preparation for the coming winter. There is no shortage of wolves prowling in the wilds, especially to the west. I expect you'll have no difficulty obtaining some furs for me.
'Wolves are vile creatures, but at least their fur is warm.'
'The Dwarves of Gondamon will be grateful for these pelts when winter arrives, ${PLAYER}. Thank you.'
'A cold dwarf is a grumpy dwarf, ${PLAYER}. Have you had any luck getting those pelts for us?'

Collect wolf-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our huntsmen are skilled, but this year's hunt has proven particularly difficult, what with the cold and the wretched Dourhands. I have found myself short of stocks for the coming winter.
'You can help us by bringing in some bear meat. There are plenty of bears in the wilds around Gondamon, especially to the north.
'We'll preserve and store the meat for the coming months.'
'Thank you for bringing in this bear meat! I'll see that it's properly salted and stored for the winter months.'
'We still have need of that bear meat, ${PLAYER}. You ought to be able to find some in the wilds surrounding Gondamon.'

Collected stolen dwarf-gold ingot
Collected Ancient Dwarf-chest

'I see...so you were sent by a dwarf from the Blue Mountains, did you? Perhaps it is the long years alone here, but I believe you. Now, allow me to tell you a tale.
'Long ago, the first Halmur Stoneshaper, son of Vithurr, was charged with guarding the treasures here. He stood sentry day and night, maintaining his post even on days of feasting. Yet, he let his guard drop but once, and a vile dwarf, Hjortur Dourhand, slipped in and stole a single ingot of dwarf-gold. Having failed in his duty, Halmur swore that he and his sons would keep vigil over the remaining gold until that ingot was returned. I am but one in a long line of Halmurs who have kept his oath.
'If you return the stolen ingot, the oath will be fulfilled. The strongbox will then be yours to return to the dwarf who sent you. I cannot say, though, where to find Hjortur, although the legends of Halmur's failure tells that Hjortur fled with his gold to Orod Laden. Perhaps there you will be able to find the gold.'

'Ha! You've come from one of those fool Stoneshapers, haven't you? You've heard the tale of their \qoath\q over that strongbox, haven't you? Well, allow me to tell you a tale!
'The first Hjortur Dourhand stole the gold not for his own treasure, but to make Halmur Stoneshaper look the fool! Upon hearing of Halmur's oath, Hjortur swore one of his own: he and his sons would forever keep the ingot and forever keep the Stoneshapers looking the fool!
'I too come from a long line...a long line of Hjortur Dourhands! And I shall keep the oath! You shall only have the ingot if you can take the strongbox from my dead body. And I don't think that's too likely....'

'My eyes must betray me, you ${RACE}, you trickster. You cannot have the stolen ingot that has kept me and my kin chained to this place for the long years.
'And yet, it is...it is! Can it be so? Has my duty at last been fulfilled?'
'You have not retrieved the stolen ingot, faithless ${RACE}. I maintain my vigil.'

'Good, good! I hope the strongbox wasn't too hard to find! Heikki Goldwatcher is sure to be pleased with this. Those records of his won't have a bad thing to say about me!
'Now, I know you've already done so much, but perhaps there is a bit more I could ask of you?'
'Have you found the other strongbox yet?'
Collect stolen dwarf-gold ingot
Find Hjortur Dourhand
Search Hjortur's strongbox for the stolen ingot

The Last Ingot
Halmur Stoneshaper, a descendant of the original Halmur Stoneshaper, son of Vithurr, has been charged with guarding the strongbox you seek until all its contents are returned.
'I know not where you might find the gold Hjortur stole, although the tale of Halmur's failure says Hjortur fled to Orod Laden. Perhaps you will find some clue to the stolen ingot there.'
'You defeated Hjortur, but did not search his strongbox? Return to Orod Laden at once and reclaim the stolen ingot from the strongbox he guarded!'
'The chest is yours, friend. My oath is fulfilled. I'm free now. Free to go where I please!'

The second strongbox is within the tomb of Halmur Stoneshaper in the pass of Gabilazan. Larus Sharpshard at Glóin's camp, north of Rivendell.
After helping Halmur Stoneshaper reclaim the stolen ingot and fulfil his family's oath, he has allowed you to take the strongbox to bring it to Larus Sharpshard.

'How could I have missed this? There was a second page to Heikki's records! It describes a second strongbox, ${PLAYER}! Heikki is not the kind of dwarf you want to cross, because he'll remember it -- he'll write it down in one of his books and never let you forget how you let him down! If I don't get that second strongbox, it wouldn't surprise me if someone found his records four hundred years from now and thought badly of Larus Sharpshard, son of Tralli!
'So we've got to find it, ${PLAYER}. Let me just look at this paper and tell you where it should be. Ah, the dwarf-keep among the High Crags, to the east and south. It's the keep that guards Gabilazan, and it's full of those good-for-nothing Dourhands.
'You might want to take the farthest east pass and then come at the keep from the south. Look for a building on a hill to your right as you approach the keep. The strongbox should be just inside, so don't delay!'

'Who dares to enter the tomb of Halmur Stoneshaper, son of Vithurr of old? Not even a Dourhand is foolish enough to enter here! They know the tale of the Stoneshapers and quake in fear! Yet you are different....
'You are here for the strongbox, aren't you, thieving ${RACE}? You've only moments to tell me your tale before I cleave you in twain!'
Collect the second strongbox
The Other Chest
Larus Sharpshard discovered that there was a second strongbox, which remains missing.

'The second strongbox will be inside a building on a hill to your right as you approach the Dourhand keep in the pass of Gabilazan from the south. Journey there and bring back this strongbox, ${PLAYER}!'

Larus Sharpshard believes the second strongbox is inside a building on the hill to your right as you approach the Dourhand-controlled keep in the pass of Gabilazan from the south. Gabilazan is east and south of Glóin's camp.
Larus Sharpshard is very worried that Heikki Goldwatcher will record unflattering things about him if you are not able to recover a second dwarf-strongbox from the Misty Mountains.

'Those despicable goblins must have stolen some of the dwarf-gold ingots from this strongbox, ${PLAYER}! According to the records given me by Heikki Goldwatcher, the strongbox is missing twenty-four ingots!
'This is unforgiveable! To think that the gold of his ancestors has been pilfered by goblins is more than any dwarf could bear.
'The goblins have camps in the mountains somewhere to the north and east, ${PLAYER}. Find the creatures and slay them until you recover the missing ingots! Look especially on the ridges of Pinnath Fenui, east of the source of the Bruinen, for I have heard that many goblin-fires have been spotted that way.'

'Perfect, ${PLAYER}, perfect! This should do it! Now all of the ingots are accounted for, and Heikki Goldwatcher will be happy to know that we have recovered the treasure mentioned in his records.
'Yes, according to Heikki's records we've got everything...needed....
'Oh no, what's this?'

'Those goblins will be made to pay, ${PLAYER}. Look for their camps east of the source of the Bruinen, and recover all of the stolen dwarf-gold ingots from their filthy fingers.'

Goblins carrying dwarf-gold ingots can likely be found on the Pinnath Fenui, the ridges east of the source of the Bruinen, in the Misty Mountains.

Collected Damaged Dwarf-chest

'Hail and well-met, ${PLAYER}! Lord Glóin has established this camp so that we may keep an eye on the threat of goblins -- and worse -- that stirs within the Mountains. An admirable aim! The Misty Mountains were once studded with great dwarf-keeps and towers, and nothing moved over snow or under stone of which we were not aware!
'Great treasures, too, were kept in the stony fastness of those keeps. Indeed, Heikki Goldwatcher of Thorin's Hall has ordered me to retrieve a strongbox mentioned in his records.
'If you travel to the old dwarf-keep that overlooks the source of the Bruinen, north of here, and retrieve this strongbox, I will reward you for your trouble.'

'I am pleased to see you found the box, and Heikki Goldwatcher will be as well! It appears to be damaged, and not by the passage of time, I think. These marks might have been caused by goblin-weapons. Perhaps a party of goblins sought to carry the strongbox away and quarrelled among themselves?
'Why then did the victors not take the strongbox, I wonder? Ah, no matter. At least it still remains, ${PLAYER}?
'I'll just open it up and compare the contents with the record that Heikki gave to me before I set out.'

'The Bruinen flows out of the mountains to the north, and an old dwarf-keep can be found overlooking the water. Search the area for signs of the strongbox Heikki Goldwatcher told me about, and I will reward you for your trouble.'
Bring damaged dwarf-chest to Larus Sharpshard
Old Treasures
The Misty Mountains are dotted with dwarf-ruins, and Larus Sharpshard is eager to reclaim some of the treasures that may still remain in such stony places.

The strongbox is in the old dwarf-keep that overlooks the source of the Bruinen, north of Glóin's camp. Larus Sharpshard is at Glóin's camp, north of Rivendell.
Larus Sharpshard asked you to retrieve a strongbox from an old dwarf-keep.

'There's but one thing left to do, take the strongboxes to Heikki Goldwatcher in Thorin's Hall.
'I know it's a bit of a trek to go all the way there, but I think it's the proper thing to do. I wish I could do it myself, since it's my reputation that will be besmirched in Heikki's records if he's not happy, but I'm far too busy here to make such a journey.
'You'll find Heikki in Thorin's Hall in the Blue Mountains. Hopefully Hekki won't be too unhappy when you get there!'

'Finally, word from Larus Sharpshard. What, what's this? You've brought the strongboxes? That fool, did he even read my note to him? I wanted the name of Halmur Stoneshaper's father! I will make a note of this in my records!
'Wait, you met Halmur's descendant? Good, good! Did he tell you his father's name? Halmur? Oh, Vithurr was the first Halmur's father! Ah, very good! That is exactly what I wanted to know.
'I suppose I'll add the gold here to the treasury, although it really matters not to me. I honestly did not expect there to be any treasure left, after all these years. No, the name of Halmur Stoneshaper's father is really all I needed. Filling in the gap in the records is the real treasure!'
Bring the strongboxes to Heikki Goldwatcher

'Greetings! I wonder if you could lend me a hand? I've been trying to repair this device, which opens access to the old Vault of the Mountain, but some key pieces, ancient gears, were removed and scattered long ago to prevent the Dourhands getting their grubby hands on the vault treasure.
'Now that we've finally ousted the Dourhands from Thorin's Hall, it's time to open the Vault, but first this device must be repaired. Old Sindri Winchmaster, the artificer who made this, had skill far beyond mine, so I'll need the actual pieces that were lost to have any hope of getting it to work again.
'They say the first missing gear was hidden somewhere in an old cave in the Winterheight, up the path south-east from Thorin's Hall. You'll probably find it in a chest somewhere in the cave. There's a trick to the chest, by the way, you have to press in at the corners to open it....'

'Ha! This looks like the gear! It goes here...or maybe here....
'No matter. I'll work it out given time, I'm sure of it!'
'Please find the gear that is hidden in the abandoned mine west of here. It's in a chest somewhere in the cave. Beware of cave-claws!'

'I'm not sure exactly where you'll find the gear, but I would not be surprised if it was well-guarded, as the Dourhands know very well that it is essential for getting into the Vault.'

'Finally! It's working.... I think.
'I'm going to have to stay here to care for this machine. You go open the vault! It's quite a distance away -- on the other side of Thorin's Hall -- here, to the north and up the stairs. The chains and cables run all through the walls -- a real work of art!
'Make sure you get the order of the levers right, or you'll have to come back here so I can reset the gears. Perhaps those clues you found in the boxes will help with the order.'

'This was in the vault? This?
Bávor stares incredulously at the black rock. 'Amazing! Fantastic! Incredible!
'Listen, no one knew just what was sealed in that vault! This is one of the greatest of all the treasures of the Dwarves!
'Oh, I know it doesn't look like much, but the story goes that Durin himself hewed this from Gundabad, the mountain where he first awoke! It's the first chunk of ore ever mined by the father of our line! This is the most ancient artifact of the Dwarves and serves as a symbol of our heritage. You have unearthed a true treasure with all your hard work, and you deserve all our thanks.'
'Please don't tell me there was nothing in the vault!'

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}! I trust you have been practicing your woodworking? Good, good! I remember the days of effort I had to put in before I was able to make my first Twistwood Staff. They were long days, too!
'You haven't made a Twistwood Staff yet? Well, you'll need to be able to do that if you want to get any better, you know! I'll give you the recipe for making one, and I'll also write down my notes on the process -- just look at them, and you'll be able to make one in no time.
'Once you collect the components, use the recipe to guide your fashioning of the staff. Then return to me, and I'll examine your handiwork! Don't use or trade the Twistwood Staff until I have a chance to look at it, though -- if there's anything wrong with your work, I don't want other people thinking ill of you for it!'

'This Twistwood Staff is very finely made, ${PLAYER}! You are absolutely ready for more intricate projects! I am glad you were able to retrieve a twisted branch from that Harmon so you could make this staff.
'I can't believe Harmon thought my grove was magical! There is no magic in the wood, unless you count the magic of drinking deep from the rain and enjoying the feel of the soil beneath your roots! 'I will talk to you later, ${PLAYER}, and keep practicing!'
