'There is something you could do for me, if you insist on taking up my valuable time. Supervisor Beecher at Trestlebridge has sent word that he, too, has trouble retaining skilled labour, and the Trestlespan is in need of repair. I cannot afford to send any of my workers to aid him.
'You, however, are dispensable. Speak with Beecher in Trestlebridge and render him your assistance. If I hear from him that your work is satisfactory, I will speak with Erandir on your behalf. Ranger he may be, but he is still a friend and can grant you access to the superior workbenches of Esteldín.
'You will find Beecher north of here in Trestlebridge. I expect that he will be surveying the supports of the Trestlespan bridge.'

'Beecher was satisfied with your work? I see. Thank you for running this errand -- we have enough problems retaining labour here on the Bree-fields for me to send my workers to Trestlebridge, the very edge of danger. They would never return!
'I will send word to Erandir. When next you come to Esteldín, you will be permitted usage of the superior workbenches there.'

'Millicent has finally sent someone to aid me! Thank goodness! You'd think she would have realized that if Trestlebridge falls and the Trestlespan is taken by the Orcs, all of her work on the Bree-fields would be for naught.
'But no matter! You're here now, and for that I am grateful! Look up there -- do you see the gaps in the side of the bridge? Raiding parties of Orcs are sometimes able to send arrows whistling through those gaps, endangering the defenders. We need to cover up those gaps, my friend!
'The Trestlespan is old, and pieces of wood are sometimes wrenched free in the wind and fall into the river. Make your way down to the water's edge and collect some of the driftwood that catches up on the rocks. Bring it back to me, and we can repair some of the breaches in the Trestlespan!'

'Thank you for your work, ${PLAYER}! I'd like to see the Orcs try and shoot their arrows through the breaches you've patched up, my friend!
'I think we'll be fine here for now. If you see Millicent when you return to Thornley's Work-site, be sure to tell her how pleased I have been with your work!'

'I hope you didn't have too much trouble collecting these, ${PLAYER}. It is damp work, but necessary.
'I charge you now with repairing the breaches in the Trestlespan. Start at this end of the bridge and work your way through it, repairing the breaches as you come to them.
'Once you have repaired ten or so, return to me.'
'I am still waiting for you to return with the driftwood I tasked you with collecting from the river below, ${PLAYER}.'

You have safely escorted Lalia out of the Barrow-downs

'I came here to find \qThe Last Prince,\q like Mr. Butterbur talks about in his stories. I was going to find him, and then be with him forever and be his princess! But he wasn't here to be found! There's just all these skeletons and bones and walking dead! It isn't nice to go misleading young hobbits like that!
'When you are ready to go, could you help me get back home to Bree? I couldn't leave before, but now with a strong warrior like you here, I'm sure you can get me home safely!
'Oh, and I lost my cloak. I simply must find it or dad will yell at me something terrible!'

'Oh, that is a relief! It seems I know my daughter well. She actually had gone after that \qLast Prince\q of hers. Well, maybe she's learned her lesson and won't be so foolish in the future.
'Although knowing my daughter like I do, that doesn't seem to likely. I only hope I can survive her tweens. Maybe then she'll get some hobbit-sense. Maybe....'
Escort Lalia to safety
Bring Lalia's cloak to Bob
Lalia's Safe Passage

You've come across a very frightened Hobbit girl, Lalia, on the Barrow-downs. She's asked for your help in getting back to Bree and her father, Bob, who works for Barliman Butterbur at the Prancing Pony.
'Oh, do help my daughter get back to Bree safely!'
'Thank you for bringing my Lalia home!'
'I do wish Mr. Butterbur wouldn't tell stories like \qThe Last Prince.\q'

You must take Lalia to the north-gate of the Barrow-downs.
Lalia has asked you to help her get back to Bree safely. In addition, she has asked for your help finding the cloak she dropped somewhere on the Barrow-downs. You must protect her as she searches for her cloak, then leaves the Barrow-downs.

Bob can be found at The Prancing Pony in Bree.
You have helped Lalia make her way home, and as thanks she has given you her cloak. She has asked you to bring her cloak to her father, Bob, Barliman Butterbur's assistant, as proof that she is safe.
You have found Lalia

'Pardon me for asking, but have you seen my daughter Lalia about? I'm a bit worried about her. You see, she's been going on about \qThe Last Prince,\q one of Mr. Butterbur's tales. It's one of his better ones, that's for sure, but I'd say the tale isn't quite the truth of it.
'The way Lalia was talking last night, I think she might have gone out to the Barrow-downs in search of this \qprince\q of hers. And with what folks are saying about that place, I think she could be in trouble. Would you look for her?
'Now, in the tale, the Last Prince's barrow is between the Northern Barrows and the Dead Spire, by a large stone. I would start searching there. I would take some friends if I were you...those Barrow-downs are said to be haunted!'
Find Bob's daughter, Lalia
The Search for Lalia
Bob's daughter, Lalia, has gone missing, and Bob fears she may have gone off in search of the \qLast Prince,\q a character in one of the tales Barliman Butterbur tells to travellers.

'Have you found my girl, Lalia, yet? If she's gone off in search of her \qLast Prince,\q she's probably gone to the barrow Barliman talks about in his tale. His tale says the prince's barrow could be found near a standing stone, between the Northern Barrows and the Dead Spire.
'Please check on her soon, if she did go out there, I'm worried she got herself into quite a bit of trouble, what with the tales of the Barrow-downs lately!'

According to Butterbur's tale, the barrow of the Last Prince lies between Northern Barrows and the Dead Spire, near a large standing stone.

'The Quick Post service will surely live up to its name again if we continue at this rate, ${PLAYER}! There is something you can help me with, and maybe that will....
'Oh, don't start towards the mail satchels just yet! I'm actually on top of the deliveries for today and don't need you to take any of these anywhere. No, what I want you to do is to bring word to Postman Oddfoot in Frogmorton about our efforts to improve the speed at which we deliver the mail. He's been rather depressed lately -- hobbits in Frogmorton are not shy about expressing their complaints, and Oddfoot has always been one to take things rather to heart.
'Frogmorton is east of Bywater. Tell Oddfoot that we're repairing the reputation of the Quick Post service and offer him whatever help you can.'

'Hello there. I'm the postman for Frogmorton. I'm sorry for any inconvenience the Quick Post service may have caused you....
'What's that? You're not here to complain? Oh. Oh, I see. That's nice. Yes, I'm glad we haven't disappointed you today. I get so many complaints, you know. It does get to a hobbit, after a while.
'You say that Postman Cotton is trying to revitalize the Quick Post service and make it what it used to be? Even with all the letters that get sent these days? That's incredible news! If we can recapture our old reputation, maybe we won't need to spend so much time answering complaints!'
Inspire Postman Oddfoot

'You seek to help the Earth-kin? Wargs come from the northern hills in great packs. They slaughter the lehmä herds -- what you call aurochs -- for no reason, leaving carcasses rotting in the sun, uneaten.
'The lehmä are our food. With the herds gone, we will starve! There are too many Wargs for our hunters to slay.
'You will hunt them? Drive the packs from our herds, or this winter is our last!'

'Ah, a young and inexperienced tailor! Tales of my great skill and bravery have drawn you here to learn, as so many others have been drawn! Rumour of which deed has prompted you to seek me out? The tale of my triumph over the evil Giants of the North, in which I wrested from them the Bauble of the Stout-hearted? Or perhaps the minstrels still sing of how I cleared an infestation of drakes from -- no?
'Well, if you want to become even a quarter of the tailor I am, you will need to get started on some deed that will win you great renown. After all, physical craftsmanship is only half of tailoring, and not even the important half! The other half depends on the reputation of the tailor!
'In any event, I will need to judge your work. Craft a drake-skin cuirass for me to examine. Only the hide of the largest and most dangerous drakes of Nan Amlug in the North Downs will suffice! Your tale must be well-earned for me to recognize you as a master tailor.'

'Well, this is fine work, ${PLAYER}. I hesitate to tell you this, but...it seems earlier I might have led you astray. It turns out that the quality of the finished product is rather more important than the reputation of the crafter. I have lost all of my customers to a young hobbit who has never slain a drake in her life! It seems the quality of her stitches is better, or some such nonsense.
'I don't think people understand what to look for in their leather goods.
'Keep up the good work, ${PLAYER}. At least I know that you have a reputation that is worth something! I recognize you to be master tailor by all accounts!'

'If you know the aurochs, you know what a menace they can be when something raises their ire. One of them is a brute of a particular and foul disposition, a beast Durin's Folk call Frostmantle.
'We can't get close to Frostmantle without him charging, and it's getting too dangerous to leave alone. I fear that someone's bound to get trampled, gored or worse! What say you go and kill the brute? Return with one of its horns and I'll see to it that you're rewarded.
'You'll find it wandering to the west of Frerin's Court here, by the old obelisk.'

'Ah, you have done it. That'll keep the area a bit safer, eh?
'Good job!'

'Someone has to deal with Frostmantle, and that might as well be you. I can't be bothered risking my beard! Find him wandering around the old obelisk west of Frerin's Court here. Defeat Frostmantle and bring one of its horns to me.'

'The weapons you found are a great help. I will see them delivered to Asikko, the Earth-kin chieftain. Now, I have one more favour to ask of you.
'Just east from Esteldín and to the north along the base of the hills surrounding this hidden fort, you will find an Earth-kin camp. The denizens there are of the Suuri-lehmä tribe, our friends. We must make sure they know of our efforts on their behalf.
'Will you take this letter to Asikko, their chieftain? It may be that he will openly declare an alliance with my people, which can only serve to strengthen our position in the North Downs.'

'My delivery was packaged and sent to the Earth-kin while you spoke with their leader.
'This news you bring is heartening. I shall make plans to assist the Earth-kin.
'Thank you for all you have done, ${PLAYER}.'

'You see that we raise no weapons against you, ${RACE}. We are peaceful and wish to remain that way.
'I see that the Men have chosen to honour our oath. This pleases me. We shall honour our oaths as well and await the return of our stolen weapons.
'We shall not rest until our brethren return to our ways or are removed. Such betrayal cannot be allowed.'
'We raise no weapons against you. Why do you brandish yours, ${RACE}? We desire peace, only peace.'
Deliver the letter to Asikko
Caught in the Wake

'You have helped us gain an ally in this dark time, ${PLAYER}. For that, I am grateful.'
'The Earth-kin, no matter how small their numbers, will be a great ally.

'I know that you have assisted Daervunn already, and I assume that you are here to learn if you might assist me. My task is not an easy one, and with all the preparations for the coming war, I find myself stretched too far across my duties.
'The Earth-kin, with whom we have long shared a distant friendship, have lost much with their brethren's betrayal. They may become more open and amenable allies should we recover some of those things which were taken from them.
'The Earth-kin of the Rauta-lehmä faction in eastern Nan Amlug use weapons taken from the fallen in their insurrection. Go there and steal these weapons back. Be careful not to destroy the weapons in your battle.'

'The return of these weapons may serve to hearten the chieftain of the Suuri-lehmä, the Earth-kin who remain our friends. It may even encourage him to join us when the time for pitched battle arrives.'

'We know for certain that the Earth-kin of the Rauta-lehmä are encamped in eastern Nan Amlug. I have also heard rumours that there is another encampment south in Rhunenlad. You must secure the stolen weapons.'
Return the Earth-kin Weapons to Elúr

'According to Asikko's book, Earth-kin hunters use the mantles of thick fur that grow upon the shoulders of the aurochs to pad the inside of their armour. This fur provides both warmth and comfort.
'I need you to make your way into the fields of Rhunenlad or eastern Nan Amlug in search of these mantles. You will have the best results hunting the aurochs bulls. Do not attempt this hunt alone, for the aurochs are mighty beasts.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}. You need not sacrifice yourself for the sake of gathering furs.'

'Ah, four fine mantles. You have taken great pains to see these delivered, and you have earned my gratitude. I will soon be done with my work, and the people of Trestlebridge will have the armour that they need.
'This assault from the North has taken a difficult toll on the people of the North Downs, but with your help, I believe they will prevail.'
'Hunt the aurochs on the plains. Be careful as an enraged aurochs bull is difficult prey, even for several Men.'

'The wings of drakes are tough and leathery, and with the right preparation, I deem they will make a sturdy suit of armour. Asikko's book contains many methods for preparing the hide, but I still lack the hide itself.
'I doubt the drakes will be as ready to give up their wings as the worms were to shed their scales. Take allies with you as you hunt the drakes. You will find the beasts in the western pass of Ram Dúath, north-west of Esteldín.
'This leather should provide me with all I need to finish the armour I owe the people of Trestlebridge.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}. With aurochs-mantles, worm-scales, drake-leather, and the methods of the Earth-kin, the folk of Trestlebridge will receive fine armour indeed.
'You have done so much, but alas this is all I have to offer you as a reward.'

Leathery Wings of the Drakes

At the request of the Ranger Gondranc, you went to the camp of the Earth-kin north-east of Esteldín to retrieve a book of leatherworking lore Asikko, the Earth-kin's chieftain, had promised him. With this lore, he will be able to make much better armour for the people of Trestlebridge.

Drakes can be found in the western valley of Ram Dúath, north of Esteldín.
To finish the armour he is crafting for the people of Trestlebridge, Gondranc is in need of the leathery hide from the wings of drakes. He has asked you to gather allies and hunt drakes in Ram Dúath.

'This task, at least, is finished. I have much work to do to help my kindred prepare for the coming war, but my oath to Trestlebridge shall at lest be fulfilled.
'I need you, if you are willing, to deliver this armour to Jarred Mason in Trestlebridge. He is a man of some crafting skill himself. I believe he is acting as the armourer for his people.
'I am sure you have crossed through Trestlebridge and know well their plight, but should you have lost your direction, it lies far to the west and south of Esteldín, along the Greenway leading to Bree-land.'

'Jarred is a good man. I have often wanted to tell him of our home here at Esteldín, but our way of life is too dangerous to explain to those who know it not already.
'If this war which rages about us ends and my Lord Aragorn takes his rightful place, perhaps there will be a time when I may tell Jarred my whole tale, but for now, his safety -- and ours -- must hold precedence.
'I have something for you. Your efforts are deserving of a greater gift. I used the remnants of what you brought me to craft you this fine armour.'

'What is this? You say this came from Gondranc? I will admit I had not thought to hear from him again!
'My friend is a wanderer, rarely staying in one place too long, and when he decided to pass north, I could not help but wonder what he hoped to find in the barrens. Then the Orcs came, and I was sure he had perished.
'My people, what few are left here, need it more than ever. If you know where Gondranc is, return to him with my thanks!'

'I fear the worst of my friend Gondranc. He is a traveller versed in the art of leatherwork. He had promised me armour for our guards before the arrival of the Orcs. Now I fear he was slain somewhere in the wilds of the North Downs.'
Deliver the armour to Jarred Mason
A Promise Fulfilled

At the request of the Ranger Gondranc, you went to the camp of the Earth-kin north-east of Esteldín to retrieve a book of leatherworking lore Asikko, the Earth-kin's chieftain, had promised him. With this lore, he has crafted armour for the people of Trestlebridge.
'Make your way west and south to the town of Trestlebridge at the border of the North Downs and Bree-land. Deliver his armour to Jarred Mason.'
'Please, tell Gondranc that he has helped to restore hope to us in this beleaguered time.'
'Our task here has only begun, but thanks to you, ${PLAYER}, we have at least aided Trestlebridge.'
'Asikko's book has given me a much better understanding of leatherwork, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for bringing it.
'This armour is much finer than anything I imagined Gondranc would send! Thank you, good ${RACE}.'
'I am pleased to know that Gondranc is alive and well...and crafting such fine armour!'

Jarred Mason is an armourer in Trestlebridge, far to the west and south of Esteldín, along the Greenway.
Gondranc completed the armour he had promised for the people of Trestlebridge and has only to deliver it. He has asked you to act as his courier and deliver the armour to a man named Jarred Mason.

Gondranc resides at Esteldín, far to the north and east of Trestlebridge.
Jarred Mason has asked you to return to Gondranc with his thanks for the armour.

'Your efforts are well known amongst all here in Esteldín, ${PLAYER}. I am hopeful that you will assist me with a small task.
'Long ago, when I journeyed abroad, I taught Asikko, the chieftain of the Earth-kin the Westron letters. In return, he offered to write me a book describing their leatherworking methods. I need this book to fulfil a promise I made to a man in Trestlebridge as I came north from Rivendell in the guise of a common leatherworker. I promised to make for his people armour suitable for use against the Orcs.
'Will you go to Asikko and ask for the book? The Earth-kin are encamped north-east of here. Just skirt the hills northward from the eastern entrance to Esteldín.'

'Ha, you come for my book! I had not thought on those days for long and long.
'Are you Gondranc? No...you are not he. You must forgive me, but it is difficult to know. You little folk look so much alike to the Suuri-lehmä, and my mind is on the pain of my own people.'
A Request to the Earth-kin
When Gondranc of Esteldín was journeying north from Rivendell, he had promised a man of Trestlebridge that he would assist them by providing armour for use against the Orcs.
'Asikko is honourable and trustworthy. I know that he will not abandon his promise.'

Asikko is at the Earth-kin camp, found by skirting the hills northward from the eastern entrance to Esteldín.
In order to fulfil his obligation to Trestlebridge, Gondranc has asked you to obtain a book of leatherworking lore promised to him by Asikko, chieftain of the Earth-kin.
Collected Thick Worm-scale (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Sturdy Worm-scales (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Thin Worm-scales (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have need of your aid, ${PLAYER}. When the Orcs overran the North Downs, many suffered. Here at Esteldín, we are insulated from the ravages of the Orcs, but beyond these high walls there are those who suffer still.
'I had promised armour for the defence of Trestlebridge as I journeyed through their village, but the preparations of my own people to attack the Witch-realm of Angmar have depleted my supplies.
'You have been to the north-west where worms roam Ram Dúath. Worms shed their skin, leaving their scales behind. I need you to find these scales and of many sizes. With the knowledge of the Earth-kin, they will make a strong armour.'

'I see that some of these scales are damaged, but that is of no concern. You have brought more than enough whole scales for my purposes.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}.'
'Be wary in Ram Dúath. The worms which dwell there are very dangerous.'
Return the Scales to Gondranc
Collect Thick Worm-scale (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect Sturdy Worm-scale (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect Thin Worm-scale (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Scales of the Earthbound Foe

At the request of the Ranger Gondranc, you went to the camp of the Earth-kin north-east of Esteldín to retrieve a book of leatherworking lore Asikko, the Earth-kin's chieftain, had promised him. With this lore, he will be able to make much better armour for the people of Trestlebridge.
Thanks for getting those hides.

Worms can be found in the western pass of Ram Dúath, north-west of Esteldín.
Worms shed their skin, leaving behind their scales. Gondranc has asked you to gather these loose scales so that he may use them to craft armour.
Collected Asikko's book (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My people's pride binds us. I do not wish to raise arms against my brethren, but I have been forced to do so. I will fight them when the time comes, though it does not please me. I am also bound by honour, and that honour must be satisfied, even in the face of the First Hunter's betrayal.
'I know only names, not faces. The name I know is Gondranc, a man who knows well the crafting of leather and tanned hides. I promised to share with him the secrets of our art in return for the letters he once taught me.
'I wrote a book for the man before the betrayal, but it is lost now to the Rauta-lehmä in the east. I dare not go there yet. Will you go to the camp of the traitors and find this book for me?'

'In a time past, I would ask my brethren for the book, and it would be given freely. Since the arrival of the Men of the North, my brethren have changed. They have forsaken their oaths and follow the Men without thinking of the damage they do to the land. It is sad that the book had to be taken from them with war and death, but honour says it must be so.
'Take this book to little Gondranc and tell him honour is satisfied. May he use its knowledge well.'

'In a time past, I would ask my brethren for the book, and it would be given freely. Since the arrival of the Men of the North, my brethren have changed. They have forsaken their oaths and follow the Men without thinking of the damage they do to the land.
'If you cannot take the book from the Rauta-lehmä, then honour demands I must do so myself, and I do not think I will live. But what must be, must be.'

'Ah, my thanks to Asikko for his courtesy and to you for your assistance. With this lore, I will be able to craft the best possible armour I may for the people of Trestlebridge.
'Now, if you are willing, I have another task for you....'
'You have not brought the book from Asikko? Then the folk of Trestlebridge will have to make do with what meager armour I can provide them.'
Deliver the book to Asikko
Collect Asikko's book (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring Asikko's book to Gondranc
Techniques of the Masters

The Ranger Gondranc sent you to the Earth-kin camp to collect a book of leatherworking lore from Asikko, the Earth-kin's chieftain. However, when you arrived at the Earth-kin camp, Asikko told you the book had been stolen.
'You have my book, now bring it to my little friend Gondranc!'

Asikko's book is hidden somewhere in the camp of the traitorous Rauta-lehmä faction in Nan Amlug, east of the camp of the Suuri-lehmä.
Asikko is hesitant to go himself to retrieve the book of lore from the Rauta-lehmä for fear of provoking war too soon. Instead, he has asked you to retrieve the book for him.

Gondranc awaits your return at Esteldín.
You successfully recovered Asikko's book from the camp of the Rauta-lehmä. The Earth-kin chieftain has asked you to deliver it to Gondanc, fulfilling his promise to the Ranger.
Drake egg destroyed (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your success against the worms of Ram Dúath is a tribute to your courage and skill, but there is a greater threat lingering therein. Our scouts say that they have seen drakes as well. Though the winged drakes are still not as great as their forebears, they are formidable and intelligent.
'If we hope to use the western pass to gain entrance into Angmar beyond, the drakes will need to be driven out or destroyed. I have no doubt that there are drake-nests somewhere within the valley...destroy them before the drakes can multiply.
'I would warn you not to go alone. Drakes may be no more than intelligent beasts, but they are dangerous and will fiercely defend their nests.'
'If the nests were as well-defended as you say, then I fear there is some greater evil at work. I may have another task for you, if you are willing.'
Destroy drake eggs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Destroying the Hatchery

Not only are there worms within the western valley of Ram Dúath, but drakes as well. The winged drakes, more intelligent than their lesser kin, present a greater threat to Esteldín and the North Downs.
'You must take care near the nests, for the worms will likely be more aggressive and if there are any drake-hatchlings about you may find yourself quickly outnumbered.'
I thank you for all you have done against the winged foe in the Ram Dúath.

Drake-nests may be found in the western valley of Ram Dúath, north of Esteldín. Destroy eggs found within the nests to stop the drakes' spread.
Arastil has asked you to destroy the nests of the drakes who dwell within the western valley of Ram Dúath before they can multiply.

Arastil awaits your return in Esteldín.
You found several drake-nests in the western Ram Dúath and destroyed them, but worms were plentiful in the area, and the nests were well-defended. Arastil will wish to hear of your victory.

'One last obstacle remains before us, ${PLAYER}: the drake-matron who laid the eggs you found. If she is permitted to live, she will only breed again and close the pass to us.
'Return to the western pass of Ram Dúath and seek out the drake-matron. Slay her if you can. Our plans depend on it.
'Be wary, though, and take friends, for the drake-matron will be enraged by the destruction of her brood.'

'Such a quest is very dangerous and requires proven mettle. You have proven without doubt that you are possessed of will and strength unmatched.
'Please, take this with my thanks and know that you have made possible our push into Angmar when the time arrives.'
Mother of the Valley
A drake-matron, the mother of the brood you destroyed, resides within the western valley of Ram Dúath. The pass will not be safe until she is slain.
'As long as the drake-matron lives, the western pass of Ram Dúath will be blocked to us.'
'Your aid is not forgotten on me ${PLAYER}. Your efforts have given the Rangers more hope against Angmar.'
'A drake-matron is a formidable beast, ${PLAYER}. You have done well.'

The drake-matron resides within the western pass of Ram Dúath, north-west of Esteldín.
Arastil has set you one more task: slay the drake-matron of Ram Dúath. As long as she lives, she will only spawn a new brood. Arastil warns you to take allies, for the drake-matron is likely to be enraged by the loss of her brood.

Arastil awaits you at Esteldín.
Arastil will be pleased to know that you have slain the matron. Return to him at Esteldín with news of your victory.

'You are the one who has been aiding my kin against the army of Angmar...${PLAYER}, is it not? We have need of your services again.
'The passage through Ram Dúath north-east of here is blocked by the Hillmen of Angmar; however, not all paths are closed to us. To the north of Esteldín lies another pass, though it also is fraught with danger. Worms hide amid the crags and crevices, preying on unwary travellers.
'We need you to clear the pass of these worms, so that we may safely take a force through. Be careful.'

'You have proven capable, my friend. Though there are other dangers in Ram Dúath which may yet prove too great, even for you
'We shall see, for I have another task for you.'
Valley of the Worms
The western pass of Ram Dúath has long been home to worms, least of dragon-kind. Dwelling in the crags and caves of the mountain pass, they prey upon any who dare that path.
'The worms are creatures of little intelligence, but they are not to be trifled with. In great enough numbers, they are still a terrible threat.'

Worms can be found in the western pass of Ram Dúath, north of Esteldín.
Arastil has asked you to clear the worms from the western pass of Ram Dúath, making it safe to bring a force through the pass into Angmar.

Arastil awaits your return at Esteldín.
You made your way into the valley and slew the worms you found there. You should return to Arastil with news of your victory.
Collected Ranger Troves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have little time to bandy words. The Orcs' invasion from the North has caught the Rangers of the North unprepared. Many of our kindred are abroad in other lands, preparing a defence against the Shadow in the East, and our eyes were not turned northwards.
'This army that has come down from Angmar is too great for our forces in the North Downs to defeat without support, yet we must still prepare for the fighting that is to come.
'My predecessor stored many weapons and supplies throughout eastern Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad, but I do not know exactly where. I need you to seek out these troves and bring them to me. The thing that I do know is that these troves were all hidden near rocks and trees. This will not be an easy search, without proper guidance, but in these dark times, every resource we can gather will be of great help to us.'

'It will take some work to make many of these weapons usable, but they are better than hoes and pitchforks. We shall set about the repairs at once.
'I trust that your search was not too difficult. We must be resolute and fight back against these Orcs before the North Downs are lost. They must not be allowed to invade Bree-land, or many innocents will be killed and all the North may fall.'

'We hid the troves well, it is unlikely that the Orcs have despoiled them. Search in the area of Rhunenlad and eastern Nan Amlug.
'Be careful not to stray too close to the Earth-kin camps on the eastern edges of the plains. They have fallen under the sway of the Angmarim.'
Bring the Ranger Troves back to Faronwen
Collect Ranger Troves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Esteldin's Preparation

The unexpected invasion of the Orcs from the North have caught the Rangers of Esteldín unprepared, with many of their kindred abroad in other lands. This new threat has forced them to recall as many of their kind as they can and to arm themselves for war.

The Rangers' supply troves are hidden throughout eastern Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad.
In preparation for war, Faronwen is tasked with recovering the stores of weapons and supplies her predecessor hid. She has asked you to search Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad for these hidden stores. She only knows that these troves are hidden by rocks and trees.
Collected hillborn woad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected hillborn orchanet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'While the troves you uncovered are important to our efforts, there remains something that we will need even more, ${PLAYER} -- hope. Courage drives our people, and hope has helped us to survive. When we fight, we will look to our banners for inspiration.
'I am charged with the crafting of these banners and must make them ready with haste. I need dyes to stain the linen that will bear our symbols.
'On the plains and rolling hills of Rhunenlad and Nan Amlug in the east, you will find hillborn woad and hillborn orchanet. Many of these plants have been trampled in the Orcs' passage, but I am sure you will be able to find enough to meet our needs.'

'These shall do nicely. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. It may seem strange, but the colour of our symbol is most easily achieved by the use of these two plants.
'Aragorn will be pleased when the banner is raised once more. We have hid here in Esteldín for too long.'

'We are fortunate that the Orcs did not trample all of the vegetation. The plants that survived should be found on the hills east of Esteldín in Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad, though I do not know how plentiful they will be.'
Bring the woad and orchanet back to Faronwen
Collect hillborn woad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect hillborn orchanet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Symbol of Hope

You searched Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad for the supply troves which Faronwen's predecessor hid there and found many, but they are only a small part of the supplies needed to support the preparations of the Rangers at Esteldín.
'Our banners will fly high, and the Enemy will quail before them.'
'Your aid has been greatly appreciated, ${PLAYER}.'

Hillborn woad and hillborn orchanet grow on the hills of eastern Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad.
Faronwen has asked you to bring her some hillborn woad and hillborn orchanet, with which she will prepare dyes to colour the banners the Rangers will bear into battle.
Collected thick aurochs hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected aurochs meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I was asked to take stock of our provisions and appraise the repair of our tents. I have found that both are lacking. Without preparations, we will be forced to split our forces both to hunt the remaining game in the region and to fight the Orcs. Our numbers are too few for such a task.
'My request is simple: gather your allies and head into Rhunenlad and Nan Amlug, east of Esteldín, where the Aurochs are more plentiful. From the bulls collect hides...they can be used as shelter. The yearlings and cows will provide the best meat.
'Our needs will be great, so do not be frugal in your hunt.'

'This will help solidify our stores and allow us to remain focused on the trial at hand. We are moving closer to the inevitability of war each day.
'Take heart, for you have aided us in our hour of need, and you are to be thanked and rewarded, ${PLAYER}.'
'Search the plains east of Esteldin, in Rhunenlad and Nan Amlug. Aurochs wander those hills and plains in fair number.'
Speak with Mallennor
Collect thick aurochs hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect aurochs meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Food and Shelter

The terrible slaughter of the Orc invasion has driven away the farmers from the western Nan Amlug, and with them any trade the Rangers had maintained. Short on supplies and provender, the Rangers of Esteldín must rely on their own resourcefulness to restock their supplies.
'Our stores should hold for some time now.'
'Thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}. These stores will aid us in our efforts.'

Aurochs can be found in Rhunenlad and Nan Amlug, east of Esteldín.
Mallennor has been tasked with providing shelter and food for the Rangers of Esteldín and has asked you to help them by hunting aurochs for hide and meat.
Collected relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your arrival is proof that Hunulf and Gadaric have found folk willing to assist us with our plight. That is enough to bring hope to the Eglain.
'A year hence, we lost a rich ruin to men from the South...at least we thought they were Men. They bore the manner, height, and look of Men but were nearly as savage as the Orc-folk we learned they were descended from.
'Naerost, west of here, but far to the east of the great hill of Weathertop, fell to the half-breeds and our trade was lost with it. If we could recover some of those goods, we might restore trade with the west and some hope for Eglain. Will you help us sift through the ruins for our goods?'

'Worthy finds, ${PLAYER}. These will fetch enough food for many families here in Ost Guruth. You are a true friend to the Eglain.
'So many perished when the half-breeds approached from the south, it is painful to recall. For now, know that you have done a great good for us all.'

'In Nain Enidh, north of the Great East Road and east of Weathertop, you will find the ruins of Naerost. You will know it by the half-breeds who make it their home.
Amongst the rubble, you will find piles which appear to be nothing of import, but I tell you these relics will fetch a sum of food most bountiful from traders out of Bree.'
Return the relics to Gestr Quicksilver
Collect relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Half-breed Thieves

In the shadow of Amon Sûl, at the edge of Nain Enidh, lay an Arnorian ruin. Those ruins afforded the Eglain of Ost Guruth a wealth of material to trade with collectors in Bree-land...until the arrival of half-breeds from the South.

The ruins of Naerost are just east of Weathertop, west of Ost Guruth.
A year ago, half-orcs wrested the ruins of Naerost from the Eglain, causing the Eglain to lose a valuable source of trade goods. Gestr Quicksilver has asked you to go to the ruins of Naerost and retrieve as many of the Eglain's lost relics as you can.
Collected stolen crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated half-orcs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Many lost their lives when the half-orcs raided Naerost. Since then, we have struggled greatly. Most recently, as you likely know, we lost the ruin to goblins forced through the mountains in the north.
'Yet the half-orcs came first, and they slaughtered our people, stole our livelihood, and began despoiling the ruin. We do not know why, but we know they have collected many relics within the ruins and have packed them for delivery to the South.
'If you are willing, I would ask you to enter Naerost and seek the hirelings who guard the relics and slay them. Bring back any of the relics you find.'

'We will ensure that none of these relics were taken from the tombs of the men who perished within the ruins in ages past. If they are not, they will be used to feed and clothe our people. If they prove to be stolen from tombs, they will be buried once more to honour the fallen.
'You have proven yourself a brave and honourable warrior, ${PLAYER}, and your aid is valued by the Eglain.'
'The half-orcs slaughtered many of the Eglain and have since raped the ruins of much of their wealth. Something must be done to stop them.'
Collect stolen crates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat half-orcs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the stolen crates to Gestr Quicksilver
A Righteous Theft

In the shadow of Amon Sûl, at the edge of Nain Enidh, lays an Arnorian ruin. Those ruins afforded the Eglain of Ost Guruth a wealth of material to trade with collectors in Bree-land...until the arrival of half-breeds from the South.

Naerost lies just east of Amon Sûl, west of Ost Guruth.
Gestr Quicksilver has asked you to seek out and slay the hirelings who guard the relics packed for shipment and return as many of the relics as you can to the Eglain.

Gestr Quicksilver awaits your return at Ost Guruth to the east of Naerost.
You should return with the recovered relics to Gestr Quicksilver.

'Your efforts on behalf of the Eglain are noble, my friend, but I deem our peril is greater than first we thought. I understand these half-breeds bear a standard with the mark of a white hand? Ordinary brigands and ruffians do not bear such charges. The mark of the White Hand tells me they serve a greater master.
'Radagast the Brown, the Wizard who has come to the Ruin-hold, reports that he saw Orcs bearing such a charge while journeying through Rohan on his way to Isengard months ago. These Orcs did battle with the Men of Rohan. Perhaps this mark signifies some new devilry of Mordor?
'Whatever their purpose, such creatures cannot be allowed to take a foothold in the North. They do not belong here. If you can enter Naerost and slay Hontimûrz and his guards, perhaps the rest will flee.'

'Ah, so the half-breeds will not run? No matter...the grip of the White Hand is loosened. They will not trouble us again.
'Your efforts on behalf of the Eglain will not be forgotten, ${PLAYER}.'
Sever the White Hand

In the shadow of Amon Sûl, at the edge of Nain Enidh, lay an Arnorian ruin. Those ruins afforded the Eglain of Ost Guruth a wealth of material to trade with collectors in Bree-land...until the arrival of half-breeds from the South.
'We shall ever remember you, ${PLAYER}.'
'I can find my strength once again, thanks to all you have done.'

Naerost lies just east of Weathertop, west of Ost Guruth.
Gestr Quicksilver is concerned that the half-orcs are servants of a greater power, perhaps even Mordor. He has asked you to enter Naerost and slay their leader and his guards in hopes that the rest will flee.

Gestr Quicksilver awaits your return at Ost Guruth, east of Naerost.
Though the half-orcs did not flee, their leader and his guards have been slain. You should return to Gestr Quicksilver with the news.
Collected the necklace of Daegwalt's wife

'You do not have a dishonourable look about you, not like the evil that drove us from Naerost. My wife was slain in the assault nearly a year hence. Only I survived of my family, lame from an arrow through the leg, unable to visit vengeance upon my wife's murderers.
'Would you help lay my anger to rest and assist me in recovering some of what I lost when the half-breeds raided Naerost? My wife wore a necklace about her neck, an heirloom from her mother and her mother before her. No doubt it was claimed as a trophy by the half-breeds. If I had this, I would let my hate pass and find a proper way to mourn.
'Naerost lies to the west of here, just east of Amon Sûl.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. Nothing can bring my wife back to me, but I shall hold her close to my heart forevermore.
'The half-orcs are beasts and must be dealt with, but I am not the one to see that happen. Speak with Gestr Quicksilver...he will know better how to bring justice to my wife's memory.'

'Were my leg not lame, I would march with you and search the half-orcs myself. Alas, I am now but a shell and unable to do so. I must rely on others to assist me in seeking my revenge and setting my heart and mind at ease.'
Return the necklace to Daegwalt
Collect the necklace of Daegwalt's wife
An Honourless People

In the shadow of Amon Sûl, at the edge of Nain Enidh, lay an Arnorian ruin. Those ruins afforded the Eglain of Ost Guruth a wealth of material to trade with collectors in Bree-land...until the arrival of half-breeds from the South.

Naerost lies just east of Amon Sûl, west of Ost Guruth.
Daegwalt asked that you make your way into the ruins of Naerost and recover the necklace that was taken from his wife, who was slain when the half-orcs raided the ruins.
Collected a dwarf-banner

'I sometimes think I ought never have left the mountains and the home of my ancestors, but I sought after a life of adventure. After too many years looking, I found myself lost and then found again here amongst the Eglain.
'I have been here a long time now and consider myself one of them, but there are remnants of my own heritage that never stray, friend, and those remnants get stirred in times like these.
'I hear rumour of dwarves working with Orcs to despoil the tombs beneath the ruins of Thandobel to the south-west. I wish to know what kind of dwarf would tolerate Orcs, much less deign to work alongside them. Go to Thandobel and bring me one of their banners.'

'I know this blazon. My father told me of a revolt and battle long ago against a host of the Elves in Ered Luin. Skorgrím...a leader of the Dourhands, to whom this blazon belongs, led the assault and drove the Dourhands to near destruction.
'Buried beneath the mountains was he, by the quick actions of the Elves' leader, who sacrificed himself to deny Skorgrím victory.
'Dourhands in league with Orcs...grim news indeed, and there is no doubt of what must come next.'

'No self-respecting dwarf would abide the sight of an Orc, much less help the filthy creatures. Either the dwarves in Ost Cyrn are under the sway of a grim sorcerer, or they must be destroyed.
I need your assistance to determine which. Bring me one of the banners from around their fortress.'
Return the banner to Refr Quicksilver
Collect a dwarf-banner
Dour Dwarves

South-west of Ost Guruth lay a ruin, long abandoned by the Eglain. Picked clean and having only the depths of the ruin unexplored, the Eglain left the tombs beneath the ruin be, as is their custom. However, the ruin now teems with life again as dwarves, in league with Orcs, scour the ruin for treasures in the depths.

The ruins of Thandobel lie to the south-west of Ost Guruth in Nain Enidh.
Refr Quicksilver expressed a desire to learn what kind of dwarves would deign to work alongside Orcs and has asked you to go to the ruins of Thandobel and capture one of their banners.

'This dwarf is not one to brook betrayal, and I know now that the Dourhands are betrayers to all the Free Peoples. Consorting with Orcs is deserving of only one punishment.
'I'll not say that I am pleased by this situation, ${PLAYER}, nor will I look an opportunity side-long when it stares me in the face. Dwarf or not, these Dourhands need to be dealt with, and you seem to be more than suitable to the cause.
'I have a request of you, then. Return to Thandobel and wreak vengeance upon the Dourhands in the name of all the Free Peoples. But let us see something good come out of this evil. Bring me the axes of the Dourhands, for metal is not evil, and dwarf-metal can be used to the benefit of us all!'

'Ha! Fine iron indeed. Not as comely as other weapons but still made by dwarf-hands and crafted with care. I shall smelt the ill deeds from these weapons and craft them newly into arms and armour for all to use.
'Do not see shame in what you have done, but gain strength from the knowledge that you have done your part to stop the spread of evil.'

'The Dourhands here in the Lone-lands must not be allowed to delve deeper into the ruins. If they are delving into the mounds of Men and assisting the Orcs, then something grim and foul is at work here.'
Deliver the Dourhand axes to Refr Quicksilver
A Dwarf's Duty

South-west of Ost Guruth lay a ruin, long abandoned by the Eglain. Picked clean and having only the depths of the ruin unexplored, the Eglain left the tombs beneath the ruin be, as is their custom. However, the ruin now teems with life again as dwarves, in league with Orcs, scour the ruin for treasures in the depths.

The Dourhands can be found within the ruins of Thandobel, south-west of Ost Guruth.
The Dourhand dwarves have forsaken their ties to their brethren by consorting with Orcs. Refr Quicksilver has asked you to bring vengeance upon the Dourhands in the name of the Free Peoples and to bring him a trophy of their axes.

Refr Quicksilver waits for you within Ost Guruth, north of the Great East Road in the Lone-lands, north-west of Thandobel.
You should return to Refr Quicksilver with news of your victory against the Dourhands and bring him the axes you took as a trophy.
Collected the Dourhand leader's medallion

'Somewhere in Mithrenost there is a dwarf who oversees the labours of the Dourhands, and loyalty to those who rule over us is in the nature of my kind. Though the Dourhands have gone against their nature by consorting with Orcs, all hope for them may not be lost.
'Find the leader of the Dourhands and defeat him. His defeat may break the resolve of his followers, and they may well turn from the dark path upon which they tred. Bring me evidence of the leader's downfall, and I will hold you honoured for your efforts on behalf of the Eglain.
'The leader will be savvy and strong...you should bring friends if you hope to defeat him.'

'Hunulf and Gadaric did well with choosing you. A fine upstanding sort you turned out to be.
'Though it pains me to know that my brethren have fallen so far, I am pleased to have gained the kinship you offer, ${PLAYER}.
'I took a certain liberty with some of the metal of the axes you collected and crafted this fine piece for you. You can do with it as you will. You have earned it.'
'Search near the centre of Mithrenost for turned earth or a greater congregation of Dwarfs. The leader will be there. Remember, do not be foolhardy and attempt this task on your own.'
Deliver the Dourhand medallion to Refr Quicksilver
Collect the Dourhand leader's medallion
Enemies of the Eglain

South-west of Ost Guruth lay a ruin, long abandoned by the Eglain. Picked clean and having only the depths of the ruin unexplored, the Eglain left the tombs beneath the ruin be, as is their custom. However, the ruin now teems with life again as dwarves, in league with Orcs, scour the ruin for treasures in the depths.
'I will not soon forget what you did against the Dourhands.'
'It is fine to see you again, ${PLAYER}.'

The leader of the Dourhands may be found within the ruins of Mithrenost, south-west of Ost Guruth.
Refr Quicksilver has asked to seek out and defeat the leader of the Dourhands at Mithrenost, in hopes that his followers will turn from their evil ways. He asked you to bring him evidence of the leader's defeat and also warned you to take friends with you.
Freed restless shades from Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It is good that I have found you, ${PLAYER}. I need your help. Long ago, a great battle took place at Fornost, and many died here. Through deception, Angmar caused many of the king's men to betray their oaths, and Fornost fell. Before he fled, King Arvedui cursed the Oathbreakers never to rest until they had fulfilled their oaths.
'It is said the folk of the North Downs are descended from the Men of Arthedain, though I don't believe any of us are from the royal bloodline. Still, perhaps these Oathbreaker shades will be able to leave if they know that my people have forgiven their betrayal?
'Will you seek out the repentant and offer them their freedom? It is said that many of these wander still near the skeletons of their former selves in the upper courtyard of Fornost.'

'You have done the people of the North Downs a great service. The Dead now rest, and I am happier for it. It seems odd though that so many still remain in Deadman's Dike. Perhaps someone or something holds them to its will....'
Free restless shades from Fornost's upper courtyards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Free the Fallen

At the Battle of Fornost, centuries earlier, some of King Arvedui's men turned against him, and Fornost fell to the Witch-king. Before he fled, Arvedui cursed these men never to rest until they fulfilled their oaths of fealty.
'Please release the shades. They have remained here long enough.'
'There is still much work to be done!'
'Someone leads them all... I know it.'

The shades Emma Slee sent you to free remain near their old skeletons in the upper areas of Fornost.
Emma Slee wishes to free some of the shades of Fornost from the ancient curse binding them to Middle-earth. She hopes that as descendants of the Dúnedain of Arthedain the forgiveness of the Men of the North Downs might be enough to free the repentant shades.

Emma Slee is at the Fornost camp.
Emma Slee will be pleased to hear that the shades have been freed from their curse.
Defeated Milkeyes within Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We need to keep our enemies penned within Rath Teraig as best we may. The number of goblins seems to grow each day, but our stout barricades have been enough to keep them at bay.
'However, those vile Milkeye Cave-claws have taken to creeping up and burrowing beneath the barricades in the deep of night and threaten to undermine the walls if we can't find a way to stop them.
'If you could hunt a number of the creatures down, it should serve to put a halt to their incessant digging and gain us time to repair any damage they've already done.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! That should keep those vermin at bay for a while and give us a chance to patch up the barricades before the goblins have another try at us.'
Defeat Milkeyes within Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Cave-claws In the Narrows

Ingólfr is concerned about the cave-claws burrowing beneath the barricades. Until recently, the barricades have been strong enough to withstand the goblin assaults, but the cave-claws have now weakened them.
'The Milkeyes dwell south of the barricade, in the narrow passes within the valley.'

Milkeyes can be found beyond the barricades south of Ingólfr's camp.
Ingólfr has asked you to enter Rath Teraig and kill off a number of Milkeyes, to prevent them from gnawing at the barricades.

Ingólfr is at his camp beyond the barricade at the northern entrance to Rath Teraig.
You should return to Ingólfr and let him know that you have done as he asked.

'My thanks to you for standing by us on this. Now that you've culled the local vermin, it's time to deal with the real threat...that is to say goblins!
'The foul things have been bubbling up out of the ground like bees from a kicked hive. I don't rightly know what's gotten them all riled up, nor do I much care, so long as we can drive them back down into their holes...for good.
'If you're up for a fight, get in there and break some goblin heads! If we can keep them penned in till winter, the snows ought to block up these passes till spring, and we'll be free of them for a long while at least.'

'Hah! Nothing like a rousing tale of goblin-slaying to warm you up on a cold day! Well done, ${PLAYER}. With your help we shouldn't have too many problems keeping the goblins at bay till the passes fill with snow for the winter.
'After that, it'll be up to the folks at Gondamon and Thorin's Halls to figure out what we'll do about them come next spring.'
Goblins in the Valley
Ingólfr is tired of dealing with the goblins of Rath Teraig, which have become more aggressive of late.
'South of the barricade is goblin territory, so you should have no problems finding goblin necks to hew.'
'You've a skilled hand with a weapon, ${PLAYER}!'
'Thanks to you, we shouldn't have too many worries with the goblins in Rath Teraig until spring.'

Goblins can be found beyond the barricade south of Ingólfr's camp.
Ingólfr has asked you to enter Rath Teraig and deal with the goblins there, in hopes that they will learn to keep away from the barricades long enough for the winter snows to fill the pass.

Ingólfr is at his camp beyond the barricade at the northern entrance to Rath Teraig.
You should return to Ingólfr and tell him of your battles against the Goblins of Rath Teraig.
Defeated spiders in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, greetings! Welcome to the beautiful Rath Teraig...the finest stretch of desolate rock and goblin holes in all of the Blue Mountains. If you've come to help, we could certainly use it. Things have gotten worse of late, and now all manner of things are crawling up out of the ground around here.
'I'd personally be grateful if you could do away with a few of the spiders that infest the area. I used to run patrols in there now and again, but since they showed up, I haven't been able to bring myself to set one foot past this barricade...I've been afraid of spiders since I was a wee lad.
'So what say you? Are you up for the challenge, or would you rather join me freezing my hinder parts off till the snows come?'
'The whole barricade guard -- both of us -- thanks you, ${PLAYER}, but I am personally indebted to you for killing those eight-legged horrors. Now, the less said of them the better!'
Defeat spiders in Rath Teraig (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Spiders of the Vale
Ingólfr has asked for your help in destroying the spiders that lurk beyond the barricade into Rath Teraig.
'The spiders are scattered throughout the valley to the south. You should be able to find them without too much trouble.'

There are spiders beyond the barricade south of Ingólfr's camp.
Ingólfr, deathly afraid of spiders, has asked you to slay a few of the creatures for him.

Ingólfr is at his camp beyond the barricade at the northern entrance to Rath Teraig.
You should return to Ingólfr with news of your success.
You pick through the wood pile and select a good piece of timber.
You search through the pile of wood, but find only rotten timbers.

'While most of the work has now been done, ${PLAYER}, there is one more obstacle to be faced. If we do not store this wine in a seasoned cask soon, it will be ruined and not fit for anyone, but we have already used up our stock.
'There is a cooper, Bregedúr, here in Celondim who supplies us our casks. Would you be willing to ask him for another?
'You can find Bregedúr at the Craftsman's Plaza in Celondim. Follow the path up the hill until you reach Duillond, then turn down the southwest path. Bregedúr should be nearby.'

'I have not had time enough to gather materials, and now I have very few casks left. I am sorry, but I cannot risk giving you one of these if it means I will not be able to supply the White Ships with the barrels they will need.
'If you gather some wood for me, I will give you one of these casks. The wood-yard is in a secluded grove somewhat southwest of here. That is where timbers too small for shipbuilding have been left to season.
'You may find some small logs the appropriate size for barrel staves, but be careful -- the goblins have excited the wolves of the area, and they have been active thereabout.'

'Yes, this wood will certainly do. Now I need not be concerned about giving you one of my remaining casks. If I am asked to supply more barrels for the White Ships, I should be able to satisfy that request.'
'I am afraid that I cannot give you a cask unless you bring me enough wood to serve for a few barrels. Have you found the wood-yard? It is up the hill and to the southwest of here.'
Talk to Bregedúr
Collect cask-building wood (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Bring the wood to Bregedúr in Celondim.
Need of a Cask
You harvested the grapes and crushed them, but now Brethilwen needs a wooden cask in which to properly store the wine.
'I acquired most of my materials from the wood-yard, so you should find plenty of lengths of wood suitable for barrel staves there.'
'If you are having difficulty finding Bregedúr, look to the Craftsman's Plaza here in Celondim. He is most likely there.'
'Bregedúr asked you to collect pieces of wood for him? If it means he will give us a cask, I suppose there is no harm in it. Please, do as he asks.'
'Bregedúr asked you to collect pieces of wood for him? If it means he will give us a cask, I suppose there is no harm in it. Please, do as he asks.'

Bregedúr can be found at the Craftsman's Plaza in Celondim. Follow the path to the north, then turn down the southwestern path once you reach the branch.
Brethilwen has asked you to acquire a wooden cask from Bregedúr, the local cooper at Celondim.

The wood-yard is in a grove southwest of Celondim.
The cooper, Bregedúr, has asked you to collect pieces of wood that he can use to make more barrels.

Bregedúr is at the Craftsman's Plaza in Celondim, northeast of the wood-yard.
Bregedúr, the cooper of Celondim, is seeking pieces of wood suitable for making casks.

'I have given you the cask you asked for, ${PLAYER}. Bring it to Brethilwen the Master-vintner in Celondim, and I shall return to my work.
'You can find Brethilwen in Celondim. Take the southern stairs and then walk the northern path past the docks.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, this cask will do nicely. I understand that Bregedúr is greatly pressed to meet the needs of the White Ships, so please do not take his abrasiveness to heart.
'Your help should relieve his burden for a time. Perhaps I shall send him a bottle of wine in a week or two.'
'I am still waiting for a cask from Bregedúr, ${PLAYER}. This wine must mature in the cask. It will be ruined if we cannot get one quickly!'
Bring the wine-cask to Brethilwen
Return the Cask
It has taken more time than expected, but you now have the cask Brethilwen requested.

Brethilwen is in Celondim, to the east. Follow the southern stair to the bottom, then walk along the path to the north past the piers.
Bregedúr, the cooper, gave you a cask to return to Brethilwen.

'Welcome to Falathlorn, ${PLAYER}. You can see the harbour-city of Celondim down the hill to the north-east, and the refuge of Duillond is further to the north.
'But I can see that you have a desire to fashion goods, to practice your ability to create things of substance and use. It is my recommendation that you visit my friend Gwaloth at the terrace overlooking Celondim, where many useful and comely goods are fashioned. Go down the hill to the north-east into the city and follow the path to the left as it winds up the hillside. Atop the stairs, follow the path southward to the terrace.
'Gwaloth will be pleased to help you learn how to begin your journey as a craftsman.'

'Mibrethil sent you to me? You must be interested in learning a crafting trade, then? Wonderful! Ered Luin will be better for your efforts, my friend! Speak with the Master of Apprentices on this terrace, for he can help you choose a vocation in which to specialize. A vocation is a bundle of three crafting professions with overlapping skills -- choose your vocation with care, because you will expend a great deal of time and energy improving your skill with the professions under its purview!
'Once the Master of Apprentices has welcomed you to your chosen vocation, be sure to speak with a Provisioner. She can sell you the tools of your trade -- every Profession has its own tools, so be not over-shy with your coinpurse! The novices will be happy to sell you any recipes you might wish to have, though I can tell you now that you will already know how to make a thing or two.
'Equip the crafting tools you plan on using and find an appropriate facility -- Celondim has a forge, workbench, and oven available for your use -- and begin practising your skills! You will advance in your chosen professions as you practice and seek out the teachings of others in the field. I hope you will become a skilled craftsman, ${PLAYER}, and that it will bring joy to you and profit to Ered Luin!'
A Terrace in Celondim
Mibrethil has suggested that you speak with his friend Gwaloth at a terrace overlooking the harbour of Celondim where useful and comely goods are made.

'Gwaloth is on a terrace overlooking Celondim where many useful things are made. Go down the hill to the north-east into Celondim, and then climb the winding stair on your left as it rises along the hillside. Atop the stair, take the southern path to the terrace and introduce yourself to Gwaloth. She will gladly aid you in choosing a crafting vocation.'
'I wish you good fortune with your pursuit of crafting, ${PLAYER}.'
'May your creations bring joy to those who need them.'
'The facilities of Celondim are yours to use as you like, ${PLAYER}.'
'Ered Luin will be a better place for your efforts.'

Gwaloth is on a terrace overlooking Celondim, located south of the top of the stairs that wind up the hillside around which the city is constructed.
The Elf Mibrethil suggested that you speak with his friend Gwaloth if you are interested in learning a crafting trade.
Collected polished agate (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I am a jeweller by interest and by trade, and I have a great many pieces in various states of completion. I could finish many of these pieces, but I am missing the gems needed for the final settings.
'If you know a jeweller with a ready supply, I will give you some coins for bringing to me three polished agates of suitable quality.
'Your assistance will be greatly appreciated, for I have already neglected these pieces for too long and am eager to complete them. I have one or two items that may be useful to you, and would happily trade them to you in exchange for the agates I need.'

'These polished agates are just the sort for which I have been waiting, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for them!
'Take these coins and items with my well-wishes, for now I can finish the pieces I have kept too long undone!
'Perhaps when this affair is finished, I shall find a place on one of the White Ships and sail away into the West. I will need to think on it.'
'Without three polished agates, I cannot finish these pieces as I hoped to do.'
Bring polished agates to Guleneth
Collect polished agate (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Gems for Guleneth
The jeweller Guleneth has asked you to bring him polished agates he can use in the pieces he makes.
'I do not yet know if it is my time to take to the Ships.'
'What is left for me to do? It is a question I have long pondered.'

Guleneth is at Celondim in Ered Luin.
Jeweller Guleneth has asked you to acquire three polished agates that he can use to complete some of the pieces he has left unfinished.

'Before you leave, ${PLAYER}, I have one more boon to ask of you. I promised a bottle of last year's vintage to a friend at Duillond to the north, and my labours kept me too busy to fulfil that pledge. I hope this has not inconvenienced her.
'Could you deliver this bottle to Dolengyl for me? The refuge lies on the road that follows the river north beyond Limael's vineyard.
'If you reach the dwarf-port of Kheledûl, you have travelled too far north.'

'Splendid! I must admit that I wondered if perhaps I had slighted Brethilwen in some way for her to neglect me for so long, but clearly I was mistaken.
'Ah, this vintage has the promise of ageing nicely. Perhaps in some thirty years, it will have aged sufficiently. You have my thanks.'
'Are you in need of something? I am afraid I do not know how I may be of service.'
Bring the bottle of wine to Dolengyl.
Gift for a Friend
Brethilwen promised a bottle of the previous year's vintage to Dolengyl, an Elf at the refuge of Duillond.
'You are looking for Dolengyl of Duillond? The refuge is on the river, yes, but it is a far distance north of here. You want to head north across the tributary and past Limael's vineyard.'

'Dolengyl has been very kind to me, and I hope this has not inconvenienced her! Please bring her that bottle of wine as soon as you are able. Duillond sits on the river, but you will need to pass over the stream to the north.'
'I trust that Dolengyl was pleased to receive the bottle of wine, you delivered. Thank you again for all your help, ${PLAYER}.'
'I hope that cask was useful to you. You went through enough effort to get it.'
'Thank you for bringing me the bottle of wine from Brethilwen. If you are down that way again, please thank her for me.'

The Elf-refuge of Duillond lies on the north road by the river.
Brethilwen has asked you to deliver a bottle of last year's vintage to her friend Dolengyl.
Grape clusters picked from vines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'By this time of the year, most of the grapes have been picked and the wine already bottled. This was a very generous season, however, and many of the vines are still laden with grapes. I would welcome your assistance. Wine-making is not easy work, but performing this task will certainly add to your appreciation of the wine you drink.
'Traverse the road north from Celondim towards Duillond and turn onto the path that follows the tributary stream west, just across the bridge. Limael's vineyard is in a small valley there.
'Pick the remaining grapes from the vines that grow around the lake and bring them to me, and I shall instruct you on the intricacies of wine-making.'
'Very good, ${PLAYER}. Years from now, your efforts today will bring great joy to many. Hard work brings satisfaction, not just in wine-making but in all things.'
'Six clusters of grapes from this season's ripe vines should be enough. Any less than that, and I could not in good conscience bottle them.'
Pick the grape clusters from the vines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the grapes to Brethilwen
Gleaning the Field
Brethilwen, the Master-vintner of Celondim, believes there are enough grapes left on the vine for one last cask of wine.
'Six large clusters of grapes from this season's ripe vines should be enough. Any less than that, and I could not in good conscience bottle them.'

Limael's vineyard is across the stream, north-west of Celondim. The vines grow around a lake in a sheltered valley.
Brethilwen has asked you to pick the remaining grapes from Limael's vineyard.

Brethilwen is in Celondim, south-east of Limael's vineyard.
You should return to Brethilwen with your harvest.
Collected wine-flasks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'My friend, I wonder if I can ask you to undertake a task for me? It is bad enough that the goblins despoil Limael's Vineyard, but recently a party of the wretched creatures broke into an old wine-cellar and stole a number of flasks of a rare and ancient vintage.
'No doubt the evil creatures have already drunk or destroyed most of the wine, but if you can recover any of the bottles from the goblins in this area, I would be deeply in your debt.
'You can find the goblins throughout Limael's Vineyard to the north-west. I would not venture beyond into the Rath Teraig, however, as the goblins there are rather more dangerous.'
'Ah very good! You have done all that I could ask. Thank you for your efforts. Those wicked creatures will learn better than to raid my wine-cellars in the future!'
'Alas, I suppose all the wine is gone by now. But perhaps you can return to the field and continue your search?'
Bring the wine-flasks back to Brethilwen
Collect wine-flasks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Rare Vintage
Goblins stole a rare wine from the Elves of Celondim.

There are goblins throughout Limael's Vineyard, north-west of Celondim. Brethilwen is at her winery in Celondim, south-east of Limael's Vineyard.
Brethilwen has asked you to recover wine flasks of a rare and ancient vintage from the goblins who stole them.

'I have been thinking, ${PLAYER}. After all the trouble with Starkath over the bow, I don't believe I am worthy of it...especially since I could not even hold onto it.
'Please go back to Penglir and explain why I can't accept his bow. He may still be at Duillond to the south of Gondamon.
'I am a disappointment to my own folk and to the honour of Penglir's gift.'
'He feels unworthy? Did Celairant think that I gave my bow to him upon a whim? I did not give that bow idly to the first Man I met!'
Someone Worthy
After allowing Starkath to take the bow from him, Celairant is now certain that he is not worthy of the Elvish weapon.
'I am sure I do not deserve the bow. Please take it back to Penglir at the Elf-refuge.'

Penglir is at Duillond, south-east of Gondamon.
Celairant asked you to return to Penglir at Duillond and explain why he feels unworthy to bear the bow, having lost it once already to the dwarf-brigand Starkath.
You found Elvellon , the Elf-sword

'Celairant bears the blood of the Rangers of the North, and the name of a great hero is amongst his forebears, a Man I was proud to call my friend and companion. Perhaps Celairant is young as Men count the years, but then all Men are young by my count.
'In ages past, I honoured my fallen companion with a sword placed at his grave amongst the mounds of the Edain. It may be that the sword can yet be found in that place. It bears the motto Elvellon, or Elf-friend in the tongue of Men. Perhaps if you find the sword, that will convince young Celairant not to spurn my gift.'

'What is this? Surely not another gift? Nay, this is something else, is it not? What is the significance of this old sword?
'This is the sword of my ancestor? You say he was a friend and companion of Penglir? Now I understand. He gave me the bow in honour of my great-grandfather.
'What? You think the gift was made to me, not to my forebear? Well, it may be you are right, despite all. It will be a challenge to live up to those bygone glories, but perhaps someday I will be able to wield the bow without shame.'
'Oh, I wish I was worthy of Penglir's gift but I am just a fool, barely able to take care of myself much less such a glorious work of Elf-craft.'
Bring the Elf-sword to Celairant
Find Elvellon, the Elf-sword
The Elf-sword
After allowing Starkath to take the bow from him, Celairant is now certain that he is not worthy of the Elvish weapon.
'Find Elvellon and give it to Celairant with my blessings.'
'Thank you for your help. I will do my best to live up to Penglir's legacy and to the deeds of my great-grandfather.'
'Ah, ${PLAYER}, I have much to live up to. I can only hope to prove myself worthy one day.'
'He understands the meaning of my gift? Well, perhaps not, but at least he understands it was not given lightly.'
'I am certain that young Celairant will one day prove his worth.'

The sword Elvellon can be found at a grave marker amongst the mounds of the Edain, north-east of Gondamon. Celairant is at the hunter's lodge, west of Kheledûl.
Penglir has asked you to retrieve a sword which he placed by his companion's grave long ago and take it to Celairant.
You have recovered the stolen bow

'An Elf named Penglir gave me this beautiful bow but I've gone and lost it! Or more to the point, it was stolen from me. The Rangers make a point to stay out of the feud between the Longbeards and the Dourhands, so I was not expecting to be waylaid by brigands out of Kheledûl!'
'They overpowered me as I was looking for a good place to practice outside the town and stole Penglir's bow! The dwarves and Starkath, their leader, skulk near the walls of Kheledûl.
'I knew I wasn't worthy to deserve such a rich gift. I'm a failure...an embarassment to Langlas and to the Rangers. So hapless am I that I dare not fight Starkath. Can you go forth and take the bow back from him?'

'You recovered the bow from Starkath? You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}! I have not much but my name, so my name is precious to me. I could not have lived with the shame of dishonouring Penglir's princely gift.'
'Please, recover Penglir's bow from Starkath!'
Bring the bow to Celairant
Collect the stolen bow
A Remarkable Bow

While on his way to Duillond, an Elf named Penglir stopped at the hunters' lodge and gave his bow to the young Ranger Celairant. Celairant accepted the gift, but feels unworthy to own such a thing of beauty.
'The bow must be returned to Celairant.'

Starkath can be found outside the walls of Kheledûl. Celairant is at Thrasi's lodge, west of Kheledûl.
Celairant told you that his bow was stolen at sword-point by a Dourhand named Starkath and his minions. He has asked you to hunt down Starkath and recover the bow.
Defeated wights (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The spider threat should be lessened now that you have intervened, but I am afraid there is a worse problem still.
'Eastern Haudh Lin is home to some ancient burial mounds of the Edain, the Men who lived here in a past age. We have received reports of evil wights stalking these barrows and mounds. Such creatures are mere corpses animated by fell spirits, not the relicts of the spirits of Men. As such, they are irredeemably evil, and it is our duty to exterminate them without compunction. I do not know why these creatures are abroad in these dark days, but I suspect some working of the Enemy.
'Be that as it may, I ask you to destroy the bodies of these evil creatures, and send their spirits back to the Shadow from whence they came.'
'Well done, ${PLAYER}. The Enemy may raise more wights from the bones of the fallen, and when they do it will be our duty to send them back to their ancient graves.'
Defeat wights (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Deathly Task
Eastern Haudh Lin suffers from a worse threat than spiders; dread wights stalk the ancient mounds of the Edain, animated by evil fell spirits.
'The wights are some working of the Enemy and must be destroyed.'

Wights can be found amongst the mounds and barrows of the Edain, in eastern Haudh Lin.
Laergil has asked you to destroy the evil wights of Haudh Lin.

Laergil waits on the pier in the port of Celondim, south of Haudh Lin.

'This land has been sullied before by the dwarves and their keep on the hill and more recently by half-orcs and crebain. Now wicked spiders have entered the land, slaughtering the wildlife and endangering travellers.
'Thankfully, these evil creatures have so far only been found in the furthest northeast reaches of Haudh Lin, but these lands would be better for their absence.
'Seek out the evil spiders and drive them from their lairs in Haudh Lin.'
'Your help is most appreciated, ${PLAYER}. This blight of spiders might have spread throughout Ered Luin. Thank you.'

'If you know a scholar of some skill, I would appreciate any minor woodworking-lore you might be able to acquire.
'Thank you for your assistance. I have one or two small relics I can give to you for your trouble.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, this minor woodworking-lore is just what I had in mind. I will spend some time in contemplation of it to see if there are any lessons I can draw from within its pages. Take these small items with my gratitude.'

'These will serve wonderfully well, my friend. I thank you for them and will resume my practice at once!
'I hope these coins and materials are of use to you.'
