'Have you already been to the Michel Delving Craft-fair? You should definitely go, if you haven't already! There's a workbench, a forge, and even an oven just waiting to be used!
'If you think you have crafting in your heart, you should visit my friend Emerald Borings at the Craft-fair -- she's always happy to help someone get started making useful and pretty things.
'Pass east through Little Delving, and then follow the path south into Michel Delving. Take the south-west path from the statue of Marcho and Blanco in the town centre, and pass the stables on your right. Take the next left turn to reach the Craft Fair. Emerald will be happy to help you out!'

'Alf sent you to me? Good, good! We need more good folk with an interest in making useful and pretty things! Speak with the Mistress of Apprentices, and she can help you choose a vocation in which to specialize. A vocation is a bundle of three crafting professions with overlapping skills -- choose your vocation with care, because you will expend a great deal of time and energy improving your skill with the professions under its purview!
'Once the Mistress of Apprentices has welcomed you to your chosen vocation, be sure to speak with a Supplier who can sell you the tools of your trade -- every Profession has its own tools, so be not over-shy with your coinpurse! The novices will be happy to sell you any recipes you might wish to have, though I can tell you now that you will already know how to make a thing or two.
'Equip the crafting tools you plan on using and find an appropriate facility -- Michel Delving has a forge, workbench, and oven available for your use -- and begin practising your skills! You will advance in your chosen professions as you practice and seek out the teachings of others in the field. I hope you will become a skilled craftsman, ${PLAYER}, and that it will bring profit to you and to the Shire! I will give you a few coins to get you started. Use them wisely, and consider them an investment in your future as a skilled craftsman!'
Michel Delving Craft-fair
Alf Goodcliff thinks you could be a craftsman of some skill and suggested you visit his friend Emerald Borings at the Craft-fair on the south side of Michel Delving.

'Pass east through Little Delving, and then follow the path south into Michel Delving. Take the south-west path from the statue of Marcho and Blanco in the town centre and pass the stables on your right. Take the next left turn to reach the Craft-fair.
'Emerald will be happy to help you out!'
'The Michel Delving Craft-fair is full of useful facilities for craftsmen.'
'The Craft-fair is on the south side of Michel Delving.'
'The Mistress of Apprentices can help you choose a crafting vocation.'
'Don't forget to buy needed tools from the Provisioner!'

Alf Goodcliff suggested you speak with his friend Emerald Borings if you are interested in pursuing a crafting vocation.

'You did a fine job with that steed. It looks like the horse trusted you well enough. You also made it back more quickly than I expected. Men in my country...they would not believe a ${RACE} such as yourself could have done it so quickly!
'Now that you have proven that you can handle a steed I have another task for you...it will teach you endurance and holding your mount to its course. There is a stable-master in the land of the holbytla away to the west -- Michel Delving I believe they call it. The stable-master there is in need of a fresh Chestnut steed as well. Bring him his horse, and you will prove that you can hold to your saddle on a long journey!
'Hurry now! You have a long ride ahead of you. When you return, we shall see about continuing your training.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Clicking on the 'Mounted' induction bar gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>
'You returned! I thought you might have been thrown from the saddle or lost. Your determination is strong...I have no doubt that you will make a fine rider.'
Take a fresh Chestnut steed to the stable-master in Michel Delving
Fresh Steed for Michel Delving
Éogar, the owner of Hengstacer, has asked for your help delivering a fresh steed to Michel Delving.
'Now that the steed has arrived I can finally sit down for a proper meal.'

The stable-master can be found in Michel Delving in the Shire, far to the west of Bree.
Éogar has asked that you ride a fresh steed out to the stable-master in Michel Delving.

'Hello there! You wouldn't mind helping me out with a game of Hiders and Seekers, would you? You see, my friends Daisy and Polo have convinced me to play, even though they always hide in the same places! It isn't nearly as much fun when your friends are so unimaginative, as I'm sure you realize.
'It would be fantastic if you could round them up for me. I'll give you a coin or two if you help me out, but I don't know how many more times I can pretend to be surprised that Daisy is hiding in the bushes next to Peony Grubb's home, or that Polo is crouched behind the carved statue of Marcho and Blanco.
'You'll find the statue carved on a large tree stump just south of here, and I'm sure that Polo Brockhouse is hiding right by it. South-east of the statue, there's a small hill with several hobbit-houses behind a wooden fence -- Daisy thinks the bushes to the right of Peony Grubb's house are a clever place to hide. Find my friends for me, and next time I'll try and tell them I don't feel like playing Hiders and Seekers!'

'Rollo sent you to look for me? Oh, he always gives up so easily. I'm not sure that you can do that in a game of Hiders and Seekers -- I'm pretty sure it's against the rules. If you don't find the Hiders yourself, you aren't much of a Seeker, are you?
'Anyway, I'll wait here until Rollo finds everyone else. This is a great hiding spot, isn't it?'

'Ha ha! Rollo sent you to find me, did he? It always takes him so long to find us. Just between you and me, I don't think he's very good at Hiders and Seekers.
'I'll stay here and think about where I can hide for our next game!'

'Thanks for your help, ${PLAYER}! Hiders and Seekers is not much fun when your friends always hide in the same places. I don't think it's a game they're very good at.
'Wait a minute...you say that Daisy mentioned hiding until I found \qeveryone else?\q That's strange. I thought Polo was the only other hobbit I was supposed to be looking for! They mentioned maybe getting Odo to play, but I didn't think they'd actually do it....
'Here are the coins I promised you, but it sounds like your work as Seeker might not be done yet, ${PLAYER}!'
Find Polo Brockhouse
Find Daisy Brockhouse
Hiders and Seekers
Rollo Newbuck has been asked to play Hiders and Seekers with his friends, Daisy and Polo Brockhouse, but their unimaginative hiding places have made him lose interest in the game.
'I'll stay here until Rollo has found everyone else. I'm not convinced that you're allowed to designate someone else to be Seeker, but I guess I'll allow it since Rollo isn't very good at the game.'

'You found Daisy already? That's very good! She always chooses good hiding-places, like up near Peony Grubb's home. That's a great spot, although it isn't as good as some of mine, like right here in the shadow of Marcho and Blanco!'
'Polo is probably hiding behind the carved statue of Marcho and Blanco to the south of here, and his sister Daisy is always hiding south-east of there, among the bushes next to Peony Grubb's home.'

Polo Brockhouse is hiding behind the carved wooden statue of Marcho and Blanco in the centre of Michel Delving. His sister Daisy is hiding south-east of the carving, in the bushes to the right of Peony Grubb's home.
Rollo Newbuck is playing Hiders and Seekers with his friends, but they always hide in the same places, and he is tired of pretending to be surprised every time he finds them.

Rollo Newbuck is north of the carved statue of Marcho and Blanco at the centre of Michel Delving, within the circle of hedges that surround Town Hole.
Rollo is waiting to hear that you found Polo and Daisy Brockhouse.
'Peony said I could hide here, so it's not like I'm trespassing.'
'I wish I was as good a Hider as Odo Pipes.'
'I first thought of this hiding-place when I was working at the Bird and Baby.'
'Most Seekers look at the ground, and don't think of hiding-places that are higher up!'
'Odo Pipes was a good barrel-roller. Not as good as me, but still pretty decent!'
'Patrons at the Bird and Baby drink a lot of beer. I'm kept busy rolling barrels out, that's for sure!'

'This is serious, ${PLAYER}. I thought I was only playing Hiders and Seekers with Polo and Daisy, but it sounds like they talked to Odo Pipes and convinced him to play as well. You'd think they might have mentioned that to me!
'At any rate, Odo has a reputation for being the best Hider in all the Shire -- at least as good as old Bilbo was in his day, or so it's said among folk in The Bird and Baby. I don't know if it's true, but I do know that, unlike Daisy and Polo, Odo Pipes is sure to have a capital hiding-place, the very best!
'I'll have more coins for you if you can find him, ${PLAYER}. He'll be hiding somewhere in Michel Delving, so don't wander too far. You might want to talk to Polo and Daisy again -- they might be able to tell you where he could be hiding.'

'You found me! Very well-done, very well-done indeed! Next time I'll need to choose a better hiding-place, I suppose. I thought this one was perfect!
'You should return to Rollo and tell him that he knows how to choose good Seekers!'

'You found Odo Pipes? Excellent! He was on top of The Bird and Baby Inn the whole time?
'He must have some Tookish blood in him. You'd never get me up there, I can tell you that!
'Here are the coins I promised you, ${PLAYER}, and take my thanks as well! If they ever get me to play Hiders and Seekers again, I'll be sure to let you know -- that way you can give me a stern talking-to and ask me what I was thinking!'
Find Odo Pipes
The Top Hiding-Place
Rollo Newbuck has learned that Odo Pipes is also playing Hiders and Seekers, but Rollo doesn't know where the hobbit is hiding.

'You and Rollo haven't found Odo Pipes yet? It doesn't surprise me -- he's always been the best Hider in the Shire, you know.
'I don't know where his favourite hiding-places are, though. He really likes to climb things -- trees, fences, buildings. If you're looking for Odo Pipes, you probably should be looking in the sky!'

'Odo Pipes used to work here in The Bird and Baby -- in fact, he and I were responsible for rolling out the barrels when they were called for, and rolling them back when they were emptied.
'One time, he helped me climb up onto the roof to fix a leak up there. That was a very rainy Spring, and the rain was like to flood us out if the hole wasn't patched up!
'He was a good fellow, that Odo. After awhile he decided he didn't want to roll barrels anymore, and he moved on. I'm not sure what he's up to these days.'
'Rollo is in the square outside Town Hole, within the encircling hedges. Let him know that you found my hiding-place, and he's sure to be impressed!'

'Odo Pipes is the best Hider in the Shire -- I don't mind telling you that he's even better at the game than I am!
'I don't know where he's hiding, but I do know that he worked for a while stacking barrels at the Bird and Baby, just to the north. Maybe he mentioned his favourite hiding-places to someone in there?'
'You need to find Odo Pipes for me, ${PLAYER} -- he's sure to have found a really great hiding-place somewhere in Michel Delving!'
'Maybe I'm just not cut out for Hiders and Seekers.'
'No one ever lets me be a Hider. I'm always stuck being Seeker!'
'This is a great hiding-place. No one ever thinks of looking here!'
'Marcho and Blanco may have found the Shire... but they'd never find me!'

Odo Pipes is hiding somewhere in Michel Delving.
Rollo Newbuck has sent you to find Odo Pipes, rumoured to be the best Hider in the Shire. Odo is hiding somewhere in Michel Delving. Rollo thinks that Daisy or Polo, in their usual hiding-places, might have some clue to Odo's location.

Rollo Newbuck is east of The Bird and Baby Inn, within the stone wall around Town Hole.

'You've got to help me, ${PLAYER}! While my wife was out, I went and ate the pie crust she had baked...I couldn't help myself! I know that if I had waited, it would be filled with some delicious filling and be even better, but I've always been partial to the way my wife bakes the crust.
'Do you know any cooks? I need a replacement pie crust, and fast! If my wife gets back and sees the crust missing, why...she might not make another!
'I'll give you some coins and, and... half a dozen eggs if you can do this for me, ${PLAYER} -- now, quickly! Go get me a pie crust! I might have some other things lying about that I can give you as well!'

'You've got the pie crust there? Excellent, superb, wonderful! Here, hand it over!
'Yes, this will do perfectly! My wife will never know the difference, and she'll go ahead with her plan to fill it with something delicious: fruit filling, meat filling, who knows what she'll choose? I can't wait! Here is the reward I promised you, and my thanks for your trouble.

'My Aunt Prunella is as reputable a lady as you could hope to meet, but I'm worried that she might have done something a little reckless and could now be in terrible trouble! She'd been listening to that Tunnelly lass, and before you could say \qgoblins-in-the-Shire?\q, she'd gone off to see the creatures for herself!
'I just don't know what I'd do if my dear old Aunt actually finds goblins. Could you go look for her? Rumour has it that there are goblins in the north-west Greenfields.
'Aunt Prunella had a pretty umbrella that she carried everywhere, even on sunny days, so if you see a goblin with an umbrella, well....'

'Good gracious me, it could be that I might have gotten ahead of myself. Well, it's good that the old lady is safe. I am terribly sorry for troubling you about this. Take these coins, and I'd appreciate it if you didn't go mentioning this to anyone.'

'Oh no! You found Aunt Prunella's umbrella! I was afraid that you might.
'My poor, old Auntie! She was a tough, old lady, but I used to visit her all the time. Once every few months, at least! She will be missed, by one and all, I just know it! Scary is poorer for her loss!'
'If you do find Aunt Prunella's umbrella by one of the goblins that sneaked into the Shire out by the Greenfields...well, that's not happy news at all!'
Find Aunt Prunella's Umbrella
Collect Prunella's Umbrella
Bring Prunella's umbrella to Fosco Boffin
The Fate of Prunella Boffin
Fosco Boffin in Scary is worried about his aunt, a reputable hobbit named Prunella.
'I suppose it doesn't pay to be too hasty. Lesson learned, okay?'
'Goblins are dangerous business, even if on this particular occasion Aunt Prunella was not in trouble.'

Goblins may be found in the north-west Greenfields. If one of them took Aunt Prunella's umbrella, it might be lying somewhere inside one of their camps.
You promised Fosco Boffin that you would look for his Aunt Prunella's umbrella. He fears that she ran afoul of goblins.

Fosco Boffin is in Scary, near the centre of town.
You promised Fosco Boffin that you would look for his Aunt Prunella's umbrella. He fears that she ran afoul of goblins.

Fosco Boffin is in Scary, near the centre of town.
Fosco was distressed by your recovery of his Aunt Prunella's umbrella; however, a neighbour informed him that she had actually been visiting her all day, and that Prunella had lost her umbrella earlier in the day. Fosco motions you over.
Defeated brigands (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'These strangers are a real problem hereabouts. I'm pretty sure they've been stealing food from the local farms, and it's just a matter of time before they cause worse trouble than that.
'That girl Violet probably went that way and found trouble, so I think you should deal with those ruffians. Maybe they'll take the hint and move back to wherever it is they came from.
'The ruffians -- brigands like as not -- are camped not far west of here. Their camp is on the heights of Narrowcleeve, south past a waterfall. It looks dangerous but you can ford the stream just before the cascade goes over the cliff.'

'I wish the Bounders had more hobbits. This sort of thing wouldn't happen if the Shire was guarded better in the first place.
'Well, no matter, here, please take these coins for your trouble.'
Defeat brigands (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Rousting Ruffians
Farmer Maggot's son Hammy is concerned about the continued presence of the ruffians west of his farm.

'Please try to drive off those ruffians for us. I hope it don't come to violence, but if it does, so be it. Their camp is at Narrowcleeve, west of this farm and on the far side of the waterfall. There should be a place where you can ford the stream not far from here.'
'Those brigands won't mess with the likes of us again!'
'Narrowcleeve would be a nice place to walk if it weren't for those brigands.'

The ruffians' camp is west of Bamfurlong. You must ford a stream at the top of a waterfall to enter the camp, which is set on the heights at Narrowcleeve.
Farmer Maggot's son Hammy has asked you to drive off the ruffians.

Bamfurlong is near the Brandywine River, south of Stock.
You have done as Hammy Maggot requested. You should return to him at Bamfurlong to tell him the news.
Defeated bats (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})

'The bats of the Old Forest have been a minor annoyance in the past, but of late they have grown very aggressive and even dangerous. They could become a plague in Buckland, so we need to reduce their numbers before that happens.
'There is a tunnel through the High Hay, north-east of here, beyond the Bounder camp.'
'Well done. Here's your fee.'
Defeat bats in the Old Forest (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Forest Bats
Hodric Bracegirdle needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.

There is a tunnel into the Old Forest, north-east of Brandy Hall, beyond the Bounders' training ground.
Hodric Bracegirdle has asked you to reduce the number of bats in the Old Forest.

Hodric Bracegirdle can be found near the entrance to Brandy Hall on the western side of the hill.
Hodric awaits word of your success.
Defeated bears (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})

'The bears of the Old Forest have always been dangerous, but in the past they were not very aggressive and could be avoided. Now they are roaming all over the place and may even come out of the forest to threaten Buckland if they aren't stopped.
'There is a tunnel through the High Hay, south-east of here, beyond the Bounder camp.'
'Well done. Here's your fee.'
Defeat bears in the Old Forest (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Forest Bears
Hodric Bracegirdle needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.

The bears can be found in the Old Forest, south-east of Brandy Hall. There is a tunnel into the Old Forest, north-east of Brandy Hall, beyond the Bounders' training ground.
Hodric Bracegirdle has asked you to help lessen the threat of bears.

Hodric Bracegirdle can be found near the entrance to Brandy Hall on the western side of the hill.
Hodric Bracegirdle has asked you to help end the threat of bears in the Old Forest.
Defeated spiders (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})

'Giant spiders are a menace to everyone, but there have until recently been only a few in the Old Forest. Now their webs can be found in many places, and we are worried that they may soon spread to endanger everyone.
'There is a tunnel through the High Hay, north-east of here, beyond the Bounder camp.'
'Good job. Here's your reward.'
Defeat spiders in the Old Forest (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Forest Spiders
Hodric Bracegirdle needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.

There is a tunnel into the Old Forest, north-east of Brandy Hall, beyond the Bounders' training ground.
Hodric Bracegirdle has asked for your help defending against spiders in the Old Forest.

Hodric Bracegirdle can be found near the entrance of Brandy Hall on the western side of the hill.
Hodric Bracegirdle awaits word of your success.
Defeated wolves (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})

'Wolves in the Old Forest have always been something of a threat to foresters and woodsmen, but they've recently become more dangerous and aggressive. We don't want them coming into Buckland, so it would be best to hunt them down now in the Old Forest itself.
'There is a tunnel through the High Hay, north-east of here, beyond the Bounder camp.'
'Well done. Please accept these coins.'
Defeat wolves in the Old Forest (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Forest Wolves
Hodric Bracegirdle needs your help reducing the threats from the Old Forest.

There is a tunnel into the Old Forest, north-east of Brandy Hall, beyond the Bounders' training ground.
Hodric Bracegirdle has asked you to help reduce the number of wolves in the Old Forest.

Hodric Bracegirdle can be found near the entrance to Brandy Hall, on the western side of the hill.
Hodric Bracegirdle awaits word of your success.

'Leecher Cartwell in Combe has been wasting his healing stores on any rabble or riff-raff that wander through his door. Now, he expects me to fill his stores! It will cost him more than a few pennies this time, I can tell you that!
'Travel over to Brandy Hall in Buckland and speak with a good-for-naught hobbit there by the name of Hodric Bracegirdle. Get a crate of that oily salve he makes and bring it back to me.
'That salve should satisfy the leech.'

'What's that? Oh, that villain Stoutthrush! He's been demanding one thing or another of me ever since I lost that wager to him.
'I suppose I can spare some salve. I'll have to make more soon or I'll run out.'
'Where have you been? Cartwell might have found another supply of salve by now.'
'Where is the salve? If the leecher finds another source of salve, I won't be able to get as high a price.'
Collect a crate of oily salve from Hodric Bracegirdle
Bring the crate of salve to Bruner Stoutthrush
Healing Stores
Leecher Cartwell has ordered some supplies from Bruner Stoutthrush, who has in turn run out of stock.
'Hodric Bracegirdle in Buckland you say? It will be a pleasure not to deal with Stoutthrush the next time I need my stores filled!'
'Ha! That salve will fetch a handsome price from Leecher Cartwell!'

Hodric Bracegirdle lives on the river side of Brandy Hall in Buckland.
The hobbit Hoderic Bracegirdle supplies Stoutthrush with the healing salve he sells to Leecher Cartwell.

Bruner Stoutthrush does business at the Combe-gate in Bree.
Hodric, not entirely happily, gave you the crate Bruner requested. You should bring it to Stoutthrush straight away.

'There's a pair of fine gentlemen, Mr. Larkspur and Mr. Hawkling, what have taken up residence at Adso Haybank's camp, along the Great East Road north of the Old Forest.
'Yes, sir, fine gentlemen indeed! Hunters of game, great and small. Last time they were through here, Mr. Hawkling asked me to procure them a bit of pipe-weed.
'If you'd be so kind, deliver this cask to them with all due haste. I'm sure Mr. Hawkling will tip you if you're quick about it.'
'So, that ill-favoured fellow, Stoutthrush, finally came through with our pipe-weed. Looks like I owe you for that wager, Larkspur!'
'Have you been to Bree lately? That good-for-naught, Stoutthrush, owes me a cask of pipeweed.'
Bring the pipe-weed to Roger Hawkling
Pipe-weed Delivery
Bruner Stoutthrush, a merchant in Bree, has asked you to deliver an order to two of his customers.

Roger Hawkling can be found at Adso Haybank's camp along the Great East Road, west of Bree, north of the Old Forest.
Stoutthrush wants you to bring the cask of pipe-weed to Roger Hawkling.
Collected stolen family heirlooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, what troubled times we live in. Brigands have been raiding people's homes in Archet, Staddle, and Combe. Deplorable! Some of the poor folk have made their way here to Bree and told me their sad tales.
'Now I'd like nothing more than to help them but I'm just not made for adventures. Why don't you track down these villains and bring the stolen family heirlooms to me. Then I can return them to the rightful owners, the poor wretches. Just think of the looks on their faces!
'I hear there are brigands encamped in the Yellow Tree Ruins, south of Staddle; but it may be that some others in the Chetwood are also carrying stolen items.'
'Ah, you've found them! That was a kind deed. Now, let's just hope that I can find the poor people from whom these treasured things were stolen.'
'What are you doing lazing about while people are suffering? Go find those poor people's things so that I can return them! I'd do it myself but I'm just not the sort for such adventures.'
Bring the heirlooms to Bruner Stoutthrush
Collect stolen family heirlooms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Family Treasures
Bruner Stoutthrush, a disreputable seeming gentleman from Bree, has decided to do a good deed for the refugees from the Blackwold attacks.

The brigands can be found in a large camp in the Yellow Tree Ruins, south of Staddle; but it may be that some others in the Chetwood also carry stolen items.
Whether as an act of beneficence or complete self-interest, Stoutthrush has asked you to collect stolen heirlooms from the brigands and bring them to him at Bree's Combe-gate.
'Winter will be upon us soon, and folk around here will need to keep warm. Hunt some bears north of the camp and bring me their pelts. Mind that you only bring me pelts large enough for the task.'
'Excellent quality! These will provide much warmth this winter.'
'You are not getting paid until you bring me ten pelts!'
Bring the bear pelts to Roger Hawkling
Bear Pelts
Roger Hawkling assists Adso Haybank by supplying the lodge with furs and meat.

The bears range north of Adso's camp.
Roger Hawkling has asked you to hunt some bears and bring him their pelts.

'The boars in this area grow particularly large and dangerous. Never know when they might attack someone. I want you to thin their numbers and bring me ten of their heads. If you could, try not to damage the heads...they are quite the delicacy, I hear.'
'Ah, a very fine job, to say the least!'
'You are not getting paid until you bring me ten heads!'
Deliver the boar heads to Roger Hawkling
Boar Heads
Roger Hawkling assists Adso Haybank by supplying the lodge with furs and meat.

Boars range the wilds around Adso's camp.
Roger wants you to thin the growing number of wild boars and bring him their heads. He understands they are quite a delicacy.
Collected wolf-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You there, we've a wolf problem which needs addressing. Some time ago, Adso bought a fine, fat milk-cow out of Buckland, but filthy wolves out of the Old Forest stole it, slaughtered it, and dragged it off.
'Hunt down the foul wolves in the northern part of the Old Forest. Bring me pelts as evidence of your work.'
'I won't take any old shabby pelt, mind you. I'll only accept the largest and most lustrous.'
'These are very fine, indeed! Oh yes, I believe I owe you a reward.'
'You are not getting paid until you bring me five pelts!'
Bring the wolf pelts to Roger Hawkling
Collect wolf-pelts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Roger Hawkling assists Adso Haybank by supplying the lodge with furs and meat.

There are wolves in the Old Forest.
Roger Hawkling has asked you to help repel the threat of wolves in the area, bringing him five pelts as evidence of your work.
'I've always said that old forester's as mad as the day is long!'

'All the things you've gathered for me are useless, rotten and ruined. Something queer is going on, what with the animals all upset and the Forest seeming, well, more awake than usual.
'There's a wise, old hobbit, a forester, who oft camps a ways into the Old Forest. Look for him beyond Old Muddyfoot's Hill, which you can find south-east of the Bonfire Glade. Maybe Gilly knows what's going on. I'd appreciate it if you'd talk to him...Gillemin Brandybuck, that's his name.
'I'm worried! We had to burn part of the forest when it got too uppity years back, but this is far worse than it was before. If the Bounders have to start another fire, they might destroy the whole Forest, and then where would we be?'

'Ah, so Toly Brockhouse sent you? Good. I've discovered something very odd happening here in the Old Forest, and you may be able to help!
'I found a strange glade to the south-east, infested with monstrous spiders. I've never seen the like before...almost makes me believe those stories about old Mad Baggins down Hobbiton way! Anyhow, they chased me almost all the way back to my old camp, and in my haste, I dropped my pack.
'Would you please follow the trail back to my camp to get my pack for me? It's near the Willow Glade, south-east of here, but the way is winding. Head south across the water, west into the woods, then look for a path that works its way east and south.'

'Ah good, thank you for that pack. There's an old knife in there I wouldn't care to lose, especially with all the animals acting queer, and all those spiders about.
'You saw them, didn't you, those spiders? This is strange. There've always been a few here and there about the Old Forest, but never so many, so big, and so bold!
'I don't doubt the cause of all the trouble in the Old Forest lies somewhere in that spider nest I found. I've never seen the like!'
'Please get my pack back from where I dropped it. It's not far to the south.'
Bring the pack to Gillemin Brandybuck
New Trouble in the Old Forest
Toly Brockhouse is disturbed by the fact that everything you brought him was spoiled. This, as well as the stirring of the forest creatures has upset him.
'I'd hate to think I'd lose my things to those awful spiders. If you could get my pack for me, I'd sure appreciate it. I think I lost it near my old camp, south-east of here.'
'Please, talk to Gilly Brandybuck for me.'
'Oh, we had parties like this when I was a girl.'
'I hear you're talking to that old forester lately. He's a strange one, going in and out of the old forest all the time.'
'That old forester's a bad influence on the youth! He's convinced that wood-cutter boy it's safe to go in to the forest.'
'That's my husband playing the lute. Isn't he talented? He was quite the catch when we were younger, yes he was.'
'I hear tell you went into the Old Forest to help the young wood-cutter. Very brave of you, ${NAME}. You won't find me setting foot in there!'
'I don't know about the Old Forest being haunted, that sounds like hogwash! But I sure wouldn't go running around in there.'
'The season is treating us very well. There'll be plenty of feasting this winter!'

Gillemin Brandybuck's camp is a distance to the south-east in the Old Forest, beyond Old Muddyfoot's Hill.
Toly Brockhouse asked you to seek the counsel of an old forester named Gillemin Brandybuck.

Gillemin Brandybuck's old camp lies to the south-east, but the way is winding. Head south across the water, west into the woods, then look for a path that works its way east and south.
You found the forester, but Gillemin's news is worse than Toly probably expects. Gillemin reports running into a glade full of monstrous spiders, which chased him away. He dropped his pack at his old campsite and has asked you to retrieve it.

Gillemin Brandybuck is encamped to the north-west, south-east of Old Muddyfoot's Hill.
You have recovered Gillemin's pack as he requested. Now you should return to him.
Lumber collected
Savoury Mushroom collected (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
You have collected a bucket of maple sap

'These are strange days! Most hobbits stay away from the Old Forest, but my living depends on it, and I've never had any problems...till now. The forest creatures have all gone strange. I swear the tree-roots themselves moved to trip me up, and now I've sprained my ankle!
'I still need to collect some mushrooms -- they grow in the west part of the forest, between the Bonfire Glade and Bald Hill. Also, please bring in some lumber from my seasoning pile. The pile is to the east past the Bonfire Glade and a little south. And I need some sap from the old maple on Bald Hill, east of the Bonfire Glade.
'I'll gladly split my fee with you! Here, take my bucket for the sap, and thank you kindly!'

'My thanks, friend, for all your...what's this? This sap, it's already gone bad! And my seasoned wood...it's rotted! And these mushrooms...they're poisonous! Friend, you can't be blamed, but all this...it's useless to me!'
'Please, I need those mushrooms, and the lumber and sap, too.'
Collect seasoned lumber
Collect a bucket of maple sap
Bring the collected materials to Toly Brockhouse
The Wood-cutter's Tale
The wood-cutter has sprained his ankle and is unable to finish his chores for the day. He swears that the Old Forest intentionally tripped him.
'Have you found everything yet?'

The mushrooms can be found in the western part of Old Forest, between the Bonfire Glade and Bald Hill. The wood can be collected from the wood-cutter's seasoning pile east of the Bonfire Glade and a little south. The sap can be collected from the old maple growing on Bald Hill, east of the Bonfire Glade.
Because Toly Brockhouse, the wood-cutter, has sprained his ankle, he has asked you to gather mushrooms, wood, and maple sap for him.

Toly Brockhouse awaits you at the entrance to the Old Forest, west of the Bonfire Glade.
You should return to Toly with the things you collected for him.

'Well now, as I said before, I think that nest of spiders I found has something to do with all the queerness stirred up in the Forest. But there are too many spiders for me to deal with myself, and the Bounders will only come with fire and axes.
'If you could make your way into the heart of that nest, maybe you can find out a little more. The spider nest is south across the Willow Glade.
'I was only able to make it to the outskirts of the nesting ground before the spiders chased me away, so you'll probably want to gather some friends.'

'My word! This is worse than I thought! I've seen the trees move, but never a tree that talks. I don't know anything about witches, but they say those Barrow-downs beyond the Old Forest are haunted . . . perhaps ghosts haunt the wood now too!
'I've heard rumour that there are -- or were -- great ones even among trees, wicked and bent, who rule the Old Forest like kings. If it's one of these that haunted that old oak, it's no wonder the Forest is disturbed!
'Maybe now that you've put the spirit to rest, the trees will go back to sleep and the animals will calm. Well done...well done, I say!'
Discover the source of the Forest's unrest
Haunted Forest
Gillemin Brandybuck believes the great spider nest he found is at the centre of the stirring of the Old Forest.
'I'd wager that spider nest has something to do with what's got the Forest all stirred up. You might want to take some friends and have a look!'

The spider nest lies near the Willow Glade, to the south of Gillemin's old camp.
Gillemin has asked you to gather some friends and investigate the spider nest he found.
The old forester awaits you at his new camp, south-east of Old Muddyfoot's Hill.

'The Age of the Elves is over, ${PLAYER}, and now the time has come for us to pass into the West. But ere we come at last to the Grey Havens beyond the land of the halflings, we wish to do what little we can to help against the Shadow that is once again rising in the East.
'Long ago, the Witch-king of Angmar sent many fell spirits out of Angmar and Rhudaur to turn the Barrow-downs into a place of terror, and we sense that they are again stirring. We fear that more of these spirits have come with the intent of increasing their master's horde in Bree-land. We would have you enter the Great Barrow and send these spirits back to their master. The spirits will likely be found behind a door displaying a skull.
'You will find a southward pass leading into the Barrow-downs east from here. Othrongroth, the Great Barrow, is in the southern end of that dread place. You should not enter Othrongroth alone, for it is a dark and dangerous place. Take those you can trust.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}; nevertheless, we shall sojourn here a short while longer to see that evil does not come to the simple folk of this land.'
Heading West
Three Elves are journeying to the Grey Havens and have stopped in Andrath, briefly sojourning in Bree-land to help cleanse the land of an ancient corruption before passing into the West.
'Go forth with the blessing of the Elves and drive forth the enemies of the Free Peoples from Othrongroth and restore the Barrow-downs to the peace it once knew!'
'The Shadow of Angmar has not been lifted fully from the Barrow-downs, but your efforts were not wholly in vain.'
'Welcome and well met, ${PLAYER}. May the light of Elebereth shine upon your path, no matter how dark it seems.'

There is a southward pass into the Barrow-downs, east of Adso's Camp. Othrongroth, the Great Barrow, is near the southern end of the Barrow-downs. The fell spirits can be found within Othrongroth behind a door displaying a skull.
As one last favour before leaving Middle-earth, Aradia and her companions would like to help cleanse the Shadow of Angmar from the Barrow-downs. She has asked you to enter Othrongroth and send the fell spirits which dwell there back to their master.

Aradia is near Adso's Camp, along the Great East Road, west of the entrance to the Barrow-downs.
You should return to Aradia with news of your success against the fell spirits of the Great Barrow.
You have rescued Maribell

'Oh, it's terrible! Blake, the brigand-captain who wanted the sword, came and told me he knew Nate was dead and that he knew I had something to do with it! I tried to tell him I didn't, that I would have another sword for him soon, but he wouldn't listen. He said he's taken my daughter, Maribell! If I don't give him another sword, and soon, he'll kill her!
'You must save her! Please! Get the sword from Lofar, then go to Blake's camp. It's in the Bree-fields, up north of Bree. I'm sure he'll release my daughter when he has the sword.'
'Please hurry! I don't know what I'll do if they harm her.'

'Oh, bless you! You've returned my daughter safe to me! I can't thank you enough. You've done so much for me, in more ways than you know!
'While you were away, I busied myself with Lofar's work. I had to do something to keep myself from being overcome with worry. No sooner had I finished the work, than Lofar came over to collect it. He seemed pleased with it -- even admitted that it came close to dwarf-work! He promised to send me more work in the future!
'${PLAYER}, you've saved my family and given me a hope for a brighter future. I can't thank you enough!'

'Those accursed brigands took Thistleway's daughter? This is bad. The sword isn't ready yet! And I know these types of fellows. They won't take \qno\q for an answer. They'll kill that girl!
'You'll have to mount a rescue and free Kenton's daughter! Hurry now! And gather friends, I fear you'll need them to face Blake!'

'Thank you, thank you! I filched the key a while ago, but I was too scared to use it. Now with you here, I can use it, and we can escape.
'Hopefuly we can get away before Blake notices!'
Find Maribell Thistleway
A Blade For a Life
While you were gathering the materials Kenton needed to finish his work for Lofar Ironband, the brigand Blake took his daughter captive.
'Have you gotten the sword from Lofar yet? Please hurry, my daughter's life is at stake!'
'The sword was not yet ready? Hurry, do as Lofar said. Make your way to the Brigand's Watch and free my daughter! Please hurry!'
'Don't dawdle here! Go to the Brigands-watch and rescue that poor girl! Hurry now!'

'Aye, good tidings! Glad no harm came to the lass. While you were away, I went over and collected the work from Kenton, and I must say that I think that Man has the hands of a Dwarf. The work was excellent quality, so much so that I think I'll get double for it. I told him he could expect more work from me in the future.
'Seems my kind heart led me to a good find. Thanks to you, that is.'
'I don't know what I would have done if Maribell had been hurt.'
'Thank you again for all you've done, friend!'
'Turns out having that sword stolen was a good thing, eh?'
'Who would have thought a Man could smith as well as a dwarf?'

Lofar can be found in the courtyard of the Stone Quarter in Bree, south-east of the West-gate.
Kenton Thistleway told you that Blake, the brigand-captain, will kill his daughter, unless he gets a new sword. Kenton has asked you to retrieve the sword from Lofar.

Blake's brigand camp is in the Bree-fields, north-west of Bree-town.
When you spoke with Lofar, he told you that the sword was not ready yet. He urged you to go to Blake's brigand camp and try to convince the brigand-captain not to harm Kenton's daughter. The sword will be ready soon. He also suggested you take friends in case there was trouble.

Kenton Thistleway resides among the smiths in Bree, not far from the West-gate.
Blake, the brigand-captain, took Kenton Thistleway's daughter, Maribell, captive. You rescued Maribell, who has returned to Bree. You should return to Kenton with news of your success.

'Hail, good ${PLAYER:lady[f]|fellow}! I was wondering if you could help me with a bit of a problem. It seems that no sooner did I set my latest blade out to cool, than someone stole it!
'I didn't see who made off with the sword, but I suspect it was one of those Man-smiths who live up near Bree's West-gate. Their craft is nothing like dwarf-craft, and likely their jealousy of my workmanship moved one of them to steal my blade.
'If I were to ask them about my blade, they would just ignore me. You though, by the look of you, you're a great warrior. If you were to ask them about my blade, they'll be honest with you. How about it, can you find my stolen blade?'
'Bah, I don't be needing to steal some dwarf-blade. People like my work...it's quality! You tell that Lofar that I didn't steal his fool sword and try to pass it off as my own!'

'What...a stolen sword? Stolen from a Dwarf? I don't know what you are talking about...Please, go away, I don't know anything about it...' Kenton mops his brow, nervously.
'Yes, yes, I admit it! I took it. Please don't tell the constable! Please! I did it to save my family! See, a brigand named Nate, he told me that he would hurt my family, unless I made a sword for their captain, Blake. But I didn't have the iron to forge one, and I was desperate to save my family, so I took the dwarf's sword!
'Nate said that before he gave the sword to Blake, he was going to test the blade against some boars around the abandoned graveyard north of Bree. If you find him there, maybe you can convince him to return Lofar's sword and leave my family alone. What do you say?'

'Well, of all the insulting things to say! Those dwarves think that no one can smith as well as them. Well, if being busy means you do quality work, then mine is quality.
'Go tell that fool dwarf that I didn't take his sword!'

'Don't be bothering me with such nonsense. Dwarves always looking down on us, claiming we're jealous. Now they going to start accusing us of stealing?
'Shoo, off with you. I don't have to take this sort of nuisance! I'll complain to the mayor, I will.'
Talk to the smiths
A Dwarf Made Blade
Lofar Ironband has told you that someone has stolen his newest blade. He has asked you to find out who stole it and return it to him as quickly as possible!

'Eh, have you found my sword yet? It was one of those Man-smith's that live by Bree's West-gate who took it, I know it. Go talk to them, seeing a warrior like yourself will frighten the thief into confessing!'

Most of the smiths of Bree dwell near the West-gate.
Lofar has told you that he thinks his latest blade was stolen by one of the Man-smiths. He thinks that a warrior, such as yourself, might intimidate the thief into confessing and returning the stolen blade.

'I know that I promised you the story of the Great Barrow, but your tale has not yet ended. We need to finish the final chapter.
'Take the key fragments to Kenton Thistleway. He resides on the west side of Bree, where most blacksmiths reside. He is close to the stables, I think, and has been down on his luck of late. He is an old friend and helping me will perhaps spark his passion again.
'Return to me after Kenton has reforged the key, and I will give you your last task.'

'Naerandir sent you, did he? A good man he is, and a wonderful storyteller too. I will gladly mend that key for you.
'These are tough times. So many blacksmiths out there. I was thinking of travelling north, but I hear that Trestlebridge is even worse off.
'Oh well, here you go.'
'I'm glad the Naerandir sent you, but you don't seem to have the key fragments with you. I'm sorry I can't help you.'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}! I am glad that your story continues. Lend me the key, and we will see if my faith in Kenton Thistleway was well-founded.
'It is as I hoped, beneath the soot and grime indeed lays that which we seek. This key will open the passageway to the lower chambers of the barrow wherein were housed many of the bravest fallen warriors of Cardolan now defiled by creatures of horror and dread.
'It is time that you take the key back into the Great Barrow and face the evil within.'
'Have you found the key?'
Bring the key fragments to Kenton Thistleway
Bring the soot-covered key to Naerandir
Forging Anew
Naerandir has told you he knows the story of the Great Barrow, but that the reality of the place as it exists now must be masked beneath the splendour of legend, lest cautious fear grows into terror.

Kenton Thistleway is in Blacksmith's Row, west of The Prancing Pony and south-west of the stables.
Naerandir told you to bring the key fragments to Kenton Thistleway, a blacksmith who has had a recent run of bad luck.

Return to Naerandir, who is outside The Prancing Pony in Bree.
Kenton Thistleway reforged the key to the Great Barrow. You should return to Naerandir for further instruction.
Found trinkets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Now I'll help that Kenton Thistleway by forging another sword, but with two conditions. First one is that if that brigand don't come around, looking for the sword, I get it back. Second, Thistleway gives me a hand and does some of the simpler work I've got piling up around here, while I forge the new blade.
'Here, take these things over to him to work on. The axe needs a new haft, the bellows need new leather, and the helm needs to be reshaped and reinforced. Take that over to Kenton and tell him if he gets it done, and I'm happy with the work, we'll call it even on the cost of the two swords.
'Now off with you, I've got to get to work on this new blade.'

'Bah, he wants iron straps? Kenton never has two coins to rub together...how's he going to pay me back? He ain't getting any of my straps.
'Here, take this old iron pot. He can make some straps out of that. Can't say that old Flint ain't kind-hearted.'

'Of course I'll do this work for the dwarf. Here, let me see what he has sent...' Kenton examines the items. 'All of these can be easily repaired, but I don't have the materials to do it. I hate to ask this, but could you help me gather what I need?
'For the helm, ask old Flint over there for a few iron straps for reinforcement. The bellows will need some new leather, and I'll wager that three flawless hides from the boars near Bree will suffice.
'For the axe haft, I need something splendid to set in it. In the past, I've salvaged small gems from old trinkets that I've found in the Barrow-downs. South-east of the entrance to the Barrow-downs are a few disturbed mounds. If you search through the debris, you might find some suitable trinkets.'
'You're back, what did Lofar say? Is he going to make another blade? I have to have something to give Blake if he comes around!'
'Oh, good you've returned! Here, give me those things! While you were away, something terrible happened! Please, I need your help!'
'Have you gathered the materials I need to finish the work for Lofar yet?'
Bring the items to repair to Kenton Thistleway
Search for trinkets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the collected materials to Kenton Thistleway
Forging a New Blade

Worried that the brigand Blake will come looking for his sword and, not finding it, will harm his family. Kenton Thistleway asked you to speak with Lofar Ironband about forging a new blade. Lofar reluctantly agreed, but wants something from Kenton in return.
'Hello, ${PLAYER}. Have you gathered all the materials I need yet? I can't begin repairing those items for Lofar until I have the materials.'
'What are you doing here? The blade for the new sword isn't ready yet. Off with you! Go talk to that Kenton Thistleway if you must bother someone.'
'Has Kenton completed that work yet? Go check on him!'

Kenton Thistleway can be found among the forges near Bree's West-gate.
Lofar Ironband has agreed to forge a new blade for Kenton Thistleway, but in exchange Lofar has given you three items to take to Kenton for him to repair. The dwarf said that if he likes Kenton's work, he will call it even on the cost of the two swords he is having to make.

Flint Oakhewer lives on the north-east corner of this street. Boars can be found all over on the outskirts of Bree-town. The relic-laden debris piles are near the mounds south-east of the entrance to the Barrow-downs.
Kenton can repair the items you brought from Lofar, but needs your help gathering the materials he needs. Speak to Flint Oakhewer about iron straps to repair the helm. For the bellows, gather three flawless boar hides. Finally, search the debris in the Barrow-downs for trinkets he can use to decorate the axe haft.

Kenton Thistleway can be found among the other smiths in Bree, down the road from the West-gate.
Kenton Thistleway sent you to gather materials he can use to finish his work for Lofar Ironband. You should return to Kenton at once with the materials you found.

'Now, I want to set matters right. I do! And maybe you can help do that?
'See, Nate said that before he gave the sword to Blake, he was going to test the blade against some boars around the abandoned graveyard north of Bree.
'If you find him there, maybe you can convince him to return Lofar's sword and leave my family alone. What do you say?'

As you kneel to examine Nate, it is clear that he is quite dead. His hand grasps the hilt of a sword, but the blade has snapped off and is nowhere to be found. You take the hilt from the dead brigand's hand.

'What? The blade broke, and Nate is dead? Oh this is bad...very, very bad. What if Blake comes looking for his sword? I won't have one to give him, and they'll do something terrible to my family! I need a sword to give him! If only I had another blade to give them.
'Wait, do you think Lofar would make another, if you explained the situation to him? My family is in danger! Could you please ask him?'
'Did you see Nate? Did you find the sword?'

'Another blade...he cannot be serious! I am already behind on other work, and now I must forge a new blade in time to fill the order this broken sword was meant for. \qTime is precious, don't give it away for nothing,\q my father used to say....'
Lofar cuts himself off, lost in thought for a moment, then continues. 'Actually lost my father to brigands a few years back...wouldn't wish that on anyone....
'Bah! Give me that hilt. I must be going soft. I'll do it to keep his family safe, but he's going to have to do something in exchange!'
'So, where's the hilt from my blade? At least I can salvage that for the new sword I have to make.'
Find Nate
Bring the broken hilt to Kenton Thistleway
Bring the broken hilt to Lofar Ironband
Getting the Blade Back
Threatened by Nate, a lackey of a brigand named Blake, that he must provide him a sword or his family would be harmed, Kenton Thistleway stole Lofar's blade.
'Have you found that Nate yet? He should be up north of Bree, near the abandoned graveyard. He has Lofar's sword. I just hope you can get it back...and that you put a stop to him.'
'Have you asked Lofar yet if he'll make another sword?'

Nate may be found near the boar-dens in the valley below the abandoned graveyard, north of Bree.
Kenton told you that Nate said he was going to test the sword on some boars who roam near the abandoned graveyard north of Bree. If you can find Nate there, perhaps you can get Lofar's sword back.

Kenton Thistleway can be found near Bree's West-gate.
You found the brigand Nate, who stole Lofar's blade. Unfortunately for him, the blade broke and he was slain by one of the boars he sought to kill. You should speak to Kenton Thistleway and let him know that Nate will no longer trouble his family.

Lofar Ironband can be found in the courtyard of the Stone-quarter in Bree, along the road south-east of the West-gate.
You found Nate dead and Lofar's sword broken. Now Kenton Thistleway is afraid that the brigand Blake will come looking for his sword and will harm Kenton's family when he finds that it does not exist. Kenton has asked you to convince Lofar Ironband to forge another that he can use to appease Blake.
Recovered Oddvarr's notes

'This is not good! In fact, it is downright terrible! All my work...gone! Just like that, quick as you please. Drat and double-drat!
'My notes are missing, and I'm absolutely certain that I placed them in my pack. There was a band of Tarkrîp Orcs from around Cirith Nur, west to northwest of here in the North Bree-fields, come sniffing around the ruins. That's why I left my pack behind in such a hurry.
'I'm in no shape to take on Orcs. I'm an explorer, not a warrior. Those notes mean everything to me. Could you please find them and return them to me?'

'Who?
'Oh what's the old dwarf up to these days? Exploring? He couldn't find his nose in his beard, that one! It's always something with Old Oddvarr. He's still trying to save face after being left out of the expedition to the Lonely Mountain. And that was what? Nearly four-score years ago!
'I'm sorry he dragged you into his delusions. He's never been good at much, save getting into trouble and then conniving others into getting him out of it.'

'Orcs! I hate Orcs. Why would they run off with my notes like that? I'll tell you why...just to get my beard in a snarl, I would say!
'Now that my notes are safe, I can continue my research. Lofar will be pleased to know that my work continues unabated.
'Say, why don't you pay old Ironband a visit and let him know of my progress? I'm sure he'd reward you for helping me.'
'Drat and double-drat! I don't have time to re-write all those notes. If I don't get my original notes back, then I'll have to go home empty-handed!'
Recover Oddvarr's notes from the Tarkrîp Orcs
Return Oddvarr's notes
Stolen Notes
Oddvarr's pack was recovered, but he is no better off. The notes he wrote down are missing, and he suspects that some Orcs made off with them.
'Lofar will be most impressed with my progress!'

Tarkrîp Orcs from around Cirith Nur, west to northwest of Oddvar in the North Bree-fields, have stolen Oddvar's precious notes.
Oddvarr's notes are missing, and he suspects the Tarkrîp Orcs ran off with them. One of the Orcs must have them, if you can only find which one.

Return to Oddvarr, south-east of Hengstacer.
You found Oddvarr's notes on the body of a slain Orc.

Lofar Ironband is in the town of Bree, in the Stone Quarter, down the road south from the West-gate stable-master.
Oddvarr told you to seek out Lofar and tell him that his research into the ruins is going well.
You see a pack
Pack retrieved

'My name's Oddvarr of the Blue Mountains, and I'm here in Bree-land on very important business. The only problem is, I misplaced my pack.
'Now, I'm to investigate the old dwarf-ruins that are rumoured to exist here. I'm sure there are important discoveries to be made, and I'm the one to do it! I'm a famous explorer, you see.
'But I digress! If you could help me find that pack, I would be indebted to you. You start looking over yonder north, and I'll search this area and to the south. If you find anything, meet me back here!'

'Ah, there's my old pack! Thank you so much for returning it to me. I would be in a world of hurt if my notes....
'What? My notes are missing! Curse those Orcs! They must have thought they were valuable.'
'Still haven't found anything? Me neither. Let's keep searching.'
Search the ruins for Oddvarr's pack
Retrieve Oddvarr's pack
Return Oddvarr's provisions
The Forgetful Dwarf
You met an old dwarf named Oddvarr who seems a bit absent-minded. He is an explorer of some renown...or at least he says he is.

Oddvarr asked you to search the ruins to the north.
Oddvarr set his pack down somewhere in the area and cannot seem to remember where.
You found Oddvarr's pack in some old ruins, north of where you spoke to Oddvarr.

Oddvarr is by the haystacks south of the ruins where you found the pack.
You found Oddvarr's pack containing his much-needed provisions.

'Hullo, there. If you're here about our horses, I'm afraid we don't loan them out to just anyone. These horses are built for speed, not heavy labour. In fact, that reminds of something.
'A dwarf came to the farm and requested some horses. Not sure what he intended to do with them, but by the looks of him he needed some pack animals. I told him that our horses weren't for hire, and he left in a huff.
'Seemed a bit peculiar, he did not seem quite right in the head. If you have time, perhaps you can check up on the old fellow. I saw him wander off to the ruins south-east of here.'
'Who's that there? Oh, hello! Sorry about that. These old eyes aren't what they used to be. Do you have time to talk? I could use some help.'
Horses for Hire
Cam Applewood works on a horse-farm called Hengstacer in the Bree-fields. He was approached by a dwarf who wanted to hire some horses for an expedition.
'If it's not out of your way, can you make sure that old dwarf isn't in trouble? He seemed a bit...queer in the head.'

The old dwarf was last seen walking to the old ruins to the south-east.
Cam asked you to check up on an old dwarf who wanted to explore the ruins near Hengstacer.

'I promised you a story, and your part is almost done. I have one final task for you, however.
'The Wight-lord himself must be met and dealt with. In times past, he was a great menace to Bree-land. We cannot let this happen again. Please put an end to his new reign.
'You will find him at the furthest end of the Great Barrow, the deepest halls. This key will open the way to him.'

'A better story I never could have composed. The tale of the hero, ${PLAYER}, who braved the greatest of challenges in Bree-land, who found glory and riches and fame.
'And so, my friend, you have lived the tale of the Great Barrow. A great evil has been banished, and terror will lay to rest behind the cloak of heroic deeds.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. Take this as a small reward.'
Evil's Final Chapter
Naerandir has told you he knows the story of the Great Barrow, but that the reality of the place as it exists now must be masked beneath the splendour of legend, lest cautious fear grows into terror.
'Ah, there goes ${PLAYER}, Hero of the Great Barrow!'
'A legend walks among us! Gather round and hear the tale of ${PLAYER}, Slayer of the Dead that Walk!'

The Ancient Wight-lord is at the furthest end of the Great Barrow, in the deepest halls. The Barrow-downs are south and a bit west of Bree.
Naerandir has tasked you with the destruction of the Wight-lord, who rules over the barrow-wights of Othrongroth, the Great Barrow. He suggests you take allies.

Naerandir is awaiting further word of your deeds outside of the Prancing Pony in Bree.
You should return to Naerandir and tell him that the Wight-lord is slain.
Key fragment found
Key fragment found

'Greetings, traveller! Do you wish to hear a tale? I know many, though one, perhaps, would be of greater interest to you. Have you heard of the Great Barrow? It lies at the heart of the Barrow-downs, a place of dread in Bree-land.
'But it was not always so and perhaps need not remain so. Evil things stir in the Downs and threaten to turn cautious fear into abject terror. Perhaps you might be interested in restoring the peace of the Downs? In return, I will tell you my tale.
'First, I need you to find the fragments of a key that opens the way into the deepest halls of the Great Barrow. Legend tells that the first fragment is guarded by two wights within a great maze of tombs, while the second is held by a gaunt-man, a terrible creature of the First Age. Both fragments are to be found within the Great Barrow. Take those you can trust, for the way is treacherous.'

'Impressive. You have now seen most of the tale I have to tell, though not all of it.
'To reach the heart of the tale, the key must be reforged.'
'Have you found the key fragments yet? They are in the Great Barrow itself. The first fragment is held by two wights, the second by a gaunt-man. Do not delay!'
Bring the key fragments to Naerandir
Find the left half of the key
Find the right half of the key
An Ancient Story of Evil
Naerandir has told you he knows the story of the Great Barrow, but that the reality of the place as it exists now must be masked beneath the splendour of legend, lest cautious fear grows into terror.

The Barrow-downs are south through the gate by the stables and south of Bree. The Great Barrow is at the heart of the Barrow-downs. The first key fragment is guarded by two wights in the Great Barrow maze. The second key fragment is held by a Gaunt-lord elsewhere in the Great Barrow. Naerandir is outside the Prancing Pony.
Naerandir has asked you to find two fragments of a key that opens the way into the deepest halls of the Great Barrow from a pair of wights and a creature called a gaunt-man. He recommended taking friends.
You found Amlach's corpse

'Oh, what a fine strong person you are. You remind me of my own poor sons. They've been gone for a few days now, and I've heard nary a word from them. My wits are nearly gone with worry!
'See, it started with my son, Malin. He was sure there were treasures out in the Barrow-downs for the taking and left seeking his fortune. After a few days passed, and he didn't come back, I sent his brother, Amlach, out after him, and I've not heard from him either!
'Would you venture to the Barrow-downs and find my boys? Amlach said he'd camp at The Dead Man's Perch on the eastern cliffs. Please go there and see if you can find Amlach. Be sure to go with trusted allies, for tales say that dead men wander those hills...'

'You have returned with Malin's journal! He never let it out of his sight. What evil fate has befallen my sons?
'Amlach...dead? Malin...you must return and search for Malin, ${PLAYER}!'
'The Barrow-downs are a dangerous place. I hope my sons are safe!'
Search The Dead Man's Perch for Amlach
Bring the journal to Addie Wheatley
Addie's Missing Sons
Addie Wheatley, a poor, old woman, is afraid for her sons, Amlach and Malin, who went into the Barrow-downs in search of treasure.

'I simply must know what happened to my sons. Amlach mentioned something about camping at The Dead Man's Perch on the eastern cliffs of the Barrow-downs, so maybe you can find them there. It can be dangerous out there and I don't recommend going it alone. Please hurry!'
'Perhaps Lorgan still lives!'
'Oh, my poor Amlach'

The Dead Man's Perch is located on the eastern cliffs of the Barrow-downs.
Addie Wheatley said that her son Amlach was going to set camp at The Dead Man's Perch and search for his brother Malin in the Barrow-downs. She suggested that you go with friends, as it could be dangerous.

Addie Wheatley stands near the Mud-gate in the south-west corner of Bree-town.
You've found Addie Wheatley's son, Amlach, dead at Dead Man's Perch. In his hand, you found that he was grasping a tattered journal. You should bring the journal back to Addie as she will want to know the fate of her sons.
Defeated brigands around Dogwood's Farm (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If you're not one of Sharkey's Men, as they call themselves, maybe you can help me out. Farmer Thornley's away on business, and I have no one else to turn to. All our hands have run off -- can't say I blame them -- but I'm not going to leave my land while I'm still breathing!
'Brigands have moved into the next farm over to the South, Dogwood's old place. They've stolen food, and I'm afraid that soon they're going to raid our farm here!
'You look the sort what might be able to teach those ruffians a thing or two, if you would be of a mind.'
'Thank you kindly, friend. You'll always be welcome at the Thornley's!'
Defeat brigands around Dogwood's Farm (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Thornley's Farm
Brigands referring to themselves as Sharkey's Men have taken over the old Dogwood farm, threatening the neighbouring steads.
'Please, get rid of those brigands, or no one will be safe around here!'
'How I hope Robb comes home soon! He's away on business up Trestlebridge way, but I hear that Orcs have moved into the area!'

The brigands occupy the old Dogwood farm, south of Thornley's.
Rose Thornley's husband is away, and she is afraid the brigands at the old Dogwood farm might try raiding her stead. She has asked you to help deter them.

Thornley's Farm is north of the old Dogwood place.
Rose Thornley awaits word of your success.
Robb Thornley has escaped
'Please, you must help me! These Orcs captured me while I was away from my farm on business. Please, help me escape!'
'I'm so thankful you rescued Robb! He's resting now, but he asked me to give you a reward. He's also asked for something more....'
Free Robb Thornley and escort him to safety.
Thornley's Rescue
Robb Thornley, a Bree-land farmer, has been captured by marauding Orcs.
'Robb is still recovering, but he's getting better, thank you very much!'
Robb Thornley has asked you to help him escape from the Orc camp.

Rose Thornley can be found at their farm in the Bree-fields, south of the Orc camp.
Robb Thornley's wife, Rose, should be told of her husband's escape from the Orcs.

'Robb is resting now and recovering nicely, thanks to you, but he asks another favour of you.
'He said he can't sleep, thinking about those accursed Orcs what ambushed him up the Greenway. When he was captured, he said a giant Orc came over to torment him from a camp to the west of the place he was being held, the one behind a wooden stockade. He says the other Orcs called this monster the Red Reaver. Robb says he must have his revenge on the Red Reaver and will be glad to give you what coins he can spare if you can put him to heel.
'Now, I can't say as I like all this bloodshed, and it sounds right dangerous to me, but if you'll show that horrible monster who tortured Robb a thing or two, I guess you surely do deserve a reward.'
'Robb will be so happy to hear you've done away with that beast of an Orc! And I'll thank you too for making the Greenway a safer place. Please accept this reward from both of us.'
Thornley's Revenge
You rescued Robb Thornley from the Orcs, battered and beaten, but he is not satisfied with rescue. He wants retribution.

The Red Reaver is in the Orc-stockade on the western side of the Greenway, north of Thornley's farm.
On behalf of her husband, Rose Thornley has offered you a reward if you would go to the stockade and slay the Red Reaver.

Thornley's farm is south along the Greenway from the Orc-stockade.
You should return to Thornley's farm at once to tell Rose of your victory and claim your reward.

'The tidings you have brought grieve me deeply, for Amlach was young and strong, and I loved him dearly. The only consolation in my grief is that he died in search of his brother whom he loved more than his fear of that dreadful place.
'If this journal is true, then Amlach still believed there was hope for his brother, though my heart fears the worst.
'Please ${PLAYER} gather companions and search out the barrow over the mire where Amlach heard his brother, bring my son back safe to me.'

'Both my sons are gone. The fools, oh the fools. They meant to find riches among the dead, but the dead kept their own and claimed my sons.
'Restless fools! Whatever shall I do now? Please, please leave me to my sorrow.'
As you begin to examine Malin, suddenly the body stirs. Malin is not dead!
Search for Malin
Find Malin

Your search for the missing sons found the remains of Amlach Wheatley clutching his brother's journal. The last cryptic entries seem to reveal that Amlach heard fell voices coming from the southern reaches of the Barrow-downs.
'What of Malin? Have you found any sign of Malin? Please, find him!'
'Leave me in peace!'
'My boys, my poor boys!'
'Oh, that they never had gone to those cursed lands!'

The journal you found seemed to indicate that Malin was taken to the southern Barrow-downs to a barrow overlooking an evil mire. Hopefully you will find him there, before whatever killed Amlach does the same to him!

Addie Wheatley stands near the Mud-gate in the south-west corner of Bree-town.
In your search of the Barrow-downs you found both of Addie's sons, Amlach and Malin, but far too late to be of any help to either. The foul creatures of the Barrow-downs had killed them both and took Malin's remains for their own. You should return to Addie Wheatley and tell her what has happened to her sons.

'Who are you and what do you want at Hengstacer, ${CLASS}? I have no doubt you have used the services of a stable-master...many of the skilled and trustworthy ones use my steeds to carry travellers such as you. The swiftest horses and ponies have all been foaled here in Hengstacer...there are none swifter of hoof west of the Mountains.
'From your raiment I can tell that you are a traveller...I know the hardships of the long roads between here and the Westfold but that is a story for a later time. If you are looking to learn how to ride a steed, I can teach you, but learning the skills is not an easy task. I have to deliver a fresh steed to the stable-master near the West-gate of Bree-town, but my grooms are busy with other tasks. You can start your training by bringing this Blonde Sorrel steed to the stable-master.
'After you deliver her safely, return to me, and we can discuss your training further.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Clicking on the 'Mounted' induction bar gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}, there are many more travellers down this way than the Bree-folk are used to. The stable-master there has almost been buried with requests for horses. If you are not too sore from that ride I have another task for you.'
Take a fresh Blonde Sorrel steed to the stable-master in Bree-town
Fresh Steed for Bree
Éogar, the owner of Hengstacer has asked for your help in delivering a fresh steed to Bree.
'Hurry on back to Hengstacer and thank Éogar for the fresh Steed!'

The stable-master can be found near the West-gate in Bree-town, south of Hengstacer.
Éogar has asked that you ride a fresh steed out to the stable-master in Bree-town.

Éogar, son of Hadorgar, is located at Hengstacer, north of Bree.
Return to Éogar and inform him that you delivered the horse to the Bree stable-master.

'There is one last task I would have you do before I ask you to prove your true quality.
'The stable-master at the dwarf-mines of Othrikar is an old friend of mine. We met along the road when I left the Riddermark after the king's health failed. I had promised I would send him out a fresh steed as soon as I could find a spare rider. I think you now have skill enough to lead your mount through greater perils than the lands of the holbytla. I am a man of my word and this Bay steed must be sent out at once. Before I can give you your final test, I will need you to travel into the North Downs and deliver it.
'Be careful...the road is long, and there are more dangers than loose stones and roots hidden in the hills of the North Downs.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Clicking on the 'Mounted' induction bar gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>
'Well done, ${PLAYER}, that was the last of the horses that I needed to deliver. I hope you did not encounter many difficulties on your journey.'
Take a fresh Bay steed to the stable-master in Othrikar
Fresh Steed for Othrikar
Éogar, the owner of Hengstacer, has asked for your help delivering a fresh steed to Othrikar.
'You're a fine rider to make it all this way so quickly, hurry back to Éogar with my thanks.'

The stable-master is at the dwarf-mines of Othrikar in the North Downs, far to the north and east of Bree-land.
Éogar has asked that you ride a fresh steed out to the stable-master in Othrikar.

Éogar, son of Hadorgar, is located at Hengstacer north of Bree.
You should return to Éogar and inform him that you delivered the horse to the Othrikar stable-master.

Éogar is at Hengstacer, north of Bree-town.
You have completed the course and should now speak with Éogar.

'You have my thanks for delivering those steeds. I believe you have learned a great deal about handling yourself in the saddle.
'I have a course that I ride to clear my head and uncloud my thoughts...few have completed it besides myself. Around Hengstacer, I have placed twelve gates. My farmhand Cam was able to complete the course in a little over two minutes...if you can complete the course faster than he has, I will count you a skilled rider. Simply ride through each of the gates on your mount before racing off to the next one. Be careful not to miss any gates! You will have to start over if you run out of time, and be aware that I have a number of jumps and water pits along the trail.
'When you are ready to start, you can use the Bloodbay steeds. I will start the count as soon as you mount up, so be ready.'
<rgb=#FFFF00>Clicking on the 'Mounted' induction bar gives you the option to dismount your steed but will also cancel the quest.</rgb>

'Well done! You possess more skill than I first guessed. I will now explain to you in detail some of the finer points of tending to your steed and controlling her.
'You should now be able to handle a horse on your own, ${PLAYER}.'
Mount your Bloodbay steed and race to the first gate
Race to the second gate
Race to the third gate
Race to the fourth gate
Race to the fifth gate
Race to the sixth gate
Race to the seventh gate
Race to the eighth gate
Race to the ninth gate
Proving Your Quality
Éogar, satisfied with your work for him, is ready to complete your training.
Race to the tenth gate
Race to the eleventh gate
Race to the final gate

'Hello there! Are you here to help out Éogar? If you're looking for work to do around the farm, I could use your help. I need some assistance tracking down some of the ingredients for my famous snapper-soup.
'My soup is made with the meat of the snapper-turtle that lives in the lake to the east of Hengstacer. I usually send one of the hands to fetch me the meat, but they have been so busy, I would feel awful making them hunt down their dinner however slow it may be. I could also use more snapper-shells to make soup-bowls. Better not to waste anything, I always say.
'Hurry along now and fetch the snapper-shells and meat...the farmhands get awful hungry after a hard day of tending the horses, and I would hate to make them wait.'
'Ah! You were able to find the shells and the meat. Wonderful! I will get started on my soup right away.'
'Have you found enough snapper-shells and meat? The southern Meluinen can be found to the north and east of the farm.'
Bring the snapper-shells and meat to Emma Rosethorn
Snapper Soup
Emma Rosethorn has asked for your assistance hunting snapper-turtles for their shells and meat for her famous snapper soup.
Snapper-turtles can be found on the islands and along the shore of Nen Harn, to the east of Hengstacer.
Collected amethyst ring

'Are you a jeweller? Do you know one? I really need the services of a jeweller, for I have lost my wedding ring, and I need a replacement before my husband Barton gets back from the Forsaken Inn!
'I don't know where it's gone, but it must have just slipped off my finger. If you can bring me an amethyst ring to replace it, I'd pay you for your trouble!
'Don't tell Barton I lost the ring! I can't believe I could be so careless!'

'Thank you so much, ${PLAYER}! This ring looks exactly like the ring I lost, and Barton will never know the difference!
'Take these coins and other small items, please! You've really helped me out!'
'If you can get a jeweller to make me an amethyst ring to replace my wedding ring, I'd really appreciate it, ${PLAYER}!'
Bring amethyst ring to Verity Tyne
Collect amethyst ring
Verity Tyne Has Lost Her Ring
Verity Tyne has lost the amethyst ring given to her by her husband Barton, and she is beside herself with worry that he will find out.
'You've been a great help, ${PLAYER}!'
'Don't tell Barton I lost my wedding ring!'

Verity Tyne is in the Crafting Hall in Bree.
Verity Tyne has asked for you to find a jeweller willing to make her an amethyst ring to replace the wedding ring she lost.

'You've been a big help to me, ${PLAYER}. Something about you tells me you could be a great help to many. If you are looking to further your charitable nature, you may want to speak with Second-watcher Heathstraw in Bree-town.
'Heathstraw is very much in the know of problems facing Bree. What with the refugees coming from the south and all the whispers of the rising dark, I think he's got a fair share of details to keep track of, poor fellow.
'You can find him through the Staddle-gate of Bree standing near the Boar Fountain in the Market Square.'

'Lolo? Used to come here often, he did. Good stout little fellow, good barker and good seller he is. Strange for a Hobbit it's true, but then again they say that most Hobbits living 'round here is queer.
'His information is correct though, Bree's seen its share of new blood recently, and not all have been of your caliber.'
He offers a wry smile.
'If you need work, I am certain that I can find you something.'
Into Bree

Lolo Wendingway mentioned that Bree-town is aflutter with rumours of shadows growing and refugees pouring in from the south. He told you to seek out Second-watcher Heathstraw if you were looking to continue your assistance of Bree-land.

Second-watcher Heathstraw can be found near the Boar Fountain in the centre of the Market Square in Bree-town.
Lolo Wendingway mentioned that Second-watcher Heathstraw may have some knowledge of people needing things done throughout Bree.

'You see the watchers and I have been stationed in Staddle for only a short time to see to the defence of the Little Folk here. What with all the trouble we've heard Archet and Combe having, it seemed a wise thing to defend Staddle, especially since its crops feed much of Bree-land!
'My superior, Second-watcher Heathstraw, should know of our victories and that Staddle appears to be safe, at least for the moment. I dare not leave my post, though, so could I ask you to bring my report on to Second-watcher Heathstraw in Bree-town? He will probably be near the Boar Fountain. Just head north up the road towards Combe and turn left at the signpost.'

'You bring word from the watchers in Staddle? Very good, very good. I'll take a look at that report, if you please.
'Ah, you bring good tidings! Goblins were a most unexpected threat, but it seems you dealt with them most expediently. And a good thing too...my men are spread too thinly to defend against all the dangers that have been rising up lately.
'You have my thanks again. Perhaps you may find work here in Bree as well.'
Bring Redweed's report to Second-watcher Heathstraw
Report From Staddle
Watcher Redweed would like word of your victory against the goblins carried to Second-watcher Heathstraw of Bree.
