'Second-watcher Heathstraw should be at the Boar Fountain in Bree-town, a short way north and west up the road. He needs to see my report sooner rather than later.'

Second-watcher Heathstraw is at the Boar Fountain in Bree, north and west of Staddle.
Watcher Redweed has asked you to deliver his message to Second-watcher Heathstraw.
Collected bronze buckler
Collected bronze scale armour

'Have you ever seen such a disappointment, friend ${CLASS}? The Men of this town are wearing armour of such low quality, I'm surprised they can come out in the daylight without embarrassment!
'If Bree-town is attacked, these guards could not hope to prevail. They are badly in need of better armour.
'If you know a metalsmith of any skill, impose upon him for the making of bronze scale-armour and a bronze buckler. It might not be much, but it's a start. Bring them to me and perhaps we will be able to turn these guards into a fighting force after all!'

'These will do nicely, ${PLAYER}. We will surely get this town's guards into shape with equipment like this!
'Here are some coins and other materials as a sign of my appreciation.'
'Have you not found a metalsmith able to pound some bronze scale armour and a bronze buckler yet?'
Bring bronze scale armour and a bronze buckler to Osur Stouthammer
Collect bronze buckler
Collect bronze scale armour
Bronze for Bree-town
Osur Stouthammer is concerned by what he feels to be the sad state of the armour worn by the guards of the town of Bree and wants to ease the situation.
'You've done well for these people, as ill-equipped as they were!'
'It always pays to know a good metalsmith. Never forget that!'

Osur Stouthammer is in the crafting hall near the Boar Fountain in the town of Bree.
Osur Stouthammer is concerned by the low quality of the armour worn by the guards of the town of Bree and wants you to find a metalsmith willing to make some bronze armour and a bronze buckler he can give to the defenders.

'Gammy Boggs, one of the older Hobbits here in Staddle keeps tabs on all the Hobbits on the farms east of the town centre. If you find yourself on the road east, look to the north at the second farm and you'll find Gammy looking out over the rolling pipeweed farms.
'She's always got something to say to passers-by and likely will want something done.'

'Redweed is such a good constable, always has a moment for Gammy, he does. I've been here since I was a little Hobbit, through my tweens and on now into my older years. Seen a good crop of Hobbit grown, and seen more wander into the hill overlooking Bree or down on to the Buckland or the Shire.
'Staddle is my home and I shall not leave any time.
'I know all the Hobbits here, who has the long hair, curly hair, even the little blond Hobbit; how curious I said when I seen him!
'Listen to me, prattling on.'
Gammy Boggs

Watcher Redweed mentioned that one of the older Hobbits, Gammy Boggs, always bends his ear about the goings-on of the farms of Staddle east of the town centre. She might know a thing or two that needs doing out near the farms.
Gammy Boggs lives on the second farm north of the road east from the centre of Staddle.

'Staddle is a tranquil place, or normally so. Recently however, the guards and constables have been fearful of the Midgewater Marsh and the tall-folk moving into ruins in the south.
'If you continue following the road to the south, you'll find Staddle centre. Talk to Watcher Redweed there and tell them that I sent you on to help!'

'Hullo there! You've come from Lolo, have you?
'You've come to the right place then friend. There is much happening around Staddle that needs attention and there are too few guards and constables to reach them all.'
On to Staddle
Lolo Wendingway mentioned that the people of Staddle are dealing with some peculiar goings-on and told you to visit Watcher Redweed for more information.

Watcher Redweed can be found in Staddle centre.
Lolo Wendingway advised you to seek out Watcher Redweed to help out with troubles brewing in the surrounding areas.
Defeated goblins at the Sunken Stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated goblins at the Goblinhole Ruins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, I'm glad to see you! There are goblins in the Midgewater Marshes, or so it has been told, and if that is the case, we need to know how many we're dealing with.
'There are two sets of ruins in the southern expanse of the Marshes. I would ask you to go to these ruins and defeat any goblins you find. If there are goblins near both ruins, we'll have a better idea of how far they've spread.
'The first set of ruins are found south-east of Eldo Swatmidge's farm, east of Staddle. South of his home is a narrow stretch of land that extends into the Marshes and runs right to the Sunken Stones. The Goblinhole Ruins are far to the east and south of those.'

'That's what I feared, ${PLAYER}. If the goblins have already spread so far throughout the Midgewater Marshes, they intend to stay. If it were not for the spider infestation at the ruins in the northern stretch of the Marshes, I would expect the goblins to seize those as well.'
Defeat goblins at the Sunken Stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat goblins at the Goblinhole Ruins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Scouting the Marshes
Watcher Redweed has asked for your help dealing with goblins that have taken up residence in the Midgewater Marshes.

'If you find goblins at each of the two sets of ruins in the southern Marshes, we will know the goblin-presence is widespread, and a very real threat. Take the east path from the town square until you arrive at the Widow Froghorn's farm, and then follow the line of fences north a short way. Swatmidge's farm is down the hill to the east, within view of the Midgewater Marsh.
'South of his farm, a strip of land extends into the bog and runs right to the first set of ruins. The second set is far to the east and south of those.'

The Sunken Stones are located south-east of Eldo Swatmidge's farm, east of Staddle. The Goblinhole Ruins are far to the east and south of the Sunken Stones.
Watcher Redweed wants you to visit two ruins in the southern Midgewater Marshes and defeat goblins at each location to assess the threat the goblins pose to Staddle's well-being.

Watcher Redweed is at town centre in Staddle.
You should report your findings at the ruins to Watcher Redweed in Staddle.

'The increasing number of goblins in the Midgewater Marshes troubles me, true, but I am even more concerned about the weapons some of them appear to be wielding. Swords and axes are bad enough, but the strange oil some of these goblins carry have the potential to do much greater damage.
'I am not thinking only of the farms and crops of Staddle, though the threat of fire to food and pipe-weed is immense. I am thinking of the Little Folk. This is a threat beyond them, I think.
'The more of those fire-wielding goblins we can defeat in the Marshes, the fewer we may have to contend with here on dry land. I need you to deal with them, and quickly.'

'You have dealt with those goblins? That is quite a relief.
'The goblins in the Marshes are still a threat, but now they should be easier to deal with. You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}, and now you have some more coins for your trouble!'
The Threat of Fire
The burning oil carried by the goblin-sappers that have crept into the Midgewater Marshes are particularly worrisome to Watcher Redweed, charged with the defence of Staddle.

'From your report, it sounds like there are many goblin sappers in the southern stretch of the Midgewater Marshes. Keep a wary eye out for the guttering of flame in the mist, and you are sure to find them.'

Goblin Sappers have infiltrated the southern expanse of the Midgewater Marshes.
Watcher Redweed has tasked you with defeating the Midgewater Sappers before they can bring their deadly burning oil to Staddle.

Watcher Redweed is in Staddle town centre.
News of your success against the goblin-sappers should relieve Watcher Redweed of some of his worries.

'We might be close to dealing the goblins a decisive blow, ${PLAYER}. The only thing keeping them from fighting amongst themselves are their loyalty to the two chieftains that are rumoured to lead them: Gurzstâz and Gurzrum.
'If you were to slay these two chieftains, I think the goblins would fall to squabbling among themselves. Such squabbling will leave them unable to mount an attack on Staddle.
'The two chieftains will be fairly close together somewhere in the Goblinhole Ruins so that each of them can keep an eye on the other. You may need to gather help...those chieftains will be the strongest of the lot!'

'You have done very well, ${PLAYER}, very well indeed! I reckon the goblins will be unable to mount an organized attack on the town without the leadership of those goblin-chieftains!
'You have performed a great service for both Men and hobbits, ${PLAYER}, and I'm sure the town of Staddle is in your debt. Now, Bree must know of our -- well I suppose it really is your -- great victory!'
Two Chieftains
Watcher Redweed believes that you are close to dealing the goblins in the Midgewater Marshes a decisive blow.

'The two goblin-chieftains, Gurzstâz and Gurzram, are sure to be near each other in order to ensure neither of them is scheming against the other. Their camp is among the Goblinhole Ruins in the southern stretch of the Midgewater Marshes.'
'All of Staddle is in your debt for dealing with those goblins!'
'You have dealt a grave blow to the goblins in the Midgewater. Good work!'
'The goblins will know better than to show their faces around here again, I'll warrant!'

The two chieftains, Gurzstâz and Gurzrum, are likely to be found in the Goblinhole Ruins in the southern stretch of the Midgewater Marshes.
Watcher Redweed believes that slaying the goblin-chieftains will drive the rest away.

Watcher Redweed is in Staddle town centre.
The defeat of the goblin-chieftains in the Midgewater Marshes should be a great relief to Watcher Redweed.

'I'd wager Falco Greenhand is the best gardener in all of Staddle, and that's saying quite a lot. He's very proud of that garden of his, and not without reason -- it's quite a sight! Recently he hasn't been coming round to visit like he used to, though, and I'm a little worried about him.
'In fact, I heard that his garden is going through a rough spell, and it might not survive the season! Maybe you can find out what's going on, and put my mind at ease? Falco's farm is south-west of here.
'Falco's a good friend, and I'd hate to see him lose that garden!'
'Not trouble about him? Why I've known old Falco all my life, and I tell you there is naught he cares more about than his garden! I'm not going to stand around and do nothing!'
'Please, leave me alone! I don't need this right now. I have too much else to worry about than some busy-body! Shoo! My problems are not yours. Go tell Gammy that she should stop nosing about!'
Concern for a Friend
Falco's garden is failing for an unknown reason, causing distress among the people of Staddle.
'I'm not one to talk about friends behind their backs, but old Falco's been acting mighty queer lately. Could you have a talk with him? His farm's to the south-west of here.'
'Please, my problems are my own. Just tell Gammy Boggs not to trouble about me.'

Falco Greenhand's farm lies to the south-west of Gammy Boggs' farm.
Gammy Boggs, the local town gossip, has asked you to find out why Falco's garden is failing.

Gammy Boggs is at her farm, north-east of Falco Greenhand's farm.
Falco Greenhand did not want to trouble you with his problems and asked you to tell Gammy Boggs to stop nosing about.

'Maybe you can talk to some of the other Staddle-folk and see if they know anything about what is happening to Falco's garden? Someone surely knows something that might help!
'You can find them keeping watch over their own farms here in Staddle.
'We need to find out what is happening to Falco's garden since he will not tell us.'

'Falco's garden? It was a special one, to be sure...seemed able to fight off that mould that showed up in the other farmers' crops. Falco always was the best gardener in Staddle. It's sad if what they say is true, and it's gone to ruin.'
'I haven't seen anything out of the ordinary. There are more animals around as of late, but I don't expect any of them have gotten into Falco's garden, or we'd have heard about it.'
'You say Lily knows what's going on with Falco, but won't say anything? Why, shame on that girl!'

'So Outsiders are now taking an interest in Staddle's business? Well, I did see something a bit strange a few days back. The moon was hiding behind a cloud, so I can't be sure, but I thought I saw several shadows out by the Constable's house, south-east of town. Not sure what that would have to do with old Falco, though.'
'Gammy! I wish I didn't know what I know, but I do. I told Falco I wouldn't say anything, tell Gammy I wish I could help.'
'Gardens? I've trouble enough with my spiders. I can't be any help to you.'

'There's nothing that I can really tell you about Falco's garden, other than I would do just about anything to know his secret. Everyone else's garden got that awful mould, except his! Most beautiful garden I'd ever laid eyes on, it was.'
Talk to Staddle-folk
Eyes of Staddle
Falco's garden is failing for an unknown reason, causing distress among the people of Staddle.
'Just speak with some of the Staddle-folk mingling about town square and on their farms. One of them might know something about Falco's garden.'

The people of Staddle can be found tending and watching over their farms or in the centre of Staddle.
Gammy Boggs has recommended that you speak to some of the Staddle-folk to learn what happened to Falco's garden.

Gammy Boggs is on the second farm north of the road near the Staddle farms.
The knowledge you gained from the people of Staddle will be of great interest to Gammy Boggs, the town gossip.

'I think you should speak with Falco again. Maybe those mysterious trespassers are responsible for ruining his poor garden!
'His farm is south-west of here. Quickly, return to him and tell him what you learned.
'I hope the old fool will be more helpful to you this time.'

'Misery me, you've found me out! I made a deal with those wicked ruffians. They promised not to ruin my crops if I paid them. I did for a while, but when I stopped, they were true to their word, such as it is, and they ruined my lovely garden!
'They said their leader would be very unhappy with me if I didn't pay them, and not just that! They said he'd burn down the whole town! I heard that happened up Archet way, and now I'm worried it'll happen to Staddle too!
'I know I should have said something sooner, but I was so afraid -- this Sharkey they're trying to impress sounds fearsome. Perhaps Constable Bolger can help you stop them? Please go tell him at once! His house is south-east of here!'

'The ruffians have been driven off? They won't be coming back?
'Oh, thank you! Thank you, friend! Please accept this small token of my gratitude.
'I will do my best not to mess with Sharkey's Men again. Protecting my garden is not worth destroying my lovely town. Please tell everyone how very, very sorry I am.'

'Old Falco has put us in a tough place, sure enough. The Blackwolds have been lurking about the Chetwood for a while now, but they seem to be getting a little bolder since this Sharkey's showed up. They've started pushing folks like Falco about. Perhaps we can put an end to that here!
'All we can do now is wait...'
Talk to Constable Bolger
Falco's Garden
Falco's garden is failing for an unknown reason, distressing the people of Staddle.
'You should speak to Falco again and tell him what you've found. It could be those mysterious trespassers are responsible for ruining his beautiful garden!'
'Brigands and ruffians? Oh dear, what's old Falco gotten himself into? I'm sure he meant no harm! You'd best hurry along to Constable Bolger. His home is east of here.'

'Far be it from me to spread tales, but I hear you even killed the miscreant that was leading that band of ruffians! That would have been a fine mess for old Falco, sure enough...thank you, ${PLAYER}!'
'I'm so sorry about all this! Please hurry and tell Constable Bolger...I'm sure those ruffians are on their way here!'

Falco's farm lies south-west of Gammy Boggs' farm.
Gammy Boggs has suggested you speak with Falco Greenhand again and tell him of the mysterious trespassers that were seen near his garden.

Constable Bolger's house is located south-east of Falco Greenhand's farm.
Confronted with the truth, Falco Greenhand has confessed that he made an underhanded bargain with ruffians. He has asked you to speak with Constable Bolger and warn him that the brigands are coming to burn the town.

Falco Greenhand's farm lies north-west of Constable Bolger's home.
You and Constable Bolger have defeated the Blackwold brigands who had planned to burn the town of Staddle. Falco will be glad that you have succeeded.
Collected red lilies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If Lily knows something, we can likely get her to talk. She'll be coy, as most hobbit-lasses her age are, but if you ask nicely, I am certain that she'll tell you what we need to help poor Falco.
'We need to band together and make certain that Falco gets all the help he needs to get through this time.
'Go back to Lily at her farm beneath the hill -- it isn't far down the road to the east -- and speak with her about what she saw.'

'Big Folk! Bad enough the Men in Archet burned their town and then ran into the Chetwood. I didn't know that there were some near here.
'Oh, Falco...whatever are we to do with you.'

'I told Falco I wouldn't say anything about what I know...but I might be able to tell you without saying anything.
'I like flowers, ${PLAYER}, but not just any flowers, I like flowers that are my namesake. South of my house, down beyond the Yellow Tree, you'll find lilies, red ones!
'Get me a bundle of the lilies and keep your eyes open. If you look where you are, you'll notice the big problem facing poor Falco.'

'If you were looking around yourself down in the south Chetwood you likely noticed all the Big Folk there. Now you know my secret, and I never said a word!
'Oh, thank you for the flowers, ${PLAYER}. They are lovely.
'Now you can tell Gammy Boggs that you know what I know. I hope you can find a way to help poor Falco.'
'If you keep a watchful eye, you may notice that Falco has a //qtall//q problem.'
Collect red lilies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Deliver the red lilies to Lily Underhill
Lily's Secret
Gammy Boggs is certain that Falco Greenhand has gotten into some kind of trouble that he cannot get out of, and the cryptic message you received from Lily is not helping to ease her mind.
'Hurry along now! I'll not see a hobbit suffer while I can still be of assistance.'
'Hurry along now! I'll not see a hobbit suffer while I can still be of assistance.'
'Hurry along now! I'll not see a hobbit suffer while I can still be of assistance.'
'I hope that you can find a way to help Falco, ${PLAYER}.'

Lily Underhill can be found outside her home east of Gammy Boggs' home, at the foot of the hill, north of the road.
Gammy Boggs believes that with the proper coaxing Lily will tell all that she knows about Falco's plight.

Lilies can be found in the forested area south of the Yellow Tree, south of Lily Underhill's house. Lily Underhill can be found outside her home to the north, east of Gammy Boggs' farm.
Lily Underhill said she could not say specifically what Falco Greenhand's trouble was, but she could show you, if you looked at the right things. As a hint, she sent you to gather lilies.

Red lilies can be found in the forested area south of the Yellow Tree, south of Lily Underhill's house.
Lily Underhill said she could not say specifically what Falco Greenhand's trouble was, but she could show you, if you looked at the right things. As a hint, she sent you to gather lilies.

Return to Gammy Boggs at her farm west of Lily Underhill.
Lily told you -- without telling you -- that the Big Folk camped at the ruins in the south Chetwood are the reason that Falco Greenhand's farm is suffering.

'Asphodel keeps her farm going by selling her goods at the Farmer's Market. I made a deal with Himloc Grouse to pay double what others pay for her fresh vegetables.
'Could you go to her farm, collect the produce she means to sell, and deliver it to Himloc? Be sure to return the money to her when you are done.'

'Eldo didn't send a layabout, did he?
'And he's kind to his dogs? How about that?
'Since you've already proven yourself so useful, why not take this into Staddle and sell it to Himloc Grouse? He'll be in the town square, most likely. Maybe then we can continue our discussion of Eldo Swatmidge's good qualities, of which I am sure you will tell me there are many.'

'So you've got some produce for sale from the Widow Froghorn, do you? Well, I'll be taking it...and here's the payment.
'And before you start thinking I've gone soft in the head, that's double what I usually pay. Eldo Swatmidge and I have a standing agreement, on account of he asked me to pay double for any of the Widow's produce, then he gives me the difference. It's true what they say: a hobbit in love don't have no hobbit-sense at all!
'You bring that payment back to the Widow Froghorn and don't mention the agreement I've got with Swatmidge. That's part of the whole arrangement.'
'Are you here on account of the Widow Froghorn?'
'This seems like a bit much. Are you sure Himloc gave you the right amount? No, don't tell me. I have a feeling Eldo Swatmidge might have something to do with Himloc's generosity.'
'You didn't get any payment from Himloc? That's very unusual.'
Bring the basket of vegetables to Himloc Grouse
Bring Himloc's payment to Asphodel Froghorn
Farmer's Market
Eldo Swatmidge is a successful farmer, but he is lonely. He has sought your help to woo his neighbour, the Widow Froghorn.

'I told you that you had impressed her! It sounds like we're making progress, yes it does!
'Oh, by the way, I told old Himloc that when he buys produce from Asphodel, he should pay double what he normally would, and I'd pay him the difference. I figured you should know -- don't be surprised when you talk to him!'
'Old Himloc kept up his end of the bargain? Good, good! Well, take that money on to Asphodel now and be sure to mention my good hobbit-sense!'

The Widow Froghorn's farm is on the road west and south of Eldo Swatmidge's farm.
Eldo Swatmidge asked you to collect the produce that Asphodel Froghorn means to sell.

Himloc Grouse can usually be found in the town square of Staddle, west of the Widow Froghorn's farm.
Asphodel seems to think highly of you and has asked you to sell some of her produce to Himloc Grouse, the trader.

Widow Froghorn's farm is east of Staddle.
Asphodel Froghorn is waiting for the payment you received from Himloc Grouse for the sale of her vegetables.

'I've noticed my pipe-weed field is rather less robust than it should be. At first I suspected animals had gotten at it -- we have had some troubles with wolves ranging too near the town recently -- but I don't think that is the answer. What would wolves have to do with pipe-weed?
'I think the Blackwold brigands are to blame, ${PLAYER}! Men have had a taste for pipe-weed ever since we taught them the craft, and now I fear these villains have been sneaking in after dark to pinch some of my most promising crop!
'Take this letter to Constable Bolger and ask him what he intends to do about it! You'll find him south-east of here, on the outskirts of Staddle. He must do something. These Men have gone too far!'
'I don't know how many letters from Himloc I can put up with, friend. We'd better do something about the brigands that are stealing from his pipe-weed crop before I get another.'
'Do you have something for me?'
Bring Himloc's letter to Constable Bolger
Message for the Constable

'I am surprised at how earnest Eldo seems to be! Perhaps I shall give him a chance. A courtship could be just the thing to brighten my days.
'Tell him that I'll consider his courting me, but he'll need to sell his dog, Wanetta. I always come down with the sneezes whenever I am around dogs of her breed, and it is really unbearable.
'Hurry back with his answer! Oh, I'm all a-flutter like a little hobbit-girl!'

'What? He won't sell that dog? Now...now I want him courting me even more! What loyalty, and not even to a person!
'You were right all along, ${PLAYER}. Eldo Swatmidge might not be the most well-dressed hobbit in Staddle, or even the most well-spoken, but he's a good, hard-working, loyal fellow.
'Maybe someday there will be a cure for the sneezes I get around that breed of dog, and then not even Wanetta will keep me from my Eldo! Please go tell him at once, ${PLAYER}.'

'Sell Wanetta? I...I can't. I've had Wanetta here since she was a pup. She's given me litter after litter of good, strong pups. She's my prized dog! I can't sell her! If she was a hobbit and I was a dog, she wouldn't sell me, I know it!
'If that is what Asphodel wants...tell her I can't. I can't do it. Looks like I won't ever be courting the Widow Froghorn. Please don't think me ungrateful for what you've done, but I just can't lose my Wanetta.'

'Really!'
Eldo looks to Wanetta, 'Did you hear that Wanetta? Asphodel said yes!'
'${PLAYER}, I don't know if this is thanks enough for what you've done for me! Take this and know that I'll be everything I promised Asphodel and more!'
Wanetta the Wedge
Eldo Swatmidge is a successful farmer, but he is lonely. He has sought your help to woo his neighbour, the Widow Froghorn.
'Oh, I'm so excited! Please hurry and tell Mr. Swatmidge so he can make arrangements to sell that dog of his. I can't wait!'
'Eldo's loyalty, generosity, kindness, and caring make him a fine suitor, I think!'
'I hope she understands, but I just can't sell my Wanetta. I just can't!'
'O joy! The Widow Froghorn will let me come a-courting!'
'That Eldo Swatmidge is simply a darling, isn't he?'

Eldo Swatmidge's farm is up the road north and east of the Widow Froghorn's farm.

'Hoy there, do you know anything about dogs? Gar here has been feeling poorly since yesterday, and he won't eat a bite. I fetched him some fresh water from the well, and he just turns away!
'Maybe you could help me? Eldo Swatmidge knows a fair bit about animals, and he might have an idea about what's wrong with Gar. He lives quite a bit east of town, almost on the edge of the Midgewater Marshes, and I don't think Gar would be up for the walk. Just take the road east out of town to the Widow Froghorn's farm, then north from there and down the hill to the east.
'Eldo is a bit of a queer sort, but he loves dogs, so he can't be that bad, right? I'd appreciate anything he could do to help Gar!'

'What? Gar is sick? Why, he came from one of my Wanetta's litters!
'My own dogs occasionally eat something that doesn't set quite right with 'em. When they do I've got a herbal remedy my grandfather taught me that helps clear it right up. I have most everything on hand, but I'll be needing fennel seeds to finish it up proper.
'Fennel grows in the Midgewater Marshes, but it's hard to find because the Neekerbreekers have a fancy for it. It might be easier to find a Neekerbreeker that still has fennel caught in its pincers, than to find a fresh plant. Bring the seeds back to me, and I will mix up a remedy for Gar.'

'That remedy should make him feel a lot better!
'Good boy, Gar! That'll do it! You must have eaten something that disagreed with you, that's all. Here, you can wash that remedy down with -- hey now, what's this?
'I drew this water from the town well this morning, but it sure smells odd! Is this what made Gar sick?'

'You've brought me the fennel seeds? Good, good, give them here, and I'll boil them up with the rest of this.
'There we go. Take this remedy to Gar and let him drink it. He may not much like it, but make sure he drinks it all the same. He should recover soon.'
'Neekerbreekers in the Midgewater Marshes often get fennel tangled up in their pincers. If you can retrieve some seeds, I can make a remedy that should help Gar.'

Gar sniffs at the herbal remedy, and then laps some of it up. He slowly drinks the rest of the mixture.

Gar looks at you unhappily. He does seem to be very ill.

'Eldo lives east of Staddle, almost on the edge of the Midgewater Marshes. Take the eastern path from the town square until you reach the widow Froghorn's farm, and follow the line of fences north, then down the hill to the east to Eldo's place.

'This is a fine farm, wouldn't you say? Yes, life has been kind to me. My only regret is that I haven't anyone to share it with!
'I think you might be able to help me, if you're of a mind. The Widow Froghorn lives up the hill to the west, and she's a fine lady, but she won't hear of me courting her. I've been sending letters to her for a while now, asking her to tea, to the dance, to watch o'er my dog...but she refuses every time!
'Now, Widow Froghorn -- Asphodel is her right name -- is always needing help around her farm. Maybe if you lend her a hand, saying a kind word about me now and then, she'll change her mind! Go west up the hill, then turn south by the fence at the top. Her farm is at the crossroads.'

'Who might you be? Another farmhand Eldo sent to help me? I don't need his help, thank you very much and good day to you!
'No matter how many times I tell him \qno,\q he just won't give up. I swear, there's only one thing he loves, and it's those dogs he raises! If it doesn't bark or have a tail to wag, he doesn't know the first thing about it!
'I must beg your pardon, but it's been a bit of a trial since I lost my Bodo. If you're here to lend a hand, I won't stop you. The pipe-weed is ready for harvest, so if you're still intent on helping out, you can bring it in. It's right there, on the other side of my wheat field.'
Widow's Farmhand
Eldo Swatmidge is a successful farmer, but he is lonely. He has sought your help to woo his neighbour, the Widow Froghorn.
'Asphodel's farm is west of here, closer to Staddle. Go up the hill to the west and turn south at the fence on the top. Don't forget to put in a good word for me every chance you get!'

'Sent you again, did he? That Eldo Swatmidge is certainly persistent. I'll give him that, at least.

'I think there is something wrong with the water in the town well, ${PLAYER}! It certainly smells peculiar, that's for sure, and would explain why Gar has been feeling poorly.

'Go and tell Lily Underhill -- we can't have people drinking from the well until we can clean the water somehow! Lily lives over yonder, east of Boggs' Farm.'

'Longo thinks the well is poisoned? I don't know -- it seems a bit far-fetched. Perhaps he's just imagining it?

'I have an idea how to fix things, but I'll need your help to make the water safe to drink.'

Longo Daegmund is convinced that something in the Staddle town well caused Gar's illness.
'You must do something about this foul water before someone else falls ill!'
Lily Underhill's home is east of the town square, past Boggs' Farm.

'There's a wise-woman named Willowsong, who dwells by the Silverwater Spring. She may know a way to clean the befouled water. Draw a bucket of water from the well and bring it to her. Perhaps she'll know what to do.
'Take the road east from the town square to the Widow Froghorn's farm, then south to Constable Bolger's house. The Silverwater Spring is south-east of there.'
'This water smells most foul. Tell me, ${RACE}, why have you brought it to me?'
Draw water from the Staddle town well
The Wise Woman

'Hurry up with that bucket... and don't spill any!'
'You brought the bucket of water to Willowsong, yes? What did she say? Can she help us?'

The Staddle Town Well is in Staddle town centre. To find the Silverwater Spring, take the road east from the town square to the Widow Froghorn's farm, then south to Constable Bolger's house. The Silverwater Spring is south-east of there.

'I do not know who would do such a thing to the good folk of Staddle, but I know a remedy to cleanse the poison from their wellwater.
'Bring me six handfuls of the wildflowers that grow near the Yellow Tree south-west of the Spring. The blossoms possess a cleansing virtue that will purge the poison from the well.
'The Yellow Tree was a place of peace in times past, but now it is home to fearsome creatures. You must be courageous if you are to collect the flowers I require.'
'Yes, these are just what I needed. This will take but a moment. The water was indeed poisoned, but the blossoms of these wildflowers will drive the poison away.'
'Time is of the essence, ${RACE}. Return to me when you have the flowers and not before.'

Seeking help, you brought a bucket of fouled well-water to the River-maiden of Silverwater Spring.

'Good, you have the flowers I need. The evils of Man tainted this water with poison. The power of nature will make it pure once more.
'Now return this bucket to Staddle and pour its contents into the well. The water inside will retain its curative properties and drive out any remaining poison.

'After all that trouble, you just pour the dirty water back into the well? I don't understand....'
Longo sniffs the well water, then takes a sip.

Willowsong needs fresh wildflowers to clean the well water.
'Do you intend to stand around all day? I believe you have a task to complete.'
'There are few who remember the Yellow Tree of old. The Master remembers, but he does not come this way often.'
'The Yellow Tree was once a place of peace, but times have changed and it is no longer so.'
'I am glad to help the good people of Staddle.'
'In a way, my Gar solved the mystery of the poisoned well! Good boy, Gar!'
'I wonder how the well got poisoned in the first place? It must have been those no-good Blackwolds!'
'I'm glad no one got sick! I feel bad for Gar of course, but you know what I mean.'
'We need to keep a close eye on the well and make sure those brigands don't poison it again. I'm sure it was them!'
'The water tastes delicious now. And we have you and Willowsong to thank!'

'Now that Constable Bolger is safe, I can tell you more of the story. Jasper Mudbottom is the Blackwold that came to me and got me to help them. Since then, I've felt terrible and the farm has suffered as my guilt grew within me.
'Jasper used to live here in Staddle, but joined with the Blackwolds, returning shortly before Archet burned. When he came back he was changed. Something very different about him...stronger and mean-spirited.
'If you stopped him, I might be able to get back to growing the best pipeweed in all of Bree-land! Jasper lives in that fort south of here beyond Yellow Tree. He'll be too strong for you to face alone.'

'I cannot thank you enough, ${PLAYER}. I had thought Gammy Boggs' nosey ways would just bring more trouble on me, not fix them!
'I owe so many people here in Staddle apologies, it will take me a while to draft enough letters saying so, but I will see it done.'
Fixing Falco's Folly
Falco confided that he was originally pressured by a man named Jasper Mudbottom. Mudbottom is a powerful brigand located at the Yellow Tree ruins, south beyond the Staddle farms.
'You shouldn't face Jasper alone in his camp south of Yellow Tree. He is far stronger than he appears.'
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. My farm will be green again in no time!'

'While I was trying to sell some of my wares to the farms east of Staddle, a Neekerbreeker got into my waggon here and made off with my pack! I expect it probably dragged it out to the Midgewater Marshes to eat my lunch.
'The problem is that my coinpurse was in that pack, which means I can't buy pipe-weed to trade to Burl. Worse, if I don't get it back within the next half an hour, I am sure to miss out on the good prices of pipe-weed down in Staddle!
'You've got to find the Neekerbreeker that stole my pack and bring it back to me in the next thirty minutes, ${PLAYER}!'
'My pack! You found it, and with time to spare, too! Take this as a token of my thanks, ${PLAYER}.'
'The Neekerbreeker that stole my pack is sure to be in the Midgewater Marshes, east of Staddle. You'll need to hurry if you're going to get there and back again in time!'
Bring the pack to Lolo Wendingway
Collect Lolo Wendingway's pack from the Neekerbreeker that stole it.
The Errant Coinpurse
Lolo wants to resume Burl Beeman's profitable trade between Combe and Staddle, but a Neekerbreeker ran off with his pack and the coinpurse therein.

'Now that the people of Archet have stood up against the Blackwold brigands and we've got them on the run here, the tides are turning. Things are returning to normal, and I say it's time I did my part!
'I used to send honey down to Staddle in trade for pipe-weed, a business I'm ready to pick up again. My old trading partner, a hobbit by the name of Lolo Wendingway, used to peddle wares on the road between here and Staddle, to the south. When the Blackwolds came, I'll wager he holed up down there.
'If you happen to be in Staddle and see Lolo, please let him know I would like to renew our partnership!'

'You say you've spoken with Burl Beeman? Oh, this is bad, very bad indeed! I had a good and profitable arrangement with Beeman -- I would purchase pipe-weed from here in Staddle, bring it to Beeman in exchange for honey, and then use the honey to satisfy my outstanding contracts in Staddle.
'But as much as I would like to renew that arrangement, I am unable to do so at the moment! Unless...maybe you could do something for me?'
Friendships Renewed
Now that the Blackwold brigands have been routed, Burl Beeman wants to seize the opportunity to resume his trade with the village of Staddle.
'Lolo used to sell his goods on the road between Combe and Staddle, to the south. I expect with all the Blackwold business he holed up in Staddle. You'll probably find him there.'

Lolo Wendingway can likely be found in Staddle, south of Combe.

'You are the one that helped the halfling, Dob Sandheaver are you not? It seems the situation is much graver than I first thought, and it has gone beyond stolen food-bags.
'The giant that attacked Dob is very small for his kind but he is a giant none the less. How and when he wandered down to the borders of the Shire is a mystery even to myself. He has begun to waylay many travellers north of Buckland and has even been sighted on the borders of the Bree-fields. At first I was content to watch him and wait, but his actions can no longer be tolerated...he must be dealt with.
'I would ask you to gather companions and face Svalfang. We Rangers have protected the borders of the Shire for years, but there are too few of us here to face this foe. I would not have Aragorn return to find that the land he guarded for so many years in ruin because of my inaction. Do what you must, but find the giant and drive him forth from these lands.'

'You defeated the giant? Well done! There have been many strangers lurking on the borders of that peaceful land. I don't doubt he would have caused many more problems than a few scared hobbits had he not been dealt with.'
Bring news of your deeds to Amlan
Giant Problems
The Ranger Amlan has learned that you assisted Dob Sandheaver with the giant Svalfang.

Svalfang's hut is north of Buckland, overlooking the Brandywine River.
Amlan has asked you to drive the giant Svalfang from the land.
Collected Dob Sandheaver's pack

'Why hullo there! You're the one everyone has been talking about yes? Well, I could use your help. I have big problems, and that's a fact! You see, I was on a trip to visit my dad away in Buckland after visiting my brother Gil at Hengstacer. I thought to myself, \qYou should take a shortcut...no use wandering all the way down to the Great East Road and all.\q That's when it all went wrong.
'Now I was walking along quiet as you will until about the time for elevenses, and I felt a dreadful hunger. I came upon an old bit of stonework in the Brandywood and sat myself down for a light snack. All of a sudden, quick as you will, a hefty burly fellow shows up, and with none too kind words mind you. He was much larger than the big folk of Bree...I am afraid I was quite scared of the brute and ran off without my pack!
'The stonework is north of Buckland in the Brandywood. I doubt that this giant Man -- Svalfang I heard him call himself -- will stay in his dreary little hut all day. Maybe you could sneak by and pinch my pack when he is out stomping and doing whatever large folk of his kind do.'

'You found it! You have my thanks. I don't know what I would have done if I hadn't found it.
'It looks like some of the food is a bit crushed and broken, but most of it still looks fine. Thats the last time I take another shortcut, and that's a fact!'
'Have you found my pack yet? I lost it outside that stone hut in the Brandywood.'
Bring Dob Sandheaver his pack
Big Problems
Dob Sandheaver was driven off from his meal by a giant. He has asked you to retrieve his pack for him.
Dob Sandheaver outside the Prancing Pony has asked you to search for his pack at the stone hut deep in the Brandywood, far to the north of Buckland.
Time expired!
'Come back for more, eh? Sorry...only one prize per contestant.'

'Are you here for the pie-eating contest? Wonderful! I'll explain the rules...
'The goal is to eat any six of the pies there on the table. Big ones or small ones, it makes no difference to me! But be sure you let me know you are finished before the time expires.
'Are you ready to start?'

'Well done, friend! You sure put away those pies, and just in the nick of time!
'As a winner of the pie-eating contest, you're welcome to claim your prize. Of course, you also have a wonderful title to go along with it: Pie-Eating Champion!'

The Pie-eating Contest
It is time for the pie-eating contest at the Bree-fields fair-ground. Come one, come all, and enjoy the fare.
'Go on and eat! You're lagging behind!'
'Stuffed already? You've barely begun!'
'Good, good...almost half-way done!'
'Oh dear, you look a bit flushed. Are you feeling ill?'
'This is quite disturbing to watch, let me assure you!'
'You're almost done! Don't bother chewing, just finish it!'
'Good day to you as well!'
'Ah, you still have a bit of pie on your face there....'
'Well, well. If it isn't Bree's resident pie-eating champion!'

Collected minor battle-lore
Collected minor weaponsmithing-lore

'I met a traveller the other day, a man who seemed to me to have great wisdom. We spoke for a short time, and he said something that seemed to me of much importance: \qknowledge is the best defence we have against those who would do us harm.\q
'I got to thinking, and I think that traveller was right. We need sharp swords and broad shields, but if we study the deeds of yesteryear, we are sure to draw from them lessons that will serve us well even today!
'I want to instill in the men under my command some of these lessons. If you know a scholar of some skill, he might be able to make sense of the materials of the past and give to you some teaching of past lore. Bring some minor battle-lore and some minor weaponsmithing-lore to me, and I will pay you for the trouble, ${PLAYER}, with coins and other goods.'

'You've brought me some information on the waging of battle and the smithing of weapons, ${PLAYER}? I thank you for it! Only by studying the lessons of the past can we be prepared for the dangers of the present!
'Here are some coins and a few sundries for your trouble, as I promised.'
'If you can find a scholar to put together some minor battle-lore and some minor weaponsmithing-lore, the guards here are sure to benefit from the instruction!'
Bring minor battle-lore and minor weaponsmithing-lore to Clayton Cole
Collect minor battle-lore
Collect minor weaponsmithing-lore
Knowledge is the Best Defence
Clayton Cole is hoping to improve the discipline of the Bree-town guards under his command by studying the lessons of the past.
'I have been studying the materials you brought me, ${PLAYER}. Thank you.'
'Pay attention to the past, for from it you can draw valuable lessons!'

Clayton Cole is by the Combe-gate on the east side of the town of Bree.
Clayton has asked you to find a scholar who can provide you with minor weaponsmithing-lore and minor battle-lore.
Defeated Neekers in the Midgewater Marshes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Everyone is talking about the goblins these days, but I'm worried about something other than the goblins. The sound of the Neekers in the Midgewater Marshes has gotten much louder recently. There are many more of them than there used to be, I'm sure of it! I'm afraid before long they will move out of the Marshes and descend upon the town!
'If you could kill a few of them, you would be doing this town a great service. The Midgewater Marshes are east of Staddle, beyond Swatmidge's farm.
'It would certainly put my mind at ease if this one danger was subdued before it gets out of hand.'

'Excellent, ${PLAYER}! It will be a while before the Neekers again grow to be a threat to Staddle. It is good to know I can rely on you to deal with dangers to the town that do not walk on two legs!
'Still, I fear everyone is so excited about the goblins that they've forgotten that other dangers lurk in the Marshes!
'There's another threat I would ask your assistance with.'
Defeat Neekers in the Midgewater Marshes (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Neekers in the Marshes
Though always on the watch for the goblins, Watcher Reedy believes the creatures of the Midgewater Marshes, east of Staddle, are no less of a threat to the town.
'The Neekers are in the Midgewater Marshes, east of Staddle. I suggest you search the northern stretch of the swamp, as the Neekers in that area are closest to the town and pose the greatest danger.'

The Midgewater Marshes lie to the east of Staddle, beyond Swatmidge's farm.
Watcher Reedy is worried that the growing Neekerbreeker population in the north of the Midgewater Marshes poses a threat to Staddle that is being overlooked by the watchers because of the goblin troubles.

Watcher Reedy loiters in Staddle, near town centre.
Watcher Reedy will be pleased to learn that you have succeeded in thinning the numbers of the Neekers in the Marshes.

'The Midgewater Marshes hide many dangerous creatures, as you have seen, but still Watcher Redweed insists the goblin threat is more immediate!
'I've heard the farmers complaining about finding a particularly deadly breed of spider crawling in their fields. It seems that their presence is focused somewhere between the old Marshwater Fort and the Woodsedge Ruins in the Marshes. They have overrun both those old ruins, and I worry what might happen if they decide to come to Staddle in greater numbers.
'I would appreciate it if you would lessen the threat by killing a few of those dreadful creatures and their queen.'

'Good for you, ${PLAYER}! Without the marsh-queen, it will be a long time before the spiders once again pose a threat to the town. Now that I am satisfied that the menace of the Midgewater Marshes has been overcome, I'll lend a hand to Redweed with those goblins.
'If the beastly things come too near the town, I will be sure to let you know, ${PLAYER}!'
Spiders in the Midgewater
Watcher Reedy is still concerned that the creatures of the Midgewater Marshes pose an overlooked danger to the people of Staddle.

'The marsh brood-watchers are a deadly breed of spider that makes its home in the northern Midgewater Marshes, east of Staddle. Tread carefully around them, ${PLAYER}, for they are wily and dangerous, and will be a great threat to the town if we do not deal with them.'
'The Midgewater Marshes have always been a worry of mine.'
'You took a real risk defeating the marsh-queen -- all of Staddle thanks you!'

The brood-watcher presence lies between the old Marshwater Fort and the Woodsedge Ruins in the Midgewater Marshes.
According to Watcher Reedy, a deadly new breed of spider has appeared in the northern Midgewater, and she has asked you to thin their numbers.

Watcher Reedy can be found with her fellow watchers near Staddle town centre.
Watcher Reedy will be delighted to hear of your success against the deadly marsh brood-watchers and their queen in the Midgewater Marshes.
Found Rurik's Master-key (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ahh yes! I remember. A scout returned a few hours ago and mentioned that there was an Applewood giving orders to the recruits. He then headed towards the Blackwold's main encampment in the ruins in the north most part of the Chetwood.
'If Applewood has the key, then we should set about getting it from him to aid those who have suffered so greatly at the Blackwold's hands. Be careful ${PLAYER}, reports from near those ruins tell of a great sense of dread and dismay. You will need to be cautious if you are to attempt to find Applewood and obtain the key.
'When you find the key return to me and we shall see what good news we shall bring to the people of Archet and Combe.'

'You found it! Excellent work, and I can say that we are pleased that there is one less Brigand to worry about as well.
'Now, ${PLAYER}, we can find what the brigands hid away within this chest. You have done a wonderful job friend and deserve this reward.'
'If you can find Applewood within the Blackwold's main encampment, you should be able to recover Rurik's key and then we can begin to restore the people's hope here in Combe and Archet.'
Find Rurik's Master-key (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return Rurik's Master-key to Constable Sageford
Blackwold Thieves

Constable Sageford remembered that a scout mentioned hearing a Blackwold recruit heeding orders from Sergeant Applewood near the Blackwold main encampment. He has charged you with finding Applewood and recovering the key to the lockbox.
'If you can find Applewood within the Blackwold's main encampment, you should be able to recover Rurik's key and then we can begin to restore the people's hope here in Combe and Archet.'
'Archet and Combe will benefit greatly from your work!'
'You've done well here, ${PLAYER}.'

Applewood has been seen entering the Blackwold's main encampment in the northern most part of the Chetwood. Seek him out and obtain the key he stole from Rurik.
After learning that Rurik was guilty only of fear, Sageford recalled the name Rurik provided as being a Brigand within the main encampent of the Blackwold in the Chetwood.

Constable Sageford can be found near the centre of Combe.
Having found and defeated Applewood, you took the key back from him.

'After the initial raids, when folk began fleeing for villages like Archet and Staddle, the Blackwolds found they could no longer rely only upon raids to support themselves. They seized Old Bauman's farm and began tilling the soil, though badly and without care for the land.
'The brigands at the farm must be under the supervision of some Blackwold leader, else they would fall to laziness. If you confront the Blackwolds' leader at the farm, he might know something about this \qR.F.\q fellow. Old Bauman's farm is deep in the Chetwood, at the end of the eastward path.
'I would appreciate it if you could at least try. There are many folk who would benefit from this.'

'What is this?
'Rurik? There's a Rurik Fennel living here in Combe. He's a...a locksmith! Of course! I think we have found the identity of our mysterious \qR.F.\q, ${PLAYER}. Rurik's house is south-west of here, just behind The Comb and Wattle.
'You had best have a talk with Rurik. I will be very interested to know why he's been locking boxes for the Blackwolds. Very interested, indeed.'

'Old Bauman's farm at the end of the road north-east of Combe, deep in the Chetwood. There is probably a brigand of some importance supervising the work being done there, and it could be he knows something about our mysterious friend \qR.F.\q. I want these strongboxes opened, ${PLAYER}!'
Search for information about \qR.F.\q
Bring the parchment to Constable Sageford
Blackwold Valuables
Constable Sageford has learned that the Blackwold brigands have been trying to support themselves by working a farm they seized deep in the Chetwood to the east of Combe.
'The farms north-east of Combe are sure to be under the watchful eye of some important Blackwold, perhaps this \qR.F.\q fellow himself!'

Old Bauman's farm is deep in the Chetwood, at the end of the eastward path.
Constable Sageford believes that if you confront the Blackwolds leader at Old Bauman's farm, you might learn something useful about the mysterious \qR.F.\q

Constable Sageford can be found near town centre in Combe, with his fellow constables.
Sageford sent you to confront the leader of the Blackwolds at Old Bauman's farm. You found a receipt signed by a 'Rurik' on the Blackwold's body. Constable Sageford will want to know about this.

'Rurik is a locksmith here in Combe. You should show him that receipt and ask him why the brigands appear to be common patrons of his.
'It seems odd that Rurik would be involved, he's a quiet man who keeps to himself mostly. Still we need to investigate every lead carefully.
'You should find him outside his home on the road that runs south past The Comb and Wattle Inn.'

'Yes, my name is Rurik. Yes, I'm a locksmith. What is this about? One of my strongboxes -- recovered from a brigand? -- and a letter?
'I see...
'I had hoped that I saw the last of the Brigands. You must understand, I did not willingly help them. My business is keeping things locked away, so I do not often ask questions of my customers.
'I filled an order for twenty strongboxes and upon completion was visited by the Blackwolds. One, a tough fellow, took my master key and threatened my life if I talked. One of the others with him called him Applewood.
'Please, tell the Constable that any aid was unwilling, and I only stayed silent because I feared for my life.'

'While this doesn't help us get this box open and the valuables returned, it does speak well of Rurik. I feel badly that he felt as though we could not protect him, but with what happened to Archet, I understand his hesitation.
'Let me think a moment on the name he gave us. Scouts are coming and going at all times...one may have mentioned seeing this Applewood.'
Rurik Fennel, Locksmith

After discovering a letter on the brigand supervisor at Old Bauman's farm, you delivered it to Constable Sageford to discover the identity of \qR.F.\q is Rurik Fennel a locksmith in Combe. Sageford wants you to confront Rurik about his possible involvement with the Blackwolds.
'Please tell Constable Sageford that I did not aid the brigands purposefully. I do not know who Applewood is, but he has the master key to the strongboxes.'
'Make your way down the road that runs south past The Comb and Wattle Inn and confront Rurik about the letter and the strongbox you found.'

Rurik Fennel, a local locksmith, lives on the road that runs south past The Comb and Wattle Inn in Combe.
Constable Sageford wants you to confront Rurik Fennel of the coincidences surrounding the Blackwold brigands and his name and initials appearing on their crates and letters they carry.

Constable Sageford awaits news of Rurik's involvement near the centre of Combe.
Rurik Fennel appears to have been an unwitting and bullied pawn of the Blackwold.

'I was talking to one of the other constables shortly before you returned, and it seems that he learned that some of the Blackwolds had been encamped in some ruins out in the Midgewater Marshes. It seems they couldn't handle the spiders that have overrun the ruins and fled.
'It could be they left another strongbox behind when they escaped. The particular ruins where they had encamped are near the centre of the Marshes out south-east of Combe.
'With any luck, you might find a strongbox that's not locked. It's worth trying, anyway. There are so many people who need money to rebuild, and who better to take it from than the ones that stole it in the first place?'

'You found a strongbox! I was sure the brigands wouldn't have had time to bring their valuables with them when the spiders attacked, and...this one is locked as well. And do you see these scratches, right here on the lock? \qR.F.\q just like on the other one.
'We need to get these strongboxes open, ${PLAYER}.'
'If the brigands did leave a strongbox behind when the spiders swarmed the ruins, it might contain some valuables that we can give to the people of the Chetwood so they can start their lives anew.'
Bring the strongbox to Constable Sageford
Treasure in the Web
Constable Sageford has learned that a Blackwold camp in the northern stretch of the Midgewater Marshes was recently abandoned to the spiders there. He believes they may have left a strongbox behind.

'The spider-infested ruins near the centre of the Midgewater Marshes once served as a brigand camp, and the Blackwolds may have left a strongbox there when they fled. If you can recover it -- and it is unlocked -- we can distribute the valuables to the suffering people of the Chetwood.'

The spider-infested ruins lie near the centre of the Midgewater Marshes, south-east of Combe.
Constable Sageford has asked you to search the spider-infested ruins in the Midgewater Marshes for another strongbox the Blackwolds may have left there.

Constable Sageford can be found near Combe town centre.
Sageford sent you to the spider-infested ruins in the Midgewater Marshes where the Blackwold brigands recently encamped to find another strongbox. You should return to Sageford with the news of your success.
Collected the Blackwold lockbox

'The Blackwold brigands are on the run, no question about it. They're trying to regroup at camps throughout the Chetwood, but they suffered a real defeat at Archet.
'The brigands fled their old encampment up by Archet carrying a large lockbox, bringing it to one of their smaller camps in the Chetwood, north-east of Combe. If we can get our hands on that lockbox, its contents could be used to help those who lost property to the Blackwolds. There are a number of watchfires along the road, so you'll need to find the right one.
'These villains have a great many debts to repay, ${PLAYER}. If you can return with the lockbox, the folk around here will be better for it.'

'Ah, you have returned with the brigands' lockbox! Now let me see what's inside, and we can sell the valuables to support the survivors of the Blackwold raids throughout the area.
'Locked! I should have guessed as much. Well, until we can find the key, we won't have any luck with this. There seem to be some initials carved in the lock: \qR.F.\q Most unusual.'

'The Blackwold watchfires along the road in the Chetwood are far to the east, beyond the lumber camp. When you reach the fence at the guard-house on the hill, cut across the fields to the left and keep walking until you are beneath the trees.
'The lockbox is most likely still at one of the Blackwold watchfires.'
Bring the lockbox to Constable Sageford
Collect the Blackwold lockbox
Unpaid Debts
Now that the Blackwold brigands have been largely pushed out of Archet, Constable Sageford wants to redistribute their stolen goods to those who suffered at their hands.

The Blackwolds have many camps along the road east and north of Combe. Constable Sageford is in Combe.
Constable Sageford wants you to recover a brigand lockbox from one of the watchfires in the Chetwood. Its contents can then be used to reimburse those who lost property to the Blackwold.
Collected the fishing pole

'I'm sorry, my mind is miles away. I didn't see you there. Did you help fight off the brigands? My dad did, he...he....' Gail chokes back a sob.
'During the Blackwolds' raid on Archet, someone broke into our house and stole many of our things. I don't care about most of them, but they took my dad's favourite fishing pole! I don't care if I get anything else back, but he wouldn't have wanted some filthy brigand to have it.
'Now that I've moved here to Combe, I've been meaning to ask Constable Wren if she could track down that fishing pole for me. Could you ask her if she has any idea where it might have been taken? She'll be at the guard-house on the hill east of Combe.'

'I have heard that many of the Blackwold brigands, after looting Archet, fled into the Chetwood. It seems that the Blackwold leaders are angry. They feel that the raid might have been more successful if their followers had been less focused on filling their pockets and more on acting together.
'The main encampment is east down the road and then deep into the northern woods. I suspect that many of the Blackwolds can be found within that camp.
'Mayhaps if you search in that area, you might find Gail's lost fishing pole.'

'You've found it! Oh, thank you, thank you!
'I've been thinking that the pole should be given to the waters of my dad's favourite fishing hole: the pond near the Hunter's Lodge in Archet. I think he'd like that.
'Thank you...thank you again!'
'Have you found my dad's fishing pole yet?'
Deliver the fishing pole to Gail Catchpole
Collect the fishing pole
Mourning the Dead
Gail Catchpole's father perished in the flames of The Mad Badger Inn, and many of their belongings were stolen by the Blackwold brigands.
'Gail will be pleased, I am sure, if you recovered her father's fishing pole.'

'I just know Constable Wren will have some idea where the brigand who stole my father's fishing pole has gone! She's usually out in front of the guard-house on the hill east of Combe. Please talk to her.'

Constable Wren can be found at the guard-house on the hill east of Combe.
Gail wants to find the brigands who stole her dead father's favourite fishing pole and retrieve it. She has sent you to ask Constable Wren for information about the brigands and where they might have taken her stolen goods.

The main encampment of the Blackwolds is in the Chetwood, north of the guard-house.
Constable Wren suggested that the brigand who looted the fishing pole belonging to Gail Catchpole's dead father may be near the watering hole beneath the Blackwold main encampment.

'Pardon me, do you think I could take up some o' your time? I haven't had any word o' me son Covell since this brigand nonsense began, and I'm afeared something might have happened to him!
'We lived in Archet till recently, but we had an argument -- I'm sure ye know how boys are -- and Covell left all in a huff. He said he would make his own way, down in Combe, and that's the last I heard o' him. Now that I've come to Combe, I hear he's gone east!
'If ye don't mind, could ye talk to Constable Wren for me? She watches the road east out o' Combe, and maybe she's seen Covell pass.'

'Looking for Covell Woodwright, are you? I've heard something about the boy, but I can't say his mother is going to like it.
'He's joined up with the Blackwolds. He hadn't been in Combe for long when they took him, either. He tried finding work around town, but he didn't have the stamina for hard labour.
'If you can talk to him, you might convince him to give up his new line of \qwork,\q but I doubt it. I wager you'll find him east of Combe, in the Chetwood. Just follow the path from the lumber camp north and east...you're sure to come across a Blackwold camp or two up there.'

'You fought with Covell Woodwright, but he escaped? Well, his sort will not be able to flee forever. I feel the time of the Blackwold brigands is coming to an end.
'It seems I was right, and he will never give up his lawlessness. His mother will not be pleased to hear it.'

'What? Covell has joined those villains in truth? I refuse to believe it! He's a good boy, even if he has a temper. He's a Woodwright, through and through, and would never do such a thing! Ye shouldn't say such horrible things, and to an old woman!
'Ah, what am I saying? I knew the boy had landed hisself in a spot o' trouble. Thank ye...thank ye at the least for finding him.'

'What's that? Me mother sent you to find me?
'I...I don't care! I've never been good at anything in my life, but now I've found something I can do and do right good! You're going to regret coming into Blackwold territory!'
Talk to Covell Woodwright
Reconnecting Ties
Maida Woodwright had an argument with her son Covell, and she has not seen him since. The Blackwold activity in the area has made her nervous, and she is seeking news of him.
'Covell Woodwright is probably with his Blackwold friends in the Chetwood, east of here. It could be that you will convince him to give up his lawless ways, but I rather doubt it.'
'It will not be easy, but you must tell Maida that her son has joined the Blackwold brigands. She should know the truth.'
'I hope Covell didn't get into any trouble! Constable Wren may have seen him pass. She watches the road east out of Combe.'
'Joined up with them Blackwolds? What's a mother to do! I hope ye can find him and convince him to give up them thieving ways!'
'I do hope Covell hasn't gotten into any trouble. Constable Wren at the guard-house on the hill east of Combe might know something.'
'My poor boy. I hope he'll come to his senses.'
'Covell was always a good boy! I don't understand what has come over him.'
'The worst thing about the Blackwolds is that they are normal people who've had a round of bad luck.'
'The story of Covell Woodwright is not unusual. It happens far too often.'

Constable Wren is at the guard-house, east of Combe.
Maida Woodwright has asked that you speak with Constable Wren regarding the whereabouts of her son, Covell.

Covell may be found at one of the Blackwold camps north and east of the Combe lumber camp.
Maida Woodwright sent you to speak with Constable Wren, who suggested that Covell joined the Blackwolds and would likely be found near one of their camps in the Chetwood.

Constable Wren patrols near the guard-house on the hill south of the lumber camp and east of Combe.
You discovered Covell Woodwright on the path leading through the Chetwood, and he attacked you. Though you defeated him, he escaped deeper into the woods. Constable Wren will want to hear of your encounter with the brigand.

Maida Woodwright is back in Combe.
Maida Woodwright must be told that her son Covell has joined the Blackwold brigands.
Collected bronze axe
Collected bronze blades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'These are dangerous times. Those Blackwold villains are roving through the Chetwood, nearly unchecked! Yes, they suffered a defeat at Archet, but you could just as well call that a defeat for the people who live there! It'll be a long time before the town is rebuilt!
'I need to defend my family from those brigands, and I don't think the constables are up to the task. They mean well, but I trust the strength of my arms more than any well-meaning constable.
'Trouble is, the smiths are tasked with too many duties and their prices are far too high! If you have any connexions, or a weaponsmith that holds you in friendship, I'd pay you reasonable rates for a bronze axe and two bronze blades, and throw in a few sundries as well. The axe will serve me until I can replace the blades of my own sword and my son's with whatever you can bring me. Hurry now! The Chetwood is full of those villainous Blackwolds!'

'You've got a good heart, ${PLAYER}, and I know my whole family thanks you: my wife Kate, my son Nate, and my daughters Piper and Pepper.
'I give you these coins and a few odds and ends for your trouble, and I will get to replacing the blades of my old weapons with these new ones you have brought to me.'
'I need a bronze axe and two bronze blades, ${PLAYER}, if I am to defend my family from the brigands of the Chetwood!'
Bring a bronze axe and two bronze blades to Leighton Howard
Collect bronze axe
Collect bronze blades (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Weapons for Leighton Howard
Leighton Howard has asked you to obtain some weapons of bronze with which he can defend his family.
'You have my thanks, and also those of Kate, Nate, Piper, and Pepper, I am sure!'
'Weaponsmiths around here have been making a fortune. Everyone needs weapons!'

Leighton Howard is in the town of Combe, in Bree-land.
Leighton has asked you to obtain a bronze axe and two bronze blades for him, because the local weaponsmiths are charging too much for him to pay, and he needs them to protect his family.
