You find nothing of note near this stump

'Me old dad was a robber some years back and got his hands on a good deal o' riches, as I hear it. Constable caught him, but afore he was hanged, me dad told me where he buried his loot! I never needed it afore now, so I was content to let it stay buried. But I figure it's time to get my hands on \qwealth enough to keep you warm and shod,\q as me dear old dad called it. Can you take this pick-axe and dig the treasure up?
'Just take the road east from Combe to Constable Wren's post up by the guard-house. Climb over the hill on the right and walk down to the riverbank, where the Hanging Tree grows -- it'll have an X carved into it.
'You'll be helping me make a new start of things, and you'll have me everlasting thanks!'
'What? They chopped down the Hanging Tree? And ye dug at all the trees with an X? This is terrible! How will I ever find me dad's buried treasure now?'
'Where's the pick-axe?'
Find the Hanging Tree
Dig near stumps in the stump field (${CURRENT}/${MAX})
Bring the pick-axe back to Ted Pickthorn
Beneath the Hanging Tree
Ted Pickthorn has found himself near penniless and in desperate straits. Rumour of his father's stolen wealth has brought him some hope, however.

'There are many other trees around the Hanging Tree. There were more hangings in those days, and they didn't want children seeing too much, so the surrounding trees helped to hide the robber-hangings from young eyes.
'Take the road east out of Combe, and at Constable Wren's post, head south. The Hanging Tree is on the downward slope of the hill south of the guard house, on the bank of the river. You'll know it by the X carved into it.'
'All the trees are cut down? Maybe the X is still there. Please see if you can find a tree with the mark. Perhaps we'll get lucky and find my dad's treasure!'

The Hanging Tree sits along the riverbank south of Constable Wren's post, south-east of Combe.
Ted Pickthorn's father was once a robber in the Chetwood and had purportedly garnered a significant amount of wealth. Ted believes his father's ill-gotten gains are buried at the foot of the Hanging Tree. The tree is supposed to be marked with an X.
Although there is no way to tell which stump was once the Hanging Tree, it can't hurt to dig near a few of the stumps in search of the treasure.

Ted Pickthorn can be found on the east side of Combe.
Ted Pickthorn sent you to retrieve his father's loot from beneath the Hanging Tree, but you discovered that the tree, among others, was chopped down by the woodcutters of Combe. You dug at several places on the field, but found no sign of Pickthorn's buried treasure.

'Let me just...hmmm...find the right page. Ah! Here we go. I see, I see. So, you stand in the field of stumps and...hmmm...take this many paces...and then that many strides...of course! I remember! The Hanging Tree was the south-east-most tree in that bunch. It was standing there closest to the Staddle Falls!
'Now just...hmmm...go back to that Stump field and you'll find that thing you wanted. What was it you wanted, again? You were digging for something, right? Here, take this pickaxe, it'll make it easier to dig. Least I could do, you finding my ledger!'

'Wh-what are these? These boots were buried beneath the Hanging Tree? Me dad was a villain to the end! \qWealth enough to keep you warm and shod.\q Shod, indeed!
'Wait...there's something rattling around inside the heel of this one.' Taking a knife from his pocket, Ted slices into the heel, and gold pieces tumble out into his waiting palm.
'Well, I'll be! My dear old dad told me true! \qWealth enough to keep you warm and shod,\q indeed! You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}! With this money, I'll be able to get a new start. I'll do better than my dear old dad, you wait and see!'
'You haven't brought me the treasure my dad buried beneath the Hanging Tree yet! Quick, hurry, before someone else finds it!'
Collect Pickthorn's boots
Collected Pickthorn's boots
Bring Pickthorn's boots to Ted Pickthorn
Pickthorn's Treasure
Mason Thorne's ledger revealed the location of the old Hanging Tree. Now you can search for Ted Pickthorn's treasure.
'You found out which stump was the Hanging Tree? Well, what're you standing here for? Go dig up me dad's treasure and bring it back here!'
'I gave you what...hmmm...you wanted to know, didn't I? You should go find...hmmm...whatever it was.'
'Did you find what you...hmmm...wanted? It looks from your face like you...hmmm...did. Good for you!'
'Thanks to my dad, I'll be able to make a new start!'
'I wonder if my dad buried any more treasure around the place?'
'All that for...hmmm...old boots....'
'You ever find that...hmmm...what was it? Tree, was it?
'Oh, isn't it exciting? Young Ted's sure to do well.'
'It was so nice of you to find Ted's treasure for him!'

The southeasternmost stump in the stump field, the one closest to Staddle Falls, was once the Hanging Tree.
After reading through the ledger you recovered for him, Mason Thorne was able to point you to the location of the Hanging Tree.

Ted Pickthorn is on the east side of Combe.
Following Thorne's instructions, you found the stump of the Hanging Tree. You dug up something buried beneath the stump, but it is not what Ted Pickthorn had led you to believe. His father's treasure appears to be a pair of old boots.
Collected Mason Thorne's ledger

'Maybe the woodcutters at the lumber camp up east of here remember which tree was the Hanging Tree! ${PLAYER}, you've got to have a word with Mason Thorne, the man in charge there. He just has to remember which o' the stumps used to be the Hanging Tree. He just has to!
'The lumber camp is along the road, north o' the Big House. Please, I need that money to make a new start for meself.'

'The Hanging Tree? Oh, I remember seeing a few...hmm...hangings in my day. I...hmmm...do believe I wrote the site o' the Hanging Tree down in my ledger. I write down all the things I want to remember. So I can just look it up in....
'Well...hmmm...bless me! I think I dropped my ledger in the woods not far from here. Yes, I remember! We were surprised by some o' those Blackwold, and I dropped my ledger on the road. I'd wager a captain o' those brigands picked it up!
'There are a quite a few campfires to the north and east, along the forested road. You might find my ledger on one o' them Blackwolds! Bring it back here...hmmm...and I'll look up that thing you wanted to know about. A tree, was it?'
'Ah, you found my ledger! Now I can find that...hmmm...thing you wanted!'

'I expect a...hmmm...Blackwold has my ledger. One o' them captains is probably using it to plan their movements in the Chetwood! They're camped to the east. You'll have to get it from them, if you want to know...hmmm...where that tree is.'
Bring the ledger to Mason Thorne
Collect Mason Thorne's ledger
The Logger's Ledger
Ted Pickthorn was greatly distressed when you told him the Hanging Tree and all the trees surrounding it had been chopped down.

'You tell those woodcutters at the lumber camp that they can't go around chopping down trees willy nilly like that! I realize that the people of Combe depend on the sale of that wood to get by, but this is me dad's legacy we're talking about! How am I ever going to find it now without digging holes up and down the Chetwood?'

'You say the site o' the Hanging Tree is inside Mason's ledger? Good, good! I'd love to see that ledger, uh, well...truth is, I can't read. Once you've got the ledger, you best get old Thorne to look it up.'

Mason Thorne is at the lumber camp, north and east of the guard-house.
Ted Pickthorn asked you to speak with Mason Thorne, the foreman at the Combe lumber camp. He may recall which tree had been the hanging tree.

Mason Thorne awaits you at the lumber camp that lies east and north of Combe, south of the Chetwood.
Thorne sent you to retrieve his ledger from the Blackwold brigands encamped along the road. You should return the ledger to him at once.

'I look at you, ${PLAYER}, and I see a blank canvas, an uncarved block of wood, an untempered blade, an unread book...any number of things that have the potential for greatness, but are still waiting for that potential to be realized.
'I look around at my home, and I see wreckage, a memory of the comfort that this town once had. It can have that peace and comfort again, ${PLAYER}, if those like you will rise to the challenge! Skilled hands must be kept busy if they are to improve in their craft!
'My brother Roderick stands near the Craft Hall in Combe, south of Archet. From the Combe town centre, take the left path as it climbs up the hill. You'll see my brother part of the way up the hill. Tell him that you wish to learn a crafter's vocation. The towns of Bree-land can only benefit from the application of your skills!'

'My brother sent you, eh? As well he should! The business up in Archet is unfortunate, but it serves to remind us of the importance of skilled craftsmen. It will take a great deal of labour to rebuild Archet and supply the people of Bree-land with everything they need to prosper.
'The Mistress of Apprentices in the Craft Hall across the road there can help you choose a vocation in which to specialize. A vocation is a bundle of three crafting professions with overlapping skills -- choose your vocation with care, because you will expend a great deal of time and energy improving your skill with the professions under its purview!
'Once the Mistress of Apprentices has welcomed you to your chosen vocation, be sure to speak with the Provisioner within the Craft Hall. She can sell you the tools of your trade -- every Profession has its own, so be not overshy with your coinpurse! The novices will be happy to sell you any recipes you might wish to have, though I can tell you now that you will already know how to make a thing or two.
'Equip the crafting tools you plan on using and find an appropriate facility -- the Craft Hall has a forge, workbench, and oven available for your use -- and begin practising your skills! You will advance in your chosen professions as you practise and seek out the teachings of others in the field. I hope you will become a skilled craftsman, ${PLAYER}, and that it will bring profit to you and to the Bree-land.'
Strong of Arm and Sharp of Mind
Following the burning of Archet, Edward Carver and his brother Roderick are hoping to encourage all those with potential to take up a crafting vocation for the good of the Free Peoples.

'Speak to my brother Roderick in Combe, to the south if you're interested in learning a vocation, ${PLAYER}. When you arrive in the town centre, take the left path as it climbs partway up the hill, and you should see him right away.'
'I hope your crafting successes bring prosperity to the region!'
'The Craft Hall of Combe is a gathering place for skilled craftsmen.'
'If you watch the craftsmen at work, you are certain to have a greater appreciation for their skills.'
'The Craft Hall in Combe is south of Archet. Head east from the Combe town centre.'
'It is important to gather the finest materials with which to craft. This is true of people as well!'

Roderick Carver is by the Craft Hall in Combe, south of Archet. The left path from the Combe town centre climbs up the hill past the Craft Hall.
Edward Carver wants you to speak to his brother Roderick about taking up a crafting vocation.
Collected padded gloves

'I work up at the lumber-camp most days, and I'll tell you this: I'm always getting splinters. I hate it! These tiny little pieces of wood are always flying up from the wood as we cut it, and they get their revenge through annoyance! Small annoyances, to be sure, but after a full day of it, you'd be sick to death of the things, and I've been working there going on three weeks now!
'And that's not all! The axes we use have wooden handles, and if you don't get splinters from gripping those things, then I'm a dwarf! I'm just about at the end of my wits!
'If you know a tailor of even small skill, I could do with a pair of padded gloves. I'll pay you for the trouble, of course, with coins and a few materials, and I'll be in your debt!'

'You've brought me some padded gloves, haven't you? Let me see them!
'Ah, these are just the thing, ${PLAYER}! I'd like to see the splinters from my axe-hilt get through these! Or rather, I wouldn't!
'These things aren't much, but I hope you can use them for something as useful as these gloves you have given me!'
'Find a tailor for me, ${PLAYER}, and fast! I need some padded gloves or those thrice-cursed splinters will drive me right out of work!'
Bring padded gloves to Geoffrey Fuller
Collect padded gloves
Geoffrey Fuller Hates Splinters
Geoffrey Fuller has a real problem with the splinters he gets daily from working at the Combe lumber-camp.
'You saved my job at the lumber-camp, ${PLAYER}. Those splinters have met their match!'
'Those gloves were just the thing! I thank you again!'

Geoffrey Fuller is in the village of Combe.
Geoffrey is sick to death of the splinters he encounters every day during his work at the lumber-camp and has asked if you can bring him some padded gloves. A tailor should be able to make the gloves.

'Ah, a fine day to you! It's good to see the backs of the Blackwolds broken and peace settling over Archet once more. Now we can concern ourselves with less dire problems!
'Actually, you might be able to help with one of those problems, if you are interested. There seems to be an illness spreading among the local boars. And a terrible affliction it must be, for the beasts are more hostile than normal!
'We really must put an end to this illness, and the only way is to slay those afflicted. Would you do this?'

'Ah, you've taken care of the poor, blighted creatures. Every boar that has caught that foul plague will, in the end, have to be destroyed, but the few you've dealt with will slow the spread of the plague.
'Thank you!'
Disease Among the Boars

Constable Thistlewool is troubled by the disease spreading through the boars in the wake of the destruction wrought on Archet. The boars must be destroyed before they infect the other wildlife and eradicate the diminished food supply in Archet.

'Are you looking for those diseased boars? They should be roaming south and east of the gate.
'It may seem a bit harsh, slaying the beasts without any concern for their meat, but the spread of that illness is to slay those afflicted. It is a sad duty, but one that must be done!'

Diseased boars roam the lands to the south and east of Archet's gate.
Constable Thistlewool thinks that the best way to end the disease afflicting the local boars is to slay those already infected.

Constable Thistlewool can be found near the ruins of The Mad Badger Inn in Archet.
Constable Thistlewool will wish to hear of your success.
Collected Builder Earur's toolbox

'Working with wood has always been my trade, so I thought to put my hands to the rebuilding of Archet. I had loaded up my tools and set out, when suddenly this mad boar came out of nowhere and overturned my cart!
'It was all my son Borin and I could do to make it here to Archet, and we had to leave the tools in the wreckage of the cart! If you head south to the gate that leads to Combe, you might be able to recover my toolbox. I'd really appreciate it, and the folk of Archet are sure to be better for it as well -- the sooner I can get started, the sooner this town will be back to the way it was!
'Watch out for that boar, though. You might be able to get my toolbox without attracting his attention, but you'd need more luck than I have to manage it!'
'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER} -- now Borin and I can get to work rebuilding this town. Take these coins for your trouble.'
'I'd really appreciate it if you could recover the toolbox from the wreckage of my cart. It's south of Archet, near the gate to Combe, but be careful -- that mad boar might still be nearby!'
Bring Toolbox to Builder Earur
Collect Builder Earur's toolbox
Builder Earur
Builder Earur has asked you to recover the tools he lost when a mad boar overturned his cart on the road south of Archet.
'We'll have Archet rebuilt as good as new in no time!'
'I wonder what drove that boar mad? I've never seen anything like that before!'

Builder Earur's cart was overturned south of Archet, near the gate to Combe. Builder Earur is in Archet, north of the overturned cart.
Builder Earur has asked you to recover the toolbox he left in the wreckage of his cart, overturned by a mad boar south of Archet.

'Supplies here in Archet are limited and will certainly not suffice to repair the damage wrought upon the village. Now that I have my tools, I will be able to begin shoring the fences and repairing the buildings where I can.
'Archet will need more lumber if it is to recover completely from this attack. If you find yourself in Combe, to the south, seek out Taylor Green and let him know that I will need another order of wood from the lumber yard.
'If you've not been there before, listen well. The Combe Lumber Yard can be found by following the road south. Pass through the gate toward Combe and follow the road east up the hill. It will bend softly to the north east towards the Chetwood. There, in a soft dip before the North Chetwood you should find Taylor Green.'

'Archet's woes did not escape us here in Combe, and it's good what Earur is doing, no doubt in that. But the evil of the Blackwold has spread and now rests in the same wood where we need to collect the wood for Archet.
'I will see that we do what we can, but as you can see, we've troubles of our own.'
Message to Taylor Green

Earur wishes to aid the people of Archet and believes that there are enough supplies to begin the rebuilding process. To ensure that supplies do not dwindle too quickly he directed you to visit Taylor Green at the Combe Lumber Yard.
'Hurry along now. I'll get to work on what I can, but the lumber will not last long. Find Taylor Green at the Lumber yard east and north from the centre of Combe.'

Tell Taylor Green at the Lumber Mill in Combe that Builder Earur needs more wood in Archet.
Builder Earur mentioned that Archet would need more wood to completely rebuild. He asked you to visit the Combe Lumber Yard and tell Taylor Green that Archet needs more wood.
Gathered kingsfoil leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Oh, hello! Thank you again for your help the other night. I shudder to think what might have happened if you hadn't freed me!
'While he's putting on a brave face, I am quite worried about Amdir's knife-wound. I asked how I could help, and he told me of some sort of remedy from the Old Kings involving some plant called \qathelas.\q He said I might know it as kingsfoil, but I've always thought that was naught but a weed. He says that some grows outside of Archet, but I'm afraid of the wolves and Men that prowl out there.
'Amdir said the kingsfoil could be found south of Archet, near some old ruins the men call \qBronwe's Folly.\q After you gather some of the leaves, could you bring them back here to me?'
'Thank you! I hope the draught Amdir told me of will help him. I wouldn't have thought such a small wound would have caused him so much pain!'
'Do you have those kingsfoil leaves I asked for? Please, do hurry! I hate to think of that brave Amdir in such pain.'
Gather kingsfoil leaves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the kingsfoil leaves to Celandine Brandybuck
Must be completed prior to the \qIntroduction.\q
Intro: Remedy of the Old Kings
The Ranger Amdir told you that he had asked Celandine Brandybuck to gather an herb called \qathelas\q to make a remedy for his wound, in case the blade was poisoned.
'Kingsfoil grows to the south, near some old ruins the men call Bronwe's Folly. You should hurry...Amdir doesn't look too well.'
'I do hope that remedy helps. Amdir is so pale!'
'I owe Amdir so much for saving my life. I don't know what I'd do if he didn't get better.'

Kingsfoil grows south of Archet, near some old ruins called Bronwe's Folly.
Celandine Brandybuck, too frightened to pass beyond the gates of Archet, has asked you to collect kingsfoil leaves for her, so that she can prepare the remedy Amdir asked her to make.

Celandine Brandybuck can be found with Amdir outside The Mad Badger Inn in Archet.
You have gathered enough leaves for Amdir's remedy. You should return with them to Celandine Brandybuck.
Defeated wolves at the wolf-den (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Combe has always relied on this lumber camp for her livelihood, and now the people of Archet will be relying on us to supply the wood to rebuild their town, I expect. There's no shortage of work, that much is certain!
'We'll need to start taking down some of the trees to the north-east, along the cliffs, but there's a wolf-den up that way that endangers our workers!
'Could you deal with those wolves for me? It's not safe to chop down trees near there, and I'm afraid we might lose some of our best loggers. Follow the cliff wall. You'll see the wolves, or they'll see you.'

'You took care of the wolves! That will make harvesting the trees by that den much safer. Rebuilding the burned buildings in Archet will require more wood than we have, and that's only one village!
'I don't think the Blackwolds have the numbers to try anything funny around Combe, but there's still Staddle. Too many raids, and we'll need to cut down the whole Chetwood to make the repairs!'
Defeat wolves at the wolf-den (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Den of Wolves
Woodcutters from Combe moving further into the Chetwood in search of quality lumber are seeking protection from the local wildlife.
'The wolf-den is north-east of here. Just follow the bend of the cliff wall, and you'll see it. It's not far.'
'Thank you for dealing with the wolves. It should be safer for us to do our jobs now.'
'That wolf den caused us a great deal of trouble before you showed up.'

The wolf-den is set in the cliff wall north-east of the lumber camp.
Woodcutter Taylor Green is concerned that the wolves roaming the woods to the north-east may be a threat to the woodcutters and has asked you to cull their numbers.

Woodcutter Taylor Green waits at the lumber camp to the south-west, north of the guard-house.
As Woodcutter Green requested, you put the fear of Men into the wolves of the Chetwood. He will be pleased to hear of your success.
Collected Sally's chain

'Have you heard that Archet gave them Blackwold villains what-for? Kicked 'em right out, they did, and good on 'em! If little old Archet can manage it, I say Combe can do one better, and sweep them Blackwolds out o' the Chetwood for good!
'Now I lost my Sally's chain when them brigands took over my farm. She's been gone for many a year, but that chain always did bring me comfort. One o' them Blackwolds probably picked it up, and I want it back! Farm's far to the east -- just follow the road past all them brigand campfires.
'Eh, what's that? No, it's a chain, not a necklace. What a queer question.'

'You found my Sally's chain and showed those Blackwold villains a thing or two, I don't doubt it! A lifetime o' thanks, ${PLAYER}!
'Ah, Sally was a good hound. We'd go hunting in the fall, and she could sniff out a coney from what seemed near a mile! It's good to have her chain back. It's all I've got left o' her, now.
'Take these coins for your trouble, ${PLAYER}, with my thanks.'
'My old farm is east of here, deep in the Chetwood. You'll pass by a lot of those brigand camps on the road, and the farm is on a small rise.'
Bring Sally's chain to Old Bauman
Collect Sally's chain
Old Bauman's Farm
The Blackwold brigands seized Old Bauman's farm during the early days of their uprising.
'I can hear her barking, barking away at some old squirrel. You get 'em, Sally! Ha ha!'
'Sally was a good dog, and no mistake.'

Old Bauman's farm lies far to the east of Combe, beyond the brigand camps in the Chetwood, at the end of the eastward path. Old Bauman is at the logging camp, south of the Chetwood, east of Combe.
Old Bauman lost his farm to the Blackwolds when they retreated from Archet, and he would like you to go there and retrieve his Sally's chain for him.
Collected Filbert's handkerchief

'My Uncle Filbert and I were having tea and discussing the state of things in Bree-land -- about how the folk in Archet showed the Blackwold brigands a thing or two -- when Uncle Filbert stood up and said, \qSomeone ought do something about these villains. I'm going to give them a piece of my mind.\q And then he left, without even finishing his tea!
'Up the road in the woods east of this camp, past the brigands' watchfires, there's some ruins where the Blackwolds are holed up. Uncle Filbert has probably gone there to have a word with them. Though I don't think he will make the full journey, he's not as young as he once was.
'If he has, he's likely got himself into trouble. I dare go no further to search for him, but could you go look for him and make sure he's all right?'

'It's good to hear that Uncle Filbert is all right. He always says that I'll develop good hobbit-sense when I get older, but if he's any example, I'm not sure I will!
'Thank you for looking in on him, ${PLAYER}.'

'Finally, someone respectable! I was beginning to think no one out here in the woods had any manners! I simply couldn't stand by any longer while the Blackwolds have their way in the Chetwood! I marched right in and told them just what I think of their sort.
'They laughed me right out of their camp! \qGo back to Hobbiton, little boy!\q they said to me! I've never been spoke to like this, never! I wanted to leave, something in that big ruin is just a bit off, I say!
'One ruffian, Cole Sickleleaf -- he used to be a nice boy -- took my handkerchief. Could you bring it back to me? He ran off to the ruins all the way to the east, between the frightening ruins to the north and that Skunkwood's farm.'

'You, at least, have some decency. I thank you very much for returning my handkerchief and bid you a good day, as civilized folk are wont to do!
'I'm going to stay here and keep an eye on these impolite troublemakers. Maybe it's the Tookish blood I get from my mother's side of the family, but it'll take more than insults to send me back to town unsatisfied! Perhaps my presence here will remind these ruffians what it means to live in Bree-land!
'If you can tell my nephew, Posco, that I'm fine, I'd appreciate it. Good day!'
'One of those brigands inside the ruins has picked up my handkerchief. I just know it!'
Bring the handkerchief to Filbert Burrows
Collect Filbert's handkerchief
Posco's Uncle
Posco Burrows is concerned that his uncle, Filbert Burrows, has gone deep into the Chetwood to 'have a word' with the Blackwold brigands and wants to make sure he has not gotten himself into trouble.
'Uncle Filbert is probably sitting on a stump or rock right now! I would wager he never made it by the split in the road!'
'I'm going to keep an eye on these Blackwold villains. I don't trust 'em one bit! You go back to the Lumber Camp by Combe and tell my nephew Posco that everything's fine, and I'll be back soon.'
'It won't be long before these Blackwold brigands are kicked out of the Chetwood, if there's any justice!'
'Can you believe the brass of these Blackwold brigands?'
'Uncle Filbert is sure to get himself into trouble, sooner or later.'
'Uncle Filbert is a grand hobbit, but he's always challenging authority.'

Filbert Burrows should be somewhere along the road east of Combe heading towards the Chetwood.
Posco Burrows has asked you to look for his uncle, Filbert, and make sure he is unharmed.

Cole Sickleleaf is at the ruins between the main Blackwold encampment and Skunkwood's Farm.
You found Posco Burrow's uncle, Filbert, sitting on a stump at the crossroads in the Chetwood. He wants you to collect a handkerchief taken by Cole Sickleleaf.

Filbert Burrows is waiting at the crossroads in the Chetwood.
You should return Filbert Burrow's handkerchief to him and convince him to leave the area.

Posco Burrows is waiting for you at the Lumber Camp by Combe.
Filbert Burrows, determined to remain where he is until the Blackwolds relent, has asked you to return to Combe to tell his nephew, Posco Burrows, that he is fine.
Collected rowan hammer
Collected rowan haft (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hello there, do you have a moment? I'm sorry to bother you, but I thought I would ask this of you, just in case you know something about woodworking.
'Mason Thorne has charged me with purchasing supplies for the camp here, but I've had a difficult time finding woodworkers willing to sell me some of the supplies we need.
'If you don't mind, could you bring me some supplies made of rowan wood? A rowan hammer and some rowan hafts would be perfect. I'd really appreciate it, and I'd pay you for them, of course, with coins and some odds and ends!'
'You have the items crafted from rowan wood I requested? Thank you so much! These look to be just what Mason wanted me to procure for the lumber-camp. I'll pay you, just as we agreed. Here you go.'

'No luck finding someone to supply rowan hammers and hafts yet? Me either! You'd think that Combe would be crawling with woodworkers, but it seems that everyone is out of stock or is just charging too much!'
Bring a rowan hammer and three rowan hafts to Ember Hayes

Supplies for the Lumber-camp
The Combe lumber-camp is in need of supplies with which its workers can increase the production of useable timber.
'Thank you for the supplies.'
'Thank you again for obtaining the supplies I needed.'

'There you are, ${PLAYER}. The order came in a few moments ago. Take this key and claim your order.
'You'll want to use this on the pile of soft wood.'

'Everything looks to be in order ${PLAYER}. One order of soft wood. We'll get some woodcutters out into the woods soon enough.
'Give us a few hours -- six ought to do -- then return and speak to Woodcutter Hornbeam. He'll be the one handling your order.'
'Without a work order, we won't be able to do what you ask. Of course, I do sell work orders.

'I joined up with the guard when I made it to Archet, but now I'm stuck watching this lodge and can't get back what's mine! I'd be most grateful if you could go to Blackwolds' Roost to the south of here and get my satchel back!'

'Hello there! Enjoying a nice stroll through the Marshes? I don't meet too many folk that can stand the smell, or the bugs, or the damp, so it's always nice to meet a kindred spirit! Say hello, Sniken! Who's a good boy, then?'
The Neekerbreeker in the cage responds only with an angry clicking sound.
'That wasn't nice, Sniken. I don't know what's gotten into you.
'He might be hungry. In fact, he might be wanting his favourite food: sickle-fly wings. If you kill a few of the greater sickle-flies, you might find enough wings to satisfy Sniken. That might cheer him up!'

'Those wings are just the kind that Sniken likes. You saved me some trouble hunting down those greater sickle-flies.
'Now, here's a treat for you! I'll give you a key to my chest over there. I put all the treasures I find in the Marshes in there. Maybe you'll find something you like!
'And the next time you take a pleasant stroll through the Midgewater Marshes, stop by and say hello!'

'The greater sickle-flies here in the southern Midgewater Marshes are a noisy lot, what their swooping around and collecting the midges in the air. My neeker here, Sniken, loves their wings, probably his favouritest food about.

'You wouldn't happen to be a jeweller, would you? Or maybe you're friends with one? I'm in a real situation, you see, and I need someone to fashion an amethyst ring for me...and soon!
'I had some business at the Forsaken Inn, helping unload some of the crates from a delivery of foodstuffs sent from Bree, and somewhere along the way, I lost my wedding ring. My wedding ring! My wife is going to be furious!
'If Verity sees that I don't have it, well, I don't even want to think about that! That's why I need the services of a jeweller -- I need an amethyst ring, and fast! I can't go back to Bree without one! I have any number of useful things to offer, if you'll just help me!'

'This amethyst ring looks just like my lost wedding ring, ${PLAYER}! Verity will never know the difference!
'You've really helped me out, my friend. Here, let me give you these coins and other odds and ends along with my thanks!'
'I really need a jeweller to make me an amethyst ring, ${PLAYER}! My wife Verity is going to kill me if I don't have my wedding ring when I get home to Bree!'

'You've really helped me out, ${PLAYER}, and I won't forget it!'

'Goblins! They swept in from the north and overran the ruins in the south, then were pressed into service by the strange Orcs in the north. Their leader, a cunning, little runt called Nishrûk, hides in the ruins south-east of the Inn.
'You've likely fought the goblins, by now. Would you be willing to make a strike against their leader? If you are, I'd advise you to gather friends to assist you. The goblins deeper in the ruins are far stronger, even than the Orcs...it's why they haven't been pressed into service.
'Go far to the eastern section of the ruins and kill Nishrûk. I'll have a reward for you when the deed is done.'

'Heroes come from unlikely places. You've done very well, ${PLAYER}. Were I younger, I would have waded into those goblins on my own.
'While we may have dealt a blow against the goblins here in the west, it's unlikely that the tribe will scatter to the wind. They're well organized for goblins, almost as if there is a purpose to their actions. Something tells me that the Lonelands is in for bad times...well, worse than usual.
'We'll survive -- we always do -- and thanks to you we may be able to handle the goblins near our Inn. I promised you a gift. This was mine when I was still young enough to use it...I pass it now to you. May it treat you as well as it did me.'
The Goblin Leader
The goblins in the ruins to the south-east of The Forsaken Inn hearken to the call of a ferocious leader, who could bring ruin to the inhabitants of the inn.
'Nishrûk won't be troubling anyone anymore...good work, ${PLAYER}!'
'These goblins are a problem, but I daresay they'll be easier to handle now that you've killed Nishrûk.'

The goblin's leader, Nishrûk, dwells in a Goblin fort built among the ruins south-east of The Forsaken Inn.

'Greetings, young ${RACE}. I'm the Constable here at the Forsaken Inn. My body's too old for adventure, but my mind is young enough to know there's work to be done around here.
'Up north, beyond Weathertop, there are wolves and Orcs in the Midgewater Pass, and boars scattered throughout Annunlos, all causing no end of trouble. I've a bit of a proposition for you: clear out the threats. If you bring me proof of your noble deeds, I will see that you get a fair reward.
'Are you interested?'

'Wolf-tails, boar-tusks, and Orc-shields...you are quite the skilled warrior. It may seem a menial task to you, but believe me when I say this is much appreciated.
'The people here at the Inn struggle enough without worrying about the wildlife and evils that are spreading unhindered. Ever since those lights appeared atop Weathertop, we've had one trouble after another, and there isn't a sign of relief in sight.
'Take this small reward...you've earned it.'
'Are you taking a rest so soon or aren't you up to the task? I need you to take care of those wolves, Orcs, and boars.'

'You likely know by now that there are Orcs in the south holding vigil on the ruins where once Men stood proud...and foolish. Now disease threatens to spread from Ost Cyrn. The Orcs have no concern for what they breed in their filth. Meat is left to rot and spoil and the innards of the fetid dead bloat and give birth to all manner of disease and corruption.
'We must seek to curb the plague before it spreads, and so I turn once again to you. There is only one way to destroy the plague-bearing filth left by the Orcs: fire.
'Take this tinder and flint and make your way to Ost Cyrn in the south, where the Orcs dwell. Set fire to the bloated corpses and barrels of filth therein.'

'You have our gratitude, friend. It pains many to know that the Orcs have claimed the lives of many Eglain who fought against them.
'We will breathe easier knowing that the winds will not carry pestilence from the South.'

'Death, pestilence, and terror stalk us, ${PLAYER}. Two have been dealt with, thanks to your effort, the third still soars above us with ever watchful eyes.
'It is the eyes that I want. I speak of the gore-crows, the black birds with sharp beaks and piercing eyes. They are spies along the road east and west from this place, and they are ever vigilant.
'Take their eyes and they cannot see and what they cannot see they cannot spread to their masters, the Orc and half-breed. Seek the gore-crows along the Great East Road and bring me their eyes to prove that the creatures will no longer speak of us to their fell masters.'

'Dead, yes? No more will these eyes spy down on us from above. Can we not find a bit of peace in that? I think that we shall.
'You have done us a great service once again, ${PLAYER}. There is little else needed for us to become well-prepared for what lay ahead.'

'While they fly through the sky, the gore-crows may see us here at Ost Guruth. I can tell you, ${PLAYER}, no matter how strong our people may appear, we cannot withstand an onslaught from the dwarves, half-breeds, or Orcs here in the Lone-lands. Their spies must be blinded.'

'Always we struggle to survive -- and we have done well in all the years I have dwelled at Ost Guruth -- but this is something the like of which I've not seen before. With the Elders working to defend against the evil in Agamaur, it falls to the rest of us to see to other defences.
'This, my friend, is where I come to you. Our numbers are few, and those capable of wielding a weapon are best kept close to Ost Guruth. You, however, are able to walk freely through the land and assist us in ways in which we cannot help ourselves.
'In the west, beneath the shadow of Amon Ros, lie great nests of venomous spiders among the ruins. Some are more potent than others. Now we have ways passed down through the ages of distilling the venom of the lesser spiders and making a medicine which helps to cure poison. If the venom is too potent it cannot be distilled. I need you to collect the poison sacs from Ruin-web hunters and ambushers and bring them to me.'
'You have done well, my friend. This will aid us in preventing the deaths of many should we find ourselves beset by spiders.'
'In the west, beneath the shadow of Amon Ros, slay the less deadly of the spiders and take their venom sacs. The crawlers and the trappers should suit our needs well.'

'No more spies among the clouds, my friend. You have done your part, and I can now turn my attention back to keeping the Eglain fed and watered.
'We had a pen of boars once, poached now by Orcs and spiders in the west and south. Frideric means to make peace and asks such a meagre price to find that peace, but I lied about our stores. They will not hold long, and we need meat and water soon, or we will face famine.
'In the east, along the Road, you will find boars. The boars must be killed for their meat and bellies. Their bellies will make good bladders for water, and the meat will be cured and put aside for our winter stores.'

'The bellies will be cleaned and the meat will be cured and salted. I will be able to fill our water barrels and feed my people.
'You have my thanks, friend.'
'Quickly now! I will need haunches of meat and boar-stomachs. We need better ways of carrying the water back to Ost Guruth.'

'All that you have done proves your honour. I shall not doubt your intentions again, but I shall ask one more favour of you.
'I am sure you have seen that a variety of spiders stalk the shadows of Amon Ros. You may also have seen the elders of this vile brood. It is they who are to be feared the most.
'I ask now that you return to Amon Ros and slay the elders. They have lived for too long, preying upon the helpless, and must be destroyed.'

'This news will ease the suffering of many. Though it seems a task without thought, we are not a people accustomed to venturing against such foes.
'You are a hero to the Eglain and deserve all that you shall receive in reward.'
Speak with Tortwil at Ost Guruth
Elders in the Shadows

Since long before Orcs and undead crept into the Lone-lands, the Eglain has had to deal with the menace of spiders dwelling within the ruins across the lonely stretch of Eriador. Now as the spiders are driven from the depths of their ruined homes they creep closer and closer to Ost Guruth and threaten the Eglain who dwell there.

The elders of the brood can be found in Amon Ros, west of Ost Guruth.
You earned Tortwil's trust through your efforts against the spiders, but he asked one last favour of you: that you return to Amon Ros and slay the elders of the spider-brood.

Tortwil awaits your return in Ost Guruth, east of Amon Ros.
Tortwil will be pleased to hear of your victory against the spiders of Amon Ros.
Defeated spiders in Amon Ros (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Have you been to the ruins of Amon Ros, west of Ost Guruth, and seen the vile brood that dwells there? No doubt you've seen spindly crawlers weaving their webs and trapping their prey, which happens to be anything that has life within its veins. Crawling monstrosities is what they are! Nothing good comes from them, and I have seen too many fall prey to their hidden nests.
'I have heard rumour that you are here to aid the Eglain, but I should like proof that you speak the truth. Hunt the spiders of Amon Ros. Slay them and return to me.
'These foul vermin do not deserve the life they take so freely. Bring my vengeance upon them!'

'I have not been wholly forthcoming with you, ${PLAYER}, but I was afraid you might not be as honourable as rumour tells. But I shall now tell you my tale, so that you may understand my hatred.
'I was at Naerost when the goblins came. My son and I fled as the Wargs and goblins poured into the ruins, slaughtering all who could not escape them. My son stumbled at the edge of a ruin and slipped into the chasm below. I struggled to reach him, but there was no hope, the spiders were upon him nearly as soon as he touched their webs.
'They took my son from me as they took his mother many years back. My heart is heavy with shame for not telling you the truth.'

'Filthy creatures! Snatching the life from whatever they ensnare. They deserve death.'

'By my word, you now know that my wife and son fell to the brood you visited my vengeance upon, but they were not the only ones to fall to the spiders in that vale. The Eglain have lost so many through the years. Other families have lost siblings and loved ones to the spiders and, more recently, to the Wargs stalking the wild.
'I have another request for you, which may prove fruitless, yet I hope it shall yield solace for many. In Amon Ros, where the spiders dwell, you likely saw many sacs of eggs. These sacs will bring more evil into the world and the grief will continue.
'Will you go and destroy the eggs before they hatch? The spiders' numbers grow each day, while the good folk of Ost Guruth dwindle.'
'Your efforts to kerb the spread of the spiders may bring at least some respite from our grief. You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}.'

'It is a great and wonderous thing that you have rescued me, ${PLAYER}. I had feared I would be lost here forever.

A terrible sense of dread overcomes you

'There have been worrisome signs for the past few months that something has not been right in the Trollshaws, but wherever I search I am unable to find the cause. And once more I have found what seems to be a symptom rather than a cure: the wolves that prowl the Bruinen Gorges have been greatly disturbed, but by what I cannot determine.
'It is true that servants of the Enemy pursued a small company along the road not more than two months ago, but the wolves have become more unruly in recent days, and I cannot determine the reason.
'Travel south-east into the Bruinen Gorges and seek out the wolf den in the south-western valley. Defeat as many wolves as you can and put an end to their pack-leader. It may be that you will find some clue I have missed in the deep reaches of the valley.'

'I am glad to see you return from the valley of wolves, ${PLAYER}, and your story helps me to piece together what may have crazed the wolves. Only a terrible evil could have scarred the land in such a way for it to be felt so strongly in its absence.
'Whatever it was, it has moved on, though the memory of it is enough to trouble the minds of the wolves. Any more than this I cannot say. Do not return to that valley, ${PLAYER}. There is little we can do to heal the mark that has been left -- only time can do that.'
Defeat wolves in Drauglad (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Explore the deep reaches of Drauglad

The Elf Fimgris has noticed the wolves of the Bruinen Gorges have been acting queer and wonders what could have put such rage and fear into their eyes.

'The Bruinen Gorges are to the south-east of Thorenhad and the wolves I am concerned about are in Drauglad, its most south-western valley. Defeat the wolves and their pack-leader, and travel into the deepest reaches of their dens. Perhaps you will find some sign of the evil that has caused this new madness in the creatures.'
'Only time can heal that valley, so marked by evil as it is.'
'Do not return to the valley of the wolves. It is not safe.'

You have investigated the wolf-den in Drauglad and defeated some of the crazed animals, but the sense of dread there was almost palpable. You should return to Fimgris with your report.

'The snowbeasts are a threat near the source of the Bruinen, but they have not spread throughout the mountains as much as other creatures. It is easier to guide travellers past them in a way that is impossible with the more widespread threats.
'This is not true of the bears that prowl the slopes, not only near the source of the Bruinen, but also further east among the high crags beneath Pinnath Fenui and as far south as the Giant Halls around Iorbar.
'If you can defeat many of the bears in each of these areas, the slopes will be made safer for travellers. Watch yourself as you hunt the bears of these regions, for they may surprise you with their numbers and their savagery.'
'You have become a true foe of the savage bears that prowl the mountains, ${PLAYER}, and I am glad of it! Every beast that is slain makes the wild country safer for those who must journey there.'

Hidden by Fur and Snow
Malthenor is concerned about the bears that prowl the mountains and wants you to fight against them in many areas.

'Bears can be found throughout the Misty Mountains, but if you can defeat the creatures near the Bruinen Source, the High Crags, and the Giant Halls, travellers along the road will be made a good deal safer.'

'If you are heading into the mountains, friend ${RACE}, you should know the dangers that await you. All manner of creatures can be found among the drifts, bear and aurochs and mammoth, and they are more ferocious than their cousins in the low-lands.
'More dangerous even than these creatures of the wild are the deadly snowbeasts that prowl among the high ridges. When the snow flies about your head, listen for a howling in the air -- it may be more than the cry of the storm, and the claws of the snowbeast may be not far off!
'If your travels bring you to the source of the Bruinen, slay what snowbeasts you may. You will be making the mountain passes safer for those who must pass that way, if you are able to come back again.'

'You have survived the claws of the snowbeasts and returned with a tale to tell, ${PLAYER}! I am glad to hear it and to tell you that you have performed a great service for those forced to travel into the mountains.'
Defeat snowbeasts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Malthenor has taken it upon herself to warn travellers passing into the mountains of the dangers that await within.

'Snowbeasts are ferocious creatures that fight with tooth and claw on the high ridges, ${PLAYER}, and they are a grave danger to those forced to travel through the mountains. They must be defeated wherever they are found.'

'Everyone knows there are goblins in the Misty Mountains, but few know the way to Goblintown. Lord Glóin has been there, but he doesn't often talk of the adventure and you'd be wise not to press him on the subject.
'The goblins come out of Goblintown with their foul wargs, and hunt for prey among the high passes. The mountains are home to a great many of these wargs, savage beasts of teeth and claws. If you are a proven warrior, you might make them the prey, rather than the predator.
'Look for them around Pinnath Fenui, far to the east, and slay the foul hunters. We cannot allow them to prey on even the few travellers in this land.'
'I am glad you have returned from your hunt, ${PLAYER}! Wargs are dangerous prey, and you have slain many!'

'The wargs of Pinnath Fenui have been a great worry since we came to this place.'
'The goblins and the wargs are close allies, and a great trouble to us.'
'Thank you for your aid, ${PLAYER}. The wargs are more wary than they were.'

'It's my job to keep these passes safe for travellers, ${PLAYER}, but especially for the trade my kin wants to reestablish through these mountains. And there are threats everywhere!
'While you were away, I prepared another sign. This one warns travellers away from the good-for-nothing, oath-breaking, false-speaking, thin-bearded Dourhands that have taken over the keep in the pass of Gabilazan. That wouldn't all fit on the sign, so I shortened it to \qBeware of Evil Dwarves.\q
'If you don't mind helping me out again, I'd ask you to post this sign outside the northern entrance to their keep. Head east from here and cut through the narrow gap north of the frozen pond, and you'll arrive at a path. Follow the path east until it comes to an end, then strike south-west a short distance. A slope rises up to Gabilazan and the Dourhand keep. There should be a suitable post you can affix the sign to.'

'You have returned, ${PLAYER}, and I know I need not ask if you posted the sign I gave you, for you are a trustworthy ${RACE} indeed!
'I have fashioned another sign for you to post! I see from your eye that you expected it and are eager to assist again!'

'Evil dwarves have occupied the keep that guards the pass of Gabilazan, and you need to post that sign before the northern entrance of the pass to warn travellers of the danger.
'To reach Gabilazan, head east of Glóin's camp and pass through the narrow opening north of the frozen pond. Follow the path there until it comes to an end and strike south-west across the snow to the slope that rises to Gabilazan. There should be a post you can affix the sign to somewhere before the keep.'

'You have done admirably with the task of posting those signs for me, ${PLAYER}, and I am sure you will exceed my expectations with this latest one!
'This sign warns travellers to beware of giants. I realize this might seem a little obvious, but the trouble with giants is that they can usually see you from a good deal further away than you can see them. One of the Elves in Rivendell told me a story about a giant that could fell an aurochs with a single stone from a distance of two miles! I'm not worried for myself, of course, but if any traders begin passing through the mountains, we'll want them to have at least some warning before entering giant country. Two miles, at least!
'Two passes run south through the mountains. You've already seen the pass of Gabilazan, but the pass of Rakhâs-bizar is further to the east. Travel south through Rakhâs-bizar and post this sign. You should find a suitable post before leaving the pass, and beware! I won't be responsible if you run afoul of the giants south of the pass!
'In fact, these giants are so dangerous, I would recommend that you go with friends to attempt this task.'

'You have returned earlier than I expected, ${PLAYER}, and I have not had time to prepare any more signs!
'Perhaps I will come up with something else for you to do, friend ${RACE}, but it will take some time. In the meantime, you have my hearty thanks!'

'I have not yet thought of another sign to make, ${PLAYER}.'
'I will come up with something for you to do, never fear!'
'The mountains may not be safer, but at least travellers will now know their dangers.'

'Would you say you are skilled with hammer and nail, friend? It doesn't really matter, but it would be a help if you were. Some of my kin have been looking to get the trade passing through the mountains again, and I'm doing my part to help.
'The trouble is that the mountains are dangerous even in summer, and during winter only a fool would expect to come through without incident. And there are threats in the mountains beyond the cold and the snows -- goblins and worse!
'There's an old keep far to the north, and evil Men have overtaken it for their own purposes. It's a ways north of the road, but I don't want any dwarves to get turned about in a storm and happen upon it unawares. I'd appreciate it if you could post this warning sign I've made in front of the slope leading up to the keep. There's already a suitable post at the base of the slope -- just affix the sign to it and hurry back. Head north along the road, and then leave the road and cut north and east across the snowy fields. It's quite a ways, so be prepared for a good hike!'
'You have returned, ${PLAYER}! I trust that you have posted my sign? I am glad to hear it, for now I have another!'

'There is a dangerous plant spreading from the goblin cave north-west of here. The dwarves call it \qSkorgrím's Bloom\q after that vile dwarf slain many years ago when Edhelion fell.
'This foul weed is foreign to Ered Luin, and its spread must be contained. The plant is quite deadly, and I fear that many unknowing creatures will be poisoned if they graze upon it.
'We cannot wipe it out in one blow, but we can halt its spread. The plants can be found flowering along the path leading to Mirkstone Tunnels, north-west of here. Uproot some of these plants, and you will be rewarded.'
'Thank you, kind ${RACE}. If we can keep the plants from spreading, perhaps they will die out on their own. The creatures of Thorin's Gate are safer thanks to you.'

'Welcome and well met! I could use your help, if you have a moment. I've a bit of a problem -- nothing terrible, mind you, but difficult for this old dwarf. You see, it's my son, Gísli. He's a good fellow and all, but he is young and doesn't have the experience of his elders. He has just received his first post, down at Noglond in the Vale of Thráin.
'I want to send Gísli his favourite meal so he knows I'm thinking about him, but I don't have the most important ingredient: Cave-claw legs! If you can bring me a batch, I just know Gísli will be pleased! You can find cave-claws in the old mine west of Thorin's Halls.
'You've not had a good meal, until you've tasted my stew!'

'I am at your service, ${PLAYER}! I'll just add these to the stew...give me a few minutes.
'There we are! Could you take this meal to Gísli? You can find him south of here at Noglond, the way-station in the Vale of Thráin. Just follow the road south!
'Gísli will be pleased, I am sure.'
'I have started preparing the stew, but I need those cave-claw legs to finish it, ${PLAYER}. They are the most important ingredient!'

'Not again! This is the third meal my father has sent me in as many days! When will he realize I'm a grown dwarf, and not a child to be coddled and fretted over?
'Ah, you're not to blame. Thank you for the food. Maybe someday my father will realize I'm not the thin-bearded dwarf of sixty he remembers.'

'I m so proud of Gísli! Perhaps someday he will be a guard here at Thorin's Halls.'

'I was a jeweller of no small skill some time ago, and though I have now put down my tools, the pieces I fashioned during my youth are still precious to me.
'It is thus with sadness that I report to you that one of the necklaces I crafted but a few years ago has lost its setting! It has been too long for me to fashion a replacement, but if you know a jeweller who could do so, I would appreciate it.
'Bring me an agate necklace, and I will pay you a fair sum. I have a few small items as well, including some leftover gemstones, with which I would be willing to part.'

'You have done as I asked, and brought to me an agate necklace. I thank you for it and give to you these coins and materials!
'I must admit, however, that this necklace does not seem as special to me as the one that I crafted with my own hands. Perhaps I will come to appreciate this one, but I had not expected to feel this way. That's a little strange, isn't it?
'Thank you for it, friend. I am sure I will feel differently in the morning.'
'Were you planning on bringing me an agate necklace or not?'

Nefi Gemcutter has broken the setting of a necklace he once fashioned, and desires a replacement.
'I did not think that necklace meant so much to me. How strange.'
'I did not mean to offend. The necklace you brought me in replacement is appreciated.'

'The Lonely Mountain seems so far away. Ah, how I wish I were there now! Our larders here in the Blue Mountains are scant, and we Longbeards are going to be here for some time.
'If you want to make yourself useful, go out and hunt some of the aurochs for me. There are plenty of those beasts wandering west of Frerin's Court to last all season, and we could use the meat.'

'Bravo, ${PLAYER}! We'll have a grand feast tonight and salt the rest of the haunches to last the rest of the season.
'Here, you may find use of some of this as well. It will keep you strong. If ever you are in need of such provisions, come and see me.'

'Aurochs herds are all about west of Frerin's Court. You can't miss them, what with their wooly hides and large horns. I reckon a half-dozen should do the trick. Don't want to take more than we need!'
Bring the aurochs-meat to Bogi

Stocking the Larder
Bogi is concerned that the Longbeards do not have enough food for a prolonged stay. He needs aurochs meat to help stock the larder at Thorin's Hall.
'We'll have a fine feast of Aurochs meat tonight!'

Herds of aurochs are found throughout the hills to the west of Frerin's Court.
Kill some of the beasts and bring their meat back to Bogi.
Collected bronze leggings

'I don't know what the problem is, stranger. My father was a metalworker, and my father's father was a metalworker, but I do not seem to have inherited their skill with hammer and anvil. I do not know where it could have gone, for I have no brothers, but that skill certainly has avoided me!
'You see, I decided it was time to make a new pair of bronze leggings for myself, but I did something wrong with the heat of the fire and my hammer-blows and ended up with something more akin to a belt. A belt fused in on itself, with something like a sleeve on one end. I can't wear that! And I wouldn't wear it even if I could figure out how exactly to try it on!
'If you know a metalworker of even small skill, I'll pay you for some bronze leggings. I'll give you my leftover materials as well! And don't tell anyone about my...mishap...if you don't mind.'

'These will do very well, ${PLAYER}! I don't understand how mine could have turned out so very differently, because these seem easy enough to make. I just don't understand.
'Here are the coins and materials I promised you. Take with them my thanks!'
'I need bronze leggings, ${PLAYER}. You haven't forgotten, have you?'

'Could you go and get my pick for me...and while you're at it, kill off a few of those cave-claws, so I can continue my digging in peace.
'The cave is to the east in the Winterheights. Hurry now! I think I was nearing a vein of gold when they drove me out!'

'Ah, there she is! Thank you, ${PLAYER}. But I've sad news...a friend of mine told me that cave's been tapped dry. There's naught but fool's gold in there.
'But don't you worry...I'll find my claim one of these days!'
'Did you find my pick-axe? I'll need that if I'm to find my claim. You've no knowing how many years I've been digging, trying to find a stake of my own.'

Flosi, an elderly dwarf-prospector, lost his pick while digging in an old cave infested by cave-claws.
'My pick-axe must still be in the old cave east in the Winterheights.'
'Well, the mine may be tapped dry, but at least you found my pick-axe!'
'You've my thanks for retrieving my pick-axe ${PLAYER}.'

The cave is east of Thorin's Hall, in the Winterheights.
Certain that he was nearing a vein of gold before being driven out of the cave, Flosi asked you to retrieve his pick-axe, as well as clear some of the cave-claws from the cave.

Flosi is on the stairs in front of the main gate to Thorin's Hall.
You should return the pick-axe to Flosi and let the old prospector know it should be safe for him to return to the cave.
Defeated cave-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The cave-claws are destroying the land with their rampant digging. Without some way to reduce their numbers, I fear the ground will collapse beneath our feet. Even the Dourhands are aware of the menace.
'If a few of the scourges were killed, it would prevent further damage.
'You will find the cave-claws around the caves and ruins of Thorin's Gate or inside the cave at Winterheight to the south of here.'

'Blasted nuisances! Even the dullest dwarf knows that you don't over-mine a cavern. Riddle it with holes, and the whole floor is apt to collapse. Well, the cave-claws don't know that and their incessant digging is going to be the ruin of us all!
'What? You expect the Dourhands to do something about it? A clever joke, but I'm not laughing. Can you give us some help dealing with the pests? The cave-claws, mind you...not the Dourhands. Although....
'Be that as it may, the Rockbelly Pit is overrun with cave-claws. Head east and up the hill to Winterheight. The entrance to the Pit is there.'
'We cannot undo the damage wrought by the cave-claws, but their future impact on the caverns will be minimal. Thank you, ${PLAYER} for all you have done.'
'You certainly took care of that problem. I'll see to it that the Dourhands do their part from now on.'
Defeat cave-claws (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak to ${RACE:Selur[D]|Orodlin}
Fear of Collapse
The stone beneath Thorin's Gate is honeycombed by cave-claw burrows. If the damage continues, the entire area could be weakened enough to collapse in on itself.
'The mindless beasts dig and dig without a care for the damage they do. Someone must kill the cave-claws before they do any more damage.'
'Cave-claws! I hates them! Always ripping up the ground, leaving piles of earth in their wake. And who has to clean up their mess? The Longbeards, that's who! Give us a hand, will you?'
'Thank you for your assistance with our cave-claw problem.'
'You did a good thing back there!'

Cave-claws are found near the buildings and caves to the east of Thorin's Gate and inside the Rockbelly Pit caves near Winterheight, south of the Elf-camp.
${RACE:Selur[D]|Orodlin} asked you to defeat cave-claws found throughout Thorin's Gate.
${RACE:Selur can be found at the Berghold.[D]|Orodlin can be found in the ruins of the old Elf-refuge of Edhelion.}

'You there! I sent Vífill to cut a quarter-cord of firewood for Noglond, but he hasn't come back. See if you can find him.
'Just follow the road to the west. There's a clearing out that way where we gather our wood.
'Be wary though...who knows what's delayed Vífill.'
'Goblins, here in Vale of Thráin? Nay, that's not likely. Surely not!'

'Ha! Well met! I was wondering when Grímkell would send someone. I was in the clearing, cutting wood for Noglond, when goblins fell on me from the shadows of the trees.
'I managed to kill two and wounded the last, enough to drive it off, but was wounded myself in the fight. The foul creature ran off to the south. Tell Grímkell what happened and to send help!'
Find Vífill
Cutting Cords
Grímkell, the commander at Noglond, sent one of his guards, Vífill, to cut some firewood and is concerned because Vífill has failed to return.
'Vífill still hasn't returned from the firewood grove just up the road.'
'I'll be fine...leave me. Grímkell must be told about the goblins immediately!'

Vífill is somewhere in the firewood grove down the road west of Noglond.
Grímkell has asked you to go out and search for Vífill.

Grímkell is at Noglond, east of the firewood grove.
Vífill tells you to inform Grímkell of the presence of goblins in the firewood grove.

'I don't doubt Vífill made up his story of goblins after hitting himself with his own axe!
'Oh? You think he told the truth? Not likely! But if you're so sure he's met up with goblins, maybe you can go find them.
'The goblins of the Blue Mountains sometimes carry these little things, fetishes I guess you might call them. Bring me one of their fetishes, and maybe I'll lend Vífill's tale my ear.'

'What's this? Oh....
'I must beg your pardon. It seems you and Vífill were right. Let's see now. Goblins in the Vale?'
'No goblins, eh? I knew Vífill made it up.'
Bring the fetish to Grímkell
Hunting Goblins
Grímkell scoffed at Vífill's story of goblins in the Vale of Thráin, blaming Vífill's injury instead upon his own clumsiness.

'What? He doesn't believe me? Well that beard-chewing...! Forget I said that. He's a good commander, just a bit contrary at times.
'I suppose that you'd best go find one of those fetishes Grímkell wants. There are goblins to the south of my camp and a bit to the west.'

Vífill said there were goblins south of his camp.
Grímkell told you he would only be convinced of Vífill's tale if you could bring him an authentic goblin fetish.

'It is unthinkable that these goblins managed to sneak into the Vale of Thráin under my very beard. Well, there's nothing to do about it now but prepare for the worst.
'I need you to take the fetish you found to Bolli, the Captain of the Guard in Gondamon to the east. He must know of the goblin's incursion from the valley into Vale of Thráin.
'I've no doubt this is a sign of a larger threat.'

'You carry with you a fetish of the Blue Crag goblin tribes. It's clear that the vile creatures are on the move and intend to launch an offensive against the Vale of Thráin. Troubling news, to be sure.
'We must crush the goblin forces before they become an even greater threat. Their presence in the Vale is a festering blight on the land and if we don't stop it now, it will spread like a shadow across the land.'
'You said Grímkell sent you? Do you have anything to deliver?'
Bring the goblin fetish to Bolli
Goblins in the South
You raided the goblin encampment in the Vale of Thráin and slew their chieftain, but the threat still looms over the peoples of Ered Luin.
'That fetish must be brought to Gondamon with all haste. Proof of the goblin threat must be seen by the Captain of the Guard himself.'
'The goblins are growing more bold...we must redouble our vigilance.'
'It is well that you brought me the goblin-fetish. At least now we know what tribe we are dealing with!'
'Hopefully, Bolli will send more dwarves to defend the Vale against the goblins!'
'Thank you for your aid, ${PLAYER}. I only hope it was in time.'

Bolli is at Gondamon, east of Noglond.
Grímkell has asked you to take the goblin fetish to Bolli, the Captain of the Guard at Gondamon, and warn him of the threat the goblins pose.
Defeated goblins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I think I know what's going on. There are some sprawling old ruins just south-west of here. I think the goblins have occupied those ruins.
'I'd be sorry to have to send a message up to Thorin's Halls or off to Gondamon for help. I guess I'd feel like Vífill must have. They would laugh and leave it lie.
'I wonder if you and some friends, perhaps, could deal with these goblins? If you could raid their camp in those ruins and defeat their chieftain, I wouldn't have to ask for help from elsewhere. I'd gather some allies, though -- the camp is likely to be well-guarded.'
'Ha! Good work. I'm sorry I ever doubted Vífill, but who would have known that goblins would actually dare to enter the Vale of Thráin?'
Defeat goblins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Villains in the Vale
Grímkell thinks the goblins have occupied a large ruin, a former Dourhand city, to the south-west of Noglond.
'Ha ha! Good job with those goblins!'

The Blue-crag Chieftain is at the large goblin camp in ruins to the south-west of Noglond.
Embarrassed by his previous skepticism, Grímkell has asked you to raid the goblins in their camp and slay their chieftain. He suggested you take allies.

Grímkell is in Noglond, north-east of the goblin encampment.
You should return to Grímkell with news of your victory.

'This key will unlock the crate marked, Common Ore. Feel free to collect your order at your leisure.'

'Vicious beasts have grown numerous in the copses along the road, and we don't have enough dwarves to keep the paths clear. It's shameful, really, that we have let the wild overrun our paths. As long as dwarves dwell here, the ways should be safe.
'If you want to be of help, patrol from Noglond to the top of the Vale of Thráin and clear out any beasts you find. We're having the most trouble with bears, hendrevail, and lynx.
'With your help, we will make the road safe once more.'
'Thank you for helping keep the ways clear. If it's not too much to ask, please don't tell anyone that I needed help.'

Defeat hendrevail in the Vale of Thráin (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Clear the Roads
Vicious animals have grown numerous in the copses along the road through the Vale of Thráin, making travel through the Vale unsafe.
'There are still wild and savage beasts plaguing the roads. Continue patrolling the Vale of Thráin for bears, hendrevail, and lynx.'
'The roads should be safe, for a time anyway, thanks to you, ${PLAYER}!'
'No one has made an effort to keep the roads clear for a long time. Well, that's going to change!'

The road runs northwards from Noglond through the Vale of Thráin to Thorin's Halls.
Ketill has asked you to patrol along the road through the Vale of Thráin and cull the numbers of bears, hendrevail, and lynx.

You should return to Ketill and report the results of your patrol.
Collected minor metalworking-lore
Collected minor woodworking-lore

'If we are to defeat the goblins of Rath Teraig and the sneaking Dourhands that even now remain in the hidden corners of the Blue Mountains, we'll need to make better use of the resources we have available.
'The wild lands around Gondamon are a bounty of such resources, but if we don't make full use of them, we might as well be giving them to the goblins!
'If you know a scholar of some skill, I would have him prepare for me some minor metalworking-lore and some minor woodworking-lore. Armed with these, I can surely prepare a plan for better using what we have. I will pay you for your efforts, of course.'

'Thank you for these, ${PLAYER}! Now I must engross myself in study and take what lessons from these I can!
'Here is your payment, as I promised.'
'I need minor metalworking-lore and minor woodworking-lore if I am to make best use of the resources to be found on the low-lands surrounding Gondamon. Have you forgotten?'
Bring minor woodworking and metalworking-lore to Solvi Scrollbearer

Collect minor woodworking-lore
Making Use of the Low-lands
Solvi Scrollbearer is certain that better use could be made of the resources found outside Gondamon and wants your help in acquiring information to support this idea.
'It is taking me a while to make sense of the lore you brought to me, friend.'
'I have no doubt we will overcome both the goblins and the Dourhands, if we are true!'

Solvi Scrollbearer is at Gondamon, on the low-lands of Ered Luin.
Solvi Scrollbearer asked you to have a scholar prepare some minor metalworking-lore and some minor woodworking-lore for him to examine.
Collected bronze gloves
Collected bronze helm

'Goblins infest the narrow reaches of Rath Teraig, and stout-hearted dwarves keep the southern barricade against them. Their armour will fail before their spirits do, ${PLAYER}, so we must do for them what we can!
'If you can ask a metalsmith to fashion bronze gloves and a bronze helm, then bring them to me, I will see that the staunch defenders of the barricade receive them.
'You will be paid for your trouble, of course, in coin and other small things, though given the importance of this task no one would presume to ask for payment.'
'Thank you for these, ${PLAYER}. Take these coins and other items. I insist, even though the knowledge of the good you are doing for the defenders should be enough.'
'I am still waiting for bronze gloves and a bronze helm, ${PLAYER}.'

Collect bronze helm
Outfitting the Defenders
Efi Plateshaper is eager to outfit the dwarves guarding the barricade to Rath Teraig and asked for your help collecting the necessary pieces of armour.
'The defenders at the barricade will be glad to see the armour you have given me.'
'We will triumph over both goblins and Dourhands! How could we not?'

Efi Plateshaper is at Gondamon, in the Low-lands of Ered Luin.
Efi Plateshaper asked you to bring him bronze gloves and a bronze helm with which he can outfit the defenders of the barricade at Rath Teraig.
