Defeat goblins in Fornost City (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Pre-emptive Measures
The army of Orcs and goblins inhabiting Fornost constantly press upon the Free Peoples' encampment. The North Downs camp will fall unless the Enemy's forces are weakened.
'The sheer numbers of the Orcs and goblins are our greatest threat, I believe. I am depending on you to balance the odds.'
'Seen any Orcs around lately? Ha! Well done!'
'You have helped greatly in our battle against Angmar!'

Orcs and goblins can be found near the base of the keep within the city of Fornost.
Gareth Copp has asked you to help the forces of the North Downs by reducing the numbers of the Orcs and goblins at Fornost.

Gareth Copp is at the camp of the Free Peoples in the southernmost part of Fornost.
Your efforts have weakened the forces of Angmar, as Gareth Copp requested. You should return to Gareth at once with news of your victory.
Destroyed a siege part (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It appears my assumptions were false. Indeed, the true intentions of the Blogmal are far more nefarious than crushing our little resistance. They are building siege weapons for an invasion. They are preparing to move south!
'Those siege weapons must be destroyed before they can be completed and brought to bear against Trestlebridge and Bree-land. Take your allies and search the Blogmal camp for the weapon parts and make sure they will never be used.
'Hurry, ${PLAYER}. The safety of of the Free Peoples depends upon expedience!'
'You have thwarted Angmar's plans, ${PLAYER}! It will take them much longer now to amass the siege weapons they need. For a time, at least, Trestlebridge and Bree-land should be safe.'
Destroy ${TOTAL} siege parts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Stopping the Siege
The Orcs of the Blogmal tribe are preparing siege weapons to bring to bear against Trestlebridge and Bree-land beyond.
'If the Blogmal are permitted to complete those siege weapons, Eriador will not survive the ravages of Angmar. You must destroy them!'
'Angmar will question the wisdom of attacking us again!'
'Trestlebridge is safe for now! Well done, ${PLAYER}!'

The siege weapon parts are being assembled in the Orc camp at the base of the keep within the city of Fornost.
Gareth Copp has asked you to destroy the siege weapon parts being assembled by the Blogmal Orcs, thus crippling Angmar's efforts to invade Eriador.

Gareth Copp is at the camp of the Free Peoples in the southern reaches of Fornost.
You should return to Gareth Copp and let him know that the siege weapon parts have been successfully destroyed.
Collected Blogmal Orders

'Your ambush upon the Orcs and goblins of Fornost hurt them greatly, but I fear the danger has not passed. The Orcs within the city are of the Blogmal tribe, far more cruel and cunning than the utterly brutish Tarkrîp. I have no doubt they are already devising a reprisal for the loss of their brethren.
'You should return to the Blogmal camp near the foundations of the keep and see if you can learn what their plans are. You might discover some evidence upon the person of one of the Blogmal-warlords.
'Take allies, for the danger is great. Be wary, lest the Enemy overcome you.'
'This crudely-drawn map you found appears to be the extent of the orders the Blogmal possessed. It will take me a moment to study this....'
'Have you found the Orcs' orders? One of the Blogmal-warlords at the camp in Fornost should have the orders on him.'
Bring the orders back to Gareth Copp
Collect the Blogmal Orders
True Intentions

The Orcs which inhabit the ruins of Fornost are drawn from the Blogmal tribe, more cruel and cunning than their completely brutish cousins of the Tarkrîp. Gareth Copp is convinced they are devising a vicious reprisal for the recent loss of their brethren, whom you slew.
'These Orcs must be stopped!'
'We must protect the Northdowns! We stand here!'

Blogmal-warlords can be found within the Orc camp near the base of the keep within Fornost.
Gareth Copp has asked you to gather your allies and search for some evidence of the Orcs' plans, most likely to be found upon the person of a Blogmal-warlord.

'You acquitted yourself very well, my friend. However, killing a few worms is not enough. I have learned that these worms are under the dominion of a worm-elder which the Orcs call Gajarpan.
'If we are to drive the worms from these ruins once and for all, Gajarpan must be destroyed. That will be your task, ${RACE}. Find Gajarpan and slay him!
'When the worm-elder is dead, the lesser worms will be much easier to deal with.'
'Very well done, ${RACE}! It was no dragon-slaying, but neither is it a small deed to kill a worm-elder. Your deed shall be remembered!'
Ending the Elder
The worms infesting the ruins of Fornost are led by an elder named Gajarpan by the Orcs. Gajarpan must be destroyed if the worms are to be driven from Fornost.
'Gajarpan is dead! The Dwarves of Othrikar shall sing your praises forever!'
'You have the gratitude of the Dwarves of Othrikar, ${PLAYER}.'

Gajarpan can be found somewhere within the ruins of Fornost.
Bôrk has asked you to slay Gajarpan, the worm-elder whom the worms of Fornost follow, in hopes that the worms might be driven out once and for all.

Bôrk is at the camp of the Free Peoples in the southern reaches of Fornost.
Bôrk awaits word of your victory against the worm Gajarpan.

'If it weren't enough that the Angmarim have allied with Orcs and goblins and trolls, the passing of their army has even attracted the attention of dragons! Well, not dragons exactly, but dragon-kind. Worms have begun to spawn in the hills of the North Downs, and many have even made their way into these ruins.
'Do you know how much trouble worms can cause in a mine? I need you to go into those ruins and kill the wretched vermin.
'If we just let them roam free, they are likely to attract drakes...and worse. If any full-fledged dragons still lurk in the nothern mountains, they might get wind of the fabled father-lode in Othrikar and decide to make a home of our mines.'
'Well, it's a start, but the task is far from finished! Nevertheless, well done, ${RACE}.'
Rock-worms, drawn to the North Downs by Angmar's passing, have begun to spawn in the hills and many have wandered into Fornost itself.
'Well done, ${PLAYER}.'
'Mining shall begin shortly.'

Worms can be found in the ruins of Fornost.
Bôrk the Dwarf has asked you to rid the ruins of the worms that infest them, hoping that the dangers the presence of such creatures could attract might be allayed.

Bôrk is at the camp of the Free Peoples at the southern edge of Fornost.
You should return to Bôrk and tell him of your great deeds against the foul worms of Fornost.
Defeated goblins in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Orcs in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hello there. Perhaps if you are going into Fornost, you could help me? I'm from Trestlebridge, and Nellie and the rest of us are very worried about the forces amassing here, particularly the Orcs and goblins.
'If such a large host is allowed to leave Fornost, Trestlebridge won't stand a chance against it. Perhaps you could go into Fornost and deal a blow to the Orcs and goblins?.
'Come back to me when you have completed the task.'
'You've done well indeed, my friend. I don't doubt these brutes will think twice about pressing towards Trestlebridge now.'
Defeat goblins in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Orcs in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Stem the Invasion
The bulk of Angmar's host in Fornost is comprised of Orcs and goblins, a formidable force that Arch Widdup fears may be brought to bear on Trestlebridge if they are allowed to march south.
'Well done, ${PLAYER}! You have saved Trestlebridge...at least for now.'
'Good day to you, Defender of Trestlebridge.'
In order to improve Trestlebridge's chances against the armies of Angmar, Arch Widdup has asked you to enter Fornost and slay as many Orcs and goblins as you can.
You have dealt a serious blow to Angmar's host, and while not a complete victory, your efforts should at least lend courage to Arch Widdup.
You have defeated Riamul

'It troubles me that so many of the shades remain. Are there so many that have not repented of their betrayal? It is hard for me to believe this. Perhaps the will of one keeps them here.
'There is a legend of the Battle of Fornost which tells of a great captain, Riamul, who led his men forth from the city, only to betray his oath and lead them instead against King Arvedui in favour of Angmar. Perhaps you should seek Riamul and bring him word of his pardon?
'I do not know whether he remains unwittingly or willingly, for I cannot know the mind of the Dead, but I cannot see why he should choose to suffer so.'
'I am sorry that it had to come to such an end, but some things must be done. Already Fornost grows lighter. Thank you, kind ${RACE}. You have done the North Downs a great service!'
Find Riamul and release his spirit
Captain Riamul
A legend of the Battle of Fornost mentioned a great captain of the armies of Fornost who led his men onto the field, only to betray his oath and lead them against King Arvedui instead.
'Please, you must find Captain Riamul. These shades need no longer suffer!'
'Hero of the North Downs! Freedom-bringer!'
'A hero walks among us.'

Riamul is somewhere within Fornost.
Emma Slee has asked you to seek the shade-captain, Riamul, and bring him word of his pardon. She hopes that his freedom will allow his men to follow.

Emma Slee is at the Fornost camp.
Riamul, loyal to Angmar even in death, refused his pardon, believing that the Witch-king would restore him. You should return to Emma Slee and let her know you had to defeat him to free his men.
Defeated bears in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated boars in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated aurochs in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'By some foul art, the Enemy has captured and corrupted animals from the wilds of the North Downs. Bears, boars, and even the docile aurochs have become vicious predators.
'There is no hope left for these creatures. Whatever the Angmarim have done, it has twisted these beasts beyond reclamation. For the safety of all that dwells in the North Downs, the corrupted beasts must be destroyed before they can be released into the wild.
'Take your allies and enter Fornost. Once there, destroy as many of the corrupted animals as you can.'
'You have done as I asked, and for that I must thank you. It may not be enough, however. If they have corrupted beasts once, they will do it again.'
Defeat bears in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat boars in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated aurochs in Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Eliminating the Beasts

Foul, corrupted beasts of all kinds wander the ruined and crumbling streets of Fornost, twisted and unnatural mockeries of the wildlife of the North Downs. These creatures pose a threat to all that lives in the surrounding lands.
'Such corruption cannot be allowed to spread. The unclean beasts must be destroyed before they can be released into the wild.'
'Well done, my friend.'
'You have purified the earth.'

Corrupted bears, boars, and aurochs roam the ruined streets of Fornost.
Dismayed by the corruption brought about by the Angmarim, Lovenol has asked you to destroy the twisted bears, boars, and aurochs in Fornost before they can be released into the wild.

Lovenol is at the camp of the Free Peoples at the southernmost reaches of the city of Fornost.
Lovenol will be relieved to learn that you have succeeded at the task she set you.

'Such vile corruption is oft the result of feeding beasts foul meats and unclean draughts, as well as training them with cruelty. This is no doubt the work of a \qdefiler\q, an Orc skilled in the uses of poisons and foul medicines.
'If this threat is ever to be truly ended, the Blogmal's defiler must be slain. Seek him out within Fornost and put an end to his corruption!
'The free and wild creatures of the North Downs must be allowed to remain so.'
'It is well that the foul Orc perished before he could release his corrupt progeny upon the North Downs. My thanks to you, ${PLAYER}.'
Seeking the Source

Lovenal has determined that the beasts of Fornost have been corrupted through some twisted mixture of foul meats, unclean draughts, and cruel training. She is convinced it is the work of an Orc-defiler.
'What the Orc-defiler is doing within those ruins is an abomination. He must be stopped!'
'This land will remain clean.'
'Thank you yet again, ${PLAYER}. The defiler will no longer trouble the North Downs.'

The Blogmal Defiler is somewhere within the ruins of Fornost.
In order to end the corruption of the local wildlife, Lovenol has asked you to kill the Blogmal-defiler who is feeding and training the captured beasts.

Lovenol is at the camp of the Free Peoples in the southern reaches of Fornost.
Lovenol will be relieved to know that the Blogmal-defiler met his end at your hands, removing the threat of his corrupting influence.
You have escorted Sara Oakheart to safety

'Oh my, it's you again, ${PLAYER}. I had feared I would be lost here forever. Those terrible monsters took me captive as I was gathering herbs.
'I'm not sure that I can make it out on my own. Do you think you could help me get to the front gates of this dreadful place?
'Perhaps if you follow me, I can find a way out.'

'You have done a wonderful deed for me. Thank you so much. Take this as a reward.
'I am sure we will meet again, good ${RACE}.'
'Hurry let's get out of here before more Orcs come. Follow me!'
Talk to Sara Oakheart again
Talk to Sara Oakheart
Oakheart's Flight
Sara Oakheart was found prisoner in the depths of Fornost. She needs your help getting free and back to the safety of her home.
Sara Oakheart was apparently taken captive by the Blogmal Orcs while she was gathering wild herbs. She needs you to escort her out of Fornost.
Now that you have successfully escorted Sara Oakheart to safety, speak with her again.

'All right, while Noll here and I put this wheel on the cart, there's one last thing I'd ask you to do. Go back to Elsie in Trestlebridge and tell her that all's well here.
'Once the cart is fixed, Noll and I are going to take down a couple more trees and then bring our load down to the town. Of course, we couldn't have done that without your help! Thanks for that!
'Now hurry...won't do to stand around here waiting for Orcs!'

'Mattie and Noll are safe and sound? Oh, bless you! Bless you! That's the best news I've heard in many a day. I was fearing the worst, but I'm glad to hear my worries were for naught!
'I just hope they hurry up and get back to Trestlebridge! I don't think I'll get a bit of rest until I see them back.'
All's Well

Searching the Orc camp, you were able to find a wheel for Mattie Woodruff's cart. Although the wheel is a bit small, he thinks it should work well enough to get the cart and a load of lumber back to Trestlebridge.

'I think we'll be fine here. Noll and I should be able to get this wheel on without too many problems.
'All I'd ask of you is to go back down to Trestlebridge and tell Elsie that we're all right!'
'Thanks for that wheel. Noll and I should have it on the cart in no time!'
'I'll be a lot happier when we've got back to Trestlebridge with this wood!'
'I'm so glad to know that Mattie is safe!'
'I do hope Mattie and Noll start back for Trestlebridge soon!'
'It's good you found that wheel. I'd hate to be caught out here much longer.'
'What with all these Orcs around, it ain't safe to be out here. Thanks for finding that wheel!'

Elsie Woodruff is in Trestlebridge.
While Mattie and Noll fix the cart and load it with the lumber they've collected, Mattie asked you to go back to Trestlebridge and tell his wife that he's safe.

'You see, the other thing needed for the barricades is wood. In the past we would fell trees in the Nan Wathren when we needed lumber, but now the Orcs lurk there.
'We were so desperate for lumber that my husband, Mattie, and my brother, Noll Tobbit, risked leaving Trestlebridge and went north along the Greenway proper in search of trees to fell. It has been too long since I've heard from them, and I'm worried something terrible has happened.
'Would you search north along the Greenway for them? I can't bear to think that something bad might have happened to them.'

'So Elsie sent you? Well I'm glad for it!
'Well, we did run afoul of them Orcs...fortunate to have escaped with our lives, we are! But our cart here...well, it didn't get off quite as well, as you can see!
'No matter how many trees we fell, if we don't have our cart fixed we can't bring 'em back to Trestlebridge!'
Felling Trees
Elsie Woodruff told you that her husband, Mattie, and her brother, Noll, left Trestlebridge in search of trees to fell for the barricades.
'Mattie and Noll said they were going north along the Greenway, so hopefully you'll find them there! I'm so worried something terrible has happened to them!'

Mattie Woodruff and Noll Tobbit should be found somewhere along the Greenway north out of Trestlebridge.
Elsie told you that she hasn't heard from either her husband Mattie or Noll Tobbit, her brother, since they left and asked you to look for them.
Collected the cart wheel

'If we don't get a wheel for this cart, this lumber ain't going anywhere. I'd send you to Trestlebridge, but I doubt they'd have anything to spare. Every little bit there is precious.
'But there's some hope yet. See, there were some farmers escaping to Trestlebridge and their waggons got overrun by them Orcs. Well, their supplies were stolen and their carts broke up, but there might be a wheel from one of their carts that we can salvage.
'I don't think they dragged the carts into the Nan Wathren, so I think you'll find the remains of them carts in that Orc camp straight east of here. If we're going to find a wheel to salvage, it'll be there, I'd wager!'

'Aye, you found one! This one looks like it'll work! It's a bit smaller than the other wheels, so the ride will be a bit rougher. But as long as we get this lumber to Trestlebridge, it won't matter how rough the ride is!'

'I don't think them Orcs dragged the broken waggons from that caravan into Nan Wathren, so I would search their camp due east of here for a wheel.
'I sure hope you find one, because without a wheel, this cart isn't going anywhere!'
Bring the wheel back to ${NOS}
Collect the cart wheel
Salvage a Wheel

Mattie Woodruff and Noll Tobbit did run into Orcs, but managed to escape unharmed. Their cart however was not as fortunate and needs a new wheel if they are going to use it to haul lumber back to Trestlebridge.

The broken waggons were dragged off by the Orcs to their camp outside of Nan Wathren.
Some of the farmers, while escaping from the Orcs, were waylaid and their waggons were ruined. Mattie hopes that among the wreckage of the farmers' waggons you will find a wheel that he can use to fix his cart.
Collected the barrel of nails
Collected the crate of hammers
Collected the crate of saws

'You there, I need your help! Our poor town is constantly under attack from those foul Orcs. All of us are doing our part to help Trestlebridge survive, and I'm charged with getting supplies to maintain the barricades.
'The problem is that the outlying farmers were supposed to be bringing some of the supplies we need, only their farms were overrun by Orcs. They barely escaped and the Orcs scattered their goods. I would send for supplies from the south, but Orcs block that route as well. We need those stolen supplies!
'The three things we need are the barrel of nails they were carrying, a crate of hammers, and a crate of saws. The Orcs should have them at their camps to the north-east.'

'Oh wonderful, you've found the supplies! Thank you!
'There is something else though that I would have you do, if you would....'

'I need those supplies if I'm to have what is needed to maintain the barricades.
'You should find the barrel of nails, the crates of saws, and hammers at the Orc camps north of Trestlebridge near the Greenway.'
Bring the collected materials to ${NOS}
Collect the barrel of nails
Collect the crate of hammers
Collect the crate of saws
Bolster the Defences
Elsie Woodruff was charged with acquiring the supplies needed to maintain Trestlebridge's barricades, but is now having trouble finding the supplies she needs.

The stolen supplies can be found in the Orc camps to the north-east.
Elsie told you that the outlying farmers were supposed to be bringing some of the supplies she needs -- specifically a barrel of nails, a crate of hammers, and a crate of saws -- but their farms were overrun and their goods stolen. She has asked you to go to the Orc camps north along the Greenway and gather the supplies the Orcs scattered.
This crate does not contain the Founder's Book
Collected the Founder's Book

'Oh, maybe you can help me. Since time out of mind, our town treasure has been a book, the Founder's Book, that tells of the early years of Trestlebridge, many generations ago. That book has gone missing!
'There's a big Orc encampment to the east of town now. It may be that they have the book there still. I know it's foolish to think of a book at a time like this, but I can't help worrying about it. The Orcs stole many things from us when they raided the town, and the book is likely still in one of the crates they stole.
'I wonder if you can possibly help get that book back for us?'
'Oh, I'm so happy you got the book back! But wait...what is this?'
'I wonder if you can get the Founder's Book back for us from the Orc camp?'
Collect the Founder's Book
Bring the Founder's Book back to Marla Shelton
The Founder's Book
Marla Shelton is concerned that the history of Trestlebridge may be lost because the Founder's Book has been stolen by Orcs.

There are Orc encampments to the east, once you cross the Trestlebridge to the north.
Marla Shelton has asked you to search Orc encampments near Trestlebridge for signs of the Founding Book.

Marla Shelton is back in Trestlebridge.
You have found the Founder's Book and should bring it back to Marla Shelton.
Collected map page (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})

'It seems that the book has been damaged! It looks like all the maps at the end of the book have been torn out.
'I wonder if the Orcs might not be using these maps to plan their further attacks! They were driven out of Trestlebridge once, so I'm sure they're planning to return. Perhaps the raiders in the smaller camps around here have these pages and are using them as guides to the area. I think there are eight missing map pages.
'If you can hunt these pages down, not only will you be restoring our town treasure, but perhaps you'll be thwarting the Orc attacks as well!'
'Oh, thank you so much! Now we have our book back! Maybe this will make it harder for the Orcs to attack us again.'
'I hope you can get the map pages back from the Orcs.'
Bring the map pages back to Marla Shelton
Collect the map pages (${NUMBER} / ${TOTAL})
Restoring the Founders' Book
You recovered the Founder's Book for Marla Shelton, but it seems some of the map pages are missing. She is concerned that the Orcs will make use of them to plan another raid against Trestlebridge.
'Without those maps, the Orcs might not have as easy a time raiding our town.'
'Oh, I am so glad you recovered the Founder's Book!'

There are many Orc camps around the Greenway.
Marla Shelton has asked you to recover the map pages stolen from the Founder's Book, thereby restoring the book and thwarting the Orcs' attacks.
Tarkrîp Orc slain (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'So you be helping out Marla there, are ye? Maybe ye'd do something for me too, eh? Don't mind spilling a little more Orc-blood, do ye?
'At my age, I learned there ain't no shame in asking for help. Them Orcs need a little justice brought down on them, but I'm too old to be doing it myself. Ye, though...ye look like ye got a strong arm. If ye go out and kill a few of the Orcs from the tribe what attacked Trestlebridge, I'll give ye a reward.
'Don't matter where ye find them, just as long as they are of that Tarkrîp tribe, the same that been attacking my town.'

'Pretty handy with a weapon there ain't ye? While it don't make up for all that we lost here, it's good to know that some justice been served on them Orcs. I lost me closest friend in the attacks, Lovelle Boskins, Nellie's father.
'I can see quite a bit of Lovelle in Miss Nellie there. She's got his spirit. Means to save this little town, she does, and I means to help her. Least I can do to make up for what happened the first night them Orcs came....'
Defeat Tarkrîp Orcs in the North Downs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Kemp's Revenge
Kemp, the old wheelwright, seeks revenge against the Orcs that attacked Trestlebridge.
'Don't matter what type of Orc you kill, just as long as they're of the Tarkrîp tribe!'

The Tarkrîp, the tribe of Orcs that attacked Trestlebridge, can be found throughout the North Downs. Their main encampment is likely to be near the town.
Kemp the Wheelwright asked you to exact his revenge upon the Orcs of the Tarkrîp tribe.

Kemp the Wheelwright can be found in Trestlebridge.
You should bring Kemp the Wheelwright word of your success.
Collected Kemp's stash

'See, the night the Orcs first came, Nellie's father, Lovelle, and I were talking and drinking. Well, I must've had one too many mugs, because I woke up that morning in an alley. Near as I can guess, Orcs must've thought I was already dead. Suppose I was lucky, but sure don't feel that way.
'All me life I been hiding a little money away outside of town. I reckon now it's enough to help Nellie keep this town going. Problem is I can't get to its hiding place. Can you go get it for me?
'I buried it in the ruins of Minas Vrûn, north and east of here. I buried it in an archway in the ruins. You'll know you're at the right spot if you see a big \qX.\q Be careful though, wild beasts and worse prowl those ruins!'

'Aye, that's me money. Thank'ee. I'll give this to Nellie right away.
'Nellie's a dear girl, and I know she'll say I don't need to give it to her. And while she may not blame me for what happened, I know I wish it had been old Lovelle who survived and not me. I know I can't change it, so I'll try and help Nellie save this town. It's the very least I can do for her and her dad, good old Lovelle.'
'I need my money if I'm going to be a help to Nellie and keep this town afloat.'
Find Kemp's stash
Bring the stash to Kemp
Collect Kemp's stash
Kemp's Stash
Kemp told you the tale of how he survived the Orc-attack and how Nellie Boskins resolved to save Trestlebridge.

'Here's how ye find me money. Go north from Trestlebridge along the road. When the road branchs east, follow it until ye see some ruins north of ye. Those are the ruins of Minas Vrûn.
'Explore the ruins a bit, look for an archway with an \qX.\q The stash is buried there.'

Kemp the Wheelwright said his stash lay buried in the ruins of Minas Vrûn north and east of Trestlebridge. The hiding spot is in an archway marked with an \qX\q.
Kemp the Wheelwright asked you to collect his hidden stash of money, so that he can help to maintain Trestlebridge for Nellie Boskins.

Kemp the Wheelwright can be found in Trestlebridge.
You should return to Kemp the Wheelwright with his stash.
Defeated barghests on the Fields of Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Now I understand why Amarion fears the Fields of Fornost and does not want travelers journeying there; this corruption that has taken the bears sounds dreadful.
'I have hated the bears that stole my livestock for years and years, ${PLAYER}, but hearing about this evil what lives on the Fields of Fornost has given me pause. I would not call it fear, exactly, but my heart beats faster when I hear the howls of the hounds on the fields now.
'Throughout the Fields of Fornost, even near to that fell city, corruption spreads. The bears are made corrupt by the bite of the barghest, near as I understand. I have no love of the bears, but they need not suffer such a twisted madness.
'I say we cut the heart out of the source and stem the corruption from spreading further. Search for barghests all along the Fields of Fornost and return to me when you have finished.'

'I am glad that you have done this, ${PLAYER}. Even the bears that have made my life so difficult for many years do not deserve to be twisted and corrupted by the evil that has sunk into the grass of the Fields of Fornost.'
Defeat barghests on the Fields of Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Corruption From Fornost
Agnes Martlet listened to the tale of your time in the Fields of Fornost and feels some pity for the creatures corrupted by its dark past.

'The closer you get to the city of Fornost, the worse the corruption will become. Seek out and defeat the barghests on the Fields of Fornost, and grant the bears release from the evil that has so twisted them.'
'I have long had troubles with bears at my farm.'
'The Fields of Fornost are not to be treaded lightly, but you returned safely.'
'It will be good to return to my farm, when this warg business has passed.'

Barghests can be found all through the Fields of Fornost.
Agnes Martlet has asked you to defeat some of the barghests on the Fields of Fornost in order to save the bears from their corruption.

Agnes Martlet is in Amon Raith, south-east of the Fields of Fornost.
Agnes will be glad that you have given freedom to the bears from the corruption of the barghests on the Fields of Fornost.
Bear of Fornost Slain (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'While you were away, I told that young Amarion that it wouldn't be long before we were out of his way, since the Wargs are sure to be driven soon from Annúndir. He didn't even manage a smile. Such a gloomy fellow!
'Well, When I told him you were taking care of the bear-hides for me, he seemed surprised. \qThe bears of Fornost have come into Annúndir? The deathly ones have come east?\q I told him I didn't think so.
'But he couldn't take back his words, ${PLAYER}, and if the bears on the Fields of Fornost are coming east, I don't want them coming to my farm! If you travel north-west, you are sure to find the bears of which he spoke.'
'You have returned from the Fields of Fornost, victorious against its deathly bears? Tell me the tale of your struggle against them and take these coins for your trouble.'
Slay Bears in the Fields of Fornost (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
More Business With Bears
Agnes Martlet learned from Amarion that there is something wrong with the bears on the Fields of Fornost, and she is worried that some of them may find their way to her farm.

'Agnes Martlet may be old, but she is wily and misses nothing. I should have been more careful with my words, and not mentioned the bears on the Fields of Fornost.
'Yes, you will find them to the north-west, but I would ask you not to go. The Fields are dangerous and the creatures there unnatural. Great battles were fought there, long ago, and the ground remembers the bloodshed. You will find no peace in that place.'
'You have returned from the Fields of Fornost? That is well. It is a place of danger and evil, and one should not tread there lightly.'

'Take care when journeying into the Fields of Fornost, north-west of here. I don't think that Amarion wants you going up there -- something about the place frightens him. But if the deathly bears he mentioned come into Annúndir, they are sure to be even more interested in my livestock than the ordinary bears are!'

There are bears on the Fields of Fornost, north-west of Amon Raith.
Agnes Martlet has asked you to deal with the corrupted bears on the Fields of Fornost before they make their way to her farm.

Agnes Martlet is at Amon Raith, south-east of the Fields of Fornost.
Agnes will be pleased to hear that you have defeated many of the corrupted bears on the Fields of Fornost.
Collected Heavy Bear-hide (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Wargs forced me from my land, same as the other folk here, but it won't be long before we can go back, I expect. You learn to weather things like this once you've put some years behind you, and this Warg business is just one more setback in the long road.
'I'm more concerned about the great bears prowling the wilds in northern Annúndir. They've carried away more than their share of my livestock over the years, and now that I'm not on my land to chase them away, I'm afraid they'll be up to their old tricks!
'I am not without a heart and know that the bears are doing just what is their nature. So I told Amarion I would use their hides to make cloaks and tents if we need to weather the winter. Two birds, one stone.
'The bears can be found west of the Warg camps. Be careful not to stray too far towards the Fields of Fornost, I'll not use bear-hides from those foul beasts! Only bears in Annundír will do.'

'I'm glad you defeated some of the bears of Annúndir for me, ${PLAYER}. William and Camilla are so concerned with this Warg business that they talk about nothing else! It's worth remembering that there are many threats in this world, and all of them must be dealt with.'

'There are bears roaming the hills of northern Annúndir, and I don't want them carrying off any of my livestock while I'm stuck here with this Ranger! I can't go down to my farm yet, but that's no reason to let the bears eat any of my livestock! Go remind those bears that Agnes Martlet of Annúndir hasn't left for good!'
Return the Heavy Bear-hides to Agnes Martlet
Collect Heavy Bear-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Thinking Ahead
Agnes Martlet has kept her own farm for years, and although she left it when the Wargs appeared, she is already thinking ahead to her return.
'If I get back to my farm and those bears have carried off even one of my animals....'
'This Warg business won't last much longer, I expect.'

Bears can be found on the northern hills of Annúndir, east of Amon Raith.
Agnes Martlet believes the threat of Wargs will soon pass, and she is more concerned with the bears that have troubled her livestock over the years. She has asked you to cull the bears' numbers and collect their thick hides for tents and clothing while also reducing the threat to her livestock.
Collected Bones from the Bone-piles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Do you think you could do me a favour, ${PLAYER}? I tried asking Amarion, but he told me he can't leave Amon Raith without endangering the rest of us. I suppose that's true, but it's still of little consolation.
'A friend of mine was visiting my farm when the Wargs attacked -- a sturdy, little fellow from a place called Tuckborough in the Shire. I thought he was right behind me, but by the time I met up with the Peakes, Ailward was gone!
'It's a morbid task, but could you sort through the bones of the Wargs' victims, up in northern Annúndir? There's a whole pack of the beasts at the burial mounds there. If you bring some of the bones back to me, maybe I will find some hobbit-sized ones...though I hope not!'

'I see you've found some bones, ${PLAYER}. Some of these are fairly small, but I wouldn't say any of them are hobbit-sized. Unless I'm very much mistaken, I'd say most of these are goblin bones!
'It seems to me that the Wargs and the goblins must not get along well all of the time -- and that's good for us! Let them fight among themselves, and there will be fewer for us to worry about!
'Well, I'd say none of these belonged to my friend. Thank you for giving me this small hope, ${PLAYER}.'
'You haven't collected any bones from the Wargs yet. You should find their killing-ground east of here, at the burial mounds in the far north of Annúndir.'
Collect Bones from the Bone-piles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring gnawed bones to Nathan Hodges
Fallen to the Wargs
Nathan Hodges is worried that a hobbit who was visiting him might have been attacked by the Wargs during the retreat to Amon Raith.
'The Wargs are north-east of here, in the far north of Annúndir. If you could collect some of the bones of their victims, we can see if there are any...hobbit-sized ones.'
'I think my friend may have escaped the wargs. He was a tough little fellow.'
'The goblins and the wargs fight among themselves? I say we let them finish each other off!'
'The wargs cannot be driven from Annundir soon enough for me, I tell you true.'

A large pack of Wargs have moved into northern Annúndir, and the bones of their kills litter the burial mounds in the north.
Nathan Hodges is worried that a friend of his, Ailward Took, a visitor from the Shire, did not make it safely to Amon Raith. Hodges has asked you to retrieve the bones scattered around the Warg-occupied burial mounds, but hopes you will not find any of hobbit-size.

Nathan Hodges is at Amon Raith, west of southern Annúndir.
Nathan Hodges is waiting for you to return with the bones you scavenged from the Wargs.
Defeated Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You've done some good work for us here, and we appreciate it, but we still aren't back on our own land. I know my husband is frustrated that he can't do anything about those Wargs, but judging from your work for Amarion, I think you just might be able to!
'There's a pack of Wargs in far north Annúndir, around the old barrows in Haudh Eglan. If you can defeat some of the creatures, maybe that will encourage them to go back to wherever they came from! The Wargs prowl all around those mounds, and you won't be able to miss them.
'May fortune go with you, ${PLAYER}.'

'You learned those Wargs a lesson? Good.
'It won't be long before William and I are back on our own land. Not that we don't appreciate Amarion's hospitality, but these ruins are hardly comfortable. Still, you do the best you can with what you have available.'
Defeat Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fighting Back
Camilla Peake and her husband were driven off their land in Annúndir by the invading Wargs.
'The Wargs that drove my William and me from our farm can be found around the burial mounds in Haudh Eglan far to the north-east. Encourage them to leave our land alone!'
'Those Wargs can't leave quickly enough to suit me.'
'My William would have fought the Wargs himself, but his leg pains him some.'

Wargs have seized Haudh Eglan, north-east of Amon Raith.
Camilla Peake has asked you to drive out the Wargs in Annúndir so that she and her husband can return to their farm.

Camilla Peake is at Amon Raith, west of Annúndir.
Camilla Peake is waiting for you to return with news that you have defeated the Wargs encroaching on her land.
The bog-guardians appear uninterested in the rune

'When the Stone-trolls learn that Elves have returned to Lin Giliath, they are sure to attack again. There are too few of us, and we cannot hold out long. There is one defence which we can call upon, but there is no certainty that those I speak of will still answer the summons.
'I give you these runes -- \qcanel\q they are called -- and ask you to lay them upon the pedestal stones found throughout the marshes. Long ago, many of these stones were set east of Lin Giliath in a great curve bending to the south, but only three have survived the ravages of time and the elements. We must hope the guardians remember the meaning of the \qcanel\q.
'Return to me when you have placed all the runes, and we will learn if the errand was for naught.'

'You have placed the \qcanel\q, ${PLAYER}? That is well, though it seems the bog-guardians have chosen not to come to our aid.
'I suppose I was too eager for the old friendship between Elves and bog-guardians to be rekindled that I was hopeful to the point of blindness. Only disappointment can come of...wait, what is that?
'Look! A bog-guardian has come! And more! I shamed myself with despair, but now I see that it is never wrong to hope. You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}!'
Place canel on flat stones (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Guardians of the Glade
Medlichen is concerned that the Stone-trolls will return when they learn that Elves have come back to Lin Giliath and believes that they should bolster their defences.
'There are three stone pedestals located throughout the marshes south of Lin Giliath. Seek each of them out and place a \qcanel\q upon it, and we shall learn if the bog-guardians will aid us.'
'The bog-guardians remember their old friendship with Elves, after all this time!'
'The bog-guardians were beloved of the Ents, it is said.'
'Many creatures of the bog have become wild and feral.'

The first pedestal is east of Lin Giliath, and two others are to the south of it in a great curve through the marsh.
Medlichen has given you several runes to place on the stone pedestals throughout Meluinen, which he hopes will bring the glade's guardians to its defence.

Medlichen is in Lin Giliath.
Medlichen is waiting to hear of your successful placement of the canel upon the stone pedestals throughout Meluinen.
You have escorted Lagorlam to safety

'I am pleased to see a face that does not to a troll belong. I came to Taur Gonwaith to seek vengeance on the trolls that attacked the glade of Lin Giliath and murdered my fair friend Lachenn. I can tell you that many of the Stone-trolls that attacked Lin Giliath will never again leave this place.
'The last three I faced proved a challenge, and they had begun arguing how best to cook me when you arrived. You have my thanks.
'Let us leave this place, friend, so I might return to Lin Giliath and tell my friend, Thaliollang, the course of my vengeance.'

'You survived a journey to Taur Gonwaith, ${PLAYER}, and lent your strength to Lagorlam!
'Aye, he has already spoken to me of what transpired. I am grateful that you were able to find him, though he insists he could have returned to Lin Giliath without any aid.
'He told me something else, as well, which begins my grief anew.'
Escort Lagorlam to safety
Rescuing Vengeance
Lagorlam, a member of the company of Elves who came north with Gildor Inglorion, entered Taur Gonwaith, seeking revenge against the trolls who attacked Lin Giliath.
'Lagorlam has always been quick to action, and slower to thought than he might.'
'The stone-trolls of Taur Gonwaith surely wish they had stayed there.'
Lagorlam was injured while visiting his vengeance on the trolls. With his anger saited he has offered to leave Taur Gonwaith with you.

Thaliollang is at Lin Giliath, north-west of Taur Gonwaith.
Thaliollang will be pleased to hear that you rescued Lagorlam from the forest of Taur Gonwaith.

'Lagorlam told me that as he hunted the Stone-trolls, he spotted a chieftain of great size, called by the others Gurmagath. This Gurmagath had in his great fist a sparkling ornament that once belonged to poor Lachenn!
'Lagorlam was driven into a rage and raced towards Gurmagath, but before the battle was joined, he was attacked by three other Stone-trolls, and Gurmagath retreated to a clearing east of where you found Lagorlam.
'This wretched creature cannot be permitted to keep Lachenn's ornament, ${PLAYER}. Seek out this Gurmagath and wrest Lachenn's ornament from him, so it may be kept in Lin Giliath in a place of honour.'

'Aye, this is Lachenn's ornament. It is truly a shame that it has been broken by Gurmagath's brutish fingers.
'There is something odd about these markings on the back of the ornament. These scratches almost look to form letters. A...N...G....
'The rest is broken off, but I believe I know what it would say.'
'You have not yet found Lachenn's ornament? Gurmagath cannot be permitted to keep it, ${PLAYER}!'
Bring the broken ornament to Thaliollang
The Stolen Ornament

Lagorlam, the Elf you rescued from the Stone-trolls at Taur Gonwaith, reported to Thaliollang that the chief of the trolls had in his possession an ornament once belonging to Lachenn, Master of Lin Giliath.

'Gurmagath can be found on a rise in the north-eastern part of Taur Gonwaith. He cannot be allowed to keep Lachenn's ornament any longer, ${PLAYER}. You must defeat him and bring it to Lin Giliath, where it belongs.'

Gurmagath can be found on a hillock east of where you rescued Lagorlam, in the north-eastern area of Taur Gonwaith, south-east of Lin Giliath.
Thaliollang has asked you, in memory of Lachenn, to hunt down the chieftain of the Stone-trolls, Gurmagath, and retrieve Lachenn's ornament so that it can be restored to a place of honour.

Thaliollang is at Lin Giliath, north-west of Taur Gonwaith.
Thaliollang is waiting for you to return with the ornament you retrieved from Gurmagath.
You have found Lagorlam!

'When we arrived here, there was much debate concerning what should be done about the Stone-trolls, and many thought, as I did, that they should be driven from their fastness in Taur Gonwaith.
'There were some of us, among them Aglardir and Gildor, who counselled restraint. I regret the stern words I had for them, but at the time their plan to rebuild this place seemed to do Lachenn's memory a disservice.
'My friend Lagorlam believed as I and journeyed forth to slay the Stone-trolls, but he has not returned. It would put my mind at ease if you could find him. Look for him in the forest of Taur Gonwaith to the south-east.'
Search for Lagorlam in Taur Gonwaith
The Wayward Companion

Lagorlam, a member of the company of Elves who came north with Gildor Inglorion, entered Taur Gonwaith, seeking vengeance against the trolls who attacked Lin Giliath. He has not returned, which concerns Thaliollang.
'The death of Lachenn has troubled us all, and Lagorlam may not use as much caution as he ordinarily would. Seek him in Taur Gonwaith to the south-east and lend him whatever aid he may need.'
'Taur Gonwaith is a place of evil where the stone-trolls hold sway.'
'Had Gildor and my company arrived earlier, Lachenn might still be alive.'
'I had harsh words for Aglardir, and I now regret them. His sorrow is no less true than mine.'

Lagorlam has gone to the forest of Taur Gonwaith, south-east of Lin Giliath.
Thaliollang has sent you to find Lagorlam and make certain he is well.

'Lachenn left us a message, ${PLAYER}. He tried to write the name \qAngmar\q on his ornament even as he lay broken and dying at the hands of Gurmagath. That explains Lagorlam's tale of strange North-men lingering near the caves of Taur Gonwaith. He would have assayed these strangers further but his fury was on him and his thoughts were of fair Lachenn and the trolls that did him harm. It is clear some dark evil out of Angmar has come to Meluinen and stirred the Stone-trolls!
'Return to Taur Gonwaith and seek out the caves on its southern edge, near the lake beyond Merenost. Lachenn's last hope was for us to heed his message, and stop this pawn of Angmar before the Stone-trolls do even more damage.
'Baranwen, particular among us, was disturbed by Lagorlam's news. Speak with her before you travel to the cave. Lin Giliath will not be safe until you have put an end to Angmar's influence over the Stone-trolls of Taur Gonwaith!'

'You have earned more thanks than I have to give, ${PLAYER}, for defeating the troll-keeper of Angmar.
'Lachenn would have been pleased to know you. I name you Elf-friend and will not forget what you have done here, ${PLAYER}. I expect the Stone-trolls are not likely to forget either. Lin Giliath may have peace for a time.'
The Troll-keeper
Thaliollang believes that Lachenn had tried to write \qAngmar\q on the back of his ornament and takes it as a sign that it is an emissary of Angmar that had stirred the Stone-trolls.
'Deep inside the caves of Taur Gonwaith, some emissary from Angmar has gained the allegiance of the Stone-trolls and is using them to do the work of Angmar in Meluinen. They must be stopped.'
'Lachenn has been avenged, and the Stone-trolls may never again attack Lin Giliath.'
'That Angmar should already have power even in Meluinen is a sad tiding.'
'Cross the Downs with caution, ${PLAYER}, for the dangers increase with each passing day.'

Angmar's emissary must reside deep within the cave in Taur Gonwaith, south-east of Lin Giliath.
Thaliollang has asked you to defeat the emissary of Angmar that has gained the allegiance of the Stone-trolls.

Thaliollang is at Lin Giliath, north-west of Taur Gonwaith.
Thaliollang will be pleased to know that he was correct in his belief: there was an emissary from Angmar among the trolls. To the benefit of all, you have defeated him.
Defeated Orcs in Meluinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Thaliollang and Lagorlam are so intent upon vengeance against the Stone-trolls that they are blind to all other threats, and I fear they will not retain enough strength of will to fight the other dangers that lurk nearby.
'Orcs of the Tarkrîp clan have established a foothold in Nan Wathren, the valley to the south-west, and their scouts intrude further into Meluinen with each passing day.
'Slay any Orcs you find that have crossed into Meluinen, ${PLAYER}, for they pose a great threat to Lin Giliath. You will surely find them south and south-west of here, along the line of the mountains.'

'You have done well, ${PLAYER}! I hope your efforts will serve as a warning to the Tarkrîp: they are not welcome in Meluinen, nor ever will be. This company of Elves may only be temporary stewards of Lin Giliath, but we shall oppose them as surely as Lachenn would, were he still alive.'
Defeat Orcs in Meluinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Orc Excursions
Meluinen is threatened by the presence of a large encampment of Tarkrîp Orcs in the valley to the south-west.

'Orcs of the Tarkrîp tribe have begun creeping into Meluinen from Nan Wathren, south-west of here. Defeat the Orcs that have already crossed into Meluinen to the south and south-west, and we may prevent, or at the least delay, any further incursions.'
'The Orcs of Nan Wathren will be wary now of sending scouts into Meluinen.'
'We will stay at Lin Giliath for as long as it takes to repel the Orcs.'

Orc-scouts have crept into Meluinen from the valley to the south-west of Lin Giliath.
Brethilwen has asked you to slay any Orcs you find in Meluinen, thus reducing the Tarkrîp threat.

Brethilwen is in Lin Giliath.
Brethilwen will be heartened to hear of your victory over the Orcs that had entered Meluinen.
Collected weapon-chests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Lagorlam has told us of his bloody expedition to Taur Gonwaith and of your part in it. He also spoke of North-men carrying chests laden with weapons into a cave, in the south. While the others dwell upon the malefactions of the trolls, I am concerned by the very presence of Men from Angmar not to mention their arms.
'Every sword-hilt we remove from the grasp of an Angmarim is one less blade that may be brought to bear against the Free Peoples. Seek out weapon-chests in the troll-cave and bring them to me. I shall destroy the foul blades.
'If even one of the blades we seize would have otherwise slain an innocent, I shall count this day's labour worth the toil.'

'These weapons are poorly made, and none of them exhibit the care needed to make a truly fine sword. I am not surprised by the lack of craftsmanship, for the Angmarim care little about such things, and these blades are as effective as they need to be to slay the innocent people who were their intended prey.
'You have done well to bring me these weapons. I will destroy them, and by so doing I hope we have together saved some lives. You have my thanks for this errand.'
'You have not yet recovered enough weapon-chests from the troll-cave in Taur Gonwaith.'
Collect weapon-chests (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring Angmarim weapon-chests to Baranwen
Disarming the Valley
Lagorlam learned of the presence of North-men during his excursion into Taur Gonwaith. Upon hearing Lagorlam's tale, Baranwen has grown alarmed at this bold move by the Men of Angmar.

'Taur Gonwaith was once a shady vale to the south-east of Lin Giliath, but the trolls have despoiled it at the hands or their Angmarim masters. If you can return here with several chests of the Angmarim weapons, I will destroy them.'
'The fewer weapons the Angmarim can draw, the safer the Free Peoples will be.'
'Taur Gonwaith was once beautiful, but now it is a dark and ominous place.'

The mysterious Angmarim are at the troll-cave in the southern part of Taur Gonwaith, south of Lin Giliath.
Baranwen has asked you to collect weapon-chests from the Angmarim and to return them to her so she can destroy the foul weapons.

Baranwen is at Lin Giliath, north-west of Taur Gonwaith.
Baranwen is awaiting your return with the Orc-weapons, which she will destroy.
Collected Ongbúrz venom-pouches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I have need of your assistance, ${PLAYER}. The stream that feeds the fens of Meluinen falls from the hills north-west of Lin Giliath. Beside this river, Orcs of the Ongbúrz tribe are threatening Lin Giliath from on high. An Orc Defiler, skilled in the use of poisons, joined the ranks of the Ongbúrz. His presence makes the Ongbúrz an even deadlier enemy.
'The defiler hunts the spiders in the eastern Kingsfell for their venom sacs and the Ongbúrz smear this poison on their arrows and blades. Slay the Orcs in Gurzlum and collect their venom pouches. I will make sure the pouches are never again used for evil purposes.
'While you are in the camp, put an end to the source of the vile poison once and for all by killing the Ongbúrz-defiler. Be careful, ${PLAYER} -- these Orcs are brutal and without mercy, and you may have need of allies.'

'The venom pouches. I take it that the defiler was slain as well? Many lives will be saved through your efforts.
'I find it strange that the Orcs would hunt their spider allies. They make themselves stronger at others expense...and in the end, weakening the Enemy as a whole. Such is the way of evil things, for the spiders would not hesitate to drink of the blood of their Orcish fellows.'
'You have not yet obtained the venom-pouches I asked for, ${PLAYER}?'
Collect Ongbúrz venom-pouches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the Ongbúrz venom-pouches to Gandelin
Touch of Corruption
The Orcs of Gurzlum in the Kingsfell use spider venom to coat their blades and arrows.
'You have made the Ongbúrz much weaker than once they were.'
'The time will come when we must push the Orcs from the Kingsfell.'

The Ongbúrz Orcs can be found in their fortification at Gurzlum, on the rise beside the waterfall north-west of Lin Giliath.
Gandelin asked you to slay the Ongbúrz-defiler and return with the Ongbúrz venom-pouches.

Gandelin is back at Lin Giliath.
Gandelin asked you to slay the Ongbúrz-defiler and return with the Ongbúrz venom-pouches.
Defeated sickle-flies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The attack of the stone-trolls on Lin Giliath has upset the natural order in Meluinen, and the creatures that have lived here for years have become feral and aggressive. The sickle-flies have been particularly disturbed, and though they have so far remained within the marshes, it may not be long before they swarm further north into the Kingsfell and beyond.
'We should handle the sickle-fly problem in Meluinen while we still can. If even one of the creatures leaves the marshes, it may call the rest, and all of the Downs will be endangered.
'Kill as many of the flies as you can in the marshes to the south. That may be enough to contain the threat.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}, and the sickle-flies will not now leave Meluinen.'
Defeat sickle-flies (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Insect Menace
Silefalas believes the sickle-flies in the marshes of Meluinen have been disturbed by the recent aggression of the Stone-trolls.

'There are sickle-flies throughout Meluinen, and they must be dealt with before they swarm north into the Kingsfell. Search the marshes south of Lin Giliath for the flies, but use caution. The waters of the marsh can hide unseen dangers.'
'We have prevented the sickle-flies from spreading into the Kingsfell, for now at least.'
'The marshes of Meluinen have been disturbed by the Stone-trolls.'

Sickle-flies can be found throughout the marshes of Meluinen, south of Lin Giliath.
Silefalas has asked you to end the threat of the sickle-flies of Meluinen, which have been stirred to anger by the Stone-trolls.

Silefalas is at Lin Giliath.
Silefalas is waiting for news of your victory against the sickle-flies of Meluinen.
Collected slabs of aurochs-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The supply wain from Bree is late, our food stores are running low, and I've one less hunter thanks to those Wargs you vanquished. Would you do some hunting for us?
'Search out the aurochs herds in the eastern Nan Amlug and bring their meat back to me. I can taste it now...roast aurochs and a flagon of ale!'
'At last! I'll get to dressing some of the meat for dinner and salting the rest.'
'You haven't enough meat to feed the camp. Believe me when I tell you, friend, that a hungry dwarf is an ill friend and a worse enemy.'
Bring the aurochs-meat to Orgrin
Collect slabs of aurochs-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Meat for the Hungry
Quartermaster Orgrin has asked you to help replenish Othrikar's food stores.
'${PLAYER}, be welcome in Othrikar. We owe you greatly for all your help.'

The aurochs herds roam the foothills and plains of eastern Nan Amlug.
Quartermaster Orgrin is short handed with the recent loss of one of his hunters, he has asked your aid in hunting aurochs.
Collected lynx-furs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There's a cold winter coming. I feel it in my bones. We dwarves are a hardy folk, but if we're going to survive the winter, we will need more supplies.
'Hunt the troublesome lynx that seem to cover the lands hereabouts and bring me their fur. I'll craft their hides into warm gloves for our miners.'
'Thank you for your help, friend. I will fashion these furs into gloves to protect the miners from the bitter cold of the deep mines. Old Nine-fingered Doli will be happy about that, I can tell you.'
'I'll need more furs than this if I am to craft as many gloves as needed.'
Bring the lynx-furs to Quartermaster Orgrin
Collect lynx-furs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Winter Gloves
Orgrin, the quartermaster at Othrikar, requires your aid in maintaining the camps stores.

Lynx roam the hills surrounding Othrikar.
Hunt the lynx that roam the hills around Othrikar in western Nan Amlug and bring them to Quartermaster Orgrin at the entrance to the dwarf-mine.
Defeated Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Well, it appears the Dourhands are not the only danger to our hunters...poor Vigfúss was mauled while you were gone. Looks like the work of Wargs.
'I'll need you to go out there and show those Wargs that dwarves won't be provender for them.'
'Well now, that should keep the Wargs at bay. My thanks, ${PLAYER}!'
Defeat Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Hunting Wargs
Quartermaster Orgrin has asked for your help in making the hills safer for his hunters.

Warg packs prowl the hills of eastern Nan Amlug depleting the Aurochs herds that serve to feed the dwarves of Othrikar.
After receiving a report that one of his hunters has been savaged by Wargs, Orgrin asks you to clear the Wargs from the hills.

Orgrin is the quartermaster for the dwarves of Othrikar.
Return to Orgrin with the tidings that the aurochs herds of Nan Amlug have a few less Wargs to fear.

'You have aided us well ${PLAYER}. The time for battle is very near now.
'One last thing I ask -- take this to Othrikar, the dwarf-mines north-west of here, and give it to Quartermaster Orgrin. This satchel contains many healing herbs we collected as part of our pact with the dwarves there, who will also aid us.
'Be well. We may not meet again.'

'Eh, what is this? Ah, the herbs promised by the Jorthkyn. Thank you for bringing them!
'They are strange allies, are they not? But these times are dangerous, and any force we can raise to halt the advance of Angmar is welcome.
'The Jorthkyn seem to have an odd affinity for plants, though they do not raise crops...I am not sure where they learned such lore but it is of great value to us now. Many of us shall doubtless be wounded in the battles to come, and the poultices that can be made from these herbs are potent for healing.'
Bring Iivari's herb satchel to Quartermaster Orgrin
Sealing the Pact
There exists a pact between the Suuri-lehmä and the Dwarves of Othrikar, that each would provide aid to the other.
'Take the herbs to Othrikar. The dwarves will have need of them.'
'The Jorthkyn's herbs shall help us against Angmar and the Dourhands.'
'Thank you for your delivering these herbs, ${RACE}.'
'You are a good friend to the Suuri-lehmä and to the dwarves.'
'The Rauta-lehmä have no honour. With your help, ${PLAYER}, we have taught them the meaning of the word.'

Quartermaster Orgrin is at Othrikar, north-west of Rusfold.
Iivari has asked you to perform one final task for him: he wishes you to deliver a satchel of herbs to Orgrin, the provisioner at Othrikar, as fulfillment of a pact between Earth-kin and dwarves.

'Greetings, traveller. I must ask your aid, for my tribe cannot help me. I am preparing the Suuri-lehmä for war, but I am not prepared myself.
'My brother stands across from me, armed with the weapons of Angmar, his mind filled with their lies. I have not been able to speak with him since this rift grew between my people and the Rauta-lehmä, who serve Angmar. I do not know where my brother's heart truly lies, whether he is torn within, as am I.
'I cannot lead my people to war while this doubt gnaws at me! Take this message to Oskari - he is somewhere within the Rauta-lehmä encampment at the place called Fashat Laug, well to the east of here. Perhaps he and others may yet be convinced to return to us before the end.'

'You bring a message from my brother? I see.
'Iivari is a fool who refuses to see the world as it truly is. He thinks that words alone can chase away the darkness - he does not understand the meaning of power.
'Take this to him. It is all the answer from me that he will receive. Now go, or the Rauta-lehmä shall crush you.'

'Ah. Now I know the truth. The rune you carry is a gift I gave my brother many years ago. The symbol upon it in our language means \qkinship\q. It has been etched over with a symbol we use to mean \qwithout value.\q
'The lies of the Angmarim run too deep, and my brother is beyond my reach now. I find my heart no less troubled by what I must do, but now I know that there is no choice....'
Bring Iivari's message to Oskari
Bring Oskari's rune to Iivari
A Brother's Plea

The two factions of the Earth-kin -- the free Suuri-lehmä and the Rauta-lehmä, who serve Angmar -- are preparing for war. Iivari, the War-master of the Suuri-lehmä, and his brother Oskari have found themselves on opposite sides of the conflict.
'Go. Take the rune. I have nothing more to say.'
'Please carry the message to my brother.'

Oskari is somewhere among the camps of the Rauta-lehmä at Fashat Laug in the eastern North Downs.
Iivari has given you a message to take to his brother Oskari. Iivari hopes that his words may be able to sway his brother and others of the Earth-kin to return to the Suuri-lehmä.

Iivari is in the Suuri-lehmä encampment, west of Fashat Laug.
Oskari refused his brother's plea and gave you a rune to take back to Iivari.
Defeated Hillmen Armourers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our path is clear. We make ready for war, and in so doing must weaken the strength of our enemies.
'Our corrupt kin wield weapons crafted specially for them by the Hillmen of Angmar. In their camp, at the mouth of the path to the north, these men twist earth and shape metal. Defeat these Men, and you will be taking the fangs out of the mouths of our enemies. With their bite lessened we might survive yet still.
'The armourers camp a short ways south-east of the mountain cleft path, called the Ram Dúath by dwarves and Men. Hunt them down and make it so they craft weapons no more, but be careful: their pack is many and strong.'

'It is like the winter wind to think our lost kin would wield steel forged by our enemy against us. This is a battle we can no longer lose or run from.
'You have done well. I hope your deeds shorten the battles to come and bring us swift victory!'
Defeat Hillmen Armourers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tell Iivari of your victory over the Armourers
Staunching the Flow
Special weapons are being forged in the eastern camps for the Rauta-lehmä by the Hillmen of Angmar, who journey down from the mouth of the Ram Dúath.
'You must hunt the armourers from the North! Armed with claws of metal, the Rauta-lehmä will cut my people down like the tall summer grass.'

The Hillmen Armourers are encamped south-east of the Ram Dúath.
Iivari has asked you to defeat the Armourers before they can craft anymore weapons for the Rauta-lehmä. He believes if you succeed, the Suuri-lehmä can win the forthcoming war and with fewer lives lost.

Iivari is at the camp of the Suuri-lehmä.
You succeeded in defeating the Armourers Iivari told you of. You should return to the Earth-kin War-master at once with the news.
Collected gem pouch

'Oh, stranger, perhaps you will hear my sad story. I was a member of a group of merchants who were crossing the North Downs when we encountered a party of marauding Orcs.
'We fled from them, but did not escape tragedy. We encamped not far south of here, in a place I later learned was called the Snares, and with good reason. As we slept, our camp was raided by spiders! Only I escaped and was rescued by these Rangers.
'One of my companions was bearing a pouch of valuable gems on his person, which we were taking to Othrikar for trade. I do not doubt that it was still on his body when the spiders dragged him off. Could you go to the spider-lair and retrieve it? Without it, I will be destitute. The lair is to the south of here.'
'Indeed, these are the gems! Thank you so much for your help. I must give you a small reward for your courage!'
'Please find those lost gems, or I am ruined.'
Collect the gem pouch
Bring the gems back to Holger Tanner
Spider Gems
Holger Tanner is the survivor of a party of merchants ambushed by spiders in the Kingsfell. The merchants were carrying a valuable pouch of gems, which the spiders dragged off with one of the bodies.
'Thank you so much for recovering those gems. I'll be journeying back to Bree as soon as the Rangers say it's safe.'
'You are a brave ${RACE} to face those spiders for my gems.'

The lost pouch of gems is somewhere in the area called the Snares, south of Esteldín.
Holger Tanner, a merchant who escaped an attack by spiders, has asked you to recover his companions' missing pouch of gems from the spiders' lair.

Holger Tanner is at Esteldín.
Holger Tanner, a merchant who escaped an attack by spiders, has asked you to recover his companions' missing pouch of gems.
Defeated trolls in Dol Dínen(${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I had never seen a troll until the Orkish siege-weapons rolled past us in the night. Enormous mounds of stone-coloured flesh pulled the siege-towers, catapults, and other terrible machines south towards Dol Dínen.
'I dared not attack them, not without greater numbers. Since then, I have struggled to convince Halbarad that something must be done about the trolls in Dol Dínen, but he would not permit us to risk ourselves. With the aid of yourself and others like you, he has now relented.
'I would set you this task: gather allies and go to the troll-camps south-east of Esteldín, beyond the trenches of Dol Dínen and slay as many as you can.'

'With so many of the trolls slain, the Orc-host will find it more difficult to put their siege-engines to effective use. However, this is only a minor setback for them and by no means assures us of victory.'
Defeat trolls in Dol Dínen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Masters of the Black Siege

A great host of Orcs spilled through Ram Dúath, driving the Men of the North Downs from their farms. Esteldín, home of the few remaining Dúnedain of the North, was spared discovery. It is from there that the Rangers begin to plan their counter-offensive against the black tide of Angmar.
'Defeat the trolls, and the siege-engines will be stranded!'

Trolls can be found beyond the trenches of Dol Dínen, south-east of Esteldín, under the cover of the smoke.
Hithlim told you of the night that the trolls pulled the great siege-engines of Angmar past his watch-post. Since then, they had been his greatest concern, and he has asked you to gather allies and slay as many as you can.

Hithlim awaits your return at Esteldín.
You have defeated a large number of trolls. Now you should bring your report to Hithlin.

'The Orcs of Dol Dínen have weapons greater than their siege-engines. We have learned that there are some among them who have dabbled in fell sorcery.
'We know that there have been Orcs, unseen by any Ranger before, keeping watch beyond the siege-engines, deep within the encampment, and they are not great in number. If these are the sorcerers that we have heard of, they must be destroyed.
'Do not attempt this task alone, ${PLAYER}. Take allies if you intend to engage these foul creatures.'

'You have earned this reward, ${PLAYER}. I have never heard of Orcs of such power in my lifetime. Tales of the past hold rumour of such creatures, but they were of a more fell breed than any living today.'
Weakening the Tide

A great host of Orcs spilled through Ram Dúath, driving the Men of the North Downs from their farms. Esteldín, home of the few remaining Dúnedain of the North, was spared discovery. It is from there that the Rangers begin to plan their counter-offensive against the black tide of Angmar.
'The Orc-sorcerers must be defeated!'
'We will soon be prepared, thanks to your efforts.'
'You have faced greater challenges than I believed you would and have survived. Well done, ${PLAYER}!'

Ongbúrz Bone-speakers can be found in the deepest reaches of Dol Dínen, beyond the siege-engines, south-east of Esteldín.
The Rangers of Esteldín discovered that there are sorcerers among the Orcs of Dol Dínen, and Hithlim has asked you to seek them out and destroy them. He warned you to take allies.

Hithlim awaits your return at Esteldín.
You should return to Hithlim with news of your victory against the Orc-sorcerers of Dol Dínen.
Collected ballista locks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected catapult pinions (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected trebuchet swing-arms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your success against the trolls gives me hope that you can accomplish this task, as well.
'The Orcs at the encampment in Dol Dínen are cunning; they have taken their siege-engines and moved them to higher ground, giving them a more deadly vantage. They will be fortified soon and ready to use against us if we do not act quickly.
'I need you to once again gather your companions and enter the encampment. Disable or destroy the catapults, trebuchets, and ballistae. If you fail here, we will stand little chance of victory in the future.'
'You have once again shown your cunning and prowess, ${PLAYER}. With the loss of their siege-engines, the Orc-host will be weakened, but it is not yet destroyed.'
'Do not go too deeply into the Orc-encampment alone, ${PLAYER}, but do your best to disable the Orkish siege-engines you find there.'
Collect ballista locks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect catapult pinions (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect trebuchet swing-arms (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Deliver the siege-engine parts to Hithlim

A great host of Orcs spilled through Ram Dúath, driving the Men of the North Downs from their farms. Esteldín, home of the few remaining Dúnedain of the North, was spared discovery. It is from there that the Rangers begin to plan their counter-offensive against the black tide of Angmar.
'The siege-engines must be destroyed!'

Catapults, trebuchets, and ballistae can be found on the hills and high ground deep within the Orc-encampment in Dol Dínen, south-east of Esteldín.
Though you have slain several of the trolls who transport and maintain the Orcs' siege-engines, the weapons themselves still remain. Hithlim has asked you to gather allies and disable or destroy the catapults, trebuchets, and ballistae.

Hithlim awaits your return at Esteldín.
You entered Dol Dínen and disabled several of the orc's ballista, catapults, and trebuchets. You should bring news of your success back to Hithlim.

'You have returned at a most opportune time, ${PLAYER}. Our scouts tell of a great, armoured troll who walks among his kindred which maintain the siege-weapons of the army at Dol Dínen. They believe he is their captain.
'Trolls, as a rule, are not very smart, but there are those among them with a much greater wit, and these are the most dangerous. If we can destroy this troll, it may throw his brethren into disarray. That will be your task.
'The scouts reported that the great beast retreated deep into Dol Dínen, within the shadow of the mountain overlooking the valley. You must not enter that place without many friends, for the danger is too great.'

'The troll-siegemaster was responsible for the march from the Ram Dúath. His loss, as well as the damage done to their siege-weapons, will hinder the Orc-army for at least a short while.
'For your efforts on behalf of Eriador, you have earned this, ${PLAYER}.'

A large, armoured troll has been seen walking amongst the siege weapons overlooking the approach to the hills in the southernmost reaches of Dol Dínen. The Ranger Hithlim believes that this great brute leads the trolls who maintain the siege-weapons at Dol Dínen.
'Use caution and do not think that you can simply assail this foe. He will be amongst the leaders of this invasion and likely well-defended. Use your cunning and numbers to defeat this foe.'
'You have done a great service for the Rangers and the Free Peoples of the North Downs, ${PLAYER}.'
'The Orcs of Dol Dínen will have much to consider before continuing along their destructive path.'

The armoured troll can be found within the shadow of the mountain overlooking the valley of Dol Dínen, far to the south-east of Esteldín.
Hithlim has asked you to gather allies and seek out the armoured captain of the trolls in Dol Dínen. With the death of their captain, the Ranger hopes the trolls will be thrown into disarray.

Hithlim awaits your return at Esteldín.
You ventured deep into the heart of the Orc-encampment at Dol Dínen and defeated the troll-siegemaster. You should return to Hithlim with the news of your victory.

'Your efforts were admirable, but the goblins have not been broken. Their numbers are too great, and they are held to their duty by a ruthless taskmaster. The bond is a frail one, however, founded upon fear.
'I would ask you to return to the goblin-camps on the outskirts of Dol Dínen and find this goblin-taskmaster. If he is slain, the will of the goblins may be broken.
'Whatever advantages we can attain against this host will be of great aid, for we are too few, and we stand alone.'

'The Orcs have greater control over the goblins than I feared. Nevertheless, we must persevere. Many long battles lie ahead of us, and we must not lose heart.
'We will defeat this foe and restore order to the North Downs. Thank you for your assistance, ${PLAYER}.'
Breaking the Front Lines

A great host of Orcs spilled through Ram Dúath, driving the Men of the North Downs from their farms. Esteldín, home of the few remaining Dúnedain of the North, was spared discovery. It is from there that the Rangers begin to plan their counter-offensive against the black tide of Angmar.
'You must slay the goblin-taskmaster!'
'If victory is to be ours, I fear it will be won in the South, not here. Nevertheless, we must persevere.'
'We are beaten before we have begun, but not yet crushed. For that, we have you to thank, ${PLAYER}.'

The goblin-taskmaster patrols the goblin-camps on the outskirts of the Orc-host in Dol Dínen.
Celephadh congratulated you on your efforts against the goblins of Dol Dínen, but told you that their will had not been broken. He has asked you to cut the one last thread holding them together: the goblin-taskmaster who leads them.

Celephadh awaits your return at Esteldín.
You found and defeated the goblin-taskmaster among the goblin-camps in Dol Dínen. Celephadh will be eager to hear the results of your raid.
Defeated Orcs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Orcs have begun to increase in number and move northwards, becoming a terrible threat to the peoples of Eriador.
'If you could make forays against their camps around the lakes in the southern plains, perhaps they will be discouraged from spreading further.'
'Your efforts are not to be dismissed, but I do not think they will be enough. You do have my gratitude for what you have done, however.'
Defeat Orcs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Celephadh has asked for your help in securing the safety of the lands around Esteldín.

The Orcs threatening the central North Downs can be found around the farm fields and rolling hills of Kingsfell.
Celephadh asks that you foray against the Orcs, hoping to drive them away.

Celephadh can be found in the hidden Ranger stronghold of Esteldín.
Fulfilling your duty to Celephadh, you should return to him and give him news of your victory.
Collected the helms of the fallen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Orcs in the ravaged lands of Dol Dínen have become bold, pillaging much further north where they hold no lands.
'Bring the battle back to their camps and recover the helms of their victims. The Orcs of the ravaged lands are not to be counted lightly. Recruit your fellows for assistance in this task.'
'These vile creatures have no respect for the dead, but I suppose there is little hope they will learn the meaning of honour.'
'Have you slain the Orcs and reclaimed the helms of their victims?'
Return to Celephadh with the helms of the fallen
Collect the helms of the fallen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Ravaging Orc-bounty
Celephadh has asked for your help in securing the lands around Esteldín.
'You stand high in my esteem, ${PLAYER}. Your deeds here have been great. I foresee things greater still in your future.'

The Orcs make their camp in the ravaged lands of Dol Dínen, far to the south-east of Esteldín.
Not every traveller or resident of the North Downs has your good fortune and skill. Some have fallen to sword or spear of the twisted Orc-hoards. Celephadh asks you to hunt Orcs in the ravaged lands and reclaim the helms of the fallen. He suggested you take allies.
Defeated spiders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The spiders which dwell in the south-eastern Kingsfell, near the mountain, have long been a threat and a plague to us. My kindred are stretched thin across the North Downs and beyond on missions of great import and are unable to deal with this threat.
'Would you seek out and slay the spiders?'
'Your help is appreciated, ${PLAYER}, but I have no doubt they will return, as they always have.'
Defeat spiders (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Celephadh has asked for your help in securing the lands around Esteldín and warding off any threats.

The foul spiders reside in the south-eastern area of Kingsfell in the shadow of the mountain.
