Celephadh make his lodging in the valley camp of Esteldín.
You should return to Celephadh and let him know that you have done as he asked.
Defeated Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Wargs, the hounds of the Enemy, prowl the foothills and eastern plains of Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad, threatening inhabitants and travellers alike.
'If you could slay a goodly number of them, they may become frightened enough to cease their hunts for the flesh of Men.'
'The vile Wargs are one of the most dangerous threats that plague this land. Your deeds have been helpful, but it will not be enough, I fear. Nevertheless, take this as a reward for your assistance.'
Defeat Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Celephadh has asked for your help in securing the safety of the lands near Esteldín.

Wargs prowl the plains and foothills of Nan Amlug and Rhunenlad, east of Esteldín.
Celephadh asks that you hunt down and slay the cruel hounds of the Enemy.

Celephadh can be found in Esteldin with his fellow Rangers.
Now that you have completed your task of thinning the Warg-packs, you should return to Celephadh and inform him of your success.
Collected goblin slave-collar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Until recently, small goblin raiding-parties were the worst threat faced by the North Downs. But with the arrival of the Orcs out of Angmar, the goblins have themselves been forced by their greater brethren into servitude.
'Now, they watch the front-lines of the host at Dol Dínen, under command of the Orcs, awaiting their turn to be sacrificed for the greater glory of the Iron Crown. We should not make them wait overlong. If you are willing, make your way south-east out of Esteldín to the outskirts of the Orc-encampment at Dol Dínen and kill the goblins there.
'Bring me the slave collars worn by the goblins as evidence that your task has been accomplished.'

'Ah, you have returned...and successful, I see. Perhaps the Orc-generals will feel less secure with the wall of goblin-flesh thinned around them.
'In truth, though, this is but a small victory. The Orc army is vast, and the Dúnedain of the North are a dwindling people.'
'Be careful not to stray too far into the Orc-encampment...scouts report that the forces beyond the trenches include trolls. We cannot risk such an assault at this time.'
Bring goblin slave-collars to Celephadh
Collect goblin slave-collars (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Forced into Service

A great host of Orcs spilled through Ram Dúath, driving the Men of the North Downs from their farms. Esteldín, home of the few remaining Dúnedain of the North, was spared discovery. It is from there that the Rangers begin to plan their counter-offensive against the black tide of Angmar.

Goblins can be found on the outskirts of the Orc-encampment at Dol Dínen, south-east of Esteldín.
According to Celephadh, the goblins of the North Downs have been forced into servitude by the Orcs of Angmar and act as the advance forces of the Orc-host. The Ranger has asked you to dispose of the goblins, bringing him their slave collars as evidence that you have completed your task.

'Rumour has reached Esteldín that a chieftain has risen up among the Wargs of Dol Dínen, uniting the packs that run with the Orcs gathered there. Even a tenuous unity among such foul beasts is a danger to us all.
'I ask you then to slay the chieftain of the Wargs and shatter their courage. The vile creatures linger near the Orcs, protecting their masters, so you will need cunning and the strength of numbers. You should take allies with you.
'Dol Dínen, where the Orc-army has gathered, lies to the south-east of Esteldín. Be careful, friend ${PLAYER}.'

'We have learned through many forays with the Wargs in the North Downs that they are possessed of a mind far beyond most beasts. It is said they even speak in their own tongue.
'I cannot attest to the truth of the belief, as I neither speak nor understand the language, but Mincham -- the watcher at the Fields of Fornost -- has assured me that it is true.
'You have done much to assist us, ${PLAYER}. Please accept this with my thanks.'
Rumours have reached the ears of the Rangers at Esteldín that a chieftain has arisen within the ranks of the Wargs at Dol Dínen, uniting the packs.
'Do not venture too deeply into Dol Dínen. The danger would be too great, even for your fellowship.'
'One less leader walks amongst the Wargs, thanks to you.'
'You have slain the chieftain of the Wargs of Dol Dínen, and within his own den. Your courage is great, ${PLAYER}.'

The Wargs mingle with the Orcs at Dol Dínen, south-east of Esteldín.
In the hope of breaking the will and courage of the Wargs of Dol Dínen, the Ranger Celephadh has asked you to slay the Warg-chieftain. He warned you to take allies with you.

Celephadh resides at Esteldín.
You made your way amongst the Wargs, Orcs, and goblins in Dol Dínen and defeated the Warg-chieftain. Now you should return to Celephadh with your report.
You have mined Angmar Coal (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, Outlander. I am a smith of Aughaire, but at the moment, I have precious little work to do. It is not for a lack of iron though -- the ancient battlefields of Angmar are full of broken weapons and stores of old black iron.
'The problem is that a very hot fire is needed to work this old metal. Since time out of mind, we gathered a hard, hot-burning coal from the hills in the north. In these days, though, we cannot venture near Donnvail, as the other clans would attack us if we entered their lands, and we have not the strength ourselves to assert our old rights.
'But I am told you are a fierce warrior of the south. Perhaps you can gather coal for my forge where I cannot. At any odds, the coal outcroppings lie just to the north of Donnvail-town, a stone's throw from its walls. Donnvail is a considerable distance north of here, east of the fortress of the Angmarim.'
'Here, take this pick. It is the same as those commonly used by the workers of Donnvail and should serve you adequately in this task.'
'Yes! That is it...the hard black coal of Angmar. Just the thing for the forge. You have my thanks, Outlander!'
'Please gather the hard coal from the northern hills. The soft coal of the south will not do at all, I am afraid.'

The coal of Angmar can be found just north of the hostile town of Donnvail, far to the north of Aughaire.

Please retrieve it for us, and you will have done us a great service.'
'Well done, my friend! This trove will serve us well when next we must trade for food and weapons.'
'I fear I have set you too hard a task. But there is no shame in failure in this thing.'

'You have gained something of a reputation as a warrior, it seems. Perhaps you can assist our clan anew. We have little wealth here, but what we have comes in part from bloodstones -- gems we use for ornaments and in trade. With the coming of so many drakes in the hills to the north beyond the old gates of Angmar, we have been unable to gather these stones, as the drakes have occupied the place the bloodstones can be found.
'Our scouts say that the drakes actually eat the bloodstones they find. With all those teeth, it is hard to believe they need them to chew their food, but perhaps they just like the taste. Be that as it may, we need those stones. The stones can frequently be found amongst the remains of the drake's victims.
'Remember the drakes are terrible foes, so you would be wise to take friends.'
'Good, this is all I asked for. You are truly a fierce warrior to have braved the menace of the drakes.'
'Please, bring me the bloodstones I require.'

You must return the bloodstones you have gathered to Lakhina of Aughaire.
Collected crawler-flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Placed roasted crawler-flesh
Tasgall has survived the Beast-lord's assault!

'These hill-beasts are growing more and more dangerous. We have heard that their leader is a matriarch of their kind, secretive and cunning, who in turn serves the drakes. If we can lure out this beast-mother and defeat her, the other hill-beasts may be cowed or routed.
'We know that these beasts greatly prize roasted crawler-flesh. I would ask you first to hunt crawlers in the area, bring their flesh back to me to be roasted, and then take the meat out to the hill-beast lairs where we may draw out this mother of the beasts.
'Beware though -- while the crawlers are no great threat, the matriarch may be a foe beyond the power of any lone warrior to overcome.'

'These Crawlers have been roasted to a fine... something.'
'In any case, take this vile stuff to the hill-beasts. You will find the old gate into the valley occupied by the hill-beasts and drakes. A short way into these valleys you will find a small cave within which the Beast-mother is believed to make her lair.
Place the roasted crawlers on the great stone just within the entrance to draw the creature out. It is then that you must strike!'

'Ha! Well done, Southron! I guess those rumors of the Beast-lord were false then - I had half expected you to face a mated pair of the horrid beasts!
'Wait... Do you hear something?'

'Revolting stuff, is it not? But keep in mind, if you have got nothing else, you can live off it. Anyway, roasted it is even worse than raw, but the hill-beasts seem to like it.
'Hold a few minutes while I cook up this lot.'
'Bring me the flesh of crawlers so that I may prepare it for the beast-mother.'

'I am most greatful for your intervention. I had heard rumours from the hunters that there might be a mated pair of those horrible creatures up in the hills, but I had dismissed them as folly.'
'Alas it was my own folly that drew the wrath of her mate down upon us and nearly cost us all our lives, please accept my sincerest apology and accept these tokens of my appreciation for saving my life.'
Bring the crawler-flesh to Tasgall
Collect crawler-flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Tasgall
Lure out and defeat the Beast-mother
Speak with Tasgall
Speak with Tasgall
The Great Beast

The strange hill-beasts have become a serious problem of late. It seems that they are ruled by a secretive matriarch who serves the drakes. If she can be defeated, perhaps the threat of the hill-beasts will fade.
'You must slay the beast-mother!'

Crawlers can be found in the general area not far north of Aughaire.
Hunt crawlers for their flesh and bring it back to Tasgall to be roasted.
Tasgall has roasted the crawlers you brought him. You can return to him to learn the next step in his plan to defeat the Beast-mother.

The rock in the hill-beast lair is at the entrance to the valley, not far north of Aughaire.
Tasgall has given you some roasted crawler-flesh, which you should bring to a certain rock in the lairs of the hill-beasts.
Having successfully defeated the Beast-mother, you should return to Tasgall's camp and speak with him.
You have defeated the vengeful Beast-lord and saved Tasgall's life. Speak with him.

'We have kindred who hunt in the great swamp of Malenhad to the east. It is a dangerous place, full of poisonous brimstone-clouds, foul water, and strange beasts, but there are many good things to be had there, too. Our brave hunters bring us much food and other things of worth from Malenhad, but we need to send them supplies so they can do their work.
'If you would, please bring these goods to Othran at the hunting camp in the south-west corner of the swamp. It may be that you will find hunting challenges there for yourself.
'Be wary of the patrols of the Angmarim. They do not hunt us -- yet -- but they may not be so kind to outlanders like you.'
'You have come with supplies from Talaghlan? That is good, for ours were running short.'
'Why do you come to this place?'
Bring the hunting supplies to Othran
The Brimstone Swamp
Taraghlan told you of a hunting camp of his people in the south-western parts of Malenhad.
'Bring those supplies to Othran in Malenhad...the hunters will have need of them.'

Othran is at the hunting-camp in the south-west corner of Malenhad.
Taraghlan has asked you to bring the supplies to Othran at the hunting camp in Malenhad.
You defeated Bloodwing!

'The most dangerous game of these hills are the wicked and cunning drakes. In truth, they hunt us as much as we hunt them. It is by the death of these great beasts that true hunter's mettle may be tested.
'Already you have proved your strength in battling these lesser beasts, but now we have lost several of our hunters to one drake in particular, who rules the rest of this brood, mighty in strength and cunning.
Perhaps you might enjoy the challenge of slaying this mighty drake, whom we have called Bloodwing.'
'Ha! You have proven more the hunter than you seem, Outlander! I salute you. You have earned this reward, and more!'
Defeat Bloodwing

Drakes are the most dangerous game in the foothills of Angmar, and the Hillmen consider them the truest test of a hunter's skill.
Now they have challenged you to defeat the most powerful of the drakes in the foothills - Bloodwing.
'How goes your quest to slay Bloodwing? I would hold no shame against you, should you choose not to face him - many have died in his jaws.'

There are drake lairs north of Aughaire in the high hills by some ancient ruins.
You have been asked to hunt the most dangerous among them, the vicious drake Bloodwing.

Cuinthorn is back at Aughaire.
Having slain many drakes, you should return to Cuinthorn for your reward.
Defeated hill-beasts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There have always been vicious and wicked drakes in Angmar. Whether they came to serve the legendary dragons of old or arose naturally, no Man can say. But now there is something new under the sun.
'Strange beasts have been seen in and around the drake lairs north of Aughaire. It almost seems as if these monsters are servants or pets of the drakes. No matter, for they have been wandering out of the camps to attack hunters and travellers. One way or another, we must put a stop to these beasts, and I ask you to help us in this matter.
'Slay them until they learn to stay by their masters' sides and not trouble us. We have enough troubles already....'
'Very good. You have done well. There are still many hill-beasts wandering the hills, but perhaps they will not be so ready to attack our people.'
Defeat hill-beasts (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Strange Beasts
Strange bestial creatures have invaded the foothills north of Aughaire. It seems to the Hillmen of Aughaire that these beasts are servants or pets of the evil drakes of the region.
'There are many hill-beasts left to kill. They must trouble us no more.'

There are hill-beasts in the highlands north of Aughaire.
Tasgall has asked you to slay the hill-beasts who have become a danger in the area.
Having slain many hill-beasts, you should return to Tasgall for your reward.
Collected turtle-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected turtle shell-plates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You have done well hunting vermin, Southron, but let us see if you can handle more substantial prey.
'The giant turtles of Malenhad are valued by my people both for their meat, which is edible, and for their shells. They can be deadly foes at close quarters, and if you fight them, you may damage their shells before you manage to kill them.
'I will pay for both their shell plates and meat if you think you are up to the challenge. The turtles live throughout this part of the swamp.'
'Good shells. Meat isn't spoiled yet. I will pay for this.'
'The turtles aren't too much for you, are they, Southron?'
Bring the turtle meat and shell plates to Othran
Collect turtle-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect turtle shell-plates (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Malenhad is home to turtles of enormous size, which the Hillmen value for their edible meat and tremendous shells.

The turtles live throughout the western reaches of Malenhad. Othran is at Tyrn Lhug, in the south-west corner of Malenhad.
Othran has offered to pay you for the meat and shell plates of the giant turtles of Malenhad.

'So, Southron, you have proved yourself more than worthy to hunt in the brimstone swamp of Malenhad. Perhaps you wish to gain even more glory? There is prey in this swamp that is too dangerous even for we who have hunted these swamps since time out of mind.
'I speak of the dreaded Ancient Ironscale, a monster so deadly that none of my people have ever faced it...and survived to tell the tale of it.
'I think it will be impossible for one southron, however doughty, to defeat such a foe, but even were you able, with companions, to kill this beast, I would be forced to admit you are true hunters and warriors of renown. The Ancient Ironscale is a rare beast, but it can sometimes be found amongst its lesser brethren in the swamp.'

'What? You have slain the Ancient Ironscale? I am astonished! I admit that I had not expected you to even make the attempt, not after telling you of its terrible menace.
'I must be honest with you, Southron, this was not quite the legendary foe I made it out to be. In fact, we hunters seek out the beast when we come of age in an ancient ritual amongst our people. Of course, not all of the youths return from these hunts....
'But still, it is a great accomplishment for one not born to the harsh, blasted hills and fetid bogs of the North. I must praise you for a worthy deed. You are a true hunter of Angmar.'
The brimstone swamp of Malenhad is also home to a terrible breed of beast, which the Hillmen call the \qAncient Ironscale\q.
'The Ancient Ironscale is too great a challenge for you, Southron? I am not surprised.'
'You are stronger than you appear to hunt so well within Malenhad.'
'Welcome, mighty ${PLAYER}, slayer of the dreaded Ironscale.'

The rare Ancient Ironscale can sometimes be found amongst its lesser brethren in Malenhad.
Othran has challenged you and your fellows to slay the dreaded Ancient Ironscale, lord of the fell turtles of Malenhad.

Othran is at his camp in the western part of Malenhad.
You should return to Othran to tell him the tale of your victory against the dreaded Ancient Ironscale.
Collected chunks of leech-flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected swamp-fly wings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected norboglir-legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'There are many strange beasts in this swamp. Vile creatures abound in this place -- perhaps the evil air fosters their growth -- but even the vilest of vermin has its use.
'The flesh of the loathsome swamp leeches can be used by our healers to prepare medicines. Swamp-fly wings are light, flexible, and tough and can be used for many crafting tasks. Nerbeglir are little more than monstrous crickets, but for all their odd appearance, their legs make a tasty meal when roasted.
'Hunt these verminous beasts, and I will pay well for these trophies. You can find these creatures scattered throughout this part of the swamp.'
'Good, good. In Malenhad, we must make use of any beast we find.'
'Can you not find enough of the vermin?'
Bring the trophies to Othran
Collect chunks of leech-flesh (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect swamp-fly wings (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect norboglir-legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Value of Vermin
Malenhad, the vile brimstone swamp of Angmar, is rife with vile and disgusting creatures, but even the strangest of these creatures has its uses to the Hillmen of Angmar.

Huge nerbeglir, leeches, and swamp-flies can be found throughout the swamp near the hunters' camp.
Othran has asked you to collect norboglir-legs, leech-flesh, and swamp-fly wings, which his people use to their benefit.
Collected hill-claw beaks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You there...you help Reko?
'Hill-claw claws. No, how do you say it? Beaks? Like birds? Yes, hill-claw beaks.
'You go get hill-claw beaks. I will give you shiny pieces of metal taken from Orc-folk. Many hill-claws not far.'
'You have brought me many beaks. That is good. Here is the shiny metal.'
'No beaks? No shiny metal.'
Bring the hill-claw beaks to Reko at Lehmä-koti.
Collect hill-claw beaks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Claws of the Earth
Reko, the Earth-kin hunter, desires the beaks of the hill-claws, though for what, the creature would not say.

Hill-claws can be found throughout Ram Dúath.
Reko has asked you to collect the hill-claw beaks he desires.
Collected root vegetables (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen, little one. You are brave to come here and help us. Maybe if you are fighting Orcs and flying bat-women anyway, you will do us another service? We eat the fruits of the earth -- root vegetables -- that grow in the gorges to the east, the old little people call it Duvairë. But now the Orcs and flying bat-women make it hard for us to gather them. If you are there killing, maybe you can bring us some vegetables, too?'
'Very good! These will make a good stew. You have our thanks, little one.'
'We want the root vegetables that grow to the east in the Duvairë.'
Bring the root vegetables back to Eetu at Lehmä-koti
Collect root vegetables (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fruits of the Earth
The Earth-kin are fond of a certain kind of tuber that grows in the gorges in the east side of Ram Dúath in the Duvairë -- the places now frequented by the Orkish-army and merrevail.

The root vegetables grow in the gorges on the east side of Ram Dúath in the Duvairë.
Eetu has asked you to gather vegetables for the Earth-kin of the Suuri-lehmä.
Collected spider-silk skeins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You there...you will help the Jorthkyn, yes?
'Spiders make silk. We need silk. You kill spiders, take their silk, then we give you the Orcs' shiny metal.
'We have much shiny metal taken from Orcs. Little people like shiny things, yes?'
'Good silk. Here is the shiny metal.'
'No silk? No shiny metal.'
Bring the spider-silk to Aarnikka
Collect spider-silk skeins (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Silken Strands
The Earth-kin, rugged, practical, and earthy as they are, make extensive use of silk, which they obtain almost exclusively from spiders.

There are spiders throughout Ram Dúath.
Aarnikka has asked you to collect silk from the spiders of the Ram Dúath.
Collected battle standards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your prowess has already impressed the warriors of Aughaire and instilled them with some hope - yet the Angmarim are well fortified behind great walls of stone and gates of steel, and their hearts yet quail at the thought of assaulting such strongholds.
I need your help again, to stand as an example of valour in the face of such monumental dangers. There is a fort to the north-east of Aughaire that is ripe for a raid. The banners of the enemy clan show their allegiance to the Iron Crown of Angmar. Infiltrate the fort and bring back those dark standards... Show the warriors of Aughaire the way to battle such powers.'
'Ha! If this does not stir the Men of Aughaire, nothing will!'
'What happened to the battle standards?'
Collect battle standards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the battle standards back to Raith
Dark Standards

Your prowess has already impressed the warriors of Aughaire and instilled them with some hope - yet the Angmarim are well fortified behind great walls of stone and gates of steel, and their hearts yet quail at the thought of assaulting such strongholds.
'Collect the battle standards of our enemies. It will give great heart to my warriors to see Angmar bloodied in this war!'

The fort of the enemy clan is to the north-east of Aughaire.
Raith has asked you to raid an enemy clan's fort and take their banners of war.

Raith is back at Aughaire.
Having collected the enemy battle standards, you should bring them back to Raith.

'I face now an unexpected and most difficult obstacle in my quest to raise the warriors of Aughaire against the Iron-crown. There is a very important figure amongst the clans of the Hill-men - he is called the Silent Judge, and he is chosen by a council of all the clans to mediate in conflicts between us, and act as the final arbiter of justice in such matters.
The Silent Judge is traditionally supposed to be neutral in such matters, but it seems this one has fallen under the sway of Angmar. Worse yet, if dark rumour holds true he will shortly rule against our clan and cast us out, setting all our people against us. This must not come to pass.
What I ask of you now is not something I ask lightly... You must strike down the Silent Judge before he rules and brings down all our bretheren upon us. He must not become the mouthpiece of Angmar or my people are lost!
The Silent Judge resides far to the north-east in the town of Donnvail, be swift about this matter, and I will see that you are well rewarded!'

'At last! The final obstacle to our uprising has been swept away. Bereft of the guidance of Angmar's pawn, they will be confused and conflicted, now I shall prepare the warriors of Aughaire to strike! My thanks to you ${PLAYER}!'
The Silent Judge
One obstacle remains before the men of Aughaire may engage in true battle against Angmar. The Silent Judge has fallen under the sway of Angmar and will not sanction the war. He must be removed.
'Go to Donnvail and slay the Silent Judge before his ruling seals our doom.'
'The Men of Aughaire shall know what it means to be free!'
'It will not be long now, my friend... the warriors of Aughaire are ready to strike!'

The Silent Judge is in the town of Donnvail, north and east of Aughaire.
The Silent Judge, formerly a neutral resolver of clan disputes, has become a mouthpiece of the Angmarim. Yet the men of Aughaire hesitate to raise any hand against him, bound yet by the ties of tradition. Raith has asked you to slay the Silent Judge, to free his folk to strike against the evil of the Iron-crown.

Raith is back at Aughaire.
With the Silent Judge dead, you should return to Aughaire to tell Raith the tale of your deeds.
Collected skull amulets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected bloodstone pendants (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected charm bracelets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen, Southron, to my sad tale. We of Aughaire are at odds with all the clans of the hills, who have abandoned their ancient freedoms and now serve their Angmarim masters at Carn Dûm.
'They have been raiding our folk, taking our goods, murdering where they can, and breaking the clan-law with abandon. Yet our chief, Crannog, still will not move openly against them. I say that it is time to fight, but no one heeds me. Wise old Arzhur just strokes his beard, and that other Southron, Corunir, shakes his head.
'Mayhap you can help us where our own folk have lost heart. The Hillmen you will see outside Aughaire to the north and north-east are almost all our enemies. They carry various tokens that signify their status as men of blood, as warriors, and as servants of the Iron Crown. If you can take these trophies to show to our people, I hope they will realize that it is better to fight than to yield.'
'Well done, Southron. I wonder what the elders will say when I show them this hoard of trophies!'
'I need those trophies of battle to show to the other Men of Aughaire.'
Bring the trophies back to Raith
Collect skull amulets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect bloodstone pendants (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect charm bracelets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Trophies of War

Raith is at odds with the Aughaire chieftain, Crannog. Crannog has tried to avoid hostilities with the other Angmar-dominated clans, but Raith believes that the Men of Aughaire should fight their enemies.

There are hostile Hillmen to the north and north-east of Aughaire. Raith is at Aughaire, south-west of the evil Hillman-encampments.
Raith has asked you to collect trophies from the hostile Hillmen of Angmar to show his people that it is possible to fight their foes and win.
False orders planted (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Many of the people of Aughaire would rather forget that the Iron Crown even exists, much less strive against it. Yet I have faith in the words of the man Golodir who once led us to break with those evil ones. I believe that all of our problems can be laid at the feet of Carn Dûm.
'The Angmarim must be stopped. In truth, though, we lack the strength to fight them in the usual way, so I hope that you will be able to aid us to fight them without shield-walls and trumpets. Deceit and misdirection may serve us better. The Angmarim control their vast armies through a long chain of command. Through spies amongst those supposedly loyal to them, I have learned something of their methods of passing orders and have forged several sets of documents that will sow confusion and possibly even conflict amongst their ranks, but I need you to make sure these false orders fall into the 'wrong' hands.
'You must slip them into the strongboxes used by their sub-commanders to store and protect important documents. You can find such strongboxes in the Orc-camps on the outskirts of Dûn Covád.'

'Ha, very good! The Angmarim will no doubt be days figuring out where those orders came from!
'If we are particularly lucky, there may even be a few brawls between unruly bands of orcs over who has the right to march here or pitch a tent there.'
Plant orders in the Angmarim chain of command (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Soltakh
False Orders
Soltakh believes the problems of the folk of Aughaire are all the fault of the Angmarim for corrupting the other clans and inciting them against Aughaire.
'The sub-commander's strongboxes can be found far to the north of Aughaire in the outer camps of Dûn Covád.'

The sub-commanders' strongboxes can be found far to the north of Aughaire in the outer camps of Dûn Covád.
Soltakh has asked you to slip false orders into the Angmarim chain of command.

Soltakh is back at Aughaire.
Having slipped the false orders into the Angmarim strongboxes, you should return to Soltakh in Aughaire.

'I am afraid that we may have pulled on a Dragon's tail. I have learned that the commander of the Angmarim is most wroth with the chaos sewn among his commanders by the false orders you planted. He is said to be planning an attack on Aughaire, clan treaties or no clan treaties.
'Though the blame is mine alone, I must ask you now to undertake a most dangerous mission. If this evil man, Angmar's Lord of the Western Marches, the gate-keeper of Carn Dûm, can be defeated before his plans are set in motion, we may be safe here for a while. But this will be a very perilous task, as he will surely be very well-guarded in his fortress, north of Aughaire.
'I must advise you to go there with a group of stout and fearless allies.'

'A truly great deed! You have redeemed my folly with a victory! It will be some time before the Angmarim name a new Lord, and we can hope he will have other things to worry about when he assumes his office.
'Aughaire is in your debt this day.'
The Gate-keeper
Soltakh has learned that a commander of the Angmarim plans to order an attack on Aughaire. This man, the Lord of the Western Marches, commands the fort that guards the western pass into Carn Dûm.
'You must defeat the Lord of the Western Marches. That is our only hope!'
'Your great deeds have saved Aughaire from the Angmarim!'

The Lord of the Western Marches rules the Angmarim fortress north of Aughaire.
Soltakh has asked you to raid the Angmarim and to slay the Lord of the Western Marches before he can assemble a force to attack Aughaire.

Soltakh is back at Aughaire.
Now that the Lord of the Western Marches has been defeated, you should return to Soltakh to let him know the good news.

'The Silk Lady....I wish I knew more about her. I have kin in Donnvail, a town of the Angmarim. My cousin Cormag is from one of the clans that cleaved to the words of the Iron Crown, and they are now the enemies of Aughaire, but still he has a blood bond with me and will answer your questions if he can.
'He knows much of the doings of the evil folk of the Iron Crown, and I think he will tell you where the Silk Lady can be found. Donnvail is in the north-eastern hills of Fasach-falroid, far to the north of Aughaire.
'Go there and learn what you may!'

'Tell me why I should speak to you at all, Outlander! Just being here is a crime for your kind. You must have the blood of my kin on your hands...Lornë sends you? Ah...I suppose I must. Blood tells....
'The Silk Lady is a great lady in service to the Iron Crown, from what I hear. She is said to be as cruel as she is beautiful...much like my cousin, I must say.
'Well, in any event, she is not to be found here. I have heard she has gone to Malenhad, to an outpost that guards the path into the heights of eastern Angmar. That is all I know. Now begone from this place!'

'What? The Silk Lady is here in Malenhad!
'I am sorry, my friend. I have sent you on a long weary road to learn that our foe is on our very doorstep. But you have my thanks for those many miles you have walked on my behalf.'
The Blood-bond
Lornë only knows the Silk Lady as a name of fear, but may know someone else who can import greater knowledge.

Cormag is in the Angmarim-controlled town of Donnvail in the north-eastern hills of Fasach-falroid, far to the north of Aughaire.
Lornë has asked you to seek out her cousin Cormag and ask him what he knows of the Silk Lady.

Lornë is at the hunters' camp in Malenhad, far to the south of Donnvail.
It seems that the Silk Lady resides at an Angmarim outpost on the north side of Malenhad that guards the way into eastern Angmar. You should return to Lornë and let her know what you have learned.

'So, it seems that the Silk Lady holds the key to my sister's fate, and that she is conveniently at hand in a nearby outpost.
'I must tell you, though, that the outpost is heavily-guarded, and what I have heard of the Silk Lady, I fear that you would not be able to fight your way to find her on your own. If you will undertake to learn my sister's fate, you should bring allies with you.
'I beseech you to do this and either free or avenge my sister.'

'What have you learned? What? No! It is impossible!
'No...but I must accept the truth of what you tell me. Muirnë was ever a wilful child, spoiled selfish. But still, to become a spider-keeper of the Iron Crown! I have wasted a year of my life weeping for the fate of a monster!
'Alas, this is a bitter draught to down. But dark though these tidings be, you have done what I asked, Southron. You have my thanks...I am too deeply in your debt, but I will try to pay you what I can.'

'Muirnë? You ask of Muirnë? Do you dare to mock me? Do you dare?
'You fools! I am Muirnë!
'Oh, this is too much. Such a delicious joke! My wretch of a sister has been moping in the swamp for a year now, not knowing that I went to the Iron Crown of my own free will! I would never go down to death with those fools of Aughaire, never fight against the great and glorious rulers of the north!
'The Iron Crown welcomed me, and her great sorcerers have taught me much of the beautiful arts of darkness. I have signed a blood pact with the steward of the great Witch-king himself, and I have been admitted to the circle of power.
'And that is all you will ever know, all my sister will ever know... for now it is time for you to die! Die and fall into darkness!'
Confront the dreaded Silk Lady
You learned from Lornë's cousin that the Silk Lady resides at an Angmarim outpost on the north side of Malenhad.
'Alas, poor Muirnë! But it is better that she is dead than that she continue to serve the evil men of Angmar.'
'Would that you could have saved my sister, ${PLAYER}, but alas, it was not meant to be.'

The Silk Lady is in the outpost of the Angmarim on the north side of Malenhad, guarding the path into eastern Angmar.
Lornë has asked you and your companions to raid the Angmarim outpost and to confront the Silk Lady in hopes of learnig the fate of Muirnë.

Lornë is at the hunters' camp in Malenhad.
You confronted the Silk Lady and learned that she was in fact Lornë's sister Muirnë. You defeated the Silk Lady in combat and now must bear the dark tidings back to Lornë.

'Listen, well, stranger. To make my way here, I must do some hunting with the other men of this little camp, but in truth I am not here to live the life of a hunter. I am here for the sake of my sister, Muirnë, and if things have gone as I fear, I will take a blood price from her murderer. But I still hope that the worst has not come to pass, and if she still lives, I wish to rescue her from her captors.
'Many months past, she left our home in Aughaire to go guesting with kin, but on the way I am told she was taken by the Angmarim. From what I can tell, they were encamped at the nearby outpost, but thus far I have been unable to learn more.
'Will you help me? Go to the outpost in the south-west of the swamp, on the way to Ram Dúath. If you see no woman of the hills there, then find the commander of the camp; perhaps he will have something to say.'

'So, she was not there after all. All my patience, wasted! But I should offer my thanks. I might have waited here much longer and still learned nothing!
'The Silk Lady...that is a name I have heard, though. Recently it has become a name of dread in these hills. Whispered tales speak of a cruel and vicious woman of Angmar who commands deadly spiders. It is said she is as dangerous to her fellow Angmarim as she is to the enemies of the Iron Crown....'

'What? Muirnë? You ask for her? Ha!
'You'll not find her here, Southron! She moved on long ago. Seek you the Silk Lady if you would know more.
'But I think the Silk Lady will not be troubled with your presence, Outlander...not if I kill you here and now and redeem the incompetence of my men!'
Look for Muirnë
Ask the camp commander about Muirnë
The Blood-price
Lornë told you that she joined the hunting party to find her missing sister, Muirnë, only she fears that the worst has befallen her.
'Please, look for my sister, Muirnë. I must hold to the hope she lives, until it is proven otherwise.'

The Angmarim camp is in the south-west corner of Malenhad, on the way to Ram Dúath.
Lornë has asked you to look for some sign of her sister and if necessary to confront the outpost's commander for news of Muirnë.

Lornë is at the hunters' camp in Malenhad.
Muirnë was not in the Angmarim outpost, but the Angmarim commander mentioned a Silk Lady who may know more. You should return to Lornë and tell her what you have learned.

You have found a cloudy spring

'There is much water in Angmar, but most of it is foul, poisoned, and deadly to drink. Even the rare springs of pure water can sometimes turn foul, when some old poison leeches from the soil.
'Of course, we must know which water is pure and which foul, but it is a deadly game to tell merely by taste. Instead we collect water from various springs and feed it to swamp-fly grubs. These creatures will sicken and die if they are given foul water.
'Banners have been placed at six of the shallow springs of the swamp where once fresh water could be found. Take these water-skins, find the banners, and collect water from the six springs.'
'Well done. I trust you remember which skin came from which spring? Very good, ${PLAYER}.'
'Could you not count to six?'
Fill water skins (${CURRENT} of ${MAX})
Filled water skin (${CURRENT} of ${MAX})
Bring the water-skins back to Murdaigán
Water of Life and Death
Malenhad has long been a place of poisonous waters and vapours, corrupted by the powers of ancient Angmar during the reign of the Witch-king. There is little of value left there.
'This is not a difficult task, at least not if you can count up to six.'

There are banners placed near springs throughout the western half of Malenhad.
Murdaigán has asked you to locate the banners placed near springs believed to bear fresh water and to fill several water skins.

Murdaigán is back at the hunters' camp in the south-west corner of the swamp.
Having collected several water samples, you should bring them back to Murdaigán.
Collected fire-worm hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hold...I would have a moment of your time. You seem to be capable of looking after yourself in this harsh land. We hunt the beasts of the swamp, and our most valuable and dangerous prey are the fire-worms.
'Their hides are extremely tough, proof against both water and fire, and can be worked into armour, clothes, and all manner of useful things. If you should happen to collect any hides of the local worms, please bring them here, and I will pay you well.
'But then, you are a southron...you may not have the courage or prowess it will take.'
'Ha! This is good. We will both profit. Here are your coins.'
'Were the worms too much for you to handle, Southron?'
Bring the worm hides back to Rodakhan
Collect fire-worm hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Rodakhan the hunter has said he will pay well for worm-hides. However, worms are some of the most dangerous beasts of the swamp.

Fire-worms can be found in the south-east part of Malenhad. Rodakhan is at the hunting camp, west of the worm-lairs.
Rodakhan has asked you to collect fire-worm hides for him.
You have found Machan!

'Machan is a bold hunter. Perhaps too bold. He vowed to return with the hides of fire-worms from their lairs east of this camp, and he has not returned in good time.
'Would you look for Machan, Southron? It may be he is in need of assistance. I will reward you for your efforts....'
Find the hunter Machan
The Worm-hunter
Machan the hunter has gone missing after vowing to return with hides from the fearsome worms of Malenhad.

Machan the hunter should be somewhere in the fire-worm lairs in the south-east part of Malenhad.
The hunter Murdaigán has asked you to locate Machan, who was hunting fire-worms in Malenhad.
You have saved Machan

'Curse my foolish pride! I should never have ventured into this worm-lair on my own. There are just too many of them, and now that I have found this safe place, I do not dare try to sneak away on my own.
'Can you help me to escape? I would ask that you not tell the other hunters, for I would be ridiculed for the rest of my life.'

'Machan is safe then, is he? Good. He is an impulsive and proud man, and I had feared that he might have gotten in over his own head.
'Not that such a thing could ever happen, nor would his pride permit him to be rescued if it did.'
'I suspect that I -- and Machan -- owe you greater thanks than your tale suggests, and so I do thank you most sincerely.'
Talk to Machan when you are ready
The Worm Turns
Machan foolishly sought to hunt fire-worms alone and ended up trapped and wounded.
Help Machan to get out of the fire-worm lair.
Tell Murdaigán that Machan is safe.
Token of Deluches collected
Collected token of Deluches

'It occurs to me that this spirit you fought is after all a creature of the same ilk as those we seek to banish. He must not bear his own token, or he would not have been able to flee you so easily when he was on the brink of defeat.
'My guess is that this last token can be found in the lair of the sorcerers themselves. The necromancers of Imlad Balchorth hide in a ruin high in the hills on the west side of the area. Quite possibly one of the necromancers carries the token himself. I suspect, too, that you will find a second shrine in their lair. I was a fool to think they only had one.
'Recover the token of Deluches and bring all of the tokens to the master shrine. No doubt you will encounter your enemy again, and mayhap the chief of the necromancers as well..but this time if you are victorious, his defeat will be final.'

'You have done very well indeed. Deluches was evidently the key to the necromancers' control over those spirits. It is only unfortunate that those which have been banished are but a small part of the host of Angmar.'
The shrine flares to life....
Nothing happens.
Defeat the necromancer and claim his token
Bring the tokens to Eithel Úmfaer
Banishing the Darkness
The sudden appearance of Deluches, the captain of the fell spirits, kept you from banishing the creatures from the shrine.
'You have undone the plans of the necromancers of Angmar. Well done!'

The necromancer of Imlad Balchorth can be found at the ruins high in the western hills of the area.
The chief sorcerer of the necromancers, the Spirit-master, no doubt has the token of Deluches, the spirit-captain.

The master shrine of Eithel Úmfaer stands before you.
You retrieved the Token of Deluches and must now bring all thirteen tokens in your possession to the master shrine.
Deluches, captain of the fell spirits, has been summoned to Eithel Úmfaer, the master shrine in Imlad Balchorth, where he must be destroyed.

Banfuir is back at Gabilshathûr.
You have defeated Deluches and banished at least some of the fell spirits of Angmar. You should bring the good tidings to Banfuir.
Token of Morgoth collected (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Angmar was banned to my people long ago, for many things dwell here that are better left alone. Unfortunately, with the coming of Mordirith, those things cannot be left ignored. Perhaps the worst of the creatures which dwell here are the fell spirits, creatures that served Morgoth in the First Age of this world.
'At the height of the Witch-realm of Angmar, the Witch-king had power to command these spirits, and it is said there are other creatures which have a similar power. It was these creatures that the Witch-king sent to the Barrow-downs after the passing of our brethren in Cardolan. It is these creatures who stir the bones of the dead.
'I bid you to go north into Imlad Balchorth and confront these demons. Claim the Tokens of Morgoth they carry. Perhaps we can use the tools of the Enemy to banish the fell spirits from Arda.'
'That the sorcerers of Angmar would dare to commune with these fell spirits speaks well enough to their evil. No Man, pure of heart, would deign to do such...it is an abomination.'
'I know this is a dark task I have given you, but I bid you be of stout heart. In the end, we will be doing much to banish the dark spirits of Morgoth in Imlad Balchorth.'
Bring the tokens back to Banfuir
Claim tokens of Morgoth from Imlad Balchorth (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Spirits of Morgoth
Imlad Balchorth is the dwelling place of a host of fell spirits, servants of Morgoth from an earlier Age, now in service to Angmar.

There are fell spirits in Imlad Balchorth, to the north of Gabilshathûr. Banfuir is back in Gabilshathûr.
Banfuir has asked you to confront the fell spirits of Morgoth to learn if there might be a way to banish them from Arda.
Banished Deluches

'These tokens bear signs of Morgoth, terrible sigils that may well be what is binding the fell spirits to this place. It may be that they can be used to ward them away, as well. It will take but a moment to scratch out the signs and etch in the Star of Elbereth....
'There! I believe these tokens can be used to banish the shades from this place, for they will not be able to bear the presence of this mark. You must find the shrine used by the Angmarim in their rituals. I believe it is on an islet in a small pond in southern Imlad Balchorth. It may be difficult to find, for it appears as a large iron spike, which is not uncommon among the works of the Angmarim.
'If you return the tokens to the shrine, I believe the fell spirits will be summoned to that place one last time, there to be banished forever.'

'Alas, I had not reckoned that the spirits' master would himself be a fell spirit, able to interfere with your quest. Why, I wonder, was he able to escape you so easily?
'I have sent you into grave danger on a fool's errand. But perhaps we can still repair my error.'
'I am sorry that your quest has failed. What has happened to the tokens I gave you? We cannot hope to suceed without them.'
Banish the fell spirits from the spirit-shrine
Bring the tokens back to Banfuir

Banfuir examined the tokens you recovered from the fell spirits and discovered that they bear signs of Morgoth, sigils that may be binding the spirits to the mortal world. A name also was written upon them: Deluches.

The shrine of the fell spirits is on an islet in a small pond in the southern part of Imlad Balchorth.
Banfuir has asked you to take the tokens you collected to the shrine of the fell spirits in Imlad Balchorth. The shrine can be recognized as a large iron spike, a common feature of the works of the Angmarim which might make the shrine difficult to find.

Banfuir is back at Gabilshathûr.
You were unable to defeat the terrible captain of the spirits, Deluches, so the fell spirits could not be banished. You should bring the tokens back to Banfuir and report these events.

'Know you aught of the lore of Angmar, of the days following the Witch-king's defeat at the Battle of Fornost?
'Well, no matter. You will learn...if Nethraw has anything to say about it. He is in a lonely vale far to the east of here, musing on the Seven Sentinels.
'I have no doubt he could use your assistance.'

'Well met! I have here a mystery from times past. Perhaps you can help me riddle it out. Long ago, just after the Witch-king's defeat at the Battle of Fornost, seven knights and chiefs of the allies swore on their swords to maintain a vigil over Angmar, to ensure that the evil would never rise again. Five there were who were Dúnedain of Arnor, one a knight of Gondor, and the last an elf of Glorfindel's host. The seven set up watch-towers around Angmar, and they settled into their vigil.
'The kingdom of Arthedain's main strength was destroyed in the battle, and the nation could not rise again. The surviving Dúnedain scattered, some going to Gondor, but a few others, like my forefathers, remained living quietly in the old land, eventually becoming the Rangers of the North.
'Ah, this is a long story, and my throat is dry. I will tell you more anon.'
The Secret of the Swords
There are many old tales of the days following the Battle of Fornost, but Nethraw is interested in only one.

The lore-master Nethraw can be found at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, a considerable distance to the east of Gabilshathûr.
Banfuir suggested you speak with the lore-master Nethraw about the fall of Angmar.

'Ah yes, where was I...? Well, the Seven Sentinels had sworn to keep a watch on Angmar, but there was no more kingdom of Arthedain to support them. The Seven maintained their vigil and upheld their oaths, but after many years, the six Men died. They were not replaced, as both Gondor and the remaining Dúnedain of Arnor had forgotten them.
'In sorrow, the Elf, whose name has been lost, made a vault in the knights' honour, and then he himself sailed west across the Sea. This is the vault of the Seven Sentinels, and an old tale tells that ancient treasure, imbued with a virtue for fighting the evil of Angmar, is buried here. Yet the keys to opening it are missing. The tale says that the vault can only be opened when the seven swords of the Seven Sentinels are once again raised, but the swords of those great heroes are long lost.
'Still, I have some clues. The first sword is called the Sword of Arvedui. It was borne by a knight who served Arvedui's son Aranarth, but who took up his vigil here rather than follow the other Dúnedain into obscurity. I believe that the sword is hidden somewhere around the dwarves' outpost of Gabilshathûr, which once was the site of the knight's watch-tower. The sword may still be hidden there, someplace.'

'Remarkable! So the tales are true! If this one sword has been found, perhaps the other six will reveal themselves as well! Perhaps the vault can be opened, and it may even hold some treasure that can be of use to us here!
'But I have raced ahead of myself. Recovering the other six swords will be no easy task. Indeed, it may well be an impossible quest. But we shall see....'
'Ah, I have no doubt the old tale is a mere fable. Or else the sword was lost long ago.'
Search for the sword of Arvedui
Bring the Sword of Arvedui to Nethraw
The Sword of Arvedui
Nethraw told you a tale of Seven Sentinels who swore to hold vigil over Angmar to ensure that the evil never returned.

'I am afraid I have let my enthusiasm for the old tales get the better of me.
'I should probably not have asked you to search for the sword, considering it is likely that either the sword was lost long ago, or else that the old tale is nothing more than a fable.'

The Sword of Arvedui is supposedly hidden somewhere around Gabilshathûr.
Nethraw has asked you to search Gabilshathûr for some evidence that the Sword of Arvedui was hidden there.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels east, of Gabilshathûr.

'At last, the time has come to open the ancient vault! I believe each of these seven statues must be given the correct sword before the vault can be opened...but the tale is unfortunately a bit vague. I suppose we could try all the combinations, but that might take a long time.
'I have made a copy of the relevant verses -- here, perhaps you can puzzle it all out.'

'You have done it! This chest contains treasures of past ages forged to fight the forces of darkness!
'After all of your effort and the danger you have seen, it is only right that you choose one of these items as your just reward. The rest will be sent to my brethren to distribute.'
'Have you not recovered the treasure of the Seven Sentinels?'
