'The third sword is called the Sword of Gondor. Of the host that fought the Witch-king at Fornost, many were knights and men-at-arms of Gondor, led by Eärnur, Prince of Gondor. One doughty knight, whose name has been lost, would not be outdone by the knights of Arthedain, and vowed to keep a vigil along with them.
'According to the tale, his watch-tower was at a place not far from here, called Maethad. Unfortunately, this place is infested with evil trolls, and worse, by the mighty Gertheryg, who are fearsome masters of arms.
'It would be all but impossible for you to venture into Maethad on your own, so if you would seek the third sword, I would counsel you to venture to the evil place only with stout companions.'
'You have impressed me mightily. The recovery of the Sword of Gondor is a great triumph over the evil creatures of Angmar, even if none of the other swords are recovered at all!'
'I knew I should not have asked you to go on this mission.'
Search for the Sword of Gondor
Bring the Sword of Gondor back to Nethraw
The Sword of Gondor
With the recovery of the swords of Arvedui and Rhudaur, Nethraw has become more confident that the remaining swords may be found.
'It will be very difficult to recover the Sword of Gondor if it is still to be found in Maethad.'

The Sword of Gondor is said to be found somewhere in Maethad, north of the Fane of the Seven Sentinels.
Nethraw has now asked you to search for the Sword of Gondor, in Maethad, a place garrisoned by many Trolls and Gertheryg. For this reason, you were cautioned not to venture there on your own.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Gondor to Nethraw.

'As I told you before, the other six swords will be much harder to recover, if indeed they still can be found at all.
'The second sword is called the Sword of Rhudaur. Evidently the Dúnedain knight who bore it was a descendant of those who fled the fall of Rhudaur long before and carried a sword from the days when Rhudaur was a kingdom of Arnor.
'According to the old tale, this knight's watch-tower seems to have once been found in the same location as one of the large Orc-camps north of Gabilshathûr. I know not which camp is the right one. But even if the sword can still be found, perhaps under such a marker as you found at Gabilshathûr, it will be no easy task to brave all those Orcs.'

'The Sword of Rhudaur!
'I am greatly heartened by your success! If the first two swords can be found where the tale tells, perhaps the remaining five will be found as well.
'The difficulty of collecting the swords grows. Make no doubt, I have asked you to find the easiest two swords first.'
'Alas, what have you done with the Sword of Rhudaur? Surely you have not lost it?'
Search for the Sword of Rhudaur
Bring the Sword of Rhudaur to Nethraw
The Sword of Rhudaur
You recovered the Sword of Arvedui, leading Nethraw to wonder if the other swords might not be recovered as well.
'I hope the Sword of Rhudaur is still there to be found. For all we know, it may long since have been looted by Orcs.'

The Sword of Rhudaur may be found at one of the fortified Orc-camps north of Gabilshathûr.
Nethraw has now asked you to search for the Sword of Rhudaur.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Rhudaur to Nethraw.

'The fourth sword is the Sword of Slaughter. The tale is unclear on this point, but I believe the knight who bore it was sickened by the carnage of the Battle of Fornost, and named his blade such because of the many corpses it left behind.
'The tale leads me to believe that this knight kept watch in the middle of one of the most dread areas of Angmar, in some high ruins a far distance west of the central island of Imlad Balchorth. Even then this region was known as a place of dread, a suitable place for this sword to be hidden.
'Again, I must warn you that allies will probably be required to recover this sword.'
'Four of the seven swords! Well done! But I fear the final three are in yet more dangerous parts of Angmar.'
'I fear this was but a foolish dream.'
Search for the Sword of Slaughter
Bring the Sword of Slaughter to Nethraw
The Sword of Slaughter
With every sword you find, Nethraw becomes more determined to find the others.
'I hesitate to ask you to venture into the accursed land of Imlad Balchorth merely for the sake of an old tale, but it seems there is some truth to the old story.'

The Sword of Slaughter is said to be found in a ruin in some high hills west of the large lake in Imlad Balchorth..
Nethraw has sent you to recover the Sword of Slaughter. You have been cautioned that it will be difficult to obtain without allies.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Slaughter to Nethraw.

'Next comes the Sword of Sorrow. This sword was carried by a knight who lost his lands and all his kin to the Angmarim. He swore his oath while bearing a terrible burden of sorrow and hatred.
'The tale says that this knight set up his tower not far east of here, in heights infested by evil drakes. These fell creatures are too fierce for any to fight on even terms, so yet again I must ask you to bring allies with you in the search for the sword.'
'We are near the end of our quest. There are but two swords left to collect!'
'Where is the Sword of Sorrow?'
Search for the Sword of Sorrow
Bring the Sword of Sorrow to Nethraw
The Sword of Sorrow
Four of the seven swords have been recovered, leaving only three.
'The Sword of Sorrow lies to the east, so the tale tells.'

The Sword of Sorrow is said to be found in drake-infested heights east of the Fane of the Seven Sentinels.
You have been sent to recover the Sword of Sorrow from its resting-place. Nethraw again suggests you take allies.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Sorrow to Nethraw.

'Finally, the last of the seven swords! This weapon is called the Sword of the Vigil, and it was borne by the leader of the Seven Sentinels, a knight who made his post in the most dangerous part of Angmar -- a place perhaps even more deadly than Carn Dûm itself!
'I speak of Nan Gurth, a place inhabited by terrible beasts and the most evil of foes. The tale tells not where in this dread place the sword can be found. Truly, I hesitate to ask you to go to such a terrible place, merely to satisfy my curiosity, and perhaps to uncover an ancient hoard. But too, it would be a shame to stop now, when we are so close!
'Certainly, as before, this quest is far too dangerous for a single adventurer to attempt alone.'
'The seven swords! Collected at last! I am trembling with excitement. But one small obstacle remains....'
'Where is the Sword of the Vigil?'
Search for the Sword of the Vigil
Bring the Sword of the Vigil to Nethraw
The Sword of the Vigil
You have recovered six of the seven swords, and Nethraw is most pleased.
'I would never forgive myself if I sent you to your death! Please be careful.'

The Sword of the Vigil is somewhere in Nan Gurth.
Nethraw told you the last of the seven swords may be found in a deadly place called Nan Gurth. He again warned you that allies will be required to obtain the sword.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of the Vigil to Nethraw.

'The Sword of Twilight was carried by the lone Elf in the company of the Seven Sentinels. The name of that sword perhaps derives from the feeling amongst some of the Elves that their time in Middle-earth draws to an end, and perhaps is an allusion to the direction of their retreat. Who can say?
'At any odds, the tale says the Elf's sword may be found far to the north, not all that distant from the place my kindred have made for themselves to spy upon Carn Dûm. I believe the sword's hiding place is in a lair of great and terrible spiders. No one adventurer would be able to retrieve the sword alone, so once again I must counsel you to seek allies in your quest'
'You have done well to this point, but there is one great challenge left.'
'Where is the Sword of Twilight?'
Search for the Sword of Twilight
Bring the Sword of Twilight back Nethraw
The Sword of Twilight
Five of the seven swords have been recovered, leaving only two.
'I hope you will be able to retrieve the Sword of Twilight.'

The Sword of Twilight is in a lair of spiders far to the north, near Gath Forthnír.
Nethraw has sent you in search of the Sword of Twilight, It seems once again that allies will be required to obtain the Sword from its hiding-place.

Nethraw is back at the Fane of the Seven Sentinels, east of Gabilshathûr.
You should bring the Sword of Twilight to Nethraw.
Collected rough gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, ${RACE}. I heard what you did for us. We are all at your service, I'm sure. So perhaps I can point you to a good thing in the way of thanks.
'Hiding out here, we can no longer go out prospecting or mining some of the outlying gem-bearing lodes we found. We know, though, that some of the minions of the Enemy -- trolls, Gorthorogs and the like -- have found those old mining locations and are gathering gems themselves.
'If you wish, you could go out hunting the Enemy in Gorothlad, in the general vicinity of Maethad. Many of those evil folk are no doubt gathering what gems they can, and you may be able to retrieve some of them. I'll give you a good price if you could bring me some.'
'Ha, you've done very well to gather all these stones. Have no fear...I'll give you a good price!'
'Of course not every troll is carrying around a hoard of gems! You'll have to look harder!'
Bring the rough gems to Bothwar
Collect rough gems (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The Dwarves of Gabilshathûr are unable to go out and prospect in these dark days, but they know that the armies of the Enemy have discovered some of their old mining locations and are extracting gems themselves.
Bothwar, the dwarf-miner of Gabilshathûr, has offered to pay you for gems you can find on Enemy-minions such as trolls and Gorthorogs in Gorothlad.
Collected the gemstone-hoard

'You've done very well for us, I must say. But -- if you can keep a secret -- let me tell you about one last thing.
'On my own time, you understand, I once found a small cave with a lovely little vein of gems. I mined it out and set it aside for a suitable occasion so I could brag to the other miners here, but before I could collect the gems, these accursed Orcs settled down around here. If you'd retrieve them for me...well let's say you won't regret it.
'The hoard is in a sort of narrow gulch far to the east, in the southernmost part of Maethlad. I believe I left it at the deepest part of the gorge, a cranny with steep rock walls. It's a place much frequented by cave-claws, and I'm afraid those things have a way of turning aggressive at times. Could you go and retrieve those gems for me?'
'Yes! Those are the gems! This is a great day for me, I must say! I had thought them lost and gone forever. Now you really deserve a reward, and my true thanks to boot!'
'Ah well, I suppose I'll never get those gems back. Lovely things they were, too. Pity.'
Bring the gemstone-hoard back to Bothwar
Collect the gemstone-hoard
Hidden Gems
The dwarf-miner Bothwar has confided to you the location of a hidden hoard of gems he once mined before the revival of Angmar.
'Ha! You have a nose for gems!'

The hidden hoard of gems is at the end of a gorge, in the southernmost part of Maethad, in a place frequented by cave-claws. Bothwar is at Gabilshathûr, far to the west of Maethad.
The dwarf-miner Bothwar has asked you to retrieve a hoard of gems for him.
You have found gem-bearing rocks
You did not find anything

'I can offer you some more work if you're interested. There are many possible gem-bearing lodes in Gorothlad that we have not yet found. If you like, you could take a pick-axe and go out to the area north and west of Maethad and see if you can find anything worthwhile.
'I'll give you a pick-axe suitable for taking samples out of the hard, gem-bearing rock. Any rocky outcropping in the whole area south of the Arena might be suitable, so it might take a while to find a good spot.
'I've noticed that the cave-claws seem to gather around gem-bearing rocks, if that's any help.'

'Good, good! This is an excellent sample. We may not be able to mine it properly now, but someday....
'Well, here is a reward for your hard work.'
'Prospecting is hard work and often unrewarding. But I'm sure there are gem-bearing rocks in that area someplace.'
Find gem-bearing rocks with your hardened pick-axe
Bring the gem-bearing rock and the pick-axe back to Bothwar
Prospector of Angmar
Bothwar the dwarf-miner is seeking news of any gem-bearing rock.
'Prospecting is hard work and often unrewarding. But I'm sure there are gem-bearing rocks in that area someplace.'

The whole area north and west of the Maethad is suitable for prospecting. Cave-claws tend to gather around gem-bearing rocks.
The dwarf-miner Bothwar has given you a pick-axe and sent you off looking for gem-bearing rock. He gave you little guidance, but told you that any rocky outcropping in the region north and west of Maethad might be suitable.

Bothwar is back at Gabilshathûr.
Having found some gem-bearing rock, you should bring your sample back to Bothwar.
Defeated Arngrim

'One of the miners here, Arngrim, has been acting strange lately. He has long claimed that there was mithril to be found in this land, but that is madness...any dwarf in his right mind knows that mithril may only be found in Khazad-dûm.
'Recently Arngrim told some of his fellows that he knew the location of a mithril vein and was heading out into Imlad Balchorth to mine a sample. This seemed very strange to me, for ever since these Orc-troubles, and since the rise of the evil to the north, I have kept our prospectors here out of harm's way. There is no way that Arngrim could have spent any time prospecting on his own, much less in a dangerous place such as Imlad Balchorth has become.
'At any odds, I ordered Arngrim to remain here, but it seems right before that last Orc-raid, he slipped away. Though he has brought it upon himself, I am concerned for his foolishness. Please speak to the other miners and see if they know where he has gone. It may be that you can fetch him back.'

'Arngrim? Ah, yes, the mad mithril-hunter! He said he could smell it out. Now all dwarves have a nose for a lode or a vein of rich ore, but no one can smell out ore a league away!
'Anyhow, he said there was a lode on a ridge somewhere in the south-east part of Imlad Balchorth -- that was where he was headed.
'He tried to get a couple of us to go out with him, but we said no.'

'This is terrible news you bring. But alas, I suppose it is our fault for staying on too long in this accursed land. At first we thought the evil would abate of its own accord.
'Fools we were! And now it is too late for us to flee to the south. Arngrim would never have been driven mad -- never have fallen -- if we had just left when we should have.
'Ah, but you have done all that we ever could ask of you. None of this is your fault. I should thank you for your bravery.'
'You! You're here to steal it, aren't you! My mithril! My beautiful lovely mithril! The voice has told me so. The true sweet voice of the mithril! Nay, get back I say! Don't make me! Don't make me!'
Speak to the miners of Gabilshathûr about Arngrim
Find Arngrim
The Scent of Mithril
The dwarf Arngrim has vanished, after telling some of the other miners that he was sure he knew the location of a mithril vein in the hills of Imlad Balchorth.
'He's a strange one, all right. Kept to himself, always talking about mithril. But I'm afraid I don't know where he might be.'

'I don't want to get Arngrim in trouble...what? You say he's missing? He must actually have gone haring off after his imaginary mithril.
'Blasted fool! I wish I could tell you where he's gone, but I don't know.'

'I'd stay away from that one. He'll talk your ears off for hours about his mad, imaginary mithril! What? He's missing? Oh! I didn't even realize he was gone.
'Maybe someone else around here would know where he went, but I've been avoiding him lately...didn't want to waste an entire shift listening to him go on and on.'
'The miners may be a bit uncomfortable about telling me, their chief, what their fellow has done. I hope they will talk easier to you.'
'Oh! You've found where Arngrim went! But that's a foul dangerous place...I wonder if you can try to track him down?'

Bothwar, the chief miner of Gabilshathûr, has asked you to speak to other miners there to discover the whereabouts of Arngrim, a miner who claimed he was going to find mithril in the hills of Imlad Balchorth.

Arngrim may have headed out to a ridge in south-east Imlad Balchorth to look for mithril.
The miners of Gabilshathûr have been avoiding Arngrim for the most part, but at least one has heard that Arngrim thought there was mithril on a particular hill in the evil land of Imlad Balchorth.

Bothwar is back at Gabilshathûr.
Arngrim is dead, and the fell spirit who drove him to madness has been banished. You should return to Gabilshathûr and tell the sad story to Bothwar.
Collected First Marshals' marks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your weak frame and tender flesh will bruise too easily if you attempt this, sluggard! But if you desire great favour and glory in the name of the Great Eye, then perhaps you will throw your life away on this endeavour.
'Within the towers and keeps of these lands, our enemy takes root from time to time. When they do, First Marshals of their army stalk the halls as attendants and support for their masters.
'Storm their holdings and collect their marks. Bring them to me, and I will be well-favoured indeed. Accept this task and fail, and I will feed your gizzard to the trolls!'

'Scraps! You bring me scraps! What am I to do with these, you pathetic excuse for a ${RACE}. I should gut you where you stand and use your entrails to season the gruel.
'Such failures cannot be tolerated...but they must, only because you are the troops we have for our menial tasks. Begone from my sight.
Chieftain Durulkum mutters. 'Yes, these suit my purpose well.'

'Standing around, are you? What value you add to this army, ${RACE}. I can see you at the head of our army, strapped to the front of battering-ram, repeatedly slammed into the enemy's fortress!
'Get me what I need! Only towers and keeps controlled by the enemy will house the First Marshals, you worthless scum!'
Return to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect First Marshals' marks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
First Marshals' Marks

First Marshals stand only behind the Captain-General in rank amongst the enemy army. Chieftain Durulkum wants their marks of rank to further the favour this war-host gains with Angmar, Mordirith, and Lugbúrz.

First Marshals can only be found in towers and keeps claimed by the enemy.
Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag informed you that the marks borne by the First Marshals of the enemy army gain great favour with Mordirith in Angmar.
Collected footmen's badges (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen well, ${RACE}. I'm not here to wipe your nose and look after you. I'm here to see that the war-host out of Angmar clears the way of the enemy. To do that, I need to prove that we're doing well against these curs.
'I need your help for that. These duties are beneath an Orc of the Krahjarn, and I'll not dirty my hands with such worthless creatures. You, on the other hand, seek the approval which I've already earned.
'So here's what we're going to do. You'll kill the footmen you find out there and bring me their badges.'
'These badges are barely worth my time, worm, but they'll have to do. Now, get out of here before I gut you!'
'What are you doing standing around here, slug? Get ou there and get those badges!'
Return to Dâr-gazag and speak with Chieftain Durulkum
Collect footmen's badges (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Footmen's Badges

Footmen, wardens, and scouts patrolling the wild of the Ettenmoors adorn their uniforms with badges denoting their rank. You have been tasked with recovering these badges and delivering them to Chieftain Durulkum at Gramsfoot.

Seek footmen, wardens, or scouts throughout the Ettenmoors and slay them.
Chieftain Durulkum directed you to seek out the weakest of the enemy soldiers and claim their badges as proof of your duty.
Collected Lieutenants' seals (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Across this fetid land you will find many who are clinging to the hope that they can defeat this war-host. I know as well as you their hope is ill-placed. We grow stronger with every passing hour, and there is no stopping the forces Mordirith sends forth from his palace in Carn Dûm.
'Keep your head about you when you face these foes, you pile of dung. I'll not tolerate failing easily. Your failure will cast me in an ill shadow, and I will see your failure purged before my name is tarnished.
'Collect the seals carried by the lieutenants in their army and return them to me. Much favour is earned by their acquisiton.'

'This pleases me. Not enough to pay you a compliment, though, vermin. Yet, I am obligated to reward your efforts with something. This pittance will suffice.
'Whine or prattle on about how little I give, and I will drive my sword through your gullet!
'I serve Mordirith, Angmar, and Lugbúrz without question, so you should follow me as well.'
'Snivelling wretch! Why do you still stand here. Seek the lieutenants in the enemy holdings or areas they control. I will not tolerate failure. Go!'
Return to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect Lieutenants' seals (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Lieutenants' Seals

Lieutenants watch over the sergeants and lesser guards of the enemy as they drive their war-efforts deeper into the Ettenmoors. Plucking the seals worn by each of these warriors will earn you greater favour with your leaders.

Positions held by the enemy are often watched over by the lieutenants in their army. You may even find a lieutenant flanked by sergeants in the wild-lands.
Chieftain Durulkum commanded that you retrieve the seals worn by the lieutenants in the enemy army and return them to him at Dâr-gazag.
Collected Captain-Generals' symbol: (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Weakling! I charge you with a task that will see your body bloodied, broken, and left for the crebain. You will do this task because I say you will do this task.
'Fail me and live, and I will cover your flesh in the sweet drippings from the roasting rat-folk and drop you near the trolls. Your end will be painful and merciless, and I shall revel in it. Do well, and I will forgo the threat and let you live out your miserable life.
'Captain-Generals are present wherever the enemy controls. Slaughter them, skin them if you like, snap their bones and consume them...I don't care. Save the symbols they wear and return them to me!'

'A pitiful display of battle! Took you longer than a slug to crawl out of the dead târk's belly.
'Still, you've done what I asked...poorly, but you still deserve something for your efforts, worm!'
'You pathetic worm! Captain-General symbols will only be found on the leaders of the locations the enemy has taken! Get out there and do your part for this war!'
Return to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect Captain-Generals' symbols: (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Captain-Generals' Symbols
At the head of the enemy forces stand the Captain-Generals. Their symbols garner great favour amongst Angmar's army, and presenting these to Mordirith will undoubtedly earn you favour with Lugbúrz.

Captain-Generals can only be found at locations where the enemy army holds power.
Chieftain Durulkum directed you to collect Captain-General symbols from enemy leaders and then return to him.
Collected sergeants' patches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Maggot! You try my patience by the very sight of you. Skulking about with a sluggard's look about you. You make me sick and long for the vile bile spewed from Carn Dûm's underbelly.
'I'd sooner speak with the Pale Folk than you, if I had the choice. As I cannot choose where I am forced into duty, I shall take pleasure in causing you limitless pain.
'Our enemy calls feeble creatures leaders. Simple things who command small units. Sergeants, they call them. Our war-host will thrive only when we show our strength, and what better way than by defeating the lowliest of their leaders. Find them and take their badges off their warm corpses. You will do this for me, or I will see that you are fed the leavings in the bile from the north.'

'Feeble, yes? Such creatures cannot hope to match the might of Angmar's Army. Mordirith will be pleased with my progress!
'You did well for me, filth. I will see that you are given favour.'
'You do not want to make a mockery of me ${RACE}. I will see that you are relegated to scrubbing the stones of Carn Dûm clean for the rest of your days, if you fail me!'
Return the patches to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag
Collect sergeants' patches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Sergeant-at-Arms' Patches
Sergeants command smaller units of the enemy army. These feeble creatures believe that they can stand up to the might of Angmar's army, but they shall soon learn that they face a relentless foe.

Sergeant-at-Arms lead small numbers of Men, Elves and Dwarfs throughout the Ettenmoors.
Chieftain Durulkum directed you to obtain sergeants' patches before returning to him at Dâr-gazag.
Pathetic beast! Defeat earns failure!

'Another stripling barely ready to face their shadow! Well, maggot, you'll learn quick or die. Out there, in the wild of the Ettenmoors, we've got foes that'll fight harder than a few scattered farmers like in the North Downs.
'Pitiful little ${RACE}! You'll be dead within a week, I think, and set into the evening gruel. Nevertheless, I've orders from War-tyrant Akúlhun that I'll not disobey, and you'd be wise not disobey mine. We Krahjarn are Mordirith's favoured, which means we've got the favour of the Eye as well, and that power is undeniable! So listen well, slime!
'South of here, along the ridge at the foot of these mountains, you will find Dâr-gazag. Seek out Chieftain Durulkum and tell him you are the newest recruit!'

'You've the look of a coward, ${PLAYER}. You'd best prove me wrong. This is Dâr-gazag. Our central keep. The enemy lay across the field of battle far to the east at Ost Ringdyr. We control this keep -- they control theirs.
'We've a number of things that need doing here to keep the war-machine turning, and you're the maggots that'll be doing what we need. Speak to Soldiers, Taskmasters, Chieftains, and Tyrants to learn what they need doing.
'Fail us, and your corpse will litter the battlefield or feed the forces. Succeed, and you might find yourself favoured by Mordirith, Angmar, and Lugbúrz!'
Defeat is not an option!
Report to Dâr-gazag, Maggot

Driven by a harsh Krahjarn Taskmaster you find yourself within the Gramsfoot stronghold in the shadow of Mount Gram on the border of the Ettenmoors. Here to support your Ongbúrz brothers under the watchful eye of the Krahjarn, you are ushered south into the Steps of Gram in search of Chieftain Durulkum.
'Maggot! I've a mind to rend your flesh open and tear out your innards! Move now! I ordered you to Dâr-gazag and Chieftain Durulkum!'

Seek out Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag, along the ridge south of Gramsfoot.
Uglash ordered you to find your way to Chieftain Durulkum at Dâr-gazag.

'You little maggots make me want to vomit! Worthless sores on the hide of Mordirith's great army. Never killed before, never seen steel in the hands of a filthy târk, or Elf, or worse...a Dwarf. You're nothing more than a heap of dung piled as high as you stand, and none will show you respect until you done proved yourself worthy.
'I don't see that happening, you worthless, good for nothing ${RACE}! You look like a slimy scum that crawled out from the deepest cave near the sludge spilling from the gutters in Carn Dûm! I've got to find something simple for a piss-ant like you to kill with ease...and I know just the things! We found them only recent-like, and they're a tasty bunch of rats. Not much fight in them, being as small as they are...might be a tough wrangle for you though.
'Rat-folk with big bellies meant for stabbing, live near the water in the wood south of here. Kill their farmers and gardeners, and if you don't fall on your face and break my cold black heart, return to me! Get a move on, you dung-hill rat!'

'Killed them did you? A fine start, ${RACE}. You may find yourself on the front lines someday, doing your service to the Iron Crown by being a body on the heap!
'Keep working like this, and we might find a way to promote you to the top of the filth-pile one day!'
Tasty Little Farmers and Gardeners

Upon arriving in the Ettenmoors, scouts were sent to the far corners in search of allies and enemies within the land. In the south, just across the Hoardale river, a secluded village of plump rat-folk was found, and the inhabitants there were found to be resistant to the forces of Angmar. It was also discovered that the folk were quite tasty.
'Get out there and kill them rat-folk, you worthless gob of flesh! Hoarhallow is found south of here and across the Hoardale river.'

Rat-folk with fat round bellies are rumoured to live in a village far south beyond the Steps of Gram.
Taskmaster Fikdag wants you to make your way into the southern area of the Ettenmoors in search of rat-folk.

Taskmaster Fikdag is at Dar-gazag.
You slew the rat-folk with ease and now should return to Taskmaster Fikdag.

'When we discovered the rat-folk village in the south, our scouts engaged them to force them into the service of Angmar. Their leader rallied them together and organized their number into a fighting force that bested all but one of our scouts.
'I tell you this so you understand the disgrace that awaits failure in this task, ${PLAYER}. Seek out the leader of these rat-folk and carve his heart out of his chest!'

'You think this was a victory? My scouts tell me that Wat Mudbottom still lives.
'You beat him, yes! But he is not dead. There is no end to the incompetence found in the lesser tribes!
'A victory indeed, but a hollow one!'
Leader of the Rat-folk

When the Rat-folk in the south were discovered, they scored a blow against the scouts who found them, slaughtering all but one. The leader of the rat-folk village was responsible for the attack, and Taskmaster Fikdag thinks that you can assist with exacting vengeance.
'Bring no more disgrace to this war-host, ${PLAYER}. We fight for the glory of Angmar and the favour of Lugbúrz! Find and kill the rat-folk's leader!'

Make your way south along the Hoardale river to the village of Hoarhallow.
Taskmaster Fikdag directed you to find and kill Mayor Wat Mudbottom, the leader of the rat-folk village.

Taskmaster Fikdag is at Dâr-gazag.
You stalked through the trails to the centre of Hoarhallow and struck down their leader. You should return to Taskmaster Fikdag with the news.
Collect hobbit-legs: (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'One thing that the rat-folk have proven to be, ${PLAYER}, is a tasty source of food. Their flesh is sweet and soft, tasting better than the flesh of any Man I have ever eaten.
'I will tell you this, while you stalk through their trails and amongst their homes, be wary not to destroy the meat on their legs. If you return them to me, I will be sure to give you a worthy reward.'

'Ahh, a tasty treat to fill my belly. Their flesh is supple and slides from the bone with ease when boiled in a stew.
'Keep up your efforts here in the Ettenmoors, and one day I might share some of the stew with you, ${PLAYER}.'
'Try my patience if you must maggot, but my appetite will be sated. I would prefer the tender and tasty flesh of the rat-folk, but I will settle on yours, if you continue to taunt me!'
Return to Dâr-gazag and speak with Taskmaster Fikdag
Collect hobbit-legs: (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tasty Little Legs

Though the Rat-folk have proven a thorn in the side of Angmar's Army, they have also proven a viable source of food. Not only do the rat-folk have seemingly endless food-stores, but their flesh is sweeter than Man's.

Hoarhallow lay to the south on the eastern side of the Hoardale river.
Taskmaster Fikdag at Dâr-gazag has grown fond of the flesh found on the bones of the rat-folk, and he has asked you to collect some of their legs.
Collected brittleleaf-seeds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ar, ${RACE}. You can find a way to carry something back to me, I'm certain. It's a little task, hardly worth mention, I will admit, but then again so is feeding a bunch of thankless maggots like you!
'The rat-folk in the south grow a strange leaf. The leaf tastes terrible and more often than not the rat-folk burn it after drying it out, strange little blighters. But the seeds can be ground up and used as a fairly tasty addition to gruel.
'If you can gather up a bundle of the seeds, I would be very grateful.'
'These will do nicely and make the gruel taste more bland and less terrible!'
'The seeds can be found on the rat-folk, though more frequently in their fields or even in the areas of the woods nearby.'
Return to Taskmaster Gukthor at Dâr-gazag
Collect brittleleaf-seeds (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
A Dash of This and That

Taskmaster Gukthor admits hating the taste of gruel, but has found that the seeds the rat-folk use to grow their leaf adds a nice bite to the mash he uses in his gruel. He has asked that you collect ten seeds for the evening meal.

The rat-folk living south of Dâr-gazag along the river grow a plant that can be crushed to make a tasty spice.
Taskmaster Gukthor waits for you to return with the brittle-leaf seeds.
Collected slug-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If you are looking for something more violent than scouting, who isn't, ${RACE}? You could help Taskmaster Gukthor out of Dâr-gazag.
'He cooks the meals for the forces there and needs help with gathering supplies. He told me to set new recruits out hunting for slug meat.
'You heard me right, maggot. You'll be hunting slugs for their meat. When you've got a large bundle make your way to Dâr-gazag far to the south in the Steps of Gram and give him the meat you got to Taskmaster Gukthor, or come back here and I'll see they gets where they needs to be.'

'Dallying about, shifting your weight to and fro, is not helping the army in any way. Want to make yourself useful then, do you?
'Right then. All over the Steps of Gram are these giant slugs...we seen 'em before in the slave pits of Carn Dûm. They're tough things with a grand bit of meat on 'em.
'You want to eat, and I want to cook! So we got a bit of a good thing happening here. Go out there and kill the slugs and bring me their meat.'

'You bring the guts back to me, do you? This is just like the lazy sluggard everyone thinks you to be.
'I tell you that they need this at Dâr-gazag and you bring it back here! Fine then, I said you could so you does.
'Here, take this...it's all you are getting from me, whelp!'
'These'll do nicely. Firm and fresh. Time'll come soon enough to mash the meat up and make it into something edible.'
'Go out there are get some tasty, chewy slug-meat so I can make us some gruel!'
Return to Taskmaster Gukthor at Dâr-gazag
Collect slug-meat (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Gruel comes from somewhere, and with an army as large as the forces Angmar have sent to the Ettenmoors, gruel is needed in great abundance. You have been charged with collecting the main ingredient in the mush Taskmaster Gukthor makes.

Giant slugs make the Steps of Gram their home.
Taskmaster Gukthor awaits your return with the slug-meat he demanded.
Collected food-sacks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen well, maggot! I'm charged with feeding our forces, and though I'd have no problems throwing good for nothing sluggards like you on a spit to serve for dinner, the war-masters have other plans.
'So I give you a task that you'll complete, or I'll go about changing the minds of those who can cover up their trails better than I, and you will be dinner.
'The rat-folk in the south grow food, and we steal it to keep our army full and happy. Now listen well! Men, Elves, dwarves, and even the rat-folk that stalk through the Ettenmoors can be carrying the foodstuffs we need. If you find any bring it to me...or they'll be no dinner!'

'It's not meat, but it tastes better than the mash we mince from slug-meat.
'We'll eat well tonight!'
'Get out there and get us some food!'
Return to Taskmaster Gukthor at Dâr-gazag
Collect food-sacks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Not Just for Eating

Rat-folk living on the banks of the Hoardale, south of Dâr-gazag, are not only a succulent meal, but they are a source of replenishible food. The rat-folk are farmers, supplying the enemy forces with foodstuffs. Foodstuffs can be stolen and eaten by your army as well.

Rations are portioned to enemy forces and found in locations where they hold power.
Taskmaster Gukthor charged you collecting food for Angmar's Army.
Collected dwarf-beards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Long have we fought in the mountain-hearts, through caverns and ice floes, over the halls of dead dwarves across our bridges and theirs. It is a battle that scars my folk, stays with us always. We hate the dwarves!
'Slaughter them all, we say. Take their beards and destroy them. They take pride in beards, or so it says. So we strip them of their pride, make them suffer as they make the goblins suffer.
'Bring us their beards, and we speak well of you. Bring the beards of the dwarves to me.'

'Look at these, so thick and full! We burn them on the fires and praise the Great Eye! We cull the Dwarfs! We meet them in battle and face them with our brothers from Angmar!
'Dead dwarves! Dead dwarves! We cheer your name by the light of fire, ${PLAYER}! We cheer and praise you to the Eye!'
'Take the dwarf-beards. Bring them here.'
Return the beards to Fim the Worm at Dâr-gazag
Collect dwarf-beards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

The Snowreap long struggled against the remnant of the dwarves in the Misty Mountains. Even now, they dislike the thought of dwarves being so close to their home. As allies to Angmar's Army they are permitted to speak on the behalf of any who aid them.

Dwarves encroaching throughout the Ettenmoors wear full beards on their faces.
The goblins believe that the beards are a matter of pride amongst the dwarves and want you to help them humiliate their hated foes. Fim the Worm bade you strip the beards of the dwarves in return for favour from the Snowreap.
Discovered the Grimwood Lumber-yard
Worhtless maggot! Defeat earns you failure!

'Maggot! You need to learn your way about these lands, and I am tasked with seeing that you do.
'South and east, across the Hoardale River you will find a swath of land called Hithlad. A forest, ripe for harvesting, covers the land there. It is called the Grimwood. We found rat-folk working there and drove them out, only to have the enemy come to their defence.
'You must scout through the wood and find the camp so you know where the battles will be fought in that wood. Return to me, only when you discover this location!'
'Favour earned! Not for you, of course...you've simply been prepared for your future sacrifice for the glory of Angmar, Mordirith, and Lugbúrz!'
Scout the Grimwood Lumber-yard
Return to Uglash at Gramsfoot
Defeat is not an option!
Into the Grimwood
Uglash sent you to Hithlad, east of the southern stretch of the Hoardale River to find the Grimwood Lumber-yard.

'My ire rises each time I see your face, worm. Let us be certain of one thing: you do as I say, and you live. Press me, and I will slaughter you. Find the Grimwood and return to me only after you know the location of the camp.'

The Grimwood Lumber-yard is found in the heart of the Grimwood within Hithlad, south and east across the Hoardale River.
Uglash ordered you to learn the location of the Grimwood Lumber-yard.

Uglash awaits your return at the Krahjarn-encampment at Gramsfoot.
You scouted through the Grimwood and discovered the Grimwood Lumber-yard. Now you should return to Uglash.
Worthless Cur! Your reward is failure!

'A great goblin-king once lived within Mount Gram, ${RACE}. Now his kin are worthless wretches, easily beaten into submission and only worthy of labour. We've agreed to assist the miserable curs in their village to the east of here.
'Travel to Arador's End and seek out the village of Grothum. You will find Bok and tell him you are there to assist.'

'Help comes, yes! You here to help, Snowreap! Snowreap helps Angmar! Snowreap helps Mordirith! Snowreap help Lugbúrz!
'You come here, we give thanks!'
Defeat is not an option!
Get to Grothum, Maggot

Grothum is the village in the north-eastern stretch of the Ettenmoors known as Arador's End. It is here that the Snowreap-goblins, who dwell in old dwarf-ruins throughout the Misty Mountains have congregated to assist the war-host with the Isendeep Mine!
'I'll not tolerate this, ${RACE}. Get your carcass to Grothum, or I'll see it in this night's gruel!'

Bok is at the goblin-village of Grothum located in the north-east stretches of the Ettenmoors.
Uglash directed you to make yourself available to the Goblins of Grothum.
Simpering wad! You have failed!

'Listen well, slug. Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag tower in the Steps of Gram has work to be done.
'If we've lost control of the tower -- which you'd best hope we haven't, worm -- you'll need to wait for him to return to his post. He's far too valuable a soldier to risk in recovering the point!
'Lugazag is south and east of Gramsfoot in the greener section of the Steps of Gram. Hurry along, pissant!'

'Another recruit! Listen well. These lands teem with the enemy of the Great Eye. We must slaughter them all and clear the way for Mordirith! To arms!
'My task might seem worthless, but so too will the tasks given by Taskmaster Fash outside these walls. But they will earn you favour with Mordirith, Angmar, and Lugbúrz!'
Speak with Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag
Defeat is not an option!
Report to Lugazag
You have been ordered to make your presence known to Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag.
'Still here? Do you need me to thrust a sword into your ears! I wonder if you even have them! Go, maggot! Go to Lugazag!'

If the tower has not been taken by the enemy, you should find Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag, south and east of Gramsfoot, in the greener sections of the Steps of Gram.
Uglash directed you to speak with Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag.
Tirith Rhaw scouted
You worthless cur! Defeat only earns you failure!

'Far to the east is a tower which often belongs to the enemy. We assail it now and again, but far too often we are driven out.
'In time, we'll build a wall of bodies of recruits like yourself that we can use to shield the true forces of Angmar as we storm into the enemy's base and crush them!
'For now, I must send you on a fool's errand to learn the location of the tower. Travel east, across the Hoardale River and into the Coldfells, find Tirith Rhaw and scout the area. Then return to me!'
'Survived the journey? Good for you, maggot. Before you get excited, you should learn your place...firmly beneath my heel, worm!'
Scout out Tirith Rhaw
Return to Uglash at Gramsfoot
Defeat is not an option!
To Tirith Rhaw
Your education continues with a trip far to the west to Tirith Rhaw, a tower in lands controlled by the enemy.
'Listen well to me, maggot. Standing here talking to me only draws my ire. Make your way east, across the Hoardale, and find Tirith Rhaw. Then, and only then, do I want to see your face!'

Tirith Rhaw lay far to the east beyond the Hoardale River.
Uglash directed you to scout out Tirith Rhaw in the Coldfells.

Uglash awaits your return at Gramsfoot.
You discovered and scouted the area surrounding Tirith Rhaw.
Tol Ascarnen scouted
You worthless wretch! Your defeat earns only failure!

'You're an ambitious one, ${RACE}. Very well then, I've a simple enough task for you. Simple indeed.
'Make your way east towards the Hoardale River. Find the island in the centre...just scout it out and have a look through Tol Ascarnen! If you survive, come back to me.'
'I had expected you sooner, maggot. You found it, though, and this means you survived! You might not be as worthless as I assumed!'
Scout out Tol Ascarnen
Return to Uglash at Gramsfoot
Defeat is not an option!
To Tol Ascarnen
You have been ushered out on a simple scouting mission to find the central keep called Tol Ascarnen.
'Still here. Perhaps I was right, and you are a coward. Tol Ascarnen, worm. Go there now, or I will bury my blade in your belly and spill your innards on this ground!'

Tol Ascarnen is on an island in the Hoardale River, east of Gramsfoot.
You were ordered to find and scout out Tol Ascarnen.

Uglash awaits your return at Gramsfoot.
You discovered and scouted the area around Tol Ascarnen.

'You! You here to help, yes? Of course, of course! Angmar and the Snowreap serve the same lord, the Great Eye. You help us, good.
'The mines, digging claws, nasty beaks, terrible flesh. They bite us, break us, sometimes kill! The terrible stone-eaters. The crawling death.
'You go now, kill the creeping claw-skittering cave-dwellers, yes?'

'Good, good! No more crawling claws in the cave. We work now, help the army!
'Glory to Angmar! Glory to the Eye! Glory to the Snowreap!'
Speak with Bok in Grothum
Menace in the Mines

Cave-claw dig through the stone and threaten the goblins working the Isendeep near Grothum. The leaders of the village implored you as an ally to the Snowreap to assist them in destroying the terrible little creatures.
'You help now, yes! The mines, go to the mines!'

Cave-claws can be found in the Isendeep mine.
Bok begged you to help defend the goblins in the mines.

Bok awaits your return at Grothum.
You slaughtered the cave-claws you encountered to defend the pathetic goblins. You should return to Bok with the news.
Collected hobbit-feet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Caught me one of the rat-folk, I did. Tasty little morsel, sweet toes melting in the mouth. Can't have him! He's mine...ours, the Snowreaps! I'll call the trolls if you try to take him! But I tell Angmar's army how nice you be to Snowreap if you help me.
'Rat-folk has such tasty little toes, but this one makes such tasty little dishes with his little hands that we keeps him around to make our gruel better. The trolls like his food and eats less goblins, so we keeps him hidden. But I like their toes, the rat-folk toes.
'Get me their feets, get me the rat-folk feets, and I tells others how good you are to Snowreap!'

'You brought me feet! I tell everyone you help the Snowreap, everyone I sees will know you helped us, filled my belly.
'Such a treat, a treat to eat the tasty rat-folk feet!'
'I wants to lick the toes, lick the toes off the bones!'
Return the hobbit-feet to Bok in Grothum
Collect hobbit-feet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tasty Little Toes

Bok captured himself one of the rat-folk one day, and he has proven a great asset. His toes tasted good when the goblin ate one, but the little man is a better cook than anything, and so they keep him alive to cook their meals. But this does not deter Bok from wanting to eat more rat-folk toes.

Hoarhallow is far to the south-west on the eastern bank of the Hoardale River.
Bok waits for you to return to him with the hobbit-feet you were sent to harvest.
Defeated guards at Tirith Rhaw (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Maggot! You've been conscripted, like it or not, to assail our enemy at the walls of their tower in the east.
'Travel across the Ettenmoors, always east, beyond the Hoardale River and Tol Ascarnen, to the shadow of Ost Ringdyr where you will see the tower Tirith Rhaw rising upon a great hill.
'Kill the guards about this tower to weaken our enemy, and you shall see respect. Fail, and you will face your doom.'

'A victory today, maggot! A victory!
'We shall drive these fools from the Ettenmoors yet, then bring the full might of Angmar into this land and drive forwards to meet the armies of Mordor in the south!'
Defeat guards at Tirith Rhaw (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Speak with Soldier Gazlup at Lugazag
Guards of Tirith Rhaw
Tirith Rhaw stands in the east, near the camp of the Free Peoples at Ost Ringdyr. The tower is under the control of the Free Peoples, and you are tasked with killing the guards in the area.
'Go to Tirith Rhaw, maggot! Kill the guards and give our army the chance that it needs to slaughter these fools!'

Tirith Rhaw is a tower in the eastern area of the Ettenmoors. It lay between the central keep of Tol Ascarnen and Ost Ringdyr.
Soldier Gazlup ordered you to slaughter the guards keeping watch over Tirith Rhaw.

Soldier Gazlup is at Lugazag.
You were tasked to kill the guards at Tirith Rhaw by Soldier Gazlup of Lugazag. You should return to Gazlup with news of your victory.
Collected fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected slabs of Troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Battles ebb and flow, ${RACE}. We fight war as we can and with the weapons at our command. One such weapon are the trolls. As strong as they are stupid, massive as they are clumsy, and killing machines unmatched! With their benefits come drawbacks.
'The largest is their penchant for smashing walls apart. Holes in the wall mean that an enemy can easily breach our forces, so we must repair those holes. But the trolls pound the stone to dust and we haven't the numbers to dig a quarry here in the Ettenmoors, so we use the trolls.
'How, you wonder? Ever seen them in the sun? Solid as the rock from whence they were first drawn. The Coldeve-trolls wandering throughout the Ettenmoors often get caught in the sun and die. Chip away their stone and return it to me for repairs.'

'What's this? Ah, troll-stone, just as I asked. This will prove well for you, worm.
'Your efforts will continue to draw attention, and you will continue to earn the favour of the Krahjarn!'
'You're pushing me to wits' end, wretch. I'll not tolerate failure with a simple wave of my hand. Fail me and I'll slice your gullet wide and spill your innards on the ground. Now, get to work!'
Return to Gazlup at Lugazag
Collect fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect slabs of Troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Set in Stone

Enemies assail the walls of Lugazag often. Trolls are clumsy and strong and often throw enemy soldiers through walls, shattering the stone therein and making holes in the stonework that must be repaired. Fortunately, trolls are also dumb and turn to stone in the sunlight.

Soldier Gazlup is at Lugazag.
Soldier Gazlup directed you to collect troll-stone to repair the damage the trolls delivered to the walls of Lugazag.
Collected Morningthaw-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You trespass where you are not welcome, ${PLAYER}. I shall allow this, for I know you mean to cull the enemy from our home, and I shall even pledge my bite to your effort for recompense.
'Long has my pack struggled to oust the Morningthaw-bears beyond the borders of the Misty Mountains. Long have we battled them and sometimes won. With the arrival of the Elves, the bears drove us back and flocked to their side. My pack came to your leaders and chose to work with them in service to Lugbúrz. I will order my pack to slaughter in Angmar's name, and now, I ask that you slaughter to sate my hunger.
'I want meat. Meat from the Morningthaw. Deliver me enough to sate the hunger of all my years, and I will drive the enemy from that tower by your side.'

'My hunger dies a little with every swallow, so sweet is the taste of revenge. They shall pay more than they know for their intrusion into these lands.
'Come ${PLAYER}! Let us tear the throats from the enemy and slake our thirst now with their blood!'
'I shall not join you in assailing this fortress until I am appeased. Bring me those hides and I will lead you against the foes within Lugazag.'
Return the meat to Mazauk
Collect Morningthaw-haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Maw of Mazauk
Mazauk, a grizzled Warg of unknown years, pledges to join the battle against the enemy should you provide his den with the meat of his hated enemy, the Morningthaw-bears.

Morningthaw-bears can be found throughout the Ettenmoors.
Mazauk directed you to get meat from the Morningthaw bears.
Captain-General Lainedhel defeated!

'Ost Ringdyr is a thorn, ${PLAYER}. A place we can penetrate and nearly destroy, but one we cannot hold for any true time. Like us, the enemy is entrenched deeply at their camp of Glân Vraig, and Ost Ringdyr is simply too close to hold the keep.
'We can however slaughter their numbers and kill the master of the keep. This is what I ask of you, ${RACE}: go to Ost Ringdyr and kill the lord who commands the enemy there. Do this and you will earn favour with Angmar and Lugbúrz.'

'A day of victory for Angmar and Lugbúrz! This victory shall echo through the moors and mountains.
'You have earned the favour of the Great Eye, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat Captain-General Lainedhel at Ost Ringdyr. You must not be defeated when the Captain-General falls.
Raid: Captain-General Lainedhel of Ost Ringdyr

Attempts to weaken the enemy forces are proving fruitful, and the keep east of Tirith Rhaw, where the Elf Captain-General Lainedhel rules, is the target of assault. You are charged with organizing a war-band to assault Ost Ringdyr in an effort to slaughter the lord of the keep.
'Do not test me, ${PLAYER}. Seek the Captain-General of Ost Ringdyr and do not return to me until they are dead!'

Ost Ringdyr is far to east beyond the Hoardale river and Tirith Rhaw.
Taskmaster Krul directed you to make your way to Ost Ringdyr to slaughter the lord of the keep.

Taskmaster Krul is at Gramsfoot.
After storming the walls of Ost Ringdyr, you fought through the enemy and defeated the leader of the keep. You should return to Taskmaster Krul with news of their defeat.
Poisoned the Hoardale!
The waterfall here looks ripe for the poison

'My time is better spent speaking to something with a spine. You'll likely wilt as a flower in the face of the dangers in this land, whelp! Still...you stand before me. Perhaps I should order you to cower and wait to be given a task.
'Very well. I shall quicken your death or return you to the slave pits in Carn Dûm, ${RACE}. Take this barrel. It is filled with poison from the spider-keepers of Angmar. Mordirith is specific in his orders. All that stand against this army must perish.
'We will poison the Hoardale river and slaughter all who are made weak by the poison. Take the barrel to the waterfall that overlooks Tol Ascarnen at the centre of the Ettenmoors and dump the poison into the river. Fail me, and I will flay your flesh open to let the rats consume your innards...but I will see that you live to feel the pain. Succeed...I will see you are not made to labour in the slave pits of Carn Dûm a while longer.'

'I am almost impressed with what you have done, ${RACE}. You might one day prove a fine conscript in this army. I shall take great satisfaction when I grind my boots on your corpse as we scale the walls of the târk cities!'
Poison the Hoardale River
Return to War-tyrant Akúlhun at Gramsfoot
Poisoning the Hoardale

War-tyrant Akúlhun provided you with a barrel of poison and a directive. Make your way to the waterfall overlooking the fortress Tol Ascarnen and empty the barrel into the water. With enough poison, you may force the enemy to leave the wood.

The source of the Hoardale is at the waterfall overlooking Tol Ascarnen.
War-tyrant Akúlhun sent you to poison the enemy's water source.

War-tyrant Akúlhun awaits your return at Gramsfoot.
You climbed to the top of the falls and poisoned the waters of the Hoardale. You should return to War-tyrant Akúlhun with the news.
Angmar claims Lugazag!

'${RACE}! Your brethren failed us. Lugazag, our tower here in the west, has fallen to the hands of a târk! We must make our way to the tower and slaughter the forces standing watch.
'Do this, and I might think more of you than a maggot, ripe for smashing. Fail me, and I will see you posted to the slave pits of Carn Dûm!'
Defeat Captain-General Harvestgain and claim Lugazag. You must not be defeated when the Captain-General falls.
Raid: Captain-General Harvestgain
Captain-General Harvestgain is the leader of the Free Peoples at Lugazag.

'You best be back to tell me you've followed your orders, sluggard! Else I'll throttle you and put you on a cart bound for the muck beneath Mordirith's throne!
'Get out there and slaughter the Captain-General at Lugazag!'

Captain-General Harvestgain, a târk, leads the forces within Lugazag.
Soldier Súmtharb made it clear that the only objective is to strike down the enemy's leader.
Angmar claims Tirith Rhaw!

'You miserable cur! You lack ferocity or strength in your arms to face down a troll and ask me to find something for you to do? Best thing I can find for you involves mixing that pile of dung into that stew for the goblins!
'I've something you might yet prove yourself useful for. Far to the east, beyond the Hoardale river and Tol Ascarnen, there is a tower: Tirith Rhaw. We want to take the tower, but a force lead by the târk, Verdantine, stands in our way.
'If we gain that post, we'll give ourselves a position to launch more direct assaults on their camp and keep. Get some more of these worthless maggots about to help you take down the târk! Win this battle, and we'll feast on man-flesh in your honour! Fail...and we'll still feast on flesh and in your honour.'
Defeat Captain-General Verdantine and claim Tirith Rhaw. You must not be defeated when the Captain-General falls.
Captain-General Verdantine

Târks control the tower on the eastern front of the battlefield in the Ettenmoors. The tower, Tirith Rhaw, is held by the Captain-General Verdantine and must be crushed for Angmar's Army to drive the enemy to the precipice of destruction.
'You maggot! Get to the east and Tirith Rhaw. Slaughter that târk! For the glory of Mordirith, Angmar, and Lugbúrz!'

Captain-General Verdantine is at Tirith Rhaw, far to the east and south, beyond the Hoardale river.
Soldier Dahámab directed you to gather others and lay siege to the tower Tirith Rhaw in an effort to kill the leader of the forces there.
Angmar claims Tol Ascarnen!

'Stand fast, worm. There is a task that needs doing, and your blood will stain the ground as well as any others.
'Where the Hoardale splits the battlefield, there is a keep. It was there that the Witch-king of Angmar stopped to give strength to the betrayers before returning to the Great Eye's service in Mordor!
'The keep is now in control of the enemy, and a dwarf stands as the head of the forces watching over the keep! You are charged with the recovery of the keep and return of it to the rightful holders!'
Defeat Captain-General Mákan and claim Tol Ascarnen. You must not be defeated when the Captain-General falls.
Raid: Captain-General Mákan of Tol Ascarnen

The ancient keep Tol Ascarnen was once home to the Witch-king of Angmar as he returned to Mordor after facing the armies of Glorfindel in the north. The keep long lay in ruins, but still it holds majesty for the minions of Mordirith. You are tasked with assembling a force to liberate the holding from the dwarf who now calls the place home.

'Stop wasting time! Get your feeble innards out on the field of battle and earn your glory or die in the attempt!
'Go now, to Tol Ascarnen and face down the dwarf there!'

Tol Ascarnen sits on an island in the centre of the Hoardale River.
You have been tasked with finding and slaughtering the dwarf-leader who now stands in command of Tol Ascarnen.
Angmar claims the Isendeep mine!

'Look lively, you sack of filth! I've no time for chatter, only time for killing!
'The Snowreap-goblins in Arador's End sent scouts to us with news that the mine has fallen into the hands of a dwarf. We've got to go there and show this dwarf he's stepped into something far more terrible than a mine with a drake and cave-claw problem!
'Get in there and tear the dwarf's beard off his face before you gut him like a Nimwaith!'
Defeat Captain-General Meldún and claim the Isendeep Mine. You must not be defeated when the Captain-General falls.
Raid: Captain-General Meldún of Isendeep
A dwarf poses as the Lord of the Isendeep Mine in the north. This dwarf's beard is ripe for shaving and his flesh ready for the feasting tables at Gramsfoot.

'Get out there and slaughter that dwarf, you piss-ant! I'm not here to see you dally behind the safety of these walls! Mordirith demands that mine, and I will see it taken or flay your hide and hang it from the walls of this fort if I must!
'To Isendeep...slaughter the dwarf Captain-General.'

The Isendeep Mine is at Arador's End.
Soldier Dalgumthak directed you into the Isendeep Mine to kill the dwarf-lord in power there.
Angmar claims the Grimwood Lumber-yard!

'South across the river and east into the dark depths of the Grimwood, you will find a lumber-yard. We happened upon this yard a while ago, and it was devoid of any sign of enemy, but the small houses left behind were made by the rat-folk far to the south.
'The forest is ripe for harvesting and the lumber-yard still functions. We must take this location back from the enemy, lest they continue to make their bows and arrows to garner strength for their number.
'We will also strike a blow against their leadership as an Elf stands against us at the lumber-yard.'
Defeat Captain-General Bordagor and claim the Grimwood Lumber-yard. You must not be defeated when the Captain-General falls.
Raid: Captain-General Bordagor

The Grimwood forest covering most of Hithlad, is home to a lumber-yard established by a race of small, tasty folk. The rat-folk dwell far away from the lumber-yard, but the enemy is there now. What is worse, an Elf stands at the head of the enemy's army.
'Make your way into the centre of the Grimwood and slaughter the Elf who leads the enemy at the Grimwood lumber-yard.'

The Grimwood Lumber-yard is at the heart of the Grimwood Forest.
Soldier Bagfra directed you to find your way to the Grimwood Lumber-yard and destroy the Elf-lord in charge of the enemy forces there.

'We welcome the arrival of our tall friends to Hoarhallow. With them, we hope to end the plight which has faced our people for a great long time.
'In the north, beyond the place where the Hoardale rises sharply by the Tall Folk fortress and bends to the east, at the crest of the hill, thou will find Grothum where the goblins dwell. We wish to show them that we are not afraid of their ilk, and truly we are not. There are some of us willing to fight, but they have gone off to protect the wood and help the Tall Folk.
'If thou are willing to help us, make your way northeast and defeat the goblins.'

'Such heroism! We are indebted to thee, ${PLAYER}. We will not forget all that thou have done for us.
'Please take this, the Tall Folk at Glân Vraig said that a -- Quartermaster Ash -- there would assist all those that give us aide.'
Return to Ned Claybrick at Hoarhallow
Sundering the Snowreap

Goblins have been the main foe the Hobbits of Hoarhallow have contended with in all their years. They believe with the aid of the Tall Folk they can score a final victory against the Snowreap-goblins.
'You will find the golbins in their village, Grothum. It is far to the north and east in Arador's End.'

Snowreap-goblins inhabit Grothum, a village they established east of the Isendeep Mine in Arador's End.
Ned Claybrick asked you to assail the goblins in their home to deter them from future raids on Hoarhallow.

Ned Claybrick awaits your return at Hoarhallow, south and west of Grothum.
You found the Snowreap-goblins in Grothum and defeated them at their village. You should return to Ned Claybrick with the news.
Defeated Darktide-wolves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, good ${RACE}. It is so nice to see friendly faces about, and at such a difficult time, too. If thou have a moment, I could put on some tea and offer thee a nice hearth to warm thyself near, or I could make an offer to thee that we have been told thou might find interest in.
'Tall folk are helping us as these battles rage about us. Terrible things are happening all around our village. People go missing now and again. We know that the forces north of us are a great evil, but they stirred the Darktide-wolves of the Grimwood into a terrible state.
'If thou would...go into the wood, west and east of here, and kill some of the wolves. They are proving a danger to us all, and it is only a short matter of time before they attack our village.'

'Oh, it seems that the Big Folk are right! Thou are a true help to us here in Hoarhallow. They said that there would be people of all race to help us here, and I am pleased to see that they were right.
'It is hard to know who to trust these days. Here, they told us to give these out to those deserving of our thanks, and thou, ${PLAYER}, are certainly deserving.
'They mentioned a man too, Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig -- a silly name for a place if you ask me. I think it lies far to the east of here.'
Defeat Darktide-wolves (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Emerald Twospade at Hoarhallow
Wolves at Our Walls

Hoarhallow has always been in a difficult position. Being a village of hobbits in a place so filled with corruption and death is difficult, but these hobbits had lived in quiet obscurity until the Ongbûrz poured through the mountains north of their home. With the arrival of evil, came new threats as the foes surrounding the village suddenly became aware of their presence.

'Thou will find the Darktide-wolves all throughout the Grimwood, east of our village, and west in the hills and valleys of the Steps of Gram. They are not too good at hiding, and they smell dreadful.
'Find them and kill them so they may prove less a threat to people here.'

Wolves can be found east and west of Hoarhallow, scattered throughout Hithlad and into the hills of the Steps of Gram.
Emerald Twospade explained that the wolves of the Ettenmoors have long been the true threat against the Little Folk of Hoarhallow. She enlisted your aid in destroying the creatures and lessening their threat.

Emerald Twospade is in Hoarhallow.
You scoured through the Grimwood and slew a large number of the Darktide-wolves. You should return to Emerald Twospade with the news.
Collected Wintersebb-fangs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'One cannot muster pride in such a time, ${RACE}, and I know that I shall question why I ask this when this war is done, but times are hard, and we need supplies.
'To the north and east of here there are drakes that soar the skies, stalk the caverns of the Isendeep, and perch on the outcroppings of the Misty Mountains. Their teeth can be fashioned well and made into arrowheads. We're low on ore and most we collect is meant for the forge at Tol Ascarnen.
'I swallow my pride to ask you to collect fangs for me. Seek the drakes -- do not go alone -- and return to me with their teeth, so I may assist those here who man the walls.'

'I'll not forget this in all my days, ${PLAYER}. We shall have arrows to spare now that you have given us these. Now to the next task of polishing and sharpening these into arrow heads.
'If you find yourself back in Glân Vraig, present this to Quartermaster Ash. She will see that you are treated well for your efforts here.'
'You will find the drakes I speak of in Arador's End. The Hobbits of Hoarhallow called them Wintersebb because they fly from the part of the mountains where the winter withdraws first each year.'
Speak with Lieutenant Sturla at Lugazag
Collect Wintersebb-fangs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Fangs for Arrows
Removed so far from the fortresses of Ost Ringdyr and Glân Vraig, Lieutenant Sturla asks you to undertake a dangerous mission for a deadly weapon.

Drakes can be found in Arador's End to the north and east of Lugazag.
Lieutenant Sturla asked you to retrieve drake fangs to assist in the crafting of arrows for the war effort and reinforcement of Lugazag.
Collected untreated leather-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our foothold here is tenuous, ${PLAYER}. Driving the forces of Angmar from the tower was only the beginning but their seige will not relent. Many were injured and much of our arms and armour has been terribly damaged.
'I have been ordered to assist in the collection of much needed resources to aid in the rearming process.
'You should be able to find leather to service our needs from any of the more natural creatures strewn throughout the Ettenmoors. Collect them and return them to me, and I will see that you are rewarded for your efforts.'

'I care not to know where these were gathered. It is bad enough we cannot send for aid at Rivendell. War, ${PLAYER}, makes us all do things we shall regret. Be safe as you travel through this marred and dangerous land.
'You may visit Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig for further rewards. Thank you.'
'Seek hides from the wild beasts of the Ettenmoors. The battle here is harsh, we cannot be too particular in what we accept.'
Speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Ambeng at Lugazag
Collect untreated leather-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Patching the Holes
As the battle in the Ettenmoors rages, the Free Peoples struggle to keep up their armour and weaponry for the seige.

Wild beasts with strong hides roam the Ettenmoors. The leather made from their hides will be useful to the war effort.
Sergeant-at-Arms Ambeng asked you to seek out untreated leather from the wild beasts throughout the Ettenmoors.
Collected Sun-touched tailfeathers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Your presence in my wood disturbs me, but not so much as the bearers of light, ${RACE}.
'My brood grows weak and is culled further by the enemy, and I seek my revenge. My first thought must be for my children, and so I task you with this:
'Eagles from the north join with your enemy and their lords have long sought to end my reign. Bring me proof of their destruction by way of their feathers, and I shall lend you my strength against the enemy.'
'Yes. This will do. The talons of the enemy will no longer harm my children. Let us march forwards and give them a lesson they will not soon forget!'
'Pluck the eagles clean. Return their plumes and I shall come with you against the enemy.'
Return the feathers to Gorgoris
Collect Sun-touched tailfeathers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Gorgoris the Gorger
Gorgoris, the ancient brood-mother of the Grimfang, will assist you in claiming the Grimwood Lumber-yard, if you help her defend her brood.

Eagles can be found throughout the Ettenmoors.
Gorgoris wishes to know that the threat against her brood is dimished before she enters the fight against the enemy. She asked you to slay the eagles and bring her their feathers as proof of the deed.
Collected hobbit-feet (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected legs of Men (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected Elf-ears (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected dwarf-beard (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Let nothing ill be spoken of you this day, ${PLAYER}. I shall heed your call and storm the castle with you.

'We shall rise for the favour of Lugbúrz!
'We shall die to see that Mordirith's Army does not fail!

'Get me what I need you worthless wretch. I will not fight alongside sluggards and maggots.'

Storming the Castle
Tyrant Uzulthrang is here for battle and only battle. Stationed outside of Tol Ascarnen, the Tyrant pledges that he will fight against the enemy if you prove that you are worthy of his notice.
Tyrant Uzulthrang told you to assemble proof of your deeds, then and only then will he assist you in destroying the fools within Tol Ascarnen. He did not, however, tell you what proof he requires.

'Not that I've reason to explain myself, you worthless wretch, but I'm sending you into dangerous climes that I fear you will not return from, and I'd rather cover myself first.
'Within this wood are trees that walk. Terrible things that need death more than the little folk east of here...only the tree things aren't good eating. Now listen well, cur.
'I've need of the heartwood from these trees for the coven of witches in Angmar. I'll earn favour from them, and you in turn will earn favour from the Krahjarn. This makes things right all around, and if you do well enough, I will look to you in the future. What do you say?'

'The witches in the north will reward me well for these, and I will share in the strength that I gain, ${PLAYER}.
'I will speak your name to the Krahjarn leaders. They will know you well.'
'What are you waiting for, a spoon? Go carve out those trees' hearts!'

Carving OutHearts
The Angmarim within the city of Carn Dûm have a desire for the heartwood cut from the centre of the Leafcull-trees within the Grimwood. He has offered you a reward for collecting the heartwood.

'Maggot! Your role in this war is clear. You do as the Krahjarn say!
'In the wood are saplings. These saplings and some of the fallen timber might have long roots attached to them. We need roots from the Grimwood to tie the posts together.
'We need this place in perfect repair for when the enemy returns. If you prefer something more martial, you might find the wood crawling with creatures that have roots as well! Get out there!'
'These will do, but you took longer than I would have liked, worm! Make your way through these woods faster in the future, or I'll do some culling of my own.'
'Repairs need to be made, maggot! You'll aide us, or I will gut you. It is that simple. Get the lashings we need.'

'I look about me and know that this wood is corrupt and still the life that dwells here pains me. We are fighting a war and each day we gain or lose ground, and yet life still teems here! I have learned hatred, ${PLAYER}. I have learned to slaughter and destroy and in this wood, where corruption has so long held sway, I am not at peace.
'We need more weapons. We need more wood to fire the furnaces at Dol Dínen and within Carn Dûm. We need molten metal to forge our blades!
'Tear down this forest, scour the land in the north. Bring me fire, bring me molten metal to make the weapons this war so desperately needs!'

'Fuel for the fires and metal for the blades. This war will not end until all we need fills the land and lodges in the flesh of our enemies. We shall stand atop a heap of corpses as high as the central spire of Carn Dûm, ${PLAYER}.
'Then shall the Great Eye see that we are his greatest servants! Then shall Mordirith and his servants kneel to the Uruk!'

'Ore and fire, flame and metal. They will twist on the forge and build the weapons to drive into the hearts of our enemy! Metal in the north and wood in the south. Rape the land, steal all it offers, and return it here.'

'A moment, ${RACE}. I am troubled by this wood -- not surprising given the corruption long seeping into the world -- but there is something more. Since our arrival, I have felt a sense of encroaching dread.
'To the west, there are a host of spiders stalking through the woods. I believe that the brood-mother may have returned to their home.
'If this is true, we must move at once to destroy her, lest Angmar's army convinces her to join the battle against us.'

'With Gorgoris defeated, the brood will not be drawn into the battle against us. We may be able to stand against this foe for some time now.
'Take this with my thanks and seek out Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig.'
Speak with First Marshal Núrdram at the Grimwood Lumber-yard
Raid: Culling the Brood
Within the depths of the Grimwood, beneath a great stone shelter west of the Grimwood Lumber-yard is the lair of a terrifying spider, Gorgoris. She is a terrible threat to the Free Peoples.
'Seek out the brood-queen west of our camp and destroy her before Angmar's army draws her into the battle against us.'

Gorgoris, the brood-queen of the Grimfang, dwells somewhere within the Grimwood forest in Hithlad.
First Marshal Núrdram asked you to find the brood-queen of the Grimfang and destroy her.

First Marshal Núrdram awaits your return within the Grimwood Lumber-yard.
You found and destroyed Gorgoris, the Grimfang brood-queen.

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. It is good to see the faces of so many willing to aid in this battle. As you know, we are an island in this dangerous land. We have no true supply lines and must rely on our own number to satisfy the many needs this war-host commands.
'At the moment, we are in need of arrow-shafts. Scattered throughout this wood, and perhaps on the vile and corrupted Leafcull-trees, you will find small branches. Some, though certainly not all, of the branches will suffice, and we will offer you rewards for your assistance.
'Seek the wood throughout the Grimwood and Hithlad.'

'At a cursory glance it appears that many of these will make fine arrow shafts. You are due a reward, and I am Elf of my word. Take this with my thanks.
'Should you find yourself with several of these, deliver them to Quartermaster Ash.'
'You will need to scour the Grimwood, within the bounds of Hithlad, and perhaps face down the corrupted Leafcull to obtain the shafts I require.'
Return to First Marshal Núrdram at the Grimwood Lumber-yard

Shafts for Arrows
Arrows are a commodity that will eventually run out and while bone and metal can be used to fashion the shafts, only the straightest of branches can be used for the shaft.

Small branches can be found scattered on the ground and on the Leafcull-trees throughout the Grimwood.
First Marshal Núrdram asked you to search along the Grimwood and Hithlad for small branches that might be turned into arrowshafts.

'In the north, at the edge of the Mountains of Angmar, there are drakes the Hobbits of Hoarhallow call Wintersebb. So named for their trek down the mountain when the winter breaks and the Hoardale flows strong again.
'These drakes have become active since the arrival of the Free Peoples, and often they hamper our efforts to mine the Isendeep. We are in need of help culling their number to ensure that our efforts there go smoothly.
'If you are willing, gather allies and make your way north to confront the Wintersebb brood.'

'A great victory is earned this day, and it is by your hand that it has been gained. You have proven your worth to the Free Peoples and deserve this reward for your efforts.
'Should you wish to claim your ultimate prize, seek out Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig.
'You have earned your honour well, ${PLAYER}.'

End of the Wintersebb
Far to the north, where the Isendeep Mine runs beneath the shadow of the Mountains of Angmar, a brood of Drakes threatens the workers within the mine.

'You will find the Wintersebb-drakes north of here in the land called Arador's end. Seek out and destroy the drakes and drakelings you find there. A word of caution, friend: you will not want to venture there alone.'

Wintersebb-drakes can be found north in the area of Arador's End.
Lieutenant Swithulf directed you to make your way north with others in search of a way to destroy the Wintersebb-drakes.

Lieutenant Swithulf awaits your return at the Grimwood Lumber-yard.
Climbing high into the foothills of the Mountains of Angmar in Arador's end, you faced down many foes from the Wintersebb-brood and emerged to collect your reward.
