'The battle goes poorly, if you ask me, ${CLASS}. We drive the Enemy back, and then they return to run us out. All the while, our resources dwindle, while the Enemy continues to garner strength.
'We are in dire need of replenishing our supplies for the effort, and that is why I need your help. To the north there is a mine, where our dwarf-allies delve when the Snowreap-goblins are not within the caverns. There are stores there, or unrefined ore. We can refine the ore and build axes, swords, and hammers...but first we need the ore.
'Ore alone, however, will not solidify the war effort. There are thicker logs, some already hewn to the ground, scattered throughout the Grimwood and others still may be obtained from the deadly, walking Leafcull-trees. If you mean to aid us, gather logs and ore for me and bring them back so I may continue to fuel our efforts.'

'You are to be commended for your efforts, ${PLAYER}. This was a difficult undertaking, and you have performed it well. Take this with my thanks and the thanks of the Free Peoples.
'Should you desire to exchange the token, seek Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig.'

'Seek the ore in the north within the confines of the Isendeep Mine or on the bodies of the Snowreap-goblins. In the Grimwood, search amongst the fallen logs or the fallen bodies of the Leafcull-trees.'

'${RACE}, listen here. As the battle rages about us, we must remember that we serve the glory of the Great Eye and his servant Mordirith in the Army of Angmar. There is no better way to show our prowess in battle than to fly our standards when we take these fortresses!
'Our enemy tears down our flags and destroys them and materials are hard to find in this desolate land so we must hunt for the materials we need. Scattered throughout the land here, there are massive aurochs. Their hides are sizable and can easily be used to make the flags we need.
'Hunt them in packs and skin them for their hides.'

'These hides will suffice. With them we shall rebuild the flags torn and burned by the enemy. These fields will run red with their blood, and soon the air will burn, and these flags shall fly throughout all lands!
'For the glory of Angmar, Mordirith, and Lugbúrz!'
'Retrieve those hides, maggot! We can't claim our land without flags!'

'${RACE}, you want to eat, and though it pains me to waste even the lowliest gruel on a pathetic thing like yourself, I've orders to keep you well fed. You'll not taste the tribute collected for the Tyrant, nor the foods we eat.
'Your meal comes from the bugs outside these walls. If you don't like it, you can take the chance that a wandering giant or drake doesn't gobble up the goblins or couriers from Dâr-gazag. Oh, we've got food from the rat-folk too...but that is for the Krahjarn, you lowly little beast.
'You'll eat what you get and nothing more. Be thankful I'll prepare it for you! Catch your meal and bring it back here!'

'Mash this together, boil it well, and your dinner will be ready.
'Now is not time for eating, worm.'
'If your'e not hungry, I'll watch you rot. I can cover myself fairly well, you little maggot. If you want your nerves strong, you'll get the meat for which I ask.'

Nerbyg can be found along the banks of the Hoardale River surrounding Tol Ascarnen.

'Pay attention to everything I say, wretch, else I'll stretch your hide from the west bridge of this island to the east bridge. Our leader, Tyrant Trintrû, is deserving of our praise and our tribute. Time for you to pay your tribute, dog.
'The one thing, above all else, that Tyrant Trintrû desires is Man-flesh. So you will oblige him. You will go into the wild, find the Men at their holdings or wandering through the wood, ripe for picking, and you will cut their legs from their bodies.
'Bring their legs back to me, and I will see that the Tyrant knows you have paid him proper tribute! Go now, worm!'
'For the glory of Angmar, Mordirith, and the service of Lugburz! You serve your masters well, cur!'
'You worthless, scum! I gave you an order to fetch Man-flesh, and you come before me without all that you need! Back into the fight and don't return to me until you have collected enough Man-flesh!'

'Listen well, ${CLASS}. We're in a battle that will rage for a good long time, and we're in need of supplies. Though the land will give up some edible meats, much of what is here is useless.
'Now, food stores are raided often, and we've lost a good portion of our supplies. We need to be mindful of the future and think about ways that we can increase our existing food sources. This might turn your stomach some -- it does mine -- but there are nerbyg surrounding this fortress, and though they might seem a might unsavoury, we've found that cooked long enough and with enough spice, they can make a good source of food...in a pinch.
'Round up a bundle of their gizzards and meat, and I'll reward you for what you bring.'

'Terrible sort of thing to do, but we're not here to be making a comely home. We are in a war, ${CLASS}. War makes you do things you would ought not normally do.
'You've earned this, ${PLAYER}. Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig is collecting these for greater rewards.'
'Bring me the gizzards and meat from the nerbyg within the Hoardale.'

'Listen here. Captain-General Makán looks out for the Free Peoples as best he can, and that's why he has me working on restocking food and ale.
'Hoarhallow, that little village of hobbits to the south-west, makes the finest ale in the region -- well, the only ale in the region. Slightly bitter to appeal to the taste of dwarves and Men, with a sweet finish that the Elves desire.
'Raiders from the forces of Angmar have looted so much of the ale that there is not enough left to go around. Find some Hoarhallow-ale and make your way back to me, and I will see you suitably rewarded.'

'Ah yes! A great many of the draughts, indeed! This'll warm our bones on long nights looking out over the walls of this fort.
'You've earned this, ${PLAYER}. Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig is collecting these for greater rewards.'
'I'll need a goodly number of draughts before I can cede a token of valour to you, ${CLASS}. You'd best get out there and find them.'

Liquid Courage

Captain-General Mákan does his best to assist the morale of the troops stationed at Tol Ascarnen. The relentless battle takes its toll on a being over time, and ale is the best way to keep the Free Peoples prepared.

You may be able to find some in Hoarhallow itself, but it will likely be costly. You may even find the draughts stored at Grothum and Dâr-gazag.
Lieutenant Solvi asked you to find and recover draughts of Hoarhallow-ale.
Collected food-sack (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ho there, ${CLASS}, you look like the sort who might help me fix some of the problems we found soon as we took this fortress. We and the Orcs fight here often, and we sometimes get beat back from within only to return later.
'During the last siege, it seemed like a score of Orcs stormed over me and got to our stores. We lost a good number of supplies in that assault, and we need to get them back. I've heard tell that the Orcs, trolls, and even the goblins are walking about with the food-sacks on their person. Hobbits need it too, those poor folk down the river a pinch.
'Slaughter the Orcs in the area and look for the food-sacks. I've heard tell you can find mountains of the stolen food at their camp, Dâr-gazag, in the west or maybe some up north near the goblin's village of Grothum.'

'I may seem a bit harsh, ${PLAYER}, that is true. But I want to see that we do what must be done to see this battle won. You helped us more than you know, and for that, I am grateful.
'Speak with Quartermaster Ash to learn of the importance of these tokens.'
'You've been given an order, and I expect you to follow it! Get out there and get that food back to us!'
Return to Lieutenant Solvi at Tol Ascarnen

Thieving Orcs

West of Tol Ascarnen, across the Hoardale River, the Orcs make their main keep. It is here that Lieutenant Solvi believes the Orcs have stolen precious food stores moved into Tol Ascarnen during the initial push by the Free Peoples, and he wants them back.

Food-sacks might be found on the Orcs, trolls, and goblins in the Ettenmoors.

'Long have the Elves of Mirkwood spoken of spiders with great intelligence, but until I came here, I did not believe such tales.
'Now, we see them amongst the rank and file of the Enemy. They are terrible, cruel and calculating. In the west, along the moors beneath Mount Gram, the Cragstone-spiders lair and breed.
'I challenge you, ${PLAYER}, to seek out the beasts in the crags and slaughter them. That will hopefully alleviate the plight facing our warriors who head into the rocky Steps of Gram.'

'A good number of the spiders are gone, but the brood is plentiful, and it will not be long before they replenish their numbers and must be culled again.
'For all that you have done, I offer you this, ${PLAYER}. Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig will exchange these for something more suitable.'

'Search among the moors west of Tol Ascarnen, beyond Lugazag, for the Cragstone-spiders. Slay as many as you can and then return to me.'

Quartermaster Cynwiss asked you to defeat the Cragstone-spiders in the moors of the Steps of Gram.

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. No doubt you are here to assist us in seeing that the flags over our positions here in the Ettenmoors continue to fly. There are a few ways that you can contribute to that cause.
'First, continue your battle against the forces of the Enemy...this will ensure that we continue to drive the front forward. Second, assist me in acquiring the materials to make new flags. As each of our strongholds is overrun -- and it does happen, despite our best efforts -- we lose munitions and our flags. The material cost and shipment of new ones would take too long, so artisans amongst us are handling the craftwork, but we still need to gather the materials.
'We are only using the hide of the Thistledown-aurochs as they are the creatures least corrupted in these lands. If you are willing, help us collect their hides and return them to me.'

'You return with all that I asked for, ${PLAYER}. This may not seem as important as defeating the Enemy on a field of battle, yet knowing that your standard still waves above a fortress can instill fear into the heart's of the foe and inspire those under your command.
'Take this...Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig will reward you well.'
'I need more hides. It will take time to properly prepare them for the artisans.'

'We know that there are trolls scattered throughout the north and certainly in service to Angmar. What we did not expect was the number of the trolls in service to the Snowreap-goblins, and worse, the Coldeve that roam the Ettenmoors.
'We need to do something about these beasts, lest they become a greater threat to us over time. Gather a fellowship of like-minded people and seek a way to destroy these deadly beasts.'

'Knowing that their number has been culled gives me reason to pause and reflect on my youth. I was once a brazen youth willing to face down such foes without concern. I envy the wild nature you possess, ${PLAYER}. It suits you well and is needed as this battle begins to progress.
'Here, take this, you should seek out Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig to claim your true prize.'
Defeat Snowreap-trolls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Coldeve-trolls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Lieutenant Osur at the Isendeep Mine
Reaping the Snow and Cold

The Ettenmoors is home to many terrifying beasts, but the most frightening are the trolls. It is from here that the trolls pushed to infest the Trollshaws, and still many stalk through the wilds of the Ettenmoors.
'You'll likely find the Snowreap in areas where you would find the goblins. The Coldeve may be a bit harder to locate. They migrate all throughout the Ettenmoors, from what we have seen.'

Snowreap-trolls are likely to be found in the northern stretches of Arador's End, near the Isendeep Mine. You may also find Coldeve stone-trolls, but they have been known to wander the entirety of the Ettenmoors.
After speaking to Lieutenant Osur, you were enlisted to assist in destroying the Snowreap and Coldeve-trolls.

Lieutenant Osur awaits news of your success at the Isendeep Mine.
You found and slaughtered the Coldeve and Snowreap-trolls as directed to by Lieutenant Osur. Now you should return to him with the news.
Defeated Shadowmaw-wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'In the west, in the shadow of Mount Gram, a pack of Wargs with a vile and dark bite roams freely and stalks out towards our holdings. These Wargs, the Shadowmaw, are responsible for many attacks on our number.
'We must find a way to cull their number. If you are willing, travel west and cut them down. Strike a telling blow against this foe lest their danger grow over time.'

'While the battle rages there is no rest from the foes that we face, but for the moment we are spared. Take this reward, ${PLAYER}.
'In time, you will learn that these shall earn you great wealth. Seek out Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig to learn more.'
Defeat Shadowmaw-wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Lieutenant Octa at the Isendeep Mine
Mouth of Shadow
In the crags to the west of the Isendeep, the Shadowmaw pack bolsters the forces of Angmar.
'You will find that the Shadowmaw are drawn to the Steps of Gram. Be cautious when travelling through that land. It teems with the forces of Angmar and is perpetually cast in shadow.'

The Shadowmaw stalk the Steps of Gram.
Lieutenant Octa at the Isendeep Mine asked you to reduce the threat posed by the Shadowmaw-wargs.

Lieutenant Octa is at the Isendeep Mine.
Lieutenant Octa will be pleased to learn that you have succeeded at destroying a good number of the Wargs in the Steps of Gram.

'Goblins will aid us in this place, and this is good. Mining is for such lowly races.
'It is the place of warriors, like you, to seize moments and become great! We are vulnerable -- I fear assault at the hands of the eagles who are not far from here.
'The greatest among them, Golloval, is a lord of the sky, and it falls to you and others to bring him at last to the ground!'

'A threat such as this will not last. I have word that even as he fell and you left him to rot, that the eagle-lord took to the sky again.
'He will return, but we have earned a reprieve by your will!'
Return to Taskmaster Bárzqhosh at the Isendeep Mine
Raid: Grounding Golloval

Taskmaster Bárzqhosh wants you to ensure that the threat posed by the eagles and their leader, Golloval, are diminshed. He has ordered you to gather a great number and assail the eagle-lord at his eyrie in Arador's End.
'Do not fail, or this mine will fall into the hands of the enemy, and you will suffer in the slave-pits of Carn Dûm.'

Golloval can be found south of the mine in an eagle-eyrie.
Taskmaster Bárzqhosh tasked you with finding and slaughtering the eagle, Golloval.

Taskmaster Bárzqhosh awaits your return within the Isendeep Mine.
Golloval found his end at your will. You should return to Taskmaster Bárzqhosh with the news.
Collected Grimwood-kindling (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The mine spills ore from every new scar we open in its walls, but the tools our slaves use grow weaker with every swing.
'There is a place, far to the south, where the wood is strong. Go there, to the Grimwood. Find healthy stocks of wood and bring them to us. They need only be better than roots, some may call it kindling but the wood will prove sturdy enough for our purposes.
'Make haste, ${RACE}. We must continue our assault and drive the enemy from this land!'

'We will go about refitting the tools now and see that the mine gives up ore at a faster pace. This shall fuel our war-machine and we shall crush our opponents with ease.
'For the glory of Angmar! For the Great Eye!'
'Get a move on, sluggard. We need the ore within these walls!'
Return to Taskmaster Bárzqhosh at the Isendeep Mine
Collect Grimwood-kindling (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Tools for the Mine
Your war-host claims to have enough metal now that the mine is in-service and under your control, but the picks used by the goblins are dulled with time and the wood rots out from their hands.

Kindling can be found in the Grimwood.
Taskmaster Bárzqhosh tasked you with garnering enough wood to repair the picks used to pull ore from the Isendeep.
Collected Sun-touched tailfeathers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Me no likes eagles.
'Eagles go...on dead troll.
'You kill eagles, take feathers.
'Make me like you.'

'No more fouling dead troll...eagle-bird!'
The troll eats the feathers. Peculiar.
'Go get feathers! No more fly....'
Return to Taskmaster Izubuzri at the Isendeep Mine
Collect Sun-touched tailfeathers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Slaughtering Eagles
Taskmaster Izubuzri communicated that he wants proof that you killed many eagles. Apparently the eagles are too free with where they perch.

Eagles can be found throughout the Coldfells and in a small section of Arador's End to the south of the Isendeep Mine.
Taskmaster Izubuzri wants you to return eagle feathers to him to prove that you have slaughtered a good number of the birds.
Defeated Orc, Uruk, and troll-guards at Lugazag (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Greetings, friend ${RACE}. I urge you to listen and consider my words, for this battle is one that shall assist in deciding the fate of all who are threatened by the shadow growing over Middle-earth. To the west of this tower there is a place of evil. Within the walls once held by the Men of Rhudaur, corruption seethes and grows.
'A host of the Enemy awaits an assault from the Free Peoples that must be levied with swiftness, strength and courage. The tower is called Lugazag, and I ask you to assist us in defeating the Enemy that guards the tower.
'You will likely need the assistance of others as they will fight to the death if need be. Find them and meet them, return to me when you have done as charged.'

'You have proven to be a ${RACE} of honour. You shall be rewarded and your tale shall be told amongst the forces here in the Ettenmoors.
'For all you have done to aid us, I salute you, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat Orc, Uruk, and troll-guards at Lugazag (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Guards of Lugazag
Lugazag, the western tower in the Ettenmoors, is defended by a host of Orcs, Uruks, and trolls.

'I only wish to know that the guards near and within Lugazag are slain. Though the battle is fought on many fronts, I wish to liberate and sieze this tower above all else. Return to me when the guards are defeated.'

Lugazag lies far to the west of Tirith Rhaw.
Sergeant-at-Arms Milbrethil instructed you to find and slay guards in the area of Lugazag.

Tirith Rhaw is far to the east of Lugazag.
Making your way across the Ettenmoors, you found and faced a host of the Ongbûrz defending the tower, Lugazag. You should return to Tirith Rhaw and inform Sergeant-at-Arms Milbrethil of your success against the guards near Lugazag.
Collected Morningthaw-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Stop looking at me that way. I've no fear! I've got my orders, and my orders are to pass along a message to you from the War-tyrant! The army is tired and cold. I've been dispatched here to see that we do something about this.
'I'm not going outside the safety of this tower! Too many of the enemy nearby for my liking! You go get the hides that I need, and I'll be sure to tell all others that you helped.
'Get hides from the bears around us. They are the most dangerous thing we face in these parts!'

'I shall be a hero! You have made me a hero!
'Ha! You pathetic beast! I will not honour my word. You are my slave, and I a hero!'
'Go get the hides, I can hear the bears even now. Don't carry any food near me, I don't want them to find me.'
Deliver the Morningthaw-hides to Soldier Fandmau
Collect Morningthaw-hides (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bedding of Bears
Soldier Fandmau, stationed at Tirith Rhaw, ordered you to collect the hides of the Morningthaw-bears to use as bedding for the army.

Bears can be found around Tirith Rhaw.
Soldier Fandmau waits for you to return with the bear-hides he ordered you to collect.
Coldfells Army member slaughtered! (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Taking this tower puts us in harm's way, and the Free Peoples will not sit idly by while we are so close to their keep. We must slaughter them now and slaughter them quickly, lest they enter the tower and do us all in.
'Go quickly! Kill them!'

'Dead? Yes, dead. You did well. Perhaps we will survive a bit longer.
'Leave now. Please, keep watching the area.'
Slaughter members of the Coldfells Army (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Return to Soldier Fandmau at Tirith Rhaw
Flay the Free Peoples
Soldier Fandmau fears reprisal for the assault of Tirith Rhaw and wants you to attack the Free Peoples quickly before they retaliate.
'I don't smell the blood of innocents on you. Get out there and kill the enemy! Only then will I respect you enough to not see you as a worthless wretch!'

Defenders of the Free Peoples can be found throughout the Ettenmoors.
Soldier Fandmau directed you to slaughter the defenders loyal to the Free Peoples.

Soldier Fandmau is at Tirith Rhaw.
You found and slaughtered a good number of the enemy.
Collected fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected shard of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected slab of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Guarding this post makes me nervous. So close to the enemy and trolls bashing holes through the stone. We need to shore the walls here and fast.
'Get stone from the dead trolls throughout the Ettenmoors and return them to me. No stone is too small!'

'I'd build a wall if I could to keep the enemy from getting into our halls. We should be more defensible. Higher walls, larger tower...more trolls!!!
'You did well, ${PLAYER}. I will speak well of you for a time.'
'What is this? Coming back to me empty handed!? Sluggards like you are why we run the risk of assault from everwhere!? Get out there and get me what I need.'
Return to Soldier Fandmau at Tirith Rhaw
Collect fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect shards of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect slabs of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Stonewall Fandmau
Soldier Fandmau needs stone to repair the holes blasted through the walls of Tirith Rhaw and sent you to find the materials from the trolls caught in the sun.

Trolls that have been turned to stone by the sun are scattered throughout the Ettenmoors.
Soldier Fandmau tasked you with obtaining a fair number of large to small bits of troll-stone to repair the walls of Tirith Rhaw.
Collected Sack of Food (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I've been thinking of ways to keep the eagles away from this place. Their claws make me wince, and I'm not one to like blood.
'You're the perfect fool to test this theory with, or at least to be an accomplice to me. So you'll do as I say, or I'll call for the trolls.
'Shards of troll-stone, wrapped in foodstuff might fill the bird's bellies with so much weight that they can't fly anymore! I need you to get me little shards of troll-stone and some food to test the theory.'

'Ha! When next the eagles come to prey on us, we will feed them the stones and they will fall to the ground and die!
'If this fails...you will serve as a suitable reason for the failure!.'

'You've done nothing you worthless pile of festering dung! Have you been beaten so daft you cannot follow simple orders. Do you not understand the terror that will assail us from the skies! Go! Leave my sight and do not return until you have redeemed yourself.'
Return to Soldier Fandmau at Tirith Rhaw
Collect Sacks of Food (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect fragments of troll-stone (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
I've Got a Theory
Soldier Fandmau believes that he can aid in ending the threat posed by the eagles from the north by feeding them troll-stone. How an Orc like this one became a leader is beyond you.

Troll-stone shards will likely be found from smaller or larger pieces of the trolls caught in the sunlight. Food can be found on the enemy or the rat-folk in Hoarhallow.
Soldier Fandmau needs some help proving out a theory he has.
Collected Sun-touched tailfeather (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Feathers...good...crown.
'Get feathers...or smash you.'
'You get me feathers!'
'You get me feathers?'
Return to Taskmaster Núrsufum at Tirith Rhaw
Collect Sun-touched tailfeathers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Feather for His Cap

Not all who rise to military prominence are capable of complete conversations. Trolls, known for their strength, sometimes manage small words. For instance, Taskmaster Núrsufum. Apparently, Taskmaster Núrsufum likes to place feathers in his helmet and wants you to go about getting the feathers he desires.

Sun-touched eagles are found throughout the Coldfells and sections of Arador's End.
Taskmaster Núrsufum wants you to get him tailfeathers for his helm.

'Big bear...head of gold...come...fight.
'You go stop.
'Now!'

'Good.
'Me no kill you.'
Return to Taskmaster Núrsufum
Goldhead Must Die

Trolls do not communicate well, as is proving true time and again. You think you were able to piece together a terrible truth from what Taskmaster Galinzarza tried to say. A bear named Goldhead may be aligned with the enemy, and if they act quickly enough, may assist the enemy against the tower.

'Smash bear!
'Now!'

Old Goldhead may be within a bear-den near Tirith Rhaw.
Taskmaster Núrsufum seems to have communicated that a great bear nearby named Goldhead may be allied with the enemy.

Taskmaster Núrsufum is at Tirith Rhaw.
You found and destroyed Old Goldhead. Now you should return to Taskmaster Núrsufum.
The Free People reclaim Tirith Rhaw!

'The Orcs proved strong enough to overwhelm our forces in Tirith Rhaw. Now, a fell foe has taken control of the tower. We must muster our forces and drive them from that place at once.
'Gather a force together and make your way north into the Coldfells. Tirith Rhaw stand overlooking the valley to the west. You must enter and defeat the master of the Ongbûrz at this location.
'Seek out the Tyrant Barashish at Tirith Rhaw and defeat him. Fight with honour and return the tower to our control.'

'You did well, ${PLAYER}. We need to continue our efforts in driving these Orcs from the Ettenmoors. Take this and know that you are well-thanked for your efforts.
'Seek out Quartermaster Ash in Glân Vraig to retrieve your greatest rewards.'
Defeat Tyrant Barashish and reclaim Tirith Rhaw. You must not be defeated when the Tyrant falls.
Speak with Sergeant Hesten
Raid: Tyrant Barashish
A powerful Orc warrior, the Tyrant Barashish has taken command of Tirith Rhaw. Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten has enlisted your talents in removing the Orc from the tower.
'We must retake Tirith Rhaw. Make your way to the tower, north of this location, in the centre of the Coldfells. Defeat the Tyrant Barashish, then return to me.'

The Tyrant Barashish is at Tirith Rhaw, north of Glân Vraig, in the centre of the Coldfells.
Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten at Glân Vraig directed you to seek out and defeat the Orc Tyrant, Barashish who holds command at Tirith Rhaw.

Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten awaits your return at Glân Vraig.
You defeated the Tyrant Barashish to reclaim Tirith Rhaw, You should return to Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten with the news.
The Free People claim Lugazag!

'Lugazag is a tower claimed wholly by the Enemy. If we are to tame this battlefield and control it for the cause of the Free Peoples, we must overwhelm their position and defeat their leader.
'With the head of the tower removed their forces will sunder, and we shall win the day. Take heart and seek the aid of many.
'Journey to the west beneath the shadow of Mount Gram in the Steps of Gram and siege Lugazag. Drive within its heart and defeat the leader of the Ongbûrz there, the Tyrant Tharbil. Do this, and you will earn great honour.'
'You did well, ${PLAYER}. Take this with our thanks and seek out Quartermaster Ash here to lay claim to the rewards which await you.'
Defeat Tyrant Tharbil and claim Lugazag. You must not be defeated when the Tyrant falls.
Speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten at Glân Vraig
Raid: Tyrant Tharbil
Lugazag, a tower far to the west of Glân Vraig, is held by the Ongbûrz Orc-tribe and commanded by the Tyrant Tharbil.
'We must defeat these curs. Make your way to the tower, north and west of Glân Vraig in the Steps of Gram, defeat the Tyrant Tharbil, and return to me.'

Lugazag looks east out over the Hoardale river.
Once Lugazag was a great tower, part of the Rhudauran kingdom. Now, in the corrupt lands of the Steps of Gram, the tower stands as a location controlled by the Ongbûrz tribe and their Tyrant, Tharbil. Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten at Glân Vraig directed you to seek out and defeat the Tyrant Tharbil who holds command at Lugazag.

Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten awaits your return at Glân Vraig.
You defeated Tyrant Tharbil with the help of others to reclaim Tirith Rhaw. You should return to Sergeant-at-Arms Hesten and tell him of your victory over Tharbil.
Tyrant Durgrat Slain

'We face an organized tribe of Orcs here, ${CLASS}. We will need the assistance of all capable peoples to defeat these foes.
'Scouts, reporting from the deepest parts of the front, have discovered that the leader of this war-host resides at Dâr-gazag, an encampment built on the ruins of an ancient Rhudauran fortress, far to the west of Ost Ringdyr.
'I am authorized to present you with much acclaim if you assist in defeating this warmaster. Be cautious as the enemy is strong at this fortress. You will need a great number to overwhelm their forces and defeat the War-tyrant, Durgrat.'

'Durgrat's defeat is a great one, but he will return. His forces will not allow his defeat to influence them for long.
'We have earned a brief respite from their assaults thanks to you, ${PLAYER}, but we must not rest on these successes.'
Kill Tyrant Durgrat at Dâr-gazag. You must not be defeated when the Tyrant falls.
Speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent at Glân Vraig
Raid: Tyrant Durgrat
A great leader of the Ongbûrz, Tyrant Durgrat, is holed up in Dâr-gazag, far to the west.
'You will find the War-tyrant in the upper reaches of Dâr-gazag. Make your way there and defeat him and his war-host. Return here when the deed is done.'

Dâr-gazag, built on the ruins of a Rhudauran citadel, lay far to the west of Ost Ringdyr, across the Hoardale River. Make your way to the fortress and defeat War-master Durgrat at this location.
Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent directed you to kill the Uruk-warmaster Durgrat at Dâr-gazag.

Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent awaits your return at Glân Vraig.
Facing down the Enemy, you destroyed the War-master at Dâr-gazag. You should return to Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent with the news.
The Free People reclaim Tol Ascarnen!

'Captain-General Mákan wishes to retake Tol Ascarnen, and we are enlisting all who are able to take the fight to the Hoardale and defeat the Uruk in charge of the Ongbûrz war-host.
'North and west of Glân Vraig lay the Hoardale and on an island in the centre of the river is Tol Ascarnen. Make your way there and defeat the Tyrant and his war-host.
'Return to me when you have done this. Do not be fool-headed, this is not a mission for one or a handful. You will need a great many to best this foe.'

'You have scored a great victory for the Free Peoples, ${PLAYER}. We honour your accomplishment and duty, but also warn that we cannot relent in our battle against the Enemy.
'If we do not remain resolute, the Enemy will drive south and swallow this land in war.'
Defeat Tyrant Trintrû and reclaim Tol Ascarnen. You must not be defeated when the Tyrant falls.
Speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent at Glân Vraig
Raid: Tyrant Trintrû
Tol Ascarnen has fallen to the Enemy. You have been tasked by Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent at Glân Vraig to find and defeat Tyrant Trintrû within the walls of Tol Ascarnen.
'You will find the Tyrant in the upper reaches of Tol Ascarnen. Make your way there and defeat him. Only then can Captain-General Mákan retake Tol Ascarnen and secure this most important location.'

Tol Ascarnen, once the citadel responsible for the manufacture and storage of Rhudauran weapons and armour, lay to the north and west of Glân Vraig.
Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent directed you to kill Tyrant Trintrû at Tol Ascarnen.

Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent awaits your return at Glâin Vraig.
Facing down the enemy, you destroyed the Tyrant at Tol Ascarnen. You should return to Sergeant-at-Arms Thurimbent with the news.
The Free People claim the Isendeep Mine!

'Goblins! Goblins mining in the hills. There is a mine, north in the land called Arador's End, called the Isendeep. It holds strong dwarf-iron, and I've even heard tell of other rare ores.
'The mine is overrun, and we know from scouts that there is a powerful foe within the mine overseeing the goblin-digging. It's a troll-tyrant by the name of Bûrzgoth. We're asking all who are willing to go north into Arador's End in search of the beast. Find him, defeat him, and then we'll take handle of the mine.
'You'll want to bring an army to face this foe, ${CLASS}.'

'Finally a place worth the strength of the dwarves! We shall do what we can to hold the mine, though no doubt the Ongbûrz have already ordered a counterattack. You've done well, ${PLAYER}.
'If we had more like you, the fight to keep the enemy from the south would be won quickly.'
Defeat Tyrant Bûrzgoth and claim the Isendeep Mine. You must not be defeated when the Tyrant falls.
Raid: Tyrant Bûrzgoth

Along the northern edge of the Ettenmoors, in the low-lands of the Mountains of Angmar in the lands called Arador's End there is a mine: Isendeep. Here, goblins toil and delve into the metals, plundering from the earth.
'Preserve the ore, but defeat that troll. We need to take that mine to strengthen our forces here in the Ettenmoors.'

The Isendeep Mine is in Arador's End.
Sergeant-at-Arms Ingi asked you to make your way to the Isendeep to defeat the troll-tyrant Bûrzgoth.

Sergeant-at-Arms Ingi awaits news of your victory over the Tyrant Bûrzgoth at Glân Vraig.
You met the Tyrant Bûrzgoth at Isendeep and drove him from the mine. You should return to Sergeant-at-Arms Ingi with the news.
The Free People claim the Grimwood Lumber-yard!

'There's been a terrible turn in the Grimwood over in Hithlad, ${CLASS}. A troll moved in and swept clean the people that were watching over the area.
'We received orders to recruit folk willing to make the journey west into Hithlad in search of the Grimwood Lumber-yard to face down and defeat the Tyrant Gundzor. If you are willing, make your way west in search of the beast and strike him down. Then return to me when you're done.
'Don't try to be too much of a hero, ${CLASS}. You'll not face a foe like that on your own, nor with a company of friends. Take a lot more to defeat a terrible foe like Gundzor.'

'Better news has not blessed these ears in many days, my friend. You proved a mighty warrior and asset to the Free Peoples here, ${PLAYER}.
'I shall not forget what you have done!'
Defeat Tyrant Gundzor and claim the Grimwood Lumber-yard. You must not be defeated when the Tyrant falls.
Raid: Tyrant Gundzor
Within the depths of the Grimwood there is a grove where the trees have been cleared and a small lumber-camp built. The grove has fallen to the Ongbûrz and must be reclaimed.

'Take the beast down quickly so we can move back into the wood and have a better spot to strike at the enemy from.
'I'm rambling too much...get out there and defeat that troll!'

The Grimwood Lumber-yard lay near the centre of Hithlad.
Sergeant-at-Arms Ingi asked you to find and defeat the troll-tyrant Gundzor at the Grimwood Lumber-yard.

Sergeant-at-Arms Ingi awaits news of your victory over the Tyrant Gundzor at Glân Vraig.
You met the Tyrant Gundzor within the lumber-yard and defeated him and his forces, taking the yard back for the Free Peoples. You should return to Sergeant-at-Arms Ingi with the news.
Collected tokens of valour (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Do you see this? This is my Orc-cleaver. I was given this by Captain-General Lainedhel himself. That's right, this weapon was cooled in the rapids of the Noisewater in Rivendell. It barters for roughly one-hundred and ten beryls. It's got a sturdy oaken shaft and hardened Elf-steel blade. With me on the job, it's ready to fight at any moment.
'Now I know you are wondering how you can come by such a masterful piece of work. Well, I'll tell you: Valour. You prove your valour to the Free Peoples, and I'll see that you're fairly rewarded. No, you can't touch my blade. Your primitive mind wouldn't understand the relation of woods and alloys...things like magic.
'You want one of these types of weapons, you will need to earn it. Return to me when you've acquired enough tokens of valour, and we'll talk.'

'You got them all...excellent work! This key opens one of the chests behind me. I know what you're thinking: \qWhat am I supposed to do? Open one chest, open all the chests, or what?\q
'I can solve this for you simply. The key will only open one chest. You want to open more, you need more keys. You want more keys...you go through me. You got that?
'All right. These are treasures found while we fight this war. Do yourself a favour and don't ask from where they came.'

'Valourous or not valourous, it doesn't matter. I'm the one with the keys.
'Until you prove to me that you're something more than another would-be warrior who stands about asking, \qHow will we stop this army of Angmar at our walls? How will we fight that?\q you're not getting a thing.
'Get out there and earn some tokens of valour.'
Deliver the tokens of valour to Quartermaster Ash
Collect tokens of valour (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Valourous

Having assisted the Free Peoples in their battle against the war-host of Angmar, you have earned much respect. The respect you earn entitles you to receive rewards from Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig.

Quartermaster Ash is at Glân Vraig in the Ettenmoors.
Ash sent you to earn tokens of valour by assisting members of the Free Peoples.

'People come and take the mine, and the Snowreap retreat to the village. You come now to take back the mine so we work and give you ore again?
'Too many dwarves. Too many dwarves poking about in the stone, digging the ore for themselves. Kill them, says I. Kill them all.
'You kill them, and we work extra hard and speak good of what you done. Kill them, aye?'

'You done? Killed them good. Good. No more dwarves means goblins can mine and then give ore to Angmar!
'Kill them all, says I. For the glory of the Great Eye!'
Dwarfs in the Mine
Goblins complain that the mine is overrun by dwarves, and they are not pleased by the intrusion. They bid you to enter the Isendeep to slaughter the dwarf-miners.
'You go to the mine and kill dwarves. Come back when done.'

The Isendeep mine lay to the west of Grothum. If there are no dwarfs within the mine, make your way to the western entrance and search for them there.
Gasham asked you to enter the mine and slaughter the dwarves so the goblins can return to work.

Gasham awaits news of the mines at Grothum, the goblin-village in the north-east Ettenmoors.
You entered the mine and slaughtered all the dwarves you found. You should return to Gasham with the news.

'Swoop down they do. You'll see when they come, flying on armoured wings, swooping into the tunnels, eating up a goblin in one gulp!
'Now you here to help. Snowreap help Angmar, Angmar help the Snowreap. Into the mine, out of the mine flying, walking, stalking, they seek us in the hills and snow. They are the ebb of winter and have fangs as tall as me!
'Kill the drakes, yes? Kill them to help the Snowreap.'

'We thanks you! We thanks you great for the help you give.
'No more gobbled up goblins. We fight, but they strong. We give them meat, but they eat us. Too strong the drakes be, but not for Angmar!
'Glory to Angmar!'
Return to Gasham at Grothum
Gobbled Goblins
Gasham conveyed a tale of goblin-miners and goblins out and about from the village attacked by drakes stalking down from the mountain. He asked for your assistance in ridding the peaks of the beasts.
'Seek them in the hills here and there to the west. They like the winter land and snow.'

Wintersebb Drakes and drakelings can be found throughout Arador's End.
Gasham begged for your help against the Wintersebb Drakes.

Gasham is in the goblin-village of Grothum.
You hunted the drakes in the mountainous area of Arador's End and culled their number. You should return to Gasham with the news.
Collected Chieftain seal

'You there, ${RACE}, I have task for you.
'Chieftains command great numbers of the Enemy's forces, second only to the tyrants that lead the war-host.
'Should you run afoul of these terrors, slay them and bring me their seals so that I might see you rewarded for their defeat.'

'Each Chieftain that falls strengthens our position, ${PLAYER}. You are a hero to all the Free Peoples. Seek Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig to earn greater recognition of your efforts in the Ettenmoors.'
'Five Chieftain's seals will earn you a Token of Valour, ${PLAYER}. Keep hunting the Enemy.'
Return Chieftain's seals to First Marshal Sathryth
Collect Chieftain's seal
Angmar's Chieftains
First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr is collecting seals found on the Chieftains of Angmar's army in the Ettenmoors.

The Chieftains of Angmar may be found among the Enemy in the Ettenmoors.
Chieftains amongst Angmar's army bear seals that denote their station. Slay them and take their seals to earn recognition amongst the Free Peoples. First Marshal Sathryth has promised a reward for the seals you bring her.
Collected tracker's badges (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ho there, ${RACE}, lend me your ear!
'There are many servants of Angmar scattered throughout the Ettenmoors. Search amongst their army for the tracker's badges. These can be found on the lowliest of their forces.
'If you collect some of these badges and return them to me, you will be honoured with a commendation of valour.'
'Your efforts are welcomed, ${PLAYER}. Please take this with my thanks. Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig will recognize you for your efforts in the Ettenmoors should you visit her.'
'I need more of the tracker's badges before I can bestow a Token of Valour upon you, ${PLAYER}. Keep hunting the enemy down.'
Return tracker's badges to First Marshal Sathryth
Collect tracker's badges (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Angmar's Scouts
First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr is collecting badges taken from Angmar's weakest forces.

Trackers can be found among the Enemy in the Ettenmoors.
Forces in the service to Angmar may each carry a seal of their station. Search among the enemy for these badges. First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr has promised a reward for the badges you bring her.
Collected soldier's patches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Have you been ignoring me, ${RACE}? I have need of your services.
'Above the rank and file, the soldiers of Angmar act as lesser leaders of the Ongbûrz forces. These beasts are savage and cruel and capable of leading only small numbers before their tempers lead to bloodshed amongst their own kind.
'Find these vile forces and bring me the patches that adorn their armour. I will reward you for ten such patches.'
'Your efforts are heralded, ${PLAYER}. Take this with my thanks. Remember that Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig will recognize you for your efforts in the Ettenmoors should you visit her.'
'I need more soldier's patches before I can bestow a Token of Valour upon you, ${PLAYER}. Keep hunting the Enemy.'
Return soldier's patches to First Marshal Sathryth
Collect soldier's patches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Angmar's Soldiers
First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr is collecting badges taken from Angmar's soldiers.

Soldiers in the service to Angmar may each carry a seal of their station. Search among the enemy for these badges. First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr has promised to reward you for the patches you bring her.
Collected taskmaster's honourifics(${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You there, ${RACE}, what are you doing? I need your assistance.
'Beneath the chieftains of the Ongbûrz are the taskmasters who drive the host into a frenzy and force them to set upon our forces with sadistic glee.
'Seek them out and take their honourifics. Return some of these honourifics to me, and I will see that you are justly rewarded.'

'Your continued efforts fuel the strength that fills the arms and hearts of the Free Peoples. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. Visit Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig to earn greater recognition of your efforts in the Ettenmoors.'
'You need to bring me more of the taskmasters' honourifics to earn you a Token of Valour, ${PLAYER}. Keep hunting the Enemy.'
Return taskmaster's honourifics to First Marshal Sathryth
Collect taskmaster's honourifics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Angmar's Taskmasters
First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr is collecting badges taken from Angmar's taskmasters.

The taskmasters of Angmar can be found among the Enemy in the Ettenmoors.
The taskmasters who drive the Angmarim war-host into a frenzy bear honourifics of their station. Collect these to earn commendation from the Army of the Free Peoples. First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr has promised to reward you for the taskmaster's honourifics you bring her.
Collected a Tyrant's lash (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Pay attention, ${RACE}...I need your services.
'At the head of the war-host of Angmar are the Tyrants who drive all others ahead of them. They are without fear and know only how to bring destruction to the world.
'Should you defeat one of these terrors, return to me with the lash which is the symbol of his command, and you shall be rewarded.'

'With every victory we achieve against the Ongbûrz leaders, we not only claim the land where they stand, but also weaken the war-host of Angmar. Your involvement is a blessing, ${PLAYER}. Deliver this to Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig to earn greater recognition of your efforts in the Ettenmoors.'
'Should you obtain one Tyrant's lash you will earn a Token of Valour, ${PLAYER}. Keep hunting the Enemy.'
Return Tyrant's lash to First Marshal Sathryth
Collect a Tyrant's lash (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Angmar's Tyrants
First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr seeks the honourifics of the true leaders of Angmar's army, the Tyrant's lashes.

Tyrants can be found among the Enemy in the Ettenmoors.
Known by many names, the true leaders of Angmar's army are nothing more than tyrants, and the symbol of their station will earn you favour with the Free Peoples. First Marshal Sathryth at Ost Ringdyr has promised to reward you for the Tyrant's lashes you bring her.
Collected food-sack (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'A moment of thy time ${RACE}, if thou would? I am Pip Diggins, from Hoarhallow. We have a small village on the eastern side of the Hoardale River and have lived here in the place thou call the Ettenmoors for as long as my grandfather's grandfather's....'
'I think thou understand my words. The arrival of these tall folk was providence, ${RACE}, simply providence. We had been set upon by all manner of foul folk and were not well-prepared to defend ourselves.
'We had seen trolls before, but the Wargs, Orcs, and goblins were another story. Since their arrival -- and yours -- our little village has seen a number of raids where they have stolen villagers, pipe-weed, and food! If you are willing to visit the goblin-village of Grothum to recover some of our food. I would be very grateful. Grothum is a good distance north of here near the place your folk named Arador's End.'

'Thou have found it! This is a fine day indeed! A fine day, and I have thee to thank for it, ${PLAYER}. There are many here who have learned thy name!
'Thank thee, thank thee for all thou have done!'

'Thou may also find some of the other creatures in the area with the food sacks, for there is no end to those who thieve us. Still, we know that, though it is stormy now in our part of the world, with the help of our new friends, we shall weather it well.'
Deliver the food-sacks to Emissary Pip Diggins at Ost Ringdyr
Collect food-sacks (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Hoarhallow's Dwindling Food
Emissary Pip Diggins of Hoarhallow told you a tale of woe concerning the destruction wrought on his village by the Snowreap-goblins far to the north-east of Hoarhallow.

The goblin-village of Grothum lies far to the north-east of Hoarhallow.
Emissary Pip Diggins asked you to recover food stolen from Hoarhallow. He directed you to search among the goblin village at Grothum or on the persons of the enemy.

'There is something going on in the mountains, my friend, and I fear what it might signify. Long has the dwarf-city of Helegrod stood empty, abandoned by the dwarves who made it, but cruel folk have come there of late, and I have seen evil Men on the walls.
'I fear the mischief they might do, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps I worry for naught, but this fear has been steadily growing on my mind and I can no longer dismiss it as needless.
'Tell Lord Elrond of my fears, friend. Perhaps he will have some insight that can put them to rest, but I cannot find any good that might come of Helegrod inhabited again.'

'Your news gives me pause, ${PLAYER}, for Anornaneth is not one to lightly give voice to such concerns. If Helegrod is indeed inhabited by creatures of evil, the darkness may be closer to Imladris than we had supposed.'
Stirrings Within Helegrod
Anornaneth has observed an increased level of activity on the walls of Helegrod, the lost dwarf-city in the Misty Mountains, and is worried about what it might signify.
'I hope that my worries are baseless, ${PLAYER}, but I fear that they are not. Go to Lord Elrond in his library, and tell him that Helegrod is inhabited again, and not by dwarves.'
'Some evil stirs within Helegrod. I am sure of it.'
'I fear no good can come of Helegrod inhabited again.'

Lord Elrond is in the library of his house in Rivendell.
Anornaneth has asked you to bring word of her fears concerning Helegrod to Elrond.

'I charge you with seeking the scouts I sent forth to Helegrod. Hear what they have uncovered, ${PLAYER}, and we may better know how to deal with the new threat that lurks within that dark place.
'They will have taken shelter somewhere to the north, within sight of the Bitter Stair that climbs up to the walls of the keep. Ask Sigrun for the rest of Durin's sad tale when you find him, for it concerns him most directly, and he will relate it to you if you wish to hear it.
'Use caution among the snowy slopes and search among the trees in sight of the Bitter Stair to find Sigrun and Greip, my scouts. They have authority to deal with any matters concerning Helegrod.'

'You must be a messenger from Lord Glóin, friend, for no right-minded ${RACE} would climb so close to Helegrod without such an errand, and I tell you truly that evil has come to live there again! Greip and I have seen all the proof we need to know the truth of that!
'Lord Glóin would have me tell you the tale of Durin, fifth of that name? I cannot refuse, though it is a painful story. If he spoke to you of the coming of Thorog, I will tell you then of what happened when Durin learned that the dragon had taken the city.
'A dragon sleeping on the treasures of Helegrod? Durin could not abide this terrible insult! He strapped to his back Mírdanant, a gift out of Eregion to his grandsire, passed from father to son through the long years, and strode with a small company of dwarves to the gates of Helegrod. Durin bellowed a challenge, and Thorog responded in kind! The battle was joined! So fierce was the fighting between dragon and dwarf that the very gates of Helegrod were split asunder!
'After weary days and nights, Durin began at length to tire; all those in his company lay dead or dying, save Bruni who was called Yellowbeard in later years, whose wounds were too severe for him to continue. Still mighty Thorog fought on, refusing to surrender the treasures of Helegrod to their rightful masters. Thorog prepared a white-hot jet of flame with which to roast Durin, whom he judged to be near death, but too late he realized his error. Too late! For lo! Durin swung Mírdanant with all that remained of his strength, and there ended Thorog's cruel reign.
'But Durin would not live to see victory, for Thorog's final gout of flame proved too strong for Durin's stout shield, and he was ended. Mírdanant was lost with Durin; it remains to this day buried in the neck of dead Thorog.
'Woe upon the dwarves! The Elves of Eregion had spoken words of protection upon the forging of the axe: \qDarkness shall not fall upon Hadhodrond while the line of Durin bears Mírdanant in friendship with the Gwaith-i-Mírdain,\q but those words were proved false with the death of Durin!
'I trace my lineage through many fathers to Bruni, Yellowbeard that was, the only survivor of the battle of Helegrod. That he did not die a hero's death before the gates was his lifelong shame, and it is a mark that all his descendants have borne. I bear it too, and have taken onto myself the duty of seeing that the story is not forgotten: not the treachery of the Gwaith-i-Mírdain, not the cruelty of Thorog, and certainly not the last valiant deeds of fifth Durin in defence of his people.
'Evil has crept back into Helegrod, ${PLAYER}, and we will need the help of many folk if we are to combat it. Speak with Greip and myself to learn what must be done!'
In Sight of the Bitter Stair

Glóin related to you a small portion of the history of Helegrod and asked you to speak with the scouts he sent forth to watch the Bitter Stair for signs of the threat growing now behind the walls of Helegrod.

'We have seen evil things behind the walls of Helegrod. The city is once again occupied, though not by dwarves.
'Sigrun will relate to you the tale of that place, and then we must decide what can be done about the new evils within Helegrod.'

'Sigrun will tell you the tale of fifth Durin, for it affects him most directly, though it happened so long ago. You will find him and his brother Greip among the trees in sight of the Bitter Stair, far to the north, near to Helegrod.'
'The tale of Durin is a sad one, ending as it does in both victory and defeat.'
'Sigrun has long borne the mark of Bruni Yellowbeard's cowardice at Helegrod.'
'After the defeat of Thorog, dwarves repaired the gates, carving on them a record of the battle.'
'Dwarves tried to reclaim Helegrod after the death of Thorog, but it was not meant to be.'

The dwarves Sigrun and Greip were sent north of Glóin's camp to scout Helegrod and have likely established a small camp among the trees in sight of the Bitter Stair.
Glóin has sent you to speak with the scouts he dispatched to watch the Bitter Stair that climbs to the gates of Helegrod, far to the north of his camp.

'Glóin and a company of dwarves from the Lonely Mountain have established a camp to the north, among the snows of the mountains. Tell him what you have told me, and I will devise some plan by which we can prepare to face whatever evil has come to Helegrod.
'Your news fills me with forboding, ${PLAYER}, for the tale of that place is a sad one, as hostile as the mountains in winter. Durin, the fifth to bear that name, came to a grim end within the walls of that keep, despite words out of Eregion concerning the axe he bore: \qDarkness shall not fall upon Hadhodrond while the line of Durin bears Mírdanant in friendship with the Gwaith-i-Mírdain.\q
'Perhaps the strength of those words had waned during the many years since Mírdanant was gifted? I do not know. Glóin may tell some of the tale to you, if that is his mind. Go now with haste. I do not know how much time we may have to counter this threat. Helegrond inhabited again is a troubling matter.'

'It was good of Master Elrond to send you to me, ${PLAYER}, though the shadow growing within Helegrod is not news to my company. Indeed, I sent two of our number northward to scout the base of the Bitter Stair that wends up to the gates. They will see what is happening in Helegrod.
'Elrond spoke to you of the fifth Durin? It is true that he came to the end of his days in Helegrod, once-great city of my people. The dragon Thorog coveted the riches that lay within and assaulted the city, slaying dwarves beyond count. Durin took up Mírdanant, the axe given to his grandsire by the Elves of Eregion, and sought to defeat Thorog in battle. Words had been spoken of the axe at the time of its making, words that were thought to ensure the safety and power of its bearer. The words were false, for Durin died in battle with Thorog at the gates of Helegrod.
'That song is a sad one, and I find I am loathe to relate it now to you.'
The Deeds of Durin
Lord Elrond believes the dwarf Glóin should be warned of the evil that might hide within Helegrod, not far to the north of his camp in the Misty Mountains.

'Glóin may not wish to share with you the tale of Durin who met his end in Helegrod, but he must be told that evil stirs again within that place. Find him at his camp north of Rivendell, among the snows of the Misty Mountains.'
'Durin came to the end of his days within Helegrod. The words concerning Mírdanant were false.'
'The Elves of Eregion spoke falsely of Mírdanant, for it did not protect its master or his people.'
'The Elves of Eregion gave Mírdanant to Durin's grandsire and spoke words of friendship upon its making.'
'The dwarves believe the words spoken at the making of Mírdanant were false, but I do not believe it is so.'

Glóin is at his camp in the Misty Mountains, north of Rivendell.
Lord Elrond asked you to warn Glóin of the threat rumoured to be growing within the walls of Helegrod.
Collected Helegrod barter-stick (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Storvâgûn seized control of the cliffs above the old dwarf-city, and with riches from robed Men, he bought the loyalty of many giants!
'Some giants that were my friends, but no more! They are traitors now, slaves to the robed Men who pay Storvâgûn. They do not deserve to be called giants!
'If you have brave friends, go to the old dwarf-city and take away the riches Storvâgûn bribed the giants with! Giants record wealth on notched barter-sticks...take them away! Giants sold their loyalty to Storvâgûn and the robed Men...they do not deserve to keep them! I will burn the sticks when you bring them.'

'Barter-sticks record the weakness of the giants. I will destroy them, and they will not trouble the giants anymore. The robed Men will not able to buy the loyalty of giants while Arifael lives!
'Thank you, tiny ${RACE}. You are good friend to Arifael and to all giants, though they do not know it, maybe.'

'The giants that serve Storvâgûn and his new masters are still on the cliffs above the old dwarf-city! Take away the notched barter-sticks they were paid with and bring them to me so I can burn the bad riches.
'No one will trouble the giants anymore once they are gone.'
Bring Helegrod barter-sticks to Arifael
Raid: Giants in Service of Angmar
Arifael has told you of the giants that now follow treacherous Storvâgûn, who has claimed the cliffs above Helegrod for his own.
'Arifael likes you. You are a good ${RACE}.'
'Giants will not be bought by the robed Men...not while Arifael lives!'

Giants in the service of Storvâgûn and his new masters can be found on the cliffs above Helegrod. Arifael is on Amon Nendir, southwest of Rivendell.
Arifael has asked you to take the notched barter-sticks on which the giants recorded the wealth paid to them by robed Men of Angmar away from them. When you bring him enough of the barter-sticks, he will burn them.

'Helegrod's pride has always been its mighty halls, stretching as they do for many miles into the mountains, but Greip and I have discovered that someone -- something, I should say -- has been adding to their expanse.
'As we explored near to the walls of Helegrod, the snow gave way and Greip fell into an icy cavern, a great hollow space beneath the mountains. I returned to our camp to retrieve enough rope to pull him back to the surface. I moved with all the haste I could manage, but in the few moments I was gone, Greip heard the foul language of spiders and knew the truth of where he had fallen. When I pulled him back to the surface, he related to me his brief adventure in the dark, a story of webs and evil voices.
'An evil brood of spiders have taken root in the caverns beneath Helegrod, ${PLAYER}, and the name of their queen is fell: \qZaudru,\q she is called, and I know one who has encountered her before. Look for Atli Spider-bane in Bree-land, in the town of Archet, for he will be most interested to hear of the spider-plague that festers beneath Helegrod.'

'You have come to me by long and weary roads, ${PLAYER}. What has brought you here with such urgency? I see from your face that it can be no small matter.
'What is this? I had not thought to hear the name \qZaudru\q again in my lifetime, ${PLAYER}. She is a cruel and wretched queen among her kind, and we have been face-to-face only once, though the memory is evil. She cannot be allowed to haunt the caverns beneath Helegrod, friend ${RACE}, for she will in the span of timeless years come forth with her brood to cover all of Middle-earth with her spawn.
'If you are willing to take up arms against this wretched foe, tell me so. If not, leave my sight a coward.'
Ancient Foes of the Spider-bane
Glóin's scouts have learned that a venomous brood of spiders and their wretched queen lurk now beneath Helegrod.

'The strangest thing happened, ${PLAYER}. I returned to the place where Greip fell through the snow -- he refused to go himself, but I wanted to see if there was anything else to see -- and the hole is gone, sealed by a thick mat of spider-webs.
'These spiders must not be underestimated, ${PLAYER}. They learned of our intrusion and resented it; they will not permit another.'

'I fell a good distance into the cavern, ${PLAYER}, and my fall was broken by a sheet of ice -- I am fortunate that it was so thick! The spiders of that place....
'I really do not want to talk about it. I am sorry.'
'Greip does not willingly speak about his adventure in the spider-caves.'
'Atli Spider-bane once encountered wretched Zaudru, and the meeting was nearly his last.'
'The spiders sealed off the hole into which I fell. I am grateful, for I wouldn't want it to happen again!'
'I am fortunate that Zaudru was not nearby when I fell into her cave, or I would not be here today!'

Atli Spider-bane is in the town of Archet, in Bree-land, far to the west of the Misty Mountains.
Sigrun and Greip learned that an evil plague of spiders has taken root in caverns beneath Helegrod, and their fell queen is known to Atli Spider-bane.

'All who remember the story of mighty Durin and fierce Thorog know of Helegrod, ${PLAYER}, but I did not think to hear its name spoken aloud in my time. Though dwarves repaired the gates and tried to reclaim it after the passage of the dragon, it was not meant to be, and my father and his father before him assumed Helegrod would always stand empty.
'But word now comes to my ears of weaving beneath the city, weaving and the clicking of many legs. The Shadow-brood spiders that infest the caverns beneath Helegrod might stay there for years...any spider-hunter knows that the creatures prefer the darkness beneath the mountains to the light of the sun. But if the wretched creature that birthed these monstrosities turns her eyes towards the exit of her cave, towards the snow-covered slopes of the Misty Mountains....
'We cannot let this happen, ${PLAYER}. Despite the danger, you must descend into the caverns beneath Helegrod and defeat as many of the Shadow-brood as you can. Bring to me their venom, for the venom of one brood is often poisonous to others, and I might be able to make use of it against other of the vile creatures. Only mature spiders are likely to have the potent venom I require, and even then, it will be difficult to slay the spiders that carry it without spilling it.'

'You have done very well! This venom will be a valuable asset in my war against any spider that does not belong to the brood of Zaudru.
'It need not be said, perhaps, but you and your allies remain my greatest weapon against the brood of Zaudru herself, ${PLAYER}. I await word of your further triumphs over the wretched creature and her terrible spawn.'

'The caverns beneath Helegrod seem to be overrun with Shadow-brood spiders, the spawn of vile Zaudru. If you can collect their potent venom, I may be able to turn it against other broods of spiders.
'Go with valour, ${PLAYER}!'
Bring Helegrod Shadow-brood venom to Atli Spider-bane
Raid: An Evil Place, Crawling With Spiders
Atli Spider-bane has asked you to collect the venom of the Shadow-brood spiders that dwell in the caverns beneath Helegrod.
'The venom of the Shadow-brood is particularly potent and must be handled with caution.'
'Zaudru is the most fearsome beast I have encountered, and her brood is numberless.'

The Shadow-brood spiders in the caverns beneath Helegrod possess the venom Atli Spider-bane is seeking. Atli is in the town of Archet, in Bree-land.
Atli Spider-bane has asked you to collect venom from the Shadow-brood of Helegrod.
Collected Zaudru's crimson mandible

'The city of Helegrod has stood empty for long years, ${PLAYER}, but if wretched Zaudru has chosen as her lair the caverns beneath it, it will not remain so for long. Corcur, Angmarim, giant, or drake will not be able to stand against her, though each of them may believe Zaudru to be an ally. When her brood has grown to sufficient size, she will come forth, and woe to any who stand before her! Helegrod will have a new queen!
'Long years ago, I beheld Zaudru in all her bloated majesty, and it is a sight that will never fully leave my mind. My father and brothers and I had begun mining a decent vein when all about there came a great shaking. Rocks fell from above, and dust filled the air. We ran for the surface, but she was upon us before we had gone fifteen paces. The sound of her evil voice still fills me with dread, though I could not make out many of the words she spoke, save one: \qZaudru\q she said, over and over, \qZaudru!\q I stumbled into the sunlight, and as I turned back to the entrance of the mine, I saw her great, bloated mass moving through the dust, saw the glint of her small and angry eyes. Then the roof gave way and the entrance collapsed, sealing Zaudru behind a wall of stone. It was all that saved me from her.
'Of a dozen dwarves, only I and two of my brothers escaped her clutches that day. I swore vengeance upon Zaudru and took to hunting any of her kind that crossed my path. She must have followed secret paths through the stone, mile after mile, until she came at last to Helegrod. End her, ${PLAYER}. End her and bring me her crimson mandible. She had only one, but it will be the proof of my vengeance.'

'I have no words, ${PLAYER}. That Zaudru no longer lives brings me such joy as I cannot relate to you.
'I am forever at your service and your family's. Walk with honour, my friend, for you have slain Zaudru, most wretched of the spiders that creep beneath the mountains.'
'Zaudru is still alive, ${PLAYER}, and many good dwarves are dead. Journey to the caverns beneath Helegrod and make things right. I charge you with carrying out my vengeance.'
Bring Zaudru's crimson mandible to Atli Spider-bane
Raid: A New Queen for Deepest Helegrod
Atli Spider-bane has, at long last, learned the location of his greatest foe, the cause of his deep hatred for the foul creatures.
'I am forever at your service, ${PLAYER}.'
'My father and brothers smile upon you, my friend, for Zaudru is no more.'

Zaudru has made her lair in the caverns beneath the old dwarf-city of Helegrod, in the Misty Mountains. Atli Spider-bane is in the town of Archet, in Bree-land.
Atli Spider-bane has told you the story of his encounter with Zaudru long years ago and has charged you with carrying out his vengeance.

'If the caverns beneath Helegrod are now home to wretched Zaudru, as it seems they must be, every day that passes must see the increase of her spawn. The hatchlings of Zaudru possess an unusually ravenous appetite, even for spiders, and will feast on anything that stumbles near. They have need of great amounts of flesh and blood if they are to grow to adult size.
'We must stop them before they do, ${PLAYER}, for Zaudru gives to her brood the strength and toughness that she herself possesses. Much easier to slay them as hatchlings, I tell you truly!
'The caverns beneath Helegrod are almost certainly riddled with cracks and crevices within which Zaudru's Shadow-brood hatchlings vie for dominance. Approach these holes and slay as many of the creatures as emerge into the light.'

'You have emerged from the caverns beneath Helegrod, ${PLAYER}, and I am happy to see it!
'You have done well to slay the hatchlings you encountered, for the creatures are numerous beyond count and bear great hatred for anything that moves beneath the sun and moon! The spawn of Zaudru are hateful.'
Raid: Zaudru's Brood
Atli Spider-bane has told you of the wretched spider Zaudru and the army of spiders that are surely hatching beneath Helegrod every day.

'The caverns beneath Helegrod are riddled with cracks and crevices surely filled with the spawn of wretched Zaudru, Shadow-brood hatchlings waiting to emerge into the light to feed. End them, ${PLAYER}.'
'You have done well to combat Zaudru's brood, ${PLAYER}!'
'I count you among the greatest spider-hunters I have met, friend.'

The caverns beneath Helegrod are riddled with cracks and crevices, home to Zaudru's hatchlings.
Atli Spider-bane has asked you to slay as many Shadow-brood hatchlings as you can find beneath Helegrod.

Atli Spider-bane is in the town of Archet, in Bree-land.
Atli Spider-bane is waiting to hear that you have dealt a blow to the Shadow-brood hatchlings spawned by wretched Zaudru beneath Helegrod.

'Lord Glóin sent us to the Bitter Stair to scout Helegrod, for he thought some evil had come back to live there, but I do not think he suspected things to be this grave. The dragon Thorog reborn? No dwarf could have imagined such a terror!
'You must return to Elrond of Rivendell and tell him of the danger that lurks now on his very doorstep. His home may be hidden from prying eyes due to some Elf-craft, but few things are safe from dragon-fire, as the grandsires of the Men of Dale could tell you!
'Go now with haste, ${PLAYER}! Greip and I will continue our vigil here, and the Elves of Rivendell will need time to prepare some plan of their own.'

'You have returned, ${PLAYER}, and your news is as I expected, for I sent some scouts of my own to investigate while you were away. Armed with this knowledge, we may now plan not only our defence, but our offence as well.
'The evil that hides behind the walls of Helegrod must be swept away. You must help both Elves and dwarves accomplish this charge, ${PLAYER}.'
The Extent of the Threat
Sigrun and Greip learned that the evil that has taken Helegrod is much worse than Glóin had suspected.
'Elrond must be told what is happening in Helegrod, ${PLAYER}. Tell him that the situation is more grave than we thought!'

Elrond is in his library in Rivendell.
Sigrun has asked you to return to Elrond with news of the extent of the threat lurking now within Helegrod.

'The evils we have spied within the walls of Helegrod are numerous and hateful, ${PLAYER}: cruel Men of the Corcur and of Angmar, bloated and filth-covered spiders, crawling worms and armoured drakes, monstrous and mean-tempered giants, and worst of all, Thorog alive once again, his malice undiminished by the passage of the years!
'Long have I and my fathers before me, in line unbroken back to Bruni, Yellowbeard that was, held in our hearts enmity for the Elves of Eregion. \qDarkness shall not fall upon Hadhodrond while the line of Durin bears Mírdanant in friendship with the Gwaith-i-Mírdain?\q False words, used to lull Durin into complacency!
'If we are to see Helegrod returned out of the darkness, I think the time has come to set aside these ancient squabbles. The old friendships must be remembered. While Lord Glóin met with Elrond of Rivendell, some time ago, Greip and I were engaged in conversation with an Elf named Gonediad, who seemed learned in the lore of Eregion. Perhaps he can illuminate the matter of Thorog returned to life. Keep to yourself the doubts I have expressed concerning the Elves of Eregion; it will be some time before the old enmities can be fully washed away. Look for Gonediad in Rivendell.'

'You have come with messages from the dwarves? I do remember the two of which you speak, for one of them seemed rather uncomfortable when I spoke to him of my studies of the Elves of Eregion. Sigrun, he was called? Yes, that is he. He seemed a stout fellow, but behind his beard I sensed the resentment of his people. Most of the dwarves I have met are more adept at hiding it; he was not.
'I suspect the gifting of Mírdanant is the root of this resentment, though it should not be. If my studies of Eregion have taught me nothing else, they have taught me this: the gifts of the Gwaith-i-Mírdain were always made true, and with good intent, though they were as prone to misuse and pretty words as were any good people that walked in those days.'
Old Friendships
With some trepidation, Sigrun has decided that he must cast aside his old enmities if the evil within Helegrod is to be cast out.
'Gonediad is sure to be somewhere among the trees of Rivendell, ${PLAYER}. He is learned in the lore of Eregion, and may know something that can aid us in the defeat of Thorog.'
'Gonediad seemed a decent Elf. His studies will help us cleanse Helegrod.'
'Words have power, of a sort. Never misuse them, or you will suffer the consequences.'
'Durin, the third of that name, was given Mírdanant as a sign of friendship.'
'Many beautiful things were forged in Eregion before it fell.'

Gonediad is somewhere in Rivendell.
Sigrun has expressed his doubts about the gifting of Mírdanant to Durin by the Elves of Eregion, but has decided such old enmities must be cast aside if the new evils lurking within Helegrod are to be defeated. He has asked you to speak with Gonediad, learned in the lore of Eregion, about the return of the dragon Thorog.

'The keep of Helegrod has stood empty for years beyond count, ${PLAYER}, but now it has become home to worm and drake, a vile warren filled with many clutches of eggs and guarded by the watchful eyes of the great beasts.
'Few of the Corcur or Angmarim that we have spied from afar seem willing to brave the stronghold. Perhaps the fire-breath of the creatures keeps the Men at bay, or they are under some command not to disturb the beasts. One of the Angmarim, a man of great importance, seems to have no fear of the worms or drakes and passes often through the doors of the keep. It is curious.
'But we do not have the time to muse on such things! Ormulf Worm-hunter, a dwarf of Othrikar on the North Downs, should be told of the infestation of worms and drakes that lurk now within the keep of Helegrod. He will know how best to fight the creatures. Go with haste, and leave the mystery of the Angmarim worm-friend to Greip and myself!'

'Worms within Helegrod? Sigrun was right to send you to me, ${PLAYER}, for no one knows as much about fighting the fell creatures as I do!
'And I am worried about this Man of Angmar you mentioned. If he can pass safely among drakes and worms, he may hold a power far greater than anything I have yet faced. But the situation here on the Downs needs all my attention, and I cannot travel all the way to Helegrod! How I wish it were not so, but I gave my word that I would not abandon my post here, and a dwarf's word is stronger even than mithril bonds!
'I hope no ill comes of it, but there is nothing I can do. I will put it out of my mind. If you are willing to combat the threat of worms and drakes within Helegrod on my behalf, give me your word you will do so, and will not cower before such mysterious power as this Man seems to wield. If you are not prepared for such danger, I will waste no more of my breath upon you!'
The Worm-hunter's Lament
Sigrun told you of Ormulf Worm-hunter, a dwarf at Othrikar renowned for his brave deeds against the worms and drakes that stalk the crevices of the North Downs.
'Ormulf Worm-hunter is at Othrikar on the North Downs, ${PLAYER}. He will know what to do about the worms and drakes that slither now within Helegrod's inner keep!'
'Ormulf Worm-hunter is a good dwarf, brave and loyal, if a bit too bold.'
'I do not know what power this mysterious Angmarim possesses that he may walk unharmed among worms and drakes.'
'Ormulf Worm-hunter and I once hunted the worms of Dol Dinen. He is stout-hearted.'
'The central keep of Helegrod is full of worms and drakes, and therefore danger.'

Ormulf Worm-hunter is at Othrikar, far to the west in the north-central North Downs.
Sigrun has seen from afar that the keep of Helegrod appears to be crawling with worms and drakes and has asked you to consult with Ormulf Worm-hunter about what must be done.

'I know not how it has happened, ${PLAYER}, but Thorog has been returned to life through some foul craft! Sigrun and I have seen him, with our own eyes, perched atop the walls of Helegrod like an evil memory given hateful shape.
'So long as the beast lives, the honour of the dwarves is tarnished; both Durin and Mírdanant are lost and cannot rid us of this scourge.
'I do not know if you have allies to rival Durin's great company of old, but it will take many stout hearts to best evil Thorog. If he can be drawn from his perch atop Helegrod, you must do what you can to defeat him, or all the lands will be threatened.'

'We heard from here mighty Thorog's tumult and thought you had surely perished, ${PLAYER}, but my heart rejoices to see you safe! And not just safe, but triumphant!
'You have done what only Durin has done before in all the ages, and I feel certain that Thorog's sleep will now be forever; his tale of cruelty has been ended, and the honour of the dwarves restored!
'Our thanks can never equal the mighty deed you have performed this day, ${PLAYER}, but know that we will have no end of trying! Thorog has been slain! Rejoice, for ${PLAYER} has triumphed!'
Raid: Thorog Defeated
Greip and Sigrun have seen the unthinkable: the great dragon Thorog has returned to life and makes his perch once more upon the walls of Helegrod.

'Thorog is no ordinary foe, ${PLAYER}. I will understand if you shrink from this task. If your resolve is strong and your allies loyal, you will find him perched atop the walls of Helegrod. Draw him into battle, if you dare!'
'We are well-met, ${PLAYER}, Thorog-bane!'
'You have returned triumphant out of Helegrod, den no longer of fearsome Thorog!'
'I am pleased beyond words that you have defeated Thorog!'
'Thanks to your efforts, Helegrod will no longer be the home of that vile creature!'
'Thorog is no more! Durin has been avenged once again!'
'I am certain Thorog will no longer trouble the counsels of the Wise and the Great. You have done well!'
'Some foul craft returned Thorog to life, as should not have been. You have done well to end him.'
'The ways of dragons are unknown to us, for they are cruel and ill-tempered.'

The dragon Thorog has been seen atop the walls of Helegrod, in the Misty Mountains.
Greip and Sigrun have seen Thorog from their small camp north of the source of the Bruinen and have charged you with his defeat.

Greip is at the small camp he has established with his ally Sigrun, southwest of the Bitter Stair, in the Misty Mountains.
You have overcome all odds and slain the great dragon-wight Thorog, animated by fell spirits and the spirit of the Gaunt-lord Drugoth.
