'It happened like this: as one of the world's greatest lore-masters, I happened to be doing some research on the ruins of Tollobel. It seems the last owner was a great warrior, and he took a number of trophies from the Angmarim at the Battle of Fornost. These trophies included a pair of eggs....
'Such little eggs, too! Well, naturally, it was a challenge to see if they could be quickened after all these generations. You can imagine my pride when they hatched! Cute little salamanders, tiny little efts, they seemed. Truly learned lore-masters call them \qefts,\q you know, and I encourage you to do the same! But these little efts just would not stop growing! And soon they began to grow hostile, and after that came the fire....
'The things breed so fast! I managed to pen the original dam and sire in a cellar in the ruins here. Since then, well, I've been trapped...I mean, I've been studying them. Yes! But now you've come. You can kill them! You're a hero, aren't you? Right! Here, take this key! Slay the dam and sire -- the other salamanders breed much more slowly. Now that you know the terrible secret of the salamanders, it's up to you to stop them! I truly recommend you do not go it alone...and no, do not look at me!'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}! I had begun to fear for your safety. What have you learned?
'Indeed? An amazing story. That mad old man. It is a pity we are unable to patrol these lands better, or we should never have permitted him to go near those ruins.
'It may be that these salamanders will never be fully driven from the area now, but at least we know their origin. If what Rumming said is true, it also may be that your actions have slowed their spread. I thank you too for that.'

'Oh! You killed them! Poor things! I mean, well done! Well done indeed. At last I can leave this accursed place. I mean, well, perhaps there is a bit more to study here after all.
'Anyway, you've done a great deed here and helped the pursuit of knowledge immensely. Immensely, I say! Of course, nothing I couldn't have handled myself. I was just letting you learn a little for yourself.
'Go talk to the Rangers on the island far to the east and tell them that I am very displeased with their handling of the salamander problem. A great lore-master can only do so much, and at some point the Rangers should have stepped in! Now give me back my key.'
'Where's my key?'
Bring Cellar Key to Humfrey Rumming
The Terrible Secret of the Salamanders
Now that you have defeated Humfrey Rumming in his riddle-contest, he may at last be willing to tell you the terrible secret of the salamanders.

'Well, what are you waiting for? Get to it! Kill those two salamanders! Scholarship requires it!
'Use the key I gave you to unlock the Tollobel cellar-door. Oh! And, er, bring friends. The two original salamanders are vicious creatures and have no respect for authority.'

'You return to the Rangers and tell them that Humfrey Rumming is very displeased with their treatment of the salamander problem! They should have done something earlier, and not left it all to Humfrey Rumming, great lore-master though he is!'
'I have the problem of the salamanders perfectly under control!'
'No trouble with salamanders while Humfrey Rumming is on patrol!'
'You did well to solve the mystery of the salamanders.'
'Where did this Humfrey Rumming come from, I wonder?'

The two original salamanders can be found in the cellar of Tollobel, on Tyl Ruinen.
Humfrey Rumming confided in you that he was the one responsible for the plague of salamanders on Tyl Ruinen and gave you the key to the cellar where he trapped the two original creatures. He asked you to slay the two originals to help reduce their numbers.

Humfrey Rumming is by the ruins of Tollobel on Tyl Ruinen.
Humfrey Rumming is waiting to hear of your victory over the two original salamanders he brought to Tyl Ruinen.

Calatherdir is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, east of Tyl Ruinen.
Having learned the origin of the salamanders and helped to slow their proliferation, you should return to Calatherdir to tell him the tale of your deeds.

'Calenglad is a wise Ranger who has seen many summers, and I trust his judgement as my own. If he is not convinced of your honesty, I remain unconvinced as well.
'North of Tinnudir, in Tyrn Fornech, an ancient stone overlook stands watch atop one of the tallest hills. Jabe Grimshaw, leader to one of the robber-bands that has caused us so much trouble, plans his band's activities from its heights.
'If you seek to prove yourself to me and Calenglad, you will put an end to Jabe Grimshaw. You will find Barad Rath, the flat stone platform atop the tall hills of Tyrn Fornech, northeast of Tinnudir and north of Tham Ornen. You will find Jabe there as well.'

'Grimshaw is no more? This is excellent news, ${PLAYER}, and I begin to believe your tale.
'It is not yet enough, I am afraid, but perhaps you are telling the truth. If you succeed at my next errand I will be free of doubt!'
They Spy from the Heights
Naethmunn has asked you to defeat Jabe Grimshaw, a leader among the tomb-robbers who often plans their activities from high atop Barad Rath, an overlook in Tyrn Fornech.
'Barad Rath is atop one of the tallest hills of Tyrn Fornech, northeast of Tinnudir and north of Tham Ornen. You will find Jabe Grimshaw there, planning the activities of his robber-gang.'
'Jabe Grimshaw is no more, and I feel the winds begin to change in our favour.'
'The tomb-robbers cannot hold out forever. They will soon be defeated.'

Jabe Grimshaw plans his band's attacks from atop Barad Rath, a flat stone overlook atop the tall hills of Tyrn Fornech, north-east of Tinnudir and north of Tham Ornen.
Ranger Naethmunn has asked you to find and defeat Jabe Grimshaw, leader of a band of tomb-robbers that has plagued the Rangers of Evendim for a long time.

Naethmunn is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim, south-west of Barad Rath.
You should report your victory over Jabe Grimshaw to Naethmunn.

'Gwindeth has agreed to lower the flood-waters in the tomb of Elendil? I am filled with amazement, ${PLAYER}, that you were able to accomplish such a wonder! I do not know what you will find in the freshly-unflooded portion of the tomb -- it might be best to bring allies with you.
'I fear that the tomb-robbers that prowl Evendim will take advantage of Gwindeth's decision; long have the waters prevented them from gaining access to the lowest levels of Elendil's tomb. Now that this barrier will be gone, the robbers will rush to seize what treasures they may. One such band is led by Idella Crypt-breaker, a notorious robber, and she will not remain idle with the promise of riches unclaimed.
'Gather allies and speak to me when you are ready to journey to the tomb, and I will show you inside. Confront Idella if you find her within the tomb and reclaim the Silithar for Lord Aragorn!'

'You have emerged from the darkness, ${PLAYER}, and have truly made an old man glad to see this happy day. The light of Narsil shall be kindled once again!
'Gwindeth appeared shortly before your return and gave to me the Silithar; to see such a wonder return from out of the mists of history fills me with amazement!'
Talk to Calenglad and travel to the tomb of Elendil
The Tomb of Elendil
Gwindeth has agreed to lower the flood-waters in the tomb of Elendil so that you can recover the Silithar for Aragorn.

'Are you ready to journey to the tomb of Elendil, ${PLAYER}? I hope you have gathered allies, for Idella Crypt-breaker is sure to be making her way into the deepest chambers with the rest of her band!'
'You did well in the watery half-light of the tomb of great Elendil, ${PLAYER}. I am pleased to know you, and the Lord of the Dúnedain is fortunate indeed to have such a friend!'
'You fought bravely against Nornagol, ${PLAYER}.'
'Aragorn, son of Arathorn, is fortunate to have such friends as you.'
'I did not think the Silithar would emerge again into the light.'
'Idella Crypt-breaker has paid for her villainy.'

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Calenglad is waiting to speak with you about travelling to the tomb of Elendil to reclaim the Silithar for Aragorn.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Calenglad is waiting for you to speak with him about your adventures in the tomb of Elendil.

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! You have done well to come this far into darkness, but the Silithar is no longer here!
'Listen well, for I will tell you where now it lies!'

'You have done well to defeat Nornagol, ${PLAYER}! I have taken the Silithar and will deliver it to Calenglad. Return now to him with the tale of your adventure!
'I will show you the way by hidden paths back to the surface.'
'Let us leave this place, ${PLAYER}. The Silithar must come safely to the surface, and I would speak with Calenglad before I return to my home.'
Find the Silithar
Instance: The Tomb of Elendil
You have journeyed into the Tomb of Elendil in search of the Silithar needed to reforge Narsil.

Idella Crypt-breaker is somewhere within the depths of the tomb of Elendil.
Calenglad was right -- Idella Crypt-breaker's gang of tomb-robbers have taken advantage of the newly-lowered waters to plumb the depths of the tomb for treasure. She must be stopped.

Gwindeth has come to the Tomb of Elendil, and is waiting to speak with you in its deepest chamber.
You have dispatched Idella Crypt-breaker, but there is no sign of the silithar.

The Silithar is somewhere in the caverns beneath the tomb of Elendil.
You did not find the Silithar in the final chamber of the tomb of Elendil -- it must have been carried somewhere by the retreating waters.

Gwindeth is now in the cave beneath the tomb of Elendil.
You have recovered the Silithar, and Gwindeth waits to speak with you.
You delivered the chest of relics to Astiul
You have been seen by an unfriendly man

'Life is hard in Tyrn Fornech, ${PLAYER}, and some of the folk who live here at Ost Forod have begun dealing with the robbers in order to better their fortunes. It pains me to say this, but even now in Ost Forod you can find relics stolen from Annúminas.
'We should return these relics to the Rangers of Tinnudir, ${PLAYER} -- it's the right thing to do! You can find a chest full of stolen artifacts among the tents on the highest level of Ost Forod, north of here. Please understand that the folk of Ost Forod who trade with the robbers are not bad people; their desperation makes them unfriendly and more willing to compromise their values, but I do not want you to hurt them.
'Carry the chest to the Ranger Astiul in Tinnudir, to the southwest, and avoid the unfriendly men of Ost Forod! They will find other means of sustaining themselves if this easy, but reprehensible, road is closed to them. Be sure to speak with Astiul when you have delivered the chest.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. I trust that you have delivered the chest of stolen relics to Astiul? Excellent.
'But enough dilly-dallying! I have great news!'

'Robin sent you to bring that chest of stolen relics, then? Very good, very good! He is an old man and can be crotchety at times, but his heart is in the right place. He has long been a good friend to the Dúnedain.
'Return to him with my thanks, and I will see about returning these artifacts to their proper places.'
Collect Chest of Relics
Avoid being seen by unfriendly men
Unfriendly Eyes in Ost Forod
Robin Dunkley is concerned by the presence of relics stolen from Annúminas in Ost Forod and wants you to return them to their rightful caretakers, the Rangers of Tinnudir.

'The chest of stolen relics is north of here, among the tents on the highest level of Ost Forod. Carry it to Astiul in Tinnudir, to the southwest, but avoid the gaze of the unfriendly Men of Ost Forod! They are not evil, and I would not have you hurt them, so if they see you the game will be up!
'Be sure to speak with Astiul when you have delivered the chest.'
'You didn't speak to Astiul after delivering the chest of stolen relics? Please go talk to him! I want him to know where from where the chest came!'

'Robin Dunkley lives in Ost Forod, the remains of the great fortress that once watched the northern road. His people dwell there and maintain the watch, though some have turned to villainy, dealing and trading with the tomb-robbers of Evendim.
'Robin has always been a good friend to the Dúnedain, and you should continue to render him your aid. It is what Calenglad wants for you.'
'I haven't known Astiul for very long, but he is a solid fellow.'
'Calenglad and I go way back. I wonder how old he is?'

The chest of stolen relics is among the tents on the highest level of Ost Forod, north of Robin Dunkley.
Robin Dunkley has asked you to find a chest of stolen relics and carry it to Ranger Astiul in Tinnudir, avoiding the eyes of the unfriendly Men of Ost Forod.

Astiul is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Robin Dunkley asked you to speak with Astiul after delivering the chest of stolen relics.

Robin Dunkley is in Ost Forod, north-east of Tinnudir.
Ranger Astiul has asked you to return to Robin Dunkley with his thanks for the delivery of the stolen relics.

'Calenglad wants you to return to him at once so he may tell you of his meeting with the Blue Lady. Do not delay, ${PLAYER}!
'You have been a great help to me and have done much good for the people of Ost Forod. I hope to see you again, but for now you should return to Tinnudir and speak with Calenglad!'

'I am glad to see you again, ${PLAYER}, and to know that you have not been idle while I journeyed. Robin spoke of the aid you rendered, and I believe that the people of Ost Forod are better for your service.
'I have spoken with Gwindeth about acquiring the Silithar for Aragorn, but she is not satisfied with what I have told her of you. She wants to meet you herself.'
Word from Calenglad
Calenglad sent word to Robin Dunkley that he has returned from his journey to meet with Gwindeth and wants to speak with you.
'What are you waiting for, ${PLAYER}? Calenglad waits for you at Tinnudir, to the south-west!'
'The Blue Lady of Nenuial is as changeable as the surface of the lake itself.'
'Gwindeth has lived by Lake Nenuial for years uncounted.'

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, south-west of Ost Forod, in Evendim.
The Ranger Calenglad has sent word that he wishes to speak with you.

'Many years have passed since I first beheld Gwindeth, the Blue Lady of Nenuial, but on that day I resolved to do anything in my power to preserve her peace and the safety of the lake she loved. My duties here are twofold, oaths folding in on oaths, for I swore to Aragorn in his youth the vow I swore to his father: to uphold the line of Elendil using all of my strength.
'The protection of Gwindeth and Lake Nenuial also serves this oath, for Gwindeth is the protector of the Silithar. Long has she maintained the flood that keeps the stone safe from robbers and plunderers. True-hearted she is, but slow to trust -- she shares that in common with the Dúnedain. I must speak with her alone, but the work of keeping Evendim safe will not stand for the delay caused by my journey to her home.
'I would have you travel northeast to Ost Forod in Tyrn Fornech and offer your aid to a friend of the Rangers, Robin Dunkley. He is our ally against those who would plunder Annúminas. I will send word to Robin when I have returned from my meeting with Gwindeth.'

'You've come from Calenglad? I am very glad to hear it, for friends of the Rangers are fewer now than they were of old. There's no shortage of trouble among the hills of Tyrn Fornech, and it seems that more and more of these ruffians appear every day!
'If we don't turn them out of Evendim, they're sure to plunder every last relic that remains from the height of the old kingdom! That would be a real shame, if you ask me.'
A Friend in Ost Forod
While Calenglad meets with Gwindeth about obtaining the Silithar for Aragorn, he wants you to render your aid to Robin Dunkley in Ost Forod.
'Robin Dunkley lives in Ost Forod, among the hills of Tyrn Fornech to the northeast. I will send word to Robin when I return from my meeting with Gwindeth.'
'I am preparing to begin my journey, ${PLAYER}.'
'Gwindeth is as changeable as the surface of the lake. I hope she will help us.'
'I welcome you to Ost Forod, friend of the Rangers!'
'There are many unsavoury types in Tyrn Fornech these days. It's a shame.'

Robin Dunkley lives in Ost Forod, north-east of Tinnudir in Tyrn Fornech, in Evendim.
Calenglad has decided to meet with Gwindeth about acquiring the Silithar and has asked you to aid Robin Dunkley while he makes the journey.

'By reclaiming the last of the Silithair, you have done what Aragorn sent you here to do, ${PLAYER}, and along the way you made yourself a great help to all of us that live along the shores of Lake Nenuial. I am sorry to see you go.
'But go you must, for Narsil is to be reforged! Return at once to Rivendell, far to the east, and deliver the silithar to Aragorn! The time has come at last for the blade that was broken to be remade!'

'You return from out of the wild, ${PLAYER}, and my heart rejoices to see you! Unless my eyes are very much mistaken, you have passed the challenges of Gwindeth and return bearing the last of the Silithair!'
'We have need of the Silithar, ${PLAYER}. Without its light, the sword we make from the shards of Narsil will never be as worthy as its forebear.'
Bring the Silithar to Aragorn
The Last of the Silithair
You have recovered the last of the Silithair, shining adamants crafted by Elves of the house of Fëanor in days of old. It must be used to reforge the blade that was broken.
'I am sorry to see you go, ${PLAYER}, but go you must! Aragorn awaits the Silithar!'

'The son of Arathorn has learned much since I confronted him those many years ago. He will become a great leader, if the battles to come do not cut his life short.
'Deliver unto him the Silithar, for it is of his line, and he has passed my test.'

Aragorn is in the House of Elrond, in Rivendell, far to the east of Evendim.
Calenglad has given you the Silithar to bring to Aragorn. Its light will be used to remake the blade that was broken.

'Gwindeth has agreed to speak with you, ${PLAYER}, but do not misunderstand: she will only allow us to recover the Silithar if she believes that you are worthy of her trust and that Aragorn is ready for the burden that awaits him. She did not hesitate to rebuke him when he and I encountered her almost sixty years ago; I have no doubt that she would do so again, if it was in her mind.
'Speak to her with respect and do not seek to hide anything from her! The Blue Lady has lived in these lands for years uncounted, and she had patience only for the kings of Annúminas. It is said that Elendil consulted her often on various matters, and she grieved his passing.
'She lives at Gwindethrond, a cave in Western Emyn Uial, behind a clear waterfall that pours from the heights and feeds a shady pool at Rushingdale. You will need to circle the lake, for the pool is tucked among the hills on the far side of Nenuial. It will be a long journey, for Rushingdale is on the far side of Nenuial, west and slightly south even of Tinnudir.'

'You are the messenger from Aragorn son of Arathorn, Lord of the Dúnedain? You speak with his voice, and he shall be judged by yours, messenger, for he chose you as his agent.
'If there is much of Elendil in him, I do not doubt that Aragorn son of Arathorn will be found worthy. If there is not, the Silithar will remain where it has lain for centuries.'
A Meeting With the Blue Lady
Calenglad spoke with Gwindeth about acquiring the Silithar for Aragorn, but she refused to agree without first meeting you.

'The Blue Lady lives at Gwindethrond, a cave behind the waterfall at Rushingdale in western Emyn Uial, on the far side of the lake, west and slightly south even of Tinnudir. Only she can grant you access to the Silithar.'

The Blue Lady lives at Gwindethrond, a cave behind the waterfall at Rushingdale in the hills of western Emyn Uial on the far side of the lake, west and slightly south of Tinnudir.
Calenglad has arranged a meeting with Gwindeth and warned you to speak to her with respect and honesty. Only Gwindeth can grant you access to the Silithar needed by Aragorn.

'Listen well, Messenger: Elendil never returned from the wars to which he marched in the South, but the Silithar came by various keepers to Valandil his heir, who placed it in the deepest chamber of the tomb. I wished often that the body of Elendil might be brought to rest in Annúminas, but it was not to be.
'When the Dúnedain abandoned the city, Amlaith spoke to me as the kings were wont to do: \qGwindeth,\q he asked, \qLong have you aided the line of kings descended unbroken from noble Elendil. Your counsel is true, and the respect we bear for you unquenchable. I fear that Arnor cannot stand divided. There are too few of us left to hold Annúminas; we will move the people to Fornost, in the east, and I hope we can survive the dangerous days that lie before us. It is said that you have the gift of foresight. I beseech you, Gwindeth, to give me an answer: will Arnor survive the days ahead?\q
'I will tell you the rest of the tale if you are able to satisfy my final demand, the demand that Aragorn could not. I ask you to give me that which I value most. If you cannot, the Silithar will remain forever out of your reach and out of the reach of Aragorn son of Arathorn. Give me that which I value most, Messenger, and I will tell you what I beheld for Arnor and the line of kings.'
'You have returned, ${PLAYER}! What is Gwindeth's decision?'

'You are no mere messenger. Tell me your name....
'Welcome at last to Gwindethrond, ${PLAYER}. Your time among the Dúnedain has not been wasted, and I see that Aragorn made his choice of agents with care. He has indeed learned much since I beheld him deep within the tomb of noble Elendil. He was young then, and did not understand the greatest gift of all, the gift that Elendil and his line gave sparingly, if at all: the gift of respect.
'I told you I would finish the tale of Amlaith and the Silithar, and I will do so. Amlaith asked me if Arnor would survive the coming darkness, and I told him what I saw. \qYour kingdom will fall, Amlaith, king and son of kings,\q I said to him. \qI cannot see what misfortune awaits you at Fornost, but my heart tells me that if you bring the Silithar from Annúminas, it will come by unknown paths to rest beneath the deepest ocean.\q
'He received these sad tidings with grace, and after a moment appeared to strengthen his resolve. \qMy kingdom may be already lost, Gwindeth, but I would ask you one last favour. Raise the waters of the lake over the walls of the city and allow the flood to preserve what treasures remain here. The Silithar will stay where it lies, at the bottom of the tomb of Elendil, and none shall disturb its rest until one of my line has need of it beyond all hope. You shall be its caretaker, fair Gwindeth, if you will accept this duty.\q
'It was done as Amlaith requested; when the last of his people had left the city, I raised the waters and drowned the city beneath the deluge. So it has remained for hundreds of years. Return now to Calenglad, ${PLAYER}, and tell him that I will lower the waters of the flood to allow you access to the deepest chambers of the tomb of Elendil. Aragorn will have his Silithar.'
Give Gwindeth what she desires most
You have given Gwindeth what she desires most: respect
That Which I Value Most
Gwindeth has presented you with her final task: she wants you to give her what she desires more than all else.
'Give to me what I desire most, Messenger, and I will tell you the rest of my tale concerning the Silithar and the line of kings.'
'Return to Calenglad at Tinnudir, and tell him that I have agreed to lower the level of the water in the tomb of Elendil. You will be able to claim the Silithar in Aragorn's name.'
'I am pleased with your bearing, ${PLAYER}.'
'Aragorn chose his messenger well.'

The Blue Lady is at Gwindethrond, behind the waterfall at Rushingdale in western Emyn Uial.
Gwindeth has given you her final task, the task that Aragorn was unable to complete seventy years before: to give her that which she values most.

The Blue Lady is at Gwindethrond, behind the waterfall at Rushingdale in western Emyn Uial, in Evendim.
You have given Gwindeth that which she desires most, and that which the kings of Arnor gave to her -- respect. She is waiting to speak with you.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, east and slightly north of Rushingdale, in Evendim.
Gwindeth has agreed to allow you access to the tomb of Elendil, where you can recover the Silithar for Aragorn.

'You have come from Gwindeth? She does not often pass the waterfall that covers the entrance of her home, but I have seen her beneath the trees now and then.
'I know too of the great respect she bore for the kings of Annúminas, and that they bore for her. It is said that the last king of that city asked her to raise the waters of Nenuial over the walls, but I do not know why he would ask such a thing.
'You seek a draught that may cleanse stone of the corruption of the salamanders? I can give such a draught to you. Take it to Tyl Ruinen and use it to restore the statue of which you speak. I have no need of thanks! It is enough to have a refreshingly brief conversation with someone new -- Longbough is slow of speech in the nature of his kind, and Erchiel does not have the patience she once had for my mischief, though that is to her credit!'
Cleanse corrupted statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen
The Corrupted Statue
Lithuifin gave you a cleansing draught with which to purify the corrupted statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen.
'I have given you a cleansing draught to use on the statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen, to the east. Did you change your mind and decide to leave it to the salamanders?'
'The statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen has not yet been cleansed,Messenger.'
'Have you cleansed the corrupted statue? I am glad!'
'We are well-met, ${PLAYER}! It is good to see you again.'

The corrupted statue of Elendil is on one of the islands of Tyl Ruinen, to the south.
Lithuifin gave you a draught to cleanse one of the statues of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen.
Defeated salamanders on Tyl Ruinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Before he went away to his doom, Elendil often spoke with me beside Nenuial; we would walk among the reeds and speak of his kingdom, and he treated me with grace and respect. It is for the memory of great Elendil that I maintain the lake and protect the relics of his line.
'At the behest of Amlaith, the last king to sit enthroned in Annúminas, I permitted the waters of Nenuial to wash over the walls of the city, and the treasures of proud Elendil now sleep soundly in the watery half-light. The adamant you seek, the Silithar that passed from Gil-galad to Elendil and his line through the safe-keeping of Círdan the Shipwright, cannot be reclaimed without my permission. It was the will of Amlaith that the Silithar be kept safe, even from those of Elendil's line, for fear that its light would be wasted unduly or the stone taken by the Enemy.
'The islands of Tyl Ruinen have been overrun by salamanders, corrupted beasts that singe the grasses and taint the waters of Nenuial. Swim north-east to Tyl Ruinen in the centre of the lake and defeat the salamanders you find there. Perhaps when you return, I will have proof of the worthiness of Aragorn son of Arathorn through his messenger.'

'You have defeated some of the salamanders that lurk now on Tyl Ruinen? There are many who would do such a thing, when asked. Why should this prove yourself worthy of what you seek or prove that Aragorn has grown since last I saw him?'
Defeat salamanders on Tyl Ruinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Corrupted Beasts of Nenuial
Gwindeth wants you to prove yourself worthy of recovering the Silithar by fighting the salamanders of Tyl Ruinen.
'The islands of Tyl Ruinen are to the north-east, in the middle of the lake. Defeat the salamanders that have corrupted them, and I may be able to judge your worth, Messenger.'

The islands of Tyl Ruinen are located north-east of Rushingdale, near the middle of the lake, in Evendim.
Gwindeth has asked you to defeat the corrupted salamanders you find on Tyl Ruinen.

The Blue Lady is in Gwindethrond, behind the waterfall at Rushingdale in western Emyn Uial, south-west of Tyl Ruinen.
Gwindeth is waiting to hear that you have dealt a blow to the salamanders of Tyl Ruinen.
Restored the corrupted statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen
Restored the missing statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen

'Did you see the statues of noble Elendil that stand upon Tyl Ruinen, Messenger? One of them has been corrupted by the vile salamanders, tainted with dread ichor, and the other has been removed from its pedestal -- the statue itself has been lost.
'If you can restore both of the statues, I may be able to more readily judge your worth and the worthiness of Aragorn son of Arathorn. When both statues of mighty Elendil once more stand untroubled on the south-west and south-east shores of Tyl Ruinen, I will speak with you again on this matter.
'You will need a cleansing draught of some kind to restore the statue the salamanders have ruined. Elves have come to the Eavespires, far to the north and east of Rushingdale, where a stream flows into the lake; they may prepare such a draught for you. I do not know where you may find the missing statue.'

'You have restored both statues of fair Elendil, Messenger? I am pleased with your doings. Perhaps Aragorn son of Arathorn chose well when he sent you to me with his request. Calenglad spoke well of you, and he has always been true.
'I was always a friend to the kings of old, and I will not betray the trust they placed in me or the respect they bore me.
'There is one final test, Messenger. If you are able to meet my last request, I will allow you access to the tomb of Elendil and the Silithar. Surely the Lord of the Dúnedain has prepared you for this test. If he has not, it must be that he has learned nothing since last I saw him, and I will not surrender the Silithar to you.'
Restore the corrupted statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen
Restore the missing statue of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen
A Friend to the Kings of Old
Gwindeth told you that two statues of Elendil stood on the islands of Tyl Ruinen: one corrupted by the salamanders and the other lost.

'Two statues of noble Elendil once stood on the main island of Tyl Ruinen, to the north-east, at its south-west and south-east corners. One has been corrupted by the salamanders and the other has been lost to time, but if you restore both statues, I will speak with you again.
'Elves at the Eavespires, far to the north and east of Rushingdale where a stream empties into the lake, may be able to prepare a cleansing draught for one of the statues. I do not know what has happened to the other statue; you will need to find it on your own.'

Two statues of Elendil once stood on the south-east and south-west shores of Tyl Ruinen, but one statue has been corrupted by salamanders and the other statue is missing. The Eavespires are far to the north and east of Rushingdale.
Gwindeth wants you to restore two statues of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen. Some Elves at the Eavespires may be able to prepare a cleansing draught for the corrupted statue. Gwindeth does not know where the missing statue may have ended up or in what condition it may be.

The Blue Lady is in Gwindethrond, behind the waterfall at Rushingdale in western Emyn Uial, south-west of Tyl Ruinen.
You have restored the two statues of Elendil on Tyl Ruinen, as Gwindeth requested, and should return to her with the news.

'I expect that the robbers that prowl Tyrn Fornech are carrying more pieces of this broken statue, ${PLAYER}. If you can recover more of these fragments, I might be able to reassemble it. Wouldn't that be something? I expect Calenglad and the rest of the Rangers would be so pleased!
'Look for robbers among the hills of Tyrn Fornech and take statue pieces from them, ${PLAYER}. You'll most likely find only small pieces on these robbers, but one or two might carry larger pieces. The villains have also established a camp of sorts to the west, on the island of Rantost in the lake; you might find larger pieces of the statue there.
'Return to me with any statue pieces you can recover, and I'll see if I can remake it.'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}, very good indeed! It doesn't look like all of these belong to the statue I'm trying to put back together, but I think enough of them do that I can make a good start of it.
'Do you know, I think this might be a statue of Elendil? I wonder where once it stood? Perhaps it shall stand there again some day!
'There is troubling talk around Ost Forod, my friend. Stay, and I will tell you of it.'
'I am still waiting for more pieces of statuary, ${PLAYER}.'
Bring statue pieces to Robin Dunkley
Ancient Statuary
Robin Dunkley, encouraged by your retrieval of the broken statuary carried by the ill-fated robbers that ran afoul of bears at Nan Orngon, has charged you with recovering more of its pieces.

'The tomb-robbers that prowl Tyrn Fornech may be carrying small pieces of the statue, and their camp on Rantost, the island to the west, might hold larger pieces. One or two robbers might have large pieces as well.
'If you can recover enough pieces, I might be able to remake the statue! Wouldn't that be something?'
'I do believe this is a statue of Elendil I'm remaking!'
'I wonder where this statue stood in its day?'

Tomb-robbers in Tyrn Fornech may be carrying small statue pieces, and larger pieces can likely be found in their camp on Rantost, the island west of Ost Forod.
Robin Dunkley has been inspired by the broken statuary you recovered with the dream of remaking the complete statue and wants you to recover the pieces of it.

Robin Dunkley is at Ost Forod, east of Rantost, in Tyrn Fornech in Evendim.
You have recovered many pieces of statuary, and now you should bring them to Robin Dunkley to see if they belong to the statue he seeks to repair.

'I do not know what made the Gauredain choose the life they lead, whether it be fascination with the form of the wolf or some other reason, but I do know that they have become entirely evil. These men wear wolf-skin cloaks and bedeck themselves with ornaments fashioned from bloody teeth and fangs, and it is said they move with unbelievable speed and attack with strength beyond that of a normal man.
'Nat must be avenged, ${PLAYER}, and the Gauredain taught not to attack the people who live around the lake. Journey north-west into Emyn Uial and defeat some of these evil Men. Return to me some of their weapons as well, that I may destroy them.'

'These claws fill me with dread, ${PLAYER}. The Gauredain are cruel indeed to hunt their own kin with these, for kin we are, despite the beast-hides they wear and the blood-thirst they possess. I hope that Nat has found peace, and I thank you for avenging his memory.
'I have nearly finished remaking the statue of Elendil from the pieces you brought to me, ${PLAYER}. I do not have all of the missing fragments, but some other adventurers are helping me search the camps of the tomb-robbers for the pieces that remain.
'But that is not what I must speak with you about. I have received word from Calenglad! He has returned from his meeting with the Blue Lady of Nenuial!'
'You do not have the weapons I asked you to take from the gauradan? What have you been doing, ${PLAYER}?'
Bring makeshift claws to Robin Dunkley
The Gauredain of Emyn Uial
Robin Dunkley has asked you to defeat the Gauredain of Emyn Uial and return with their weapons.
'The Gauredain prowl the hills and forests of Emyn Uial, to the north-west. Defeat these evil men in memory of Nat Rapkins and bring me the unusual weapons they carry.'
'The Gauredain are still Men, despite their cruel ways and the kinship they hold with evil.'
'Nat has been avenged, but he will never again hunt the forests he loved.'

The Gauredain prowl the hills and forests of Emyn Uial, north-west of Ost Forod.
Robin Dunkley desires revenge for the death of Nat Rapkins and wants you to defeat the evil men that slew him. He has also asked you to bring him some of the Gauredain's unusual weapons.

Robin Dunkley is in Ost Forod, in Tyrn Fornech of Evendim, south-east of Emyn Uial.
You have defeated a number of the Gauredain that slew Nat Rapkins and collected some of their unusual weapons. Robin Dunkley will be pleased to hear the tale.

'A hunter by the name of Nat Rapkins often travels far to the north-west, crossing the cold waters of the Even-rills that feed into the lake, and conducts his hunts in Emyn Uial. Nat is a woodsman of no small skill and should have returned by now. His family is overcome with concern.
'I did not want to say anything to them about it, but I heard a terrible howling along the shore last evening. It had been driven from my mind with all of our doings against the tomb-robbers, but now I wonder if those dreadful howls had something to do with poor Nat.
'If you would journey north-west to the northernmost tip of the lake and cross the Even-rills there to search for Nat Rapkins, I would greatly appreciate it. He has been gone for far too long, and I fear what end he may have found. He is sure to have remained in sight of the lake, if that was within his power, so do not stray too far from it.'

'You there...I...attacked by Gauredain! Terrible creatures....
'Take my pack...bring it...Ost Forod....'

'I was afraid you would return with such news, ${PLAYER}. Nat was a good hunter, well-liked by the people here, and will be missed. I will return the pack to his family and give them these sad tidings.
'You say he spoke of the Gauredain? Yes, I feared as much. They have always been a danger to those who find themselves in Emyn Uial, but it has been many years since last they proved so bold. Something must be done, ${PLAYER}.'
'Did you not find Nat?'
Find Nat Rapkins
Bring Nat Rapkins's pack to Robin Dunkley
A Howling in the Hills
Robin Dunkley has told you that the people of Ost Forod are worried about one of their own, a hunter named Nat Rapkins, who has not returned from a hunt in the eastern Emyn Uial.

'If old Nat is in trouble, you'll find him somewhere near the Even-rills at the northern reach of the lake. Head north-west of Ost Forod and cross the waters at its northern reach, but beware of whatever evil made that terrible howling -- it froze my blood cold to hear it.'
'We must do something about the Gauredain, ${PLAYER}!'
'Poor Nat. He was a good man.'

Nat Rapkins crossed the Even-rills at the northern tip of the lake, north-west of Ost Forod, and never returned. Robin Dunkley wants you to search along the edge of the lake near the Even-rills for the missing hunter.
Robin Dunkley heard a dreadful howling along the shore at night and is worried that Nat Rapkins might have fallen to some evil beast. He wants you to try and find the lost hunter.

Robin Dunkley is in Ost Forod, south-east of the Even-rills, in Tyrn Fornech in Evendim.
Nat Rapkins spoke of the Gauredain with his dying breath and gave you his pack to return to Ost Forod. You should bring it to Robin Dunkley.

'${PLAYER}! I had not thought to see you again so soon, but I am glad indeed to have been mistaken. In point of fact, it seems that a fortuitous wind has brought you here to me on this day, for I have good news: I have finished remaking the statue of Elendil you brought to me in pieces!
'You say you know from whence this statue came? How wonderful! You would do well to return it to its rightful place, ${PLAYER}!
'I will give you the statue and trust you to bring it to the pedestal on which it once stood. Tyl Ruinen, you say? Very well! Go carefully, and let us set right what the robbers of Evendim have despoiled!'
Place statue of Elendil on pedestal
The Lost Statue
Robin Dunkley has given you the statue of Elendil he remade from the pieces you brought him during your time in Ost Forod.

'The statue of Elendil that once stood upon the island of Tyl Ruinen no longer graces that place with its presence. Find the statue, in whatever condition it may now be, and restore it to its pedestal.'

'I am still amazed at this turn of fortune, ${PLAYER} -- for you to return just when I have finished remaking the broken statue of Elendil proves to me that there are forces for good in this world that have not abandoned Evendim!
'Take the statue now to the islands of Tyl Ruinen and restore it to its proper place!'
'I am delighted that together we restored the lost statue of Elendil, ${PLAYER}!'
'You are always welcome at Ost Forod, ${PLAYER}.'

There is a pedestal on the islands of Tyl Ruinen, in the middle of Lake Nenuial, where the statue of Elendil you bear once stood. Tyl Ruinen is across the lake from the island of Tinnudir.
While you journeyed to meet with Gwindeth, Robin Dunkley set about remaking the broken statue you recovered from robbers in Tyrn Fornech. This is the statue that once stood upon Tyl Ruinen.

'While you were gone, I heard that a group of robbers transporting relics from the islands ran into a spot of trouble with the bears of Tyrn Fornech. Isn't that wonderful?
'Apparently, they had hoped to give Tinnudir a wide berth and had circled far to the east in a great loop, but they went too far and stumbled upon the bears at Nan Orngon. What luck: bad for them but good for us, ${PLAYER}!
'Head east of Ost Forod to Nan Orngon and search the bodies for the relics the robbers brought with them. Bears don't care about such things, so I figure they won't mind if we return them to the Rangers! Use caution while at Nan Orngon, friend -- bears do not discriminate between true-hearted friends of the Dúnedain and villainous tomb-robbers!'

'This statuary is very interesting, ${PLAYER}, and very old. I wonder how many pieces of this statue have already been claimed by robbers?
'If we can assemble the complete statue, I know that Calenglad and the other Rangers would be pleased!'
'You didn't find anything on the corpses of the robbers at Nan Orngon, ${PLAYER}?'

'Some tomb-robbers ran into trouble with bears at Nan Orngon, to the east. Isn't that wonderful?
'Go to Nan Orngon and recover any artifacts they might have been transporting. The bears don't need them, after all, and we can return them to their rightful places.'
'We should try and assemble the rest of the broken statue, my friend!'
'Even in pieces, the statue you recovered has a noble bearing.'

You successfully defended House Brumbar from the boggarts

'While you were confronting Jabe Grimshaw in Tyrn Fornech, a Ranger named Pantescal sent word of many boggarts advancing towards the ruins of House Brumbar. Brumbar was a Dúnedain line of no small importance before the abandonment of Annúminas, and we must keep the grounds of that ancient manor safe from treasure-seekers, though the buildings are mostly gone.
'Pantescal did not seem overly-concerned about this band of boggarts, but I would be put more at ease if you stood with him. The creatures are cowardly, but in great numbers even the weakest of foes can pose a threat.
'The ruins of House Brumbar are north and east of Tinnudir, in Parth Aduial. Cross the bridge to the mainland and follow the shore northward. Brumbar is little more than crumbling walls now, but we can not allow the boggarts to befoul its memory.'

'You have returned, ${PLAYER}! I must applaud you and apologize at the same time!
'I still did not believe you were trustworthy. These are dark days, and the Dúnedain cannot afford to trust so easily. But you have proven yourself to me many times over!
'I will tell Calenglad that your errand must not be hindered. Do not think less of me! The Dúnedain have not survived through the long years by having an abundance of trust.'

'Naethmunn has sent you to me? I do not think I will have need of your assistance, but I know better than to refuse help earnestly offered!
'These boggarts are weak, but their great numbers give them courage. This courage is misplaced, for we will turn them aside from House Brumbar with ease!
'Make yourself ready!'

'Your errand must not be hindered any further, ${PLAYER}.'

'An interesting find. I have always enjoyed puzzles such as this. Let us see. This one goes here...ah, that was easy. All done! Let us learn what it says.
'Remarkable! Evendim abounds with tales of old treasure, most of them completely false. But this scroll...this is an account of a man -- an adventurer shall we say, to be polite to the dead -- who scavenged the Fields of Fornost long ago, after the Witch-king's great defeat. It seems this fellow hid his finds not far away.
'From your point of view, this treasure is a legitimate trove -- there should be no reason that anyone could not honourably recover it if they happened to find its location. A word of warning, though: the ruin this scroll mentions, Ost Heryn, is said to be infested by night by evil spirits. Be that as it may, it is certainly home to brigands by day, so it will be dangerous at any time you care to visit.'
'Did you have something for me?'

'Alas! I am sorry you found no great treasure. That trove must have been looted long ago. But in truth, an old book like this is a treasure to me, though I suppose the robbers must have found it worthless.
'I have little to offer to sweeten your bitter loss, but I will give you what I can for the book and the scroll.'
'Did you have something for me?'

'Greetings, traveller. It is not often that we receive visitors here, so far from the open roads, but you are welcome to stay a little while if you wish. Take care around Longbough, however. He is a bit short-tempered for an Onod and has little trust for the folk of Eriador. In fact, if you would gain his trust, then there is a small matter with which you might aid us.
'An unusual tribe of Men called the Gauredain have recently come down from the mountains to the north and have begun to hunt these lands. Thus far they seem little more than savages, but they are hostile to most whom they meet, and I have no intention of allowing them to disturb us here in the Eavespires. Nevertheless, my husband Lithuifin frowns on unnecessary slaughter; therefore, I wish to learn more about the Gauredain before I take further steps to drive them away -- but it falls to me to maintain the watch upon this grove, and I have little time for such expeditions.
'If you could surreptitiously gather a few artifacts from their encampments in the hills north of here and bring them to me, I might learn a good deal more about them, for I have dealt with a great many tribes of Men and others in my years, and many of their customs and symbols are familiar to me.'

'Ah, I see you have returned with the artifacts of the Gauredain. Excellent.
'They are crude as I expected, but they also show more sinister signs -- some of the work is influenced by the customs of Orcs and goblins! The relationship is distant, and perhaps they have had no dealings with each other for some considerable time, but it does not bode well for our chances of coming to a reasoned understanding with them, I am afraid.
'Lithuifin's tender temperments aside, I fear that our next course may best be one of decisive action -- hopefully he will not be too upset with me.'

'Have you been unable to acquire the Gauredain artifacts I requested?
'It should be no great matter so long as you choose your way carefully and avoid unnecessary battles.
'They are encamped in the hills and valleys on the northern edge of the forest, not all that far from here.'

Gauradan Artifacts

Erchiel, an Elf living in Eavespires, has asked you to enter the lands of the Gauredain to the north and collect some artifacts from their encampments there that she might better understand the threat as they intrude further south into the forests.
'Hoom! Hom! I would not tarry here over-long, Little One. These forests are wild places, and since the fall of the old kingdoms, they are not for the likes of you.'
'Ta-rum! What you do with the trinkets of the Gauredain is of little interest to me. The affairs of Men in this age are of no import here.'

'I see that Erchiel has convinced you to help her deal with the Gauredain who have intruded on these forests. That is well, for they have become a growing problem of late.
'Please take care, however, my dear Erchiel's methods can sometimes be a bit...harsh.'

'These artifacts are crude, but revealing. I believe that Erchiel asked you to retrieve these, did she not?'
'She has never been known for her sense of patience, so I would take them to her right away were I you.'

Erchiel has asked you to collect various artifacts from the camps of the Gauredain.
The Gauredain camps lie in the hills to the north of the Eavespires.

You should return to Erchiel with the Gauredain artifacts.
She can be found at the Eavespires, south of the Gauradan encampments.
Collected oats (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If you are going to be tramping around these parts and have a day's work to spare, I would ask a favour of you, ${CLASS}. Not two weeks ago, I got a letter from an enterprising hobbit in the Westfarthing. He said to me in this letter that he was in need of a large supply of oats, the largest order I have ever seen, to be sure.
'I didn't much take a liking to the idea right away, but what with the hard times and all, well now I couldn't turn down his offer, even if I don't take too kindly to the name of Sackville-Baggins; leastwise, the Baggins part of it. Queer tales, to be sure, are told about that family.
'If you have the time, I could use more hands to collect the oats from the fields east and north-east of here. I would get out there myself, but with all those nasty bugs...well, pardon my saying it, but your clothes look more to the task what with being dressed for fighting and all.'

'Did you get the oats? Wonderful! I will have these bales sent to Hobbiton right way.
'I wonder what he could be wanting with such a large amount of oats? I'd gather he's got enough now to supply a large party with bread for a month, though I doubt he could get the guests. But it's not my business to pry into others' affairs.'
'Did you harvest all the oats yet?'
Collect oats (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring Nibs Chubb the harvested oats
Oats for the Westfarthing
Nibs Chubb needs assistance filling an order of oats for a customer in the Westfarthing.
'You can find the oats in my fields just east and north-east of here.'
'Thank you so much for helping me with my oats. You are welcome on my farm any day!'

Nibs Chubb's fields are east and north-east of his farm.
Nibs Chubb has asked you to help him collect his oats from the fields.

Nibs Chubb is at his farm, in the south of Oatbarton.

Defeated Barkskin Wood-trolls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Rotting Wood-trolls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Heart-rot has fled

'My friends call me Longbough and suggest that I may trust one such as yourself. Hoom! I have not yet made up my mind on the matter, but I am considered rather impatient amongst my kind, and the trees hereabout whisper to me of deeds that may need doing.
'Something seems to be amiss on the edge of the forest, well to the south of here. A party of Wood-trolls -- led by one called 'Heart-rot' -- have dwelled there for some time, but now their power seems to be growing and threatens to twist the forest around them to evil and hatred. If you do indeed wish to aid me, seek out these trolls and winnow their numbers. If you can slay enough of them, then Heart-rot should be driven to confront you, and you may destroy him, thus removing the source of this trouble.
'Hom! Ta-room! You are rather small though, are you not? I think perhaps it would be best if you brought allies to aid you in this task.'

'Ta-room! While your haste is somewhat unsettling, your actions are commendable.
'Unfortunately, it seems that there is more to this Heart-rot than I had first imagined. Ta-rum!
'Whatever power lies in the Twisted Grove, its roots run deeper than I had suspected, and I must learn more before we take any further action against it.'
Defeat Barkskin Wood-trolls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Rotting Wood-trolls (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Find and defeat Heart-rot
Hewing the Wood
Longbough believes that some evil power may be twisting the wood to dark ends, perhaps the Wood-trolls that have begun to appear in Evendim. Roused to anger, the Ent is ready to take action.
'Hoom! Hom! Have you been to the Twisted Grove yet? I hear the shuddering of its roots even from here, and it fills me with a foreboding I have not known for many years.'

The Twisted Grove lies to the south-west of the Eavespires.
Angered by the wanton ruin inflicted upon his grove, Longbough has asked you to defeat the Wood-trolls infesting the Twisted Grove.

Heart-rot is at the Twisted Grove, which lies southwest of the Eavespires.
As well as driving the Wood-trolls from his grove, Longbough also asked you to find and defeat their leader, Heart-rot, in hopes that the remnant will flee.

Longbough is at the Eavespires, on the northwest shore of Lake Evendim.
You should return to the Eavespires and tell Longbough of your battle with Heart-rot.
Collected rotted limbs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Hoom! I must learn more about the power which has corrupted the Twisted Grove and seeps into the surrounding forest. Return there and gather any sickened or dead plants you may find. From them, I may be able to determine what it is that we truly face.
'Hom! Ta-room! As you well know, the Twisted Grove is beset by wood-trolls of great strength, you would be wise to bring allies with you in your search.'
'Hom! Ta-room! You have brought me the fallen limbs from the trees of the grove? These should offer me some greater insight into what power now infects that dark place.'
'I will need more of the dying plants that no doubt litter the Twisted Grove before I can tell you more about what ails the forest. Ta-rum! Now go.'
Collect rotted limbs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the rotted limbs to Longbough
Seeking Answers
Longbough believes that some evil power may be twisting the wood to dark ends.
'Ta-rum! Take care as you explore the Twisted Grove. Hoom! It has become a dark place with a vile hatred of all living things, and we must learn from whence this blight has sprung.'

The Twisted Grove lies south-west of the Eavespires.
Longbough has asked you to seek evidence of the power which has corrupted the Twisted Grove. He asked you to collect rotted limbs and bring them to him.

Longbough is at the Eavespires, on the north-west shore of Lake Evendim.
You should bring the rotted limbs you have collected to Longbough.

'Hoom! From the blighted branches you brought to me, I have divined much. There was once an ancient tree in the southern forest whom I was once well acquainted with, but after the destruction wrought upon the forest during the wars long ago, it became withdrawn and would speak with me no more...even though my own despair at the acts of Men was nearly as great.
'Now it seems that the Wood-trolls -- particularly this one called Heart-rot -- have whispered long to the Huorn in its slumber and re-awakened it under their thrall. Its heart is now black and twisted with their malice, and it will suffer no living thing of flesh in its domain. Hom! Ta-room! Were that all that had transpired, I would pay it less heed, for the Twisted Heart's folly is its own, but now its roots run deep and far, ever grasping and twisting the trees that they touch, and the Wood-trolls will follow in its wake. I cannot allow the Twisted Heart to warp the entire forest to its will. We must stand against it and fell both it and the vile troll that has corrupted it.
'Gather your companions, for the Twisted Heart's power has grown fell, and I fear it will be all we can do to face it in the place of its greatest strength, but we have no choice! Ta-rum! Hoom! Speak with me again when you are ready to leave.'

Hoom! Hom! It has been ever so long since my blood has run with such heat and fervour! That was well fought, Little One! Indeed while I have little love for axes and swords, I had forgotten the enjoyable haste of battle. Ta-room! Even now though, I feel the anger of the forest subsiding as the Twisted Heart's influence fades. Soon some measure of peace shall return here, I think.
'Ta-rum! My thanks to you, Little One, your aid was most welcome. Please forgive my rudeness when first we met.
Accompany Longbough against the Twisted Heart
The Twisted Heart
Longbough believes that some evil power may be twisting the wood to dark ends.

'Have you gathered your allies? Hom! The forest seethes with anger as the power of the Twisted Heart grows, and while I fear we have little time, haste will lead only to disaster.
'Ta-room! Ta-rum! Are you fully prepared for what lies ahead? Be certain, for we face death should we falter.'

'Hoom! Thank you for your help in purging the Twisted Grove of the evils that had beset it, Little One. It is sad to see an old friend fall to such a fate, but such is the way of the world. Seasons turn, leaves fall, branches wither -- and in the fullness of time, new shoots grow to take their place. But such passing is never without pain, is it.'

Longbough is at the Eavespires, on the north-west shore of Lake Evendim.
Longbough told you to gather allies to accompany him against the Twisted Heart.

Longbough is at the Eavespires, on the north-west shore of Lake Evendim.
You should speak again with Longbough.

'I fear things have gone awry and taken a rather dangerous turn. It seems that a Hill-giant of some actual cunning and intelligence has arisen to leadership amongst the giants of Amon Môth, and I cannot ignore such an ominous portent.
'Giants are very powerful creatures and dangerous at the best of times, but they are fractious and chaotic, and it is quite rare for a strong leader to arise amongst them. The consequences of such are usually disastrous, for few forces can stand against an organized war-band of giants. Even Erchiel and Longbough would likely find themselves overmatched, should it come to that.
'In this instance, I am afraid I must defer to my wife's wisdom -- this newly arisen leader must not be allowed to strengthen his control over the giants, or they might easily overwhelm these forests. Alas, it is not within my power to defeat him, and my wife must stand guard over the Eavespires...might you gather a band strong enough to defeat him?'

'That was well done! Please forgive me for asking such of you. My wife and I have striven for many years to avoid the conflict and strife of the world at large, but in these years it presses ever closer, and I fear that she may find herself called away from my side to fight in yet another war.
'Erchiel has already fought her share, ${PLAYER}. I have seen it in her face as the dreams of ages past intrude upon her slumber and crease her beautiful brow with worry and care. I have seen the ancient fire alight in her eyes when it seems that danger may be upon us yet again.
'I would have her see no more of those dreams, if it lies within my power, and I thank you greatly for your aid. May the world show you kindness in your travels.'
Fool's Crown
Lithuifin the Elf is concerned with the giants which have been ruining the forest.

The Hill-giant chieftain is at Amon Môth, south and west of the Eavespires.
Lithuifin has asked you to defeat the Hill-giant chieftain of Amon Môth.

Lithuifin resides in the Eavespires, east and north of Amon Môth.
You should return to Lithuifin and tell him of the chieftain's defeat.
Placed false wards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Now then, as a warrior of some renown, I am all too accustomed to doing battle, and always I contend with and offer the threat of death. Against such mean foes as goblins and Orcs, this threat itself is often sufficient to break their spirits and send them back into the darkness unless they are driven by powerful masters -- but not so with the Gauredain.
'As Lithuifin has reminded me, Men such as they who are still free of spirit and pride often place greater value upon the unseen and unfelt worlds than they do upon their own lives. The wards were the clue, and it is this that we shall play upon to keep our respective camps safely separated. You may have noticed a number of Gauradan-markers along the shore of the river just north of here. Those mark the current boundaries of the Gauredain's territory -- at least as they see it. But they do not in any way prevent them from crossing further into our stretch of the forest. That we shall now change.
'I have changed the wards you brought me and added a few flourishes. If you add these to the boundary markers, they will no longer represent mere territorial boundaries, but Wards of Doom to the Gauredain, a warning that any who cross put their very spirits into absolute peril. The Gauredain may not respect our swords and bows, but this they shall not lightly ignore.'

'Ah, well done, my friend. That should greatly reduce the threat of the Gauredain for the time being.
'That line of wards will neither prevent their crossing indefinitely, nor will it stop some of their most insistent or brave hunters from intruding, but I will deal with those as I must. What it will do is prevent open war from erupting between their tribe and those of us here in the Eavespires, and that is enough for now.
'You have my deepest gratitude, and though I have no more tasks for you, you may wish to speak with Lithuifin or Longbough and see if either of them requires your aid.'

'This last task should be relatively simple. All you need to is modify the Gauradan markers along the river as I have shown you.
'After that the Gauradan should shun the river and the lands south of it - for a time anyways.'
Place false wards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Talk to Erchiel
False Wards
Erchiel is ready to move forward with the final stages of the plan Lithuifin helped her devise.

'I see. Ta-room! Erchiel hopes to frighten the Gauredain away without resorting to further conflict?
'This seems wise to me. Little Erchiel often behaves as if hers were the last bright blade remaining in a world consumed by darkness. Hoom! She should not take such burdens upon herself, lest the weight becomes too great to bear.'

'You have placed the wards, Little One? Hoom! Hom!'
'I have little love for strangers from afar, but you have aided one of my friends and helped ensure the peace of the Eavespires.
'Ta-room! I have decided that I shall trust you -- a little, at least, for Lithuifin tells me that I may, and he is ever a fine judge of character. Do not prove him wrong!'

'A line of their own spirit-wards to keep the superstitious Gauredain at bay? Yes, that should work well.
'Such is the nature of those Men, whose lives are short and brutal, to often concern themselves more with what comes after. Summoning such fears may avail us well here without having to resort to senseless slaughter.'

'You have placed the wards as Erchiel asked? Good! Even if they do not understand how they came to be altered without the blessings of their Soothsayers, the Gauredain will be loathe to meddle with them now that they are in place.
'I am sure a few of their bravest hunters will still dare to cross the boundary now and again, but with Longbough and Erchiel here to gaurd the Eavespires, we need not fear a small handful of the Men.
'My thanks, by the way, for lending Erchiel your aid. It is one less thing we need to worry about out here in the wilds.'
'This final task should be quite simple. The markers you seek can be found along the northern bank of the river that runs by the Eavespires.'
'Thank you for your assistance with the Guaradain. Due to your efforts I believe it will be some time before they disturb us here.'
'I have heard rumours now of dark powers astir in distant lands once again, and of tread of armies gathering is an ancient beat with which I am well acquainted.'
'Though my heart burns with the thought that I might now have vengeance for ancient wrongs, for Lithuifin's sake I shall not join in this song of battle. Not this time.'

'Good luck to you, for whom this world may be destined. My husband and I shall remain here and watch as this drama unfolds, and in time we too shall go into the West - though I hope that you are victorious for I am still fond of these lands, and I do not wish to see them forsaken to the hand of the Enemy of old.'

Erchiel has asked you to modify a series of Gauradan-markers into Wards of Doom to prevent the Gauredain from crossing into the Eavespires.
The Gauradan-markers are along the river to the north of the Eavespires.

You should return and tell Erchiel that you have finished placing the wards.

'I am afraid that speaking with the Gauredain is unlikely to buy us anything -- they are very nearly feral creatures, and the influence of the Orcs means they are unlikely to look upon Elves such as myself kindly at all.
'If they discover us here there is every likelihood that they will attempt to drive us out -- and while neither Longbough nor I would allow it, to have such bloodshed occur on our very doorstep would wound Lithuifin deeply, and I would not wish to involve him so.
'I would ask you to hunt down some small number of their hunters and warriors that have wandered south of the river -- not so many as to cause them grievous hurt, but enough to warn them that these lands are not theirs, nor are they welcome here. It would also be best if you could find one of their leaders, for such tribes are often deeply superstitious and the loss of such a leader can set them aback greatly in fear.'

'It seems you have fought well against the Gauredain, but from your descriptions of their savagery I realize that I have been hasty and foolish myself....
'Forgive me. I have fought a great many battles and lost many things I have cared for and become something of a creature of habit. The way of the sword comes to my hand and thoughts as readily as breathing, and I fear it may always be so. I have misjudged the Gauredain -- they are feral and brutal perhaps, but unlike the craven Orcs and goblins, it seems they are yet unbowed and carry a great pride with them -- they will not be cowed by such an assault.
'I will consult with Lithuifin on the matter, for he is gentler and in his own manner a more clever Elf than I, and certainly his mind is less clouded with thoughts of glory long lost. We will speak again shortly when I have had more time to consider our next course of action.'
Defeat Gauradan Tribesman (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Gauradan Gorge-stalker (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat a Gauradan Soothsayer
Hunting the Hunters
Erchiel has asked you to defeat several of the Gauredain in order to frighten them and keep them from exploring further south.

'Hoom, ta-room! It is of no matter to me if you wish to do battle with the Men of the Wood, nor do I care which of you are victorious -- so long as you do not bring your troubles here into these quiet glades!'
'Hom! Hoom! Take care that you do not bring your petty battles here, Little One.'

'Erchiel has asked you to do battle with the Gauredain, hasn't she?
'I am afraid that she is too old and set in her ways to accept counsel in such matters from such as I unless she comes to me for such advice.
'Erchiel was born in long ages past where the long wars against the Enemy made skill at war paramount -- and she does not easily forget those ways when she feels that our place here may be threatened. Even when there may be a better way.'

'So, you have done battle with the Gauredain who now invade these forests, but I can see in your eyes that the outcome was not what you and my dear Erchiel had hoped for -- that the Gauredain remain undetered.
'She is no fool, however, and I rather expect she will seek a more effective course soon enough.'

'You will not have to search far for the Gauradan that roam these forests.
'I fear it is only a matter of time now before they discover us here at the Eavespires, unless you can deter them from coming south of the river.'

Erchiel has asked you to defeat a number of Gauredain in order to instill in them a healthy fear of the forests.
The Gauredain she speaks of can be found in the forests north of the river that passes by the Eavespires.

Erchiel is at the Eavespires on the northwest shore of Lake Evendim.

Gathered Gauradan-wards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Ah, my dear Lithuifin has offered me a fair course of action in dealing with the Gauredain. I must say that it can be rather embarassing to be set straight by a lesser Elf, but please do not tell him I said so! At any rate, I suppose that is why I wedded him.
'As for this plan, we -- and by that, I am afraid I mean you -- shall steal several of the wards that the Gauredain have scattered about their encampments. I believe you know them well enough, as you brought me one before. These wards are simple tribal symbols, commonly used to keep evil spirits at bay by superstitious cultures. That is not to say that such spirits do not occasionally roam the world in one form or another -- but I am afraid a simple chunk of wood would do little to deter them.
'In any case, I need you to gather several of these and bring them to me, then we can embark on the rather more clever part of this plan.'

'Good, you have done exactly as I asked. I hope the Gauredain were not too much trouble?
'In any case, now I have what I need to begin setting our final plan into motion, which I will now describe to you....'
'Have you had no luck finding the Gauradan-wards I sent you for? They should be easy enough to find some ways north of here where the creatures are well encamped.'
Gather Gauradan-wards (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the Gauradan-wards to Erchiel
Wards of the Gauredain
Lithuifin has suggested a solution to Erchiel regarding the Gauradan that seems rather less violent than her previous approach.

'Ba-barum! Little Erchiel sends you to interfere with the Gauredain again, does she?
'Very well -- but be certain you do not arouse their wrath, nor lead them to this place with your games.'

'I see you are bringing more of the Gauradan-wards. Hoom!
'I suppose little Erchiel will be looking for those. You had best not keep her waiting. She is remarkably hasty, even for one who is not of the Ents.'

'Erchiel has decided on another course of action has she?
'That is well. As a master of the sword, she is oft too quick to draw it, particularly so given the vast wisdom upon which she may draw when she takes the time to consider.
'But then, we are all creatures of habit, are we not? To each of us there is the path more preferred -- but hers has brought her too much pain, and I am always glad when she is able to find other ways.'

'I think I know what Erchiel has in mind. You should bring the wards you have collected to her swiftly.'
'Did I mention that she is not the most patient of Elves? You would think that after a few thousand years she might have learned to view the passage of time more charitably.'

'Do not tarry here. It is only a matter of time before the Gauradan-hunters stumble upon this place, and then bloodshed will be unavoidable.
'Gather the wards from their encampments and return with them as soon as you can.'

Erchiel has asked you to steal a number of the wards that are scattered around the Gauradan-encampments.
The Gauradan-encampments are north of the Eavespires.

Collected colourful berries (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I must beg your pardon, for I may have forgotten to mention how I keep the giants convinced that this forest is haunted. It is easier than you might assume.
'I need you to collect some berries from the bushes that grow in this part of the forest -- they are quite sweet, but I suggest that you not sample them, lest you find yourself led far astray by their effects. The taste may be flavourful, but they are more intoxicating than the stoutest of dwarf-ales.
'Bring me several handfuls, and I will prepare a fine treat for the giants. They can be found south of the Eavespires and east of Amon Môth.'

'These seem fresh and vibrant and should do quite nicely. Allow me a few minutes to prepare a batch. Giants have a constitution to match their great size, and this is one of the few draughts that can have any real effect on them.
'Just wait and you shall see what I mean!'
'You have not been able to find the berries? They mostly grown in the forest nearby to the south, as I recall.'

Lithuifin the Elf is concerned with the giants which have been ruining the forest.
'You were unable to find the beriies. They grew quite plentifully in the forests just a short distance south of here.'

You stole a lucky stone

'Greetings and welcome to our distant outpost here in the wilds of Evendim. I am called Lithuifin. I could use your assistance. There is a band of Hill-giants who have taken up residence at the western edge of the forest. Nasty brutes they are and taken to smashing trees and tromping the undergrowth in such a fashion that it makes Longbough's knots itch just to consider it.
'Now I myself prefer battles of trickery to those of the blade when dealing with fellows thrice my height and one-tenth my wit, and so I suggest this plan to you: for some years now I have instilled a fear of wood-spirits and sprites in the giants -- nay, there are none such, at least not hereabouts, but the giants do not know that. Flickering lights in the distant woods, the unexplained disappearance of important things, strange and unearthly sounds -- all the sort of things you might use to scare children and keep them from wandering into a dangerous wood. The giants are little wiser than children themselves and much the same ploy keeps them out of this forest...usually.
'The giants have been growing bolder again of late -- perhaps you could...raise the spirits once more? I happen to know that one of the giants that guards the outskirts of their encampment has a cherished lucky stone he keeps near his person -- a rock of no true value, I would wager. See if you can snatch it away when his attention is elsewhere. There is a small rock cairn I left nearby to help provide a means of distraction. Be sure to move quickly and stay unnoticed, or you will likely be stepped on.'

'You have returned, and with the giant's keepsake no less! Well done, indeed.
'Now that you have proven yourself up to the task, I have a somewhat more complicated duty for you.'

'Ah, no luck yet with the giants? I hope you are not too much the worse for wear. Keep at it, and remember that where brawn and the glorious strength of steel fail us, a bit of humble trickery will often suffice!'
Steal a lucky stone from the giants of Amon Môth

'No luck yet?
'As I recall, the giant in question stands guard near the northern outskirts of Amon Môth. There should be a small cairn of stones nearby to mark the place.
'Do be careful. The giants are not terribly bright, but they are quite strong.'

Amon Môth is located to the west and south of the Eavespires, and the cairn Lithuifin mentioned is somewhere on the northern outskirts of their camp.

'The giants tend to gather each day for a large meal somewhere near the southern end of their encampment where they have placed an enormous stew-pot.
'Your goal is simplicity itself -- make your way quietly to the pot in the midst and slip this into their meal, then escape before you are stepped on.
'If you can manage to stay nearby, you may find the events to follow amusing.'
'That should keep them occupied for a while, though I am not sure you were as successful as I had hoped....'

The poster advertises a bounty on a vicious Warg named Thauk, described as a 'bloodthirsty creature known to be in league with the goblins that stalk Tyrn Fornech,' and invites interested parties to seek out Rowena Parker in Ost Forod for details and to apply for the commission.

'You have come to inquire about Thauk? He is a dreadful creature, bloodthirsty and dangerous! It is said that he is in league with the goblins that prowl the hills of Tyrn Fornech. If you can defeat him, they might be affected as well.
'Look for Thauk within the crude goblin-camp at Tûm Fuin, north of Ost Forod. He likely prowls throughout the camp, keeping an eye on the goblins and stirring them to greater mischief.
'Thauk is a great beast, and dangerous! You will need your wits about you if you hope to claim his bounty!'

'You have returned from Tûm Fuin? That means that you have defeated Thauk?
'Amazing, ${PLAYER}! If you report to Basil Gummidge, the arbiter here in Ost Forod, he'll give you your reward.
'Thauk will trouble us no more? I cannot believe it!'
'You defeated Thauk? Then you deserve this reward, ${PLAYER}. That bounty has remained unclaimed for a long time. I thank you on behalf of the law-abiding folk of Ost Forod!'
Bounty: Thauk, Vile Warg
A bounty has been taken out on Thauk, a vicious Warg in league with the goblins that prowl Tyrn Fornech.

'Good luck with Thauk. He is a vicious monster and will not be an easy bounty to claim!
'Look for him at the goblin-camp at Tûm Fuin, north of Ost Forod.'

'Basil Gummidge, our arbiter, is here in Ost Forod. Speak to him about the business of your reward.
'I still cannot believe that you managed to defeat vile Thauk! How brave you are, ${PLAYER}!'
'Defeating Thauk was no small thing, ${PLAYER}. He was truly vicious.'
'Your service to Ost Forod will never be forgotten.'
'I cannot believe you defeated evil Thauk! Amazing!'
'You are a tremendous help to we who live in Tyrn Fornech, ${PLAYER}!'

The poster advertises a bounty on a man named Andy Idden, accusing him of dealing with goblins and conspiring to murder decent folk in Ost Forod. It invites interested parties to seek out Poppy Seaton in Ost Forod for details and to apply for the commission.

'You're interested in claiming the bounty on Andy Idden? If you can defeat him, you'll certainly have earned it. Andy is mean-tempered and brutal and has friends of the same mind: goblins, if you believe the tales, and I do!
'I've heard that Andy Idden has gone with his wolf-hound to the ruins of Tham Andalath on some business with the goblins that lurk there. He'd sell out his neighbours to the goblins, if he thought there was profit in it, and is probably doing just that right now!
'Tham Andalath is on a hill-top a short distance east of Canadiach, the crossroads south of here in Parth Aduial, and north of the road. They're crawling with goblins, so claiming the bounty on Andy Idden won't be easy. Good luck to you, ${PLAYER}!'

'Andy Idden was a deadly foe, ${PLAYER}, meeting with goblins, and I know that you've earned your bounty!
'If you report to Basil Gummidge, the arbiter here in Ost Forod, he'll give you your reward.'

'I heard that you put an end to Andy Idden, ${PLAYER}, and none too soon! He's always been a lout, but by befriending goblins he went too far. The folk of Ost Forod are safer for your assistance, and it is my pleasure to reward you for your service.'
Bounty: Andy Idden, Goblin-friend
A bounty has been taken out on Andy Idden, a tomb-robber rumoured to have dealings with goblins.

'Remember, the ruins of Tham Andalath are south of here, in Parth Aduial. If you travel to the crossroads of Canadiach, you'll find the ruins a short distance east of there, on a hill north of the road.'
'Basil Gummidge, our arbiter, is here in Ost Forod. Speak to him about the business of your reward.'
'My advice to you, ${PLAYER}, is to never befriend a goblin!'
'Andy Idden has always been trouble, and he's often brought it to Ost Forod.'
'Thank you for your help, ${PLAYER}! Andy Idden was trouble.'
'You have been a big help to we of Ost Forod, ${PLAYER}!'
