'There's been a troubling development, ${PLAYER}, and it's best that you hear it from me before seeing it for yourself. You've done a lot of good for this town by claiming the bounties on some of the villains hereabouts, and it wouldn't be right for me to let you walk into trouble without warning.
'Someone's been putting up posters. I've been taking them down wherever I come across them, but I kept one up on the wall over there so you could have a look. Go read it and take it down, and then we can have a talk about what can be done.
'The poster is just over there on the wall, by the stairs.'

The poster is written in a messy scrawl, but the words leap off the parchment at you:
'For the death of ${PLAYER}, ${CLASS} of no account, Cuthbert Sprunt offers two gold pieces. This ${RACE} has come to Evendim and caused nothing but trouble. Just ask Mrs. Idden where her boy Andy is, or the widow Tripper why her son Will is missing a brother!'
Beneath a brief but unflattering description of you, an angry hand has scrawled something else:
'If you think you've been wronged in this, ${PLAYER}, \qbounty-hunter,\q then you come talk to Mr. Sprunt at the Sparring Circle. We'll sort it out, fair-like.'

'Well-fought, ${PLAYER}, well-fought indeed! Sprunt will not dare face you again, and his band is well-warned now of your skill!
'They know now what I have known for some time: ${PLAYER} is a bounty-hunter, not the bounty!'

'You see why I'm concerned, ${PLAYER}? I know this Cuthbert Sprunt, a villain of the lowest measure, and the sum he's offering for your head is enough to have even the good folk of Ost Forod thinking twice, and there are plenty here who need only think on it once! You're a marked ${RACE} now, my friend -- the bounty-hunter becomes the bounty!
'You want to fight this, don't you? You want to best Sprunt in single combat? If you can show that you're tougher than he is, I expect there will be few willing to claim the bounty. I'll stand by you, ${PLAYER}.
'Talk to me when you're ready, and we can see what he has in store at the Sparring Circle. He won't turn down a challenge, I expect, but I'll watch him closely to ensure that he doesn't cheat.'
'You haven't brought me the poster I pointed out to you? Why?'
Read the poster near Basil Gummidge
Bring wanted poster to Basil Gummidge
Talk to Basil Gummidge and travel to the Sparring Circle

Basil Gummidge is worried that you may have done too good a job at claiming the bounties posted in Ost Forod, and that you have made a number of enemies.
'The poster is right over there on the wall by the stairs, ${PLAYER}. Go bring it back here, and we can decide what to do about it.'

'Are you ready to travel to the Sparring Circle and confront Cuthbert Sprunt? He won't dare cheat while I'm there, and I'm confident you can defeat him and make him take down these ridiculous posters!'

The poster advertises a bounty on a man named Harry Hinchcliffe, described as 'a tomb-robber possessed of uncanny accuracy with his bow,' and invites interested parties to seek out Ballard Wilmer in Ost Forod for details and to apply for the commission.

'You're interested in applying for the commission on Harry Hinchcliffe? Very good, very good! There aren't many travellers up to Forochel these days, but what few there are have been harried by his arrows.
'Some of his friends linger by the Forochel gate at Cirith Rhîw. Just follow the northern road through Tyrn Fornech to reach it.
'If you can capture or defeat Harry, you'll be doing the law-abiding folk of Ost Forod a good turn. Be warned, however -- you aren't the first to attempt to break Hinchcliffe's bow! Perhaps you will be the last, eh?'

'You bested Harry Hinchcliffe? Ha! To be honest, I didn't think you would be successful! It just goes to show, doesn't it?
'Basil Gummidge, the arbiter of Ost Forod, is here in town. Speak to him about the business of your reward.'

'Harry Hinchcliffe is no more? Splendid, ${PLAYER}! He was a menace, and if travel to Forochel becomes commonplace again, it is good to know the road will be safer without the like of him on it!
'Here is your reward, and thank you for your service.'

'Good luck with Harry! He's a deadly shot with a bow, he is, and has made short work of others seeking to claim the bounty on him.
'You'll likely find him by the gate to Forochel, at Cirith Rhîw. It's at the end of the road that runs north through Tyrn Fornech.'
'Basil Gummidge, our arbiter, is here in Ost Forod. You should speak to him about the business of your reward, ${PLAYER}.'
'Harry Hinchcliffe was a deadly shot, but not too deadly for you!'
'It is to be hoped that one day the road to Forochel will bustle with trade.'
'I am sorry for thinking you could not defeat Harry Hinchcliffe!'

The poster advertises a bounty on a man named Bill Tripper, described as a 'notorious tomb-robber, highly-skilled with blades,' and invites interested parties to seek out Clark Standish in Ost Forod for details and to apply for the commission.

'You're here to see about the bounty on Bill Tripper? I'm glad to hear it -- the sooner we're rid of him, the better, if you ask me!
'Bill has been robbing and murdering around the hills of Tyrn Fornech for some months now, and it's well-past time someone stopped him. Last I heard, he'd travelled south into Parth Aduial and was holed up in a big ruin south of the crossroads...Tham Varan, I think it was called.
'If you do go looking to collect the bounty, keep an eye on Bill's sword -- he's deadly with it, and I'd just as soon not have your death on my conscience!'
'So you're the one that finally put an end to old Bill Tripper? Very good! If you report to Basil Gummidge, the arbiter of Ost Forod, he'll give you your reward.'

Collected the Formal Complaint

'Never in all my days have I heard of decent folk getting attacked in the Shire. Even if this is the Northfarthing, folk should still be decent and civil, though I wouldn't put such treachery past these Big Men.
'I've asked Ronald Dwale to draft a formal letter of complaint to the leader of these Men, Will Tuffin. He is always in and out of the big hole down in Dwaling centre. I would like you to get the letter from Dwale and take it to Will Tuffin straightaway. Just go down to the big hole down yonder and ring the bell until Will comes out. Make sure you don't go alone, I don't trust these Big Folk.
'Take care that you don't let them bully you this time.'

'What's that now? Shut the door in your face? Well, if that isn't the rudest thing I have heard all day!
'I have a spare key to the big hole. It's a public building, and even if they own the whole town, they haven't the right to close up a public hole!
'You march right in there and make sure he reads every word of that letter.
'Talk to me again when you are ready to go down to the big hole.'

'Ah yes, Hob asked me to draw up a letter of complaint after you found out about that business with Pearlina Gamgee.
'Business letters are not my usual fare; I am more used to crafting more fanciful stories and letters, but I daresay I did as fine a job as any could have asked for.'

'So their leader wouldn't take the letter? I can't say I didn't expect trouble from these ruffians. I am going to have another formal complaint written to this 'investor' and tell him just what I think about the character of these Men he has let into the Shire.
'You mentioned something about a goblin faced fellow and someone named Sharkey? I'm sure you must be mistaken; there haven't been naught like them in the Shire since the Bullroarer's time, and I have never heard of anyone with a name such as Sharkey.
'But what with all the excitement, I am sure you can't be blamed for your mistake.'
'Did you deliver the letter, ${PLAYER}?'
Retrieve the formal complaint from Ronald Dwale
Ring the doorbell and deliver the letter
Talk to Hob Hillbrow

A Formal Complaint
The ruffians which have moved into Dwaling are lawless and brutal, and Hob Hillbrow has had enough of their wicked ways.
'Go over and talk to Ronald, he should have the letter ready.'

'Are you ready for me to let you into the big hole?
'Make sure you bring companions; who knows what those Big Folk will do once you're inside.'
'Hob wanted you to bring the letter to Will Tuffin down at the big hole in Dwaling centre.'
'My! I had hoped that the ruffians would be more cooperative than that! Well, I suppose you've solved our problems for a while, though.'
'Well, I suppose there was naught else that could be done about such ruffians. At any rate, I do wish my words had not been wasted. Good work, regardless!'

'Now, this hobbit I was telling you about before, he let Big Men buy up all the land...right here in the Shire! I have talked to old Ronald about sending a letter to old Will Whitfoot, the mayor, but I don't know what he can do against a sound contract like the one sent to my door.
'One of my dear friends, Pearlina Gamgee, is away in the Westfarthing looking for a snug hole to start over in, and I told her that I would look after her home while she was away. Those new Men in town have a foul look about them, and I don't much trust them, even if they claim to be here to \qhelp\q.
'If you could, go down and check on Pearlina Gamgee's residence just west of here in Dwaling. You look like you could hold your own if any of those ruffians gave you any trouble.'
'Well I never...! These Big Folk are violating their contracts! What are these times coming to?'

'It must have been the beginning of fall; I was with my son on the banks of the Brandywine enjoying the sun, a fine meal, and a full pipe, while he sat and played with his favourite toy -- a piece of lead fashioned into a small dog -- by the side of the river.
'My boy was very fond of this toy, but when it came time to leave, it wasn't anywhere to be found. I tried to console him with one of my stories. I created quite a wonderful tale about the toy's whereabouts, but if you are heading that way, perhaps you could search for it?
'The toy has to be somewhere in the Barandalf, the sand marshes north and east of Dwaling. I have heard that strange burrowing creatures have since inhabited the area. There is a good chance one of them could have swallowed it up, thinking it to be food.'
'Were you able to find the toy, ${PLAYER}? Ah, I see you did. Many thanks to you!'
'One of those burrowing creatures on the river-bank should have the toy, ${PLAYER}.'

'${CLASS}, I beg your pardon, but I haven't any other to turn to in these dark times. Please hear me out. Dwaling has never been a rich town, but we have always gotten by on our own. Many of the best glassblowers in the Shire were found in these holes. My dad before me was a glassblower -- best in the North and Eastfarthings -- and I learned the trade from him.
'Recently, things turned for the worse for our little town. What with all the wild creatures about, folk are plain afraid of the north Bounds nowadays. Most of the folk have moved away and sold off their property after business stopped. A hobbit out of the Westfarthing sent letters and contracts up this way purchasing holes and land until he bought up almost the whole town...that's when all the trouble began.
'I used to get white sand for my glassblowing from a dear old friend who would travel into the Barandalf to the north-east of Dwaling, but he moved away not a week ago. If you would, travel up to the Sand Marshes and get me some. I would be deeply in your debt.'
'You have the sand, and just in the nick of time too! My lads were just finishing up the last of our supplies.'
'You should be able to find white sand in the Sand Marshes just over the hill.'

'If my last task was not too taxing, I am in great need of some assistance from a fellow lover of the written word. I would hope that a ${RACE} of your reputation would be interested in assisting me.
'Not long ago, I seemed to have misplaced a very important leaf of paper while I was walking with my notes. This paper contains the beginning lines of a story I plan on writing for my children that has been conjuring in my head for some time now. Now that most of the town has been sold off, I have not been able to search for my paper. The last time I tried to have a look around, I was chased off by a group of those ruffians.
'I would rewrite it, but I cannot seem to recall the exact wording. If you could find it, I would be deeply in your debt. I think I dropped it somewhere in town.'

'I simply cannot start my book without that page. Have you found it yet?
'Ah, I see you have. Many thanks!'
'I know I dropped that paper somewhere here in Dwaling.'

'Well now, you have been helpful haven't you? If you could, I do have one last task for you to assist me with. Among the Hobbits of the Shire, a love of languages and written works is quite uncommon. A few of my fellow colleagues and I have formed a small informal gathering of sorts for those of us who revel in such art as the writing and listening of fictional stories.
'We usually meet in the evenings, down at the Bird -- that is, The Bird and Baby Inn in Michel Delving. With the return of my lost paper, I really should get started on my new book, but I haven't an inkling how I should reach my friends in time to tell them of my absence.
'If you would, go quickly and visit Jack Lewisdown at The Bird and Baby before the meeting starts and let him know that I will not be making it tonight.'
'Why hullo there.'

'You were able to make it before the meeting started? Wonderful! I already have the first chapter started.
'Old Lewisdown thought I would be playing games instead of working? I daresay he knows I would never think of getting involved in something so silly.'
Missing the Meeting
Ronald Dwale is indisposed and will be unable to attend the next meeting of his writing society.

'Prepare yourself, maggot. This tower needs a solid defence!'

Defeat the enemy within the walls of Lugazag.
The enemy will fall as they crash against the walls, provided you stand against them as they attempt to crash the walls.

Soldier Gazlup is at Lugazag. If the tower was lost to the enemy or Soldier Gazlup was beaten during the fighting, make your way to Gramsfoot and speak with War-tyrant Akúlhun.
YOu should return to Gazlup and report of your victory.
Defeated Grimwood Lumber-camp (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen well you pathetic excuse for a warrior. Battle will soon come to this lumber-camp, and we'd best prepare for the onslaught.
'You'll defend the camp, staying within the bounds of the lumber-yard itself, and stand against the enemy as they come. You'll do this because I say you will.
'If we lose the camp or I should fall, report to the War-tyrant at Gramsfoot. Face him and tell him that you fought against the foe...he will choose your fate. If I stand, I will see that you are rewarded for your efforts.'

'You did well against our enemy at the Grimwood camp...
'Yet you return to me for your reward, which means my kin is lost. I will check my ire and curb my dissapointment, for I know that many of the Free Peoples suffered by your hand. This success is fleeting, maggot. See that you do better in the future.'

'Our victory is complete, and you have been a necessary member of the defence. You are to be commended for your assistance here, maggot.
'Do not let this meagre success boost your thoughts of rising through the ranks of Angmar, though. You are nothing more than a maggot meant to be slaughtered by our enemies, until you prove otherwise.
'For now, I recognize your contributions. You will need to perform as well in the future to earn my respect.'
Defeat Free Peoples at the Grimwood Lumber-camp (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Grinding Bones in the Grimwood
Chieftain Torbok prepares the defence of the Grimwood Lumber-yard against the Free Peoples.
'Prepare yourself, the Free Peoples will not let us stay here long without coming to liberate the camp. We are too close to their precious rat-folk.'

Fight Angmar's foes within the bounds of the Grimwood Lumber-camp.
You were instructed to stand this ground and fight for the glory of Angmar in defence of the Grimwood Lumber-camp.

If Torbol is defeated or the lumber camp has fallen to the Free Peoples, return to Gramsfoot and face the wrath of War-tyrant Akúlhun.
You should return to Chieftain Torbok at the Grimwood Lumber Camp to gloat of your victories against the Free Peoples.
Defeated Free Peoples in the Isendeep Mine (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You pathetic worm. You look as though you've soured yourself in my presence and that gives me the urge to scourge the flesh from your back.
'You'll be useful to our army if your sacrifice yourself against the enemy. Stand within the Isendeep and repel the invaders as they cross into these halls. Survive and you might just earn a little favour.
'If you succeed return to me. If you fail, and I feel the sting of arrows...know that I will find you one day and scourge your body to the bone.'

'Your efforts are noted, and the failures of others to hold their position is well-known to me. I recognize what you have done, ${PLAYER}.
'Know this...letting superiors die will be punishable by whipping and reassignment to the brimstone-pits of Angmar. Remember well that you're nothing more than a maggot, and you'll live. Try to reach beyond those bounds, and I'll see you spend your life in the brimstone-pits.
'For now, I recognize your efforts and will honour you with thanks.'

'Well done! I may have misjudged your resolve.
'I'll try to remember to look favourably upon you in the future. Don't expect that I shall!'
Defeat Free Peoples in the Isendeep Mine (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Hold the Mine
Taskmaster Bárzqhosh is preparing the defence of the Isendeep Mine against the Free Peoples.
'Leave my sight, cur! Do what I ask, or I'll lose my temper!'

Fight off invaders who meant to take the Isendeep mine.
You must fight the foe within the Isendeep mine and drive them out for the glory of Angmar.

If the mine is fallen or Taskmaster Bárzqhosh is fallen in the battle, make your way to Gramsfoot and speak with War-tyrant Akúlhun.
Your success is complete. Return to Taskmaster Bárzqhosh and tell him of your victory.
Defeated Free Peoples at Tol Ascarnen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Listen well, you maggot! Our leader says to make ready the walls and secure our position. Strike to kill the Free Peoples that move towards the walls of Tol Ascarnen.
'You'll do this, you'll do this well, and you'll report to me when your job is done.
'If I fall -- your soft belly best hope I don't end up with my back flat on the ground or my face planted in a pool of my blood -- get to the War-tyrant at Gramsfoot, and he'll chide you for your failure to keep me alive, but maybe show you some favour for slaughtering the Free Peoples.'

'You lived through the onslaught, eh, maggot? I may have misjudged your strength and ability.
'I will inform others of your success, but you best not let this meagre victory go too far to your filthy head.'

'Apsduf talks a lot, maggot. He's worth about as much as that troll-dropping over there to me.
'I need soldiers, not quartermasters. You've proven you're a soldier. Now get out of my sight, for you'll earn no greater compliment this day.'
Defeat the Free Peoples at Tol Ascarnen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Scour the Walls Clean
Quartermaster Apsduf prepares the defence of Tol Ascarnen against the Free Peoples.
'Are you testing to see if my whip-arm is strong? I can assure you it is strong and willing to strip the flesh off your backside. Make ready your preparations, worm. The battle will soon be at hand.'

Slaughter the Free Peoples in and around Tol Ascarnen to earn the favour of your masters.
Quartermaster Apsduf told you to prepare for battle against the Free Peoples and to do your part to repel them from Tol Ascarnen.

If Apsduf is slain or Tol Ascarnen was taken by the enemy, go to War-Tyrant Akúlhun at Gramsfoot.
You have successfully slaughtered the Free Peoples and should return to Apsduf to claim your reward.
Defeatesd Free Peoples at Grothum (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You, there! The Free Peoples are coming, and we are frightened. We need your help. Yes, we are whimpering creatures not fit to carry the banner of Angmar. I grovel at your mighty feet and ask you for help.
'You will give help, for you must!
'Kill the Free Peoples that come here to Grothum. Kill them in our village!'

'You protect us! You do good! We live! Angmar prevails!
'We thank you and offer you the honour you deserve.'

'My scouts told me you helped those miserable wretches at Grothum. You honour the pact we made, but do not think that the goblins are anything more than dirt.
'We should focus our attention on something other than our servants in the future.'
Defeat the Free Peoples at Grothum (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defend Us
The Free Peoples have been coming into Grothum village, killing goblins and stealing their food and ale.
'Help us! Help us now!'

Slaughter the Free Peoples as they attempt to destroy the goblins of Grothum.
You have been asked to honour the pledge made by Angmar to assist the goblins against the Free Peoples, an obligation you must fulfil.

Grothum is defended and your obligation to the goblins is complete. Return to Gasham and tell him so. If Gasham was killed return to the War-tyrant and tell him of your victory.
Fighting off the enemy within the bounds of Grothum proved a simple task for one such as you.

'In an age long past, the Misty Mountains were home to many of my kin. Now they crawl with goblins in all places save Moria where Durin's folk still hold the darkness at bay.
'The goblins in the north, at Grothum their accursed village, are the same that dwell in the place called Goblin-town. These savage little beasts are vile and cruel fiends, desiring only to serve the Dark Lord and the will of all evil manner. We can do our part, however, and crush them. Drive them back into their mountain halls and pursue them until there is nowhere else for them to flee.
'Go north, friend. North to where the hills take on the dark color of mountain slate. You will find their accursed village. Find the guards and sappers there and put an end to their fiendish ways.'

'A glorious victory for the Free Peoples! Those little beasts deserve no better.
'Your work is far from done, but this is a victory well-earned. Take this with my thanks. Remember that Quartermaster Ash will furnish you a key in exchange for a fair number of these.'
Fiendish Foes

Lieutenant Ingi explained that the Snowreap goblins are the same who inhabit Goblin-town and the bulk of the Misty Mountains. He knows that they are an ally to Angmar and wants to see their numbers culled.
'See this done, friend. Goblins are among the cruelest creatures in these hills. We'll be better served with them driven far from these lands.'

There are Snowreap-guards and sappers at Grothum, north of Ost Ringdyr.
Lieutenant Ingi wishes to cull the Snowreap goblins from the Ettenmoors and weaken the forces which Angmar can bring to bear agains the Free Peoples.

Ingi is at Ost Ringdyr, south of Grothum.
With the goblins dispatched, the time has come to return to Ingi.

'Your time in the Ettenmoors will be fraught with danger. Angmar's army is bolstered by their own allies, and they are cruel and vicious.
'If you make your way north of Glân Vraig and follow the valley to the east, you will emerge at the ruins of Ost Ringdyr. Inside, you should seek out Lieutenant Ingi. He is a dwarf of great repute who has come to help us. He is handling the assault on one of Angmar's allies.
'To reach Ost Ringdyr, travel north along the edge of the hills and outcroppings that lead towards the Misty Mountains. You will ride through a valley for a short time and emerge on a path guarded by our people. Be wary, the woods are teeming with the Enemy.'

'Another fresh recruit? Well you've come to a place in dire need of your aid, ${CLASS}.
'Ever since we arrived, Angmar's forces have made a regular habit of assailing us wherever we travel. There are very few safe places to move. You're here to learn a bit about the Enemy, and I am ready to oblige, but be warned the Enemy travels the Ettenmoors largely unchecked and in great number. You will need to use caution and stealth.
'North of our location, behind the safety of great dark stones, lies the goblin-village of Grothum, a vile place that sits at the east side of the Isendeep Mine, once a dwarf-mine. I need help in defeating those goblins.'
Ruins of Ost Ringdyr
Lieutenant Ingi at Ost Ringdyr may be able to tell you what you can do to support the Free Peoples in the Ettenmoors.

Lieutenant Ingi is at Ost Ringdyr, north and east of Glân Vraig.
Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn directed you to report to Ost Ringdyr to learn about the allies of Angmar's Army from Lieutenant Ingi.

'Lainedhel discovered the Little Folk while he was scouting the wilderness here in the north. He blames himself for Angmar discovering their location as they seem to have lived here for generations beneath everyone's notice, even the trolls.
'Since his discovery, the Uruk-warleaders have ordered continuous assaults against the village, and the hobbits there, resilient and proud, have taken up arms to defend their homes. Mayor Wat Mudbottom leads them and has asked for little help. He sent a single emissary, Pip Diggins, to Ost Ringdyr to entreat with Lainedhel and has received weapons and arms from us in return for food that he and his people grow and hunt.
'Please, if you can, visit Mayor Wat Mudbottom and assist him however you may.'

'Merry me! Did the folk over in that Elf-home send you? Good people they are, always trying to be helpful, keeping close watch over our hovels.
'We are struggling, there can be no doubt of that, ever since the arrival of these beasts. Most are smarter than a troll, and though wolves have always been a bother, the wolves that have come now are much more frightening. We're concerned with the spiders too, but only because their webs are awfully hard to pull from the hair on our feet.
'No doubt you have come to help, and we are grateful, truly we are. Emerald, along the road to the south and east, might need some help, if you ask her. Ned over at the store-house, just over this rise behind me and down to the water's edge, can always use a hand. And at the crest of the hill, north a bit, you will find Marigold. See if they might need anything, would you?'
Our Friends in Hoarhallow
Ascwyn mentioned that Hoarhallow is besieged by the forces of Angmar and that the hobbits can use any help you could offer.

Mayor Wat Mudbottom is at Hoarhallow far to the west of Glán Vraig, through the Grimwood Forest, on the banks of the Hoarwell River.
Beset by the Enemy, the Hobbits of Hoarhallow are a hardy and proud people. Their Mayor, Wat Mudbottom, leads them and refuses to give up the land they own to the forces of Angmar. Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn directed you to speak with Wat Mudbottom.

'I speak for the Free Peoples of Eriador, friend. The Ettenmoors, a land corrupt and lost to evil for many years, is the staging ground for an invasion from the north. Angmar's forces muster beneath the shadow of Mount Gram and plan to launch an assault into the south.
'Captain-General Lainedhel headed north against his Lord's wishes and called a host to stand with him. Now a small but able band of us stands against the onslaught, but we are outnumbered, and if not bolstered, we will succumb to the tide.
'If you are willing, I would ask you to make your way to Glân Vraig in the Ettenmoors. Many of the stable-masters have assisted us and trained horses to find their way to the Ettenmoors. When you arrive, speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn.'

'I ask a request for the Free People of Eriador, friend. The Ettenmoors, a land corrupt and lost to evil for many years is the staging ground for an invasion from the north. Angmar's forces muster beneath the shadow of Mount Gram and plan to launch an assault into the south.
'Captain-General Lainedhel headed north against his Lord's wishes and called a host to stand with him. Now a small but able band of us stands against the onslaught, but we are outnumbered and if not bolstered we will succumb to the tide.
'If you are willing, I would ask you to make your way to the Ettenmoors. Many of the stable masters have assisted us and trained horses to find their way to the Ettenmoors. When you arrive, speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn, she is acclimating all new recruits to the defense.'

'I ask a request for the Free People of Eriador, friend. The Ettenmoors, a land corrupt and lost to evil for many years is the staging ground for an invasion from the north. Angmar's forces muster beneath the shadow of Mount Gram and plan to launch an assault into the south.
'Captain-General Lainedhel headed north against his Lord's wishes and called a host to stand with him. Now a small but able band of us stands against the onslaught, but we are outnumbered and if not bolstered we will succumb to the tide.
'If you are willing, I would ask you to make your way to the Ettenmoors. Many of the stable masters have assisted us and trained horses to find their way to the Ettenmoors. When you arrive, speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn, she is acclimating all new recruits to the defense.'

'I ask a request for the Free People of Eriador, friend. The Ettenmoors, a land corrupt and lost to evil for many years is the staging ground for an invasion from the north. Angmar's forces muster beneath the shadow of Mount Gram and plan to launch an assault into the south.
'Captain-General Lainedhel headed north against his Lord's wishes and called a host to stand with him. Now a small but able band of us stands against the onslaught, but we are outnumbered and if not bolstered we will succumb to the tide.
'If you are willing, I would ask you to make your way to the Ettenmoors. Many of the stable masters have assisted us and trained horses to find their way to the Ettenmoors. When you arrive, speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn, she is acclimating all new recruits to the defense.'

'Our emissaries have succeeded beyond our expectations. I am Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn and this is Glân Vraig, our foothold in the Ettenmoors. We are led here by Captain-General Thurimbent...Lainedhel is to the north at the ruined keep, Ost Ringdyr.
'I am sorry, I am getting ahead of myself. There are several enemies in the Ettenmoors and few allies. The eagles led by Golloval support us here in the Coldfells, as do the golden bears led by Goldhead. Far to the west, a small town of hobbits rests on the Hoarwell. None knew they were here.
'It is good to see more arrivals. I have much to teach you, if you are willing to assist us.'
A Plea from Lainedhel

A force out of Angmar threatens to press south into Eriador. A lone Elf has organized a band of defenders to stand against the army out of the north and dispatched emissaries to the Free Peoples in search of heroes willing to make a stand against Angmar's army.

Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn is at Glân Vraig in the Ettenmoors.
Captain-General Lainedhel's emissaries are asking any would-be heroes to make their way into the Ettenmoors to bolster their small numbers. Many stable-masters have trained horses who can take you to the Ettenmoors. You should speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn upon your arrival there.
Defeated minions of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'If you are truly willing to help, ${PLAYER}, then I would ask you to take up arms against the foe stalking us here in our village. We cannot keep them out forever and even our stalwart guards must find time for rest.
'Stay in the village of Hoarhallow a while, friend. Fight and drive back the foe as they come into the village, and I will see that you are well rewarded.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You are proving an invaluable ally against this terrible foe. I think that I shall ask you to help us again one day.
'For now, I have asked too much of you and offered too little. Please take this with my thanks and know that you have earned the friendship of the Hobbits of Hoarhallow.'
Defeat minions of Angmar at Hoarhallow (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defence of Hoarhallow
Mayor Wat Mudbottom wants some assistance in clearing the beasts of Angmar out of Hoarhallow.
'Keep the wards strong! They will not retreat so easily.'

Stay within the bounds of Hoarhallow village and stop the forces of Angmar threatening the hobbits there.
Mayor Wat Mudbottom enlisted your aid in fighting back the foes within the area of Hoarhallow.

Mayor Mudbottom is in Hoarhallow.
Now that you have assisted in the defence of Hoarhallow you should speak with Mayor Wat Mudbottom about the reward he offered you.
Defeated minions of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our fortunes will not hold forever, ${PLAYER}. Soon the dark charges of Angmar will muster and crash, wave after wave upon the walls of this forsken tower. If we stand fast, we may yet survive the assault. If you are willing, stand with us, and we shall give them all we have and more. They will fall by the score to our host, and we shall hold them at bay until we drive them from this place.
'Stand with us, defeat the foe as they crash against the walls of Lugazag, and when this is done, I shall see you rewarded. If I fall in battle, scouts will inform Captain-General Tordúr of your bravery, and you may claim your reward from him.
'What say you?'

'My scouts have indeed informed me of your efforts at Lugazag. You are most welcome here in the Ettenmoors, ${PLAYER}. Long have we waited for heroes willing to do all that you have done.
'We are indebted to you. Please take this small reward and know that we strive to find more to offer those who serve the Free Peoples.'

'Your effort in defending the tower is well-known. We are pleased to offer you this reward. It is not much, but the rewards that you shall claim are taken from those who fall within these accursed lands.
'You are most welcome in the company of the Free Peoples, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat minions of Angmar at Lugazag (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defence of Lugazag

At the pinnacle of Lugazag, the tower on the easternmost edge of the Ettenmoors, once a stronghold for Angmar's army, now flies the flags of the Free Peoples. Angmar's army is well aware of this and wishes to return the tower to their control. Moreover, their taskmasters and war-tyrants will drive them to recover the location at all costs.

Fight and slaughter the foes from Angmar within the area of Lugazag.
Sergeant-at-Arms Ambeng wants to ensure that the Free Peoples are prepared for the onslaught that will ensue at the walls of Lugazag and enlisted your help in driving the foe from the field. Stay within the immediate area of the tower and stand against the foe. If Ambeng or Lugazag falls, report to Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig.

If Lugazag and Sergeant-at-Arms Ambeng still stand, report to him for your reward. If the tower was lost or Ambeng fell in battle, report to Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig.
You stood against the foe within the walls of Lugazag. Your efforts were not in vain, and you are owed a well-earned reward.
Free Person Slaughtered (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The people are coming. Pests with pointy sticks and arrows. We're not ready, I keep telling the tyrant. We only have you pathetic wretches to stand against them.
'We need your bodies, either to cast at the enemy as they draw near...or to stack in the entry way to seal it shut. I've seen you fight, and we'll not last with you on the defence, or so says I.
'The Tyrant thinks otherwise and bids me offer you favour should you defeat a goodly number of the enemy when they come rushing to the tower. Stand against them and earn his favour...or prove me right, and we'll toss your body in the hall to stop their progress.'

'Survived! We survived, and you did well. I was wrong...wrong and you proved it.
'You'll earn favour, oh yes you shall, but only the favour which I offer. This victory will be mine, maggot. Your part was such a pittance!'

'Fandmau is a whimpering sod. I've a mind to flay him and hang his skin from the gates of Gramsfoot.
'You survived against the foe and took many lives as they stormed the tower. That, at least, earns you a reprieve from Malenhad, worm.'
Slaughter the Free People in Tirith Rhaw (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
These People Be Pests
Fandmau prepares the defence of Tirith Rhaw against the Free Peoples.
'Proving my point about you already, standing here talking instead of preparing for battle. You are a hopeless wretch!'

Slaughter the Free Peoples within the bounds of Tirith Rhaw.
Fandmau seems unimpressed with your capability, but you can show him that you are more of a soldier of Angmar than he.

If Fandmau was killed or Tirith Rhaw was lost, make your way to War-tyrant Akúlhun at Gramsfoot.
Fandmau's fears were unfounded. You repelled the attack and scored a great victory over the Free People. You should return to him with your report.
Collected Hoarhallow ale (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I've something rather difficult to ask you. On my way to Ost Ringdyr, I was to bring two things with me. The first was much too large and the charge was given to your people to handle, that being a large shipment of food and brittleleaf.
'The second was in my charge, and my pony -- loaned me by Captain-General Lainedhel himself -- was doing well until we were beset by the Snowreap goblins out of Grothum. Terrible creatures those. Never had I seen one up close until that moment, and I admit that I was more than startled! I fought for a short time before they ran me off from the cart and pony. I know something terrible became of the pony, but the cargo I was hauling is most likely intact as many enjoy the spirits that we folk of Hoarhallow brew.
'If you could, make your way north from here to Grothum and recover the ale for me. I would be very appreciative.'

'The ale! You brought the ale back. I am indebted to you!
'This was meant to be a gift to the Captain-General for his assistance against the foe from Angmar. We were grateful for his offer and assistance.
'You have helped to preserve my honour and the honour of the people of Hoarhallow. Please take this with my thanks.'
'Please. We may not have much, but we are a proud folk and wish to give Captain-General Lainedhel a gift for all that he has done for us.'
Talk to Pip Diggins
Collect Hoarhallow ale (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Gifts from Hoarhallow

Pip Diggins meant to deliver a large amount of Hoarhallow ale to the Big Folk at Ost Ringdyr. As he was making his way towards the camp, he was forced to run from a pack of savage goblins and left the ale behind. He would truly appreciate any adventurer willing to collect the prize for him from the goblin-village at Grothum.

Grothum lies north of Ost Ringdyr. Pip Diggins is located within the safety of Ost Ringdyr near the cooking oven.
Pip Diggins would like you to recover some of the ale the goblins stole in exchange for a small reward.
Defeated minions of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Our time here is fleeting, ${PLAYER}. We must prepare our defence. Angmar will not let us rest long before they assail these wooden walls in an attempt to drive us out.
'Stay within the lumber-camp with our forces and strike at these villains. Together, we can defeat their forces and drive them back to the darkness from whence they come. I will see that you are rewarded. Should I fall, Tordúr, our Captain-General in Glân Vraig, will hear of your efforts and reward you for the victories you achieve in my stead.
'Stand with us, friend. Stand against this black host and earn your freedom.'

'Scouts reported of the battle within the bounds of the Grimwood Lumber-camp, and your name was mentioned as one who fought with great verve and strength. You are well deserved of this reward, ${PLAYER}.
'My lieutenants are pleased to know that you have come to the Ettenmoors to assist us against this force out of Angmar.'

'We are victorious for the moment, but we cannot rest on these laurels alone. The Enemy is numerous, and unless we remain vigilant, they will find a way to overrun our positions and drive us from this field of battle.
'For your efforts, you are to be commended. You stood strong and fought well, enabling us to maintain this location for a time. Please accept this reward for all you have done.'
Defeat minions of Angmar at the Grimwood Lumber-camp (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defence of the Lumber Camp

Once a harvesting location for the Hobbits of Hoarhallow, the Grimwood Lumber-camp now offers equipment for refining and preparing the wood needed to build palisades throughout the Ettenmoors. Lieutenant Swithulf knows that retribution will come in the form of an assault from Gramsfoot.

Stay within the area of the Grimwood Lumber-camp and defeat the enemy out of Angmar.
Lieutenant Swithulf believes that the Free Peoples can achieve victory with your assistance at the Grimwood Lumber-camp and has asked that you stay and fight to defeat the foe when they come. If Ambeng or Lugazag falls, report to Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig.

Lieutenant Swithulf is at the Grimwood Lumber-camp. If Swithulf fell in battle or the Lumber-camp has fallen to the enemy, make your way to Glân Vraig and speak with Captain-General Tordúr.
Though it was a hard-fought battle, you made your stand and have earned your reward.
The poison of the Angmarim was introduced here.

'${PLAYER}, you are known to many of the Elves of Rivendell...nay, do not be surprised. I have a delicate matter that needs attention, and I believe you may be the ${RACE} for the matter.
'The waterfall above Tol Ascarnen has seen Angmar's forces visiting near its banks. Scouts report that they dump barrels of viscous material into the Hoarwell and further investigation has yielded evidence that the river is being poisoned. I have created a draught that will counteract this poison, but it must be delivered to the Hoarwell quickly.
'I ask that you take this draught and make your way to the waterfall overlooking Tol Ascarnen and deposit it into the river to cleanse the poison. Do this, and I shall see that you are rewarded.'

'This is a great success. You are most welcome here at Glân Vraig, and I hope that you are able to assist the other Free Peoples throughout the Ettenmoors.
'Remember, this war will not be decided easily. We are too few in number to score a decisive blow to the encampment at Gramsfoot. Ofttimes we will lose our holdings, but while we retain them there is much to do.
'Be well, friend.'
The cleansing agent has been introduced to the Hoarwell
Cleanse the Hoarwell River of the poison introduced by Angmar
Cleansing the Hoarwell

Captain-General Tordúr explained that scouts near Tol Ascarnen have seen a number of Angmar's servants dumping the contents of barrels into the river. Drawing water from the river shows that the river is slowly being poisoned. If this is allowed to continue, then the hobbits at Hoarhallow will certainly perish.
'Is it yet done, ${PLAYER}? We must be swift, else the Little Folk at Hoarhallow will suffer a terrible fate at the hands of Angmar.'

The poison was introduced to the Hoarwell at the waterfall overlooking Tol Ascarnen, in the central area of the Ettenmoors. Northwest of Glán Vraig.
Captain-General Tordúr asked you to make your way to the top of the waterfall overlooking Tol Ascarnen to assist in cleansing the poison that the goblins of Angmar introduced into the Hoarwell River.

Captain-General Tordúr is at Glân Vraig.
You should return to Captain-General Tordúr with news of your success.
Defeated minions of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'This mine is mostly stone now, ${CLASS}, but mostly is not all. There is enough ore here to harvest and turn into viable weapons and armour, and so we must keep her from the hands of our enemy.
'I am charged with defending this mine with my life. Our numbers were thinned as the drakes swoop in from above and the cave-claws chewed through the floor to assail us. I need able bodies to help defend against the enemy, and you look capable.
'Stay within the confines of the mine and help us defeat the foe from Angmar. I will see that you are rewarded for your efforts!'

'Your success at the Isendeep Mine is known to me. My scouts tell me that you showed ferocity and zeal as you cleaved through the forces of Angmar.
'Take this reward and know that your efforts are very much appreciated by myself and all the Free Peoples who stand against the army assembled against us.'

'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. Those dogs will think twice before they try to reclaim this mine again.
'You are a hard warrior. Here, take this reward for your efforts and know that I may have need of one with such strength in the future.'
Defeat minions of Angmar within the Isendeep Mine (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defence of the Isendeep

Mines provide the ore that is needed to build weapons and armour for the war. The Isendeep long ago stopped being a mine capable of great production, but there are still veins of ore within the stone there and this makes the location desirable to both the forces of Angmar and the Free Peoples.

Lieutenant Otur is within the Isendeep Mine.
Lieutenant Otur asked for your assistance to help defend the Isendeep Mine against the forces of Angmar. If you succeed, speak with Otur or if he or the Isendeep falls into enemy hands, report to Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig.

Lieutenant Otur is within the Isendeep Mine. If Otur has fallen or the Isendeep Mine is in the hands of the enemy, you can speak with Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig in his stead.
Through a hard fought battle, you defeated great number of the enemy within the Isendeep mine.

'My concern over the true desire of Angmar's forces within the Ettenmoors grows with each passing moment, ${PLAYER}. I have acquired and translated only a few documents, but I have learned that the Witch-king very likely visited these lands as he fled after his defeat.
'The dealings of the Hillmen of Rhudaur with Angmar confounds me, and I must learn more before I deliver my findings to Captain-General Lainedhel. Please, if you recover any tomes from the Enemy deliver them to me so that I might learn more of the history of this place.'

'I will begin my translation of this work immediately. You have helped us greatly, friend.
'For your efforts, I give you this token. I will have need of your service in the future, ${PLAYER}, so remember me.'
'My fears continue to grow, ${PLAYER}. We must learn what Anmgar's true purpose here is and quickly.'
Talk to Lieutenant Unferth
A Scholar's Fears

Lieutenant Unferth wishes you to find books from the libraries of Rhudaur to support his fears. The more he learns from recovered notes and tomes, the more he believes that there is something within the Ettenmoors that the army of Angmar seeks.

The books and tomes Unferth desires may be carried by Orcs, Uruks, and possibly even goblins or trolls, which can be found throughout the Ettenmoors.
Lieutenant Unferth has asked you to collect any books or tomes which might uncover what Angmar seeks in the Ettenmoors.

'Greetings, ${CLASS}. I am Lieutenant Unferth. Before my arrival here in the Coldfells, I was a student of ancient lore.
'I know much about Rhudaur, the kingdom which once stood here in the Ettenmoors, but my knowledge of this specific place is limited. Most documents surrounding the kingdom's decline were lost to the ages and in the great war that saw their ruin. When I arrived here in the Ettenmoors, we fought many skirmishes against the host out of Angmar, and I discovered that many of the Orcs and Uruks carried parchment from the ancient libraries of Rhudaur.
'I fear that they seek something here in the Ettenmoors, and these texts may reveal what that is. Would you return any that you find to me? You would receive a reward, of course.'

'These will take me time to translate, but they will help me to know what evil was done in these lands. If there is something foul here, we will learn what it is, and we will root it out.
'For your efforts, I give you this token. I will have need of your service in the future, ${PLAYER}, so remember me.'
'If there is a more nefarious purpose for Angmar's arrival here, we must discover it quickly, else we face an unknown foe. I would much rather face a ravening horde of Orcs than something darker.'
Talk to Lieutenant Unferth
A Scholar's Woe

Lieutenant Unferth is concerned over items whic he found on the corpses of many of the Orcs and Uruks he killed when first arriving in the Ettenmoors: scraps of text cataloguing the history of Rhudaur.

Goblins, Orcs, and Uruks may be found throughout the Ettenmoors. Lieutenant Unferth is located within the relative safety of Ost Ringdyr.
Lieutenant Unferth is concerned that Angmar's army may be searching for something terrible in the Ettenmoors, but little of the history of the region survived Rhudaur's destruction. He is looking for any shred of information that he may find.

'You will face a great many foes here in the Ettenmoors, some more dangerous than others. Specifically, the Uruks, Orcs, Wargs, and Spiders. We have seen that their cunning is unmatched.
'They bear the brunt of their commanders' derision and still attack without care for their lives, continuously crashing against the walls of the strongholds throughout the Ettenmoors. You must use caution once you leave the safety of this fortress...and yet, you must learn the paths available to you in this wild place.
'You should strike out into the Ettenmoors and visit the locations which enhance our ability to fight on this front. In the south, deep in the Grimwood Forest, is the Grimwood Lumber-camp; once used by the hobbits in Hoarhallow, it is now a contested location with rich wood for constructing palisades. North of the Lumber-camp, on the west side of the Hoarwell river, is Lugazag, a tower oft in the control of the Enemy. Deep in the hills at the base of the Misty Mountains in the lands called Arador's End, you will find the Isendeep Mine, where rich minerals and ore can be found. South from there, on an island in the centre of the Hoarwell, is Tol Ascarnen. The last location east from Tol Ascarnen and not far to the north and west of Glân Vraig is Tirith Rhaw. Make your way to these locations, and when you have visted them all, return to me. I will see that you are well rewarded.'

'Welcome back, ${PLAYER}. Scouts reported that you visited each location. It is good to know that you were so diligent in accomplishing this task.
'We have need of people like you. As promised, I have a gift for you. You will find that many here are willing to part with these tokens in exchange for assistance. Quartermaster Ash, in the stonework gazebo to the east of my location will exchange these tokens for keys to the chests we have at Glân Vraig.
'These chest contain the odds and ends we find during the battles which occur throughout the Ettenmoors and are only a small piece of what we can offer you in exchange for your assistance. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. If you have a chance, speak with Captain-General Tordúr before heading back into the wild.'
Visit the Grimwood Lumber-camp, Isendeep Mine, Tol Ascarnen, Tirith Rhaw, and Lugazag.
Ettenmoors Location Visited
Talk to Ascwyn
A Hike Like No Other
The Ettenmoors has several locations which allow for an advantage over the foe.

'Be cautious as you make your way through these lands. You will find support in smaller numbers as you venture further from our holdings here. Remember, the bears and eagles are our allies. They will assist you should you come under attack.'

The Grimwood Lumber-camp is west of Glân Vraig. Lugazag is west of Glân Vraig, on the west side of the Hoarwell. The Isendeep Mine is far to the northwest of Glân Vraig. Tol Ascarnen is south of the Isendeep Mine, northwest of Glân Vraig. Tirith Rhaw is east of Tol Ascarnen and north-west of Glân Vraig. Observe your map to see who currently controls the location. Red locations are held by the Enemy, and blue by the Free Peoples.
Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn explained that the contested locales throughout the Ettenmoors hold some manner of importance to the Free Peoples and the forces of Angmar and suggested that you visit each.

Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn is at Glân Vraig within the Coldfells.
You have found your way through the Ettenmoors and located the Grimwood Lumber Camp, Lugazag tower, Isendeep Mine, Tol Ascarnen and Tirith Rhaw. Now you should return to Glân Vraig and speak with Sergeant-at-Arms Ascwyn.
Defeated minions of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I've spent long years fighting, ${PLAYER}. I never shy from battle, and I never show my enemy fear. Courage is one thing as is common sense, and common sense tells me now that we must prepare ourselves for a coming battle.
'This fortress may not look to be much, but in a bygone age it was a seat of great power for the Men of Rhudaur. Now it lies in ruins, but affords those who control it a view of the east and west sides of the Hoarwell that cannot be seen elsewhere.
'We must keep this site out of the hands of the Enemy, else we fall to a disadvantage. Stand with me and defeat the Enemy within the walls of the keep. We shall reap the glory this day!'

'The battle at Tol Ascarnen was hard fought, and you proved to be an able warrior.
'You have earned this reward, ${PLAYER}.'

'A well-earned reward. Your arms must have grown tired as you cleaved your way through the battle. Yet, here we stand victorious against our enemy.
'You have earned my resepct and more this day, ${PLAYER}. Take these with my greatest thanks and know that you shall be revered among the defenders of this ancient ruin.'
Defeat minions of Angmar at Tol Ascarnen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defence of Tol Ascarnen

South of the falls of the Hoarwell River there stands a keep upon an island. This keep, once a seat of Rhudaur's strength within the Ettenmoors, long ago fell to ruin, but the vantage afforded at the top of the towers makes the location a strategic point within the Ettenmoors. It is for this reason that Lieutenant Solvi believes Angmar's army will strike at the location in an attempt to claim it for their own.

Stand with Lieutenant Solvi at Tol Ascarnen and defeat the enemy there.
Lieutenant Solvi wants to prepare for battle and hold this all-important location out of the hands of the Enemy. If you succeed, speak with Solvi or if he or Tol Ascarnen falls into enemy hands, report to Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig.

Report to Lieutenant Solvi at Tol Ascarnen if he stands and you control the location. If he has fallen or the enemy claimed the keep, return to Glân Vraig and speak with Captain-General Tordúr.
The battle at Tol Ascarnen earned you victory over your foes.
Defeated minions of Angmar (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We must prepare for the inevitable attack, ${PLAYER}. It is unlikely that there will be a long peace. We must make ready the walls and steel ourselves for the next assault. Stand fast, and we shall persevere.
'If you are willing to stand with us, slaughter the foe as they crash against the walls of Tirith Rhaw, and when this is done, I shall see you rewarded. If I fall in battle, scouts will inform Captain-General Tordúr of your bravery, and you may claim your reward from him.
'What say you?'

'My scouts have indeed informed me of your efforts at Tirith Rhaw. You are most welcome here in the Ettenmoors, ${PLAYER}. Long have we waited for heroes willing to do all that you have done.
'We are indebted to you, please take this small reward and know that we strive to find more to offer those who serve the Free Peoples.'

'Your efforts in defending the tower are well-known. We are pleased to offer you this reward. It is not much, but the rewards that you shall claim are taken from those who fall within these accursed lands.
'You are most welcome in the company of the Free Peoples, ${PLAYER}.'
Defeat minions of Angmar at Tirith Rhaw (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defence of Tirith Rhaw

Tirith Rhaw, the tower on the western-most edge of the Ettenmoors, is a stronghold for the Free Peoples. Angmar's army is well aware of this and often organize raids to overrun the location to provide themselves a strong foothold in the west.

Defeat the foes from Angmar within the area of Tirith Rhaw.
Sergeant-at-Arms Mibrethil wants to ensure that the Free Peoples are prepared for the onslaught that will ensue at the walls of Tirith Rhaw and enlisted your help in driving the foe from the field. Stay within the immediate area of the tower and stand against the foe. If Mibrethil or Tirith Rhaw falls, report to Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig.

If Tirith Rhaw and Sergeant-at-Arms Mibrethil still stand, report to him for your reward. If the tower was lost or Mibrethil fell in battle, report to Captain-General Tordúr at Glân Vraig.
You stood against the foe within the walls of Tirith Rhaw. Your efforts were not in vain and you are owed a well-earned reward.

'You have done well with very difficult tasks, but there is more yet to be accomplished. While you were gone, I spoke with Laerdan about Amarthiel and where she might be heading with the palantír. We need to find her quickly and put an end to her schemes.
'However, Laerdan knows much more than I thought before. Go and speak with him and learn how you can help him find Amarthiel.'

'I am loathe to confess that I know more of Amarthiel than perhaps any other living, yet still I knew nothing of her secrets as Sara Oakheart. She has become much more powerful than I had imagined...indeed, I had believed her dead since the Battle of Fornost.
'It matters not. She is alive, and my pursuit of her must continue. I believe that she is heading to Evendim. She has a palantír--I am guessing that of Osgiliath, the master of the south, thought lost in Anduin--and if she has any hope of staying in power, she will need to confer often with the Lidless Eye. She may also use the palantír to find Narchuil, that token of power she lost long ago.
'The only place left for her is Annúminas then, for it may be that the pedestal where once sat the palantír of Annúminas still stands. You should go to Evendim quickly and speak with Calenglad. He is at the Ranger-camp at Tinnudir on the eastern shore.
'It is my dearest hope that we will meet again on a happier day, ${PLAYER}.'
'Laerdan and Golodir sent you, did they? There must be more than we thought to the growing presence of the Angmarim then. I am glad then that they have sent a proven hero to help.'
Chapter 7: Amarthiel's Trail
Golodir was pleased with your success in the south, but is still concerned with Amarthiel and her possession of a palantír.
'Go and speak with Laerdan. It is urgent that you find Amarthiel.'
'You must do as Laerdan says. Hurry, for I deem time is short.'
'Calenglad is in Evendim at the Ranger-camp at Tinnudir. The camp is along the eastern shore of Lake Evendim, on an island there. Hurry!'

Laerdan is on the other side of the cave at Garth Forthnír.
Golodir instructed you to speak with Laerdan to learn how you can help him track down Amarthiel.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp at Tinnudir on the eastern shore of Lake Evendim.
Laerdan instructed you to go to the Ranger-camp in Evendim to speak with the Ranger Calenglad.

'The Angmarim presence in Annúminas is most disturbing, and hearing the news you brought me, I think that is the best place to search for Amarthiel. She cannot yet have gone too deep into the ruined city, and we cannot let her go any further.
'I will let you bring five of my men with you. Whatever you do, you must come back with information about her plans. This is most urgent for the Dúnedain and for Eriador. We cannot let the Lidless Eye have any more influence in this region.
'Speak with me again when you are ready to leave.'

'This is grave news indeed. I will send word to Elrond of Rivendell and to Golodir my kinsman. We need help, and quickly, if Mordor is so deeply involved.
'Thank you for your help with this and for dispatching one of Amarthiel's Black Númenórean lieutenants. We have made a strike, but unless we follow it up with one more sure, Amarthiel will surely recover from it and seek to crush us utterly.'
Discover Amarthiel's plans at Annúminas
Chapter 8: Amarthiel's Hope
Calenglad has informed you that there has been a recent growth in the number of Angmarim outside of Annúminas.

'Are you ready to search for Amarthiel? My men have been ordered to protect you no matter the cost.'
<rgb=#FF0000>This is a Solo quest, and cannot be completed with a Fellowship.</rgb>
'Your news is dire, but at least we can prepare a defence against Amarthiel.'

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp at Tinnudir on the eastern shore of Lake Evendim.
Speak with Calenglad when you are ready to leave for Annúminas.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp at Tinnudir on the eastern shore of Lake Evendim.
You should speak with Calenglad again, now that you have discovered Amarthiel's plans.
'Hurry, they were ready for us. We must push through if we are to find Amarthiel before it is too late! Follow us!'
'We must return to Tinnudir, ${PLAYER}. I fear that Amarthiel has won this hour. We must plan our next move, and quickly, so her victory will be short-lived!'
Talk to the Ranger Protector standing before you
Find and stop Amarthiel
Instance: Amarthiel's Hope
Calenglad has asked you to find Amarthiel and discover her plans. He has sent you to Annúminas with five Rangers to help fight off the Angmarim.
Speak with the Ranger Protector before you search for Amarthiel.
Find Amarthiel and discover her plans.
You must defeat the Black Númenórean.

'Well met! I know you to be a great traveller, and it occurs to me that I might be able to make use of your road-lore. Long ago, an Elf-warrior named Erchiel was one of my company. She was a doughty fighter and a boon companion. But since I had heard nothing from her in recent years, I had supposed she had sailed over the Sea and departed Middle-earth.
'Yet now comes word from a traveller that she is living in a glade near Lake Evendim. If you would be so kind, I will send you to her with my greetings and with an invitation to come to Rivendell now that Middle-earth is once again threatened by the Enemy.
'If you accept this task, I will send you first to the Ranger lore-master Culang at Tinnudir, an island just off the eastern shore of Lake Evendim. Since before the fall of Sauron, Evendim has been the domain of Men, not of Elves, so not only is it a courtesy to call on him first, but it may be that he knows just where Erchiel can be found.'

'Glorfindel...It is an age and more since last I saw his face. You bring back many memories....
'I have fought many battles for my kindred, yet long ago I laid aside my sword, and that was no idle choice. Even Glorfindel's words will not sway my resolve.
'I thank you for your kindness in bearing Glorfindel's invitation, but I think I will not go to Imladris.'

'You come from Lord Glorfindel himself? Well then, you are welcome here -- it is a great honour to receive a messenger from such a renowned Elf!
'Erchiel, you say? I know not that name. There are few Elves who come to these lands, and those are mostly travellers, not residents. Still, it may be....
'I have heard tell of an uncanny glade across the lake, on the north-west shore. That shore is dangerous these days, but they say the glade itself is different. If an Elf lives anywhere around the lake, it would be in or near that glade. Go if you will...but be wary!'
Glorfindel's Company
Glorfindel has heard that his former comrade Erchiel has taken up residence in a glade by Lake Evendim.
'Please seek out Culang at Tinnudir, as it may be he knows where Erchiel may be found.'

Culang is at Tinnudir, an island off the east shore of Lake Evendim, west of the North Downs.
Glorfindel has asked you to seek out his old battle-companion Erchiel who is said to be living near Lake Evendim. He has sent you first to speak to the Ranger Culang at Tinnudir, for it may be that he knows where she can be found.

Erchiel may be found in a glade on the north-west shore of Lake Evendim, by a stream that empties into the lake.
Culang received you warmly but confessed he had not heard the name Erchiel before. He suggested it may be that she can be found in or near a strange glade on the west shore of Lake Evendim, but he warned you that the area is very dangerous.

'Greetings. You have the look of a wayfarer who has walked many a long road, and I wonder if perhaps I could convince you to walk another in my stead.
'In the normal course of things, I should be on my way to Lake Nenuial, in Evendim, to serve for a time in caring for the old Dúnedain manors and crypts found near Annúminas. Truly, for most of my brethren, this duty is a pilgrimage to the past, to another time when Arnor was a great kingdom that ruled all these lands in peace and prosperity.
'However, what with the amassing Orc-army just on our doorstep, I will not be able to make my journey just yet. I would ask you to seek out Calenglad at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, just off the east shore of Lake Nenuial, and give him my regrets and this explanation.'
'Ah. Thank you for carrying Ferrif's message. We are already so few in number and hemmed in on all sides by danger -- this unwelcome news comes as little surprise.'
A Pilgrimage to the Past
The Ranger Ferrif has asked you to bear his compliments and regrets to Calenglad, the leader of the Rangers at the island of Tinnudir on Lake Evendim.
'Please give my regrets to Calenglad at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir on Lake Nenuial, in Evendim.'

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, off the east shore of Lake Nenuial, west of Parth Aduial in Evendim. Evendim is west of the North Downs and north of the Shire.
The Ranger Ferrif has asked you to speak with his leader Calenglad in his stead.

'Greetings, traveller. I have a favour to ask of you, if you will listen.
'We are short on supplies, as always, and we rely in some measure on deliveries of food from the Forsaken Inn. If your travels bring you back westward, could you speak to Old Mugwort in the Forsaken Inn about arranging a delivery of oatmeal to be sent to Ost Guruth?
'It would be a great help to us, ${PLAYER}.'

'Hana the Young needs oatmeal? Well, I'm afraid we're all out, and there's little to be done -- my supply has dried up because of the problems they're having up at Oatbarton!
'A cousin of mine lives in the town, a Bounder, name of Nod Gardener. He says that there are all kinds of problems there that the Bounders can't solve by themselves. You look like you can handle yourself pretty well, so if you should happen to swing around that way, you might be able to do some good. There won't be any oatmeal delivered out this way until problems in Oatbarton are sorted out!
'You can get to Oatbarton by heading north from Brockenborings in the Shire, across the Greenfields.'

'Old Mugwort! Wonderful! I haven't seen him in a dog's age! Nice of him to think of us back in Oatbarton.
'In truth, we have some serious problems around here, so it's a good thing you've come!'
Oatmeal Problems
Hana the Young wants a shipment of oatmeal sent to Ost Guruth from the Forsaken Inn; something has happened to the supply of oatmeal in recent days.
'When you get the chance, I sure would like it if you could head over to Oatbarton in the Shire. Just head north of Brockenborings, across the Greenfields, and look for my cousin Nod.'
'Old Mugwort is in the Forsaken Inn on the Great East Road, west of here in the Lone-lands. Speak to him and arrange for a delivery of oatmeal to Ost Guruth, ${PLAYER}, and I will be grateful.'

Old Mugwort is in the Forsaken Inn, located in the Lone-lands along the Great East Road, between Bree and Ost Guruth.
Hana the Young has asked you to inquire at the Forsaken Inn about acquiring a shipment of oatmeal for Ost Guruth.

The Bounder Nod Gardener lives in Oatbarton on the border of the Shire, north of Brockenborings and across the Greenfields.
Old Mugwort of The Forsaken Inn has asked you to journey to Oatbarton to talk to his cousin Nod Gardener. He has heard that there are problems on the northern boundary of the Shire that the Bounders have not been able to solve, and that shipments of oatmeal will not be possible until the trouble in Oatbarton has been resolved.

Grisgart boasted of a crown that gave him special powers. The crown is now in your possesion. This is one of the three items that were entrusted to the Angmarim. They can be used to summon the Gaunt-lord, Drugoth.
Place the crown on the pedestal
Drugoth's Crown

Having killed Grisgart and his drakes, you have obtained Drugoth's crown from the treasure pile found there. The crown must be used on the appropriate pedestal in the main courtyard of Helegrod to summon Drugoth awake.
HAving obtained Drugoth's crown, you now need to bring it to the courtyard to summon Drugoth from his sarcophogus.
Zaudru had consumed Drugoth's Ring when killing Breosal. You have now gained possesion of the ring. You must now take it to the main courtyard of Helegrod if you wish to awaken Drugoth.

Having killed Zaudru, you have obtained Drugoth's Ring from her. The ring must be used on the appropriate pedestal in the main courtyard of Helegrod to summon Drugoth awake.
Having obtained Drugoth's Ring, you now need to bring it to the courtyard to summon Drugoth from his sarcophogus.
Storvâgûn has taken Drugoth's Staff from Adhargal before killing him. You have now gained possesion of the staff. You must now take it to the main courtyard of Helegrod if you wish to awaken Drugoth.
Place the staff on the pedestal
Drugoth's Staff
Having killed Storvâgûn, you have obtained Drugoth's Staff from him. The staff must be used on the appropriate pedestal in the main courtyard of Helegrod to summon Drugoth awake.
HAving obtained Drugoth's Staff, you now need to bring it to the courtyard to summon Drugoth from his sarcophogus.

'I want to help the Rangers here, ${PLAYER}. They have gone through so much hardship during the long years...they deserve now our aid and friendship.
'To that end, I have been keeping an eye on the ruins of Barad Tharsír, in the Barandalf far to the south-east. The ruins are on the far side of the river Brandywine. The Ranger Astiul collects pottery, relics, and other artifacts that once belonged to his people, and I have offered to help him with this task.
'If you can recover certain relics from Barad Tharsír, I know that Astiul will be pleased. Do not worry yourself with the condition they may be in, or how worn by time: broken swords, shields, or bottles will be equally well-received. Look for these things among the ruins and beware of the robbers that now dwell there, unconcerned for the history of the Dúnedain.'

'Astiul is so well-spoken, like most of his people. Thank you for his kind words, ${PLAYER}!
'As I promised, I will reward you for your efforts. Thank you again, and do what you can to aid the people here and in all of Evendim!'
'These relics do not seem of any real value to my eyes, but bring them to Astiul. He is here at the camp and will be pleased to have them.'
'Look for old and time-worn relics at Barad Tharsír, ${PLAYER}: broken swords, shields, bottles...that sort of thing.'

'These are from Barad Tharsír? Thank you very much for collecting them. It saddens me to know that the tomb-robbers of Evendim have taken that place, but there are too few of us left to protect every Dúnedain site.
'Tell Harmony I appreciate her help -- and yours -- with this matter.'
'I thought you had some relics for me?'
Bring old relics to Harmony Grayson
Bring old relics to Astiul
Relics in Barad Tharsír
Harmony Grayson has volunteered to help the Rangers collect relics from the ruins of Barad Tharsír.
'Barad Tharsír is south-east of Tinnudir, on the far side of the Brandywine, in the Barandalf. If you search the grounds you are sure to find old relics of the sort for which I have asked.'
'Astiul is just over there, ${PLAYER}. Bring him the relics you recovered from Barad Tharsír.'
'We must help the Rangers as best we may.'
'Thank you for your help earlier, ${PLAYER}.'

Barad Tharsír is south-east of Tinnudir, in the Barandalf, on the far side of the Brandywine.
Harmony Grayson wants you to bring her any relics that you can find from Barad Tharsír.

Harmony Grayson is at the Ranger camp on the island of Tinnudir, north-west of the Barandalf and west of Parth Aduial.
You have gathered several relics from the ruins of Barad Tharsír and should return to Harmony Grayson.

Ranger Astiul is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, north-west of the Barandalf and west of Parth Aduial.
Harmony Grayson has asked you to bring the relics you collected to Astiul, as he will appreciate their significance.

Harmony Grayson is in the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, north-west of Barandalf and west of Parth Aduial.
Astiul has expressed his gratitude for your efforts and wants you to thank Harmony for him.
Defeated tomb-robbers at Barad Tharsír (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Ansley Atwood
Defeated Ogden Oakes

'We have to do something about the tomb-robbers, ${PLAYER}. I have spoken with the Rangers about this matter, but they are stretched thin. They must focus on the threats to the tombs of their ancestors in Men Erain and the crypts of Annúminas, even while other areas fall into danger.
'South-east of Tinnudir, the sands of the Barandalf and the dune-grasses are swept by the breezes that come off the Brandywine, but now the gentle breezes carry too the harsh cries and commands of a band of tomb-robbers. They have established a camp in the ruins of Barad Tharsír, on the far side of the Brandywine, and I fear that before long they will cross the river and pass into the peaceful lands to the south.
'You will be rewarded if you can defeat the tomb-robbers at Barad Tharsír, including some of their more infamous members: the archer, Ansley Atwood, and the hound-keeper, Ogden Oakes.'

'You have defeated Ansley and Ogden? I am pleased to hear it and to know that the robbers have less of a hold on Barad Tharsír than they did!
'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}! Please take this reward with my gratitude.'
Defeat tomb-robbers at Barad Tharsír (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Ansley Atwood
Defeat Ogden Oakes
The Robbers of Barad Tharsír
Unity Tilden is concerned that tomb-robbers have taken control of the ruins of Barad Tharsír in the Barandalf.

'Barad Tharsír is south-east of Tinnudir, in the Barandalf, on the far side of the river Brandywine. You will be rewarded if you can defeat the tomb-robbers there before they cross the river and pass into the peaceful southern lands. Look too for Ansley Atwood and Ogden Oakes and put an end to their cruel legacies.'
'Barad Tharsír has been made safer by your efforts.'
'The promise of treasure brings out the worst in Men.'

Barad Tharsír is located south-east of Tinnudir, in the Barandalf, on the far side of the Brandywine.
Unity Tilden has asked you to defeat members of the robber-band that has taken Barad Tharsír, as well as their most infamous members: Ansley Atwood and Ogden Oakes.

Unity Tilden is at the Ranger camp on the island of Tinnudir, north-west of the Barandalf and west of Parth Aduial.
Unity is waiting to hear that you have defeated the robbers at Barad Tharsír.

'I am a healer by trade, ${CLASS}, and have studied the behaviour of many creatures in order to further my studies. Listen to me, then, when I tell you that a great danger is breeding among the sands of the Barandalf!
'I speak of the nerbyg, vile insects that can be found now among the dunes in great numbers. If we do not do something, and quickly, I fear that the nerbyg will swarm -- and whether they swarm north or south is immaterial, for there are good people in both directions!
'Travel south-east of Tinnudir onto the sands of the Barandalf and defeat any sand-nerbyg that you find! West of the road that runs through that place, if it can even be called a road, is a small rise called the Sand-mounds; you are likely to find huge sand-nerbyg there.'

'You have destroyed some of the sand-nerbyg? Thank you for this, ${PLAYER}. You have put my mind at ease, and I cannot say that often enough in these dark days. The nerbyg will always be a danger, but it is to be hoped that we have forestalled their swarming.'
An Increase of Nerbyg
Uiriel is concerned about the number of nerbyg that have begun to appear throughout the Barandalf and fears that the creatures may be preparing to swarm.

'Sand-nerbyg can be found all throughout the Barandalf, and the huge sand-nerbyg often gather at the Sand-mounds west of the road that passes through those lands.
'Destroy the vile creatures before they swarm, ${PLAYER}!'
'It is to be hoped that the sand-nerbyg will not swarm now for some time.'
'The sands of the Barandalf are always dangerous for the unprepared.'

Sand-nerbyg can be found in great numbers on the Barandalf, south-east of Tinnudir, and huge sand-nerbyg often gather at the Sand-mounds west of the road that passes through the Barandalf.
Uiriel has asked you to defeat sand-nerbyg on the Barandalf before they swarm, bringing destruction in whichever direction their paths take them.

Uiriel is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, north-west of the Barandalf and west of Parth Aduial.
You have defeated many of the sand-nerbyg that have been breeding on the Barandalf and should return to Uiriel with news of your victories.
Defeated sand-lurkers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I pride myself on the wide array of supplies I carry, ${PLAYER}, and I do my best to maintain my inventory. You can imagine the disappointment if I were to travel to the southern lands and not have the various knick-knacks of which the hobbits there are fond! No, I must maintain my stock at all times.
'But it's not easy! To get to Dwaling and Oatbarton, you have to travel south-east of Tinnudir and pass through the Barandalf; the sands and dunes of that place are now home to creatures vile and dangerous. On my last journey, I was quite surprised by the grasping tendrils of a number of sand-lurkers -- I barely managed to escape with my life and my inventory!
'That is unacceptable, ${PLAYER}. If you can defeat some of the sand-lurkers, I would greatly appreciate it and reward you in kind! You will find many of the creatures near Lithost, on the banks of the Brandywine. Lithost is on the other side of the river and slightly south of Barad Tharsír, if you are familiar with those ruins.'
'You have defeated the sand-lurkers of the Barandalf? I am glad to hear it and will reward you for your efforts accordingly!'
Defeat sand-lurkers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Danger Among the Dunes
Rudbessain had an unfortunate encounter with the sand-lurkers that prowl among the dunes of the Barandalf and wishes to end the threat they pose to travellers.
'The sand-lurkers can be found throughout the Barandalf south-east of Tinnudir, but especially near Lithost. Lithost is on the opposite side of the Brandywine from Barad Tharsír.'
'The sand-lurkers are less of a worry now, ${PLAYER}.'
'My inventory of goods is second-to-none!'

Sand-lurkers can be found throughout the Barandalf, but especially at Lithost, south-east of Tinnudir, on the other side of the river from the ruins of Barad Tharsír.
Rudbessain has asked you to defeat some of the sand-lurkers that make travel through the Barandalf dangerous for her and her inventory of goods.

Rudbessain is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, north-west of the Barandalf and west of Parth Aduial.
You have put an end to some of the sand-lurkers that prowl among the dunes of the Barandalf and should report of your success to Rudbessain.

'Have you seen the salamanders that crawl among the dunes of the Barandalf, to the south-east?
