They are a dangerous foe, ${PLAYER}, and must not be underestimated -- travellers sometimes fall prey to their deadly claws and biting fangs, and the shifting sands take their luckless bodies. A careless tread sometimes unearths the sad remains, an unhappy reminder that we cannot protect everyone that passes into these lands.
'If you are willing, I would ask you to travel into the Barandalf and defeat the creatures. Bring to me their teeth and scales, and I will fashion some equipment for you.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}. The salamanders can be vicious if you are not prepared.'

'These are most impressive, ${PLAYER}: the teeth are sharp and the scales sturdy! I will certainly be able to make something with these. Take this with my thanks and the knowledge that you have made the Barandalf safer for any travellers that must pass through these lands.'
'You do not have the teeth and scales I asked you to bring me? Without them I will make you nothing.'
Bring teeth and scales to Halsey Reed
Tooth and Scale
Halsey Reed is concerned about the salamanders that crawl among the dunes of the Barandalf.
'Salamanders slither among the dunes of the Barandalf, to the south-east of Tinnudir. Defeat the creatures and bring me their teeth and scales, and I shall fashion you some equipment from them.'
'The salamanders are not as great a threat now as they were.'
'Your efforts have made the Barandalf safer, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you.'

Salamanders slither among the dunes and sands of the Barandalf, south-east of the island of Tinnudir.
Halsey Reed wants you to defeat salamanders in the Barandalf and bring him sand-swept scales and sand-crusted teeth.

Halsey Reed is at the Ranger camp on the island of Tinnudir, north-west of the Barandalf and west of Parth Aduial.
You have collected the teeth and scales that Halsey asked you to gather and have thinned the population of deadly salamanders that make dangerous the sands of the Barandalf. You should return now to him so he may fashion for you the equipment he promised.

'I have come to this camp to enlist the aid of the Rangers with the problems that face my people, but these men seem so distrustful!
'It's almost as if they think Ost Forod is full of tomb-robbers! Certainly times are hard, and some of my people have turned to plunder, but there are far more decent people at my home than the unsavoury types these Rangers fear.
'Will you come to Ost Forod? There are some rewarding bounties posted, and an adventurer of your skills could well find yourself gainfully employed in no time! Just cross the bridge back to the mainland and then follow the road to the crossroads. Once you reach it, take the northward road up into Tyrn Fornech, and you'll see Ost Forod in no time! One of the arbiters, Basil Gummidge, will be pleased to see you.'

'Kelsey finally found someone to help us, I see. The Rangers are good men, to be sure, but they are distrustful and seem to believe that the people of Ost Forod have all given in to the lure of tomb-robbing. That is ridiculous, of course.
'Calenglad trusts Robin Dunkley, to be sure, but there are more good Men in Ost Forod than our Robin!'
Ost Forod in Tyrn Fornech
Kelsey West has told you something of Ost Forod, an old watch-post in Tyrn Fornech that has become settled by the hardened Men of Evendim.

'To reach Ost Forod, cross back onto the mainland and take the northern road from the crossroads in Parth Aduial. Look for Basil Gummidge and offer your services, my friend! There are good people in Ost Forod, and they need your help!'
'Were you able to lend your aid to my people, ${PLAYER}?'
'The Men of Ost Forod are noble and honest! Very few of us are tomb-robbers!'

Basil Gummidge is in Ost Forod, located in Tyrn Fornech along the road that runs north of the crossroads in Parth Aduial, northeast of Tinnudir.
Kelsey West has asked you to travel to Ost Forod to speak with Basil Gummidge and offer your help to the people there.

'Do you know what? I've had a conversation or two with those strange Big Folk, those Rangers, up on the moors. Queer folk, to be sure, but they always spare an ear for any news I might be willing to give to 'em.
'They have a camp a good ways north, on an island off the shore of Lake Evendim they call Tinnudir. It seems that if you follow the road northwards across the Barandalf sand-marshes and across the Brandywine, you'll come to a crossroads. If you take the left fork -- that'll be the westward road -- you'll eventually come to Tinnudir.
'Or so this Calenglad fellow tells me. I've never been there myself. If you do find your feet taking you up that way, be sure to give him a \qhullo\q from me, Hal Gamgee!'

'Hal Gamgee always has an interesting story to tell. He is unusually stout-hearted for one of his folk -- perhaps it runs in his family.
'Make yourself useful around Tinnudir or move along. We have many concerns at the moment and cannot allow for sloth in Evendim.'
Rangers of the North
Hal Gamgee told you of a camp of Rangers on the island of Tinnudir, north of the Shire and beyond the Brandywine.

'The Ranger-camp I've heard tell of is on an island called Tinnudir off the shore of Lake Evendim, far to the north. Just follow the road through the Barandalf sand-marshes and across the Brandywine and then take the westward road when you reach the crossroads. Give Calenglad my greetings when you arrive!'
'How are Calenglad and the rest of his Rangers? Are they well?'
'I would visit Calenglad, but it's such a very long way from here.'

The Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir is north of Oatbarton along the road that runs through the Barandalf. Hal told you to follow the road north across the Brandywine until you reach a crossroads and then to follow the westward road until you reach Tinnudir.
Hal Gamgee has mentioned the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir in Lake Evendim and suggested that you speak to the Ranger Calenglad.

'We face many fell foes in this dark place. Though the strength of the Enemy is weakened, so, too, is it strengthened by the discovery of this great ruse. Now, we learn that the dark tower standing amidst the forces within the forsaken valley to our south teems with enemies long kindling flames from a place I shall not speak of.
'It falls to you, ${PLAYER}, to gather your allies and make an assault on Barad Gúlaran, to stand against the horrors awakened within that dark citadel. One horror, Wisdán, once a man in service to Angmar, sacrificed his life to watch over Barad Gúlaran. Lore-masters dispatched from Esteldín brought us all we know of him and Barad Gúlaran. Little is known beyond his service to the Witch-king and his close ties with the Shadow in the North. It is possible that he is a sorcerer, like a few others within Barad Gúlaran.
'He must be slain, ${PLAYER}, lest his darkness be used to spread evil towards the south to become the bane of all. Gather your allies together and enter Barad Gúlaran. Return to me when you have done the deed, and I will see that the Council's gifts are bestowed upon you.'

'A sign of hope in these dark times, ${PLAYER}. This news will hearten Halbarad and those who worry of our tenuous position here. You have earned a great deal of our respect and this reward.
'Take it and know that we are honoured by all you do to keep Evil from spreading to the south. We must endeavour onward.'
Master of Barad Gúlaran

Long ago, a servant pledged himself to the Witch-king's cause. His service lasts to this day, and his dark embrace on Barad Gúlaran brings terror into the hearts of those fighting to unseat Shadow in the North.
'Do not tarry, ${PLAYER}. Though the citadel of Barad Gúlaran has long lain in slumber, recent events will surely set the inhabitants within to their task. We must disrupt their intentions swiftly.'
'Hail, ${PLAYER}, slayer of the Castellan of Barad Gúlaran. What need have you this day?'

Barad Gúlaran rises out of the center of Nan Gurth, south and east of Gath Forthnír.
Uidon directed you to enter Barad Gúlaran in search of Castellan Wisdán. You are to slay him and return to Uidon for your reward.

Gath Forthnír is northwest from Barad Gúlaran.
You entered Barad Gúlaran and after some time found and defeated the Castellan within his chambers. You should now return to Gath Forthir, the hidden refuge in the north-east area of Angmar, and inform Uidon that you have defeated Castellan Wisdán.
You have dispatched the Rogmul of Barad Gúlaran

'If Amarthiel's words are true we must strike swiftly and concisely. We will not be given reprieve or quarter should we fail.
'We must rely on others to assist us against this foe while we work with Golodir to determine our best course of pursuit. If the sorcerers within Barad Gúlaran succeed at calling forth the ancient evil they mean to control, we shall face a foe we do not have the numbers to defeat.
'I ask you now, ${PLAYER} to gather your fellows enter the accursed halls of Barad Gúlaran and face the enemy called to the service of Angmar. I do not know how you will defeat this horror, I only know that you shall see great reward for your success.'

'We cannot discount all you have done, ${PLAYER}. Your efforts have given Eriador another breath of life and returned hope.
'I will send word south to Halbarad of your success and your name will be spoken of and written in the annals kept by the lore-masters of Esteldín.
'You are well-deserved of this reward, my friend. Be safe in your journeys and know that we shall ever regard you as a hero for all your sacrifices.'
Defeat the Terror within Barad Gúlaran
Army of One

Brúnfair called you to his aid to seek out and stop the creation of an army within the walls of Barad Gúlaran. With the discovery of Amarthiel's plan, the Council of the North has swiftly reacted to the newly discovered threat and wishes to dispatch those brave enough to face the enemies within the fortress.
Their hope is that the army Amarthiel promised to summon can be stopped when there is but one such enemy to stop the destruction of Eriador.
'Be swift and safe. Stand with your fellows and do not lose heart. The enemy you will face will be greater than any other you have seen. I think even the False King will pale against this enemy.'
'Eriador owes you a great debt. You are a true hero in this age.'

Find the terror called to service in the halls of Barad Gúlaran and put an end to it before the sorceresses can summon more of the beasts to Angmar's service.
Brúnfair dispatched you to Barad Gúlaran to face and defeat the great evil the sorceresses call to the service of Angmar. This army must be destroyed before it grows too large for the few defenders of Eriador to face.

You have succeeded in defeating the terror within Barad Gúlaran. Return to Brúnfair and tell him of your victory.
After a grueling battle your successfully faced and slew the first Rogmul enslaved by the sorceresses of Barad Gúlaran.

'Within the walls of Barad Gúlaran you will find many enemies. One enemy in particular concerns me and intrigues me more than any other. I know we must destroy the keeper of Barad Gúlaran, but the servants who have walked the halls for ages intrigue me more.
'Clad in ancient iron, these spirits from the Shadow keep an eternal watch over the former home of the Witch-king.
'I wish to study the armour and determine how these creatures were able to manifest themselves in such a way. Perhaps there is a way we can defeat them without bringing forth our swords and arrows.
'Enter Barad Gúlaran and collect twelve pieces of the armour so I may sate my curiosity and discover a weakness to these creatures.'

'I am pleased to see that you are hale and whole, ${PLAYER}. I am pleased greater still that you acquired such fine specimens. I shall begin my research immediately.
'You have earned much thanks from myself and others, ${CLASS}. Accept this token, though it is a pittance compared to all you do it is what we can spare.'

'I do not know what I will learn from the armour, but my hope is that some secret will reveal itself to me should I be given the chance to examine the armour. Please, be swift and cautious. Do not tread lightly into Barad Gúlaran. Bring strength of arms and your kin to that accursed place.'
Return to Uirod
Sheathed in Ancient Iron

Danger lurks within Barad Gúlaran and Uidor, an elf dispatched to the north to support those sent there by the Council of Esteldín, wishes to examine the armour worn by the fell spirits within the citadel. You must smite the defenders and warriors within Barad Gúlaran to obtain the armour.
'My research continues thanks to your efforts. When I am finished I will send word to the south to the Rangers.'

Ancient armour wreathes terrifying creatures within Barad Gúlaran. Collect these items and return them to Uirod at the encampment in the northeastern area of Angmar.
Uirod asked you to obtain samples of the armour worn by the defenders within Barad Gúlaran so he might learn a weakness to better defeat them. Make your way into Barad Gúlaran, with the assistance of others and collect the samples.

'We face a grave enemy in these lands, ${CLASS}. The work ahead of us is perilous but we cannot falter.
'With the discovery of Amarthiel and her ties to Angmar, we have learned a great deal of the enemy we face. Within Barad Gúlaran we face a cabal of sorcerers who are trained in dark arts that threaten life.
'I must ask you for assistance. I require you to enter that accursed place in search of the three sorceresses who carry out the will of Amarthiel. End their plot before they succeed and return to me with news of your victory.'

'This reprieve must be used to gain a stronger foothold here, friend. We shall not relent in our efforts to secure Angmar and crumble the swelling shadow here.
'You have played an instrumental part in forging a better future fo Eriador and you are well-deserved of this reward. You have my thanks and the thanks of all who would remain free throughout Eriador.'
Sorceresses of the Black Tower

Brúnfair, recently dispatched to the north, brings ill tidings and carries a heavy concern on his careworn shoulders. Recent events within the black citadel of Barad Gúlaran have forced him into action.
He has requested that you gather assistance from your fellows in seeking the destruction of a cabal of sorceresses who are attempting to see Amarthiel's will carried forth.
'Quickly, now. We must crush this coven before it grows into a larger threat to all of Eriador.'
'In these dark days it is good to know that there are still some who are willing to fight for the good of all.'

Find the three Sorceresses within Barad Gúlaran and defeat them. If they are stopped, then there will be no others to carry out the will of Amarthiel.
Brúnfair asked you to search through the halls of Barad Gúlaran in search of the sorceresses left in charge of carrying out Amarthiel's will. Find them and destroy them.

You have defeated the sorceresses within Barad Gúlaran. Return to Brúnfair at the Ranger encampment in the northeastern section of Angmar and tell him of your success.
Searching through the halls of Barad Gúlaran you discovered and defeated the Sorceresses responsible for carrying out the machinations of Amarthiel in Angmar.

'Hold, friend. Are you passing into Evendim? I would have you deliver a message to Calenglad, a friend of mine and true. The fighting on the Fields of Fornost continues, but we are holding our own -- tell Calenglad he need not spare any Rangers to come to my aid.
'Calenglad is in charge of the Ranger camp on the island of Tinnudir, far to the west along the road that passes through Parth Aduial, and beyond the crossroads of Canadiach. The Rangers of the North have an encampment on Tinnudir, just off the eastern shore of Lake Nenuial.
'Tomb-robbers and other unsavoury Men plague the shores of Evendim, and I would have Calenglad dedicate his forces to combatting them, rather than dividing his forces and preparing less-effective defences! Go now, and good fortune go with you into Evendim!'

'Torogethir speaks the truth: the tomb-robbers that plague Evendim must be fought. I cannot spare any men for the Fields of Fornost, unless the situation becomes more grave. It would need to be dire indeed for me to abandon Annúminas to the tomb-robbers!'
An Island in the Lake
Torogethir has asked you to bring word of his struggles in the North Downs to Calenglad, a leader of the Rangers.

'You will find Calenglad at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, west of the road that runs through Parth Aduial and the crossroads of Canadiach.
'Tell him not to spare any men for battle on the Fields of Fornost; it is more important to safeguard the treasures and history of Annúminas!'
'Did you bring my message to Calenglad? I am pleased to hear it!'
'The Ranger camp on the island of Tinnudir is far to the west, beyond the crossroads.'

Calenglad is at the Ranger camp on the island of Tinnudir, west of the road that runs through Parth Aduial and the crossroads of Canadiach.
Torogethir has asked you to bring word to Calenglad that his efforts on the Fields of Fornost are going well, and that Calenglad should focus on combatting the tomb-robbers that plague Evendim.

'I understand you're an adventurer, ${PLAYER}? Have your travels ever taken you to Rivendell?
'Ha! You look at me with such surprise! I understand your dismay, but do not fear! Yes, the Last Homely House is far to the east, beyond the Lone-lands and within the wilderness of the Trollshaws, but I will tell you this and true: you can make the journey. It will be dangerous, and you will need to stay alert, but I believe that you too can find your way to the House of Elrond. Stay to the road wherever possible, and do not travel by night!
'If you push yourself to the limit and do find your way to the House of Elrond in Rivendell, look for Aragorn, my chieftain -- tell him that Ferrod hopes he will return before long to Annúminas. It has been many years since he was here, I have heard it said.'
'I am pleased to hear your tidings of Ferrod, ${PLAYER}. It will be some time before I can spare a journey to Evendim, but I would look upon Annúminas again. Thank you, my friend.'
A Dangerous Road
Ferrod has asked you to make the dangerous journey to Rivendell to speak with Aragorn.

'You can make the journey to Rivendell, ${PLAYER}. Stay on the road wherever possible, do not travel by night, and be watchful of the dangerous creatures of the Trollshaws! Speak to Aragorn in the House of Elrond, and tell him that I look forward to the day he will return to Evendim!'
'One day Aragorn will come again to Evendim.'
'I knew you could survive the dangerous journey to Rivendell, ${PLAYER}!'

Aragorn is at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, far to the east within the Trollshaws.
Ferrod has asked you to speak with Aragorn in the House of Elrond, telling you that with dedication, sticking to the roads, and travelling only by day, you can safely reach Rivendell.

'Are you thinking of travelling to the far side of the lake, ${PLAYER}? That is a long journey!
'If your travels take you to the far side of Nenuial, I ask that you bring my greetings to any Elves that stay at Eavespires -- I heard that some of that kindred have come to the glade, and I wish them to be welcome in Evendim.
'Cross to the mainland, and follow the shore of the lake in a great loop north and then west. You will cross the Even-rills at the northern tip of the lake; continue to follow the lake shore until you see a stream that feeds into Nenuial. Near that place you will find Eavespires. You will find Elves there, and even greater mysteries, if the stories are to be believed.'

'Hello, friend. My name is Lithuifin, and it is my pleasure to welcome you to Eavespires. I return Ferrod's greetings with good cheer, and hope you will find comfort and safety at the end of your road!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}. I return Ferrod's welcome to these lands with my own, for Elves passed through this place even before his oldest ancestors! But I am glad to see you on this side of Nenuial, and I hope you will not find sorrow in these lands.'
Friends at Eavespires
Ferrod has asked you to bring his greetings to the Elves staying at Eavespires.

'Eavespires is on the far side of the lake. Cross to the mainland and follow the shore north and west until you reach the Even-rills, and cross even them! Continue along the western shore until you reach a stream that feeds into the lake, and you will not be far from Eavespires. Speak to the Elves there, and bring them my greetings!'
'You spoke with the Elves at Eavespires? My heart is filled with joy, ${PLAYER}.'
'It is good to know that there are friendly folk even on the far side of Nenuial.'

Eavespires is on the opposite side of Lake Nenuial from Tinnudir; you were told to cross the Even-rills at the northernmost tip of the lake and continue to follow the shore as it curves westward, until you arrive at a stream that feeds into the lake.
Ferrod has asked you to bring his greetings to the Elves currently staying at Eavespires.
You have defeated Miluidir
Dawn has come...you have failed

'Do you hear those terrible cries rising from Ost Heryn? It is this way every evening, for the robbers who have made those ruins their home are plagued by the shade of one of the Oathbreakers, one who was once a captain of Men, Miluidir.
'While some would say the robbers have earned what they deserve for their greed, I cannot help but feel that something should be done. Perhaps those robbers can someday be redeemed.
'Would you travel to those ruins and find Miluidir and defeat him? It would be but a brief reprieve, for none but a higher Power can banish him from this world. Be warned though, Miluidir must be defeated before dawn, or he will hide once more and plague the robbers again upon the morrow.'
'You have done well, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps by seeing your noble efforts on their behalf, some of the robbers will see the error of their ways. At least hope still remains for them.'
Defeat Miluidir before dawn
Terror in Ost Heryn
Torogethir wishes to show the robbers at Ost Heryn mercy and perhaps show them the error of their ways by relieving them of the shade-captain Miluidir.
'Please, ${PLAYER}, travel to Ost Heryn and defeat Miluidir before dawn. As greedy as they are, the robbers that make those ruins their home deserve some reprieve from that horrible creature.'

Miluidir is at Ost Heryn, south-west along the road from Torogethir's camp.
Torogethir has asked you to drive forth the shade of Miluidir at the ruins of Ost Heryn.

Torogethir is at his camp, northeast of Ost Heryn.
You should return to Torogethir with news of your success.

'Although not many know this, I heard about that business down south of here with the goblins. They are up to no good around these parts too! I swear I saw one of them kill one of them spiders and drag it back to their camp, though why they would want something so vile, I surely can't say.
'I wonder if those goblins consider spider a delicacy of some kind, though that thought makes me shudder. Maybe you ought go out to their camp at Bleakleaf Crest, out east of here, and see if you can find that spider they dragged off.
'Mayhaps that spider-corpse might tell us something about these goblins.'
A quick examination of this spider's remains reveal that the goblins have let it lie, virtually untouched. All of the ichor and venom of this spider seem to have been collected by the goblins.
A quick examination of this spider's remains reveal that the goblins have let it lie, virtually untouched. All of the ichor and venom of this spider seems to have been collected by the goblins.
'They took the venom from the spiders? Well that's no good. And you found hobgoblins as well? That's even worse....'
Examine the corpse of the spider
Examined the corpse of the spider
Goblins and Spiders
Bob Proudfoot is familiar with the troubles the Greenfields have seen with goblins and is concerned that those troubles are spreading further into the Northfarthing.
'The goblins' camp is out east of here, in the Bleakleaf Crest. Go find that spider they dragged off. It might give a clue as to what the goblins are up to!'

The goblin-camp is at the Bleakleaf Crest, east of Oatbarton.
Bob Proudfoot has asked you to find the corpse of the spider the goblins dragged off, in hopes that you might learn something important about the goblins.

Bob Proudfoot is at Oatbarton, west of the Bleakleaf Crest.
You should return to Bob Proudfoot with the information you discovered.
Defeated Wood-web Spinners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Wood-web Hunters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'What those goblins want with the spiders' innards is a puzzle, to be sure, but there's one thing I do know for certain: they are up to no good!
'Maybe if you kill off the spiders, the goblins will go away? There's more than anyone can handle out east of here. The North Moors are crawling with them.
'It certainly won't make any of us sorry to see the beasts dead. You just be careful though.'

'Good, you're back, and you've dealt with a few of those spiders, I see.
'Well, I've had me an idea about what those goblins are up to with the spiders' innards...and it ain't a pretty thought!'
Defeat Wood-web Spinners (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Wood-web Hunters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Goblins' Source
Bob Proudfoot is confused by your discoveries among the goblin-camps.
'I don't know what those goblins are up to, but maybe they'll leave off when there's no more spiders to hunt.'

There are spiders in the North Moors, east of Oatbarton.
Bob Proudfoot asked you to go out and slay spiders, in the hopes that the goblins will leave.

Bob Proudfoot is in Oatbarton, west of the North Moors.
You should return to Bob Proudfoot with news of your success.
Burned bubbling pots with torches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You see, I think I finally figured out what those goblins are up to. It was the presence of the hobgoblins that cleared it up for me. Stories always said they were the worst lot of the bunch, scheming up new ways to hurt and kill folk! I think they are taking the spiders and cooking them down, making them into that tar of theirs that they throw! Never heard of them using spiders' innards for such a thing, but wouldn't surprise me a bit.
'They are probably sore from their defeat south of here and are itching for another fight. But this time they plan on burning hobbits out of house and hole! You've got to put a stop to this!
'You should head back to the Bleakleaf Crest and burn the pots they are cooking the spiders in -- they'll probably have torches or such nearby that you can use. And you'll need to take the recipe for the tar away from them as well, or burning the pots won't do any good. Defeat one of them hobgoblins out there and search him for the recipe!'

'Good, you've done it! I'll take that recipe there and destroy it. That should keep them from making any more of the foul stuff.
'Never would have thought I'd be saving spiders from a horrible death. Well, if you don't tell anyone, I won't either!'
Recover the hobgoblins' recipe
Burn bubbling pots with torches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring the hobgoblins' recipe to Bob Proudfoot
Hobgoblin's Recipe
Bob Proudfoot believes he has discovered the plans of the goblins.
'What are you doing about here? Those hobgoblins are up to no good! You should burn their pots to get rid of the foul stuff they've made so far. And get rid of the recipe to make more of the tar.'
'Well, you did right well with those hobgoblins, I must say!'

The goblin-camp is in the Bleakleaf Crest, east of Oatbarton.
Bob Proudfoot wants you to burn the pots the goblins are using to cook down the spiders, as well as recover the recipe for their tar.

Bob Proudfoot is in Oatbarton, west of the Bleakleaf Crest.
You should return to Bob Proudfoot with the news of your success.

'Well, we must not let life's day to day upsets get to us, ${PLAYER}. There may not be boars in Evendim, but they say there are a great number of bears throughout the hills of Tyrn Fornech, and especially at Nan Orngon to the east.
'Bear-steaks, while still delicious, are certainly no match for a sizzling boar-steak. My friend Ronald Dwale once went on at great length about the similarities between those two words, you know, \qboar\q and \qbear,\q but I must confess that I do not share his same love for words. Words are often an inconvenience and get in the way when you are trying to express yourself...to get to the real meat of an idea, if you will.
'The meat in question here, for example, is certainly a choice cut of bear-meat! Bring me back several cuts, and I will share them with some of my neighbours. There will be a bit of coin in it for you, as well, and we can mourn the absence of boar over a delicious bear-steak. How does that sound?'

'You have brought the bear-meat? Good, good! I'll just prepare it, and we'll have a grand old time. Still, it's a shame this isn't boar-meat. You can make a really delicious steak out of boar-meat, if you know what to do.
'Still, I don't mean to sound ungrateful! Bear-meat is still quite good, and to tell you the truth, people here at Ost Forod don't have it quite as easy as my folk in Oatbarton. I'll call over some of these folk and share these steaks with them -- it's only right!
'Thanks again, ${PLAYER}. Keep an eye out for boars!'
Bring choice cuts of bear-meat to Parr Chopley
A Curious Number of Bears
Parr Chopley has decided that he will make do with some delicious bear-steaks instead, since Evendim seems to have a striking absence of boars.

'There are bears all over Tyrn Fornech, ${PLAYER}, but you'll find them especially at Nan Orngon, to the east of Ost Forod. Bring me choice cuts of bear-meat, and we can drown our sadness at the absence of boars in Evendim.'
'I wonder where all the boars went?'
'Evendim once had dozens and dozens of boars! The hills and fields were covered with them!'

Bears roam the hills of Tyrn Fornech and can especially be found at Nan Orngon, east of Ost Forod.
Parr Chopley has asked you to bring him choice cuts of bear-meat from the bears that roam Tyrn Fornech.

Parr Chopley is in the old watch-post of Ost Forod, in the hills of Tyrn Fornech, west of Nan Orngon.
You have collected several choice cuts of bear-meat and should bring them to Parr Chopley.
You have found no sign of boars in Evendim

'Well, another stranger to this town! Now I'm not the only one! My stomach is always getting me into trouble, and this is no exception. I was in the mood for a nice, thick boar-steak -- cooked to perfection, sizzling in its own juices -- and so I decided to go hunting in the North Moors. Well, I went a little further than planned and wound up here! Never knew anyone lived in this place...they say it's haunted!
'Well, anyway, I decided I never had Evendim-boar before, so I thought I might as well try some while I'm here...it should have been a simple matter of finding a nice, healthy boar, but you know what? I haven't seen a single boar since I've come here! That can't be right. How do people up here manage without plenty of boars to satisfy their cravings for delicious steaks? That's just unnatural!
'There have to be boars in Evendim; there just have to be! Go look for boars, ${PLAYER}, and don't come back until you've searched high and you've searched low! I'm not interested in boar-meat from other places, either; it's Evendim or nothing! Now it's a matter of professional responsibility and curiosity -- find me an Evendim-boar, and find one quick!'

'No boars? No boars at all? How odd, ${PLAYER}. Now, you really looked for them, right? You didn't just waste time doing errands or working on some craft or another, right?
'No, I trust you. But this means I'll have to do without a delicious Evendim boar-steak, and that just won't do!'
Spend time looking for boars in Evendim
A Striking Absence of Boar

Parr Chopley let his stomach lead him too far, wandering the northern ways into Evendim, where he chanced upon the rough town of Ost Forod. Nevertheless, he has not let it daunt him. He is in the mood for a nice, hearty boar-steak, but he is concerned that he hasn't seen any boars in all of Evendim.
'There must be boars in Evendim somewhere...spend some time looking for them! I can't believe that there isn't a single boar in the entire place!'
'A land without delicious boar-steaks is not a land of which I am fond!'
'No boars in Evendim? No boars at all?'

Evendim is a big place. There should be boars somewhere.
Parr Chopley is convinced that there must be boars somewhere in Evendim and wants you to spend some time looking for one.

Parr Chopley is in Ost Forod, the old watch-post in the hills of Tyrn Fornech.
You have found no sign of any boars in Evendim and should report your sad discovery to Parr Chopley.
Defeated white Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Have you encountered the fearsome white Wargs of Tyrn Fornech yet, ${PLAYER}? The creatures are vicious, bloodthirsty beasts, and they strike without warning! A few nights ago, I was taking in the air around the northern wall of Ost Forod, and I thought I saw something gleaming in the moonlight. I wandered towards it, foolishly, so foolishly, but I was curious as to what it might be. Before too long, I had strayed beneath the eaves of the forest and had become quite turned around.
'Suddenly, I heard a snarl from my left! As I spun to face the sound, I saw only a splash of bright white fur, matted with blood and mud. I ran, and the great brute pursued me! It sprang towards me with a great leap; I felt its hot breath steaming in the cool night air! And then -- lights! Lights from Ost Forod! Basil Gummidge had come with a party and lanterns to the outskirts, and on seeing them, the Warg gave up its pursuit!
'Those beasts are dangerous, ${PLAYER}, and something must be done. Not everyone will have the benefit of a fortuitous encounter with our arbiter, you know. If you're up to it, I'd ask you to defeat some of the ferocious white Wargs. You'll find them all throughout Tyrn Fornech, but especially at the Duskencleft, north of Ost Forod.'

'You survived your encounters with the white Wargs, ${PLAYER}, I am quite glad to see -- good work! One day, perhaps, a traveller will be able to walk in these lands without fear of danger!
'One day, perhaps. For now, I will give you this reward and hope that day comes soon rather than late.'
Defeat white Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Ballard Wilmer and the White Warg
Ballard Wilmer had an encounter with white Wargs in the hills of Tyrn Fornech and is now deathly afraid of the creatures.
'Find and defeat the white Wargs of Tyrn Fornech, ${PLAYER}! You'll find them throughout the hills, but especially up near the Duskencleft, north of Ost Forod!'
'That day of which we spoke draws nearer, ${PLAYER}!'
'I am afraid to pass the town walls after dark because of those white Wargs.'

White wargs stalk the hills of Tyrn Fornech, but can especially be found in the vicinity of the Duskencleft, north of Ost Forod.
Ballard Wilmer told you of his harrowing encounter with a Warg and has asked you to defeat some of the vicious white Wargs of Tyrn Fornech.

Ballard Wilmer is at the old watch-post of Ost Forod, in the hills of Tyrn Fornech, south of the Duskencleft.
You have defeated many white Wargs and should now report your victory to Ballard Wilmer.

'A few days ago, I encountered a band of tomb-robbers outside Tûm Fuin, rejoicing over a haul of relics they had stolen from some Dúnadan-tomb. Well, you can be sure that I ran them off, but when I caught up to them there was no sign of the satchel over which they had gloated.
'I think one of them dropped the satchel of stolen relics during the chase, but I was too winded to go back and look for it. You can be sure that their allies will return for it, if we don't recover it first!
'Tûm Fuin is north of Ost Forod and full of goblins. Look for the satchel somewhere among the bushes, south-west of Tûm Fuin, possibly in the break in the hills called the Duskencleft. The satchel of relics may have fallen somewhere in there.'

'You found the satchel of relics! Thank you, ${PLAYER}! I'll have this delivered to Astiul at the Ranger-camp right away.
'Take this reward for your trouble -- if only I had thought to return to the Duskencleft right away, it wouldn't have been necessary. Alas, I was winded after the chase and did not consider it until I had come home.'

'You have not yet recovered the satchel of relics? The Duskencleft is north of Ost Forod and south-west of Tûm Fuin. The satchel must have been tossed into one of the bushes as I pursued the tomb-robbers up through the Duskencleft.'
Bring satchel of relics to Clark Standish
Escape from Duskencleft
Clark Standish encountered a gang of tomb-robbers at Duskencleft, and believes they might have hidden a satchel of stolen relics there.

'The tomb-robbers were in a hurry to escape. I'm sure they didn't mean to drop the satchel of relics they had stolen, and their brothers will surely return to reclaim it when they find out.
'Go to the Duskencleft and search through the bushes for the dropped satchel! Start your search by Tûm Fuin, north of Ost Forod, and work your way south-west to Duskencleft.'
'Beware the Wargs and goblins that prowl the Duskencleft and Tûm Fuin.'
'Most of the people at Ost Forod are good folk, but there are some bad apples.'
The satchel of stolen pottery is somewhere in the Duskencleft, south-west of goblin-infested Tûm Fuin. Tûm Fuin is north of Ost Forod.

Clark Standish is in Ost Forod, the old watch-post in the hills of Tyrn Fornech, south of the Duskencleft.
You have reclaimed the satchel of stolen relics and should return it to Clark Standish.

'The hills of Tyrn Fornech are the refuge of several different tomb-robber bands, ${PLAYER}, and each of them is becoming increasingly bold.
'If you are sure enough in your abilities, perhaps you could venture north and west of Ost Forod into the hills to confront some of these outlaws? The tomb-robbers that prowl throughout Tyrn Fornech are tougher than those who inhabit Parth Aduial; these are veteran robbers and scouts who have adapted to a harsher life in the hills.
'You'll find veterans and scouts throughout Tyrn Fornech, ${PLAYER}, and if you don't...they'll find you.'
'Thank you for this news, ${PLAYER}. There will always be tomb-robbers in these lands, but perhaps you have helped lessen their numbers or influence somewhat. Take this reward with my thanks.'
Practised Villainy
Rowena Parker is concerned at the increasing boldness of the tomb-robbers that creep among the hills of Tyrn Fornech.
'You'll find the tomb-robbers throughout Tyrn Fornech, ${PLAYER}. Defeat these villains and these lands will be made safer.'
'The tomb-robbers will always be a nuisance here.'
'You have been a great help to us, ${PLAYER}.'

Veteran tomb-robbers and scouting tomb-robbers can be found among the hills north and west of Ost Forod, in Tyrn Fornech.
Rowena Parker has asked you to defeat the experienced tomb-robbers that prowl the hills of Tyrn Fornech.

Rowena Parker is at Ost Forod, the old watch-post in Tyrn Fornech.
You have defeated many experienced tomb-robbers in Tyrn Fornech and should return to Rowena with the tale of your success.
Defeated tomb-robber captain at Cirith Rhîw

'At the end of the northern road, at Cirith Rhîw, there stands a gate. For years, my family has brought goods that way to trade with the Snowmen of Forochel, but recently, a tomb-robber band has seized the gate and made passage impossible.
'If you are a brave adventurer and true, you would surely be able to defeat the captain of that robber-band and recover any trade goods they have stolen.
'Just follow the road north through Tyrn Fornech until you reach the gate at Cirith Rhîw. You might want to bring a friend or two, for the robber-band has held the gate for a long time.'
'It will be some time before trade with Forochel resumes, but you have taken a step on that road for all of us now, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for it!'
Defeat tomb-robber captain at Cirith Rhîw
Trouble at Cirith Rhîw
Spring Standish is concerned about the lack of trade with the Snowmen of Forochel ever since tomb-robbers seized the gate at Cirith Rhîw.
'The tomb-robber captain and his cronies currently hold the gate at Cirith Rhîw, and trade with Forochel is impossible. I hope you will be able to defeat him!'
'We once maintained a thriving trade with the Snowmen of Forochel.'
'The tomb-robbers have caused many problems for us, but still we oppose them.'

The captain of a robber-band has seized the gate of Cirith Rhîw, north of Ost Forod along the road that leads to Forochel.
Spring Standish has asked you to defeat a tomb-robber captain at Cirith Rhîw, in hopes that the rest of his band will disperse.

Spring Standish is at Ost Forod, the old watch-post in the hills of Tyrn Fornech, south of Cirith Rhîw.
You have defeated the tomb-robber captain at Cirith Rhîw and should return to Spring with news of your victory.
Defeated goblins at Tûm Fuin (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'You might have heard mention of this around town already, but if you haven't: there are goblins at Tûm Fuin, a hollow a short distance north of Ost Forod!
'We have enough problems with the Wargs and tomb-robbers stirring up trouble in Tyrn Fornech; we don't need goblins and boggarts as well!
'I have set aside some coins for any adventurer able enough to do something about the goblins. Are you such an adventurer, ${PLAYER}? If so, you'll have no trouble journeying north to Tûm Fuin and defeating the goblins there!'

'Tûm Fuin sounds dreadful, ${PLAYER}! I am glad you were able to defeat some of the goblins there, but I don't know if the hollow will ever be the pretty place that once it was. The corruption the goblins have wrought sounds severe.
'Take this reward, ${PLAYER}, and let us both wish for the day that Tûm Fuin will be restored.'
Defeat goblins at Tûm Fuin (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Goblins in the Hollow
Poppy Seaton is distressed by the fact that goblins have taken up residence so near to Ost Forod and wants something done about them.

'The goblins are at Tûm Fuin, ${PLAYER}, a hollow to the north of Ost Forod, among the hills of Tyrn Fornech. It is to the north-east of the Duskencleft, if you have ever been to that pass between the hills.'
'Tûm Fuin was a place of beauty before the goblins came.'
'One day, Tûm Fuin will be restored.'

Goblins have made a camp at Tûm Fuin, north of Ost Forod in Tyrn Fornech.
Poppy Seaton has asked you to do something about the goblins that have taken up residence at Tûm Fuin.

Poppy Seaton is at Ost Forod, the old watch-post in the hills of Tyrn Fornech, south of Tûm Fuin.
You have defeated many goblins and should now return to Poppy with news of your victory.

'There can be no greater insult than this, ${PLAYER}. For Angmar's foul regent to walk the stones that Elendil walked of old is an outrage for which there can be no forgiveness! Amarthiel's minions may hold Annúminas for now, but the Dúnedain will not rest until she and all her servants are swept from its courtyards and the very flagstones wiped clean of their taint.
'While you were away, a visitor came to Tinnudir. His name is Laerdan, and he is an Elf of great reputation; my friend Golodir spoke very highly of him in our youth, though I had not met him before now. He has been given the use of the mustering room in the keep here on Tinnudir and says he has information about Amarthiel that will be of use to us. He asked for you personally, ${PLAYER}. Hear what he has to say, and I pray you will return to me with some secret lore of the Elves that may aid us in this battle!
'Turn right as you enter the keep, and you will find Laerdan's room atop the stairs.'

'It is good to see you again, ${PLAYER}, but we seem cursed to meet always in sadness. The happier day of which I spoke in our last meeting, alas, has not yet arrived, and the days seem to grow darker still.
'Amarthiel has revealed herself and sits now in judgment within the ruins of Annúminas. Her armies fight within the streets and beneath the shadows of the towers against the Dúnedain -- this much you know. But there is more about Angmar's new regent than is known to Calenglad and the Rangers.
'I have written down much of the story in this letter. Read the tale and bring it to Calenglad so he may decide what can be done. You must do this with utmost speed, ${PLAYER} -- more than the city of the Dúnedain rests upon our answer to Amarthiel's challenge.'

'Laerdan has written his thoughts down in a letter? Very well, let me see it....
'Laerdan would ask me to abandon the city to Amarthiel, if it meant reclaiming the palantír from her? He does not know what he is saying! Golodir always spoke well of this Elf, but now I must question his judgment.
'I will not leave Annúminas in the hands of the Enemy! We will save both the city and the Stone, ${PLAYER}, or we will save neither! That is my decision!'
'You do not have Laerdan's letter for me?'
Bring Laerdan's letter to Calenglad
Book X, Chapter 1: The Champion of Angmar
Amarthiel and her minions have seized Annúminas, the ancient city of the Dúnedain, and Calenglad now struggles to form a plan by which she may be opposed.

'Laerdan says he knows something about Amarthiel that we must be told, ${PLAYER}. Speak with him in the room we have provided for him, then return to me with any useful information he has to share.
'Laerdan's room is inside the keep on this island, atop the stairs on your right as you enter the keep.'
'Read the letter I have given you and bring it to Calenglad. It is of utmost urgency, ${PLAYER}. There are difficult choices ahead -- for all of us -- and Calenglad will need to make the first.'

Laerdan has been given a room in the keep on the island of Tinnudir. His room is atop a flight of stairs on the right as you enter the keep.
Calenglad has told you that Laerdan the Elf has come to Tinnudir bearing information that might help you combat Amarthiel's forces in Annúminas. He said that Laerdan asked for you by name.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Laerdan has written a letter to Calenglad explaining the threat Amarthiel poses. He has asked you to read the letter and deliver it to Calenglad.

'Forgive me my anger, ${PLAYER}; it was not seemly. There is wisdom in Laerdan's words, but you must see the danger of leaving Annúminas to the Angmarim. If we do not stop Amarthiel's ambitions here, beside Lake Nenuial, she will fortify the old city. Where then do you think her armies will go? Think of the Shire, a short march to the south, or of Trestlebridge to the east, already beset by Orcs out of Angmar!
'We must turn the tide of battle in our favour, ${PLAYER}, before we try to reclaim the palantír. If we keep Amarthiel's attention focused on battles within the city, she will be forced to meet our challenges. She will have less time to use the seeing-stone to find Narchuil!
'My heart tells me this is right, ${PLAYER}. If you stand with us, speak with Rosselloth in Annúminas; she will tell you how fares the battle. Pass through Minathranc in front of the city, and you will come to the courtyard of Gwaelband. Rosselloth will tell you what you can do to help in this fight.'

'Hush, ${PLAYER}! You will bring them down upon us! As you can see, the battle goes ill: we sought to secure Gwaelband from the forces of the Enemy, but met only with defeat. A few adventurers sought to help us, but too few, too few....
'You will want to speak with Fainneleg -- he is coordinating our defences from Echad Garthadir, a position we have thus far managed to hold. Unfortunately, we have been cut off from his camp; it is south-west of here, on a higher level of the city.
'If the gate had been under our control, you could have gained access to the higher level much more simply. Now there is nothing for it: instead, you will need to swim west past the Port of Annúminas until you reach Gaerannon, and then climb through the city to Echad Garthadir. Fainneleg will surely have some way for you to help.'

'Welcome to Echad Garthadir, ${PLAYER}. I am sorry that you must see Annúminas thus: taken by Angmar, corrupted by Amarthiel.
'We will all do our part to drive them out! Listen now, for there is much to do and little time in which to do it!'

'Hail, ${PLAYER}! As you can see, the battle goes well: we have managed to secure Gwaelband from the forces of the enemy! The battle was fierce, but we were joined by a number of adventurers and victory was ours!
'You want to speak with Fainneleg -- he is coordinating our defences from Echad Garthadir, a position we have thus far managed to hold. You will find it south-west of here, in a higher level of the city.
'You are fortunate that we have taken Gwaelband; now that the gate is under our control, you can gain access to the higher level much more simply. You will just need to climb the short hill to the south-west, pass through the gate, and work your way south and west until you reach Echad Garthadir. Otherwise, you will have quite a journey ahead of you: a long swim west to Gaerannon, and then a climb through the city.'
Talk to Rosselloth
Chapter 2: The Tide of Battle
Laerdan has told you that the palantír must be taken from Amarthiel at any cost, but Calenglad insists that retaking Annúminas must come first.
'You will find Rosselloth in Gwaelband, at the front entrance to Annúminas. Gwaelband is west of Men Erain, beyond Minathranc. Rosselloth will tell you what you can do to help in this fight.'

'If the gate here had been under our control, you could have gained access to the higher level much more simply. Now there is nothing for it: instead, you will need to swim west past the Port of Annúminas until you reach Gaerannon, and then climb through the city to Echad Garthadir.
'Fainneleg will surely have some way for you to help, ${PLAYER}!'

'You are fortunate that we have taken Gwaelband; now that the gate here is under our control, you can gain access to the higher level much more simply. You will just need to climb the short hill to the south-west, pass through the gate, and work south and west until you reach Echad Garthadir. Otherwise, you would have quite a journey ahead of you: a long swim west to Gaerannon, and then a climb through the city.
'Fainneleg will tell you what to do. We will reclaim the city from the Angmarim, ${PLAYER}!'

Rosselloth is in the courtyard of Gwaelband. Gwaelband is west of Men Erain, beyond Minathranc, at the front entrance of Annúminas.
Calenglad has decided that Amarthiel's forces should be engaged in Annúminas in order to keep her from focusing her attention upon the palantír. He has sent you to speak with Rosselloth for advice on what you can do to help.

The Ranger Fainneleg is at Echad Garthadir, a small camp south-west of Gwaelband, on a higher level of the city. If the Rangers hold Gwaelband, the gate provides easy access to the higher level. Otherwise, you will need to swim west past the Port of Annúminas to Gaerannon and then climb through the city to reach Echad Garthadir.
Rosselloth has told you to speak with Fainneleg, the Ranger organizing the defence of Annúminas.
Defeated Bow-wielding Angmarim in Annúminas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We have had both gains and losses in the past few days, ${PLAYER}, but we cannot hold out forever. We are stretched too thin, and Amarthiel simply has too great a force. Every position we lose brings us one step closer to utter defeat.
'I have need of your strength, ${PLAYER}, and the strength of your allies. Two of my Rangers have repelled attacks on vital positions, and I worry that their strength may be faltering.
'Gwonil has fought to drive the Angmarim from the Port of Annúminas, north of here, upon the water. I fear that she cannot withstand another assault. So too is the situation for Torchirion, currently on guard at Adannon, a small gate west of the docks that provides access to the western shore of Nenuial. Hurry now to Gwonil and to Torchirion and learn how stand their defences. While you seek them out, I would ask you to defeat any of the bow-wielding Angmarim archers you see within the city; these ranged attackers are extremely dangerous, and several of my brothers have fallen to arrows let fly from hiding.'

'You have my thanks, friend, and those of Gwonil and Torchirion as well, I am sure, despite their insistence that everything it under control. But now there is more work to be done! For the moment, our defence of Annúminas holds true; we need now to form a plan of attack.'

'Fainneleg worries too much. I have everything in hand here, despite repeated Angmarim attacks on my position! I have not yet faced a force that was too great for me to handle -- you expected something different?

'The gate of Adannon is still defended, ${PLAYER}, but I thank you for coming to see me -- it has been some time since the last assault on the gate, and it is good to break up the boredom with a new face.
'The city will not long be in Angmarim hands, if you ask me!'
Talk to Gwonil and help defend her position
Talk to Torchirion and defend his position
Defeat Bow-wielding Angmarim in Annúminas (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Chapter 3: The Battle for Annúminas
Fainneleg's Rangers are stretched too thin to defend the city from repeated attacks by the minions of Amarthiel.
'The Angmarim will not get past me!'
'I have everything in hand, ${PLAYER}, but I thank you for your concern.'

'Our situation is dire, ${PLAYER}. Hurry to the aid of Gwonil, north of here at the Port of Annúminas, and to Torchirion, west of the docks at Adannon, the gate that gives access to the western shore of Lake Nenuial.
'I fear they cannot long stand against the forces that harass their positions. And do something about any bow-wielding Angmarim you see within the city while you are at it!'

Gwonil is on the docks at the Port of Annúminas, north of Echad Garthadir. Torchirion is at Adannon, a small gate in the city wall west of the docks that provides access to the western shore of Lake Nenuial. Angmarim archers lie in wait throughout the city, often in hiding.
Fainneleg has asked you to hurry to the defence of Gwonil and of Torchirion, for he fears that these Rangers cannot withstand another assault on their positions. He also wishes you to defeat any bow-wielding Angmarim you come across within the city.

Fainneleg is at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-camp on the middle level of Annúminas.
You have spoken with Gwonil and Torchirion and defeated several bow-wielding Angmarim in Annúminas and should return now to Fainneleg to report of your victories.

'I think we have earned a small reprieve through your efforts, ${PLAYER} -- battles still rage throughout the city, but it will be some time before Amarthiel can regroup and challenge our forces with the same intensity. We must go on the offensive, if we can, and to do that, we need information.
'Several positions throughout the city have changed hands numerous times in recent days, and it is my belief that these sites are of particular significance to Amarthiel. We fight to reclaim them whenever possible, but ownership of these sites is as fluid as the shoreline of Lake Nenuial: always in motion.
'I would ask you to journey to these volatile areas and defeat the minions of Amarthiel there, for some of them are sure to carry orders containing the future plans of her armies. If the Dúnedain hold the site, look for corpses of enemies killed in the fighting and search them for such orders. We need orders from these three locations, ${PLAYER}: from the courtyard of Gwaelband, to the north-east, where you encountered Rosselloth; from Clorhir, in front of the pools of Glinghant, east of Echad Garthadir; and at Menelband, on the highest level of the city.'

'You have done as I asked, but I am afraid these orders do not tell me much: they are written in the Black Speech, and I do not know enough of that fell tongue to translate them. I had thought to send you to one who could read such letters, but it seems that may not be necessary now.
'I have received word from Calenglad that fills me with hope -- our fortunes may be about to change, ${PLAYER}!'
'Have you found the orders I asked for, ${PLAYER}.'
Collect orders from Angmarim at Gwaelband, Clorhir, and Menelband
Bring the orders to Fainneleg
Chapter 4: Marching Orders
Fainneleg has decided that the Rangers must form a plan by which they can go on the offensive and take Amarthiel by surprise.

'We need orders from these three locations, ${PLAYER}: from the courtyard of Gwaelband, to the north-east, where you encountered Rosselloth; from Clorhir, in front of the pools of Glinghant, east of Echad Garthadir; and at Menelband, on the highest level of the city.'

Fainneleg is seeking orders from the Angmarim that occupy the courtyard of Gwaelband, to the north-east of Echad Garthadir, where you encountered Rosselloth; from Clorhir, in front of the pools of Glinghant, east of Echad Garthadir; and at Menelband, on the highest level of the city.
Fainneleg has told you of three volatile locations in Annúminas. He wants you to defeat the Angmarim and search their corpses for any orders they may carry. If the Dúnedain hold any of these locations, Fainneleg told you to search for the corpses of any Angmarim that may have been killed in the fighting; they too may have carried such orders.

Fainneleg is at the Ranger camp of Echad Garthadir in the center of Annúminas.
You have recovered the orders and should return at once to Fainneleg.

'Calenglad has asked you to return to his camp on Tinnudir, and you should go at once! I will say only this: if the information we have received can be trusted, Amarthiel may have made a crucial error. If we seize this opportunity, the Dúnedain may once again have the advantage, ${PLAYER}! Annúminas could be returned to us within the week!
'Go to Calenglad with all speed, and you can judge the news for yourself. I will return to you the orders you collected. Calenglad may have need of them after all.'

'My heart leaps with joy, ${PLAYER}, for we have done what I could never have imagined: taken one of Amarthiel's trusted servants captive! She will feel this loss, ${PLAYER}, I am certain of it. This may be the advantage we need to push Amarthiel's forces from Annúminas once and for all!
'It seems my decision was the right one: we are now closer to retaking the city than ever we have been. When we have done so, we will take the palantír from Amarthiel and put an end to the threat of Angmar forever!'

'Fainneleg was right to send you to me so quickly, ${PLAYER}. We have received information that could change our fortunes in the battle for Annúminas.
'One of our Rangers, a good man named Torchirion, overheard a number of Angmarim speaking near Adannon, the city-gate on the western shore of Lake Nenuial. They spoke of Mordrambor, one of the Black Númenóreans sworn to Amarthiel; a fell sorcerer, Mordrambor is one of her cruelest lieutenants, and Torchirion knew to listen closely.
'Before the Angmarim moved beyond his hearing, Torchirion heard them speak of some urgent errand Mordrambor plans for tomorrow night: he will travel with a small retinue, beneath the light of the moon, to Haudh Elendil. What he hopes to accomplish there Torchirion did not learn, but he learned enough!
'This is our chance, ${PLAYER}. This is our opportunity to gain the advantage in this battle. We must capture Mordrambor. Speak to me if you and your allies are willing to do this.'
'Why are you here?'
Bring sheaf of papers to Calenglad
Talk to Calenglad and capture Mordrambor
Chapter 5: Springing the Trap
The Dúnedain have received some news that cause Fainneleg and Calenglad to believe that their fortunes may be about to change.

'Are you ready, ${PLAYER}? We may not get another chance at this, our opportunity to capture one of Amarthiel's trusted lieutenants. You must be ready. Ranger Tadan has come up with a plan, so be sure to speak with him when you arrive.'

'You should speak with Calenglad at once, ${PLAYER}. He has received new information that could change the situation in Annúminas considerably.
'Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir. Bring him that sheaf of papers, the orders you collected. He may have need of them yet.'

'Torchirion's information was true, then? This is a joyous day, ${PLAYER}: one of the Amarthiel's trusted lieutenants, imprisoned by the Dúnedain! This blow to Angmar will surely help us to have Annúminas back in our hands before the week is out!'

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir.
Fainneleg heard some news from Calenglad that renewed his hope and has sent you to the old Ranger to hear it. He gave you the orders written in the Black Speech you collected from Gwaelband, Clorhir, and Tirband, and said Calenglad might have need for them after all.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir.
Calenglad is waiting to hear if you will agree to undertake the dangerous mission to capture Mordrambor, one of Amarthiel's Black Númenórean lieutenants.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir.
You and a contingent of Rangers have captured Mordrambor, one of the Black Númenórean sorcerers sworn to Amarthiel.
Tadan has fallen in battle and the plan has failed!

'Well done, my friend, well done! Amarthiel will not be pleased with this turn at all.
'Let me know when you are ready to leave, and we shall return to Tinnudir with our captive.'
'Let us return to Tinnudir with our captive, then. Perhaps our fortunes are finally beginning to turn around!'

'Calenglad speaks highly of you, ${PLAYER}. If we are successful this night, he will speak more highly still!
'Mordrambor has entered the tomb of Elendil and will surely emerge in a moment with his servants. If we can retain the element of surprise, my brethren and I will be more than a match for him. Present yourself to this lieutenant of Amarthiel and lure him to this end of the causeway! We will fall upon him and take him prisoner, and then we shall see what this trusted servant of Amarthiel may be able to tell us.
'This foe is in no way weak, ${PLAYER}. You will be in danger as you lead Mordrambor to our position, and we will not be able to help you -- if we reveal ourselves too soon, all will be lost. You must survive his attacks until he comes to the end of the causeway; until that moment, our hands will be tied. Luck be with you in this, ${PLAYER}.'
Talk to Tadan
Talk to Tadan
Tadan must survive
Instance: Springing the Trap
Tadan and his fellow Rangers have come up with a plan to capture Mordrambor, one of Amarthiel's Black Númenórean lieutenants, as he travels from Haudh Elendil with an unusually small retinue.

Ranger Tadan and his fellow Dúnedain are hiding at the end of the causeway to Haudh Elendil, waiting in ambush for Mordrambor to emerge.
Tadan needs you to lure Mordrambor into the Dúnedain ambush at the end of the causeway.

Ranger Tadan is at the end of the causeway in front of Haudh Elendil.
Tadan is waiting to speak with you, following the capture of Mordrambor.

'I can hardly believe our good fortune, ${PLAYER}. Take now these orders and show them to our prisoner. He will tell us their meaning willingly, or he will be made to tell us their meaning. I do not imagine Amarthiel inspires anything other than fear in her lieutenants, and this Black Númenórean will surely tell us what we need to know, if he feels he will be spared.
'My people have prepared a prison for the captive, and Ranger Tadan has volunteered to guard him. Tadan is a good man, a strong man, and will see that Mordrambor's bonds remain unyielding. Enter the keep here on Tinnudir and take the door on your left to the stairs that lead to the prison.
'Bring this sheaf of papers to Mordrambor and demand that he tell us their meaning. He surely has knowledge of the Black Speech and will tell us what we must know before long. The sooner he does, the better our fortunes will be, but I have no doubt that he will do so.'

'I remember thee, foolish ${CLASS}. I know the number of thy days, and they are few. Let us speak a while, then, for thou wilt soon fall beneath the tread of Angmar.
'What hast thou brought to me? Writings in the Black Speech, most beautiful of all the tongues? Thou canst not read these words? I weep for thy ignorance, foolish ${CLASS}, but I will take pity on thee, for thy struggle will soon end in pain and grief. I will tell thee what great Amarthiel plans for the wretches who cling still to this lowly city.
'Show me these pages. I will delight in foretelling thy demise.'
'Thou hast nothing for me?'
Show sheaf of papers to Mordrambor
Chapter 6: The Secret of the Orders
With the capture of Mordrambor, the fortunes of the Dúnedain may be changing. If he can be made to translate the orders you found, the tides of battle may turn in the favour of the Free Peoples.

'Our prisoner will translate the orders for you. The only question is when he will do so. I hope only that the Dúnedain can stand against Amarthiel as long as it takes!
'Bring the sheaf of papers to Mordrambor in the keep on this island. As you enter the keep, the door on your left leads to the stairs that climb up to the prison we have prepared for our captive.'

'Hello there, ${PLAYER}. I am still filled with amazement from our victory outside Haudh Elendil! I think it no exaggeration to say that together we may have changed the course of the battle for Annúminas, and for the better!
'I will see to it that this villain stays under lock and key. He does not seem very happy about his fate, does he?'
'The Dúnedain have captured the Black Númenórean Mordrambor? I can hardly believe this news, ${PLAYER}, but do not let down your guard! Even imprisoned, Mordrambor will seek to do his master's will.'

Mordrambor is being held prisoner in the keep on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim. As you enter the keep, the door on your left leads to stairs that climb up to the prison.
Calenglad has given you the orders you collected from the Angmarim in Annúminas, so that you may show them to the Black Númenórean prisoner. Mordrambor will know the Black Speech and must be made to translate the orders for you.
You have defeated Mól Choluim
You have defeated Roibárd
You have defeated Cailin

'These words sing of thy death and of the deaths of all the Dúnedain, foolish ${CLASS}. The pages tell Amarthiel's loyal servants to await the return of her emissaries, who have travelled to many lands seeking new allies.
'The waters of the lake have been as a road for Amarthiel's emissaries, and they carry gold with which to buy the loyalty of new servants: cold-hearted Men on an island far to the north-east; the Gauredain of the north-western hills, fierce and savage; the Kergrim, great beasts that stalk among the crypts of long-dead kings.
'When these servants return from across the great water, such a number of new allies sworn to the Iron Crown will come in their train that none shall hope to prevail against them.'

'You bring both good news and bad, ${PLAYER} -- that the emissaries have been defeated is one worry put to rest, but I fear the loyalties of the tomb-robbers of Rantost and the Gauredain of Emyn Uial are already purchased.
'We can count ourselves fortunate that the Kergrim have no love for Angmar's gold, but that is no large gain in the face of such great opposition.
'Cuguminuial brought me some baked goods and a few choices for dinner; you're welcome to help yourself to some of it. I think she felt badly that I have to spend all this time in the company of the prisoner. I don't like carrot cake, so you'd be doing me a favour by taking that off my hands, but you can help yourself to some of the rest of it as well.'
'If you seek to stop my negotiations, you are too late! The Gauredain fight now for Amarthiel! To me, my allies!'
'These beasts have no interest in gold? No matter! I will crush you myself, and bring your skin to Amarthiel as an unexpected gift!'

'You are too late, fool! Amarthiel rewards those who serve her faithfully and well, and such have I done!
'These Men will serve her well when they come to fight in the old city, and I will be rewarded for bringing them. But first I will destroy you!'
Find Amarthiel's emissary to the Gauredain
Find Amarthiel's emissary to the Kergrim
Find Amarthiel's emissary to the Men of Rantost
Chapter 7: Emissaries of Evil
Mordrambor has translated the orders you recovered from Angmarim in Annúminas and revealed a deadly plan to gain more allies in the fight for the city.

'Mordrambor willingly translated the orders for us? I must confess that I did not believe he would do so easily!
'We must use caution, ${PLAYER}, for he is not to be trusted, but if we can hinder the plans of these emissaries, we might prevent much bloodshed.
'Look for boats along the shore of the lake near each of the three allies of which Mordrambor spoke. You should find the emissaries not far from their landings, unless we are too late.'

'You have defeated Amarthiel's emissaries? This is wonderful news, ${PLAYER}, even if some loyalties had already changed. Tadan will be delighted to hear that the prisoner has lightened our burdens with his information, no matter how untrustworthy he may be.'

'Speak to thy friend, if thou must. Tell him that his days will be shorter than thine.
'Amarthiel will soon have new allies, their loyalties bought with gold, and thou shalt feel the sting of their blades and the bite of their teeth.'
'It has been some time since I have seen thee, foolish ${RACE}. Hast thou been scurrying about on futile errands?'

'This is just the sort of information for which Calenglad was hoping, ${PLAYER}! If you can defeat these emissaries before they can coerce the loyalty of these three enemies, Amarthiel's plans will be hindered!
'We may not be able to trust Mordrambor's words, but we do not have a choice -- this is a chance we must take. If we can prevent Angmar from receiving these new allies, our capture of Mordrambor will have paid for itself a hundredfold!
'His words tell us that three Angmarim emissaries set forth across Lake Nenuial by boat, seeking to buy three new loyalties: the tomb-robbers on the island of Rantost, to the north-east; the Gauredain of the north-west hills of Emyn Uial, and the Kergrim of Men Erain. Find and stop these emissaries of evil, ${PLAYER}! Look for their boats along the shores of the lake, near to each of these threats, for they are sure to be near, unless we are too late.'

Mordrambor told you of three Angmarim emissaries sent to buy the loyalties of new allies for Amarthiel's armies in Annúminas: the tomb-robbers on the island of Rantost, in the north-east corner of the lake, the Gauredain near the north-west corner of the lake, and the Kergrim among the tombs of Men Erain, along the south-east corner of the lake.
Mordrambor has told you of three emissaries sent by boat across Lake Nenuial to buy the loyalties of some of the evils that plague Evendim.

Ranger Tadan is in the prison atop the flight of stairs on your left as you enter the keep on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
You have defeated the three emissaries sent by Amarthiel to recruit new allies for the battle of Annúminas and should now report of your victories to Tadan.
You have successfully defended Gwonil's position
You have successfully defended Torchirion's position

'I understand thou hast already seen the sites of Amarthiel's next assault, friend ${PLAYER}, and their defenders believed in the strength of their defences.
'But this time will be different, for Amarthiel has new servants, and thy struggles have come to naught. Hurry now to thy master, to Calenglad of Tinnudir, and tell him where his friends will be slain: at the Port of Annúminas and the gate of Adannon.
'Amarthiel has told me the names of those marked for death: Gwonil and Torchirion. Tell Calenglad they will come no more out of Annúminas. Pay close attention to his grief, friend ${PLAYER}...I look forward to hearing news of it!'

'What ails you, ${PLAYER}? You do not look well. Perhaps you should take some rest? The foes arrayed against us are fearful, but we must renew our strength from time to time -- you cannot fight such an enemy for so long without rest.
'What is this news you bring? Mordrambor has given us the locations of Amarthiel's next assaults on the city? The Port of Annúminas and the gate of Adannon, as before? What does she hope to accomplish with this renewed assault? Go quickly now to Gwonil at the docks and Torchirion at Adannon and help them repel these new attacks!
'I am sorry, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps you can take some rest when this attack is ended? We cannot lose those positions now!'
'Once again the words of Mordrambor have guided us true, ${PLAYER}? It was good fortune indeed that allowed you and Tadan to make him a prisoner of the Rangers.'
'I do not see anything, ${PLAYER}. Are you sure the prisoner said they were planning a fresh assault upon the docks?'
'It has been quiet since last you were here, ${PLAYER}. I suspected the Angmarim might be planning a fresh assault, but I have seen no signs of it thus far.'
Talk to Gwonil and defend her position
Talk to Torchirion and defend his position
Chapter 9: A Renewed Assault
In exchange for bringing his message to Laerdan, Mordrambor has given you the locations of Amarthiel's next planned assault upon Annúminas.
'You have my thanks once again, ${PLAYER}! I am deeply saddened to face Men of Evendim in battle; the gold of Angmar has too easily turned their hearts from mischief to evil.'
'All else might fall, but still you and I will hold the gate of Adannon against all aggressors! Is it not so, ${PLAYER}?'

'These have been trying times for all of us, ${PLAYER}, but I promise you: once you have aided Gwonil and Torchirion in the defence of the Port of Annúminas and the gate of Adannon, we will try to rely less heavily upon you. You will be able to take some rest.'

'Run and tell thy master, Calenglad, that he will soon have reason to mourn his friends at the Port of Annúminas and at the gate of Adannon.
'Thou shalt report his grief to me, friend ${PLAYER}, will thee not?'

'Thou spakest with Calenglad? Good, good. Perhaps now he will see that there can be no victory against Angmar's regent. Dost thou wish to aid thy friends at the Port and at Adannon or hast thou decided to see the truth? These fools cannot stand against us.'

'Pay no heed to the prisoner, ${PLAYER}. Laerdan was right: his words are vile and mean nothing!
'He toys with us, but still we can learn things of value. Gwonil and Torchirion are friends of mine, and if we can come to their defence as a result of Mordrambor's words, I will be willing to suffer his vile whisperings.
'Bring this news to Calenglad! He must be told what awaits us!'

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Mordrambor has told you to tell Calenglad of the planned locations for Amarthiel's next assaults: the Port of Annúminas and the gate of Adannon.

Gwonil is on the docks at the Port of Annúminas, north of Echad Garthadir. Torchirion is at Adannon, a small gate in the city wall west of the docks that provides access to the western shore of Lake Nenuial.
Calenglad has asked you to hurry to the defence of Gwonil and Torchirion; according to the words of Mordrambor, they will bear the brunt of Amarthiel's latest assault upon the city.

Calenglad is at the Ranger-camp on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
You have defended Gwonil and Torchirion from the assaults foretold by Mordrambor and should now return to Calenglad with news of your success.

'The prisoner has been smirking about something the whole time you have been gone, and it has had me worried.
'He is feeling sure of himself about something. He keeps muttering something about new attacks upon the city, but whenever I ask him about them, he refuses to talk to me.
'Perhaps you can get something out of him? He does not seem to be concerned about withholding information from you, ${PLAYER}.'

'Thou sayest Amarthiel's emissaries art defeated? I read more in thine eyes than thou hast spoken. Perhaps their duties were already fulfilled, their missions completed? Aye, I read you a-right. But smile on, fool ${RACE} -- against Angmar and its regent there can be no hope for thee. She plans a new assault upon certain sites within the city, and thy Dúnedain friends cannot hope to stand against her.
'And yet...I will tell thee where these assaults will come the hardest. I greatly desire to hear thy weeping and the weeping of this fool Ranger when Amarthiel seizes the city in spite of thy meagre defences. But I will tell thee where the hammer will fall only if thou dost something for me.
'An Elf has come to this keep; he looked on me from afar when this fool Ranger brought me to this pathetic prison. This Elf is named Laerdan, and I would have thee bring him a message. The message is this: \qLaerdan, thy time is soon ended, thy mistakes soon accounted. Amarthiel awaits thee in Barad Tironn, where she will sit in judgment over thee.\q Thou shalt bring him these words, or thou shalt learn naught from me.'

'I am glad to see thee return, my friend, for I know that thou hast delivered my message to Laerdan. I know too what he must have said to thee: \qSteel yourself to his words! Remain alert against his subtleties!\q
'What did thou callest thyself? ${PLAYER}? I give thee my thanks, ${PLAYER}, for upholding our bargain. I will now do the same.
'I will tell thee where the next assaults upon the city will come, friend ${PLAYER}.'

'Steel yourself against the words of Mordrambor, ${PLAYER}, for he is skilled in the tangling of thoughts, as are most of his kind. He will seek to confuse you with artful trickeries and misleading phrases, and through them lead you only into treachery. Remain alert to his subtleties, and he will be unable to hold any power over you!
'I have heard his message and ask that you now heed mine: do not relax your guard! Even imprisoned, a Black Númenórean is a dangerous foe, and he will lead us all to harm if we do not take care to guard against his devices!
'Return now to your prisoner and tell him that you have fulfilled your side of the bargain. And remember my words!'
Chapter 8: The Prisoner's Message
Mordrambor has told you that Amarthiel plans renewed assaults at specific locations within the city, but he will only tell you where if you deliver a message for him.

'The prisoner is in no position to make demands, ${PLAYER}! But I must admit that it is a tempting offer: what lives might we save with the foreknowledge of where Amarthiel will strike next?
'Laerdan is a wise Elf. There can be no harm in delivering the prisoner's message, and there is much to gain.'

'Hurry now to our prisoner and tell him you have upheld our end of the bargain! There is little time to waste, ${PLAYER}, for on this matter I do not doubt that he was speaking truth: Amarthiel is planning fresh assaults, and we must know where she will attack!'
'Thou hast not delivered my message to the Elf Laerdan, and I will tell thee naught.'
'You should try talking to Mordrambor, ${PLAYER}. I know it is not pleasant, but if we can get more information about what Amarthiel has planned for Annúminas, we will be better for it!'

'I do not like this, ${PLAYER}. What harm can these words do, ill-tempered and objectionable as they are? Still, they make me uneasy. And yet, if he tells us where next to expect Amarthiel's assault, many of my brethren might be saved.
'I do not see what choice we have. Laerdan is a wise Elf; he will see these words for what they are -- the foul insults of a desperate prisoner -- and dismiss them.
