'Laerdan has been given a room atop the stairs behind the door on your right as you enter the keep.'

'I do not need Laerdan to tell me that our prisoner is not to be trusted! Still, he has been very useful to us so far, and for once the battle seems to be turning in our favour. Amarthiel surely rues the night we took one of her prized lieutenants from her!'
'Do not trust him, ${PLAYER}. Mordrambor will try to confuse you with his words, to ensorcel you with his speech. You must guard yourself from this, even as he appears powerless, for he is not so.'

Mordrambor is in the prison atop the stairs through the door on your left as you enter the keep on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
Mordrambor has been muttering about new attacks upon the city, but refuses to give Tadan any further details. Tadan hopes you may be able to get some information from the prisoner.

Laerdan has been given a room in the keep on the island of Tinnudir, atop the stairs behind the door on your right as you enter the keep.
Mordrambor has told you that Amarthiel plans renewed assaults on the city of Annúminas, but will only reveal the locations for these new attacks if you deliver a message to Laerdan: 'Laerdan, thy time is soon ended, thy mistakes soon accounted. Amarthiel awaits thee in Barad Tironn, where she will sit in judgment over thee.'

Mordrambor is being held prisoner in the prison atop the stairs on your left as you enter the keep on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.
You have delivered Mordrambor's message to Laerdan as he requested, and the Elf told you to beware the Black Númenórean's treachery, for even imprisoned he poses great danger. If he upholds his word, Mordrambor should now tell you the location of Amarthiel's latest planned assault on Annúminas.

'Listen to me! I would do well to remember Laerdan's words to you -- Mordrambor is still a servant of the Enemy, and despite the usefulness of his information, he would bring us all to harm if given the chance. I temper my words of good fortune with a reminder to use caution when dealing with him; it is a reminder we both should take to heart!
'Laerdan came to speak with me while you were away; he wished to know if any progress had been made in recovering the palantír. I told him of our military victories, but he did not seem encouraged by the news. We do not see eye to eye on this matter, he and I, but surely you must see that our successes in Annúminas are crucial for taking the seeing-stone from Amarthiel?
'I could not ease his mind, and Laerdan asked that you see him in his room in the keep when you return. Perhaps you can make him see the rightness of our course? Annúminas must be reclaimed before we can hope to wrest the palantír from Amarthiel's clutches. We have time, ${PLAYER}. Tell him this.'

'Didst thou repulse the attacks on thy friends? It matters not, but I admire thine efforts in the face of such overwhelming odds.
'Thou canst not prevail against Guldurchir, friend ${PLAYER}, no matter how strong or wise thou thinkest thyself to be, for Guldurchir wields Tann Morgul.
'The defeat of the Dúnedain will be complete when he brings its power to bear upon the city.'

'I will look forward to Laerdan's visit, ${PLAYER} -- the prisoner is not very good company, and I have seen him giving me unpleasant looks out of the corner of my eye.
'The air in this room feels so stifling, too! I may see if I can have Forchon or Naethmunn take a shift or two, after Laerdan's visit. It will do me good to clear my head and put an end to the prisoner's constant ramblings.
'He has taken to rattling off the exploits of his fellows, one of them in particular. If I never hear the name \qGuldurchir\q again, I would be greatly pleased.'

'${PLAYER}, welcome! I am glad that you have come. You do not seem well, my friend. You cannot defend all of Annúminas yourself, despite Calenglad's wish that you might.
'I asked you to come because I want to know if Mordrambor has spoken at all of the palantír to you. He has not? I find it most interesting that he has kept you busy with military matters in the city, while we know that Amarthiel has a palantír in her possession. My heart tells me that Mordrambor is delaying us for his mistress. Her goal has not changed: she seeks Narchuil. Do not be distracted by the errands on which he sends you!
'Will you bring my words to Tadan, the Ranger that guards Mordrambor? Tell him that I will come to see him in a few hours -- I want to ensure that he is alert to the danger of his prisoner's whisperings.'
Chapter 10: Do Not Trust Him
Mordrambor has been a useful prisoner, but Calenglad and Laerdan are both concerned that he still wields some power for deceit.
'Laerdan is in his room atop the stairs on your right as you enter the keep on this island. Tell him that we must retake Annúminas before it will be possible to reclaim the palantír!'
Mordrambor stares at you coldly and says nothing.
'Listen to him! It is enough to drive a man mad, ${PLAYER}. I am looking forward to Laerdan's visit, if only to have a reprieve from the prisoner's constant mumbling!'

'My heart tells me that our prisoner is using us, ${PLAYER}. He is spinning words to make Calenglad do exactly what Amarthiel wants him to do -- waste time fighting meaningless battles while the real work, the dangerous work, is being done with the palantír.
'If you would, speak with Tadan and tell him that I will come see him in a few hours. I want to remind him of the danger Mordrambor poses for us all, even imprisoned.'

Laerdan is in his room atop the stairs behind the door on your right as you enter keep on the island of Tinnudir, in Evendim.

'Guldurchir has been defeated? I am filled with wonder, ${PLAYER}!'

'Thou wishest to hear more of Tann Morgul, friend ${PLAYER}? I thought thou wouldst. It is a relic of ancient Númenor, corrupted through the dark arts of my brethren and gifted to Guldurchir for safe-keeping. Thou wonderest why he has not brought it to bear upon the city? The reason is simple: Amarthiel forbade him from using it until she had derived as much amusement as she could from the pathetic struggles of the Dúnedain.
'That time draws near. If thou wishest to postpone thine utter defeat, thou wouldst do well to relieve Guldurchir of Tann Morgul, and soon. His restraint will not last forever.
'My jailor has something to say? What could that be, ${PLAYER}?'

'We have come to it at last, ${PLAYER}, I can feel it! I have not had an easy time guarding the prisoner, but it will all be worthwhile if we can defeat this Guldurchir before he is permitted to use Tann Morgul against us!
'We are in luck, too, because I have fought against Guldurchir and know where he is! Shortly after Annúminas was taken, a small group of us fought to the uppermost level of the city. There, in a courtyard full of fell idols and cursed trappings above Echad Garthadir, we encountered Guldurchir. He drove us away, and our assault ended in defeat.
'That courtyard is called Menelband. If you can fight your way up through the city to Menelband, you might be able to defeat Guldurchir and take Tann Morgul from him -- the day could be ours!'

'Yes, my friend, yes....
'Untie my bonds and give me the relic you have taken from Guldurchir, Tann Morgul, heirloom of fallen Númenor....'
'Thou hast not taken Tann Morgul from Guldurchir? How can this be?'

'What do you think you were doing, ${PLAYER}? I do not know what happened to me, but something seemed to shake me from a deep slumber, and I saw you about to untie the prisoner!
'You need to steel yourself against his wiles! Did not Laerdan tell you that? He is treacherous, our prisoner, and we cannot let down our guard for an instant!
'I will take Tann Morgul and bring it to Calenglad. I do not think it is wise for you to spend too much time in the company of Mordrambor, ${PLAYER}. Calling you \qfriend\q all the time...I do not trust him, and neither should you!'
'Where is Tann Morgul, ${PLAYER}? Where can it have gone?'

Chapter 11: Guldurchir's Restraint
Mordrambor has told you that one of his brethren, a Black Númenórean called Guldurchir, possesses an artifact of great evil that will be used to destroy the Dúnedain.

'Guldurchir is known to me -- he is one of Amarthiel's Black Númenórean lieutenants, and as such is one of Mordrambor's brethren. That our prisoner would betray him so readily feels strange to me.
'Still, Mordrambor has spoken true until now. If this artifact is as deadly as he has led us to believe, we cannot allow it to remain in Guldurchir's hands.
'Menelband is a courtyard on the uppermost level of Annúminas, and it is the site from which Guldurchir oversees the battle.'

'We have had several run-ins with Guldurchir -- he is known to me, and every encounter with him is an evil memory.
'The courtyard of Menelband is his station. Head east of Echad Garthadir until you see a steep slope leading southward; you must climb the slope and immediately double back westward. That will take you to Menelband, on the highest level of the city.
'Your news of this artifact he bears, Tann Morgul, does not surprise me. What surprises me is that Amarthiel would command him not to use it. What will happen when he abandons his restraint on this matter?'
'Get thee from my sight, thou worthless worm! Thou shalt pay for thy failure!'
'I will not keep thee from speaking with my jailor, friend ${PLAYER}. He is most tiresome, but perhaps thou canst teach him to mind his betters.'

'My pitiful jailor is correct -- Guldurchir oversees the battle from Menelband, a courtyard on the highest level of the city. Thou art strong, friend ${PLAYER}, but Guldurchir is stronger. He will slay thee, and thy friends will be utterly destroyed.
'Thou canst not hope to take Tann Morgul from him. That is folly.'
'Guldurchir oversees the battle for the city from Menelband, the uppermost courtyard of Annúminas. Defeat him and wrest Tann Morgul from his clutches, ${PLAYER}!'

'I have not been feeling very well of late, ${PLAYER}. My head feels heavy, as if it is full of water, and I cannot shake it out.
'I must just be tired. I just wish I could have a rest from our prisoner's constant muttering!'
'I have never heard of Tann Morgul before now, ${PLAYER}, but Guldurchir is known to me: wholly evil and merciless. Be mindful of the danger should you seek to confront him.'
'I have never heard of Tann Morgul before now, ${PLAYER}, but Guldurchir is known to me: wholly evil and merciless. Be mindful of the danger should you seek to confront him.'

'Laerdan came to see me, as you said he would, and he told me much the same: that our prisoner remains dangerous. I did not pay as much attention to these words as I should have, it seems!
'But I have something to tell you that this unfortunate business with Tann Morgul drove from my mind until now -- Laerdan has learned the location of Amarthiel's palantír and has devised a scheme by which it might be recovered!
'He is waiting for you in his room. I do not want to say any more about it while in the presence of the prisoner, but you should talk to Laerdan about this at once!'
'${PLAYER}! I had not expected to see you again so soon. Why have you come to me?'

'${PLAYER}, welcome! You look better than when last I saw you -- did you manage to take some rest at last? The time for open fighting is over. Calenglad is wise and strong, but he has been blinded by his pride: he will not retake Annúminas before Amarthiel locates Narchuil.
'Mordrambor is a creature of lies, but in taunting me, I believe he has made a mistake. He said Amarthiel waited for me in Barad Tironn, do you remember? Barad Tironn was where the kings of Annúminas sat in judgement and heard the concerns of their people. The histories do not agree on this point, but a number of them record that the palantír of Annúminas was kept at Barad Tironn for the use of the kings. That palantír of Annúminas is gone, drowned beneath the sea, but surely that is where Amarthiel strives with the palantír she has recovered.
'We must assault Barad Tironn and reclaim the palantír, ${PLAYER}. But hold! Do not rush to Calenglad just yet! This palantír has been bound to the evil of the Enemy, and the merest touch of it will cause us harm. We need some means to carry it. Golodir has such a means at Gath Forthnír. Though it may cause him grief to remember the events of his fall, you must speak with Golodir on this matter. Only he can provide us with what we need.'

'You say you have come from Laerdan, and that he believes I may play a part in reclaiming the palantír that was taken from Carn Dûm? The seeing-stone is wholly evil! I see that now, and wish I had never been made to gaze into it. Mordirith has paid for his torment of me, but even that will never be enough to satisfy his debt! No act of vengeance will bring back my poor, lost Lorniel!
'Laerdan speaks the truth. Even as Mordirith brought me forth from the gates of Carn Dûm, the hateful images of the palantír still burned into my mind, I clutched in my hand the black cloth with which the seeing-stone was covered when not in use. The terrible events of that day had all but pushed it from my memory, but I remember it now. Hold the palantír only with this finely-woven cloth bag, else the stone will seek to show you such things that might bring you to despair. Do not touch the palantír without this bag! I do not wish for you to endure what I was made to endure!
'Give Laerdan my good wishes, but warn him not to underestimate our enemy. He is a good Elf and true, but in him alone have I recognized the terrible burden I have borne in the days since Lorniel was lost to me. Something gnaws at his heart, and I fear it will bring him to harm if he does not guard against it.'

'My jailor is a fool, ${PLAYER}, but even he is not the fool thou art, given to pride and an irresistable desire to do good. And yet, what is good? Thou hast done only what the regent of Angmar, and I, her greatest servant, desired of thee! It was no accident that brought me to the tomb of long-dead Elendil with so few servants. Thou didst not think Amarthiel would needlessly risk the life of one so valuable, surely?
'While I have had thee running errands about the city and on pilgrimages to the far shores of vast Nenuial, she has been gazing into the palantír she retrieved from Carn Dûm, willing it to show her that which she seeks. I am greater now than Guldurchir, for it was at her suggestion that I told you he bore Tann Morgul! He thought to use it to challenge her for leadership of Angmar; thou wert a useful pawn in his removal. Amarthiel shall thank thee for it.
'But now I have completed my greatest task, the task for which she sent me to thee, ${PLAYER}: the delivery of Laerdan to her at Barad Tironn. She has much in store for the Elf, much for which she has waited long. Didst thou think that Laerdan was innocent? Thou art twice the fool, then, or thrice so! Run to thy master, ${PLAYER}, and tell Calenglad of thy folly: Laerdan will not return from Barad Tironn, or if he does, it will be in a form none shall recognize, wholly twisted and evil. I have but one task remaining to me, and I will relish its execution.'

'What is this? A note from Laerdan?
'This is my fault, ${PLAYER}! How could I have been such a fool? Laerdan offered to watch the prisoner for a time, and I agreed -- I have not felt well for some time, and I thought some fresh air would do me well; I said as much to you, if you recall.
'The prisoner must have said something to Laerdan during that time, woven some foul tangle of words! What sad irony, for Laerdan to succumb to this treachery, when he oft spoke to us of its danger!'

'Every decision I have made has gone ill, ${PLAYER}; my thoughts of victory turn to ash, even as it seemed so near! For Laerdan to pay this price for the mistaken pride of the Dúnedain fills me with sorrow. May a thousand curses fall upon the heads of Mordrambor and his fell mistress!
'Nay, I will not give in to despair, though things seem darkest. Our prisoner is a creature of lies and deceit, and despite his cruel whisperings, we have won great victories in Annúminas. Can this be a ruse, risen from the desperation of a captive whose plans have not borne the expected fruit? Can it be that Amarthiel's search has gone less well than she hoped, and that Mordrambor seeks now to fill us with despair where none should be?
'We may be able to save Laerdan and recover the palantír, as he intended, ${PLAYER}. Though he has left us, perhaps the Dúnedain can repay Laerdan for his friendship. One last assault on the steps of Barad Tironn may get you and your friends within its walls, ${PLAYER}, and we shall see if there is any truth to Mordrambor's words. We shall see if the time has come yet for despair, or if our greatest victory is at hand!'
'You do not have anything for me, ${PLAYER}? How can this be?'

Laerdan believes that the time for reclaiming Annúminas has passed. Now, all of your attention must turn to wresting the palantír from Amarthiel before she can learn the location of lost Narchuil.

'If you touch the palantír with your hands, the Enemy could show you such things as would freeze your heart. Use only the finely-woven cloth bag I gave you to carry it; even then, the effect of the seeing-stone upon your mind may be great. Steel yourself against it!
'Return to Laerdan with this and with my good wishes, but caution him not to underestimate our enemy. I recognize in him the burden I have borne since the loss of Lorniel, and I fear for him.'

'What is this? A note on Laerdan's door? I fear this can signify only evil, ${PLAYER}, and I fear for him.
'You must read the note, my friend, though it may be hard. We must know to what end Laerdan has set himself.'
'I can feel thy despair, ${PLAYER}. To me it tastes sweet and cries out that thine end comest quickly.'
Mordrambor stares at you smugly, a half-smile playing across his lips, but says nothing.

'This is terrible news, ${PLAYER}! We have been so careless, and Laerdan must pay the price for our folly!
'Bring these ill tidings to Calenglad at once, my friend -- surely he will know what we can do, if there is anything to be done!'

'Too long have I delayed, hoping to reclaim the city from the forces of Angmar, but I see now that victory in Annúminas will not be complete if Amarthiel learns the location of Narchuil. We will have traded victory here for defeat elsewhere -- this was the lesson of Laerdan, but I did not see it!
'Speak to me when your allies are ready, and we will launch a final assault upon Barad Tironn! If we are successful, you will have access to the inner chamber, where one of you must pick up the palantír and carry it back to the entrance, where I will be waiting -- if you have the finely-woven cloth bag given to you by Golodir, the palantír should not harm you. Protect the bearer of the palantír from the attacks of the enemy!
'Much depends upon this, ${PLAYER}, for we will not have another chance. If you see Laerdan within the depths of Barad Tironn, do what you can, but do not endanger yourselves needlessly. The retrieval of the seeing-stone must come first -- it is what he would have wanted: the eye of Angmar blinded once more.'

'The victory is bittersweet, my friend, for Laerdan has been taken by the Enemy and we do not have the numbers to stage another assault upon Barad Tironn. I fear that he is lost to us, and although the palantír is now free of Amarthiel's clutches, it seems she learned at least some of the information she sought. Only Time now keeps her from reclaiming Narchuil, the ring she lost so long ago.
'I will bring the palantír to one that will keep it safe. We have done what we could, ${PLAYER}, but it was not enough. A hundred curses upon the Iron Crown! It has taken so much from us, and for every victory it deals us a dozen hurts!
'And yet, we fight on. It has always been the way of the Dúnedain, and I know it is your way as well, ${PLAYER}. What else is there to do? We will fight on in Laerdan's name, and in the names of all those who have fallen, and one day Amarthiel will pay for each and every one. I swear it on the bones of my fathers and my fathers' fathers. We will see it done, ${PLAYER}.'

'The Angmarim are cruel beyond measure, ${PLAYER}, drowning the prisoners they have taken off the docks of the Port of Annúminas. They take pleasure in the suffering of their victims and must be stopped! We must put an end to these barbaric acts!
'I beg of you, if you are a friend to the Dúnedain and to the people of this land, hurry down to the docks that extend into the waters of Nenuial and put an end to these practices!
'Such cruelty deserves to be repaid tenfold, ${PLAYER}, but we must be content to free the prisoners from their cruelty. Would that we could devise even worse punishments for these servants of the Iron Crown!'

'I thank you from the very bottom of my heart, ${PLAYER}. I am relieved that some of the prisoners, at least, were given freedom.
'A day will come when Angmar will pay for the full extent of its crimes!'

'The battle rages across the streets of the city on each level, and the Angmarim push us back at every opportunity. Let us give them a taste of defeat, ${PLAYER}!'

'Thank you for your efforts, ${PLAYER}! Every sword-swing, staff-thrust, and bow-shot that finds its mark ensures that there will be fewer Angmarim to fight tomorrow!

'${PLAYER}, we are in a difficult position. The Angmarim have been unable to force us from Echad Garthadir thus far, but every assault taxes our strength more than the last. We cannot hold out forever, despite Badhordam's efforts to resupply and Fainneleg's cunning strategies.
'Long ago, the Dúnedain hid a number of supply stores of weapons and armour throughout the city, against the fear that some enemy might attempt to take and hold Annúminas. If you can find some of these hidden stores and return to me with their contents, we will be able to replace our damaged equipment and better continue the fight with the Angmarim in the city.
'I do not know the locations of these hidden stores, but if you search in out-of-the-way locations within Annúminas, you will surely find them. It is possible that the Angmarim will have come across some of the stores and looted them.'

'You have done very well, ${PLAYER}. Thank you for searching for these stores! They had to be well-hidden for them not to have fallen into the hands of the enemy, so I know you have been particularly wise to have found them.
'Fainneleg will be pleased that we can replace some of our damaged equipment. With these supplies, the fight against the Angmarim here in Annúminas can continue for some days yet!'

'Glinghant was once the most beautiful place in all of Annúminas -- no small feat given the splendor of the ancient city at its height. Descriptions of the pools and gardens of Glinghant hold a special place in the hearts of my people. Even after the long years of decay, you could see the memory of its beauty.
'The coming of Amarthiel and her legions to Annúminas is cause itself for sorrow, but of all the harm they have caused to this city, their possession and despoiling of Glinghant stirs me most to rage. I would cast them out of this place and restore the splendour it had of old, even should the rest of Annúminas fall. In that, I am not joined by most of my kindred, but such is my horror at the spoiling of Glinghant.
'Amarthiel has many servants, but to Glinghant she has sent the darkwater: foul spirits of corruption led by a grisly demon called Nengon. If you should venture beyond the gate into the terraced steps of Glinghant, I would account you highly should you defeat Nengon and his corrupting brethren.'

'It is good that you have defeated Nengon, for the darkwater cannot be allowed to remain within Glinghant.
'I will reward you for this brave deed.'

'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. Fainneleg and Calenglad want the entire city retaken, and certainly I do as well, but Glinghant is most dear to me. I am overjoyed that you have bested Nengon and his vile allies. There is nothing so sad to me as natural beauty despoiled, and that is what Glinghant has become.
'But perhaps not for long, my helpful ${CLASS}!'

'Knowledge can be the greatest weapon in war, ${PLAYER}. It can turn the tide of battle, for good or for ill. I speak to you now of a matter so urgent that there can be no delay, for it concerns knowledge that could spell doom for my people...not here in the city, but elsewhere in Middle-earth.
'When the darkwater first came to Annúminas, some of my kindred attempted to banish them from the pools of Glinghant. I would have joined their fight, for its pools and gardens are dear to me, but Fainneleg commanded that I help with the initial defence of Gwaelband. I and Gwonil fought bravely and turned back an Angmarim assault, but while we survived to receive other assignments, the Dúnedain that fought in Glinghant did not. The darkwater overwhelmed them and the gardens were taken.
'But worse still, one of my fallen brethren bore on his person a map to the hidden refuge of Esteldín, in the North Downs. Folly, perhaps, to carry such a map, but what has been done has been done. We must retrieve the map before it can be taken by the Enemy. The darkwater may not appreciate its significance, but one of Amarthiel's more corporeal servants might. We must not let it fall into their hands, ${PLAYER}. Seek out the fallen Rangers in Glinghant and retrieve the map to Esteldín from him that bore it. Do this quickly, my friend, for there is little time to waste! If I am not around when you return, please bring the map with all haste to Captain-General Daerdan, at Echad Garthadir, here in the city.'
'You have done as I hoped you would, ${PLAYER}, and the safety of my kindred at Esteldín is ensured. I thank you.'
'You have not retrieved the map to Esteldín, ${PLAYER}. Why have you come back without it?'

'I will take the map, ${PLAYER}, in Harthadril's stead. I will tell her of your success when she returns, and reward you in the meantime.
'Many of my brethren have fallen within the city, but we may take some comfort that the location of Esteldín remains, for now, a secret.'
'You do not have the map to Esteldín, ${PLAYER}? Why is this so?'

'Ost Elendil, beyond the bridge of Ariant, was once the high seat of the kings of Annúminas. No longer -- after lying abandoned for a terribly long count of years, it is now held by the evil that came out of Angmar.
'Of Amarthiel's lieutenants, the Black Númenórean named Balhest is surely the most cruel. He it is that sits in Ost Elendil and holds it against us, behind an army of fell spirits and Angmarim sworn to him.
'Balhest must be defeated if we are to retake the city, ${PLAYER}. If it can be done, it must be. The Dúnedain cannot fight this foe alone. If I am not here when you return, bring this news to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, for he will be most pleased at your success!'

'You have put an end to Balhest? I can hardly believe it, but I know you speak the truth! Legrindavor will be as surprised as I am, but as pleased!
'Please take this reward for your victory!'

'You have defeated Balhest, ${PLAYER}? You have succeeded where many have failed! Surely Ost Elendil will not be in the hands of the Enemy for much longer, if we continue to have victories such as this!'
Balhest, Lord of Ost Elendil
Legrindavor told you of the Black Númenórean which Amarthiel has left in command at Ost Elendil.

'You will find Balhest deep within Ost Elendil, ${PLAYER}. If you can make it into the palace, across the bridge of Ariant...you will have done better than many of my kindred. The battle will not be easy, for Balhest is both powerful and cruel.'
'The defeat of Balhest is more than we could have expected, ${PLAYER}. Very well done!'
'Amarthiel's Black Númenóreans are her greatest servants.'

Balhest, one of Amarthiel's mightest Black Númenórean lieutenants, is in Ost Elendil.

You have defeated Balhest and should now return with news of your victory to Legrindavor.

'The Black Númenórean that sits in Ost Elendil is named Balhest. He is a powerful foe, but he is not the only evil that resides now in that place. We have learned that the passage into the throne room where Balhest commands his forces is guarded by the Cargûl known as Guloth. If you are to defeat Balhest, you will first need to do something about Guloth.
'He possesses some terrible power over creatures of shadow, drawing strength out of the darkness with which he commands them to his will. You must somehow sever Guloth's ability to strengthen the fell spirits under his command.
'Ost Elendil lies across the bridge of Ariant. Go there only if you are able and willing to face not only Balhest, lieutenant of Amarthiel, but also Guloth the Cargûl. If the battle has drawn me elsewhere by the time you return, report of your victory to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment here in the city.'
'You have defeated Guloth? I will tell Legrindavor when next he returns, and he will be overjoyed! Accept this reward for your victory.'

'You have defeated Guloth, ${PLAYER}? I rejoice at your success, for any Cargûl is a foe beyond measure, and Guloth is more dangerous than most. The Enemy will surely rue this defeat, as we are brought that much closer to retaking Annúminas from the Iron Crown!'

The Cargûl Guloth is inside Ost Elendil, beyond the bridge of Ariant on the highest level of Annúminas.
Legrindavor has warned you that Balchest is defended by a fearsome Cargûl, Guloth by name, who wields power over creatures of shadow.

Valandil is once again at peace.

'We have learned some troubling news, ${PLAYER}. It seems that Dolvaethor, one of Amarthiel's Black Númenórean lieutenants, has entered Haudh Valandil. I can think of no good reason for Dolvaethor to enter the tomb, but many terrible ones!
'Whatever Dolvaethor plans within the depths of wise Valandil's crypt, he must be stopped. You must do this, ${PLAYER} -- fighting your way across the bridge of Ariant and onto the island upon which sits Ost Elendil and Haudh Valandil will be terrible, but the Dúnedain lack the force of arms needed for this task. You and your allies, however, might be able to fight through.
'Once you have defeated Dolvaethor within Haudh Valandil, set right whatever harm he has caused, then return to me. If the course of battle has drawn me elsewhere, speak instead to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir.'

'Every moment Dolvaethor spent in Haudh Valandil is an insult to the king's memory, but I am pleased that his time is ended. I will reward you for this victory, but more than that you have my earnest thanks.'
'You have put an end to Dolvaethor's menace, ${PLAYER}? This is wonderful news! The tomb of Valandil shall remain undisturbed as long as we defend this place.'

'Dolvaethor will never again trouble us.'

'Ost Elendil, the great palace of the kings of old, is on the island beyond the bridge of Ariant. At its base is the entrance to Haudh Valandil, the tomb of Valandil son of Isildur. I fear that the tomb, long-undisturbed, has become the home to great evils: both of Angmar's design and otherwise.
'Have you seen the vile creatures known as Kergrim? They are believed to be some relative of the cave-claw, but more prone to disease and the desecration of hallowed places.
'Some of these beasts have come to Haudh Valandil, and they must be cleared from the tomb, especially their brute of a leader: Shingrinder, he is called, and he is vile. You will do this, ${PLAYER}, if you honour the ancient places of the Dúnedain, and you will return to me with news of your success. If I have been drawn elsewhere, report instead to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment here in the city.'
'Fewer kergrim now stalk the hallowed halls of Haudh Valandil? I am delighted to hear it, ${PLAYER}! I will reward you for this victory.'
'Fewer Kergrim now stalk the depths of Haudh Valandil? I am pleased to hear of it, ${PLAYER}. You are a true friend of the Dúnedain!'

'The kergrim stalk Haudh Valandil, ${PLAYER}, despoiling that ancient tomb with their filth and disease. They must be defeated if the peace of the tomb is to be maintained. Beware of Shingrinder, their vile leader!
'The tomb is on the island where stands Ost Elendil, beyond the bridge of Ariant.'
'The Kergrim are vile, filthy creatures and do not belong in the tombs of the kings.'
'Haudh Valandil must be kept free of evil.'

Kergrim stalk Haudh Valandil, the tomb on the island beyond the bridge of Ariant, in Annúminas.
Glangilith has asked you to defeat the kergrim that stalk the depths of Haudh Valandil, including their leader Shingrinder.

Glangilith is probably in Tirband, the court beneath the great watchtower on the highest level of the city. If he is not, he asked you to report instead to Captain-General Daerdan at the Ranger-encampment of Echad Garthadir at the heart of Annúminas.
You have defeated the Kergrim that stalked Haudh Valandil and should report news of your victory to Glangilith.
Collected priceless relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'The Black Númenórean Dolvaethor has gone to Haudh Valandil at Amarthiel's bidding, ${PLAYER}, and I fear the mischief he may cause in that hallowed place. The halls and tombs are lined with precious relics of the past -- relics of both great historical and personal value to the Dúnedain -- and they must not be despoiled!
'I ask you to recover as many of these priceless relics from the depths of Haudh Valandil as you can; my brethren will keep them in a safe place until the Angmarim have been defeated and the tomb is once more a place of peace.
'The entrance to Haudh Valandil is located on the island, beyond the bridge of Ariant. Beware of Dolvaethor and the kergrim that have awakened within its depths and recover the relics with all haste! If I am not here when you return, report to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment here in the city.'

'Thank you for this, ${PLAYER}. My heart is filled with song to know that the Angmarim these relics are not in in their foul clutches.
'My people will keep these safe until Amarthiel and her forces are cast out of Annúminas.'
'You have not recovered the relics from Haudh Valandil?'

'Glangilith has given me word that if you returned from Haudh Valandil, you would do so bearing priceless relics for safe-keeping. I see that you have, and I will reward you for bringing these relics out of the darkness.
'One day, when the Angmarim have been pushed out of Annúminas, we will return these relics to their proper home. Until then, we will keep them safe.
'I will reward you for this good deed.'
'You have not returned with the relics Glangilith thought you would.'
Collect priceless relics (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring priceless relics to Glangilith
Bring priceless relics to Captain-General Daerdan

'The entrance to Haudh Valandil is on the island beyond the bridge of Ariant. Recover the priceless relics from the depths of the tomb before the Angmarim can despoil them, and the Dúnedain shall preserve them until such time as Amarthiel and her forces are cast out of Annúminas.'

The entrance to the tomb is on the island beyond the bridge of Ariant, on the highest level of the city.
Glangilith has asked you to recover priceless relics from Haudh Valandil before the Angmarim ruin them.

Glangilith is in the court of Tirband, at the base of the watchtower that overlooks Annúminas. If he is not, he asked that you return the relics to Captain-General Daerdan at Echad Garthadir, the Ranger-encampment in the center of the city.
You have recovered several priceless relics from the depths of Haudh Valandil and should now give them to Glangilith, so that his people can keep them in safety until the Angmarim are cast out of Annúminas.

'Unni, the dwarf stablemaster just outside Ost Guruth, likely saw her as she left. Speak with him if you need to get your bearings, but following my sister's trail from that point will be up to you.'

The trail here is quite clear. Whoever made these tracks was moving without haste eastward.

'Another of my brother's ridiculous challenges? Well, I must offer you my congratulations, even if I do not appreciate the stream of hunters he always sends following me on my errands! He insists that he does not do it to keep an eye on me, but I know better.
'Trumswith once hunted Trampletusk, a great aurochs, but when he finally encountered the beast he was so struck by its majesty that he spared its life. I understand that the beast has left these lands now, but I do not know where it might have gone.
'Return to my brother in Ost Guruth and tell him of Trampletusk; he will know that your hunt has been successful. I hope too that he will cease with these silly challenges! You hunters have enough to do without following me!'

'Your name is ${PLAYER}, and you are a hunter? The Eglain have lived in these wilds for many a year; the ways of the wild are the ways of the Eglain. If you seek to learn of secret paths through the Lone-lands, you are right to come to me.
'I, Trumswith, can show you the signs that will allow you to make your way through the Lone-lands at great speed, leading the way for those in your fellowship who are not skilled in the ways of the hunt. I will do this for you if you can prove to me that you have the necessary skill. My sister Hogahild left Ost Guruth this morning. If you can find her trail, follow it until you meet with her. Ask her the name of the only beast I have ever hunted and yet spared, and I will teach you what I can.
'Hogahild left Ost Guruth near Unni, the dwarf stable-master by the stairs. You can speak with him to get your bearings, but will then need to find her trail on your own.'

'You speak of Trampletusk? Very good, ${PLAYER}! You have followed the trail of my sister and proven yourself of worthy skill!
'I will teach to you what you must know of finding your way in the Lone-lands. You will now be able to show your fellowship the quickest paths to return to Ost Guruth. You have earned my respect, and I will repay you with these teachings.'

Trumswith is at Ost Guruth, the Ruin-hold in the Lone-lands, far to the east of The Forsaken Inn, just north of the Great East Road.
You have been told to speak with Trumswith, one of the Eglain at Ost Guruth, who can train you in the ways of the wild.

Hogahild left Ost Guruth near Unni, the dwarf stable-master there, but is now somewhere in the wilderness of the Lone-lands.
Trumswith has challenged you to follow the trail of his sister Hogahild. If you can return to him with the name of the only beast he has hunted and spared, information known to Hogahild, he will teach you secret paths through the Lone-lands to Ost Guruth.

Trumswith is in Ost Guruth, the Ruin-hold in the Lone-lands.
You have followed her trail to Hogahild, the sister of Trumswith, and she told you the name of the only beast her brother has hunted and spared: the aurochs known as Trampletusk. You should return now to Trumswith with this information and he will teach you what he knows about the wild paths of the Lone-lands.

'Welcome to Tinnudir, ${PLAYER}. I can show you secret paths by which you can lead your fellowship here quickly, but you must prove to me that you are worthy to be taught such skills. You must know for what to look.
'I have hidden one of my arrow-heads somewhere in Evendim. If you can pick up my trail and follow the signs, you will be able to recover the arrow-head and prove to me that you are ready. If not, well...perhaps another hunter will succeed where you fail.
'I will tell you this: I crossed the bridge from Tinnudir to the mainland. So you will want to begin your search for my trail there.'

'Yes, this is my arrow-head! See these scratches here? I carved my initials there so I would be able to recognize it. A number of burglars have tried to pass themselves off as hunters, and I needed some way to catch imitations.
'I will teach you secret paths through Evendim, ${PLAYER}, so you will be able to lead your fellowship to Tinnudir with utmost speed.'

'I have heard that you have some considerable skill in the craft of metalsmithing, ${PLAYER}. I would ask something of you, if you would aid the Council of the North in their battle against Angmar.
'There are certain intricate symbols that we use to identify our warriors in the field in order to reduce the risk of enemies infiltrating our ranks. 'Greetings ${PLAYER}. You have come to us at a time of dire tidings. Our agents have discovered that the forces of Carn Dûm have re-awakened the ancient evil that lurks within a broad region of crypts and ruins called Imlad Balchorth, some way to the west and south of here.
'We require the aid of heroes brave enough to enter that place of death and destroy the unnatural creatures and evil Men who stalk its crumbling ways.
'Many of them carry amulets carved of bone which signify their allegiance to the Dark Lord. Claim these from them and bring them to me and you shall prove your worth to all here who strive against the power of the Iron Crown.'

'So, you are indeed a stalwart spirit to have braved the haunted ways of Imlad Balchorth -- I commend you for your valour, though the war is far from won, and many more such enemies shall we all face ere it is done.'

'You have not found any bone amulets among the enemy? I cannot fault you for hesitating in the face of such evil, but neither can we afford to be faint of heart in these dark times.
'We must weaken the evil that grows within Imlad Balchorth before it spills out into the lands of the North, as it once did in the ancient wars which brought the kingdom of Arnor to its ruin.'

'The gates of Carn Dûm open into Himbar, directly to our west. It is through these lands that the armies of Angmar march forth to bring ruin to the North.
'Many of the strongest servants of the Iron Crown reside within Himbar, making clear the way for their hordes -- it is here that we must harry the Enemy. We must hinder these outriders and thus slow the passage of their armies and supplies from the dark heart of Carn Dûm.
'Many of these servants carry daggers of a wicked design as proof of their allegiance to Angmar -- defeat them, claim these symbols, and return them to me, and your unwavering strength in the face of evil will be shown to the Council of the North.'

'Ah, you bring proof of your battles against the servants of Angmar -- tales of your bravery do not carry the full story as it should be told!
'If only the Enemy was so few that one such as yourself could suffice against them, but many more remain to stand against us, and our work is far from done.'

'Poor hunting in Himbar? Alas, I fear there is no shortage of prey there along the causeway of the Enemy. Have they become so numerous that you have been driven away, perhaps?
'I hope not, for all of our sakes, for if the armies of Angmar pour forth unimpeded, then the North will surely fall.'

'I have need of your help in another matter of metalsmithy. 'At your service, ${CLASS}. We dwarves have toiled long under these Mountains and have crafted many wonderful and beautiful things as you no doubt can see. But the skill of the Dwarves of Thorin's Hall lies not in our mastery of stone and rock, but in the cutting of gemstones and the smithy of strong iron! Though we pride ourselves most on our jewel-crafting over any of our works of baser materials.
'If you bring to me finely-crafted dwarf-jewels, you might prove yourself someone of worth to the Dwarves of Thorin's Hall.
'You have returned with the dwarf-jewels. Splendid!'
'You have returned without the dwarf-jewels? I do not have time for idle craftsmen. Return when it is finished!'

'At your service, ${CLASS}. The Dourhands have been removed from Thorin's Hall, yet our anger at their deeds has not been satisfied. Many of the Longbeards suffered greatly under Gormr, and his treachery must be met with revenge!

'The lesser dwarves and servants should carry the crest of the Dourhand family; bring me these crests that we may repay blood with blood!'

'You have returned with the Dourhand crests? That is well. The blood-price set upon the deeds of the Dourhands is high, and these crests are only a pittance of their full payment to the Dwarves of Thorin's Hall.'

'At your service and your family's, ${PLAYER}. The finest jewellery in all of Eriador has been crafted by dwarf-hands in Thorin's Hall. But these Mountains do not give up their jewels willingly. 'A few veins of a very precious dwarf-stone run throughout Eriador. It is not often that even a small gem of craftable quality is found, but when one is uncovered it is a sight to behold. The gem sparkles like Kheled-zâram in the starlight and lays an enchantment of beauty and awe upon all who behold it!
'If you were to bring to me one of these necklaces crafted with a dwarf-stone, you would hold high honour amongst the dwarves of Thorin's Hall.'

'At your service and your family's, ${PLAYER}. The Dourhands have been mining in the Blue Mountains and have uncovered the remains of a lost dwarf-city, which the Elves are now calling Sarnúr.
'Though many of them are undoubtedly destroyed, ancient relics of the First Age surely still remain in the crumbling halls and deep caverns below the Blue Mountains. Can you imagine? The ancient works of the dwarves lying in the hands of those thieving murderers, it boils the blood! The Dourhands may lay claim to the treasures, but without proof of their ancestry, any dwarf may stake his claim, and I do it thus for the Longbeards!
'Retrieve any of these relics that you may find and bring them to me here at the Blue Stone Garrison. The Longbeards would be deeply in your debt for the return of any of the ancient works, great or small.'
'This is a wonderful find! I will send it off to the vaults right away. I am sure that the smiths will look over every inch of the relics. We are in your debt, ${PLAYER}'

'You have not recovered any of the relics? Dwarves often hide their treasures, but surely you weren't looking hard enough!

'Greetings, ${RACE}, you fight against the foes of Eriador in these lands, and this is good. There is no doubt within me that your resolve to win this battle is strong.
'Please, hear me out. We are assisting in this battle where we can, and we will continue to do so. I would ask, though, that you support us in our endeavours elsewhere to safeguard Eriador from the machinations of the North.
'Should you wish to assist us, return to me, and I will arrange for you to take the place of one of my brethren while he patrols the wilds of the Ettenmoors.'

'Your efforts allowed one of our number to assist the Free Peoples greatly, ${PLAYER}. You are to be thanked for the efforts that you put forth.
'The Rangers of Esteldín are indebted to you. You are truly a hero in the war against the Iron Crown.'
'Very well, this proves that you are an able and valorous person. Speak with me again and I will send you to stand in the stead of a Ranger while they come here to patrol the Ettenmoors.'
'Collect Tokens of Valour and return ten to me. I will then know that you are able enough to wake on the duties of the ranger who will come here in your stead.'

'Take heart! The battle here is ours, and though the foe has breached the walls of Lugazag, we may yet hold back their tide. Listen well, for I have an offer that you must consider strongly, ${RACE}.
'You are a proven warrior, a hero amongst the Free Peoples, and we ask this only of those who are willing. Lainedhel asked for assistance from the Rangers, and we have come to offer our aid. We have duties that need looking after elsewhere in Eriador, and if you are willing to stand there in our stead, we will remain here to fight the foes from the North.
'Think on this and speak to me when you have an answer to my request. I will wait here, friend.'
'Your duty is done, and we have done much to further solidify the strength of the Free Peoples here in the Ettenmoors. You have our thanks, ${PLAYER}.'
'This proves that you are capable, friend. Speak to me again and I will send you to take the place of ranger while they come here to patrol in your stead.'
'Return to me once you have enough of the Tokens of Valour. I will then call a ranger to patrol the Ettenmoors while you take their place elsewhere.'

'There is no rest for the wicked, ${PLAYER}. There is much yet to do...mainly getting forces here to stand against the enemy.
'Our troops are scattered throughout the wilds of the Ettenmoors, and we must make them aware of our victory. We can do this by setting a large beacon fire.
'Make your way through the Ettenmoors and gather the wood need to make this pyre, then return to me so we can light the fires to call our war-host home.'
'Yes, this will do nicely. If only there were more like you within our ranks, ${PLAYER}. The speed at which these slugs move is abominable.'
'Get out there, sluggard! You've a job to do!'
Deliver the materials to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
A Blaze for the South
Angmar claims the central keep of the Ettenmoors, but the main army has yet to receive the news. The War-tyrant has ordered his soldiers to collect the materials needed to set a beacon fire.

Head south from Tol Ascarnen into Hithlad to seek out the wood needed to build the signal fires to the south.
Though your forces took Tol Ascarnen, the keep is woefully undefended, and Kaasak has ordered you to build a pyre to call in reinforcements from the south. You should make your way into the Ettenmoors and search for kindling, timber, and larger logs to build a beacon fire large enough to call in reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen.
The Orc-archer has seen you
You worthless sack! You failed!

'${PLAYER}, I have worked with you before, and though I must continue to berate you in front of others, I believe you have earned my favour.
'I wish to assist Uzulthrang in his quest to recover Tol Ascarnen, and to that end, I would ask that you undertake a very dangerous mission for me. I have an archer who will fire a blazing arrow into the trees when you arrive within them. When this is done, a force will cross the bridge to battle into the keep.
'My only fear is that the foe is strong in those woods. This could mean your defeat.'
Stand in the open among the trees near Tol Ascarnen's western wall
Defeat is not an option!
A Blaze in the Trees
Paashum is trying to make his superiors in Angmar's army notice him. To that end he has asked you to undertake a mission involving great risk but a potential for great success.

Make your way to the copse of trees in the woods on the western side of Tol Ascarnen. Make your presence know there.
Paashum asked you to make your way into the small section of woods on the western shore of Hoardale near Tol Ascarnen. He hopes to send a force into the keep after setting the woods ablaze. You will need to be obvious enough to attract the enemy's attention.

'There is no rest for the wicked, ${PLAYER}. There is much yet to do.....mainly getting forces here to stand against the enemy.
'We need a fire so big that Lugbúrz will take notice! Ha! On the western parapet, we will build a massive beacon and call our reinforcements!
'Get your brethren together and bring us the wood we need to build that pyre. Go now, maggot!'

'We will build a fire and they will come. The western bridge will be safe! Best you think on this in the future, whelp. We might often have need of this type of defensive service.
'Best to be prepared, no?'
'Get out there, sluggard! You've a job to do!'
Deliver the materials to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
A Blaze for the West
Angmar claims the central keep of the Ettenmoors, but the main army has yet to receive the news. The War-tyrant has ordered his soldiers to collect the materials needed to set a large beacon fire.

Head south of Tol Ascarnen into Hithlad and the Grimwood forest to collect the wood needed to build the blaze.
Though your forces took Tol Ascarnen, the keep is woefully undefended, and Kaasak has ordered you to build a pyre to call in reinforcements from the west. You should make your way into the Ettenmoors and search for kindling, timber, and larger logs to build a beacon fire large enough to call in reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen.

'Listen well. In order to build a horn with which to call reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen, we need to gather some more parts, such as a strong and tall piece of heartwood to place the horn and sinew upon. Your task is to head south into Hithlad -- more importantly, the Grimwood -- to collect the heartwood of a Leafcull Huorn.
'You must be certain to collect a perfect heartwood, for no other will be able to withstand an assault from the Free Peoples. We must build a strong horn, understand?
'Go now and collect the heartwood from the Leafcull in Hithald.'
'A good find. When the horn and sinew are collected, we will have all that we need to build the horn.'
'Get a move on, sluggard. We need that heartwood, or the horn cannot be built. If I have need to warn you again, things will get very uncomfortable for you at the sulphur pits.'
Talk to Soldier Kaasak at Tol Ascarnen
Bleeding Heart

Building a horn to summon reinforcements to Tol Ascarnen requires that several pieces be collected and assembled for an Orc to watch over and use when the Free Peoples make their assault against the fort.

The Leafcull Huorns make their home in the southern woods of Hithlad. Find the huorn amonst the trees south of the Grimwood Lumber Camp in Hithlad, to the southwest of Tol Ascarnen.
Angmar's forces at Tol Ascarnen are building a horn to call reinforcements to the fight when the Free Peoples return to assault the area. Kaasak has tasked you with collecting the heartwood of a Leafcull Huorn to act as the stand upon which the horn will rest. Damaging the heartwood will make it useless.

'When the War-tyrant told me that he didn't like the bare walls we had here, I was at first confused. Don't smirk...you would be too, whelp, thinking that the War-tyrant wants to decorate the walls with something other than the mark of the Iron Crown or Lugbúrz. But then he tells me...oil, great gobs of boiling oil.
'We're going to need this oil, and we can only get it from the Free Peoples...the very ones we're trying to boil! We know there is a camp of them over the bridge to the south, so that is a good place to start.
'Scouts tell us that they can be found all throughout the Ettenmoors as well, though the best location is at Ost Ringdyr to the east. Get the oil and bring it back here. We'll cook up a nice surprise for the wretches.'
'This will do nicely. Get others to the task so we can build the iron belly and cook us some meals.'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'
Deliver the oil to Soldier Glat at Tol Ascarnen
Cooking Sauce
The Free Peoples will return to take Tol Ascarnen, and Angmar's defenders wish to strengthen the walls with deterents that will drive the foe away.

Oil can be found on the Free Peoples fighting throughout the Ettenmoors. The closest camp is over the southern bridge, though a larger group can be found at Ost Ringdyr, far to the east.
Angmar's Army is shoring up the defences at Tol Ascarnen. Glat needs oil with which to douse the Free Peoples who attempt to assail the keep.

'We won the day, no thanks to sluggards and dullards like you. Now we must continue to press our enemy, lest they regain a foothold and strike against us.
'We've received reports that there is a dwarf who arrived at the enemy encampment on the south side of the Hoarwell River. We must get to him before the enemy can call him to action.
'Gather some other maggots and make your way across the river to assail that Marshal Án at the camp. Stop him before he arrives to assail Tol Ascarnen. Do not fail us!'

'You fight well, at least within the company of a great many. You think that makes you something more than a maggot? Think again, slug. You are not worthy of Angmar's honour, no matter how much you think you have earned.
'Soon, when the true war begins and this battle is behind us, you will see. You will march in front of our war-host and fall first to the blades of our enemies.
'I hope to become a Taskmaster someday...do you think this speech was chiding enough?'
Return to Soldier Paashum at the encampment west of Tol Ascarnen
Counter Assault

An overeager dwarf-warrior made his way to the camp south of Tol Ascarnen when Angmar captured the keep. This dwarf would call the Free Peoples to his banner and make an assault against the fortress on his own, if given leave to do so.
'Quickly! We cannot risk this dwarf facing our champions in battle.'

The Free Peoples' encampment is south of Tol Ascarnen.
Paashum sent you to the enemy encampment south of Tol Ascarnen to find and defeat First Marshal Án. You should not attempt this alone as Án is a powerful combatant.

The Angmar-encampment is west of Tol Ascarnen.
A successful assault against the Free Peoples' encampment resulted in the slaughter of the First Marshal and many of the forces located in the encampment south of Tol Ascarnen.

'You there, worm. I've a mission that will get you killed or earn you great favour with the War-tyrant. This should please you. But then again, you might be the worthless slug that so many say you are, ${PLAYER}.
'Personally, I'd not give up my gruel to stand by your side longer than I must...but that may change.
'We must weaken the enemy at the southern bridge. To do this we must destroy the flag which faces south. With it gone, we will dishearten them, scattering the forces on the bridge back to their encampments and reduce a great number of defenders near Tol Ascarnen.'

'Scouts told me of your success, but I find your need for approval amusing. You did well for a worthless sack of slug-meat.
'You'd better fight harder than you work, else this battle is truly lost.'
Return to Soldier Paashum at the encampment west of Tol Ascarnen
Destroy the Southern Flag
Angmar suffers in misery as the Free Peoples hold Tol Ascarnen.
'Get to it maggot. While those forces stand, we will face a much harder fight.'

Flags call the enemy to Tol Ascarnen facing south on the Hoardale island. Cross the river and destroy the flag located north of the southern bridge.
Paashum has tasked you with a mission to destroy the flag which calls the enemy defenders to the southern bridge over the Hoardale River.

Paashum is at the encampment on the western bank of the Hoarwell River, west of Tol Ascarnen.
You carefully sneaked to the flag calling the Free Peoples to the defence of the southern bridge and destroyed it. This set-back will surely give your forces a chance to defeat the enemy within Tol Ascarnen.

'You there, worm. I've a mission that will get you killed or earn you great favour with the War-tyrant. This should please you. But then again, you might be the worthless slug that so many say you are, ${PLAYER}.
'Personally, I'd not give up my gruel to stand by your side longer than I must...but that may change.
'Our number lost out to the enemy at Tol Ascarnen, and now we must take the keep back, but there are many foes standing in our way. We can lessen this number if we can down their banners. Scouts report that the fools at the western bridge will scatter to other posts when their banner is lowered. If we can destroy that banner, we can increase our chances at winning the day.'
'I saw the flag fall, cur. You did well. Well enough that I might consider you as a warrior on the front line in the assault. Ha!'

Destroy the Western Flag
Angmar suffers in misery as the Free Peoples hold Tol Ascarnen.
'Get to it maggot. While those forces stand, we will face a much harder fight.'

Cross the bridge to the northeast of the camp and destroy the flag against the crumbling walls near the western shore of the Hoardale island.
Paashum has tasked you with a mission to destroy the flag which calls the enemy defenders to the western bridge over the Hoardale River.

Paashum is at the encampment on the western bank of the Hoarwell River, west of Tol Ascarnen.
You carefully sneaked to the flag calling the Free Peoples to the defence of the western bridge and destroyed it. This set-back will surely give your forces a chance to defeat the enemy within Tol Ascarnen.

'We've won the keep for a moment only, cur. You've a new task handed down from the War-tyrant himself, and you'll see it done or feel my boot!
'Across the river to the south, in the woods of Hithlad, stalks a great beast with shaggy fur. This beast has two great horns, though only one is needed for our purpose. The horn belongs to the mighty Rockwithers. We think it is the eldest of the Thistledown herd. Slaughter the beast and get its horn. Together with the sinew of drakes and the heartwood of a great Leafcull Huorn, we will build a horn to call our brethren to battle.
'To the south with you and don't return without the prize, maggot!'

'It's about time, you useless bag of flesh. I've a mind to flay your hide just for you taking so long.
'No matter...you did what was needed, and though I've a mind to see you suffer for your sluggard's way, I'd rather see the horn built so that there is a better chance we hold this tomb of stone.
'I'll pay you attention as you deserve. Take no solace though, you weak-livered wretch: it's a fleeting bit of accomplishment for you in a lifetime of worthless and wasted effort.'

'I told you not to return to me until you'd seen this through, you maggot. If your body wouldn't make such a nice blockade when the Free Peoples return, I'd gut you now, but I'd rather wait and use your sorry carcass as a shield myself.
'Get out there, sluggard! You've a job to do!'

'Well, the War-tyrant isn't satisfied with just oil. He wants iron, he says, for the oil.
'My head swims a moment, and I realize what he's saying. We need ore, iron ore to build a great iron belly to house the oil. Then we'll heat the oil and douse those wretches. Cooked meat for all!
'We know that the Isendeep Mine houses a great deal of ore. Go there, or if you think it too far a trek, find the dwarves. Those bearded slugs carry the ore sometimes.'
'This will do nicely, get others to the task so we can build the iron belly and cook us some meals.'
'Get to work, slug. I'm not in the habit of taking kindly to those who shirk their duties!'

'Stop staring at me all slackjawed and step-to.'

'We need more soldiers like you. Willing to do everything they are told without questioning the wisdom in the actions, mindlessly obeying my orders.

'You maggot! I gave you an order. Get it done or taste my fist.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. Perhaps during your travels through the regions around Rivendell you have noticed bands of Men gathering in force here and there -- often in obvious league with other forces from Angmar. These are the Corcur from the far North who claim descent from the ancient kingdom of Rhudaur, which once inhabited the region immediately west of the Misty Mountains.
'While it is most likely that their claims are false, it matters not, for Rhudaur was destroyed long ago after it betrayed its sister kingdoms of the North and threw in its lot with the Witch-king of Angmar.
'Any who wear the signet of Rhudaur are not welcome in our lands, and the Lords of Rivendell will look favourably upon any who wish to hunt down these intruders and show their rings as proof of their defeat.'

'It seems that you have inflicted some considerable injury upon the Corcur who seek to falsely claim these wild hills. Thanks to your efforts, it is all the less likely that the corrupt and foolish banner of Rhudaur will arise here again.'

'Many of the Corcur still stalk our hills, while our own hunters are distracted by matters most pressing. Take the battle to them, if you will, and you shall win the favour of the Elves of Rivendell.'

The Corcur falsely claim allegiance to the ancient fallen kingdom of Rhudaur, which allied itself with Angmar before it was destroyed, several centuries ago. These Men wear rings with the insignia of ancient Rhudaur as proof of their allegience to this false kingdom.

Imyl has asked you to recover the signets of Rhudaur, which the Corcur wear as a symbol of their allegiance to the fallen kingdom of Rhudaur, and bring them to her.

'It has come to my attention that your studies of the mysteries of Middle-earth have progressed considerably, ${PLAYER}. For many long centuries, those of us here in Rivendell have had limited opportunities to explore the world beyond, and soon the time shall come for us to take our leave and sail into the West with our brethren.
'Even those of us who live lives without measure cannot hope to know all the mysteries of the world, but we hope to carry with us into the West as great a trove of knowledge and history as we may, and so if you could aid us in this endeavour, we would be most grateful.
'To this end, I would ask you to pen a scholar's writs for us, so that we might add them to our libraries and ensure that they will forever adorn the shelves of luminous Valinor.'

'Ah, you have penned a few scholar's writs. Very good! These are a few more slivers of knowledge that shall not be lost to us when we embark on our journey into the West.
'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. We shall not forget your efforts on our behalf.'

'It is true that there are far more pressing matters at hand in the world today, as dark shadows sweep across the land and threaten all, but no matter how great the darkness becomes, that knowledge we collect here shall escape into Uttermost West, where it shall be forever beyond the grasp of evil...so do not dismiss the importance of this task!'

'In times long past, we traded frequently with the Men of the kingdom that was once called Rhudaur, before they fell under the sway of Angmar and turned against their sister kingdoms of the North. As a result, one may occasionally stumble upon relics of Elf-make in the ruins of their kingdom, where the Hillmen and Angmarim now search to uncover such items and return them to their masters in Angmar. Likewise, the goblins of the Misty Mountains once stole such things as they could from us in their raids.
'We would not have items of such history and memory falling into the hands of our enemies. If you should find any during your battles with them, we will look most favourably upon you if you would return them to us here in Rivendell.'

'Ah, you have come upon a relic of our time of peace with the Men of Rhudaur, long ago.
'I wonder who the crafter is? I shall have to ask my kinsmen and see to whom I should return it, though I do not recognize the make -- it is quite possible its crafter has sailed into the West, as so many of our finest smiths and artisans have already done.'

'You have not come across any of the relics of our people in the hands of the Angmarim who scour the old ruins have you? Nor among the inhabitants of Goblin-town? It is of no matter if you have not, for they are quite uncommon, but keep a watchful eye out for them nonetheless.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. You have arrived at a difficult time...we have been stretched terribly thin by the incursions of the Angmarim into our lands and by the number of lawless brigands that have been stirred up by the gathering clouds of war.
'It is against the latter which I hope you can aid us. The bands of tomb-raiders have become so bold of late that they have taken to wearing sashes of allegiance to their various unsavoury leaders. I would have you bring me these sashes as proof of their defeat.

'So, ${PLAYER}, are you ready to face the Orcs in all their strength? Many have marched down now through the passes of the Ram Dúath, and their main encampent lies south-east of here in Dol Dínen, where they prepare to strike down into the heart of Eriador. We have not nearly the numbers needed to face them in force, but we sortie forth and skirmish against them daily in an effort to slow their advance and weaken them before the inevitable battles to follow.
'Those among the Orcs who have faced and survived battles are awarded battle-medallions. If we can defeat these veterans, the resolve of the greater force will be weakened, and there is some hope that they might be held at bay.
'Bring me Orc battle-medallions as proof of your strength and valour, and we shall support your efforts in any way we can.'
'Well done! You have fought long and hard against the Orcs of Dol Dínen. We thank you for your stalwart efforts and shall find some way to reward you as our meagre supplies allow.'
'You have been unable to gather many Orc battle-medallions? Alas, there is no shortage of Orcs to claim them from, if you can find the strength and courage to face them....'

'Are you not a tailor of some skill, ${PLAYER}? If so, we have a task in which you might aid us. For many ages, it has been our practice to send those of our kindred who are coming of age on pilgrimages to notable places of our forefathers. The war against Angmar has forced us to change this.
'Here in Esteldín, we give our youths special sashes to signify their coming of age, but supplies of fabric and those with the skill to craft any quantity of them have been short. Most cloth has gone for bandages.
'If you could weave a few of these sashes for us, we would be quite greatful.'

'You have brought more Rangers' sashes? Very good. We have a need, for we have a number of youths on the cusp of adulthood -- I only wish that more of them could survive their first battles with the Orcs....'
'Both time and materials are in short supply, but if you could find the resources to produce more Rangers' sashes, it would be quite helpful.'

'Greetings ${PLAYER}. I can offer only dire news it seems. The deep halls of Goblin-town, once thought nearly abandoned in the days after the Battle of Five Armies are once again teeming with goblins and their allies.
'Rumour has even reached us that a new king has risen to the throne of Goblin-town, and that Angmar seeks to bring him under their heel, to use as a weapon against us. Indeed, we fear that this may have already come to pass given the amount of activity our scouts report from the High Pass.
'We dare not show our strength in force yet and must settle for skirmishes and guile to keep the goblins from building their forces further. Bring me the tabards of the favoured servants of the new Great Goblin -- by whatever means you see fit -- and you shall gain further favour with Rivendell for your efforts upon our behalf.'
'Well done. You bring me evidence of disorder and mayhem sewn among the ranks of Goblin-town, and for now that shall suffice until the time comes when our strength may need to be revealed.'

'Our scouts tell me that the ranks and preparations of the hosts of Goblin-town continue to develop apace, ${PLAYER}. I beseech you to take what action you may to delay and hinder them, that we may forstall the time when they come upon us, or we are forced to raise our own hand and reveal what strength we have to the watchful eyes of Angmar.'

'Greetings ${PLAYER}. I have been very interested in the doings here at the hunting lodge. It seems the only place here in Bree where people would even think about heading up to the old Barrow-downs. Well, there I go talking before explaining. You see, I am quite interested in the place -- the Barrow-downs that is. Ancient cities, old kings, and treasure beyond imagining! My dad, Newbold, has told me such wonderful stories. It seems somehow he got quite a few pieces of old histories out of the Downs, though he never would tell me how.
'I have tasked every hunter who frequents this lodge to travel to the Barrow-downs and retrieve some of the Barrow-treasure, but it seems that none of them have the nerve. I keep asking Anglinn, but he never seems to leave eyeshot of the main gate, and those Rangers aren't ones to be pushed, if you get my meaning. Anglinn seems to believe that the treasure of Haudh Iarchith is some of the finest. He goes on and on about removing the treasure and breaking some curse laid on it...all a bunch of nonsense if you ask me.
'If you would travel to Haudh Iarchith and retrieve some of the old Barrow-treasures, you would be held in high regard, I'm sure.'

'You have done it! Look here, ${PLAYER} wasn't scared to go up into those old hills, ha!
'Don't mind the other hunters, they are all superstitious fools. They think the Barrow-downs are haunted, can you believe it!'
'You have returned without the Barrow-treasures? I had hoped you wouldn't be scared of some old bones in the hills....'

'If you would, return to Haudh Iarchith and collect a bit more of the barrow-treasure, another few would be wonderful. Anglinn seems to have some fancy for it, though I don't rightly know what he does with it.
'You have earned yourself quite a name around our fires, ${PLAYER}. You wouldn't want the other hunters to think you have gone soft now, would you?'

'I have heard your name whispered before in these streets. I know who you are, and I know your intentions, so I will not waste your time. you have perhaps heard of Black Riders who came through town, causing geese to scream and dogs to howl? Well, they are more than just Men in black cloaks, and they are a far greater danger than any of these simple folk know.
'The Riders have awoken something, something that should have remained sleeping. You have no doubt heard at least a part of the tale of the fall of Cardolan? It was a nation divided by war and decimated by Plague borne on winds out of Mordor, their remains inhabited with the servants of the Witch-king! The awakened spirits have heard their master's call once more, and I fear for the safety of Bree. I have been tasked to guard it at all costs.
'What I ask of you is to enter one of the barrows and put to rest the bones that still dwell within. Once the barrow housed a great ruler of Cardolan, now it is known as Haudh Iarchith, and Men shiver to hear its name whispered. Enter into Haudh Iarchith and put to rest those that wander its halls. Some of the wights might carry trinkets of Cardolan. Bring them to me as proof of your deeds, and you will earn great respect among the hunters of Bree who would not dare to enter those halls of madness.'
'I did not doubt that you would finish the task, ${PLAYER}. It is well that you have returned, however, for your strength will be needed sooner than you think.'
'You have not recovered any of the Cardolan trinkets?'
Bring the Cardolan trinket to Anglinn

'Welcome, traveller. I would ask what brings you to Bree, but so many strangers have been arriving from the south and east that it no longer matters what they come for.
'The Men of Bree are artful woodworkers. Our crafts are carried and traded across Eriador. Just last season I had word from a dwarf that he had received one of our wooden figurines as a gift from a travelling merchant.
'That got me to thinking; why not sell these figurines as a novelty for travelling merchants to bring back as petty gifts? The woodworkers of Bree are worked hard enough as it is without the extra burden that I would place upon them, but maybe you would be able to find more of the figurines? You would be doing a mighty service for the Men of Bree, ${PLAYER}.'
'You found more wooden figurines? I can tell that this was crafted with care ${PLAYER}, the woodworkers of Bree thank you.'
'I know an adventurer such as yourself must be very busy, but if you have the time would you bring me wooden figurines?'

'Have you stopped in the streets of Bree and listened, really listened, ${PLAYER}? The sound of a minstrel's instrument can usually be heard throughout Bree, though it is becoming rarer by the day.
'You see, the usual fair for the woodworkers of Bree besides hunting bows and farmcraft was wooden instruments. Clarinets, harps, and viols...ah, the beautiful viols! Those are one of the harder instruments that our woodworkers craft here in Bree. Well, what with all the commotion with the brigands hereabouts, the woodworkers have been hard-pressed by the demand for all manner of spears, bows, and staves, and they haven't the time to craft new viols!
'If you would, find five viol and return them here to me. It would be for the worst if the streets were left without music.'

'Ah, these are finely-crafted viols. Listen to the soft, sweet sound!
'You have done a great service to Bree, ${PLAYER}.'
'I fear that without new viols, the streets of Bree may become deprived of music sooner than you would think....'

'The woodworkers of Bree have been worked to the bone ever since those brigands starting stirring up trouble. You see, Chief Watcher Grimbriar has ordered all the woodworkers in Bree and the surrounding towns to craft Bree-spears to protect against any further attacks.
'Now, I am not one to disobey Chief Watcher Grimbriar's orders, but I simply won't take any new spears that aren't crafted from black ash. It has been getting harder and harder to find black ash, what with all the newcomers to Bree-land coming in and clearing the best trees to make new houses. Without black ash, I am afraid the spear-hafts won't be strong enough.
'If you are lucky enough to find any black ash, the Men of Bree would be in your debt if you were to bring us any Bree-spears for us to help defend against further attacks.'

'I tasked you with bringing be a Bree-spear, but I never expected you to actually finish the order so quickly! Let us see here...well balanced, sharp, and a haft crafted with black ash! This Bree-spear will be a strong weapon against the brigands.
'The woodworkers of Bree are honoured to have this weapon in our stores, ${PLAYER}.'
'Have you finished finding the Bree-spear yet? I see....'

'We must call our forces to service, ${PLAYER}. If we fail at this task, we will suffer an onslaught too quickly, and the keep will fall. We require your aid in calling our forces to the bridge to the west, and so I ask you to assist us.
'We must make banners to fly near the bridge to the west, but they must be made swiftly. We need hides from the beasts found throughout these lands. Wolves and drakes are those you should hunt, for their hides will make the strongest banners. You can also find suitable hides upon the aurochs.
'You will find wolves in great number throughout the woods and drakes are found to the north in Arador's End. Move quickly, friend.'
'You have done well, my friend. These will be woven into the banners we need to call our allies to the bridge. We will stand vigilant and win this day.'
'Without the hides, we cannot make the banners, and without the banners, the defenders will not come. We cannot risk over-exposing our forces here. Please hurry, the defenders must come to our aid.'

'We must make flags to fly near the bridge to the south, but they must be made swiftly. We need hides from the beasts found throughout these lands. Wolves and drakes are those you should hunt, for their hides will make the strongest banners. You may also find usable hides on the aurochs.
'You will find wolves in great number throughout the woods, and drakes are found to the north in Arador's End. Move quickly, friend.'
'You have done well, my friend. These will be woven into the banners we need to call our allies to the bridge. We will stand vigilant and win this day.'

'Without the hides, we cannot make the banners, and without the banners, the defenders will not come. We cannot risk over-exposing our forces here to attack. Please hurry. The defenders must come to our aid.'
