'It's a fitting honour to use the blades of the fallen to slay our enemies, and so we will do so. Go into the Ettenmoors and collect these broken blades, return them to me so I can begin outfitting our troops.'
'Aye, these will do nicely. I will set about crafting these sundered weapons into something more fitting to strike down the Enemy. You have well earned your thanks for this, ${PLAYER}.'
'The blades of our fallen brethren will be used to smite the Enemy who took them from us. Quickly now, let us arm our host as best we can.'

Captain-General Makan has ordered that archers be stationed behind the safety of the walls at the tunnel entrance of Tol Ascarnen, where they will unleash arrows at all who attempt to assault the keep.

'We need straight bits of wood to craft into arrow-shafts. Elves will be making their way here once we have enough arrows to support them. We need to hasten this task along, friend: Angmar will not rest. They will press us.
'Get the kindling we need from the wood you find laying about the Ettenmoors, I will wager there is more of it near the woods of Hithlad and the Grimwood lumber-camp. Be quick so that we can supply our forces.'
'Excellent work. I will set about crafting these arrows. Soon enough we will have the support of the Elves and be better able to fight off Angmar's assaults!'
'Be swift, for we need to call the archers to service soon, else we lose their firepower at the entrance and leave ourselves open to attack.'

'This is war, friend, and in war you make choices that you might regret when all is done. Yet, if we do not make these difficult decisions, then there may be no tomorrow for regret. It is a terrible and confusing situation sometimes, but I follow my orders, and they are clear.
'I am to charge you with collecting iron ore from the Isendeep or those wretched goblins which make Grothum their home. Either way, the iron is to be used to craft a giant cauldron. We will fill the cauldron with oil and boil it to douse Angmar's forces when they assail the fortress.
'A terrible fate for certain, but no different than they shall do to us. The ore can be found in the Isendeep Mine to the north or from the goblins of Grothum in the north-east. Go quickly, friend, for we must prepare our defence.'
'This ore will do nicely, ${PLAYER}. With enough of this, I will forge a sturdy iron cauldron, which we can use to douse our enemies.'
'Move with haste. We need to get these defences into place before Angmar's forces return.'

'Hunt the Orcs and Uruks throughout the Ettenmoors and gather barrels of oil. Bring it to me, so that we can boil it for use in the cauldron. Go quickly.'
'Excellent work, friend. This will serve us well. We shall get about the forging of the cauldron as soon as we have all the materials we need. Then we shall prepare for the Enemy.'
'We need the oil to boil for a long time. It will drive the Orcs away from the walls and keep our forces safe for a time. Be quick about your task.'

'${RACE}, we have a mission of great importance for you to undertake. Provisions are low, as you likely are aware, and the Captain-General has ordered that we craft a horn to call resting troops to service. We shall do this, but we need your help, for we must hold these posts at all cost.
'What I must say next troubles me, but these are desperate times, and we must make due with what we can.
'North of here, in the place called Arador's End, you will find drakes. These creatures have very strong sinew that ties their bones and muscles together. I ask that you collect sinew from these beasts so we can make straps to bind the Horn of Tol Ascarnen. Do not travel alone and be careful not to damage the sinew.'
'You have done well. I will set others to the task of cleaning these straps so that we might yet make the Horn of Tol Ascarnen.'
'We have not time to waste, ${PLAYER}. Make your way north with your allies and collect sinew from the drakes. We must be vigilant for renewed assaults from Angmar's army.'

'While I do not condone the slaughtering of wild animals without purpose, we have a need for this culling. Rockwithers' horns will serve as the centre of a great battle-horn which we shall use to alert our forces when Angmar's host attacks. 'Excellent work, ${PLAYER}. I will set about fashioning this into a proper battle-horn. After we have collected the sinew and craft the stand, we will raise the Horn of Tol Ascarnen and prepare for Angmar's assault.

'This aggression will not stand, ${PLAYER}. Angmar has forces all over the Ettenmoors, and Tol Ascarnen is a symbol of hope to us all. I will not stand idly by and allow the forces of the Enemy to hold Tol Ascarnen.
'Nor am I fool enough to assail the keep alone, but with a force of the Free Peoples, I shall stand beside you and storm the walls, taking them for our own once more.
'Prove your valour, ${PLAYER}, in the form of the tokens we bestow at Glân Vraig and bring them to me. Should you give me enough, I will know you are a righteous ${RACE} and stand beside you as we storm the walls of Tol Ascarnen.'

'This proves to me that you are a warrior devoted to our cause. Come then, let us steel our nerves and sharpen our blades. The Enemy is many and entrenched in that holding, but we have hope and strength to spare.
'The time has come! Baruk Khazâd!'
'I'll not risk an assault until you prove to me that you will stand by my side. Bring me tokens of valour, and I shall be true to my word.'

'I've orders from the Captain-General that need following, friend. You look the type of ${RACE} that knows well how to follow them, so I find myself here asking you to undertake a simple, though possibily dangerous task that needs doing and quickly.
'To the north, at the foot of the great Misty Mountains, in the place called Arador's End, is the Isendeep. A great vein of ore runs through that place, and it is this iron we need now.
'Get the iron from the Isendeep and bring it to me, so that I may craft the cauldron to strengthen our walls. If you find no ore there or the mine is held by the Enemy, then take the fight to Grothum and slaughter the goblins who would mine there.'

'This iron would better serve us as axes, hammers, and swords in less dire times. But as we stand here now, it seems the best course of action to make the cauldron to scorch our enemies and drive them off. You are to be thanked for these efforts.'

'The iron can be found in the Isendeep or carried by the goblins in Grothum. I would prefer that you slaughter the goblins, as they are terrible pests, but the swiftest method is the best at this time, friend.'

'Why hello again. I was beginning to think you wouldn't come back after you brought me that nice present. I thought maybe you were taken by one of those terrible wolves.
'Time was when we didn't have to worry about wolves. There were so few and the farmer would always drive them off when they did try to sneak into the coop.
'But more and more of us have been disappearing lately; I think that it may be wolf-mischief. We need a brave rooster such as yourself to go warn the other coops and find out exactly what is going on! There are coops at Brownlocks' Farm to the east and slightly north on the road to Needlehole, Cotton's Farm to the east in Bywater, and Bamfurlong far to the east and south along the river.'

'Wolves? Of course, I have seen the wolves! Have you looked around? Almost our entire coop has been taken!
'There have been some folk carrying off the survivors down to Waymeet, though.'

'What is that now? Wolves, no, of course not, not here in the Shire. I have heard rumours of them, yes, but they are just that, rumours.
'Chickens get to talking, you know, and can come up with wild, fanciful stories. The only Wolf on this farm is a dog! Of course, the farmer's dogs may be why we have no wolves. They are good protectors.'

'Wolves here, in the Shire? Wolves have not dared to venture in so far since the old times, or so legends tell.
'I don't rightly know what we could do about such an attack. If there is anything that we can do here, let us know. Give my regards to Billina.'

'Hullo there! I have gotten myself into a heap of trouble; do you think you can help me? I snuck in and took a basket of eggs when dad wasn't looking...he is very particular about his prized hens and doesn't let me tend them. I just wanted a snack by the river with my friends is all.
'Well, after I snuck out the eggs I realized that they had chicks in them! Dad has been trying to get his prized hens to lay eggs for longer than I can remember; it must be the new rooster he got from Budgeford. I can't go back and return the eggs, but maybe you can! Dad hurt his leg and has so many travellers running about fetching eggs, you would be able to sneak in and replace the ones I took.
'I got so flustered trying to get away with the eggs that I forgot which hen I took them from. I put the eggs in the basket in the order I took them, so all you need to do is figure out what order the hens lay them in.
'I was able to sneak out a page from my dad's journal -- he can write you know, taught me all my letters -- though I can't make out up from down with his notes. Maybe you will have more luck?
'Be careful placing the eggs back in the nests...those hens know what eggs are their own and will roll out any that aren't theirs, then you'll have to start over.'
'You got all the eggs matched up with their hens? I can't thank you enough, ${PLAYER}!'
'Were you able to get all the eggs back in the nests? I would hate for the chicks not to hatch. Remember to look at my dad's notes if you're having trouble.'

Having replaced all the eggs, you should return and speak with Wald Sandson.
'Im a pig, you fool rooster! Can't you see I'm in enough trouble as it is, what with all these nasty shrews about? Sometimes I wish that I was a pony.'

'What do you want? Protect your coop against wolves? I have my own farm to protect and no time for others.
'My but you would make a nice snack. Be on your way, rooster.'
'Shooing off a few wolves is mighty tempting, but I've too much work to do here. Besides, what if the wolves come here?'

'Ho there, rooster! You aren't one of ours! What are you doing here? Trying to steal some of our hens for your coop?
'Wolves? We haven't any wolves around here, but if they show their shaggy faces at Bamfurlong, you can be sure we'll deal with them.'

'I thank you for your bravery, my fellow rooster, but I fear that it may not have been enough to save many of us from a terrible fate. While you were away, I had time to think over the circumstances and consider our options. If we do nothing, our numbers will surely dwindle. A similar doom befell Dora Brownlock's coop, and I fear ours is not far off.
'I cannot leave the coop; I have too many responsibilities with half of the coop under my supervision. I will set this task upon you: travel out into the world, even beyond the borders of the Shire. Speak with other animals you encounter and see if you can find anyone willing to help us in our plight.
'You should begin by seeking out animals here in the Shire.'

'Now what is this? First three hobbits sleeping in the forest, and now a chicken?
'You want me to help protect your coop from wolves? My friend, I would sooner eat you, particularly since chicken is very high among my dietary choices.
'However, seeing as you were brave enough to speak with me in the first place, I will forego my lunch for now.'

'Angmar has got hold of the mine, and we need to get back in there. There are not enough forces to call from the south to storm such a large place, but all may not be lost yet.
'Our enemy here has enemies, and if we are smart about how we handle this, we might yet turn the enemy of our enemy into an ally, at least for a moment.
'I'm talking about the drakes that make the mine and the surrounding areas their home. We might get them to fight against the Orcs if we can draw their attention to them. To do that we need to get some meat...Thistledown haunches ought to do, ${CLASS}. Collect some and bring them back to me.'

'These will do very nicely. Now you must make your way into the mine and find the flat stone near the War-tyrant watching over the mine. Place the haunches on this stone, and I'll bet the smell draws the drakes to the location.'
'Get those haunches, and I'll tell you the rest of my plan.'

'Our lumberyard is overrun by those pesky beasts from the north. I think I know a way that we can weaken them but it is a bit dangerous.
'The wolves prowling the dark places of these lands are enemies to everything and everyone, we may be able to use them as a distraction to better enable you and your number to defeat the enemy at the lumber yard.
'To do this we need to get the wolves good and angry and then get them to recognize that the lumber yard is the source of their woes. I think if you get their talons and put them on one of the stumps near the lumber yard that you can get a pack to attack the lumber yard. That is...if you are willing to.
'You should find the wolves scattered throughout these lands, some in the woods to the east and other across the river and up the hills to the west.'

'Yes, these should get those wolves riled for certain. Now we just need you to get them to a proper place. Look for the flat-top stump at the outskirts of the lumber yard on the side nearest the river.'
'Hurry along and get those talons. They might just do the trick.'
Deliver the talons to Emerald Twospade at Hoarhallow
Place the talons on the stump
Wolves of the Grimwood

Emerald Twospade hopes to score two strikes at once against the enemies of Hoarhallow. The wolves scattered throughout the Ettenmoors have no respect for life in any form. She hopes that you can raise their ire enough and leave a trail that leads to the Grimwood to fight against the orcs who now hold the lumber yard as their own.
'Quickly now, take those talons to the lumber camp and place them on the flat-top stump. The scent alone should draw the wolves to combat.'

Scattered throughout the Ettenmoors are locations prowled by the Darktide wolves. Seek out these wolves and kill them for their talons. Return to Emerald Twospade at Hoarhallow when you have collected ten of the talons.
Emerald Twospade believes that the Darktide wolves can be coaxed into attacking the forces of Angmar camped at the Grimwood Lumber Camp.

Make your way to the Grimwood Lumber camp and place the wolf-talons on the flat-top stump. This should draw the wolves to the camp to fight against Angmar's forces.
Emerald Twospade directed you to find the flat-top stump on the outskirts of the Grimwood Lumber Camp. She hopes that placing the talons on the stump will draw Darktide wolves to attack the forces at the camp.

'Troubling news comes from our agents within the ruined city of Annúminas. The Angmarim have moved forces within the walls in large numbers. Rumour has it that many of those within serve under the banner of a Black Númenórean sent from Mordor itself, wearing black badges of allegiance to the Dark Lord.
'If you can infiltrate the city, defeat those who defile its streets, and return their black badges to me, you shall earn much praise among the Wardens of Annúminas!'

'You are indeed a courageous adventurer to have braved the ruined streets of the Annúminas. I commend you for your courage, though we have many battles left to fight before we can wrest the city from their grasp.'

'I understand that to brave the streets of Annúminas against the invaders is not for the faint of heart, but I have not judged you to be of that sort. I have faith that your strength will be proven against our enemies in time.'

'Should you find yourselves battling those trespassers who have infiltrated the ruins of Annúminas, look you well for those who wear a band in the form of the ancient symbol of Númenor. These Black Númenóreans and their Angmarim allies are the favoured servants of Mordor, which has had a hand in all our woes of late -- even so far north as Evendim.
'Should you defeat such an opponent, bring the band to me as recognition of your deed and of the downfall of one of our most despised enemies!'

'Ah, it would seem that you have come across one of the favoured sons of Mordor -- and a betrayer of our ancient kingdom.

'You have had no fortune in finding one of the bands I mentioned?

'Well met in dark times, ${PLAYER}. It is possible that as you wage war against the Enemy, you will on rare occasion come across an Orc who wields a War-master's Lash -- these lashes are dispensed as marks of high favour by their masters in the black city of Carn Dûm, and the defeat of such an opponent is a victory against their evil schemes.
'Bring any such lashes you find to me, and the Rangers of Esteldín will acknowledge themselves in your debt for such deeds of honour.'

'Ah, you bring me a War-master's Lash, do you? So falls one more dark servant who would have brought great evil into the lands of Men. Your praises shall be marked highly among the Rangers of Esteldín for this act!'
'You have not yet come across one of the favoured servants of the Enemy? Such acknowledgements are rare, but they do walk among Angmar's army -- somewhere.'

'Are you not a tailor of some skill, ${PLAYER}? If so, we have a task in which you might aid us. In the past, my kindred have sent our youths coming of age on pilgrimages to notable places of our forefathers, but war has forced a change in this.
'To help identify these youths, we provide them with Ranger's Sashes that signify their coming into adulthood -- but supplies of fabric and those with the skill to craft them in any quantity have been short. Most cloth has gone for bandages.
'If you could craft a few of these sashes for us, we would be quite greatful.'
'You have brought more Rangers' sashes? Very good. We have need, for we have many youths coming into their own -- I only wish that more of them could survive their first battles with the Orcs....'
'Both time and materials are in short supply, but if you could find the resources to produce more Rangers' sashes, it would be quite helpful.'

'A fine day to you during dark times, ${PLAYER}.

'If you could craft a few Rangers' cloaks for me, I and my kindred would be much obliged!'

'There we are, cloaks fit for men who must travel far and fast.
'My thanks to you, for every bit helps during this time of hardship.'

'The Men of the North have long come to know the Rangers as folk of dangerous mystery -- how are we supposed to impress anyone wearing shoddy, worn cloaks with tatters and holes in them?

'I have a matter of sombre import, ${PLAYER}. Many of our bravest fellows have fallen in battle against the Orcs who stream down through the passes from the North, and we would honour their deeds both for their sake, and for the morale of those who must inevitably take up their standard and march forth to die in their stead.
'Your skill is such that I would ask you to weave a tapestry of the deeds of our heroes to exemplify the life and death of those who fight under the banner of Esteldín, that they might be remembered in more peaceful ages to come.'

'This tapestry, finely woven and glorious in its tales of valour, shall serve our purposes well! Would that I might some day stand beside those brave spirits whose tales are chronicled herein.

'So many have fallen with their tales and songs known only to a few. Could you see it in your heart to craft a tapestry to record their lives and deeds for those who follow?'

'Mordirith the coward has escaped us...but did you notice that the blade of Dúnachar was still lodged within his breast? I wager the pain of that blade's light shall be a constant reminder of the evil he has committed.
'While my revenge is not yet complete, I would wager there will be others who will complete this task. For now, I can take solace in this fact...
'A moment, someone approaches!'

'What an unsettling end to our battle. I fear that there is much more to that old woman than what we see upon the surface.
'However, we cannot deal with that matter now. We should leave here before we are overrun with Angmarim or their servants!'
'We should tarry here no longer. Are you prepared to leave? I will show you the secret ways out of Carn Dûm and back to Gath Forthnír.'

'It seems my long imprisonment in Carn Dûm has served us well. We have come far into the the Witch-king's keep unnoticed. It would be folly to think, though, that our fortune will hold. Already, Mordirith may be aware of our presence.
'Steel yourself for the battle ahead. I have few words of advice to offer you, other than to warn you that Mordirith is a master of trickery and illusion. He will try to break your resolve with his words. Do not let him! Keep to your hope and trust your companions.
'Shall we go now?'

'Hullo there, my young ${RACE}, have you come to learn about the Mathom Society? I know quite a bit, as I have been a member for over four years now! Come closer...my eyesight is not as good as it once was; I turn one hundred this year, you know.
'Five years ago, a group of hobbits began to take a close interest in the Mathom House and the recovery of mathoms across the Shire. We have the most splendid meetings and discuss all sorts of things: where we would be likely to find mathoms, who holds private collections of mathoms we could borrow from, or even what differentiates a mathom from a non-mathom! Most of the meetings occur over dinner, and we have begun to get quite a turnout. Why, just last week Baldwin Foxtail proposed to add to the main floor to increase the number we could fit at the table. Who would have thought so many hobbits were interested in history?
'Though we have some wonderful plans, we have not actually begun the process of going out and collecting the mathoms. That is where youngsters such as yourself come in! If you happen across any mathoms in your travels be sure to bring them back here so they can be organized and catalogued. It would be a pity to lose any more mathoms. A good deal of our collection has been diminished ever since old Bilbo took some of our most interesting pieces with him when he went and got himself killed, or lost...you know, I don't rightly remember what happened to the old fool now that I think about it....'

'You have returned with some mathoms? Oh, Brombard will be overjoyed! I will put these down into storage right away. If they ever get put on display, I will make sure your name is added to the plaque that accompanies them.'
'Are those mathoms you have there? Oh, they aren't? I knew that, of course. I was only joking with you....'

'We have been busy as bees these last few days organizing the Mathom Society members and finding storage for all the new mathoms that have been pouring in. Soon enough, we may be forced to use the old storage tunnels. We have never had this much activity before, and I think it is too much for some of the younger hobbits. I overheard some grumblings from young Baldwin outside over finding a honey-roasted chicken for the next Mathom Society meeting when he should have been labeling mathoms! Some of these young hobbits seem more interested in the meeting dinner-menu than the wonderful new mathoms.
'Anyhow, we have found that many of the mathoms are not in very good condition. I don't know what has happened to many of them -- to tell the truth I don't know what most of them do or did! What I do know is that they are not of display quality. What would we have to show of all our hard work if we have no display pieces?
'If you come across any well-kept mathoms, be sure to take extra care when delivering them to us. The more intact they are, the better. And do try to at least wipe them clean before you drop them off...some of them have had some very queer things on them.'
'A well-kept mathom! I will get it to the Master Chef right away; he is so good at cataloguing the smaller mathoms, you know.'

'Hullo there, my name is Baldwin Foxtail son of Brombard Foxtail...he's the keeper of the Mathom House, you know. I am one of the more important members of the Mathom Society; I am in charge of overseeing the collection of the delectable menu items for our extravagant Mathom Society dinners, as well as the labeling and cleaning of several of the more significant sections of the Mathom House storage collection.
'We have run into a bit of trouble, what with all the adventurers coming in with new mathoms, I have never seen so many in all my life! Old Greylond seems to fix all of us to get the mathoms sorted and organized before he thinks about the dinner menu, quite silly if you ask me.
'Our Master Chef has been locked up in the cellar of the Mathom House for so long now that I am worried he may have forgotten how to cook! I am worried even more that he will not have time to cook up his specialty, seasoned beef with cauliflower, in time for our next Mathom Society dinner.
'We can't hold the dinner without something to serve, do you think you would be able to find us some seasoned beef with cauliflower? You would be doing the Mathom Society quite a service.'
'You found us some seasoned beef with cauliflower? You have saved me! I can not thank you enough, ${PLAYER}.'

'Ahoy there! I am Argirion, First Mate aboard the Gilminuial -- or at least I was until we were beset by a great storm! The Gilminuial is a ship belonging to we Rangers that sails up and down the Baranduin providing much-needed supplies to the Wardens of Annúminas in the North.
'That work, though, was brought to an end with the storm. Our ship was grounded, the quartermaster and I were washed overboard, and our cargo lost. I know not if anyone else survived the disaster and would be pleased if you could search northward for the Captain.
'It is also vital that the cargo be recovered, for it was intended to supply the Wardens as they fight the evil that has come to Annúminas.'

'Ah! You have come from Argirion? He and Mindambeth are well? That is good.
'You may return to Argirion and let him know that all survived the wreck and are now repairing the damage. Do as Argirion requested and gather the cargo before you return, however...it is vital for the defence of Annúminas.'

'It is good to know that my kinsmen did not perish in the storm.
'Thank you as well for recovering this cargo. Bring it to Mindambeth, as well as any more you may find as you journey along the Baranduin.
'As thanks for your efforts, you may choose something from the ship's stores that have survived. Mindambeth will see to your reward.'
'Have you found some of the lost ale and cram? The Wardens will need both if they are to continue to keep Annúminas from falling completely to the Iron Crown!'

'Apparently everything that you have done out here has not gone unnoticed. Despite protests against offering you more rewards, the First Marshals have issued a writ saying that I must offer rewards to those who have proven worthy of the honour.
'Now this brings us to the question that is burning in that primitive little brain of yours: 'How do I prove my worth?' Simple answer for a simpleton; bring me tokens of valour and it will do much towards proving your worth.'

'You got them all, excellent work. This key opens the First Marshal chests behind me. I know what you're thinking.
'What am I supposed to do -- open one chest, open all chests, or what?
'I can solve this for you simply. The key will only open one chest. You want to open more, you need more keys. You want more keys -- you go through me. You got that?
'All right. These are treasures found while we fight this war. Do yourself a favour and don't ask from where they came.'

'Valourous or not Valourous -- doesn't matter. I'm the one with the keys.
'Until you prove to me that you're something more than another would-be warrior who stands about asking: How will we stop this army of Angmar at our walls? How will we fight that?
'Get out there and earn some Tokens of Valour.'
Deliver the Tokens of Valour to Quartermaster Ash

Having assisted the Free Peoples in their battle against the war host of Angmar, you have earned much respect. First Marshals throughout the Ettenmoors authorised the rewards from Quartermaster Ash at Glân Vraig.

'You work your entire life to stand against evil and spit long and hard in its face and you get stationed here handing out free items to folk like you. There was a time when I was the finest solider in all of Eriador, but now I push quill over parchment, and count the number of keys on a ring or tokens in hand.
'Let's get on with it then. Seems you made a name for yourself out there in the wild, and the Second Marshals tell me that you are owed favour and reward. Good news for you, nothing but a pain in my nethers.
'Here is what we do from now on. You show me that you have been a good little warrior by handing over the tokens of valour you collect. I hand you keys in exchange. It is simple enough for even your primitive brain to understand, I think.'

'You got them all, excellent work. This key opens the Second Marshal chests behind me. I know what you're thinking.

'Welcome warrior. This is your opportunity to prove your prowess on the field of battle. If you choose to, you may speak with me again to enter mortal battle with an opponent of great power and strength.
'You will take on the role of a ranger of Esteldín a noble Man who fights to defend and keep safe the sanctity of Middle-earth. Your opponent will be a terrible troll out of Angmar.

'Congratulations, you are victorious!'
Speak with the ranger to enter mortal battle as a ranger

'Ah, then you are prepared to take on the role of noble Man. Very well.'
Speak again to the ranger within this room and choose to enter battle as a noble ranger out of Esteldín.
Speak with the ranger to complete the quest.

'Welcome warrior. This is your opportunity to prove your prowess on the field of battle. If you choose to, you may speak with me again to enter mortal battle with an opponent of great power and strength.

'Speak with me again to launch your troll session.'
'Congratulations, you are victorious!'

'Meow! Hello, I'm Tens! Although I type slowly, due to my furry paws, I can help you complete the Epic quest series. If you complete this quest, you'll be flagged as having completed Book I of the Epic series.
'Alright, when you complete this quest you'll be flagged as having completed Book I of the Epic. Have fun!'
Level Up: Book I
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book I of the Epic quest series.
'Meow! Back so soon? Well I can complete Book II of the Epic quest series now for you, if you'd like. Just speak to me again.
'Alright, when you complete this quest you'll be flagged as having completed Book II of the Epic. Have fun!'
Level Up: Book II
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book II of the Epic quest series.
'Meow! Back so soon? Well now you are up to Book III of the Epic quest series. Want me to complete that now for you? Just speak to me again and I'll flag you appropriately.
'Since you asked so nicely, when you complete this quest you'll be flagged as having completed Book III of the Epic. Have fun and be careful out there!'
Level Up: Book III
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book III of the Epic quest series.

'Meow! Are you already up to Book IV of the Epic quest series? Goodness, so many good quests and adventures. I wish my furry paws let me make content as exciting as that, but I'm just a humble, slow typing cat.
Oh well, at least I can help you! Just speak to me again.
'When this quest is completed, you'll be flagged as having completed Book IV of the Epic. Enjoy!'
Level Up: Book IV
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book IV of the Epic quest series.

'Meow! Goodness, you are up to Book V of the Epic quest series. That is a very good series of quests, if you ask me. All those bits with Skorgrím and the Dourhands, and then you end with a Dragon. Terribly exciting!
Oh well, you'll be able to skip all that once you complete this quest.
'Here we go! When you complete this quest you'll be flagged as having completed Book V of the Epic.'
Level Up: Book V
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book V of the Epic quest series.

'Meow! Well, well, you are up to Book 6 of the Epic quest series. I wonder, are you getting tired of speaking to me yet? No? Well good! Because there so much left to the Epic quest after this book.
But that's for later. For now, if you want to complete Book 6 of the Epic quest, you'll be all set once you complete this quest.
'Well, you know how this works by now. Complete this quest and you'll have Book VI of the Epic quest completed.'
Level Up: Book VI
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book VI of the Epic quest series.

'Meow! I just realized, you are talking to me. I'm a cat! How is that possible? That's just strange... Oh well, would you like to be flagged as having completed Book VII of the Epic quest series? If so, speak to me again!

Level Up: Book VII
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book VII of the Epic quest series.

'Meow! You know sometimes I dream that I'm something called a \qSystems Designer\q and that I make jokes about Sauron destroying things. Isn't that strange?

Level Up: Book VIII
Completion of this quest will flag your character has having completed all the quests in Book VIII of the Epic quest series.

'Meow! Oh, you are up to Book IX. This was where you learned that the dottering old fool Sara Oakheart was really Amarthiel in disguise. Very exciting!
But none of that for you! You'll be flagged as having completed Book IX if you speak to me again.

'Completion of Book IX coming up!
Oh, and if I were you, I would hold on to something... you are in for a bit of a bumpy ride....'
Level Up: Book IX

'Meow! Welcome back. I think that last quest took a lot out of you, but you don't look too worse for the wear. Too bad the same can't be said for your equipment!
Anyway, it looks like you want to complete Book X now. That whole business with Mordrambor is interesting, isn't it? Well, I thought so at least, you'll be skipping over all that, so you won't get a chance to read it.
'Book X completion coming right up!'
Level Up: Book X

The haunches are placed, the drakes are sure to come. You best hide, worm.
Collect Thistledown Haunch (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
You fool! Calling the beasts now would bring them against our forces!

'Being sent here to Grothum was bad enough, now I have to deal with these fool târks and dwarfs stalking the mines. I'll not have this, maggot!
'We know them drakes stalk the mines and it is time that we use their strength against our foes! We need to call them to action and get them to fight their leaders!.
'Very near where their leader stands is a nice, flat rock just waiting for slabs of meat to be tossed atop it to get those drakes running. Get some Thistledown haunces and toss them on the slab. That ought to get the drake's attention. Then we'll see how strong these wretches truly are!'
Place the Thistledown haunches on the flat stone in the Isendeep
Collect Thistledown Haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Angmar must not control the mine
Call the Beasts!
Drakes stalk the mines and are a foe that often destroys the orcs and trolls within the mines. It is time to turn that power against the Free People.

Search the areas south of Tol Ascarnen or west along the plains south and west of Dar-gazag for the Thistledown Grazers. Collect some of their haunces and bring them to the slab within the depths of the Isendeep.
Soldier Golb directed you to turn the force of drakes often found stalking the Isendeep Mines against the Free People. He wants you to draw the drakes in with the promise of aurochs meat.
The haunches are placed, the drakes are sure to come. You should hide.
Collect Thistledown Haunch (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
The Free People control the mine, there is no reason to bring the beasts to bear.

'The mines are fallen to Angmar again and I will not stand for it, ${PLAYER}. We must get the mine back.
'I suggest that we use the drakes stalking the depths as cover for our attack. Search the lands south of Tol Ascarnen or west and south on the plains of the Steps of Gram for the Thistledown grazers. Collect haunches from those beasts and deliver them to a flat stone near where the Tyrant holding the mine keeps his company.
'The blood from the haunches should draw the drakes within range of the foe and bring about the battle needed to bring these foes down!'
Place the Thistledown haunches on the flat stone in the Isendeep
Collect Thistledown Haunches (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Free People must not control the Mine
Bringing Beasts to Bear

Angmar once again holds the Isendeep Mine and Sergeant-at-Arms Thorfinn believes that the time has come to purge them from the depths to take the mine back for the Free People. He suggests a drastic measure to do so in an effort to defeat the foe.

Search the areas south of Tol Ascarnen or west along the plains, south of Dâr-gazag for the Thistledown Grazers. Collect some of their haunches and bring them to the slab within the depths of the Isendeep.
Sergeant-at-Arms Thorfinn believes that the drakes can be used agains the orcs of Angmar and wishes to use them as a diversion while you attack the Tyrant.
Obtained a Leafcull Heart

'Listen.
'We lose Grimwood.
'Take it back. Get help. Trees have hearts. Get hearts. Put hearts on stump near Grimwood. Call Trees.
'Trees stomp târks good.
'Go now and get hearts to make trees angry!'
Place the heartwood on the stump
Obtain a Leafcull heart
Huorns of the Grimwood

To retake the Grimwood the forces of Angmar will need to be vigilant and assisted, so thinks Taskmaster Gazgortag. He thinks that the living trees near the lumber camp will come and fight for the forces of Angmar and sets you to the task of calling them to the fight.

Seek a Leafcull huorn within the southern stretches of the Grimwood. Cut out its heart and place it on the stump near the Grimwood Lumber Camp.
Taskmaster Gazgortag believes that you can draw the huorns into conflict with the Free People currently occupying the Grimwood Lumber Camp. He directed you to cut out the heart of the leafcull Huorn in attempt to draw out the enemy.
Caragdal has arrived and now calls the weavers to her

'To the west, in a tower draped in the webs of their mistress lay a great spider. She will come to us and oversee the collection of wood through her minions if we beseech her aid.
'Go there now maggot and speak with her. Bid her draw the spiders from the tower to the woods surrounding this camp.
'Be quick!'
'Be swift. I will not suffer the slings and stones of those accursed little folk.'
Escort Caragdal to the Grimwood Lumber Camp
Spider Harvesters

The Grimwood is secured for Angmar's purposes. To ensure that it remains this way, we must grow our forces and support.
You must draw the web-weavers from the nearby tower to come to Angmar's aid at the Grimwood Lumber Camp.
Lead Caragdal from the tower to the Grimwood camp to enlist the aid of the spiders of Gorogris' brood.
Mudhun has arrived safely within the mine

'Frightened are we who would work in those mine. Pitiful worms we are, afraid of the drakes and the cave-claw. More afraid of the Free People.
'You will watch over us as we walk to the mine, yes?
'If you do this we know you will protect us inside the mine. Lead me, please.'
'I will follow quickly. Come, come let us go.'
Talk to Mudhun
Mine the Deep

Controlling the Isendeep mine means that the goblins can get back to work. The mining leader Mudhun is loathe to lead his fellows into the depths without some support. It falls to you to lead this frightened wretch into the Isendeep. Pathetic.

Escort the goblin mining leader Mudhun from the base of Grothum into the mine. He said this would give him proof that you are willing to defend him and the other miners.
Mudhun is a pathetic excuse for a minion of Lugbûrz, but still his miners will prove an asset within the mines. Escort him to the Isendeep.

'Greetings, my little rooster-friend! What is this? Your coops are threatened by wolves?
'Wolves are among the most craven of the Dark Lord's servants, and this proves them even more so. Unfortunately, the troubles here are much greater, with effects more far-reaching, than those which trouble the Shire.
'I am sorry, but I cannot leave the Eglain just yet.'

'Oh, please! My dear rooster, we have much more important things to do, such as napping. Besides, we must keep our mistress's house clear of mice and rats. We haven't time to run all the way to the Shire!'

'Who art thou, rooster? I am a noble steed of Rohan. Thy troubles are beneath my hooves.
'Even were I of a mind to lend thee aid, I have not long been in this place and know not of this land called the Shire. Begone, bird, for I have naught to do with thee.'

'Wolves? Ha! We fear no wolves! They will not withstand our onslaught. They will be the next to fall!
'After we destroy the helpless red squirrels, we shall conquer the wolves, and then the world! No one can stop us!'

'Oh dear! I found such lovely grass here, but I can't seem to find my way back off the roof of this hobbit-hole. Do you see a path?
'My dear rooster, how can I help you when I am stuck here? If I could find a way down, I might speak with my bull...wolves are too vicious for me.'

'I am trapped in a cage out in the middle of the Midgewater Marshes, and you want me to help you? I think you have it backwards, rooster. I am the one in need of help.
'This Man here is more than a bit mad! If he throws any more of those dreadful dead midges in this cage, I think my carapace is going to split!'

'I have heard rumour that a hidden camp exists near unto the very gates of Carn Dûm in the far north where brave heroes gather to contest the power of Angmar itself.
'I cannot say precisely where Gath Forthnír - as it is called - lies, but should you find this place, speak with one called Annábla, and she will tell you more of their purpose.'

'You have been sent by Arohir, yes? It speaks highly to his confidence in you that he would tell you of our existance at all - and so I have high hopes that you may indeed be able to help us in our desperate cause.'
The Council of the North
Arohir of Esteldin has bade you seek the hidden camp of Gath Forthnír in the far north, somewhere east of the gates of Carn Dûm, and once there to speak with Annábla.
Speak with Annábla of Gath Forthnír.

'Have you heard of the Wardens of Annúminas? They are a branch of our order who guard the ancient tombs and ruins which mark the long-ago abandoned capital of Arnor.
'News has come to me that they stand hard-pressed, as bandits and refugees from the North-downs have begun to loot the old tombs in increasing numbers, and darker rumours of the presence of Angmarim agents who seek entrance into the ancient city itself.
'Travel to the camp of Tinnudir and you will find Cannuion, who will be most greatful for any aid you can render.'

'You have been sent by Arohir? Good, we have great need of trustworthy warriors to help us against the growing threat of robbers and the like that have grown up in recent months here - for we are few, and it threatens to overwhelm us.'
The Wardens of Annúminas
Arohir of Esteldin has bade you seek the camp of Tinnudir along the eastern shore of Lake Evendim, and once there to speak with Cannuion.

Cannuion is at the Ranger-camp at Tinnudir, in Evendim, to the west of the North Downs.
Arohir has sent you to speak with Cannuion in Evendim.

'Have you yet been to the encampment of our brothers in the North-downs? Once fair Esteldin still serves us honourably even now as a base for our Rangers to train and prepare as the forces of Angmar pour down from the northern wastes.
'Not that we don't need your help here, but you may wish to speak with Nethúr in Esteldin - I've heard that matters there have become quite dire as the Orcs encamp in ever greater numbers and threaten to overwhelm our people.'

'Calenglad sent you? Hah, and here I thought they might need your help even more than we - but it is true that matters here are not to my liking, for the Orcs outnumber our forces greatly, and it is only a matter of time before the last bastions of the North come under attack.'
The Rangers of Esteldin
Calenglad of Tinnundir has bade you speak with Nethúr of Esteldin in the North-downs concerning the Rangers of Esteldin and the orcish forces pouring down from Angmar.
Speak with Nethúr of Esteldin.

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}, have you travelled to fair Rivendell? I have had business there on occasion in the past, but lately a friend of mine by the name of Imyl sent warning to me that I should no longer travel through the Trollshaws, for fear that I should fall victim to bands of roving hill-men who have come down from the north in the last year or so.
'I count myself a friend of the fair Elves of Rivendell, and if matters have come to this, I fear that they may be in some peril. Should you find your way to Rivendell, seek out Imyl of the Last Homely House, and aid her, if you may. I would be most greatful.'

'Naerandir sent you here? To aid us?
'What a dear, foolish man he is. I doubt there is much that you can do to aid us, for our borders are tested by the shadow at every turn. However, if you are determined to lend us aid, then I will gratefully accept your help.'
The Elves of Rivendell
Naerandir, a scholar of Bree-town has bade you seek out Imyl in the Last Homely House of Rivendell, and offer aid to her if you may.
Speak with Imyl of Rivendell.

'Hello there, I was wondering if you might be able to spare a moment. My Uncle Bilbo and I share a birthday, September the Twenty-second, and I have celebrated it by holding a small gathering in his honour every year since he left Bag End. Even though the day has passed, I thought it would be nice to get the old rascal something for our birthday anyway.
'It is a small gift, but I was hoping that you could bring it to him. He wouldn't take a present from me now -- he would say \q\qIt isn't right, Frodo my lad, what with it being past our birthday and all,\q\q but perhaps he wouldn't turn down the gift if it was delivered by someone else.
'Would you do this for me?'

'Ah, he did enjoy the gift, splendid! And here I go, having you carry off presents for others without thought of yourself. A wonderful ${RACE} if I ever knew one!
'I believe I have something here for you. It isn't much, just a trinket. A small toy really. Why, I remember the day I was giving these out at my eleventy-first birthday not seventeen years ago...but I am going on with old tales again.
'Thank you for your help, ${PLAYER}.'

'What is this now? A present from Frodo for our Birthday? Well, isn't that curious, for I was planning on giving young Frodo a present of my own! It has been a tradition of mine ever since I arrived here in Rivendell to give out presents on my birthday to the Elves. They don't much understand the custom, but they always accept the gifts graciously. Wonderful folk, the Elves.
'I always set aside a present for Frodo and have in fact been carrying it around for a few days now! I would more than likely forgotten about it had you not reminded me.
'Take my present to him, if you would; he is often troubled, and it may brighten his mood.'
'Hmm, yes? Can I help you with something?'

'Bilbo accepted the present after all? Well, that did go better than I expected!
'And what's this? A present for me, from Bilbo? He is always full of surprises.
'Go back and tell him thank you very much, and that I will come to visit him later.'
'Did you deliver the present to Bilbo?'
Deliver the present to Bilbo Baggins
Deliver the present to Frodo Baggins

'We cannot grieve now for Laerdan, ${PLAYER}. Amarthiel will not hesitate to make use of her newly-found knowledge. If only we had been able to seize the palantír in time, her search for Narchuil might have remained fruitless! Nay, there is little use in dwelling on the past. Take comfort in this, ${PLAYER}: we know what Amarthiel saw within the depths of the seeing-stone, for she spoke of it when you and Laerdan entered Barad Tironn! Did she not speak of the wilderness of the Trollshaws? She has revealed to us her next movement, and if we act with haste, we may yet find Narchuil before she does.
'We have not the numbers to prevent her servants from leaving Evendim, but we can at least be alerted of their movements. Two of my brethren watch the roads out of Evendim, and they must be told what to expect: that Amarthiel may be planning to send her servants by various roads out of Evendim. Seek Torogethir at the Evendim Gate, north-east of here at the pass to the Fields of Fornost, and Galthoniel on a small rise overlooking the Barandalf, far to the south of here and east of the halfling-village of Dwaling. Tell them what we suspect of Amarthiel's plans, and that they are to send ravens to Tinnudir at the first sign of the Angmarim's movements.
'They are not to engage any such patrols in open battle! Go with haste, ${PLAYER}! When our strength in arms is found lacking, information must be our greatest ally.'

'Thank you for the news, ${PLAYER}, though it is worrisome. I think it unlikely that Amarthiel would choose to send her warriors to the Trollshaws by the road I watch, but I will send a raven to Calenglad at once if it does come to pass.
'But I must disagree with Calenglad's wishes on one matter: if Amarthiel does choose to send her Angmarim south along this road, I will not stand idly by. Though I fall in battle with the Enemy, I will keep at least some Angmarim from passing into the Shire. Nay, do not seek to change my mind! I will not be swayed in this.
'I will send my raven first, of course.'

'You have my thanks, ${PLAYER}. I wish we could prevent the Angmarim from leaving Evendim in search of Narchuil, but I know that we do not have the strength of arms to succeed in this. At least we will know when the patrols have set out.
'I should have expected Galthoniel to refuse my wish that she not engage the Enemy in battle, but I would not have her throw her life away lightly! My heart tells me that if Amarthiel chooses the long road to the Trollshaws and passes through the Barandalf, Galthoniel's sacrifice will do naught to forestall the inevitable.
'Now that we will have warning when the Angmarim begin their search, we must begin our own, ${PLAYER}. If we are to find Narchuil, we must learn everything there is to know about it. The time has come to confront Mordrambor.'
'I will take your news to heart, ${PLAYER}, and send a raven to Calenglad at the first sign of Angmarim leaving Evendim. I have seen naught yet, however. It has been unusually quiet.'
Book XI, Chapter 1: Watching the Roads
Laerdan has been lost within the once-proud halls of Barad Tironn, and now the Dúnedain must prevent Amarthiel from acting on the knowledge she gained by her use of the palantír.

'I will not be swayed in this matter, ${PLAYER}, and Calenglad was fool-hardy to ask it of me! I will send a raven to Tinnudir at the first sign of Angmarim, but I will not stand by and allow them free passage southward.'

'We may not have the numbers to keep the Angmarim from leaving Evendim and travelling to the Trollshaws in search of Narchuil, but I want to know the moment that they do. Torogethir and Galthoniel, the Rangers charged with guarding the roads out of Evendim, must be told what to expect.
'Torogethir is north-east of here, just west of the Evendim Gate to the Fields of Fornost. Galthoniel has a small campsite on a small rise that overlooks the Barandalf, south-east of Tinnudir. Look for her east of the halfling-village of Dwaling.
'Tell them not to engage the enemy, but to send ravens to Tinnudir at the first sign of Angmarim passing out of Evendim.'
'I have seen no sign of Angmarim leaving Evendim. When I do, I will send a raven to Tinnudir at once.'

Torogethir is at a small camp just west of the Evendim Gate to the Fields of Fornost, north-east of Tinnudir. Galthoniel has a camp on a small rise overlooking the Barandalf, south-east of Tinnudir and east of the Shire-village of Dwaling.
Calenglad has asked you to bring news of possible movements of the Angmarim out of Evendim to Torogethir and Galthoniel, the Rangers tasked with guarding the roads.

'Mordrambor has proven an unreliable and dangerous prisoner for us thus far, ${PLAYER}, but now he will recompense for his betrayal. He will tell us what he knows of Amarthiel's lost ring, Narchuil, or he will never again see the light of day. He cannot know its location, or his mistress would have had no need for the palantír, but anything he can tell us of its power or history may be of use.
'I will go with you to speak with the Black Númenórean. He has proven able to ensorcel the minds of others, and we will have better fortune if we confront him together and steel ourselves against his trickery.
'I have some words for our prisoner concerning the fate of Laerdan, as well. Mordrambor will rue the day he sent the Elf to his death. Speak with me when you are ready to go.'

'There are no words, ${PLAYER}, for the evil Mordrambor has done this day. I thought we had seen the last of the grief he could cause, but the treachery that sent Laerdan willingly to his doom is as naught compared to the sorrow I feel for the loss of my kindred.
'Colhamnir...Carchammadel...Tadan....
'Too many lives lost, and in the very heart of the place we held safest! How could Angmar strike us even here? We cannot search for Narchuil now, ${PLAYER}. Mordrambor has dealt a fatal strike against my kindred, and we must rest. My people need time to grieve -- they cannot fight on forever in the face of such losses! I am sorry.'
Talk to Calenglad and confront Mordrambor about Narchuil
Chapter 2: Mordrambor
Calenglad has decided that before you begin your search for Narchuil, you must learn what you can about the ring from Mordrambor.

'Are you prepared? Mordrambor has proven himself an ill house-guest, but he may know something of Narchuil which we can put to use. He has not yet seen the wrath of the Dúnedain, and I would speak to him of Laerdan's fate. He will tell us what he knows, but you must steel yourself against his sorceries!'

'My people need time to mourn, ${PLAYER}, or they will be unable to continue the fight. The greatest weapon Angmar wields in this war is hopelessness, an overpowering dread that seizes the hearts of good folk and saps their will to stand against evil. It has been brought to bear here on Tinnudir with terrible success.
'I have set my brethren to gathering stones from Annúminas with which we may construct cairns for our fallen kindred. If you would travel to the great city and help with the collection of these city-stones, I know that Tadan, Colhamnir, and Carchammadel would have been honoured by your service in their memory.'

'These will do nicely, ${PLAYER}, and I thank you for the gesture.
'There is still no word from Torogethir or Galthoniel. It seems that Amarthiel too has been delayed in the beginning of her search, or she busies herself with celebrating the escape of Mordrambor and the deaths of my people. We will have our vengeance upon them both, but the time of its coming arrives too slowly!'
'You have not collected enough stones yet, ${PLAYER}.'

Calenglad fears for the resolve of the Dúnedain and has set them to gathering stones with which to build cairns for their fallen brethren.

'Stones from Annúminas, far to the south-west, on the shores of Lake Nenuial, will be used to construct cairns in the memory of our fallen kindred. It would have filled them with honour to be buried beneath the stones of the City of the Kings.'

Stones from the buildings of Annúminas can be found all throughout the great city and would be ideal for constructing cairns in memory of the fallen Rangers.

'It is time, ${PLAYER}. There is a place not far from here of which Carchammadel was particularly fond in life -- Barad Rath, an overlook crowned in ruins high above Lake Nenuial. That the tomb-robbers had made frequent use of it was a sorrow to her. We have decided to build the cairns for our fallen kindred at its crest.
'Will you join us in remembering our fallen and add a stone to their cairns? Speak with me when you are ready, and we will depart.'

'I thank you again, ${PLAYER}. You did not know Tadan for long, but he was a good man, and I know he appreciated your visits, despite the dangerous tenor of the duty in which you found him. I do not blame him for what happened, and I ask that you do not, as well -- Mordrambor has ensnared folk greater than you or I.
'I feel that my people will be able to fight once again, and with renewed determination. We will not forget what Mordrambor and Amarthiel have done, but neither shall we wallow in our grief! Our vengeance, when it comes, shall be magnified ten-fold by our losses, and they will regret their misdeeds!'
'Yes, ${PLAYER}? What is it?'

'I had hoped we would learn something of Narchuil that might aid us in finding it before the Angmarim, but that hope, like so many others, has been dashed. We have been delayed by Mordrambor and must now follow Amarthiel's forces eastward, where I had hoped to stay before them.
'No matter. There are many tall hills between here and the wilderness of the Trollshaws, and if we must follow, we will do so knowing what to expect. You should leave Evendim heading east and pass through the Fields of Fornost. A short distance north-east of Trestlebridge stands the great hill of Amon Raith. Stand at its peak and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> eastward. If you see the Angmarim ahead of you, continue to Amon Sul, which is called Weathertop by many, in the Lone-lands, and do the same: <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> eastward from its summit.
'I am worried that the Angmarim may attack villages along the way. By scouting their position from the heights, you will be able to learn of their progress and follow them wherever they are headed.'

'You bring warning from my sister that the Angmarim have come to Tâl Bruinen? Her warning is welcome, but my scouts have already encountered the Enemy.
'Do you know why they have come to this place? Can you tell me what brings them to these woods, so far from their evil homeland?'

'You are seeking the Angmarim that passed this way not long ago? I saw them coming from a great distance and managed to hide myself before they arrived. I feared I would be found, for at the head of their number marched a man of great evil; a Black Númenórean, if I do not miss my guess. It seemed to me that he stared right at my hiding-place, but at just that moment he was interrupted by some thought that caused him to turn and gaze off into the distance to the west; I know not what it was, but he shortly resumed his march, and the company passed into the east.
'Your face tells me that you have had dealings with this man, and the memory is full of sorrow. From what I overheard, it seemed their course lay to the south, among the cheerless lands of Tâl Bruinen. My sister Candelleth has a camp in Tâl Bruinen. To reach it, follow the road east of here until you are nearly within sight of the Bruinen, and you will come to a dirt path that winds southward with the Bruinen on your left and a tall rock-face on your right. Stay on the path, even as it crosses streams and winds through the underbrush, and you will surely come across one of Candelleth's scouts, who can guide you to her camp.
'Tell Candelleth of the Angmarim that have come to the lands of her watch. Tell her, as well, to be wary. I fear to think what errand could have brought this Black Númenórean so near to Imladris.'

Chapter 5: Eastward Passage
Companies of Angmarim have been seen leaving Evendim and passing into the east, heading for the Trollshaws in search of Narchuil.

'We must find Narchuil before the Angmarim, ${PLAYER}. We know that they are likely journeying to the Trollshaws, but I am afraid they might turn aside from their path to attack villages between here and there.
'Climb Amon Raith, the tall hill in the North Downs, south-east of the Fields of Fornost and north-east of the town of Trestlebridge, and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> eastward from its summit. If you see the Angmarim in the distance, do the same atop Amon Sûl, the hill called Weathertop, in the Lone-lands.'

'We must find Narchuil before the Angmarim do, ${PLAYER}. We know that they are likely journeying to the Trollshaws, but I am afraid they might turn aside from their path to attack villages between here and there.
'Climb Amon Sûl, the tall hill in the Lone-lands, and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> eastward from its summit. If you see the Angmarim in the distance, follow them at once!'

'If the Angmarim have already reached the Last Bridge, they may be well on their way to finding Narchuil for Amarthiel!
'You must travel to the Last Bridge and find someone who knows where they went from there.'
'The Angmarim have passed into Tâl Bruinen? Return to Alphlanc at the Last Bridge on the western edge of the Trollshaws and follow her directions to learn where they may have gone!'

'The Angmarim passed through the Evendim Gate, ${PLAYER}, and I sent my raven to Tinnudir after they were through.
'I am sad to have missed the cairn-building for Colhamnir -- we fought together in the South during our young years, and his death pains me. I will visit his cairn when I am no longer needed on watch.
'If you plan to <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> eastward from the summit of Amon Raith, you will need to pass through the Evendim Gate and journey south-east over the Fields of Fornost. Amon Raith is a tall hill to the north-east of Trestlebridge and should give you a commanding view of the Downs.'

'You are here to scout the passage of the Angmarim? They passed by some hours ago, and I marked their course. Stand here upon the summit and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> to the east, and you should see them in the distance.'

'My sister's camp is called Echad Candelleth. Travel into Tâl Bruinen and warn her of the presence of the Angmarim in those lands!
'Follow the road east of here until you are nearly within sight of the Bruinen, and you will come to a dirt path that winds southward with the Bruinen on your left and a tall rock-face on your right. Follow that path as it winds southward, even as it crosses streams and through dense undergrowth; Candelleth sends scouts out from her camp, and you will surely find one who can guide you further if you can follow the path.'

Echad Candelleth is in Tâl Bruinen, south of the Ford of Bruinen. Alphlanc told you to locate the path south along the banks of the Bruinen, and to follow the path until you come across one of Candelleth's scouts, who can further guide you to the camp.
Alphlanc has told you that the Angmarim company passed into Tâl Bruinen and wants you to travel to her sister Candelleth's camp in order to warn her of the danger posed by the presence of the Angmarim.

'Your story fills me with concern, ${PLAYER}. Tâl Bruinen is a dark and wooded land, and this ring for which Amarthiel seeks could be anywhere. If the Angmarim have some guidance to its location that we do not, I can see little chance that we will find it first.
'My scouts tell me that the Angmarim seem particularly interested in the small ruins that dot the landscape of Tâl Bruinen. If you could journey to some of these ruins and defeat the searching Angmarim, I will contemplate upon possible places where a ring such as Narchuil could have been lost.
'I fear this errand may be hopeless, ${PLAYER}, but perhaps Narchuil, if it is within these wooded lands at all, will evade the Angmarim as well.'

'You have done your part, but I must confess that my list of possible hiding-places for the ring Narchuil is very short. I will tell you of them, and let you judge for yourself if they seem to be reasonable to you.'
Chapter 6: A Cheerless Land
You have told Candelleth why the Angmarim have come to Tâl Bruinen, and she is now thinking of possible places where Narchuil could be hidden.

'Many small ruins dot the landscape of Tâl Bruinen, ${PLAYER}, and the Angmarim seem particularly interested in searching these sites. While you defeat some of these invaders, I will think of some places where Narchuil could have remained hidden.'

'Certain places within the woods and crags of Tâl Bruinen have an unsavoury air. The few travellers that pass by them oft report an unsettled feeling, a troubling disquiet. This in itself is not unusual, for the land remembers many things that we have forgotten and makes such memories known to us, though we recognize them not. But to learn that such a relic of evil as the ring by which the Champion of Angmar knew her greatest strength could lie hidden within these woods -- it could explain much.
'Look to the south-east! Do you see the stone-work within that narrow pass through the rocks? That place is called Delossad, and it is a ruin of which I know little. Of Elven-make it is, but the air is heavy all about it. Look for Muildir by the narrow pass to Delossad, and he will tell you if he has seen anything of note.
'The other site I have in mind is Eryn Singor, a den of the Wood-trolls in north-west Tâl Bruinen. The creatures grow from saplings in that wooded and watery grove, and it is therefore rarely troubled by outsiders. Might Narchuil lie within the reedy beds or buried in the mud of Eryn Singor or the depths of Bar-e-Therchir beneath it? One of my scouts, Lavanthir, has studied the ways of the Wood-trolls. Look for him outside the entrance to Eryn Singor.
'When Muildir and Lavanthir have given you what aid they can, return to me with Narchuil or with any information about its location which you have learned, and we can decide our next course.'

'Do not give up, ${PLAYER}. I had thought Narchuil might have been the cause of the troubling disquiet that hangs over Eryn Singor and Delossad, but it was only a guess. Perhaps the ring does lie deep within Delossad. With no way to gain access to the ruined halls without also allowing in the Angmarim, we must trust to the locked door to delay them while we search elsewhere.
'But listen! Another avenue of search may have opened up to us.'
Investigate Eryn Singor with Lavanthir

Candelleth has decided upon several locations within the woods of Tâl Bruinen that might hide the ring Narchuil.

'Delossad and Eryn Singor have always had an unpleasant air about them. Could it be that the presence of Narchuil is to blame?
'Look for Muildir outside the narrow pass through the rocks that leads to Delossad -- you can see it from here if you look to the southeast. Eryn Singor, the home of the Wood-trolls, is in the northwestern region of Tâl Bruinen. You will find Lavanthir somewhere outside the entrance.
'Return to me when you have found Narchuil or have exhausted the search at each place!'

'It is a pleasure to meet you, ${PLAYER}, but it must be an urgent errand to bring you this far into the wild.
'I must confess to you that I have seen no sign of this ring you seek, but the Wood-trolls make lengthy exploration difficult. There is an unsavoury air about the place, and the presence of an evil relic might serve as explanation for it.
'There is a cave beneath Eryn Singor, called Bar-e-Therchir, and I believe that the unpleasant air that hangs over the land here comes from that cave. Make your way into Eryn Singor, defeating the Wood-trolls as you go, and find the entrance to Bar-e-Therchir. Once you have found it, return to me, and we will plan our next move.'

'Your story is in harmony with what I have learned of Bar-e-Therchir, ${PLAYER}, and now that we know where it is, the cave must be searched for any sign of Narchuil.
'This will be no simple feat, for the cave is the home of the Dâg Taushakhu, children of Taushakh, who ruled the Wood-trolls of the North for a time. Look for them in the deepest chambers of Bar-e-Therchir, and determine if Narchuil rests within one of their chambers.
'Hinder, too, any Angmarim you see searching the cave and return to me when you have plumbed the deepest chambers and slain the Dâg Taushakhu. Perhaps you will return with Narchuil, and the search will be at its end?'

'You found no sign of Narchuil? I am sorry, ${PLAYER}, but we may take comfort from this: the Angmarim still search the cave, but we know now it is not to be found within. May their learning of this fact be slow!
'I am pleased that you defeated the Dâg Taushakhu, for no good could come of their continued growth. Taushakh himself caused a great deal of turmoil in Tâl Bruinen before he found his way northward, and his children would likely do the same.
'I am sorry your search here proved fruitless. Did Candelleth suggest any other likely sites?'

'I am pleased to meet you, ${PLAYER}. I saw you standing with Candelleth from afar, but I do not think you saw my distant greeting.
'The Angmarim came to Delossad immediately after they arrived, but as far as I know, they have not yet gained access to the deep places of the ruins. You should investigate and discover if the door is still locked -- it has been for as long as I have known of it, and it will be a comfort to know that the Angmarim have not yet breached it.
'And if you would, ${PLAYER}, defeat some of their number while you explore Delossad. The ruins have always been covered by an unpleasant weight, but they were built by Elves, and this is not a place for Angmarim. I would have them cast out.'

'The door is still locked? I am glad to hear it, though it means we are no nearer to learning if Narchuil is hidden somewhere behind it! The key to that door has surely been lost to time, and I do not doubt that if the Angmarim believe Narchuil does lie within Delossad, they will seek to force the door open before long.
'Did Candelleth give you any other sites to search for clues? The locked door of Delossad may purchase us some time in which to find Narchuil, if it is hidden at some other location in Tâl Bruinen. If it is within Delossad, I must admit that I am at a loss. Even if we could somehow gain entrance to the sealed ruins, how could we remove Narchuil without alerting the Angmarim?'

Chapter 7: The Door of Delossad
Muildir has been keeping watch over the ruins of Delossad, and has noted a strong interest by the Angmarim in the crumbling site.
'Defeat some of the Angmarim here at Delossad and check to see if they have yet managed to open the door leading further into the ruins.'

'I had been focusing on places around which travellers and my scouts have reported sensations of uneasiness and disquiet, such as the Wood-troll grove of Eryn Singor or the Elf-ruins of Delossad, but that only because it was the avenue I felt was open to us.
'The Angmarim have also been combing the Elf-ruins throughout Tâl Bruinen, and until a few hours ago, I assumed this was because they had some information we did not. And yet, if this was so, why would they not focus on one place? If they knew Narchuil to be hidden within Delossad, would they not devote all of their efforts upon it? I am sure they would, and yet, they did not, which tells me that the Angmarim do not know the location of Narchuil anymore than we.
'One of my scouts, Idhreneth, encountered a small company of Angmarim near the burnt-out remains of a cottage not far to the north-east of Echad Candelleth -- the Crumbled Cellar, it is called. She defeated the Angmarim and sent word to me, asking if I knew any reason they would show an interest in such a trivial place. The answer is clear: they are searching everything they can in the hope that they find a clue, just as we have done, ${PLAYER}. I want you to speak with Idhreneth and learn what you may.'

'Candelleth has told me the tale, ${PLAYER}. Do you really think that Narchuil, or some evidence to its location, might be hidden in Tâl Bruinen?
'A small company of Angmarim was sifting through the debris of the cottage across the water over there. It is called the \qCrumbled Cellar\q by Garbert and Afanen, who live down the river, but I think it burned to the ground before Garbert's time.
'You should search through the rubble. I cannot imagine you will find anything of use, but if the Angmarim thought it worth searching....'

'You found this diary among the ruins of the Crumbled Cellar, ${PLAYER}? It is probably nothing, but I will see if I can learn anything from its pages....
'The name of this diary's owner is familiar to me and fills me with dread: did not Amarthiel use the name Sara Oakheart as she travelled on her fell errands through the wild? And yet, look here, upon the cover -- it is barely legible, but it can be made out: \qSara Oakheart!\q
'You must bring this diary to Candelleth, ${PLAYER}. This may be the clue for which we have sought!'
'No Blah!'

'What is this, ${PLAYER}? A journal? Can it be? I do not understand. Amarthiel cannot have...there must be more to this riddle than we know, ${PLAYER}, for I am filled with confusion. But hearken to this:
\q...brought two chickens to share with L, but his spirits were low, and I think the food brought him no joy. Understandable, of course: keeping N within the walls of Sithad must be a great sorrow to him.\q
'Whoever Sara Oakheart may have been, Amarthiel in disguise or not, it is plain to me of whom she speaks: can \qL\q be any other than Laerdan, or \qN\q anything but Narchuil? We are close. I can feel it. The secret lies within this journal, friend ${RACE}: the diary of Sara Oakheart.'
'You do not have anything for me? How can this be?'
Search debris of the Crumbled Cellar

'${PLAYER}...it was Tann Morgul. I kept meaning to bring it...to Calenglad...but....
'Mordrambor...his sorceries....'

'Let us meet with Mordrambor, ${PLAYER}. We have much to say to him...and to hear, I expect.
'We will need to be on our guard. Let us learn from Laerdan's folly, and our own: even in captivity, a Black Númenórean may cause much trouble.'

'Mordrambor is gone, ${PLAYER}, and he leaves many of my people dead or dying. It seems that he wove cruel sorceries within the mind of his jailor: how often did Tadan resolve to bring Tann Morgul to me, only to have the matter slip from his memory? It is clear that this relic of evil gave to our prisoner some measure of the power he sought.
'Nay! Do not blame Tadan for this! Any of us could have done this. His was a dangerous duty, and he has come now to the end of his service. Weep for him, but do not lay the blame at his feet! It belongs with Angmar and its cruel servants alone.'
'We must repair the damage done to the keep, but there can be no cure for some of these hurts.'

'Well met ${PLAYER}, did Elrond send you up here? No matter either way...we've plenty to do before the heavy snows set in. It seems that Rivendell is getting nervous about the rumours they've been hearing about Goblin-town falling under the sway of Angmar or some-such, so they sent me and my lanky friend here to take a look around and see what's what.
'Can't say that we know for sure whether Angmar is involved, but we did find a large goblin-encampment on the surface just a short ways north-east of here. Normally the goblins prefer to stay down in their caves away from the sun, so that's a tell-tale sign that something is wrong.
'We've been making little forays now and again against the goblins, but for now we've got to keep an eye on this pass -- make sure they don't start heading west to join with the smaller tribes scattered about the Misties. Perhaps you would care to take a try at them in the meanwhile? There are plenty to go around, and it would give you a chance to determine their strength. I would also say the exercise will do you some good -- you are looking a bit winded from the heights here.'

'Ha! Well fought ${PLAYER}. Goblins may make for poor company, but they do help keep one's skills honed.
'Now those fire-pots you mentioned, those are not weapons for little skirmishes -- they were designed as weapons of war, for burning forests and besieging fortresses. If the goblins are making so many of them, it can only mean they have plans to march beyond these mountains...and soon methinks.
'We will need to do something about that.'

'Well, the Elf here thinks I may have gone a bit daft, but hear me out and see what you think.
'I've got a plan in mind, and those fire-pots the goblins wield are at the heart of it. They are making them in large numbers in there, and while goblins may be industrious, they are also careless. You should be able to steal a number of those fire-pots, and with a bit of work, we ought to be able to use their own weapons against them.
'The thought of that entire camp in flames brings me a certain childish delight, so let's get to work!'

'Ha! Good work, ${PLAYER}. Now let us see those. There is not much a goblin can come up with that a dwarf can't sort out in short order.
'What's this...?'

'No luck with the fire-pots yet?
'From what you have described of the camp, it sounds like they keep most of the finished pots in the smaller camps up in the slopes and ravines above the main camp.'

'It would seem that there are indeed some limits to the ingenuity of dwarves, Master Eywind. Fortunately, I happen to know a Wizard who is far wiser than either of us -- particularly when it comes to matters of fire.
'I remember many years ago when Mithrandir would come to Rivendell to celebrate momentous events with us, and often his fireworks would be central to the evening festivities. It so happens that in discussing the nature of his fireworks, he mentioned a draught which he uses to enhance the virtue of his displays.
'It occurs to me now that if we happened to have a bit of this draught on hand, we might make excellent use of it when it comes time to deal with these goblins and their fire-pots once and for all.'

'What is this? An Elf named Nogmeldis sent you for what? Ah, now I recall him. Bright fellow, though a bit impetuous. He wants my fire-draught does he? Whatever for?
'Goblin fire-pots? An entire camp of them? I think I see what the fellow is about. I do happen to have a vial left...where was that? Ah, here it is!
'Now, be careful with that! No more than a few drops mind you, and keep it away from the lamp oil, or you will soon find yourself lacking your eyebrows...if you are fortunate.'

'Were you successful? Yes, that is the draught Mithrandir mentioned. It does not look like much, does it?
'I will speak with Eywind on how we might best employ this, and then we shall see....'
'You have not had an opportunity to travel to Rivendell yet?'

'By Durin's Beard, this will be a fine day indeed! This draught of Gandalf's is precisely what we need to make a shambles of the goblin's fire-pot camps.
'I went down to take a quick peek at the encampment while you were off to Rivendell, and I found what we're after. That big thing on the lower slope, with the scaffold and the huge burning cauldron on it? That is the heart of their production, and that is where we will strike.
'They've got stored materials for their fire-pots all over the camp -- all we have to do is slip Gandalf's draught into that cauldron and give it a tip, and the mixture should do the rest of our work for us...you mark my words!'

'Haha, well done! 'Tis a fine thing indeed to watch an enemy's schemes blow up in their own faces, is it not ${PLAYER}?
'Would that we could blow the entirety of Goblin-town sky high as well, but I fear that it'll not be nearly as neat a conclusion when at last that dark warren falls...'
