'It will take some time to repair the keys, and if you would be willing, you might be able to help me with a small matter.
'I gifted a number of fine gems to a traveller who possessed an interest in learning the finer points of jewelsmithy, but he was beset by goblins. Though he escaped with his life, many of the gems were stolen by the creatures. Journey to Goblin-town, which lies within the High Pass, and return to me with a handful of these coveted gems. By that time, I shall likely have finished restoring the keys you have brought to me, and I will be able to return the stolen gems to my unfortunate friend, as well.
'You will not find these gemstones in possession of goblins on the surface, for the creatures that seized these gems likely brought them into Goblin-town, the better to protect them.'

'I thank you for this service, ${PLAYER}, for Goblin-town is a vile place and not easily traversed. My friend will be surprised and pleased that you have recovered the gems he thought lost, and he is sure to learn much of jewelsmithy by studying them.'

'${PLAYER}, are you all right? The Black Númenórean appeared outside Delossad, and I only had a moment in which to hide myself. 'Very good, ${PLAYER}. Your exploration of the ruins should now be uninterrupted. I fear that something terrible came from there and would ask you to keep a clear head while you are inside.
'Examine anything that seems unusual, for I believe that the memory of whatever sorrow hangs about that place will make itself known to you. Learn what you can, but remain wary -- creatures of the dark are drawn to such places, and you may need to defend yourself from them.

'Let us leave this place. Memory hangs on its stones like a shroud and fills me with unease.'

'You say that Amarthiel's forces have recovered Narchuil? This is terrible news, ${PLAYER}, and undermines all that we have here sought to accomplish!
'Lord Elrond must be told. Seek for him in the library of Imladris and give him these grim tidings, as well as the diary of Sara Oakheart. He will know what can be done, if anyone will.'

'Your tale fills me with sorrow, ${PLAYER}. The fall of Narmaleth is a sad tale known by few, and then only in part. Of her imprisonment by Laerdan, following the battle of Fornost, I knew nothing. It grieves me that Laerdan believed I would not suffer Narmaleth to live -- the slaying of a captive is not the way of the Eldar, and she would have been safe in my house, though she remain Amarthiel.
'I believe we can guess at the sad fate of Sara Oakheart, last in a long line of Narmaleth's keepers. I do not doubt she treated the daughter of Laerdan kindly, but her payment was doom, and more than that: Amarthiel learned the dark arts from a cruel master, and it seems she took the visage of her jailor for her own. An unhappy fate!
'I am certain of one more thing, ${PLAYER}: Angmar has not yet recovered Narchuil. The ways of the Enemy are the ways of deceit -- do not give in to despair! If Narchuil had been found, Amarthiel would have recalled her minions, and she has not done so. She may have learned some new information concerning its whereabouts, but her servants have yet to find it, of this I am sure. We must remain vigilant against them, as always, and continue our search.'
'No Blah!'
Bring rotted diary to Elrond
Chapter 13: Laerdan's Failing
Deep within Delossad, Mordrambor gave you the terrible news that Narchuil has been found. Lord Elrond must be told.
'Speak with Lord Elrond in the library of Imladris and tell him what you have seen. Give him, as well, the diary of Sara Oakheart. I hope that he will know what to do, ${PLAYER}, for I do not.'

Elrond is in the library of Rivendell.
Candelleth has asked you to bring Elrond the dire tidings that Angmar has recovered Narchuil.
You find a box of broken keys buried beneath the leafy bush
You search beneath the bush but find nothing

'Listen to this, ${PLAYER}:
\qL fears the worst. I will carry out his wishes by breaking the keys to Sithad -- the stones of Tâl Bruinen are heavy and will serve -- and hiding them.\q
'I do not know where Sithad may be, but it sounds as if Laerdan was keeping this \qN,\q Narchuil, within its walls, and at some point Sara broke the keys to this place and hid them. And look at this, further in:
\q...must stand at the stairs of Sithad, looking up towards the entrance. Turn to the left and walk forward to the wall, and then turn right and follow the curve until you see four pillars through two pillars. Walk between the two and look to the right of the four. I will leave the keys always in the shade.\q
'I wonder now if Sithad is not an antiquated name for a place we already know, ${PLAYER}? Language changes over time, and Laerdan has lived for many years; the name by which he knows one place may not be that which it is called by others. As I say the names aloud, it comes to me that Sithad bears something of a resemblance to Delossad, does it not?
'I think we have deciphered the first part of the riddle, friend ${RACE}! Go to Delossad and use the journal to locate the hidden keys of which Sara has written. I am sure it is the place!'

'I am greatly heartened by your success and by my reading of the clues! I am sure that Narchuil is within Delossad, ${PLAYER}, and one of the keys within this box will open the way for us!
'A jeweller of great repute lives in Imladris. Her name is Merilos, and she will be able to remake these keys for us. Be warned: she is stern and slow to befriend, and while she will certainly help us, she will likely ask for some service in return. She does not gift her work freely, for it is of great value and precious.
'Look for Merilos in Imladris, at the Spire of Meeting. Bring her this box of broken keys and ask her to mend them. I wish you good fortune in this.'
'You found nothing? I was certain this was the place!'
'I will be able to remake about half of these keys. The rest are completely beyond repair. Are you satisfied with this?'
'You do not have anything for me?'
Search for the keys mentioned in the diary of Sara Oakheart
Bring box of broken keys to Candelleth
Bring box of broken keys to Merilos
Chapter 9: The Diary of Sara Oakheart
You have recovered the diary of Sara Oakheart, and it may contain the secret to Narchuil's location.

'I am certain I am right, ${PLAYER}. \qSithad\q must have been an earlier form of \qDelossad,\q the name by which we now know those ruins.
'Go to Delossad and follow the instructions within Sara Oakheart's journal to find the location of the keys of which she has written!'

'You will find Merilos at the Spire of Meeting, in Imladris. Ask her to remake the broken keys, if she can, and she will do it. She may ask something in return, but that is her right as a jeweller of unequaled skill.'

Delossad is located south-east of Echad Candelleth, in Tâl Bruinen.
Candelleth is sure that she has solved the riddle posed by the diary of Sara Oakheart, believing that the place of which she writes, Sithad, is an earlier form of the name Delossad, the ruins south-east of Echad Candelleth.

Candelleth is at her camp in Tâl Bruinen.
You have recovered a box of broken keys from beneath a bush at the ruins of Delossad, known as Sithad in days now gone. You should bring the box to Candelleth.

The jeweller Merilos is at the Spire of Meeting in Rivendell.
You have found a box full of broken keys buried sometime in the past at Delossad by Sara Oakheart and should bring them now to the jeweller Merilos, at Candelleth's insistence, to be remade.

'Among other tasks, Eywind and I have come up into these forsaken mountains in search of a companion of mine by the name of Glorwen. She came here some weeks ago with the same duty we have: to explore the strength and purpose of the goblins of High Pass and ensure that they do not move against Rivendell without warning.
'Unfortunately, she has always been easily distracted by the hunt, and I find it likely that she has managed to while away the past weeks entertaining herself and has quite lost track of the time.
'When last we heard from her, she was going to explore a set of giant-ruins to the east, rumoured now to be inhabited by a large pack of Wargs. If you would help us find her, you should begin your search there.'

'What is this? Glorwen's bow? Yet you say you saw no other signs of her save a torn cloak?
'Had the Wargs slain her, it is likely they would have torn her to pieces and let the evidence lie plainly about. If there was no sign of her body, then it is possible that she yet lives. Perhaps she escaped? But I think that unlikely, for she would have gone back for her bow, or come to us in need of aid.
'I have no answer to this riddle, but perhaps the Wargs might?'
'You have found no sign of Glorwen yet? Hopefully, she is simply out hunting goblins and Wargs; nevertheless, I am becoming worried...'
Return to Nogmeldis with Glorwen's bow
Find some sign of Glorwen amongst the giant-ruins
Glorwen's Fate
Nogmeldis and Eywind came to the High Pass, seeking news of an Elf-scout named Glorwen.

The giant-ruins of Starkhath are well to the east.
Nogmeldis asked you to search the Warg-infested giant-ruins for signs of the Elven scout Glorwen.

'This is an outrage, ${PLAYER}! I tracked the white hart into Tâl Bruinen all the way from the Gladdalf, and for some other hunter to steal the kill, the glory, and the meat for himself is unacceptable!
'I recognize the fletching of these arrows, you see: they are the distinctive mark of Adwold, a rival of mine. A hunter of lesser skill, he and I often compete for the same kill, and many are the times he has cost me a great deal of glory. But this is the last time!
'Take these arrows of his and confront him with them. Demand that he repent for bringing down the white hart, when clearly my arrows would have finished the job, and command him to relinquish to me the meat from the kill. The last I heard of him, Adwold was staying at the camp of Barachen the Elf, north of here in the Trollshaws. Barachen usually has one of his scouts positioned along the road; you can ask her for guidance if you get lost. Adwold will regret interfering with my greatest triumph as a hunter to date!'
'I have to tell you, ${PLAYER}, that I would normally disbelieve this tale of Adwold's. But I believe it now, for I have seen this creature, and not long ago!'

'Yes, I came across the white hart of which you speak, wounded and near death, and I loosed these two arrows at it. But I did not take the meat! Just as I approached to give it a merciful end, some terrible creature sprang out of nowhere and grabbed the hart about the neck!
'When all the air had gone out of the poor beast, the creature started to feed. I was terrified, I do not mind telling you, and could think only of escape! As I backed away, the twigs snapped under my feet, and the creature looked up -- it looked right at me! I will never forget those terrible eyes; like lamps they were in the cold light of the moon, half-unlidded but full of malice!
'I ran, and ran, and only when I was certain that the horrible creature had not followed me did I stop to rest. You go back to Wistan and tell him he can have the glory from the hart, if he wants it. But I am through with hunting in those parts! With creatures like that slinking about the wild, it is not safe! I am sticking to the Chetwood from now on! You tell him that, and tell him too that he would be wise to do the same!'
'No Blah!'
Bring Adwold's distinctive arrows to Adwold
The Hunter's Injury
Wistan is furious that the white hart he tracked across the Trollshaws may have been killed and its meat taken by a rival of his.

'You're looking for Adwold? Aye, he was here. Something gave him a terrible fright in the lands to the south, and he swore off his hunt. He said he was going back west; he's probably at the Forsaken Inn by now.'

'The hunter Adwold? Yes, he was here, but he returned from a hunt in Tâl Bruinen and lingered just long enough to say his farewells before departing for home. Something seems to have given him a great fright. I expect he has probably reached The Forsaken Inn by now.'
'Barachen's camp is to the south of here, at the top of that sloping path. I do not think the Adwold of whom you speak remains there, but Barachen might be able to tell you where he has gone.'

'Adwold has done me a great injury with this theft of my glory, ${PLAYER}, and I will not stand for it! Find him at Barachen's camp, in the Trollshaws north of here, and demand that he return the meat he stole and repent for bringing down the white hart when it should have been apparent to any that the kill was mine!'

'You go to that Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen, Echad Candelleth, and tell Wistan he would be wise to leave that place. That terrible creature might still be there, lurking somewhere beneath the trees of a night!'

Adwold may be staying at the camp of Barachen the Elf in the Trollshaws, north of Tâl Bruinen. One of Barachen's scouts often guards the road that runs through the Trollshaws and will guide you to his camp if you get lost.
Wistan is furious that Adwold has taken the meat and the glory from the death of the white hart he tracked across the Trollshaws and has sent you to confront him with a number of demands.

The hunter Wistan is at Echad Candelleth, in Tâl Bruinen.
You have learned that Adwold did not take the meat of the white hart tracked by Wistan, but was interrupted by the arrival of some creature, the sight of which filled him with fear and caused him to renounce any further hunting in Tâl Bruinen. You should report this to Wistan.
Collected a handful of arrows from the slain hart

'It is good to meet you, ${PLAYER}. I was just telling Indor here of my latest kill: a mighty and noble white hart, the likes of which I have never before seen and will never see again! I tracked him down from the Gladdalf and into Nan Tornaeth, but he became frightened, and I lost the trail. I picked it up again amid the Bruinen Gorges and followed him south into the hills alongside this camp. The light was failing, and as he passed westward and I behind him, I loosed a number of my arrows. I know I felled him, ${PLAYER}, but I could not follow in the dark.
'He is out there, my friend: the hunter Wistan's greatest kill! If you come across the body of the white hart, collect my arrows and the body and bring them back to me. My hunt of the white hart will surely make for a fine tale or three about the fire, and there will be a place for you, as well!
'The hart was making westward, but even taking his last strides, he would have steered clear of the Gauredain or the Wood-trolls. Look for the body to the west of Echad Candelleth and between the dwelling-places of those creatures.'

'I knew I brought down that hart! A great chase he led me on, I was just telling the tale again to Indor here...
'Wait. These three arrows are mine, ${PLAYER}, but these two are certainly not! Mine have yellow and green fletching, see? The fletching on these two is red and black!
'You say most of the meat was taken when you got there? It seems to me that someone has stolen the kill that was rightly mine, ${PLAYER}, and I know just who it was!'
Collect arrows and meat from the body of the white hart
Bring a handful of arrows to Wistan
The White Hart
Wistan told you of the white hart he tracked through many lands and believes that he finally brought it down, though he could not find the body.

'Wistan has been telling me about his many hunts. He is full of amazing tales. A much better hunter than I, to hear him tell it.
'Do not misunderstand, I do not begrudge him that! I am not much of a hunter myself.'
'Wistan has been telling me about his hunt of the white hart again. It is even better to hear it the second time, though you would not think it to be.'

'The white hart led me on quite a chase through the Trollshaws, but I felled him in the end! Look for his body somewhere west of this camp, likely between the Gauradan-camp and the watery fen of the Wood-trolls. Return to me with his body and the arrows I loosed at him, and you will be rewarded.'

Wistan thinks the body must be somewhere to the west of Echad Candelleth, between the dwelling-places of the Gauredain and Wood-trolls.
Wistan has asked you to search for the body of the white hart he tracked across the Trollshaws and return to Echad Candelleth with both it and the arrows with which he brought it down.

Wistan is at his campfire at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp to the east, in Tâl Bruinen.
You found the body of the white hart and recovered Wistan's arrows, but someone seems to have found the body first and removed most of the meat. You should return the arrows to Wistan and tell him what you discovered.
Collected wooden figurines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'We must do what we can for the Strawleys, ${PLAYER}. It is too late for one, but not for the other.
'The Gauredain make their home in the south-west hills of Tâl Bruinen, south of Eryn Singor. Travel to this place, this Echad Gauradan, and defeat the bloodthirsty creatures. Take from them the wooden figurines they stole from Tim Strawley, and we will try to make this right.'
'Thank you for this, ${PLAYER}. I am glad that you have recovered Tim Strawley's figurines from the Gauredain that stole them and slew their maker.'
'You have not recovered the wooden figurines from the Gauredain?'
Collect wooden figurines (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Gauradan Ritualist (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring wooden figurines to Tongannel
An End to the Enterprise
Tongannel mourns for the craftsman Tim Strawley, slain by the Gauredain while on his way south to sell wooden figurines in order to support his wife.

'Echad Gauradan is in the south-west hills of Tâl Bruinen, south of Eryn Singor. Slay the Gauredain there and take from them the wooden figurines crafted by Tim Strawley. We must do what we can to ease the pain of his wife.'

The Gauredain can be found at Echad Gauradan, in the south-west region of Tâl Bruinen.
Tongannel has asked you to defeat some of the Gauredain that slew Tim Strawley and to recover the wooden figurines they stole from his waggon.

Tongannel is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen.
You have recovered Tim Strawley's wooden figurines from the Gauredain that stole them.
Collected bristly crawler legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collected slimy crawler mandibles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
You grind the crawler bits into mush

'That Wéthorm has been having a bit of fun at my expense, if you ask me! Well, we will have some sport as well and see how he likes it!
'I will need your help, ${PLAYER}. I am going to \qimprove\q the toad stew by adding crawler bits to it, and then I will have you bring it to Wéthorm. Tell him that I made some improvements to the stew, and it is even better now! Oh, we will have the last laugh with this one, my dear ${RACE}!
'Gather some crawler legs and mandibles and bring them back to me, and we will set my plan in motion! You will find crawlers all throughout Tâl Bruinen, ${PLAYER}, so start hunting!'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}! These legs and mandibles are very unappealing and will be just the thing!
'Do me a favour and grind them into mush on that grinding stone, will you?'
'You have not brought me all the pieces of crawler for which I asked, ${PLAYER}.'

'This will do nicely, ${PLAYER}. It looks terrible, and it smells worse! It is perfect!
'Now, take this toad stew and bring it to the dwarf Wéthorm at Thorenhad. Tell him that I made some additions to the stew to make it taste even better, and I wanted to share it with him. And be sure to get a good look at his face when he takes a bite -- I want you to describe it to me, leaving nothing out! We will have the last laugh, we will!
'Thorenhad is north of here, in the Trollshaws, along the Bruinen Gorges. Wéthorm said he was going to visit one of his kinsmen there for a while, and I am sure he is still there.'
'Where's the crawler mush, ${PLAYER}?'

'Hello, ${PLAYER}. Wéthorm at your service and your family's! Ah, you are a friend of Indor! He is a good Man, if a little too trusting; in these dangerous times. He would do well to learn that lesson early.'
Wéthorm takes a tremendous bite of the toad stew, and his face lights up. He takes a second bite, and then a third, before handing the bowl back to you.
'Hello, ${PLAYER}. What can I help you with?'
Collect bristly crawler legs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Collect slimy crawler mandibles (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Bring crawler legs and mandibles to Indor
Grind crawler bits into mush on the grinding stone
Bring the crawler mush to Indor
Bring improved toad stew to Wéthorm
Best Served Cold
Indor has decided to reciprocate Wéthorm's bad humour with an ill joke of his own.
'There are crawlers all over Tâl Bruinen, ${PLAYER}, but they especially like damp places. Bring me some of their bristly legs and slimy mandibles and we will teach that Wéthorm a lesson!'
'The grinding stone is right there, ${PLAYER}. Grind all the crawler pieces into mush, and then I can add them to the stew! We will teach Wéthorm to play tricks on us!'

'Wéthorm is staying at Thorenhad, north of here in the Bruinen Gorges of the Trollshaws, north of the bear-dens. Pay close attention to his first bite of my toad stew, because I want to savour my revenge!'

Crawlers can be found all throughout Tâl Bruinen.
Indor has asked you to collect several pieces from the crawlers of Tâl Bruinen so he can have his revenge upon the dwarf who played a trick on him.

Indor is at the campfire at Echad Candelleth, in Tâl Bruinen.

The grinding stone is near the campfire at Echad Candelleth.
Indor has asked you to grind the various crawler bits you recovered into mush on a nearby grinding stone.

Indor is at the campfire at Echad Candelleth, in Tâl Bruinen.

Wéthorm is at Thorenhad, in the Bruinen Gorges of the Trollshaws, north of the bear-dens.
Indor has sent you to Wéthorm with his toad stew, and has asked you to pay close attention to the dwarf's reaction to his first bite. Indor wishes to savour his revenge on the dwarf who tricked him into tasting the unpleasant toad stew.

'Don't be ridiculous! My husband is fine -- in fact, he's inside the house right now, resting from his ordeal! You see, when those wolf-men attacked the waggon, he wasted no time at all: he broke upon the crate of figurines and started throwing them at them. While they were distracted by the cunningly-crafted missiles, he crept by them down the path and escaped into the woods! He got turned around, or he would have stopped at Echad Candelleth to see the Elf Tongannel again, but he was already nearly to the bridge when he regained his bearings. He came home, bemoaning the loss of the figurines, and I put him right to bed to rest.
'But you have recovered the figurines he meant to sell! He'll be so pleased. I think I will forbid him from making another such journey, however -- we will sell them here in Bree, and that will be more than enough. He is an enterprising sort, but he must see the wisdom in this.
'Here, take one of these figurines back to Tongannel. I know that Tim will be touched by her thoughtfulness, and he will want her to keep this figurine as a token of her friendship with the Strawleys.'

'My heart is filled with joy at your tidings, ${PLAYER}! I will treasure this figurine, and think of the Strawleys whenever I look upon it!
'Take this reward with my good wishes, though it is nowhere near the happiness you have brought to me with this news!'
'Yes? Why have you returned to me with nothing?'
Bring the wooden figurine to Tongannel
Cause for Joy
Nora Strawley has given you unexpected, but joyful, tidings: her husband survived her encounter with the Gauredain.

'Bring that wooden figurine to Tongannel with our deepest thanks. I hope that she will treasure it in memory of the concern she had for us, and as a token of friendship with the Strawleys.
'She is at the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen? Tim spoke to me of her kindness, and of the kindness of all at Echad Candelleth.'
'Welcome, ${PLAYER}! I am overjoyed to see you again!'
'See this wooden figurine? It fills me with joy to look on it.'
'My husband is still recovering from his ordeal.'
'We were able to get plenty of coin for the sale of the figurines you returned.'

Tongannel is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen.
Nora Strawley has given you the happy news that her husband survived his ordeal and has asked you to bring one of the wooden figurines to Tongannel as a sign of friendship.

'You have recovered the wooden figurines that were stolen from Tim Strawley's waggon, ${PLAYER}, and they must now be brought to his widow. It is my hope that she will be able to sell them; not for as much as Tim hoped to receive south of the mountains, but enough for her to live on for a time, I think.
'The Strawleys made their home in the town of Bree, but beyond that I do not know where you will find Nora. Bring her my best wishes, as well, and tell her of my sorrow.'

'These are my husband's figurines; I would know them anywhere!
'How did you come by them? And why the sorrowful face?'
'Hello. What is it?'
Bring wooden figurines to Nora Strawley
Cause for Sorrow
Tongannel wants you to bring the sad news to Nora Strawley and to give her the wooden figurines you recovered.

'Nora Strawley lives somewhere in the town of Bree, but I do not know any more than that. Bring her the wooden figurines her husband crafted, and it is my hope that she will be able to sell them for enough coin to live on for a time.'

Nora Strawley lives somewhere in the town of Bree.
Tongannel has asked you to bring the wooden figurines to Nora Strawley in the hope that she will be able to sell them and make enough coin to live on for a time.
Something has gnawed all the meat from these fish-bones

'I had gone down to the bank of the river to stretch my legs and take in the scenery -- and, I confess, to give some thought to what punishments I could inflict upon Adwold for interfering with my hunt -- when I saw it.
'It was sitting on a flat stone on the far bank, and I moved closer to get a better look -- I took it at first to be one of the Little Folk, but in the light of the moon it seemed much too scrawny, its skin stretched over brittle bones. I was still deciding what to do when it did something that chilled my heart: it began to sing, a shrill warbling above the sound of the water.
'I dared not stay any longer, ${PLAYER}, and came back to camp. But I want this creature caught! This will be my greatest hunt, even better than the white hart! I want you to walk along the banks of the Bruinen, east of here in the valley, and look for signs of the creature's passage. Return to me when you have found some clue that will let us bait a trap for it.'

'Fish? That sounds like a good guess, ${PLAYER}! Now that you mention it, it seems to me that the creature might have been singing about fish the night that I saw it. Hard to say -- it was a shrill little thing, but I did not want to get any closer to it, if you take my meaning.'
Find clues to the creature's habits along the banks of the Bruinen
The Creeping Shadow
Wistan has told you that he saw a creeping shadow along the banks of the Bruinen that he thinks may have been the same creature Adwold encountered.

'I do not know what that creature was doing alongside the Bruinen, but if you go search the banks, we might learn something we can use to set a trap for it! The river is east of Echad Candelleth. Be careful! That thing looked dangerous!'

Clues to some means of trapping the creature seen by Adwold and Wistan will surely be found along the banks of the Bruinen, east of Echad Candelleth.
Wistan has decided that he wants to catch the mysterious creature he and Adwold have seen and has asked you to check the banks of the Bruinen for clues to the creature's habits.

Wistan is at his campfire at Echad Candelleth, in Tâl Bruinen.
You have learned that the creature seems to enjoy fish and should report your discovery to the hunter Wistan.
A waggon lies broken on the road here
The crate is broken and empty, but the placard reads 'Property of T. Strawley'

'My heart has been ill at ease for the last few days, ${PLAYER}, and I hope you can put my fears to rest. A traveller by the name of Tim Strawley came to Echad Candelleth on his way south; a craftsman he was, and he bore wooden figurines of exquisite quality that he hoped to sell in far-off markets. He hoped to raise enough money to support his young wife, Nora, and he was enthusiastic about his prospects.
'But the road is rarely-travelled, and a worry has been growing in the back of my mind ever since he left the camp. If it is not too much to ask, could you take the road south towards Hollin and check to see that he has not run into trouble? I am sure everything is fine and you will find nothing, but I will feel better to know it.
'The road to Hollin runs south of Echad Candelleth and crosses the Bruinen at a small ford east of Garbert's cottage, where it rises steadily until reaching the Hollin Ridge. Return to me when you have checked the road, and my mind will hopefully be at ease.'

'I feared this news, ${PLAYER}, but I did not wholly believe it. Tim Strawley never made it to Hollin. Who now will care for Nora, of whom he spoke often while he was here? I do not know her, but I weep for her all the same, and for her husband, slain by the Gauredain.'
Look for any sign of Tim Strawley on the road to Hollin
Dangerous Enterprise
Tongannel has had an uneasy feeling for the last few days and hopes it does not bode ill for the southern-bound traveller she befriended.

'I hope you do not find any sign of Tim Strawley south along the road towards Hollin, but if you do I want to know about it. I have had an uneasy feeling for the past few days, and I fear he may not have reached his destination.
'The road south of Echad Candelleth fords the river east of Garbert's cottage and climbs toward the Hollin Ridge.'

Tim Strawley drove his waggon south of Echad Candelleth along the road heading for Hollin, which crosses a small ford east of Garbert's cottage and climbs towards the Hollin Ridge.

'We are going to need a lot of fish if we are to trap this sneaking creature, ${PLAYER}. If it can catch fish on its own, only a large enough pile of the things will grab its attention!
'A fisherman by the name of Garbert has a cottage to the south of here, at a fork in the river. Speak with him and see how much it will cost to purchase a barrel or two of fish. You will handle the cost, of course?'

'That is the truth of it, friend -- we cannot leave the house while that creature is still out there. I want it caught as much or more than you do, and I know Afanen feels the same, but I cannot risk leaving the cottage unguarded.
'Here is my offer, though: if you go to my nets and collect the catch, I will let you take whatever this Wistan needs to set his trap. I have nets strung all over the waters that run through Tâl Bruinen. Search them for fish and bring them back to me.
'Not every net will be fortunate enough to have snared some fish. That is the lot of the fisherman, my friend, but find what you may.'

'You want fish? My husband has not gone to bring in his catch today, and I will tell you why! Because we cannot leave the house, that's why! It is too dangerous!
'Last night, just after dark, we had snuffed out the candles, locked the door, and were just getting into bed, when I thought I heard something moving around in little Whelan's room. Whelan is just a baby, so you can understand my worry: I thought a bird might have flown into his room through the window, which we always leave open a crack so the breeze can come in, and I did not want him to be frightened. But when I went into his room to check on him, I saw that it was not a bird at all, but a monster: a terrible creeping thing hunched over on bony legs! It was moving towards Whelan's cradle, and making a terrible noise from inside its throat.
'Its intent was clear -- it meant to harm my baby! I let forth a cry such as you have never heard, and sprang towards it; I do not know what I thought to do, but the thing sprang out the window through which it had crawled, vanishing into the night. Little Whelan is fine, but what if that thing comes back? That is why Garbert has not collected his catch, and that is why we will not leave the house! Speak to my husband if you like, but you will not change his mind!'
'This should be enough, ${PLAYER}. Bring them to your hunter friend, and we will see how goes the setting of the trap! This creature will enjoy these fish, maybe, and then enjoy nothing ever again!'
'You do not have enough fish? Why is this, friend?'

'I asked for two barrels full of fish, ${PLAYER}, and you have only brought me five fish! Well, I suppose it will have to do.
'But your story has put me in mind of some better bait than fish!'
'Where are the fish? You did not bring them?'

'Most delicious! Indor has truly improved upon my original recipe. I cannot place the ingredient, but there is a whiskery sort of quality to it that makes the dish truly amazing.

'You have returned, ${PLAYER}! Describe to me the look on Wéthorm's face when he bit into my \qimproved\q toad stew!
'What? He liked it? That is odd. Do you think I stumbled upon some culinary secret, ${PLAYER}? Maybe adding the crawler mandibles legs did something to the body of the stew? Maybe in combination with the toad parts, they worked some magic in the flavour? This could be quite the discovery!'
Indor excitedly scoops a big spoonful of the Improved Toad Stew and takes a tremendous bite. His grin quickly fades to a scowl.
'By my eyes, he tricked me again! Wéthorm, you scoundrel! This is even worse than the original stew! You know, ${PLAYER}, maybe Wéthorm has a point. I will try and be less trusting from now on. 'It's no secret that I consider myself something of a skilled cook, ${PLAYER}. Folk are always giving me new recipes to try, and I spend more time preparing delicious new dishes than I do hunting! You need to follow your own path, that's what I always say.
'I spoke for a while with a very nice dwarf named Wéthorm as he passed through Tâl Bruinen on his way north. He told me he had a delicious recipe for Toad Stew, and after a little bit of coaxing, he agreed to share it with me!
'Would you help me gather the ingredients for it? I still need some toad tongues and legs. You will find toads all along the rivers that run through Tâl Bruinen, I wager.. I understand that the green river-toads have the tastiest legs and tongues! Don't come back here with legs and tongues from the red ones. Wéthorm was most specific on that point!'

'Very good, ${PLAYER}! I see that you have collected the ingredients I need to make toad stew!
'If you will grind them up on that stone right over there, I would be much obliged.'
'You do not have the toad pieces for which I have been waiting? Why not?'

'Thank you, thank you, ${PLAYER}! Now I will just stir this mush into the rest of the stew, and...it is done!'
Indor takes a big bite of the stew and chews contentedly for a moment. Then an expression of disgust crosses his face, and he spits out his mouthful.
'This is disgusting, ${PLAYER}! It is not at all as delicious as that dwarf claimed!'
'Have you not ground the toad pieces yet?'

'Have you seen them, traveller, the worms that crawl throughout the woods and crags of Tâl Bruinen? They are born in the rocks high to the east of Echad Candelleth. Their sire is Sarlug, a most vile creature, and their dam is Sarnemil, ferocious and protective.
'I sought to end their reign of this area once, but I was alone and could not finish them -- I rue now the decision that made me take flight, but I thought them grievously wounded, unable to cause more harm. I was wrong. Their wormlings have now matured, and more are on the way. Soon, Tâl Bruinen will be overrun with the creatures.
'I would be grateful if you would finish what I began, traveller. Cirith Ulunn is directly to the east of Echad Candelleth, but it is tucked amid the high mountains; you cannot reach it from the valley of the Bruinen. Instead, travel to the north-east, along the slopes that hug the eastern arm of the mountains. When you are high up, travel then to the south, into Cirith Ulunn. Sarlug you will find there, but Sarnemil will likely flee. West of Cirith Ulunn, on the very edge of the cliffs, a single monument rises from the earth. Stand there on the cliff-edge, and <rgb=#FF0000>look</rgb> into the distance: you will likely see in which direction Sarnemil has fled. Return to me when you know this, have defeated Sarlug, and have also thinned the numbers of the rock-worms.'
'Very well-done, ${PLAYER}! Your view from the heights matches what I know of Sarnemil: she goes now to protect her second clutch of eggs. She must be defeated quickly!'

'The road that passes through Tâl Bruinen is little more than a dirt path for most of its length, but it is still used by travellers who pass south heading for Hollin and must be kept in usable condition.
'I have been charged by Lord Elrond with keeping the road clear, but it is a time-consuming duty, and I am often at a loss to keep it free of hazards.
'The path runs north of Echad Candelleth and south towards Hollin, and often becomes choked with brambles and treacherous stones. Furthermore, longhorns often stray near to the road and threaten travellers. If you can clear the road of these threats, I will reward you for your time.'

'You are welcome at Echad Candelleth, ${PLAYER}.'

The road that runs through Tâl Bruinen often becomes choked with brambles and treacherous stones and is threatened by longhorns. Bainthir has offered you a reward if you can help him with his duty of keeping the road clear.

Bainthir is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen.
You have cleared the road that runs through Tâl Bruinen of many hazards and should return now to Bainthir for your reward.
Defeated Stone-trolls in Tâl Bruinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Stone-trolls are not known for their intelligence and when they wander too far from their homes in the north they often find themselves more confused than usual.
'These lost trolls are easily angered and can be a real danger to travellers in Tâl Bruinen unfortunate enough to be caught outside at night.
'If you are brave and good, you might seek to defeat a number of the Stone-trolls that wander in confusion throughout Tâl Bruinen by night, though I would recommend you not go alone.'

'The woods of Tâl Bruinen can be dangerous and frightening when the moon is hidden among the clouds, but your deeds this night have made the area more safe for unwary travellers. I thank you, friend!'
Defeat Stone-trolls in Tâl Bruinen (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
More Confused Than Usual
The hunter Cerys is concerned about the Stone-trolls that wander into Tâl Bruinen during night-time and wants something done about them.
'The Stone-trolls often wander out of the north and into Tâl Bruinen when night falls, ${PLAYER}. If you and your friends can defeat some of these angry creatures, you will be rewarded.'
'Good work against the Stone-trolls, friend!'
'These woods are still frightening at night, but you have made them less so.'

Stone-trolls sometimes wander out of the north into Tâl Bruinen by night.
The hunter Cerys has asked you to combat the Stone-trolls that come into Tâl Bruinen at night-time. He also suggested you take friends.

Cerys is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen.
You have defeated a number of confused and angry Stone-trolls and should report of your victory to Cerys.

This barrel is lying just off the road that runs through Tâl Bruinen, but most curiously, it is full of pipe-weed! It is already a rare thing to see waggons pass this way, but waggons carrying pipe-weed are even more rare.
You take a pouch of pipe-weed from the barrel and resolve to bring it to nearby Rivendell. Perhaps someone there will know what caused this barrel to come here.

'You found this pipe-weed in a barrel by the side of the road? How strange, and how lucky...my pouch is just about empty!
'I thank you for this, friend! I wouldn't worry too much about the mystery, though -- the smoking of pipe-weed must be catching on in all circles, not just those of hobbits or Wizards. And why not?
'Take this with my thanks!'
'You don't seem to have anything for me?'
Bring pipe-weed pouch to someone in Rivendell
Surprise Pipe-weed
You found a barrel full of pipe-weed just off the road that runs through Tâl Bruinen. Most unusual....

'You found a barrel of pipe-weed out in the wild? That's odd, but I say it's a pleasant sort of odd, don't you?
'I have enough already, but Frodo or one of his friends might have run out and would thank you kindly for some more.'

'A barrel of pipe-weed, just lying by the road? I know that Pippin would bring a whole barrel of the stuff with him, if he could, but I'm fairly certain he didn't on this trip!
'Just yesterday he did tell me his own supply of pipe-weed was running low, and I expect he would thank you for this pouch of it, despite the curious circumstances surrounding it.'

'You found a barrel of pipe-weed out there in the wild? You've got some fortune, and no mistake!
'Pippin has just about run out of his own supply, and he'd thank you kindly for that pouch you've got there.
'I wonder how that barrel came to be lying by the road like that?'
'A barrel of pipe-weed, just lying out there in the wilderness? That's queer, and I don't care how well-preserved the weed seems to be, I don't trust it.'
'Thanks again for that pouch of pipe-weed!'
'How did that barrel of pipe-weed come to be there, I wonder?'

Someone in Rivendell, north of Tâl Bruinen, may know how the barrel of pipe-weed came to rest off the road in the wilderness.
You found a barrel of pipe-weed in the wilderness and have taken a pouch from it to show someone in nearby Rivendell.

This heartwood was taken from one of the Wood-trolls of Eryn Singor and shines with an inner light.
A woodworker in nearby Rivendell might be able to fashion something of great worth from such a valuable find.

'Where did you find this shining heartwood, ${PLAYER}? The Wood-trolls of Eryn Singor? It is of great quality, and from it I could fashion goods both useful and powerful!
'This is the least I can do for you, friend ${RACE}. Please take this with my thanks.'
'You have nothing for me, friend?'
Bring shining heart-wood to a woodworker in Rivendell
Valuable Heart-wood
You have taken the shining heartwood of unusually high quality from one of the wood-trolls of Eryn Singor and should find someone who can make use of it.
'Thank you again for the shining heartwood, ${PLAYER}.'
'Even from the cruel Wood-trolls can come beauty, when fashioned with care.'

A woodworker in Rivendell might be able to fashion something of great worth from the shining heartwood you found.
You should bring the shining heartwood to a woodworker in Rivendell.
Defeated Tempest Warg (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeated Temptest Stalker (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Glorwen had been tasked with scouting the strength of the Warg-packs in the Misty Mountains, especially those who prowl through the High Pass, near upon the gates to Goblin-town. She has failed to return, so we must continue her mission.
'The ruins to the east were once inhabited by capricious giants, but it is said that they fell at odds with the goblins of Goblin-town, and most moved south and east of here, being unable to pursue the vicious goblins into their underground kingdom. Now those ruins appear to have become the lair of a large pack of Wargs, who are likely allied with the goblins.
'Test them, if you would, and see if they fight or flee -- if they fight in the face of losses, then it is likely they are held under a strong pack-leader and remain allied with the goblins.'
'So, ${PLAYER}, you have returned already? It seems the wargs remain organized in some fashion, and likely friendly to the goblins - would that there were some way to break their foul alliance.'
Defeat Tempest Wargs (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Tempest Stalkers (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Against the Pack
The Elf-scout Glorwen, friend of Nogmeldis, vanished when hunting near the giant-ruins.

The Wargs occupy the giant-ruins in North-east High-pass.
Nogmeldis has asked you to do battle with the Wargs to test their strength and numbers.

Nogmeldis is at Eywind's camp, west of the giant-ruins.
You should return to Nogmeldis and tell him what you have learned of the Tempest Wargs.
You have found the stone remains of three mighty Stone-trolls

'Many years ago, my grandparents lived in a quiet village not far from here. It was a peaceful place, and they were very happy, but one day three monstrous Stone-trolls came to the village and caused great destruction. My grandparents fled, and eventually my grandfather built this cottage here on the bank of the Bruinen. His son lived in the cottage with them, and I was later born here.
'I grew up and took a wife, and my parents left me the cottage when they passed on; Afanen and I have lived here ever since. I have always wondered whatever happened to those three trolls: Bert, Tom, and Bill they were called, and the names send shivers down my spine even today!
'I'm sure they must have come to a bad end, being trolls, but if you can find where they ended up and learn the tale of their undoing, I'd be very glad to hear it!'

'Bert, Tom, and Bill, you said? My goodness! Yes, yes, I know of them, and more than that; they invited me to dinner once! Well, I say \qinvited,\q but that's not quite true. You might say I invited myself, but hoping to pick a troll's purse is not as easy as you'd expect, and if caught in the act you might very well be cooked!
'I was there with the dwarves, you see, and when I didn't come back from my little bit of burglary, the dwarves came to see what had happened. Soon enough, the trolls had bagged them all, and a debate had begun concerning how best to cook us and eat us! Well, Gandalf turned up, as he does when most needed, and sure enough the trolls had spent so long bickering that they were quite turned to stone at sun-up! So that's what happened. I've written it all down in my book, but to have lived it is a much different experience than to read about it!
'If you want to visit old Bert, Tom, and Bill, you'll find them in the wilderness of the Trollshaws, off the road.'

'Ah, so that is what happened to those old trolls. I am glad to have heard the story, ${PLAYER}, and thank you for the news! It is good to know that old Bert, Tom, and Bill came to an unhappy end after what they did to my grandparents' village.
'You have my thanks for the tale, and I will give you this as well!'
Find someone who knows the fate of Bert, Tom, and Bill
Find Bert, Tom, and Bill
Bert, Tom, and Bill
Garbert's grandparents were driven from their village many years ago by three marauding trolls, and Garbert wants to learn what became of the villains.

'If you are looking for the one who defeated Bert, Tom, and Bill, three trolls who ought to have spent more time thinking and less time bickering, you have found him!
'But the tale should be told by another; look for burglar Bilbo in the Hall of Fire to tell you the tale. He knows it most intimately, and if he perhaps downplays his own part in the events, it is only to his credit.'
'The trolls probably met their end somewhere within the Trollshaws. I do not know who might know the tale of their undoing, but if you can find someone who does, I would appreciate it.'

'Garbert is always going on about the trolls that ran his grandparents out of their village. If you can find where the trolls ended up and learn the story of their undoing as well, maybe he will finally stop talking about it!'
'This Bilbo sounds like a great hero, does he not? I wonder what else he has written in his book?'
'It is good to know those trolls came to a bad end.'
'Bert, Tom, and Bill won't be troubling us, and that is a relief.'

The trolls that terrorized the village that Garbert's grandparents once lived in probably met their end somewhere within the wilderness of the Trollshaws. Garbert lives in a cottage along the banks of the river in Tâl Bruinen.
Garbert has asked you to find the location where the three trolls of which he spoke met their end and to learn the story of their undoing.

Garbert lives at his cottage in Tâl Bruinen, on the banks of the river.
You have learned what befell the trolls Bert, Tom, and Bill, and have visited the glade where they were turned to stone. You should return to Garbert with the news.

'With your discovery of Glorwen's bow, we are left with little but dire tidings in the search for her, but at least you have not come upon her gnawed bones, so we can be thankful for that.
'Unfortunately, few Wargs are inclined or even able to speak the tongues of the Free Peoples, and I am afraid my own experience with their kind can be summed up entirely on the point of a yew shaft, so I have little insight to offer. I do not know how we might learn more of her fate from them.
'Eywind's people lived up here for many years before they were driven out, and some few still linger. Perhaps he could offer more insight than I?'

'Well, while it is true that I've fought and slain many a Warg in my day, I have had little cause to speak with them beforehand.
'But if my memory serves me a-right, there is a pair of brothers who have lived up in these mountains for quite some time as hunters and trappers. If anyone might have learned something about that pack, it would be them.
'The last I heard, they were holed up in the ruins of Hrimbarg -- an old dwarf-place to the east and a bit south of here -- still pursuing their trade. If you can find them -- and they still live -- they might be able to tell you more.'

'So, this Thorgest told you of a means to pose a challenge to the leader of the Warg-pack?
'It sounds to me like a novel means of having one's self ripped limb from limb by ravening Wargs, but if there is some chance that we might be able to learn something of Glorwen's whereabouts from this Blackfang, then perhaps it is worth the risk!'

'What do you want? SOmething about that pack up there to the north? I used to hunt the aurochs up that way, before I moved into the worm-scale business, and I learned a fair bit about them in order to stay alive. If you want to find one that will talk, that would be Blackfang, the pack-leader. A few others might know the tongue of Men, but they won't talk to you. It will be him that speaks for the pack and strikes bargains with the goblins -- but he won't speak to you either...unless you were to call him out.
'You see, Wargs are big on strength and survival of the fittest and all that -- so while there is no way a pack would ever accept YOU as a leader, they would still look to the pack-leader to kill you if you laid down a challenge to his leadership, just to prove his strength. If he backed down or refused, he would lose face -- and for a Warg, that can be fatal.
'The custom of challenge varies from pack to pack, but in this one it's simple. There is an old goblin totem in the middle of the ruins they live in -- you just go stand next to that for a few minutes and that signals you want a fight. Blackfang will have to come out and face you sooner or later or lose face with his pack. Of course, he's the pack-leader because he IS the strongest one up there, so you take care or he will tear you apart.'
Way of the Pack
Nogmeldis seeks to learn more about the Tempest Warg pack to the east in order to find some way to discover the whereabouts of the Elf-scout Glorwen.

Eywind is at his camp with Nogmeldis, at the entrance to the High Pass.
Nogmeldis suggested you speak with Eywind conerning the Wargs and what the dwarves know of them.

The dwarf brothers are said to dwell at Hrimbarg, to the east and a bit south of Vindurhal.
Eywind suggested you find the dwarf-brothers he spoke of and ask them what they know of the Wargs of the Misty Mountains.

Nogmeldis is at Vindurhal, a little north and to the west of Hrimbarg.
You should return to Nogmeldis and tell him what you have learned of the Wargs.
Defeated Gauradan Wind-master <${NUMBER}/${TOTAL}>
Defeated Gauradan Wolf-born (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Forgive my lack of manners, but I have been in better sorts. You try playing host to a sorry lot of adventurers that barge into your quiet home up in these remote heights, while you have a Gauradan arrow stuck in your leg....
'Ah well. I'm not much one for company, but as you can see, I have fallen on hard times, so if you are willing to lend a hand, I suppose I would be obliged. You see, I lost the hunters that ambushed me out in that blizzard, but they've been sniffing around closer and closer to my little home here, trying to figure out where I went. If they find it and tell the others...well, that will be the end for old Thorgest, I'm afraid.
'I know it's dangerous, but if you could see your way to making the lives of those hunters difficult -- and short -- it might discourage them from trying to hunt down this dwarf.'

'Thank you, ${PLAYER}. You have taken a great burden off of my mind, what with all that has happened lately. Did you happen to see my brother Thorkell while you were wandering about? No....
'Oh, that's right, he's dead isn't he?
'Sorry, I'm not in my right head...don't feel so good....'
Defeat Gauradan Wind-masters (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Defeat Gauradan Wolf-born (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Eliminating the Trail
The dwarf-trapper Thorgest was recently ambushed by Gauradan hunters who badly injured him. He is afraid that they may yet track him back to his cave.

The Gauradan hunters can be found throughout the southern reaches of High-pass.
Thorgest has asked you to throw the Gauradan hunters off his trail by defeating several of them before they find his dwelling.
You should return to Thorgest at Hrimbarg in central High-pass and tell him that the Gauradan hunters have been defeated.
Searched Gauradan-baskets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'It...it seems the wolf-men have gotten the best of me after all....
'My body feels cold as stone, and this roaring fire is no help at all. Their shamans have laid a curse on me, or that arrow was dabbed in some kind of poison, I know not which.
'I've no healing lore beyond the setting of bones and the binding of cuts, nor are my wits about me. I hope is that if it is poison or curse, you might find something among the Gauradan camps that can cure it -- please, I beg you to go see what you can find, though I can offer little advice as to what might help.'

'What are these? I...I do not not know what to make of them.
'I have no lore to aid me. If you have not found some way to cure me among their belongings, then my last hope is gone.
'Forgive me, I have no strength left...I must sleep now and trust to fate that I will awaken again. Would that my brother were still here to watch over me....'
Search Gauradan-baskets (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Chilled to the Bone
Thorgest appears to have fallen terribly ill from the Gauredain's poisoned weapons.

The Gauradan-camps lie to the south of Thorgest's dwelling.
Thorgest has asked you to search through the camps of the Gauredain in the hopes of finding some cure for the affliction they have placed upon him.

Thorgest's dwelling is to the north of the Gauradan camps.
You should bring the Gauradan-relics you have collected to Thorgest to see if he can discover a cure among them.
Found the Ice-fang antidote

'I beseech you, ${PLAYER}! I do not think Master Thorgest has much longer to live, unless we can find some way to cure his illness. With his brother gone, I do not wish to bear sole witness to the end of his line in this harsh and lonely wilderness.
'Before he fell to this delerium, Thorgest spoke to me of the wolf-men who felled him. It seems that there is some shaman-chief among them that was likely the culprit of his downfall...and perhaps the only one who would know its cure.
'If you can find this shaman, perhaps he carries the cure to this terrible malady on his person. Whatever you do, please hurry!'

'What is that you have there? The Gauradan-shaman carried it? It looks awful...but time has run out for poor Master Thorgest.
'Whatever that is, it cannot do any further harm, and if there is any chance it might save him, we must take it! Please, see to him immediately!'
'What? What is this? Are you trying to poison me further? It is horrible! Let me die rather than drink another drop of it! No! Let me be...!'
Thorgest moans almost inaudibly, and you have found nothing to ease his suffering.
Defeat Jakka of the Gauradan

Thorgest has been poisoned by the Gauredain, and Afwald, Thorgest's assistant, believes the chief shaman of the Gauredain may hold the key to curing him.

The Gauradan-camps lie to the south of Thorgest's dwelling.
Afwald has asked you to try and find the chief shaman of the Gauredain in the last desperate hope that he may hold the cure to the poison that is slowly killing Thorgest.

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}. You have come at a most fortuitous time. Have you spoken to Lord Glorfindel? He seems troubled recently, but will not speak of it.
'You have become familiar with him, have you not? Perhaps he will reveal his concerns to you. If you are willing, go to him near the Bruinen and speak with him.'
'Glorfindel sent you? Indeed, the Shadow of Angmar reaches even here to the RIft of Nûrz Ghâshu. It is well that you have come, for we will need aid in turning back the Shadow.'

'So you have spoken with Faimir? Her concern is kind, but there is nothing she can do.
'A friend of mine, Iorelen, journeyed into Angmar to the Rift, a place the servants of the Enemy call Nûrz Ghâshu. It is said that a great evil dwells there beneath the Mountains of Angmar, and he went to seek news of it. Glathlírel, another ally of mine, had gone there long ago and did not return, though it is said among the Wise that the evil there was contained.
'Perhaps you may be of help. You have ventured into Angmar, have you not? Perhaps you can make your way to Iorelen's camp far to the north east in the land of Angmar and learn of Glathlírel's fate.'
Into the Rift
Glorfindel is troubled about recent events and the recollection of a greater evil in Angmar.
'If you are trusted by Glorfindel, I will put my trust in you as well.'

Glorfindel is near the Bruinen in Rivendell.
Faimir suggests that you speak with Glornfindel and learn what it is that troubles him.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's camp far to the north east in Angmar.
Glorfindel requested that you seek Iorelen and learn whether he still lives.

'This great broken link was once part of the great chain which bound the Balrog Thaurlach within his prison. You wonder if you should perhaps bring it and the news of the Balrog's defeat to Master Elrond in Rivendell.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! What is this you say? You found the prison of the Balrog Thaurlach?
'It is well that you defeated him. Long ago was he chained, though he should have been destroyed. It was not in wisdom that he was spared.
'But that is a long tale, full of sorrow. You should speak with Glorfindel, for this concerns him greatly. You may find him outside standing next to the Bruinen above the falls.'
'Hail and well met, ${PLAYER}. I understand you wish to speak with me?'
'Why do you wish to speak with me?'
Talk to Glorfindel
The Fall of Thaurlach
You have defeated Thaurlach and hold in your possession a broken link of the great chain which once held the Balrog in his prison.
'There are not many alive who can claim to have ever seen a Balrog, much less defeated one in combat. I know of only one in Middle-earth who can claim the latter.'

Elrond is at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, in the Trollshaws far to the south of Angmar.
You have defeated the Balrog Thaurlach and should inform Elrond Halfelven of your deeds.

Glorfindel may be found outside the Last Homely House standing next to the Bruinen.
Elrond suggested you speak with Glorfindel about the defeat of Thaurlach, for the tale concerns him greatly.

You defeated Thrâng, and in the process, learned that the Ghâshfra serve the Ever-seer. Eimyr, Chieftain of the Eldgang, should be told at once, for he has been deceived by the Ever-seer and unwittingly serves his evil purposes.

'You have defeated Thrâng of the Ghâshfra? You have earned a great reward from the Eldgang.
'What is this you say? The Ghâshfra serve the Ever-seer? The Ever-seer seeks to unleash the Great Evil upon us?
'The Eldgang will not stand idle and allow this thing to happen. We have been betrayed!'
'The Eldgang have naught to do with you, little one. Begone!'
Talk to Eimyr.
A Villain Unveiled
You have defeated Thrâng and uncovered the plot of the Ever-seer.
'You have earned the respect of the Eldgang, little one. Now we will see to the Ever-seer!'

Eimyr can be found within Norbar in The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
You have defeated Thrâng and hold his weapon as proof of your valour. You should go to Eimyr and tell him of the Ever-seer's evil betrayal.

'Hail and well met, ${PLAYER}. Were you sent here to aid us? Let me tell you of my mission, then perhaps you will know whether you may aid me or not.
'I was sent both to protect Jónsi, who is here to investigate rumours of ancient mines within the Rift, and to seek out a rare and particularly deadly variety of mushroom -- Curtamusgan -- which grows within. The spores of this mushroom might be used by the Enemy to create a terrible weapon.
'If you would enter the Rift and find one of these mushrooms for me, I can have it delivered to Rivendell, so that they may prepare a defence against the poison. Beware, though, the mushrooms may use its spores as a defence against threats to it.'

'This indeed a Curtamusgan, ${PLAYER}. I will have it delivered to Rivendell by the swiftest means possible.
'Take this reward with the gratitude of the Free Peoples.'
'You have returned without a Curtamusgan?'
Talk to Galasebdir
Mushroom for Rivendell
Lore found in the library of Rivendell tell that a particularly deadly variety of mushroom grows within the Rift of Nûrz Ghâashu. This mushroom might be used by the Enemy to create a terrible weapon.
'Your efforts have been a great help to us. If you can find any more Curtamusgan, it would be of tremendous benefit to Rivendell.'

Curtamusgan may be found within the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Galasebdir has asked you to bring him a Curtamusgan, so that the scholars at Rivendell might study it and prepare a defence against its poison should Angmar use it as a weapon.

Galasebdir is at Iorelen's camp.
You have found a Curtamusgan and should bring it to Galasebdir at once.
Defeated Barz
Defeated Zurm

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! Are you here to aid us in our struggle against the Orcs of Angmar?
'Angmar has sent two tribes of Fire-orcs into the Rift, which they call Nûrz Ghâshu, to mine the metals which may be found there -- which I suspect are of the finest quality! It would be far too dangerous for me to venture alone into their mines, but perhaps you could, with aid.
'If you go there, seek out Barz and Zurm, the Gorthorog-overseers of Bornabar, and defeat them. I understand they not only put Orcs to work, but also slaves from among the Hillmen of Angmar.'

'You have defeated Barz and Zurm? That is wonderful news, ${PLAYER}! Those vile beasts will do no more harm to the stone of the Rift.
'Take this reward...you are well-deserving of it!'
Defeat Barz
Defeat Zurm
The Craft of the Enemy
Two of the Orc-tribes of Angmar, the Blogmal and the Tarkrîp are in conflict over mining rights in Bornabar.
'You did well to destroy those Gorthorog...their mining was destroying the stone of the Rift!'

Barz and Zurm are in Bornabar, within the crumbling seal below Iorelen's camp.
Jónsi has asked you to enter the mines of the Orcs and defeat the Gorthorog-overseers, Barz and Zurm.

Jónsi is at Iorelen's Camp.
You should return to Jónsi and tell him of your victory against Barz and Zurm.

'Master Elrond sent me here to the Rift, which is called Nûrz Ghâshu by the Enemy, to investigate rumours of forays therein by Angmar's forces. There are veins of valuable metals and a variety of deadly mushrooms which might be used to produce a terrible weapon for the Enemy.
'Lord Glorfindel told me, as well, of a legend of a race of giants which dwell deep in the heart of Nûrz Ghâshu. This legend greatly interests me, for it is said these giants, the Eldgang, are not of an evil bent and may help us to combat Angmar.
'Will you enter the Rift and seek out the Eldgang? If you find them, I will reward you according to your deeds.'

'The Eldgang still dwell within the Rift? If they can be swayed to join in our fight, we could well defeat Angmar.
'Rivendell should be informed at once!'
Learn more about the Eldgang
The Eldgang

Iorelen was sent to the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu to investigate the activities of Angmar in the area and the existence of a deadly mushroom found there which could be used by the Enemy to create a terrible weapon. He is also seeking a race of giants of which he learned from Glorfindel at Rivendell.
'You are not like the other little ones who have come here, the Ghâshfra...perhaps you will help us?'

The Eldgang can be found deep within the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Iorelen has asked you to seek out signs of the Eldgang, the legendary Fire-giants of Nûrz Ghâshu.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's Camp.
You should return to Iorelen with news of what you found within the Rift.
You have defeated Thaurlach

'The Ever-seer lied to the Eldgang. We will no longer listen to his foul words.
'For many centuries, we suffered the cruelty of Thaurlach, a Balrog of the Great Enemy, and fought against him. When the Blue Wanderers came with the Elf Glathírel and chained Thaurlach, our people were glad and helped to watch him.. Now the Ever-seer wishes to free Thaurlach and use him for his own evil purposes.
'Go to Gorthban and help Glathírel, who remains here still in vigil over Thaurlach's prison. She will know what to do.'

'What is this you tell me, ${PLAYER}? The Balrog Thaurlach has been defeated? That is a hope we dared not dream of. Your name be recorded in the lore of the Elves as long as time shall last.
'Take this as a reward for your dauntless courage.'
Defeat Thaurlach
An Ancient Threat
Eimyr, the chieftain of the Eldgang, realized the folly of his ways and has chosen to stand against the ancient evil which lies within the halls of Nûrz Gâashu.
'Your name shall be remembered by the Elves for your deeds, ${PLAYER}.'

Glathírel stands vigilant outside of Gorthban.
Eimyr has instructed you to find Glathírel and aid her against Thaurlach, a Balrog of Morgoth.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's Camp.
You have slain Thaurlach and should tell Iorelen of your deeds.
Defeated Ghâshfra (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Little one, you may be of help to the Eldgang. While we did not build this place, it is our home now, and it is threatened by the Ghâshfra from the surface world.
'There are many places in Nûrz Ghâshu where the Eldgang cannot go, for they are too small. Perhaps you would go into these holes and drive forth the Ghâshfra? Then we may have peace again.
'There are many Ghâshfra in Nûrz Ghâshu. They are like a plague.'
Defeat Ghâshfra (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})
Threat of Fire
The Ghâshfra, a breed of Fire-orcs from Angmar, have invaded the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
'Many have noticed your work with killing the Fire-orcs ${PLAYER}.'

Orcs of the Ghâshfra can be found throughout the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Hyrrokkin has asked you to defeat the Ghâshfra which have invaded the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Defeated Thrâng

'Ho there, little one. Perhaps you will help with our troubles here? The Ghâshfra, the Fire-orcs from the surface world, have come to Norbar and war wih us. Perhaps you will help to drive them away?
'The name of their chieftain is Thrâng. If he is slain, the Ghâshfra may learn not to trouble the Eldgang. Asmólf sought Thrâng, but was sent instead to the intruders mine by Eimyr at the behest of the Ever-seer.
'Perhaps you will do this for us? Thrâng may be found within The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu. If you defeat him, your aid will not be forgotten.'
'Fire-orcs have invaded the Rift? We must be wary and learn more of the situation in Nûrz Ghâshu.'
Defeat Thrâng
Aiding the Eldgang
The Fire-giant city of Norbar has been invaded by Fire-orcs from Angmar.

'You have defeated Thrâng? You are a brave warrior among your folk. You will not be forgotten by Tortrygg.'
Tortrygg seems to have little more to say. It may be that Glathlírel may have more insight as to how you should proceed.
'The Ghâshfra are a dangerous breed of Orc. We must proceed with caution.'

Thrâng is within The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
Tortrygg has asked you to find and defeat Thrâng, leader of the Ghâshfra in the Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.

Iorelen is at Iorelen's Camp above The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
You should bring your report of Thrâng's defeat to Iorelen and learn how you should proceed.
Defeated Narnûlubat
Defeated Zogtark

'You are a friend to us, little one? Then hear me, Tortrygg of Norbar. Evil Fire-orcs came from the surface world to conquer us and unleash the Great Evil. THey kill us, we kill them...it does not end.
'I ask you to help us end this war. Help us to drive back the Fire-Orcs. If you can slay Narnûlubat and Zogtark, two of the leaders of the Ghâshfra, the Fire-orcs, the others might leave.
'Will you help us? Narnûlubat and Zogtark may be found within Noruidor.'
'You are a mighty warrior, little one. You are deserving of this reward, though I fear your success was not enough to drive away the Ghâshfra.'
Defeat Narnûlubat
Defeat Zogtark
The Message
Tortrygg is concerned with the invasion of Norbar by the Orcs.
'You very strong!'

Narnûlubat and Zogtark can be found within Noruidor.
Tortrygg has asked to you to find and defeat two of the leaders of the Ghâashfra, Narnûlubat and Zogtark.

Tortrygg is at the Eldgang camp within The Rift of Nûrz Ghâshu.
You should return to Tortrygg with news of your vicory against Narnûlubat and Zogtark.

'Ah, thank you for the help, ${PLAYER}. I will recover in time from these wounds, but nothing can help my brother, Thorkell. When last I saw him he was trapped in the jaws of a great worm. I can only hope his end was swift.
'The worms will have left naught to bury, but they do not eat dwarf-steel. If you dare venture within their caves and retrieve what remains of my brother's belongings, I shall reward you richly.
'You can find the worm caves to the south-east.'

'Ah, is this all that remains of my fair brother Thorkell? Would that I had fallen in his stead....
'But nay, I speak as a fool in my mourning! My dear brother was ever the warrior and adventurer -- moreso than I. He gave his life as he chose to save mine, and I'll never again gainsay his valour for doing so. Nor will I dishonour his name by failing to live as he chose that I should.
'It seems that I have much to do, ${PLAYER}, and wallowing in my grief while the merciless wind wears down these mountains will not get it done!'
Return Thorkell's belongings to Thorgest
Thorkell has Fallen
Thorgest's brother Thorkell was killed a few days earlier by worms.

The worm caves are to the south-east of Thorgest's dwelling.
Thorgest has asked you to find and return Thorkell's belongings.

'I would very much like to see to the matter of slaying the evil worm that took my brother from me, ${PLAYER}, but time is no longer a concern for him, and Afwald has informed me that other duties have become pressing.
'These past few months, we have been hunting here on behalf of the Elves of Rivendell. It seems that they are preparing for some conflict in secret. I am afraid I know little of what they intend, nor is it my business to know. In any case, the armourers there prize these worm-scales for their resilience and lightness. They cannot compare with a coat of mithril mind you, but they do make a fine undercoat for heavy armours of chain and steel. My brother and I were hunting these worms and collecting their scales when calamity befell us...but nonetheless, if I am to stay in business, I must complete the shipment I promised.
'I will give you a full share of the profits if you can help me finish collecting those scales, ${PLAYER}. What do you say?'

'Excellent, ${PLAYER}, that should be enough scales to satisfy my clients in Rivendell...but what is this?
'This scale here, the one with the golden sheen...where did you find it?'
'I am afraid the shipment I promised the Elves was quite large. You will need a fair bushel of scales before I can fulfill it, but they are simple enough to harvest in the caves to the south-east.'
Bring the Burning Worm-scales to Thorgest
Business Before Vengeance
Thorkell has an important shipment of worm-scales that he has promised to the Elves of Rivendell as they prepare for the possibility of war with Angmar.

The worm-caves are to the south-east of Thorgest's dwelling.
Thorgest has asked you to help him collect burning worm scales to make ready a shipment for the armourers of Rivendell.

'The Trollshaws are dangerous, ${PLAYER}, and it takes the labour of many Elves to keep the wild at bay. South along the river, the wooded hills of Tâl Bruinen are home to fierce Gauredain and wood-trolls, and rock-worms climb the heights.
'The Elf-camp of Echad Candelleth stands high atop one of the hills of Tâl Bruinen. Travel east until you see the river and follow the dirt path to the south that climbs the hills above the western bank of the Bruinen. After you pass into Tâl Bruinen, keep a close watch on the path, for the wilderness encroaches upon it, and it may be difficult to make out. The land, too, is damp, and the path may be crossed by several quick-flowing streams.
'If you manage to follow the path, you will come across Haradir, and he will guide you to Echad Candelleth.'

'Greetings, traveller! If you are looking for Echad Candelleth, you have nearly found it! You simply need to climb the slope to the south-east. As you crest the hill, you will see the camp among the ruins.
'Introduce yourself to Nestael, and she will tell you of these lands and what you might do to help.'

'It is a pleasure to meet you, ${PLAYER}, for we have much need of aid! Tâl Bruinen is a place of danger: the Gauredain in the south-west have become bolder than ever, the Dâg Taushakhu in the depths of Eryn Singor urge the Wood-trolls to greater and greater malevolence, and the rock-worms of Cirith Ulunn make travel most treacherous.
'A number of hunters have come to stay at Echad Candelleth for a time, and we give them what hospitality we can. Treat them with kindness, for they are our guests. Furthermore, servants of Angmar have come to Tâl Bruinen. They have focused their attention on the small ruins to be found throughout the woods, but I do not know for what they seek.
'Whether you have come to aid us or merely wish to make use of our refuge for the night, you are most welcome.'
A Road Seldom Travelled
The Elf Rochwen has told you of Echad Candelleth, an Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen, and suggested that you lend its keepers your aid.

'The Elf-camp of Echad Candelleth stands high atop one of the hills of Tâl Bruinen. Travel east until you see the river, and follow the dirt path to the south that climbs the hills above the western bank of the Bruinen. After you pass into Tâl Bruinen, keep a close watch on the path, for the wilderness encroaches upon it, and it may be difficult to make out. The land, too, is damp, and the path may be crossed by several quick-flowing streams.
'Look for Haradir on the road, and he will guide you the rest of the way to Echad Candelleth.'
'To reach Echad Candelleth, you need only climb the hill to the south-east. You will see the ruins from its top and can find Nestael within.'
'You are welcome to stay as long as you wish, ${PLAYER}.'
'I have many goods you may find useful.'
'You have not forgotten, have you? Echad Candelleth is just beyond the south-east hill.'
'To reach Echad Candelleth, you need only climb the hill to the south-east.'

Haradir is in Tâl Bruinen, somewhere near Echad Candelleth. Rochwen told you to head east until you can see the Bruinen river, and then to follow a dirt path south as it climbs the hills above the western bank of the river. She advised you to pay close attention to the path, as it is covered in brush and crossed by streams, and said that you would find Haradir somewhere along its length. He can guide you to Echad Candelleth.
Rochwen has asked you to help the Elves at Echad Candelleth with their charge of keeping Tâl Bruinen free from danger to travellers.

Nestael is at Echad Candelleth, the Elf-camp in Tâl Bruinen, just over the south-east hill from Haradir.
Haradir has told you to introduce yourself to Nestael at Echad Candelleth.
Defeated Ruinuan!

'Among those scales you gathered for me, ${PLAYER}, there was one which shined a burnished gold. It was the same gleam that I saw in the darkness before the dread worm fell upon my brother and I.
'My obligation to the Elves is complete, and now I would have my vengeance! But...the power of this worm is beyond me, even were I not still recovering from the poisons of the wolf-men. I must ask you one last favour -- fear not, I am not a dwarf who expects charity; you will be well rewarded -- but I would have vengeance for my brother's death, and if not by my hand, then by another.
'Gather to yourself some allies and hunt the monster down in his caves. Slay him in the memory of Thorkell, and I will see that it is worth your while!'

'So...it is done at last, and my brother's memory is avenged. Thank you, ${PLAYER}. It will be far easier to go on with business knowing that my debt to Thorkell no longer weighs so heavily upon my chest.
'What to do now, though? These mountains have grown ever more dangerous in these past few years, and Afwald is not the adventerous sort to join me on the hunt. Perhaps I will need to find a new partner, or give up the hunt at last?
'I've no patience for the comforts of civilization anymore -- I think I will stay here and take my chances with worm and wolf-man.'
Defeat Ruinuan
A Worm by the Tail
Among the scales you brought to him, Thorgest discovered one that surely fell from the hide of the monstrous worm who killed his brother Thorkell, and it has rekindled his desire for vengeance.

The worm-caves are to the south-east of Thorgest's dwelling.
Thorgest has asked you to gather allies and go forth to slay Ruinuan.

Thorgest's dwelling is to the north-west of the worm-caves.
You should return to Thorgest and inform him that Ruinuan is dead, slain by your hands.
