'All you have discovered will contribute to us keeping the Misty Mountains safer in the future. If our number was larger now, I have no doubt that Glóin would once again brave the depths of Goblin-town himself and destroy the goblins there. Alas, we are small in number, and there are greater threats to contain elsewhere. Let us be direct then....
'Glóin would like you to be watchful for the goblin and troll, Rakothúrz and Horm, within the Great Goblin's throne room. Lord Elrond mentioned that the forces of Angmar wanted to draw them into the conflict in the north and west, and if we can destroy them we may save the lives of countless allies.
'Search the throne room in Goblin-town for this troll and goblin, and after they are defeated, return to me. Goblin-town is far to the north and east.'

'Well done! A victory against such a terrible foe is surely a great thing.
'You have our thanks and should be content to know that you have saved the lives of many who would surely have suffered terrible fates at the hands of those foes.'
Talk to Tralli Gemfinder
Rakothúrz and Horm

Information received from the letters you recovered in Black Speech led Glóin to offer rewards for the defeat of Rakothúrz and Horm, a goblin-handler and a terrible Cave-troll found in the Great Goblin's throne room in Goblin-town.
'Seek out Rakothúrz and Horm within the throne room of Goblin-town.'
'Rakothúrz and Horm will do no ill to the Free Peoples, thanks to your efforts.'

Goblin-town is far to the north-east of Glóin's Camp and the throne room should lay straight through the many tunnels.
Tralli Gemfinder directed you to find and defeat the troll and goblin, Horm and Rakothúrz, within the Great Goblin's throne room.

Elrond has returned the orders to you

'We have no time to waste, ${PLAYER}. Take these directly to Master Elrond in Rivendell and beseech him to translate them. We have already been delayed too long.
'It is vital that we learn what the Uruks are up to. If they are able to muster the goblins of the Misty Mountains, who knows what force will be arrayed against us?
'Quickly now. Rivendell lies to the south, if you were not aware already.'

'Master Glóin was wise to send you to me. It appears that his fears of the goblins has proven true. Though I am loathe to say it, it appears a new goblin-leader has emerged within the hollows of Goblin-town. This new Great Goblin has united the goblins in there and even now defies the emissary sent from the north.
'Glóin should be told that the emissary from the north is under orders to force the goblins to heed the call of Angmar. Warn him of this and tell him to be cautious.
'Take the orders back to him and bid him read my words. Before you go, however, I would ask that you speak with me more quietly of other matters.'
'You should never see this text.'
'The Great Goblin? But this cannot be! Gandalf slew the Great Goblin with Glamdring. Another goblin has risen in his place, I am sure of it. This news is most distressing.'
'You should never see this.'
Show the orders to Elrond at Rivendell
Deliver the orders to Glóin at his camp in the Misty Mountains
Glóin looked at the set of orders recovered from the Uruks in Goblin-town and found that they were also written in the Black Speech.
'Return to Glóin swiftly. His camp is north and west through the pass leading into the Misty Mountains from Rivendell. He must be warned at once.'
'Quickly now, show those orders to Master Elrond at Rivendell. We haven't much time!'

Elrond is at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, south of Glóin's camp.
Glóin realized that another set of orders written in the Black Speech would take too long to translate and sent you to Rivendell in order to speak with Elrond directly.

Glóin is at his camp in the Misty Mountains, north of Rivendell.
Elrond Halfelven made marks upon the orders and warned you that the goblins had a new leader, a Great Goblin who was defiant of the Uruks' intrustion in Goblin-town. He sent you back to Glóin with the translated orders.

'As I mentioned before, the papers spoke of visitors from the North, and at first I expected that they were Angmarim, like the ones we have seen crawling through the hills. It seems that the Angmarim here are not dealing with goblins at all, but rather great Uruks have come to Goblin-town to press the goblins into service.
'Vighar Roadwalker has a list of names that the Elves discovered among the papers. Speak with him, and perhaps he can offer you rewards for some of the goblins mentioned therein.
'I also would have you seek out the place where these visiting Uruks have been sent in Goblin-town and discover their whole purpose.'
'More Black Speech. We cannot waste any more time, ${PLAYER}. The words written here must be translated quickly.'

'Be sure to speak with Vighar before you return to Goblin-town. He has a list of the names found in those papers.
'Be careful as you seek out the Uruks. Any one of them may carry orders for the goblins, but there may be one who is more clearly a leader among them.'
Return the orders to Glóin at his camp in the Misty Mountains
Rumours of the North
Glóin further explained the writings found on the sheaf of papers you recovered, which entailed a visitation by emissaries from Angmar.

Goblin-town lies far to the north-east of Glóin's camp.
Glóin sent you back to Goblin-town to find the orders carried by the Uruks from Angmar to the goblins of Goblin-town. You will need to locate the place within Goblin-town where the Uruks have gathered.
Defeated Wargs in Goblin-town (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'Wargs are not something we want to contend with, ${PLAYER}. I remember them circling below me long ago as clear as if it were happening now. Their eyes alone could cause the hardiest dwarf to lose heart. Even Gandalf the Grey seemed afraid of such a pack arrayed against us that night. I know that you have dealt with Wargs before with all that is brewing in the wild places, but Wargs with goblins is another matter. The goblins and Wargs have long been allied, and together, they are terrible.
'Now look here...this word appears to be a name. I am not certain what it means, nor am I a scholar wise enough in this foul tongue to know what it truly says. I know only that we must deal swiftly with these Wargs.
'Return to Goblin-town and hunt them down. Kill as many as you can and then return to me. I will see about getting these writings translated.'

'Goblin-keepers with the Wargs already? This does indeed mean that something darker and evil lies within Goblin-town. Fortunately, I received word from our friends at Rivendell about the orders you found.
'Those orders told of visitors from the North being escorted to a specific part of Goblin-town, a place where the armies of Angmar are gathering.
'It also spoke of a goblin sent there to watch over the visitors.'
Defeat Wargs in Goblin-town (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

Memory of the Wargs
Glóin noticed one word which he recognized among the papers you found: Warg.
'Hunt the Wargs in the tunnels of Goblin-town. In the meanwhile, I will work on getting these papers translated.'

Tere are Wargs in the tunnels of Goblin-town, far to the north-east of Glóin's camp.
Glóin explained that, though he cannot decipher the full meaning of the documents you found, there is something sinister within. Seeing only a name and the word for Wargs, he sent you back into the depths of Goblin-town in search of the Wargs allied with the goblins.

Glóin is at his camp in the Misty Mountains, far to the south-west of Goblin-town.
Entering Goblin-town, you found your way into the many twisting and defeated many Wargs. You found goblin-keepers with the Wargs, which may interest Glóin.
You found a sheaf of nasty looking paper on the corpse of this goblin

'You did well against those goblins, but something you mentioned has me concerned. I fear that the sheer number of goblins milling about at the entrance to that place is greater than I expected. It can only mean that they are stirred up to some task or afraid of something deeper in those accursed halls. It merits further investigation.
'Make your way back there, ${PLAYER}, and look for the goblin-leader before the main hall. Something is amiss within those halls, and we must discover the truth, sooner rather than later.
'If you find anything out of the ordinary, return to me so we can put an end to it quickly!'

'Black Speech! Accursed creatures! There is something brewing in that place, I am certain of this now.
'This sheaf of paper is more than enough evidence that the goblins in Goblin-town are working towards some nefarious end. We shall need to delve further, I think, to see the true state of affairs here.
'I recognize this word. Wargs....'

'Be swift, if the goblins are given enough time they may be prepared to move against the West. The people of the North Downs are already suffering enough, and if we can do something to ease their suffering here, we shall!'
Talk to Glóin at his camp in the Misty Mountains
Search for orders among the goblins in Goblin-town
Order from the Darkness
After hearing how you fared against the goblins at Goblin-town, Glóin grew more concerned.

The main entrance to Goblin-town is some distance to the east and north of Glóin's camp.
Glóin believes that there may be something afoot within Goblin-town and bade you return to its halls in search of evidence exposing the reason behind the muster of the goblin-forces.
Defeated goblins in and around Goblin-town (${NUMBER}/${TOTAL})

'I first encountered the goblins of Goblin-town when I was with Thorin's Company on our quest to reclaim the Lonely Mountain. They had captured us and dragged us into their vile tunnels, cracking whips and singing terrible songs. We had our vengeance upon them at the Battle of Five Armies, but they simply returned to the Mountains and began gathering their strength again.
'Now with darkness rising everywhere, they have become a threat again...a threat we must hinder as quickly as possible. The entrance we were taken through was hidden, probably a postern gate. You should seek out their main gate and wreak havoc among their number living within their town or on the surface.
'The High Pass is east and then north of here. I would search in the valley below the path leading into the Mountains Goblin-town's main gate.'

'So many goblins! You say that there were more than enough for your blades, and I have no reason to doubt your word. I fear that my friend Dwalin may be right. The Darkness reaching into the Blue Mountains may also be stretching here to the Misty Mountains.
'We must investigate further, I fear, and that means you must go back into the darkness of Goblin-town.'

The hatred between goblins and dwarves runs deep, and Glóin wants to go on the offensive against the goblins before their threat grows too great.
'Be careful, ${PLAYER}. The goblins are treacherous creatures, and they will not hesitate to throw a bag over your head and drag you down to their prisons or mines!'

The main gate into Goblin-town is far to the north and east of Glóin's camp, in the valley below the path leading into the Misty Mountains.

Glóin is at his camp, far to the south-west of Goblin-town.
Goblin-town teemed with goblins, and the forces within were ferocious and many. You steeled your nerve and struck against them, felling many as you pressed through the entrance of their terrible kingdom. Now you should return to Glóin with news of your success.

'Hail, friend, I would have a moment of your time, if you please. I have a request that may seem out of the ordinary. Long ago, I travelled through the Misty Mountains with Thorin's Company. We found ourselves in trouble within the mouth of a cave in the those mountains and ended up in a terrible place filled with goblins.
'I fear that the recent increase of goblins here in the Blue Mountains, specifically at Sarnur, might mean a greater mustering of goblins throughout Middle-earth. I have heard reports that a friend from the same company is in the area now, and I was hoping that you could seek him out and see if there is anything that he has seen with regards to the goblins.
'His name is Glóin, and he can be found at his camp in the western foothills of the Misty Mountains, far to the east of here, beyond the Lone-lands and the Trollshaws. Seek him out and warn him of the changes in the goblins' behaviour here.'

'My old friend Dwalin sends words of concern! Ha!
'To be true, his concerns are well-founded. The goblins here are as riled as those in the Blue Mountains...moreso perhaps. There is word that the Elves under Master Elrond's care have even sent scouts to see what transpires within the halls of Goblin-town.
'I have a mind to investigate myself, but the dwarves here need my assistance as the Dourhands and their allies are our main concern. Still...it may merit investigation'

Dwalin is concerned about rumours that he has heard about stirrings in the Misty Mountains.
'Be swift! There could be great danger afoot in the Mountains.'

Dwalin wants you to bring word of warning to his friend Glóin in the Misty Mountains. He believes that the increased goblin activity may not be restricted to the goblins in Ered Luin.

'I would hate to ask this of you, ${PLAYER}, but there is another place I would like you to go. The way is quite dangerous, and I simply am not sure whether I should indeed ask it of you, but it is a very important place...it is really where this whole mess began.
'Deep within Goblin-town, there is a cave. I've mentioned it before, I'm sure. A wretched creature called Gollum once lived there. Gandalf says he is related to hobbits, but I just cannot imagine it.
'At any rate, I would like you to find that cave and get me proper directions, as I stumbled into it quite by accident during my adventure with Thorin and Company. But perhaps you should speak with Gandalf the Grey and my nephew Frodo...they might have some reservations about anyone going there.'

'Well then, you have returned, and that means you have spoken to my nephew and my friend Gandalf. They aren't keen on your going to Gollum's cave? Well, I suppose I can't blame them, but I simply must know what has become of that place and how to find it again.'

'Uncle Bilbo is a dear old hobbit, and he remembers his adventure fondly, but I do not think he even now understands exactly how terrible this whole thing is.
'Gollum is loose, and he is searching for...well, he searching for something he once possessed. If you go to that place, hope he has not returned there himself.'

'Bilbo wants you to go where? While Gollum no longer dwells within that cavern, it is by no means safe. YOu will have to pass through the ranks of goblins in Goblin-town.
'What did he tell you of his encounter with Gollum? Nothing? That is good, for it entails knowledge which you need not be made aware of.
'I cannot hinder you, if you believe yourself up to the task, but I warn against it.'
Talk to Gandalf
Talk to Frodo Baggins

'You really should speak with Frodo and Gandalf before you leave. Let me know what they think of this adventure I have tasked you with.'
'I dread the place you speak of, though I have never been there myself. Bilbo's encounter there has laid on me a terrible burden and has brought me great woe.'
'Be cautious should you seek Gollum's cave, for the journey is long and perilous. The goblins will not likely let you pass unharmed.'

'All this talk about Goblin-town and my adventures with Thorin and company has brought back many memories. I was wondering if it wouldn't be too much a bother to have you visit my old friends. I have heard tell that Dwalin is at Thorin's Hall in the Blue Mountains, away west of the dear old Shire and that Glóin is encamped in the Misty Mountains, north from here.
'I wonder if they have any memories of Goblin-town which I could add to my book. Would you visit them and find out for me?
'I would go, but I pledged I had made my last journey. Well, my last journey for a long while anyway.'

'Bilbo Baggins? Old Burglar Baggins? There is a name I have not heard in many, many years.
'So he would like my impressions of Goblin-town? Well, they were not good, that is for certain. All the whips, the stench, the goblins, the wretched songs they sang...it was a dreadful ordeal altogether.
'And to make it worse, when Dori lost our burglar in those tunnels, and Gandalf demanded we go back for him...well, we nearly despaired. Then he appeared out of nowhere, alive! Oh, that was a strange day.'

'SO you were able to find Dwalin and Glóin? Oh, that is good.
'And Dwalin was impressed by my reappearance after escaping Goblin-town? Well, it never would have happened if I hadn't fallen into that dratted Gollum's cave and found...well, found my way out.
'It's a pity that Gollum-creature escaped the Elf-king's people.'

'Bilbo has you researching Goblin-town? We had a terrible time there. I was sure the Great Goblin was going to make an end of us...but then Gandalf came along and saved the day.
'The fire went out, and all we could see was Glamdring flashing blue in the dark. The Great Goblin fell dead, and his folk went all wild.
'We still might not have escaped that place, if it hadn't been daylight outside.'
Talk to Glóin in the Misty Mountains
Talk to Dwalin
Talk to Bilbo Baggins in Rivendell
My Dwarf Friends
Bilbo Baggins has completed his book and would like to make certain that his memory of the important locations and events is correct.

'Good old Bilbo. I have never met a burglar his equal. We were lost in the great Mirkwood without him. And oh the surprise he gave us when we fled Goblin-town.
'I tell you friend, Bilbo Baggins is a magnificient burglar.'
'If you would, please speak with my old dwarf-friends about their memories of Goblin-town. Dwalin is at Thorin's Hall, Glóin at his camp in the Misty Mountains.'

'I remember well of what Bilbo speaks, and I would rather not enter that place again. Darkness stirs in these lands now, and we might yet need to fight our way back through those forsaken tunnels and ancient halls.
'Be cautious if it is Bilbo's charge to send you there.'

Dwalin is at Thorin's Hall far to the west, beyond the Shire. Glóin is at his camp north of Rivendell.
Bilbo Baggins would like to know if his dwarf-friends Dwalin and Glóin have any recollections which would make good additions to his book.

Bilbo Baggins is at Rivendell in the Trollshaws, south of Glóin's camp and far to the east of Thorin's Hall.
Dwalin and Glóin both shared stories of their adventure in Goblin-town. Now you should return to Bilbo.
You have discovered the hidden entrance to Goblin-town

'Well, hullo there! You seem a bit of an adventurous sort...perhaps you wouldn't mind helping out an old hobbit?
'You see, I have been writing a book about my travels with Thorin and his Company -- off to deal with Smaug and get Thorin's gold back -- and I am afraid I may have gotten confused on some details. My memory isn't what it used to be, and I am unsure of the directions to some of the places we visited.
'Perhaps you would help me? All you need to do is find the Back Door of Goblin-town...if you find the place, I have remembered them a-right. High in the mountains, along the stretch called the High Pass, we travelled and at night found a dry place in a cave midway up the mountain. You should find the entrance there. If not, well, try and find the correct directions for me, if you would be so kind.'

'Oh, you found it! That is wonderful.
'Do you know, we found the doorstep quite by accident. We were camping there, taking refuge from a storm and some wayward boulders -- the giants were out playing catch, I suppose -- and were set upon by goblins!
'Gandalf the Grey blasted a few, but we were captured and dragged down to Goblin-town. From there, the tale only gets more exciting.'
Find the hidden entrance to Goblin-town

'I fear he may have been captured by the goblins. If this is true, then I can only hope that he lives still and is kept somewhere in the prisons within Goblin-town.
'Should you find him, do what you can to see him to safety. His name is Aeglas'

'I thank you and Master Elrond for your concern, but I am in no imminent danger.
'The goblins are strong foes, but not so strong that I cannot leave this place. Yet, there is much that we may do together.'

'Your discovery in Goblin-town has us all on edge around here, ${PLAYER}. Something terrible is amiss, and we must be vigilant against that growing darkness or face a terrible foe when they are organized.
'Glóin would like to see that this never comes to pass and has asked me to find those willing to face the strongest enemies within Goblin-town. If you are so willing, then I would suggest finding others before you head out to perform this task.
'The translation of the sheafs mentioned goblin-lashmasters keeping troll-drummers in line in the deep places of Goblin-town. We need you to go there, seek out these lashmasters kill them and their leader, then return to us.'

'This news is bright indeed, friend! You are proving an invaluable asset to us.

'I do not know where within the depths you will find these leaders, but when you do, you should deal with them expediently.

'There are prisoners in this place other than I, and of them I would know more. One is an Elf-maiden, for whom I am concerned. The other is one of the goblins' own.
'I know not how the Elf-maiden came to be here, but she has not been treated well. If you would, go to her and learn her tale. I would know how she was captured by the goblins.
'As far as the goblin goes, though I am loathe to ask this, I would have you speak with him as well. He has been treated no better than the Elf-maiden, and that makes me wonder why he was imprisoned and not simply slain.'
'Stop looking at me, ${RACE}. You have been killing goblins all through Goblin-town. I'm in enough trouble as it is to dig a deeper hole for myself. Unless maybe you help me....'

'Glorwen should not be concerned for me. I will see that she is freed in good time. For the moment, I think the goblins are otherwise indisposed.
'If the goblins and Uruks are indeed in contention one with the other, perhaps we can find a way to use that knowledge to our advantage.
'I will also warn you to be cautious of your dealings with Oghûk. He is a goblin, and we cannot trust him, but the information he may have could be important.'

'The goblins have spoken of Aeglas and I have hoped that he still lived. Knowing that he is still alive gives me great hope.
'I was taken captive while scouting the old giant ruins where the Wargs were gathering. The goblins came upon me in great number, and I could not resist them.
'I know that the goblins are displeased with the arrival of emissaries from the North. The Blogmal Orc-tribe and an Uruk-leader come to press them into service. The goblin's leader, Ashûrz, is unwilling to assist the Uruks, and tension has been growing between them.'

Other Prisoners
Aeglas is concerned for the well-being of the other prisoners in the dungeons of Goblin-town and wishes to learn how they came to be there.
'Help me first, then maybe I will help you.'
'Speak to the other prisoners and return to me when you have learned what they know of this place.'
'Please let Aeglas know what I have told you and wish him well.'

The Elf-maiden and the goblin-prisoner are both in the dungeons of Goblin-town.
Aeglas seem unconcerned that he is captured by the goblins of Goblin-town. His concerns are more for the other prisoners within the depths, and he has asked you to discover what the others know of the unrest moving through the goblins of Goblin-town.

Return to Aeglas within his cell in the Goblin-town prison.
Oghûk seemed an untrusting sort and offered no information unless you helped him. Glorwen seemed in good spirits, once she knew that Aeglas lived, and provided some important information. You should return at once to Aeglas.
Aeglas and Glorwen have found their way to freedom

'The time has come for us to leave this place, ${PLAYER}. We shall need to be cautious. Glorwen must be taken from here, and we will test the truth in Oghûk's words.
'Tell me when you are prepared, and we shall begin our escape.'

'Aeglas has been freed and has returned to the field, you say? You have done well. I am pleased that you were able to free my people.
'You are truly a friend of Rivendell, ${PLAYER}.'
'Guard me, while I free the others. Stay close.'

Talk to Elrond at Rivendell
The Great Escape

Aeglas must be protected as he attempts to lead Glorwen and Oghûk to safety. It falls to you to defend him along his way.

Elrond is at the Last Homely House in Rivendell, far to the south of Goblin-town.
With your aid, Aeglas and Glorwen escaped to safety. Oghûk proved as treacherous as any goblin. You should report your victories to Elrond Halfelven.
You have spoken with Aeglas

'I remembered where the key to my cell is, ${RACE}...on the belt loop of Matuga, the torturer.
'Matuga was called to the throne room by the Great Goblin. It is at the centre of Goblin-town, ${RACE}.
'You will need to go there and kill Matuga, if you are to collect the key I need.'

'It surprises me not that the goblin's tone is laced with menace. They are wicked creatures and cannot be trusted.
'Yet, I think that the goblin truly fears for his life and thinks that he might yet earn his freedom or escape his own demise. It is likely that his information of the key's location is true.
'You will need to go to the heart of Goblin-town and find this Matuga. Kill him and obtain the key. Return it to me, and we will see about freeing the others and testing Oghûk's resolve.'
'It appears that the goblin was telling the truth. We are close now to escaping this place. You have my thanks for all you have done thus far, ${PLAYER}.'
'If Oghûk is correct, you will find this torturer, Matuga, within the Great Goblin's throne-room.'

Matuga and the Jailor's Key
While you were hunting trolls, Oghûk remembered where the key to his cell resides.
'Get the key from Matuga. He will be in the main hall with the Great Goblin.'
'Get the key from Matuga. He will be in the main hall with the Great Goblin.'

Aeglas is in his cell in the Goblin-town prison.
Oghûk told you that the goblin-torturer Matuga has the key to his cell secured on a loop on his belt. Something in Oghûk's voice is disconcerting, however. You should return to Aeglas.

Matuga is in the Great Goblin's throne-room at the centre of Goblin-town.
Aeglas distrusts the goblin Oghûk's intentions, but he does not doubt that the goblin believes that the key is with the torturer. Aeglas agrees that you must search the Great Goblin's throne-room for Matuga and the key.

'Kaushar is to blame for this. I used to mend the drums in the place of the trolls, and Kaushar complained to Aklash who locked me away. Kaushar now mends the drums in my place.
'Kaushar must be punished for this. He is in the deep places where the trolls are. Go there and kill his drummers.
'While you're about your job, I'll figure out who has the key to my cell.'
'Ha! The sniveling worm! Kaushar is probably fuming about the loss of his trolls. You've done well, ${RACE}.'
Return to Oghûk at his cell in the Goblin-town prison
Drummers in the Deep
Oghûk wants revenge on Kaushar, the goblin who imprisoned him for causing trouble with the troll-drums in the deep places of Goblin-town.
'Kill Kaushar's trolls. This will make him angry and give me time to think where the key might be.'

Troll-drummers can be found in the deep places of Goblin-town.
Oghûk wants to exact vengeance on Kaushar, a goblin who mends the drums in the deep places of Goblin-town. He blames Kaushar for his imprisonment and wants to cause him suffering and pain. It is an unpleasant task, but Oghûk will not help you if you do not help him first.

Oghûk is in his cell in the Goblin-town prison.
The troll-drummers were found in an area deep within Goblin-town. Watched over by goblin-taskmasters, you found the trolls and defeated them as requested.

'I want out of this prison, ${RACE}. I do not belong here, locked up. I will help you drive out the nasty Orcs if you help me.
'I need the key to this cell. Look for the jailors, kill them, and take their keys. If you free me, I will help you.'

'No keys to my cell? Curse the name of Kaushar! Curse him by the darkest things in the earth! Curse him!
'I must think. I will gnaw the rat's guts out!'
'One of these jailors must have the keys to my cell!'

'They were prepared for this? It seems that the goblins are more cunning than I had anticipated. I think now it might be necessary to find my way out of this place.

The stake should be placed on a sturdy patch of earth in the place where the Orcs are gathered within Goblin-town.

'This will do just fine. Give me one moment....'
'bring me one of the sharp posts from the lashed piles in the tunnels above.'

'Gollum and his cave are very important to my book, and so I simply must be sure of the details. I don't suppose you could find the old villain, could you? No, that would be quite out of the question, I'm sure.
'Anyway, I'm not sure how I managed to fall into one of the deepest caverns in Goblin-town, but if you could find it and make sure my recollections have not failed me, I would greatly appreciate it. There was a big lake in that cavern, that much I remember clearly.
'I knwo Gandalf and Frodo don't approve, but it would bring some joy to this old hobbit if you could manage this for me.'

'Well, this just goes to show you can only trust your memories so far. I had forgotten all about Gollum's hut...I never saw it up close, thank goodness, so I had no reason to be concerned with it.
'It looks like I will have some revisions to make to my book. Thank you very much!'
'Have you had a chance to verify my writings yet? Have you even managed to find Gollum's cave? Oh, a pity.'

'Gollum's cave lay somewhere deep in the belly of the Mountains. I only know that it was deeper than the mail hall where we came upon the Great Goblin and where Gandalf saved us all from a terrible fate.
'I would be greatly pleased if you could find it again and verify the details in my book.'

Gollum's cave is deep within the tunnels of Goblin-town, beyond the central hall.

Defeated the Great Goblin

'${PLAYER}, I do not speak often of our journeys with my Lord Thorin, but I feel I must now. Long ago, we travelled through these mountains with Burglar Baggins and became captives of the goblins of Goblin-town. Taken down into the dark for what seemed forever, we eventually came to the centre of that place and met the Great Goblin.
'We were without hope in that place, for it was so dark that even our dwarf-sight was diminished and all hope seemed lost. The Great Goblin discovered weapons upon our persons that had been used to fight his kind in ages past and became furious, and hope drew ever farther from our hearts. Thorin, my lord and our leader, remained defiant, and though he attempted to placate the goblin, nothing would calm his rage. At the moment when all seemed most bleak, Gandalf the Grey appeared and slew the Great Goblin, freeing us from Goblin-town and the clutches of the goblins there.
'This news of a new Great Goblin puts a cloud of dread over my heart. If it is true, then we have no choice but to destroy him before the goblins are organized enough to march to the east against Dáin Ironfoot and the dwarfs of the Lonely Mountain, or to the west against the Men of Eriador. I ask you to make your way into the throne room with your allies and find this Great Goblin and end him before his shadow grows so large that it looms over all within it. Will you do this?'

'This old dwarf has had hope restored by your hand, ${PLAYER}.
'All dwarves everywhere will know your name when the threat climbing across this world is quelled, you have my word on this. The word of a dwarf is stronger than the mountians upon which we stand.
'Ashûrz is no more, and we have you to thank for this.'
Defeat the Great Goblin

'I remember the tunnels seeming to last forever. We were dragged down for days into the dark and then brought to a great hall wherein the Great Goblin sat on a large stone and from there ruled over the goblins of Goblin-town.
'Seek out this new wretched leader and end his reign before it truly begins.'
'We are in your debt for your defeat of the Great Goblin, ${PLAYER}.'
'Your bravery is greater than your stature, ${PLAYER}.'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! I have something to offer you. Since the eviction of the Dourhands, the prosperity of Thorin's Hall has been on the rise of late -- and with the Men of Bree-town clamouring for our goods, even more so!
'Such riches seem to draw folks out of the stonework, if you will, and so we've recently been opening out some wider tunnels and adding room for people to move in as they seek work in our mines and crafting-halls. You should go take a look and see if anything there fits your own needs!
'Seek out Rúni at the gates of the Thorin's Hall community. There is always room for another hard worker here!'

'Good day, ${PLAYER}. While you no doubt know that the presence of the Elves in Middle-earth has dwindled in the past age, it might surprise you to know that the communities along this river have grown in recent years as more and more of our brethren arrive awaiting their turn to sail into the West. We have even found it necessary to raise a new neighbourhood to accomodate those who are making the journey, as well as those who may not be travelling no further, but wish to live here and aid in the work we do here.
'I must admit, it is rather exciting to live in a community where there is such vibrance and life, and I have delayed my own journey twice already to remain here and enjoy the company of so many purposeful folk.
'But I digress. Should you seek your own dwelling here in our community upon the shores of the river, find Barchiril at the gates of the neighbourhood and speak with her. She should be able to help you.'

'Greetings ${PLAYER}! It's a fine day to be looking for a place to live, isn't it? The Shire has been most prosperous of late, most prosperous indeed, as the Men of Bree-land have come to rely upon us for ever greater stocks of quality produce and our unmatched flavours of pipe-weed.
'Of course, prosperity draws people to it, and our communities are growing. We even have a new neighbourhood now just south of Michael Delving. If you would like to see it, one such as yourself might even be interested in purchasing one of the new properities we have for sale there!
'Seek out Andy Brockhouse at the gates of the Michael Delving community and see if any of our fine holes suits your fancy!'

'Greetings, ${PLAYER}! Hear me out for a moment, or you will miss the opportunity of a lifetime! As anyone with an ear to the ground knows, troubles in the South have brought new settlers here from across Eriador. With such a migration may come such blights as crowding and refuse -- even the rumours of war from the North, as well as the South -- and old Bree-town lies huddled within these old walls, becoming ever more pressed as each new arrival joins the throngs.
'Now a new settlement has been founded within a stone's throw of town! In the hills south-east of Staddle, new homes and estates are being built for those who have arrived of late. There is room for more, however.
'Seek out Nan Henwood at the gates of the Bree community and find your destiny as a proud land-owner in our fine township!'

'Ah, it is good that you have come by, ${PLAYER}! We've just recently completed some of the new homes that we will be offering to the prosperous and industrious folk of Thorin's Hall here in our community.
'What with the Men, Elves and hobbits all clamouring for our ore, business is brisk indeed, and it has brought many a fine miner and forge-crafter to our doors of late. You too, it seems.
'Well, waste no time, I say. Go ahead in and take a look around. You will find whatever it is you are looking for! The craftsmanship of our builders is second to none other in the Hall, and your money will be well spent indeed if you buy a home from us.'

'Greetings ${PLAYER}, and welcome to the community of Duillond. The shipwrights of the Grey Havens labour ceaselessly to make ready the White Ships that depart into the West, but for many who come here the wait may still be a long one, and more come each day on the wings of the dark tidings that now stretch across the land.
'Thus we have found it necessary to build new villages here along the river's edge where travellers may await the day of their departure, or for those who do not wish yet to sail into the West, who choose to live here and provide services for those who do.
'Please enter our fair community and see if there is anything within that might suit your need, be it for but a short while or for a long time to come.'

'Hallo there, ${PLAYER}! Have you come to take a look at the fine holes of our community?
'Not in living memory has the Shire seen such a time of growth and vitality as this! It is a time of industry and wealth for the taking if you know how...why, you would think we had all become dwarves or something!
'So for those with the ambition and means, a home of your own is not out of reach any more! You can go ahead and take a look for yourself if you like. I'm quite sure something will catch your eye!'

'Ah, welcome to the gates of the Bree community, ${PLAYER}! We have built this neighbourhood to accomodate the migration of people from the South, but there is room for more. Perhaps you would be interested?
'Don't let mere rumours of war and strife from afar dissuade you! With your patronage, our community stands poised to become the most prosperous neighbourhood in all the North!'

Tralli Gemfinder is at Glóin's camp in the Misty Mountains, far to the south-west of Goblin-town.
You entered the Great Goblin's throne room and found Bhoghad entreating with the goblins there. You defeated the Uruk and should now return with the news to Tralli Gemfinder.

'It has been a long season, but it looks as if your spores have finally grown! I took the liberty of tending to the field while you were away...I have been growing mushrooms of my own alongside the ones that you planted in spring.
'I have been trying to perfect my family's mushroom growing techniques for a number of years, and it seems that I was unsuccessful once again. But look at me going on! Patience is the virtue that I have been advocating to you, and now it seems that I am in need of it the most!
'Your mushrooms grew hearty and strong, and you should be well rewarded for your farming prowess! While I won't give up my family recipe just yet, please take this black mushroom transplant, you can place it in your own garden and tend to it there. Who knows, maybe you will find the secrets that I have long been searching for!'
'Here are the black mushrooms that you planted in the spring. Do be careful with them. It would be a shame if you damaged them.'
Harvesting the Crop
You have waited a long time, but now it is finally harvesting season!

Amabel Redfern is near the Party Tree in Hobbiton
You should speak to Amabel Redfern again to recieve your black mushroom transplant.

'Ah, here it is! The Book of Festival-law clearly states that a festival-planner can be changed with a petition signed by no fewer than ten persons who reside in the town of the feast in question.
'Here, take this official petition. If you can find ten residents of Hobbiton to sign it, then the post of Hobbiton Yule-planner can be changed!'
'I'll sign your petition, you can be sure!'

'A petition for a new Yule-planner? Of course I'll sign it!
'That Lobelia has been nothing but trouble since she moved to Bag End. What I wouldn't give for young Mr. Frodo to return.'
'A petition for a new Yule-planner? Of course, I'll sign it!'
'What's that now? Why of course I'll sign your petition!'
'I'll sign your petition!'
'You were able to find a way to get Lobelia out of her office? Give that paper here!'
'A petition for a new Yule-planner? Of course, I'll sign it!'
'A petition? Why would I sign a silly thing like that?'
Talk to the inhabitants of Hobbiton
Serve Lobilia with the petition
Yule Be Sorry
The Book of Festival-law holds precedent for removing Lobelia Sackville-Bagins from her 'post,' but it will not be easy.
'What's that now? Why of course I'll sign!'
'You were able to find a way to get Lobelia out of her post? Give that paper here!'
'What do you want? Can't you see that I am busy preparing for this year's Yule-feast?'

Hobbiton lies far to the east of Michel Delving.
Will Whitfoot has given you an official petition and has sent you to Hobbiton to find ten inhabitants to sign your petition.

Lobelia Sackville-Baggins is at Bag End on the Hill in Hobbition.
Having obtained ten signatures, you should bring the signed petition to Lobelia Sackville-Baggins.
Found the Book of Festival-law

'As I said, there is nothing I can do to help you with Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, as much as I would like to.
'Your only hope for getting a new festival-planner would be to search the Book of Festival-law for any adjuncts to the existing laws.
'I sent the Book of Festival-law to the library in the Great Smials for safe keeping. If you wish to further pursue the matter, you should seek out that book.'
'You found the Book of Festival-law! Let me have a look.'
'Have you found the Book of Festival-law yet? It should be in the library at the Great Smials in Tuckborough.'
Search for the Book of Festival-law
Talk to Will Whitfoot in Michel Delving
The Book of Festival-law
Will Whitfoot mentioned the Book of Festival-law, which may contain more information about Lobelia Sackville-Baggins' supposed post as Yule-planner.

The Book of Festival-law is in the library of the Great Smials in Tuckborough, far to the east of Michel Delving.
Will Whitfoot sent you to the Great Smials in Tuckborough to search for the Book of Festival-law.

Will Whitfoot is at the Town Hole in Michel Delving, far to the west of Tuckborough.
You should return to Will Whitfoot with the Book of Festival-law.
Found an invitation

'Why hullo there! I am guessing you have come about the rumours? Well I am afraid they are true: Lobelia Sackville-Baggins is the official Yule-planner for the Hobbiton Yule-feast! It's dreadful, simply dreadful, I tell you! She has already announced that we will be getting nothing more than harvest-vegetables at the feast. The nerve of some folk!
'Lobelia also told us that we ought to end the festival early this year, what with all the roustabouts that have been coming in...says it isn't safe for decent folk to stay up late outdoors. Naught but vegetables and an early bed...what is a respectable hobbit to do!
'What's more, no one in Hobbiton is rightly sure how she came by the title. For years, old Mad Baggins held the position, and in turn Frodo Baggins took it after his disappearance. Something isn't right about the whole affair. Do you think you would be able to help us set things to rights?'

Search Sandyman's Mill for anything out of the ordinary
Talk to Will Whitfoot
Yuletide Woes
It appears that Lobelia Sackville-Baggins is the Hobbiton Yule-planner.
'Lobelia took a pony-cart up to Michel Delving maybe a month ago, but that is all I know.'

'I have heard a thing or two, but I am not one to spread rumours.
'But if you have to know, I heard she paid off Old Flourdumpling off in Michel Delving for the position.'

'Lobelia Sackville-baggins is trying to cheat Hobbiton out of their Yule-feast? I would love to help, but I fear my hands are tied in this matter.
'Lobelia came not a month ago seeking the laws relating to local Hobbiton feasts. If I remember correctly the Hobbiton-law states: Whosoever resides in the Hill at Bag End shall be charged with the planning and coordination of all local feasts and festival-activities and shall preside over said feasts in the absence of the Mayor.
'This law being a holdover from when the Baggins family was the chief residence of the Hill. Because the law was not changed or a new planner appointed, there is simply nothing I can do.'
'I haven't heard aught else save that we're all to eat our vegetables and get a proper nights rest. The cheek of it!'
'Lobelia has been coming and going on festival business, but I haven't heard how she came to the job.'
'Lobelia's post as Yule-planner? No, I haven't heard anything as to how she came by it.'

'I'm sorry, but I haven't heard anything about how Lobelia came by the Yule-planner post.
'Whatever shall we do? Yule will be ruined if Lobelia has her way!'
'The Yule-feast will be simply wonderful this year! The best that has been held for many a long season; leastwise, better than any that old fool Bilbo ever planned, that's for certain.'
'Be off! Can't you see we have a great deal of planning left to do before the Yule-feast?'
'Sorry, I haven't heard anything.'
'Lobelia? I heard she was up to some mischief away in Michel Delving...I'm sure that's how she came by the position.'
'If you need any help looking for information, I might be able to help you after another pint or two.'

'The Yule feast? Why my dad and I was personally invited by Lotho Sackville-baggins, but why I would tell the likes of you anything more is beyond me.
'Now be off! I have important things to be doing up at the mill without the likes of you snooping about my business.'
You have been asked to inquire among the Hobbiton-folk for an explanation of Lobelia's post as Yule-planner.

Sandyman's Mill is north of the bridge over the Water in Hobbiton.
Ted Sandyman's unusual behaviour might suggest a need to search Sandyman's Mill for anything out of the ordinary.

Will Whitfoot is at the Town Hole in Michel Delving, far to the west of Hobbiton.
You should report your findings to Will Whitfoot, the Mayor of the Shire.

'Well it seems your little plan worked! Fiddlesticks!
'Another party ruined, no thanks to you. Why don't you go tell your good friend Hamfast what you've done here? No doubt he put you up to all this, what with his precious Marigold being sent up here to embarrass me so.'

'So that Lobelia was planning on keeping all the best food for herself and her own? I'm glad that you were able to set things to rights, and so are the rest of the folk here in Hobbiton.
'We only thought it proper to get you something. Lobelia was right, in a way: we don't have much in the way of spare proffer, but we share what we can, especially for those who have given us as much as you!
'We would like you to have this Yule-tree. It's a transplant -- my nephew Halfast brought it down from the Northfarthing. We were going to plant it in the yard, but seeing as how you helped us so...well, Marigold thought it would be best if you took it for your house.'
A Happy Hobbiton
You were able to stop Lobelia's plan to keep all the best Yule-feast food for herself.

Gaffer Gamgee is outside his hole on Bagshot Row at the foot of the Hill.
You should tell Gaffer Gamgee about Lobelia's folied plans.

'Your pardon, friend, but could I beg a favour of you? I have this work order for materials and labour over in the Thorin's Hall community that I need delivered immediately to confirm our work dates with the purchaser. I know this is not much notice, but I can pay you well for your trouble.
'I need you to take this to Rúni over by the gates of the Thorin's Hall community, west of Thorin's Gate. You can't miss it.'

'What is this? Ah, the work order from Tyrvi. Thank you very much! We have been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Go ahead and bring this work order to Dúsi in the market square of the community. While you are there, why don't you take a look around...let me know if you see anything you like!'

'You have a work order from Tyrvi? Has this been signed yet?
'Finally! I've been sitting here on my thumbs for two days now! It's a shameful waste of time, if you ask me, but you can be sure that MY work will be done promptly at least.'
Bring the work order to Rúni
Bring the work order to Dúsi
Building the Thorin's Hall Homestead
New homes are always being built in the community of Thorin's Hall.

Rúni is near the gates of the Thorin's Hall homestead, west of Thorin's Gate.
Tyrvi has asked you to take a work order to Rúni..

Dúsi is in the market square of the Thorin's Hall homestead.
Rúni has signed the work order and asked you to take it to Dúsi.

'Ah, forgive me, traveller, could you aid me for a moment? I must deliver an important notice, but I cannot leave Duillond right at the moment.
'I have this order for fine woods in the Duillond community that I need carried immediately to confirm the time of delivery. Could you take this to Barchiril over by the gates of the Duillond community across the river and south at the crossroads beyond the bridge?
'It should require just a few minutes of your time, and Barchiril should compensate you well for the effort.'

'What is this? Ah, the confirmation from Badennas. Thank you very much! We have been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Would you be so kind as to bring this to Barthavron for me? He is a craftsman who can usually be found in the market square of the community.
'Should you see a home that might suit your needs while you are inside, please do let me know.'

'My thanks to you. It is good to know that Badennas has completed my order. Our construction of the most recent homes will soon be complete, thanks to his efforts.
'It seems strange to be building new and afresh even as so many of us seek to leave these lands. Be it one year or a thousand, our people still need places to live while they await their time to sail into the West.'
Bring the work order to Barchiril
Bring the work order to Barthavron
Building the Duillond Homestead
Though Duillond is small haven as far as Elf-refuges are concerned, there are those who dwell there for many seasons.

Barchiril is near the gates of the Duillond homestead, across the river and south from the crossroad.
Badennas has asked you to deliver a work order confirmation to Barchiril.

Barthavron is in the market square of the Duillond community.
Barchiril has signed the work order and asked you to take it to Barthavron.

'I just need you to take this to Andy Brockhouse over by the gates of the Michael Delving community, south of the town proper.'

'What is this? Ah, the work order from Overhill. Thank you very much! We've been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Could you do me a favour and take this in to Rolf Bracegirdle? He's a furnishing decorator in the community market square.
'And take a look around while you're there. I don't know if you're looking for a house right now, but you might see something that catches your fancy.'

'It seems that our wood order is finally on its way.
'Thank goodness! My stock is just about gone as it is. I was going to have to start chopping trees myself just to stay in business! Imagine!'
Bring the work order to Andy Brockhouse
Bring the work order to Rolf Bracegirdle
Building the Michael Delving Homestead
Michel Delving is a burgeoning community, with many new holes being dug.

Andy Brockhouse is near the gates of the Michel Delving homestead, south of the town proper.

Rolf Bracegirdle is in the market square of the Michel Delving homestead.

'Excuse me a moment, but could I beg a favour of you? I have this work order for materials and labor over in the Bree community that I need delivered immediately to confirm our work dates with the purchaser. I know this isn't much notice, but I can pay you well for your trouble.
'I just need you to take this to Nan Henwood over by the gates of the community a little ways south-east of here, east of those old ruins.'

'What is this? Ah, the work order from Sarabeth. Thank you very much! We've been hoping to see this for a few days now.
'Say, while you're here, could you take this to Bill Twiggins? He should be in the market square of the community.
'I don't know if you're looking for a house right now, but take a look around while you're there and let me know if anything catches your fancy.'

'What? Today? Where did this come from? Sarabeth? I didn't know this was going to be today! Oh no, Nan's going to kill me....
'Please excuse me. I have some things I need to see to immediately!'
Bring the work order to Nan Henwood
Bring the work order to Bill Twiggins
Building the Bree Homestead
Bree is a small town, but growing everyday due to the travellers coming up the Greenway from the South.

Nan Henwood is near the gates of the Bree homestead, south-east of Sarabeth Lowbanks, east of the old ruins there.
Sarabeth Lowbanks has asked you to deliver a work order confirmation to Nan Henwood.

Bill Twiggins is in the market square of the Bree homestead.

'So, Black-fang revealed Glorwen's fate to you before he was himself torn to pieces by his own pack? I deem it a fitting fate for such a monster, but not for poor Glorwen!
'There is but one glimmer of hope that remains - the hatred of the goblins for my people is such that they will not kill Glorwen if they can help it, they would much rather keep her in endless toil and torment until her will to live breaks and she either loses her mind or dies of her own accord.
'Luckily, Glorwen is no faint maiden to be easily broken by such as they, and thus we may have some time to effect her escape - but I would not have her suffer a minute longer beneath at the tender mercies of the goblins! If you can find a way into the dungeons of Goblin-town and release Glorwen, Rivendell will be forever in your debt - as will I.'

'Leave me be! Touch me again and I'll break your arm as I did the last of you filthy beasts who dared try it!'
'Oh! Forgive me! In this eternal darkness one does not come to expect a friendly face at the door... Who are you and how have you come to this hellish place?! Are you a fellow prisoner who has found a means of escape? Or a truly foolish ${RACE} who has come down here of your own accord?
'Never mind - it matters not, all that matters now is that we free the others and find our escape from this deadly prison, before we meet our ends so far from the light of the stars.'
Down, Down to Goblin-town

Having defeated the Warg pack-leader Black-fang and discovered the likely whereabouts of the missing Elvish hunter Glorwen, you now face the grim task of proceeding into the depths of Goblin-town itself to effect her rescue!

'Aye, good to see you here ${PLAYER}. As if we'd not enough to deal with here, it seems that a few of Rivendell's scouts have gone awry, somewhere east of here, up in High-pass.
'T'were a pair of them that passed through some few weeks ago, said there were rumours that a new Great-goblin has arisen in Goblin-town and were going to see if they were true, and make trouble for 'em if it was.
'We'll, there's trouble a plenty up in these mountains without a pair of flighty elves stirring up more, mark my words, but go they did and we've not heard aught from them since. One of my folk went along with 'em - fellow by the name of Eywind, so they ought to be fine.
'Hmm... Now that I think on it, Eywind is a bit of a hot-head himself. Went tagging along with the others as he fancied he'd find 'a bit more action' up in High-pass, as he put it, so maybe it'd be best if ye did go take a look and see if they're all right...'

'Ho there friend! What brings one such as you into the frozen peaks of High-pass?
'Glóin sent you, did he? Good fellow - well, it turns out we're fine here. Plenty of goblins to go around and the weather's not so bad, once you get used to it.
'Now, we do have quite a few things on the docket, if you will - that and it seems my skinny friend here has lost his fellow. Glorwen got up here a bit before us, and while she left sign of her safe arrival we've seen naught of her since. He's a cool one, but I think he's starting to get a bit worried.'
Into the High-pass

Glóin has told you of a trio of scouts sent forth from Rivendell and passed through his camp some weeks ago to scout the eastern reaches of the Misty Mountains, as they rise up into the High-pass.
These three - the Elves Nogmeldis and Glorwen, and the Dwarf Eywind - have been tasked with determining the strength of Goblin-town, where it has been rumoured that a new Great-goblin has taken the throne, and may be preparing for war against settlements on either side of the Misty Mountains.
Elrond has sent word that he would like to have someone proceed east to check up on them, as little has been heard from them since they passed through.
Find Eywind and his companions in High-pass, through the passage that runs past Pinnath Fenui and through Cirith Daur to the East.

'So you are not happy with your Harvestmath horse? Well, I can offer you an exchange, as I would not want one of my horses where it was not desired. However, this is not a decision to be taken lightly, so I will give you a moment to think about this.
'If you are really sure you want to exchange your horse, speak to me again, and I will give you a receipt in return. You can then exchange the receipt for a different horse.'

'So you have decided you want to exchange your Harvestmath horse? So be it. Take this receipt to Cam Applewood, and he shall provide you with a different horse.
'And this time, I hope you are more sure of your choice. Choosing a horse should not be something done lightly!'
'Have you made up your mind?'

'While you have come far as a Lore-master, ${PLAYER}, and have surpassed the abilities of many, there are those of such ability that no ${RACE} shall ever surpass. They are the Wizards, who were aged and wise when they first came to this Middle-earth and whose knowledge has only grown since then. Their arts lie beyond most understanding, although some insight can be gained from them.
'For instance, it is said that one of the Wizards, Radagast the Brown, resides among the Eglain in their camp near the cursed swamp of Agamaur. He is a friend of the wild and all the creatures of nature speak to him. It might be possible to gain insight into this ability from him, if you but ask him.
'If you would gain such a boon, travel to the Eglain encampment, which lies in the Lone-lands, and speak to Radagast there.'

'Have you come seeking a steed of your own? I may be able to help you. My father is teaching me to become a Horse-master in my own right someday, but currently the horses I breed lack the stamina his possess. However, they are more tame than my father's horses, so you should be able to ride one, if you so wish.
'I will grant you this boon, though, only in exchange for helping me. My father has made an arrangement with the Stable-masters of Bree. Instead of refunding their money for horses that have proven unusable in their trade, he has offered to do work for them. These tasks usually fall to me, but if you do some of these tasks for me, I will allow you to ride one of my steeds.
'The first task is to bring a sack of grain to Bill Rosewood at the stables near the West-gate of Bree. The grain is over to the east, by the silo.'

'Ah good, you have returned. You have my thanks for doing that for me. I...dislike those tasks and will be happy when the day comes when I can direct another to do such things. A true Horse-master has more to think of than delivering grain or mucking stalls.
'Now, though, to finish our agreement. You have done all that was asked of you, so now I will allow you to ride one of my tame mounts.
'Thank you again, and perhaps when you are more experienced, you can return and try to ride one of my father's mounts. Prepare yourself, though, my father won't let just anyone ride his steeds!'

'Well hello there! Without a word of direction, you come in and muck out one of my stalls. I never get that kind of service from Gaelm! Not that I need much help around here, but if he's trying to live up to the agreement his father put into place, he's not doing too good a job!
'Oh well, perhaps that's something that's learned with time. Anyway, there's nothing else I have to do today, so if you want, you can head on back to Gaelm and tell him all the work is done!'

'So Gaelm got you to do deliver the grain, did he? He has a ways to go if he's going to be half the Horse-master his father is! Never seen a boy try to avoid the less \qpleasant\q tasks that go along with breeding horses as much as Gaelm.
'Oh well, if he fooled you into doing his work for him, who am I to complain? As long as the job gets done!
'So, now that you are here, you'll need to do something else for me. The stalls at both my stables and Bert Goldenleaf's down by the South-gate need mucking out. How about drawing some water from the Boar Fountain in town and taking care of that for me?'

'Good job. Normally I would ask Gaelm to muck out all the stalls, but seeing as you probably didn't know what you were getting into, one will be fine for now.
'That's about all I need of you today, but Bert Goldenleaf's stalls are in about the same shape as mine. Why not go and give them the same treatment? Draw some water from the Boar Fountain and use it on one of Bert Goldenleaf's stalls.'
